alchemist.name: Alchemist
alchemist.guideHtml:
Alchemist is a scaling carry who turns gold into overwhelming damage through Greevil's Greed and Chemical Rage. With a 47.0% win rate across 157 k recent ranked games, he sits in the middle of the meta—strong enough to farm into late‑game power spikes but vulnerable to early aggression and mobile heroes.

How to Play Alchemist

Laning Phase

  • Use Acid Spray on creep waves to secure early lane control and force enemy supports to miss last‑hits; the armor reduction also makes your own creeps die faster, granting extra gold.
  • Stack Corrosive Weaponry on your attacks against the enemy off‑lane hero to apply the slow and armor‑reduction debuff, making ganks easier for your support.
  • Time Unstable Concoction throws to punish aggressive melee opponents (e.g., Ursa, Lifestealer); a fully brewed concoction stuns for ~2 s and can secure kills.
  • Drop Berserk Potion on yourself when you need a burst of attack speed to contest a contested pull or to escape a gank.
  • Prioritize last‑hitting with the help of the armor‑reduction from Acid Spray; the extra gold feeds Greevil's Greed early and accelerates your farm.

Mid Game

  • Hit the first Chemical Rage level (level 6) and start split‑pushing; the attack‑speed and movement‑speed boost let you take towers while staying survivable.
  • Join team fights after you have at least one Unstable Concoction ready; a well‑timed stun on a high‑damage hero (e.g., Storm Spirit) can swing the fight.
  • Use Greevil's Greed on rune pickups and enemy deaths to snowball gold lead; keep an eye on the 40‑second bonus window to chain kills.
  • Prioritize taking Roshan once you have a reliable Berserk Potion on yourself and a teammate, as the Aegis gives you the durability needed to survive enemy initiations.

Late Game

  • Position behind front‑line tanks and use Acid Spray + Corrosive Weaponry to shred enemy back‑liners; your damage spikes when you have a full stack of Greevil's Greed gold bonus.
  • Win the game by forcing high‑ground pushes with Chemical Rage‑enhanced attack speed, taking objectives while the enemy struggles to lock you down.
  • Avoid getting caught by mobile heroes (Storm Spirit, Monkey King, Luna) – they are the toughest matchups (win ≈ 44‑46%); keep a Berserk Potion on a teammate for a quick escape or dispel.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane.
  • Healing Salve — emergency HP for early ganks.
  • Iron Branch ×2 — cheap stats and can later be used for a Magic Wand.
  • Quelling Blade — faster creep last‑hits and early tower damage.

Core Items

  • Radiance — massive damage over time; synergizes with your high attack speed from Chemical Rage.
  • Mekansm — provides a team heal and armor, helping you survive the early fights where you are still fragile.
  • Assault Cuirass — armor reduction on enemies amplifies your Acid Spray and Corrosive Weaponry.
  • Black King Bar — essential against disables from Storm Spirit, Doom, and Skywrath Mage (your toughest matchups).

Situational Items

  • Satanic — huge survivability in prolonged fights; use the active to stay alive against burst heroes.
  • Heart of Tarrasque — extra HP regen for durability when you’re the primary front‑line.
  • Abyssal Blade — reliable stun to lock down mobile heroes like Monkey King and Void Spirit.
  • Butterfly — evasion against physical burst from heroes such as Luna and Ursa.
  • Linken's Sphere – blocks single‑target spells (e.g., Doom’s Doom, Skywrath Mage’s Arcane Bolt).

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑extending before Chemical Rage – trying to fight at level 5 leaves you vulnerable to ganks.
  • Neglecting Acid Spray on creeps – missing the armor‑reduction early wastes gold potential from Greevil's Greed.
  • Holding Unstable Concoction too long – waiting for max brew can cause you to miss the stun window and get killed.
  • Building damage items too early – without enough gold or a gold‑boosting rune, you fall behind the farm curve.

FAQ

Is Alchemist good in the current patch?

Yes. Alchemist sits at a 47.0% win rate on patch 7.41, making him a viable carry with strong late‑game scaling, though he requires careful early‑game play to reach his gold‑generation peaks.

What lane does Alchemist play?

Alchemist is most commonly played in the safe lane as a carry, but he can also be flexed to the off‑lane when paired with a strong support who can protect him from early aggression.

Who counters Alchemist?

Mobile and burst heroes such as Storm Spirit, Monkey King, Luna, Warlock, Skywrath Mage, and Doom have the highest win rates against him (44‑46%). Use Black King Bar, early defensive items, and keep a Berserk Potion on a teammate to mitigate their pressure.
alchemist.counterHtml:
Alchemist’s threat comes from his insane gold‑generation and the late‑game burst of damage and survivability granted by Chemical Rage. The most reliable way to shut him down is to deny him the farm and keep him constantly disabled before he can stack his corrosive effects or unleash a fully‑charged Unstable Concoction.

Why These Heroes Beat Alchemist

Storm Spirit

Storm’s Electric Vortex pulls Alchemist out of his safe corner, breaking his positioning and preventing a clean Unstable Concoction throw. Follow up with Overload bursts while Alchemist’s Chemical Rage cooldown is still on lock‑out for maximum damage.
Tip: Use Ball Lightning to chase him across the map; Alchemist’s low mobility makes him an easy target for repeated stun‑combo windows.

Monkey King

Monkey King’s Boundless Strike and Jungle‑style mobility let him dodge the area of Acid Spray and close the distance before Alchemist can finish brewing his concoction. The Wukong’s Command tree creates a shielded zone that blocks Alchemist’s Corrosive Weaponry stacks.
Tip: Initiate with Boundless Strike right after Alchemist starts brewing; the stun interrupts the charge and forces a waste of his primary damage source.

Luna

Luna’s Moon Glaives apply constant physical damage that ignores Alchemist’s armor‑reduction because the debuff only affects melee attacks. Her Eclipse burst deals massive pure damage, overwhelming Alchemist before Chemical Rage can activate.
Tip: Time Eclipse for the moment Alchemist finishes Unstable Concoction—the stun is broken and the burst kills him before the damage over time kicks in.

Warlock

Warlock’s Shadow Word provides sustained heal that outpaces Alchemist’s modest HP regen from Berserk Potion and Chemical Rage. More importantly, Fatal Bonds spreads any burst damage (e.g., Acid Spray) across multiple heroes, diluting its impact on Alchemist.
Tip: Keep Upheaval active in the lane; the slow prevents Alchemist from escaping after a Unstable Concoction stun, allowing you to follow up with a Chaotic Offering stun.

Skywrath Mage

Skywrath’s Arcane Bolt and Mystic Flare deal pure magic damage that bypasses Alchemist’s armor‑reduction and Corrosive Weaponry slow. The long‑range stun from Concussive Blast interrupts Alchemist’s brew, forcing a reset of Unstable Concoction.
Tip: Position behind a creep wave and spam Arcane Bolt; the constant poke forces Alchemist to retreat, denying him farm and stack buildup.

Drafting Against Alchemist

  • Prioritize heroes with reliable hard disables (stuns, silences) that can interrupt Unstable Concoction.
  • Pick mobile heroes that can close the distance quickly, preventing Alchemist from safely farming.
  • Include at least one hero with strong early‑game damage or lane control to deny his gold intake.
  • Avoid picking multiple melee heroes that benefit heavily from Corrosive Weaponry stacks.

Laning Against Alchemist

  • Harass him before he gets a Berserk Potion; his early damage is low and he lacks sustain.
  • Force him to use Acid Spray on creeps rather than you, then counter‑attack while the acid debuff is on the lane.
  • When he starts brewing Unstable Concoction, trade aggression—use a stun or silence to cancel the charge.
  • Keep the lane tight; a stretched lane gives Alchemist space to farm safely and stack gold.

Itemizing Against Alchemist

Eul's Scepter — provides a reliable single‑target disable that can interrupt a brewing Unstable Concoction and purge the slow from Corrosive Weaponry.
Ghost Scepter — makes you immune to his physical attacks, nullifying the damage boost from Chemical Rage and Corrosive Weaponry.
Scythe of Vyse — a strong, long‑duration stun that shuts down his mobility and prevents him from activating Chemical Rage in fights.
Aeon Disk — blocks the burst damage from Unstable Concoction and Eclipse, giving you a chance to survive his initial combo.

abaddon.name: Abaddon
abaddon.guideHtml:
Abaddon is a durable, semi‑carry hero who excels at survivability and team‑fight sustain thanks to Borrowed Time and Aphotic Shield. With a 51.5 % win rate across 170 k recent ranked games (OpenDota, July 2026), he remains a solid pick in both support and off‑lane roles, especially when paired with aggressive teammates.

How to Play Abaddon

Laning Phase

  • Use Mist Coil on yourself to trade health for damage when the enemy is low on HP; the heal component lets you stay in lane longer against aggressive opponents.
  • Drop Aphotic Shield on a creep or yourself before a tower dive to absorb burst damage and punish the attacker when the shield bursts.
  • Apply Withering Mist on enemy heroes (especially those reliant on healing like Lifestealer) to reduce their health restoration once they dip below 40 % HP.
  • Prioritize lane matchups where you have an advantage (e.g., against Axe or Dark Willow) and play more aggressively; avoid prolonged trades against hard counters such as Keeper of the Light or Kunkka, where your win rate drops to ~33–39 %.
  • Keep an eye on the enemy’s Aghanim’s Shard or Blink; if they have strong gap‑close, stay behind your Aphotic Shield and be ready to activate Borrowed Time pre‑emptively.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 6: Borrowed Time gives you a near‑instant survival tool; look for opportunities to initiate or counter‑initiate fights.
  • Roam with Aphotic Shield to protect key allies during ganks; a shielded carry can safely dive under tower or take a tower dive.
  • Group with your team around objectives; your Curse of Avernus provides attack‑speed bonus to allies and a damage‑over‑time to enemies, making you valuable in sieges.
  • Avoid isolated fights against heroes that outrange you (e.g., Keeper of the Light, Faceless Void) until you have a Mekansm or Guardian Greaves upgrade.

Late Game

  • Win condition: use Borrowed Time to soak burst from enemy ultimates (e.g., Void’s Chronosphere, Kunkka’s Ghostship) while your team focuses down the core.
  • Position near front‑line allies; a well‑timed Aphotic Shield can block tower or Roshan damage and turn it into a lethal burst.
  • Losing the game often comes from over‑extending without a shield or mis‑timing Borrowed Time, leaving you vulnerable to burst from the hardest counters (Keeper of the Light, Kunkka).

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane, especially when using Mist Coil on yourself.
  • Healing Salve — extra burst heal for early trades.
  • Observer Ward — vision to avoid ganks from mobile heroes like Kunkka.
  • Quelling Blade — last‑hit efficiency for a semi‑carry lane.

Core Items

  • Mekansm — upgrades to Guardian Greaves, adds a strong team heal and armor.
  • Phase Boots — provides mobility to land Aphotic Shield and chase down targets.
  • Vanguard → Crimson Guard — heavy physical damage block against Axe, Troll Warlord, and other right‑click cores.
  • Pipe of Insight — mitigates magical burst from Keeper of the Light and Faceless Void.

Situational Items

  • Holy Locket — amplifies the heal from Mist Coil and Aphotic Shield on allies.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target spells, useful against Kunkka’s Tidebringer or Keeper’s Solar Beam.
  • Aghanim’s Shard — gives a second Aphotic Shield charge, increasing shield uptime in team fights.
  • Black King Bar — essential when facing heavy magic control (Keeper of the Light, Faceless Void).
  • Heart of Tarrasque — massive health pool to maximize Borrowed Time uptime against burst heroes.

Common Mistakes

  • Spamming Mist Coil on enemies without considering the self‑damage, leading to early deaths.
  • Using Aphotic Shield on creeps when a teammate is about to engage; the shield’s burst damage is far more valuable on allies.
  • Waiting for Borrowed Time to auto‑activate instead of manually triggering it pre‑emptively against known burst.
  • Over‑extending into lane against hard counters (Keeper of the Light, Kunkka) where Abaddon’s win rate is below 40 %.

FAQ

Is Abaddon good in the current patch?

Yes. Abaddon sits at a 51.5 % win rate on patch 7.41, making him a reliable pick in both support and off‑lane roles, especially against heroes like Troll Warlord and Legion Commander where his win rate exceeds 60 %.

What lane does Abaddon play?

Abaddon is most commonly played in the safe lane as a durable support or semi‑carry, but he can also function in the off‑lane when paired with a strong lane partner. His flexibility lets him adapt to the team’s draft.

Who counters Abaddon?

The toughest matchups are against Keeper of the Light, Kunkka, Underlord, Marci, Clinkz, and Faceless Void, where his win rate drops to 33‑42 %. These heroes either out‑range him or apply burst damage that can overwhelm his survivability if not properly shielded.
abaddon.counterHtml:
Abaddon’s threat comes from his self‑healing Borrowed Time and the damage‑absorbing Aphotic Shield, which let him survive burst damage and turn fights into prolonged attrition. The key to shutting him down is denying him the health‑safety net and forcing him to spend his shield on non‑lethal damage.

Why These Heroes Beat Abaddon

Keeper of the Light

Keeper’s Illuminate and Chakra Magic apply pure magical damage that bypasses the damage‑reduction from Aphotic Shield, while his Spirit Form grants a strong dispel that removes the shield before it can trigger. Practical tip: pull a Mana Leak rune and spam Illuminate early to force Abaddon to waste Borrowed Time on non‑lethal hits.

Kunkka

Kunkka’s Torrent bursts damage and X Marks the Spot stun interrupt Abaddon’s automatic Borrowed Time trigger, and the subsequent Ghostship provides a massive shield that outscales Abaddon’s own shield. Practical tip: land a Torrent when Abaddon is below 40% HP to deny the health‑reduction debuff from Withering Mist.

Underlord

Firestorm deals pure AoE damage that ignores Aphotic Shield, and Pit of Malice roots Abaddon, preventing him from moving into a safe spot for Borrowed Time to auto‑activate. Practical tip: time a Firestorm just after Abaddon casts Borrowed Time; the shield will be wasted on pure damage.

Marci

Marci’s Dispose and Rebound provide high‑damage, short‑cooldown physical bursts that quickly deplete Abaddon’s health before Borrowed Time can trigger, while her Unleash grants a strong heal that outpaces Abaddon’s Mist Coil self‑damage. Practical tip: engage with Dispose from the side to avoid the shield’s initial barrier.

Clinkz

Clinkz’s Searing Arrows add true damage that pierces Aphotic Shield, and Death Pact grants massive lifesteal, allowing him to out‑heal Abaddon’s Mist Coil self‑damage. Practical tip: use Searing Arrows after a Skeletal Archer burst to force Abaddon to waste Borrowed Time on a non‑lethal hit.

Drafting Against Abaddon

  • Prioritize heroes with pure or true damage (e.g., Kunkka, Clinkz).
  • Include strong disables that can interrupt Borrowed Time (stuns, roots).
  • Pick heroes with high burst that can kill before Aphotic Shield expires.
  • Consider heroes with strong dispels to remove the shield early.

Laning Against Abaddon

  • Harass early with low‑damage spells; Abaddon’s Mist Coil self‑heal is limited by his own HP.
  • Force him to cast Aphotic Shield on creeps rather than on himself to waste its barrier.
  • Trade when his Borrowed Time is on cooldown—burst damage will be lethal.
  • Avoid prolonged fights under his shield; retreat and re‑engage after the shield breaks.

Itemizing Against Abaddon

Eul's Scepter of Divinity — silences and disables Abaddon, preventing him from activating Borrowed Time at critical moments.
Manta Style — creates illusion attacks that bypass Aphotic Shield and can trigger Borrowed Time on the real hero only.
Spirit Vessel — reduces healing, directly countering Mist Coil and the heal from Borrowed Time.
Abyssal Blade — provides a reliable stun to lock Abaddon out of Borrowed Time and forces him to take pure damage.

ancient-apparition.name: Ancient Apparition
ancient-apparition.guideHtml:
Ancient Apparition is a pure‑damage, magic‑damage‑amplifying support whose toolkit revolves around crippling enemies with Cold Feet, Ice Vortex, and the game‑changing Ice Blast. On patch 7.41 he enjoys a solid 51.2% win‑rate across 243 k recent ranked games, making him a reliable pick in the current meta.

How to Play Ancient Apparition

Laning Phase

  • Use Cold Feet on enemy supports or off‑laners who stay near the creep wave; the 4‑second stun forces them to retreat or waste regen, giving your carry lane space.
  • Drop Ice Vortex in the lane to apply a constant magic‑damage amp; it synergizes with any ally spell‑damage and makes early harass far more potent.
  • Pair Chilling Touch with your auto‑attacks to extend your attack range and add a small slow, allowing you to harass from safety.
  • Keep an eye on Bone Chill stacks on heroes that rely on strength (e.g., Bristleback, Centaur); each stack reduces their survivability and can be a decisive factor in lane trades.
  • Against tough matchups like Underlord or Spirit Breaker (win ≈ 35% in recent games), play conservatively and prioritize vision and defensive items to survive their early pressure.

Mid Game

  • Aim for Ice Blast on clustered enemy heroes during team fights; the larger the tracer distance, the bigger the explosion, turning any grouped push into a kill‑zone.
  • Follow up Ice Blast with Cold Feet on the primary target; the stun prevents them from escaping the blast radius and forces them into the damage.
  • Roam with Ice Vortex to amplify your mid‑lane or off‑lane carries’ spells, especially against heroes that lack magic resistance (e.g., Mars, Disruptor – where AA wins > 55%).
  • Prioritize buying Glimmer Cape or Force Staff to stay alive long enough to land your ultimate; a dead AA means no damage amplification for your team.

Late Game

  • Win condition: lock down high‑value enemy cores with Cold Feet + Ice Blast while your carries dish out amplified magic damage.
  • Position near the backline but within range of Ice Vortex; you must be safe from flankers yet close enough to trigger Ice Blast on time.
  • Losing the game often stems from being caught out before you can cast Ice Blast—avoid over‑extending and keep a Ghost Scepter or Eul’s ready for self‑save.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane.
  • Healing Salve — emergency health.
  • Observer Ward — vision control, essential for early ganks.
  • Sentry Ward — counter invisible heroes and protect your Ice Vortex.
  • Faerie Fire — cheap burst of damage for last‑hits.

Core Items

  • Glimmer Cape — survivability; lets you stay alive to cast Ice Blast.
  • Force Staff — mobility to close distance for Cold Feet or escape flankers.
  • Aghanim’s Shard — upgrades Ice Vortex to a larger radius, increasing magic amp.
  • Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — self‑save and additional disable to set up Cold Feet.

Situational Items

  • Ghost Scepter — against right‑click heroes like Clinkz (AA win ≈ 36%).
  • Lotus Orb — reflects targeted spells; useful versus Invoker and Tusk (win ≈ 38‑41%).
  • Aether Lens — extends cast range of Ice Blast and Cold Feet, crucial for long‑range engagements.
  • Scythe of Vyse — extra hard‑disable when you need guaranteed crowd control.
  • Shiva’s Guard — armor and AoE slow; counters physical‑heavy lineups and amplifies your magic damage.

Common Mistakes

  • Casting Ice Blast too early without confirming enemy clustering, wasting its massive damage potential.
  • Forgetting to apply Bone Chill stacks on strength‑based heroes, missing a cheap kill‑steal.
  • Over‑extending without a defensive item, leading to early deaths that nullify your late‑game impact.
  • Ignoring vision; without wards, you cannot position Ice Vortex or land Ice Blast safely.

FAQ

Is Ancient Apparition good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 51.2% win‑rate across over 243 k ranked games, AA is a solid pick. His ability to amplify magic damage and lock down key targets makes him valuable, especially against heroes weak to magic amplification.

What lane does Ancient Apparition play?

Ancient Apparition is typically played as a support in the safe lane (position 4) or as a roaming support (position 5). His early harass and vision tools allow him to protect the carry while setting up kills with Cold Feet and Ice Vortex.

Who counters Ancient Apparition?

Heroes with strong early burst and mobility—Underlord, Spirit Breaker, Clinkz, Tusk, Viper, and Invoker—have the lowest win‑rates against AA (35‑41%). Building defensive items like Ghost Scepter, Lotus Orb, and maintaining good vision are essential to survive their pressure.
ancient-apparition.counterHtml:
Ancient Apparition thrives on global, pure‑magic damage and the ability to lock enemies down with Cold Feet and Ice Blast. To shut him down you must either prevent his spells from landing, out‑range his global presence, or nullify the amplified damage his vortex provides.

Why These Heroes Beat Ancient Apparition

Underlord

Underlord’s Firestorm and Pit of Malice force constant movement, making it impossible for AA’s Cold Feet to keep a target stationary long enough to stun. His Dark Rift also lets him escape the global reach of Ice Blast or reposition for a counter‑gank. Tip: use Dark Rift to pull a teammate into a safe lane when you spot AA’s tracer heading your side.

Spirit Breaker

Spirit Breaker’s Charge of Darkness provides massive burst movement that can outrun the 4‑second window of Cold Feet, and his Greater Bash interrupts AA’s channeling of Ice Blast if timed on the tracer. The hero’s innate tankiness also reduces the impact of AA’s amplified magic damage. Tip: charge onto AA as soon as he launches a tracer to force a premature release.

Clinkz

Clinkz’s Searing Arrows and Death Pact give him high burst damage that can kill AA before he lands a vortex or tracer, while his Burning Army provides constant AoE pressure that forces AA to stay back. Clinkz’s mobility with Burning Army also lets him dodge Ice Blast explosions. Tip: keep a Burning Army on the lane edge to block AA’s line of sight for his tracer.

Tusk

Tusk’s Ice Shards creates a wall that blocks AA’s line of sight, preventing the tracer from traveling far enough to be threatening. Snowball can stun AA mid‑cast, canceling Ice Blast and Cold Feet. Tip: position Snowball to intercept the tracer’s path, forcing AA to waste the ability.

Viper

Viper’s Nose Dive and Viper Strike apply strong poison damage that outpaces AA’s magic burst, and his Corrosive Skin reduces magic damage taken, mitigating the amplified damage from Ice Vortex. Viper’s lane dominance also forces AA to stay under tower, limiting his global presence. Tip: use Nose Dive to close distance quickly and disrupt AA’s positioning before he can cast Cold Feet.

Drafting Against Ancient Apparition

  • Prioritize heroes with strong gap‑closers or global mobility (e.g., Spirit Breaker, Tusk) to outrun or intercept his tracer.
  • Pick magic‑resistant or spell‑immune heroes (e.g., Abaddon, Hoodwink) to blunt his amplified damage.
  • Include heroes with reliable disables that can interrupt channeling (e.g., Earthshaker, Lion).
  • Consider banning Underlord if you lack a reliable way to counter his area control.

Laning Against Ancient Apparition

  • Trade early harassment with ranged auto‑attacks; AA’s damage is low until he lands Ice Vortex.
  • Force him to use Cold Feet on a creep or tower to waste the stun timer.
  • Punish him when his Ice Blast tracer is on the ground—attack the tracer to force an early release.
  • Play aggressively when his mana is low (typically after a Ice Vortex or Ice Blast cast) to deny him vision and set up ganks.

Itemizing Against Ancient Apparition

Glimmer Cape — grants temporary magic immunity, nullifying the burst from Ice Blast and the amplified damage of Ice Vortex.
Aeon Disk — prevents AA’s burst from killing you outright, buying time for teammates to intervene.
Black King Bar — provides reliable magic immunity during team fights, rendering Ice Blast and Cold Feet ineffective.
Ghost Scepter — makes you ethereal, causing AA’s physical attacks and Chilling Touch to miss, while still allowing you to dodge Ice Blast with positioning.

anti-mage.name: Anti-Mage
anti-mage.guideHtml:
Anti‑Mage is a late‑game, mana‑burning carry whose strength lies in evading spells with Counterspell and Blink while melting enemy mana pools with Mana Break. In the current 7.41 meta his overall win rate sits at 49.4 % across 457 k ranked games, making him a solid but not dominant pick.

How to Play Anti‑Mage

Laning Phase

  • Mana Break early harass: trade when the enemy uses spells (e.g., Silencer’s Glaives) to deplete their mana and amplify damage.
  • Blink for safe farming: use the short‑range teleport to dodge aggressive melee heroes (e.g., Sven) and to secure last‑hits under tower pressure.
  • Counterspell passive magic resistance: position to block incoming magical harassment from lane opponents such as Lich or Ember Spirit.
  • Persecutor synergy: once the enemy’s mana drops below 50 % (common after early spells), the slow becomes significant—use it to chase or kite.
  • Prioritize mana‑draining heroes (Silencer, Lich) for lane dominance; avoid prolonged fights against high‑burst, mana‑rich heroes like Timbersaw where your win rate is only 35.9 % (64 games).

Mid Game

  • Power spike at 20 k farm: acquire Battle Fury and Manta Style to unlock split‑push and spell‑block potential.
  • Blink‑initiated ganks on isolated spell‑casters; Counterspell can reflect their spells, turning fights in your favor.
  • Mana Void combo: after a teammate drains a hero’s mana (e.g., with Dark Willow’s Bramble Maze), follow up with Mana Void for massive AoE damage.
  • Focus on tower pressure in the safe lane while keeping an eye on enemy mid‑lane heroes (Templar Assassin, Ember Spirit) whose win rates against you are sub‑45 %.

Late Game

  • Win condition: split‑push with Battle Fury, force the enemy to defend, then Blink in for a quick Mana Void burst on the core.
  • Positioning: stay just out of enemy spell range; rely on Counterspell’s active shield to survive targeted ultimates.
  • Game‑losing mistakes: over‑extending without Blink escape, or engaging heroes with strong disables (e.g., Ogre Magi) where your win rate is only 42.6 %.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain against harassment.
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery after early trades.
  • Quelling Blade — easier last‑hits under tower.
  • Iron Branch x2 — cheap stats and can build into a Magic Wand later.
  • Slippers of Agility — early damage for Mana Break scaling.

Core Items

  • Battle Fury — primary farm tool; cleave amplifies Mana Break damage.
  • Manta Style — provides Blink‑style mobility, dispels silences, and adds extra damage.
  • Black King Bar — essential against heavy magical burst (e.g., Jakiro, Ember Spirit).
  • Butterfly — evasion and damage; synergizes with Blink‑in‑and‑out play.

Situational Items

  • Satanic — survivability when you’re the primary target in teamfights.
  • Abyssal Blade — lock down elusive heroes like Morphling; also gives a stun for follow‑up Mana Void.
  • Monkey King Bar — counter evasion from heroes such as Phantom Assassin.
  • Linken’s Sphere — blocks single‑target spells (e.g., Templar Assassin’s Refraction).
  • Eye of Skadi — adds HP and a universal slow, useful against tanky heroes.

Common Mistakes

  • Relying on Blink for offense only – forgetting its defensive value leads to unnecessary deaths.
  • Ignoring mana‑drain opportunities – failing to harass spell‑casters early wastes Mana Break’s true potential.
  • Over‑committing to fights against Timbersaw or Ember Spirit – these matchups have sub‑41 % win rates for Anti‑Mage.
  • Delaying Battle Fury – without it, farm stalls and you fall behind the enemy carry’s mid‑game power spike.

FAQ

Is Anti‑Mage good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 49.4 % win rate across 457 k ranked matches, Anti‑Mage remains a viable carry, especially against mana‑heavy heroes. His win rates are strongest versus heroes like Sven (60.8 %) and Silencer (59.3 %).

What lane does Anti‑Mage play?

Anti‑Mage is typically played in the safe lane as a carry, allowing him to farm safely while using Mana Break and Counterspell to survive early harassment.

Who counters Anti‑Mage?

The toughest opponents right now are Timbersaw (35.9 % win rate vs. AM), Ember Spirit (40.7 %), Templar Assassin (42.0 %), Jakiro (42.5 %), Morphling (42.6 %), and Ogre Magi (42.6 %). These heroes either out‑burst him early or have strong disables that punish over‑extension.
anti-mage.counterHtml:
Anti‑Mage is a late‑game hyper‑carries whose threat comes from burning enemy mana, blinking in for relentless right‑clicks, and finishing fights with a huge Mana Void burst. The quickest way to shut him down is to deny him the mana pool he relies on and to lock him down before he can Blink away.

Why These Heroes Beat Anti‑Mage

Timbersaw

Timbersaw’s pure‑damage, mana‑draining abilities (Whirling Death, Chakram, and Reactive Armor) deplete Anti‑Mage’s mana faster than Mana Break can burn it, causing Persecutor’s slow to hit its maximum and leaving him vulnerable to burst. Tip: hit him with a quick combo of Whirling Death → Chakram → Timber Chain to keep his mana near zero and force a death‑spell before he can Blink out.

Ember Spirit

Ember Spirit’s high burst from Sleight of Fist and Flame Guard deals mostly non‑mana‑based damage, while his mobility lets him dodge Blink and chase down Anti‑Mage. Tip: land a Sleight of Fist followed by a stun (e.g., from a support) to prevent the Blink and force a melee trade where Ember’s damage outpaces Mana Break.

Templar Assassin

Refraction blocks the first few attacks and grants a shield that negates Mana Break’s mana burn, while Meld gives burst damage and a brief invisibility to close the gap. Tip: open with a Meld → Refraction combo, then burst with Psi Blades before Anti‑Mage can Blink away.

Jakiro

Jakiro’s dual‑spell pressure (Dual Breath, Ice Path, and Liquid Fire) constantly burns mana and applies slows, preventing Anti‑Mage from reaching the 50 % mana threshold needed for Persecutor’s full slow. Tip: chain Ice Path into Dual Breath to lock him in place and force a mana‑draining fight where his Blink is useless.

Morphling

Morphling’s Attribute Shift can give him huge burst damage while also stealing mana with Waveform, and his Replicate can create a high‑damage illusion that forces Anti‑Mage to fight on Morph’s terms. Tip: use Waveform to close the gap, then burst with Adaptive Strike before Anti‑Mage can Blink away.

Drafting Against Anti‑Mage

  • Prioritize heroes with strong pure‑damage or mana‑drain (Timbersaw, Ember Spirit, Templar Assassin).
  • Include reliable disables that can interrupt Blink (stuns, silences, hexes).
  • Pick heroes with high early‑game lane presence to keep Anti‑Mage mana‑starved.
  • Consider a magic‑immune or spell‑block hero to neutralize Counterspell (e.g., Anti‑Mage’s Counterspell is less effective against pure damage).

Laning Against Anti‑Mage

  • Harass aggressively when his mana is above 50 %; his Persecutor slow is weak and he can’t retaliate effectively.
  • Force early tower dives or rune contests to deplete his mana pool before he gets a Blink.
  • Use creep‑wave manipulation and deny to keep his farm low, limiting his ability to purchase early Blink upgrades.
  • Punish any over‑extension with a stun or burst damage before he can Blink back.

Itemizing Against Anti‑Mage

Abyssal Blade — provides a reliable stun that prevents Blink and forces a melee fight where Mana Break is less effective.
Scythe of Vyse — hexes Anti‑Mage, completely nullifying Blink and Counterspell for several seconds.
Heaven's Halberd — disarms him, removing his right‑click damage and mana‑burn while the disarm is active.
Orchid / Bloodthorn — silences him, stopping Counterspell activation and Mana Void casting.
Manta Style — creates illusion copies that split the damage from Mana Void and can purge slows from Persecutor.

arc-warden.name: Arc Warden
arc-warden.guideHtml:
Arc Warden is a high‑skill, split‑push carry whose strength lies in creating a perfect duplicate with Tempest Double and overwhelming opponents with relentless damage and map control. On patch 7.41 his overall pub win rate sits at 50.3% over 135 k recent ranked games, making him a solid but not dominant pick in the current meta.

How to Play Arc Warden

Laning Phase

  • Use Flux early to harass melee supports and force them to pull back; the damage‑over‑time and slow are especially potent when the enemy lane is isolated.
  • Pair Magnetic Field with a safe lane partner (e.g., a ranged support) to grant both attack‑speed and evasion, allowing you to farm safely against aggressive mid heroes.
  • Stack the Runic Infusion rune early; each activation on you or your double gives +1.5 all attributes, scaling your damage and survivability.
  • When facing burst heroes like Queen of Pain or Shadow Fiend (against whom Arc Warden wins only ~35‑37% of games), prioritize early defensive items (e.g., Infused Raindrop) and keep the lane tight to deny them easy kills.
  • Secure a Spark Wraith near the creep wave to scout for hidden ganks and to provide an extra source of damage when the enemy approaches.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 12 when you first unlock Tempest Double; immediately look for split‑push opportunities on side lanes while your double farms the main lane.
  • Place Magnetic Field around high‑ground towers or Roshan to protect yourself and your double while you take objectives.
  • Target enemy cores that lack reliable disables; your double can safely dive them thanks to the evasion from Magnetic Field.
  • Avoid prolonged team fights against heroes with strong single‑target burst (e.g., QOP, SF) until you have a Manta Style or Black King Bar.

Late Game

  • Win condition: use your double to create two simultaneous pressure points—one pushing a lane, the other joining a team fight or taking Roshan.
  • Position your Magnetic Field to shield yourself and your double from enemy right‑clicks; a well‑placed field can turn the tide of a 5‑v‑5 fight.
  • Losing the game usually stems from over‑extending the double without vision or failing to protect the real Arc Warden, allowing enemies to focus and kill the original hero.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango & Healing Salve — sustain in lane.
  • Iron Branch x2 — cheap attribute boost and can later be used for Magic Wand.
  • Faerie Fire — emergency burst heal against early harass.
  • Observer Ward — vision against ganks, especially important against mobile heroes like QOP.

Core Items

  • Mekansm — provides armor and a strong AoE heal that synergizes with double‑farm.
  • Manta Style — essential for dispelling silences and adding a third source of damage; also gives extra attack speed for both Arc Warden and the double.
  • Butterfly — massive evasion and attack speed, crucial for surviving heroes with high physical damage (e.g., Dragon Knight).
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Tempest Double cooldown and allows the double to cast items, dramatically increasing split‑push potential.

Situational Items

  • Black King Bar — when facing heavy magical burst or disables (e.g., Rubick, Crystal Maiden).
  • Heart of Tarrasque — if you’re being focused in prolonged fights; the massive health pool lets you stay alive while your double dishes out damage.
  • Linken’s Sphere — against single‑target spells like QOP’s Sonic Wave or Shadow Fiend’s Shadowrazes.
  • Satanic — provides lifesteal and a strong active heal for clutch survivability.
  • Scythe of Vyse — for extra crowd control when you need to lock down mobile heroes that currently give you a low win rate (e.g., QOP, SF).

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑relying on the double early – spawning the double before you have enough items or levels makes it easy for the enemy to kill both copies.
  • Neglecting Magnetic Field placement – failing to keep yourself inside the field leaves you vulnerable to right‑clicks and disables.
  • Chasing kills instead of split‑pushing – Arc Warden’s strength is map pressure; diving into team fights without a defensive item often leads to death.
  • Ignoring runes – missing Runic Infusion activations wastes permanent attribute gains that scale into the late game.

FAQ

Is Arc Warden good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 50.3% win rate across 135 k recent ranked matches, Arc Warden is a viable carry, especially on maps where split‑push and map control are rewarded.

What lane does Arc Warden play?

Arc Warden is typically played in the safe lane as a carry, using Flux and Magnetic Field to survive early harassment and to farm safely alongside a support.

Who counters Arc Warden?

Heroes with strong burst and reliable disables—Queen of Pain, Shadow Fiend, Dragon Knight, Crystal Maiden, Snapfire, and Rubick—currently give Arc Warden win rates below 45%, making them his toughest matchups. Vision, early defensive items, and careful double management are key to surviving them.
arc-warden.counterHtml:
Arc Warden’s threat lies in his Tempest Double, which can duplicate every item and ability, turning a single hero into a split‑push, team‑fight, and split‑damage nightmare. The core way to shut him down is to deny his double the space and resources to farm, and to apply hard‑kill pressure that a duplicated hero cannot survive.

Why These Heroes Beat Arc Warden

Queen of Pain

Her Scream of Pain and Shadow Strike provide burst magic damage that bypasses Arc Warden’s Magnetic Field evasion, while her mobility lets her dodge the Double’s Flux and Spark Wraith. Tip: Use Blink to jump into the Double’s field, drop a quick Scream of Pain, then retreat before the Double can react.

Shadow Fiend

Shadow Fiend’s Shadowrazes deal pure damage and stack quickly, overwhelming the Double’s health pool before Arc Warden can rebuild with Runic Infusion. The high attack speed from Requiem also shreds the Double’s low armor. Tip: Prioritize early Necromastery stacks; a 10‑stack lead already forces the Double to die in lane.

Dragon Knight

Dragon Tail provides a reliable stun that interrupts the Double’s spellcasting, and Elder Dragon Form grants bonus armor and a cleave that punishes the Double’s low survivability. Tip: Time the stun on the Double’s Tempest Double activation to cancel the duplicate before it can use items.

Crystal Maiden

Her Crystal Nova slows both the real Arc Warden and his Double, reducing their attack speed and making them vulnerable to ganks. The free mana regen from Arcane Aura lets allies spam disables, limiting the Double’s item usage. Tip: Position Crystal Maiden near the lane’s edge; a well‑timed Frostbite on the Double forces a forced death.

Snapfire

Snapfire’s Firesnap Cookie provides a burst of magic damage that ignores the Double’s evasion, and her Mortimer Kisses can zone the Double out of fights. The Cookie also silences, preventing the Double from casting Flux or Spark Wraith. Tip: Drop a Cookie on the Double as soon as it appears; the silence plus damage often kills it before it can act.

Drafting Against Arc Warden

  • Prioritize heroes with reliable hard‑crowd control (stuns, silences) that can lock down the Double.
  • Pick high burst magic damage heroes; pure or magic damage bypasses Magnetic Field evasion.
  • Include early‑game split‑push or lane‑dominant heroes to deny Arc Warden farm.
  • Consider banning heroes with strong late‑game scaling items that the Double can duplicate (e.g., Monkey King Bar, Satanic).

Laning Against Arc Warden

  • Harass him before he can secure a Runic Infusion rune; his early damage is low.
  • Force him to use Flux on a creep or tower, then trade with a spell that punishes the slowed target.
  • When his Double spawns, focus fire the double first; killing it removes half of his lane presence.
  • Use lane‑control abilities (e.g., Crystal Nova, Frostbite) to keep him from safely last‑hitting.

Itemizing Against Arc Warden

Eul's Scepter — provides a reliable disable that can temporarily remove the Double from the fight, buying time for teammates to burst him down.
Scythe of Vyse — a hard silence that stops the Double from casting Flux, Spark Wraith, or using items.
Black King Bar — prevents the Double’s magical burst (e.g., Shadowrazes, Scream of Pain) from killing you during team fights.
Abyssal Blade — a stun that forces the Double to stay in place, allowing focused fire to kill it before it can split‑push.

axe.name: Axe
axe.guideHtml:
Axe remains a high‑impact initiator and frontline tank in the current meta, boasting a solid 52.2% win rate over 724 k recent ranked games. His blend of armor, burst kill potential with Culling Blade, and relentless teamfight presence keeps him relevant across all skill brackets, though certain matchups still tilt heavily against him.

How to Play Axe

Laning Phase

  • Use Berserker's Call early to force enemy melee supports (e.g., Vengeful Spirit, Tidehunter) to attack you while you gain bonus armor, turning aggressive harass into safe farming.
  • Cast Battle Hunger on a squishy off‑lane hero (e.g., Shadow Shaman) to pressure them into using a heal or retreat, while the slow punishes any back‑step.
  • Stack Counter Helix triggers by last‑hitting with a fast attack rhythm; aim for a 3‑attack stack before a tower dive or gank.
  • When the enemy lane has a strong lane bully (e.g., Bristleback), position near your creeps and use Berserker's Call to absorb damage and let your tower chip them.
  • Keep an eye on One Man Army: if you’re alone for >3 s, you’ll gain extra Strength from your armor—use this to out‑trade isolated opponents.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 6: Culling Blade + Berserker's Call enables instant 2‑hero kills; look for isolated supports or low‑HP cores.
  • Group with your team and use Berserker's Call followed by Counter Helix to dominate early teamfights; the armor bonus lets you survive burst from mid‑lane carries.
  • Prioritize objectives after a successful fight—Axe’s tankiness lets you tank tower hits while your allies finish the structure.
  • When facing tough matchups (Bane, Naga Siren, Lycan, Chen, Monkey King, Treant), avoid 1v1 engagements; instead, wait for your team’s Culling Blade reset to secure a kill in a 3‑plus‑hero fight.

Late Game

  • Win condition: force Berserker's Call on enemy cores, let Counter Helix whittle them down, and use Culling Blade to reset and finish the fight.
  • Position near the front line but stay within 700 units of an ally only when you need to drop One Man Army for extra Strength; otherwise, stay isolated to maximize the passive.
  • Losing the game often stems from over‑extending without backup—Axe’s lack of mobility makes him vulnerable to silences and disables that can break his Call and let enemies focus him down.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane against harassment.
  • Healing Salve — quick HP recovery after early skirmishes.
  • Stout Shield — mitigates harass from ranged off‑laners.
  • Quelling Blade — faster creep last‑hits and easier Counter Helix stacking.
  • Iron Branch ×2 — cheap stat boost and later can be used for a Magic Wand.

Core Items

  • Blink Dagger — essential for initiating with Berserker's Call and catching out‑of‑position heroes.
  • Vanguard → Crimson Guard — high armor and damage block against physical burst, synergizes with One Man Army.
  • Blade Mail — punishes enemy spellcasters and heroes that rely on single‑target damage (e.g., Bane, Chen).
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Culling Blade to a longer‑range execute, increasing kill potential in late‑game fights.

Situational Items

  • Black King Bar — necessary against heavy magical disables (Bane, Chen).
  • Shiva’s Guard — adds armor, slows enemy cores, and provides an extra source of damage for teamfights.
  • Heart of Tarrasque — maximizes durability when you’re the primary front line.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target spells, useful versus Monkey King’s jumps or Lycan’s summons.
  • Glimmer Cape — defensive option when you need to survive a burst from Terrorblade or Morphling.

Common Mistakes

  • Rushing Culling Blade before level 6** – without Berserker's Call you lack the survivability to land the execute safely.
  • Staying too close to allies – this disables One Man Army’s Strength gain, reducing Axe’s damage and tankiness.
  • Using Battle Hunger on already‑dead or invisible heroes – wastes mana; instead, target heroes that are forced to chase you.
  • Over‑committing without vision – Axe’s lack of mobility makes him an easy target for Bane’s Nightmare or Chen’s creeps if you dive blind.

FAQ

Is Axe good in the current patch?

Yes. Axe holds a 52.2% win rate across over 724 k recent ranked matches, making him a reliable initiator and durable front‑liner in patch 7.41.

What lane does Axe play?

Axe is most commonly played in the off‑lane as a durable initiator, though he can also be flexed to safe‑lane or even solo mid if the draft calls for a strong early‑game tank.

Who counters Axe?

The toughest matchups are against Bane, Naga Siren, Lycan, Chen, Monkey King, and Treant Protector, where Axe’s win rates dip below 40%. These heroes either out‑disable him or avoid his Call, forcing Axe to rely on teammates for kills.
axe.counterHtml:
Axe thrives on forcing fights with his taunt and turning enemy aggression into pure damage through Counter‑Helix. The key to shutting him down is denying him the melee front‑line presence he needs to spin his helix and keeping him isolated so his One Man Army bonus never activates.

Why These Heroes Beat Axe

Bane

Bane’s Nightmare and Fiend’s Grip lock Axe in place, preventing him from triggering Counter‑Helix and forcing him to waste his Culling Blade on a stunned target. Pick a Soul Ring early to keep your mana flowing for continuous disables.
Practical tip: Drop a Aghanim’s Shard for Enfeeble; the extra damage reduction makes Axe’s auto‑attacks far less threatening.

Naga Siren

Naga’s Mirror Image creates illusion farms that soak up Axe’s taunt, while Riptide slows and silences him, breaking the combo of Battle Hunger and Berserker’s Call. Maintain distance and use Ensnare on the real Naga to punish his low mobility.
Practical tip: Position your Manta Style split‑second after Axe initiates; the extra movement speed helps you escape his Culling Blade reset window.

Lycan

Lycan’s Summon Wolves provide a constant source of ranged damage that Axe cannot reliably taunt, and Feral Impulse grants bonus attack speed that outpaces Axe’s Counter‑Helix triggers. Use Shapeshift to gain burst movement and disengage before Axe can land his Culling Blade.
Practical tip: Stack Lycan’s Wolves near your tower; Axe’s aggression will pull them into tower range where they die quickly.

Chen

Chen’s Penitence slows Axe’s attack speed, dramatically reducing the frequency of Counter‑Helix spins, while his Holy Persuasion can turn Axe’s own creeps against him. Keep a Lotus Orb to reflect the occasional Berserker’s Call if you get caught.
Practical tip: Pull a neutral camp with Holy Persuasion and place it between you and Axe; the creeps will block his taunt radius.

Monkey King

Monkey King’s Tree Dance provides constant vertical escape routes that Axe’s short‑range taunt cannot reach, and Wukong’s Command creates a zone where Axe cannot safely spin his helix without taking massive damage. Build Phase Boots for quick repositioning.
Practical tip: Time Boundless Strike right after Axe’s Culling Blade reset; the stun prevents him from re‑engaging immediately.

Drafting Against Axe

  • Prioritize heroes with strong disables or silences (e.g., Bane, Lion, Shadow Shaman).
  • Pick ranged, high‑mobility heroes that can stay out of Berserker’s Call radius.
  • Include at least one tank or initiator with true strike/armor‑piercing (e.g., Sven, Tidehunter).
  • Consider heroes that can summon or create units to absorb Axe’s taunt (e.g., Chen, Naga Siren).

Laning Against Axe

  • Harass him with ranged harass and deny creep XP; Axe’s early damage relies on farm.
  • Trade when his Battle Hunger is on cooldown; his damage output drops sharply.
  • Force him to use Berserker’s Call on a tower or neutral creep to waste the armor buff.
  • Keep a safe distance when his Counter Helix counter is low (typically after 2‑3 attacks).

Itemizing Against Axe

Blade Mail — reflects the pure damage from Counter‑Helix and Culling Blade back onto Axe.
Ghost Scepter — makes you immune to Axe’s melee attacks, nullifying Counter‑Helix spins.
Force Staff — lets you escape the radius of Berserker’s Call and reposition for a counter‑engage.
Heaven’s Halberd — disarms Axe, preventing the auto‑attacks that trigger Counter‑Helix.

bane.name: Bane
bane.guideHtml:
Bane is a durable support‑disabler whose kit revolves around long‑duration crowd control and sustained damage. On patch 7.41 his overall win rate sits at 49.9 % across 148 k recent ranked games, placing him slightly below average but still viable in coordinated play. His strengths shine against melee front‑liners, while mobile spell‑casters and high‑damage initiators remain his toughest opponents.

How to Play Bane

Laning Phase

  • Nightmare early on to lock down aggressive lane heroes (e.g., Axe, Earthshaker) and force them to waste mana on breaking the sleep.
  • Pair Enfeeble with a lane partner’s right‑clicks to cripple enemy damage output and reduce their cast range, making them easier to pull into Nightmare.
  • Use Brain Sap on creeps or a low‑health enemy to sustain yourself while maintaining lane presence.
  • Save Nightmare End for moments when the enemy dives; ending the sleep early can let you reposition or pull them into a teammate’s hook/disable.
  • Prioritize vision (warding) to protect against roaming heroes like Monkey King and Skywrath Mage, who statistically give Bane a sub‑50 % win rate (35 % vs MK, 45 % vs Skywrath Mage).

Mid Game

  • Fiend’s Grip becomes a decisive pick‑off on squishy cores; aim for heroes with limited escape (e.g., Templar Assassin, Tiny).
  • After a successful grip, apply Ichor of Nyctasha to lower enemy status resistance, making subsequent disables (Nightmare, Enfeeble) more potent.
  • Group with your team around objectives; Bane’s damage over time and mana drain from Fiend’s Grip synergize with AOE pushes.
  • Avoid isolated fights against high‑mobility heroes like Monkey King and Mars, whose win rates against Bane are 35 % and 45 % respectively.

Late Game

  • Win condition: lock down the enemy carry with Nightmare + Fiend’s Grip while your cores deal damage; the combined burst can finish fights before the enemy can react.
  • Positioning: stay behind front‑liners, using Enfeeble on the primary initiator to reduce their damage and cast range, then chain Nightmare to the nearest threat.
  • Losing the game: over‑extending without vision, allowing enemy initiators (Primal Beast, Mars) to engage before you can land your grip, often results in a loss.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — basic sustain for lane survivability.
  • Healing Salve — quick HP recovery after early skirmishes.
  • Observer Ward — essential for protecting against early ganks from mobile heroes.
  • Sentry Ward — detect invisible threats like Techies mines, which Bane actually performs well against (63.6 % win rate).
  • Clarity — mana upkeep for frequent Nightmare casts.

Core Items

  • Arcane Boots — provides the mana pool needed for frequent Fiend’s Grip and Nightmare usage.
  • Aghanim’s Shard — upgrades Nightmare to spread to allies when attacked, increasing team utility against heroes that dive.
  • Glimmer Cape — defensive tool against burst damage from Skywrath Mage and Mars; also enables safe repositioning for Fiend’s Grip.
  • Force Staff — helps you escape from Primal Beast or reposition enemies into your grip.

Situational Items

  • Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — additional disable and self‑save against aggressive initiators.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects targeted spells from Skywrath Mage or Beastmaster, improving survivability.
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Fiend’s Grip to affect multiple enemies, useful against team fights with many squishy cores.
  • Guardian Greaves — strong against line‑up heavy teams (e.g., Axe, Earthshaker) where you need burst heal and armor.
  • Black King Bar — only pick when you’re forced to stay in the middle of fights against heavy magic damage (e.g., Skywrath Mage).

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑using Nightmare on heroes with strong escape tools (e.g., Monkey King) instead of saving it for high‑value targets.
  • Neglecting Enfeeble on the primary initiator, allowing enemies to maintain high damage output and cast range.
  • Casting Fiend’s Grip without vision, leading to wasted channel time against invisible or heavily warded opponents.
  • Itemizing too aggressively (e.g., buying high‑damage items early) and losing the supportive mana/utility role Bane excels at.

FAQ

Is Bane good in the current patch?

Bane sits at a 49.9 % win rate on patch 7.41, making him slightly below average but still viable, especially in coordinated lineups that can capitalize on his long‑duration disables.

What lane does Bane play?

Bane is typically played as a support in the safe lane (with a core) or as a roaming support in the off‑lane, using Nightmare and Enfeeble to control aggressive melee heroes.

Who counters Bane?

Heroes with high mobility and burst spell damage—Monkey King (35 % win rate vs Bane), Primal Beast (44.4 %), Skywrath Mage (45.1 %), and Mars (45.1 %)—are the toughest matchups and can out‑maneuver or out‑damage Bane if you fail to secure vision and proper positioning.
bane.counterHtml:

The key to beating him is to deny those channels, force early aggression, and exploit his long‑cast, low‑mobility spells.

Why These Heroes Beat Bane

Monkey King

Monkey King’s Boundless Strike and Jingu Mastery let him burst Bane before Fiend’s Grip lands, while his Wukong’s Command creates a safe zone that blocks Nightmare’s directional pull. Tip: initiate with Boundless Strike as soon as Bane begins channeling Fiend’s Grip; the stun interrupts the channel and forces him to retreat.

Primal Beast

Primal Beast’s Onslaught provides a gap‑closer that can dodge Nightmare and close distance instantly, and his Trample shreds Enfeeble’s damage reduction. Tip: time Onslaught to intersect Bane’s Nightmare direction—if you’re pulled into a wall, the charge will break the pull and let you counter‑engage.

Skywrath Mage

Skywrath Mage’s Arcane Bolt and Mystic Flare deal massive magic burst that outpaces Bane’s mana‑draining Fiend’s Grip, while Concussive Shot silences Bane, preventing him from casting Nightmare. Tip: land a quick Arcane Bolt + Mystic Flare combo right after Bane starts Fiend’s Grip; the burst often kills him before the channel finishes.

Mars

Mars’s Spear of Mars can lock Bane in the arena, denying him the space to reposition Nightmare, and his God’s Rebuke provides a reliable stun that interrupts Fiend’s Grip. Tip: spear Bane into the arena, then immediately follow with God’s Rebuke to cancel his channel and force a fight on your terms.

Beastmaster

Beastmaster’s Wild Axes and Primal Roar give him ranged damage and a stun that can break Nightmare’s pull and Fiend’s Grip channel. Tip: use Wild Axes to harass Bane from a safe distance; once he attempts Nightmare, activate Primal Roar to stun and punish his low mobility.

Drafting Against Bane

  • Prioritize heroes with hard disables (stuns, silences) that can interrupt Fiend’s Grip.
  • Pick mobile heroes that can dodge Nightmare’s directional pull or outrun Enfeeble’s damage.
  • Include burst magic damage heroes to out‑mana Bane’s low mana pool.
  • Consider early‑game aggression heroes to force Bane into a defensive lane.

Laning Against Bane

  • Trade when Bane’s Nightmare is on cooldown (≈ 30 s after a cast).
  • Harass with ranged attacks or spells while staying out of his Enfeeble radius.
  • Force Bane to use Brain Sap on creeps; this wastes his healing and leaves him vulnerable.
  • Punish his channel start with a stun or silence to cancel Fiend’s Grip.

Itemizing Against Bane

Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — provides a self‑or‑ally cyclone to break Nightmare pulls and Fiend’s Grip channels.
Black King Bar — grants spell immunity, nullifying Enfeeble, Nightmare, and Fiend’s Grip during fights.
Manta Style — creates illusion copies that split Nightmare’s pull and can purge Enfeeble’s damage reduction.
Aghanim’s Shard (for heroes with burst spells) — adds extra magic burst to outdamage Bane’s mana drain.

batrider.name: Batrider
batrider.guideHtml:
Batrider remains a high‑impact initiator and escape specialist in the current meta, sitting at a 42.9% win rate across 52,821 recent ranked matches on patch 7.41【OpenDota July 2026】. While his pick‑rate is modest, his ability to create game‑changing lasso combos keeps him relevant in coordinated play and solo queue alike.

How to Play Batrider

Laning Phase

  • Use Sticky Napalm on the creep wave to boost your attack damage and apply the slow, making it easier to pull the enemy off‑lane with a quick Flaming Lasso.
  • Pair Flamebreak with Sticky Napalm on the enemy hero; the knock‑back disrupts aggressive supports and the lingering damage benefits from the napalm damage amplification.
  • Prioritize a Firefly‑enabled early rotation to a nearby lane if you are being heavily harassed; the speed boost and tree‑destruction can open a safe escape route.
  • Against lane opponents with strong disables (e.g., Oracle, Bane), keep Flaming Lasso on cooldown for a defensive pull, then use Flamebreak to create distance.
  • Stack neutral camps with Sticky Napalm + Firefly to secure extra gold and deny enemy junglers early on.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 12 (Flaming Lasso + Firefly + Flamebreak) – start looking for pick‑offs in the mid lane or jungle.
  • Use Firefly to traverse the map quickly; target high‑value heroes (e.g., Magnus, Beastmaster) who are vulnerable to your lasso combo.
  • Coordinate with your team’s AoE ultimates (e.g., Magnus’ Reverse Polarity) – your Flaming Lasso provides perfect positioning for follow‑up spells.
  • Prioritize vision around Roshan and the enemy jungle; a well‑timed Flamebreak can force enemy supports out of the area, opening a solo pick.

Late Game

  • Win condition: isolate a key enemy carry with Flaming Lasso, then follow up with Flamebreak and team AoE damage to secure a quick kill.
  • Positioning: stay just out of enemy vision while on Firefly, using the speed boost to flank and avoid being caught by hard counters like Oracle or Templar Assassin.
  • Losing the game often comes from getting caught without Firefly (e.g., after a failed lasso) and being burst down by heroes with strong disables or silences.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane while you focus on napalm‑enhanced harass.
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery after early skirmishes.
  • Observer Ward — early vision to protect against ganks from Oracle or Bane.
  • Enchanted Mango — instant mana for early Flamebreak usage.
  • Iron Branch x2 — cheap stat boost and can be later used for a Magic Wand.

Core Items

  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Flaming Lasso to pull multiple enemies, crucial against team fights.
  • Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — provides additional disable, mana, and a safety escape if your Firefly is on cooldown.
  • Blink Dagger — shortens the gap to initiate lasso combos and synergizes with Firefly for unpredictable angles.
  • Force Staff — extra mobility to reposition allies or escape when a lasso is broken by a blink.

Situational Items

  • Black King Bar — when facing heavy magical burst from Oracle, Bane, or Templar Assassin.
  • Shiva’s Guard — armor and aura against physical carries; the slow also aids napalm damage.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects targeted disables (Oracle’s Fate’s Edict, Bane’s Nightmare).
  • Octarine Core — reduces cooldowns on all abilities, especially valuable for frequent Flamebreak and Firefly usage.
  • Glimmer Cape — defensive tool against burst from Chen or Magnus.

Common Mistakes

  • Wasting Flaming Lasso on low‑value targets – focus on high‑impact heroes; pulling a support rarely changes the outcome.
  • Using Firefly without a clear escape plan – you become vulnerable if the lasso is broken and you’re caught in enemy vision.
  • Neglecting vision – Batrider’s mobility is useless without map control; lack of wards leads to frequent ganks from Oracle and Bane.
  • Over‑relying on napalm damage – remember napalm only amplifies damage; you still need proper positioning and follow‑up damage from teammates.

FAQ

Is Batrider good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 42.9% win rate across over 52 k recent ranked games, Batrider is a solid pick, especially in coordinated play where his lasso combos can swing team fights.

What lane does Batrider play?

Batrider is typically played in the safe lane (radiant / dire off‑lane) as a solo initiator, using his early Sticky Napalm and Flamebreak to harass and control the lane.

Who counters Batrider?

The toughest matchups are Oracle (36.6% win rate), Naga Siren (41.1%), Bane (43.1%), Chen (45.0%), Templar Assassin (45.1%) and Marci (45.6%). These heroes either dispel or break the lasso, or have strong disables that punish Batrider’s aggressive play.
batrider.counterHtml:
Batrider is a mobile, burst‑damage hero whose strength comes from Flaming Lasso—a hard‑crowd‑control that drags an enemy into his fire‑laden wake. The quickest way to neutralize him is to pick heroes that can either break the lasso, out‑range his fire, or punish his low early‑game health pool.

Why These Heroes Beat Batrider

Oracle

Oracle’s False Promise lets him delay damage from Flaming Lasso and Sticky Napalm, while Fate’s Edict grants magic immunity that blocks the lasso’s pull and the fire damage from Firefly. Tip: Cast Fate’s Edict just before Batrider initiates; the lasso will snap, and you can follow up with a Purifying Flames purge.

Naga Siren

Naga’s Mirror Image creates untargetable copies that Batrider’s lasso can’t latch onto, and Ensnare roots him when he tries to chase the real hero. Tip: Position the real Naga near a tree line; when Batrider flies in, the copies absorb the lasso and you can quickly turn his own fire against him.

Bane

Bane’s Nightmare provides a reliable spell‑interrupt that breaks Flaming Lasso, and Fiend’s Grip silences Batrider, preventing him from re‑activating Sticky Napalm or Flamebreak. Tip: Use Nightmare the moment you see Batrider lift off; the lasso will break and you can follow with Fiend’s Grip for a guaranteed kill.

Chen

Chen’s Penitence slows Batrider’s flight speed, making it easier to land a Holy Persuasion on a neutral creep that can block the lasso’s path. His Hand of God heals the team through the fire damage. Tip: Pull a neutral creep into Batrider’s line of fire; the creep will absorb the lasso and die, denying the pull while you heal up.

Templar Assassin

Templar’s Refraction gives a shield that absorbs the burst from Sticky Napalm and Flamebreak, and her Psi Blades provide burst damage that can kill Batrider before he finishes a lasso drag. Tip: Stack Refraction before Batrider engages; when he lassoes you, the shield will soak the initial damage and you can retaliate with a quick Psi Blade combo.

Drafting Against Batrider

  • Prioritize heroes with spell‑interrupts (e.g., Bane, Silencer) to break Flaming Lasso.
  • Pick high‑mobility or blink‑based heroes that can dodge Firefly’s trail (e.g., Anti‑Mage, Storm Spirit).
  • Include strong early‑game sustain (e.g., Oracle, Witch Doctor) to survive his low‑HP start.
  • Ban or avoid heroes that synergize with Batrider’s fire (e.g., Ember Spirit, Dragon Knight).

Laning Against Batrider

  • Harass him before he gets Flamebreak; his early health is low.
  • Keep distance when he casts Sticky Napalm—the damage scales with each stack.
  • Use tower range to force him to use Flamebreak defensively, wasting its cooldown.
  • When he attempts Firefly, stay behind trees or in fog of war to break line of sight and force him to land.

Itemizing Against Batrider

Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — provides a reliable way to cyclone Batrider, breaking Flaming Lasso and interrupting Firefly.

Ghost Scepter — makes you ethereal, nullifying the damage from Sticky Napalm and Smoldering Resin while you wait for the lasso to snap.

Lotus Orb — reflects Flaming Lasso and Flamebreak back at Batrider, turning his own control against him.

Heaven’s Halberd — disarms Batrider, preventing his auto‑attack‑based Smoldering Resin and reducing his overall damage output.

beastmaster.name: Beastmaster
beastmaster.guideHtml:
Beastmaster is a durable initiator and disabler who excels at controlling team fights with his summons and crowd‑control ult. In the current 7.41 meta his win rate sits at 44.2% over 115 k recent ranked games, placing him below the hero average but still viable in coordinated play. He shines when he can secure vision and lock down high‑damage cores, but struggles against mobile, burst‑heavy heroes.

How to Play Beastmaster

Laning Phase

  • Use Wild Axes on the enemy off‑lane hero or creeps to harass and pull creep aggro; the axe’s damage amplification helps your Boar and Raptors trade better.
  • Pull the Boar with its passive poison to zone opponents and secure early lane equilibrium; the Boar’s slow makes enemy ganks easier to avoid.
  • Drop Raptors on the enemy hero when they step into melee range; the root and damage are especially effective against low‑mobility matchups like Vengeful Spirit or Clockwerk.
  • Stack the Inner Beast passive by attacking with both yourself and your summons to gain attack‑speed spikes for last‑hitting and early tower pressure.
  • Keep an eye on the enemy’s positioning: against mobile heroes such as Batrider or Slark, stay behind your Boar and use Wild Axes from a safe distance to avoid being caught by their burst.

Mid Game

  • Primal Roar becomes a decisive pick‑off tool once you have a few levels of Aghanim’s Shard (adds extra damage) – aim for squishy cores who lack blink.
  • Push lanes with Raptors and Boar while placing deep wards; the summons provide constant pressure and vision, forcing the enemy to spend resources on detection.
  • Group with your team for 4‑v‑4 fights; the combination of Drums of Slom healing and Primal Roar stun creates a strong front line that can soak damage and disrupt enemy positioning.
  • Prioritize taking Roshan after you have a solid Raptor‑Boar combo and a reliable Primal Roar cooldown, as the Aegis gives you a second life to continue initiating.

Late Game

  • Win condition: lock down the enemy carry with Primal Roar while your Raptors and Boar apply continuous damage; the healing from Drums of Slom lets you stay in the fight longer.
  • Position near your summons and the frontline; over‑extending without a Raptor or Boar nearby makes you vulnerable to burst heroes like Juggernaut or Pugna.
  • Lose the game if you fail to secure vision and your Primal Roar is on long cooldown, allowing enemy mobility heroes (Batrider, Slark) to pick off your backline.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane, especially against aggressive off‑laners.
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery after early skirmishes.
  • Iron Branch x2 — cheap stats and can be later used for a Magic Wand.
  • Observer Ward — early vision to protect against ganks and to start stacking neutral camps.

Core Items

  • Boots of Speed → Phase Boots — provides the burst movement needed to land Primal Roar and chase down heroes.
  • Drum of Endurance — upgrades to Drums of Slom (via Aghanim’s Shard) for the heal on each attack and extra damage.
  • Aghanim’s Shard — adds extra damage to Primal Roar and reduces its cooldown, turning Beastmaster into a more reliable pick‑off.
  • Mekansm — synergizes with the heal from Drums of Slom, giving team‑wide sustain in fights.

Situational Items

  • Vanguard — against burst heroes like Juggernaut or Pugna; mitigates early damage.
  • Solar Crest — amplifies damage on a chosen ally (often the carry) and provides armor against physical threats.
  • Pipe of Insight — counters magic burst from heroes such as Grimstroke and Pugna.
  • Black King Bar — necessary when facing heavy disables or magical burst (e.g., Grimstroke, Pugna).
  • Heart of Tarrasque — for games that go long and you need to stay durable in front‑line fights.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target disables, useful against Batrider’s Flamebreak or Slark’s Shadow Dance.

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑extending without summons – diving in without a Boar or Raptors leaves you easy prey for mobile heroes.
  • Neglecting vision – Beastmaster’s strength is map control; forgetting wards lets enemies pick off your summons.
  • Saving Primal Roar for late fights – using it early on a low‑value target wastes a key stun that could secure a high‑impact pick‑off.
  • Ignoring the Drum heal – failing to position near allies when attacking means you miss out on the substantial self‑heal from Drums of Slom.

FAQ

Is Beastmaster good in the current patch?

Beastmaster sits at a 44.2% win rate on 7.41, which is below the overall hero average but still viable in coordinated teams. His strength lies in vision control and reliable crowd control, though he struggles against highly mobile or bursty heroes.

What lane does Beastmaster play?

He is typically played in the safe lane (position 1) with a support, allowing him to farm his Boar and Raptors while providing early harassment with Wild Axes. The lane also gives him space to stack camps for later mid‑game pressure.

Who counters Beastmaster?

The toughest matchups are against Batrider, Slark, Juggernaut, Pugna, Grimstroke, and Dazzle, where his win rates hover around 40 %. These heroes either out‑maneuver his initiations or burst him before he can land Primal Roar. Vision denial and early aggressive pressure are key to mitigating their impact.
beastmaster.counterHtml:
Beastmaster’s threat comes from his persistent lane pressure, global presence with summons, and the burst crowd‑control of Primal Roar. The key to shutting him down is denying his summons and exploiting his reliance on melee attacks and low mobility.

Why These Heroes Beat Beastmaster

Batrider

Batrider’s Firefly and Flamebreak give him constant movement speed and a damage‑over‑time aura that punishes Beastmaster’s melee‑focused attacks and the Boar’s poison. Tip: Keep a Firefly‑up hero near the lane; the speed boost lets you dodge axes and chase down the Boar before it can lock you down.

Slark

Slark’s Dark Pact instantly removes the Boar’s poison and any lingering slows from Primal Roar, while Pounce can lock Beastmaster in place, preventing him from repositioning his summons. Slark’s Essence Shift scales with the damage Beastmaster deals, turning the Beastmaster’s own aggression against him.
Tip: Play aggressively after a successful Pounce; the brief window before Beastmaster can cast Primal Roar lets you burst him down.

Juggernaut

Juggernaut’s Blade Fury provides magic immunity that blocks the damage from Wild Axes and the Boar’s poison, and Healing Ward out‑heals the modest sustain from Drums of Slom. The Omnislash burst can instantly eliminate the Boar and Raptors, removing Beastmaster’s primary sources of damage.
Tip: Time Blade Fury to coincide with Beastmaster’s axe throw; the immunity also prevents the axe’s damage amplification on you and your allies.

Pugna

Pugna’s Nether Blast deals massive pure damage to the Boar and Raptors, while Decrepify amplifies incoming magical damage, making Beastmaster’s Wild Axes and Primal Roar far more lethal. Life Drain sustains you through the modest heal from Drums of Slom and can out‑heal Beastmaster’s passive regeneration.
Tip: Use Decrepify on Beastmaster before he initiates with Primal Roar; the stun will still land, but the amplified damage will often finish him.

Grimstroke

Grimstroke’s Dark Artistry silences Beastmaster, preventing the use of Primal Roar and Drums of Slom during the stun. Ink Swell provides a shield that blocks the first axe hit, and the Soul Bind tether can pull Beastmaster away from his summons, isolating him.
Tip: Land Dark Artistry right after Beastmaster’s first axe lands; the silence forces him to waste his stun and gives you a clean window to trade.

Drafting Against Beastmaster

  • Prioritize heroes with mobility (e.g., Batrider, Slark) to dodge axes and close the distance on summons.
  • Pick magic‑immune or damage‑shield heroes (Juggernaut, Grimstroke) to nullify Wild Axes and Drums of Slom.
  • Include strong single‑target burst (Pugna, Slark) to eliminate the Boar and Raptors quickly.
  • Consider silence or purge abilities to stop Primal Roar and the Boar’s poison.

Laning Against Beastmaster

  • Trade when his Wild Axes are on cooldown; his damage spikes are then much lower.
  • Harass the Boar early; killing it removes the poison aura and the extra damage amplification on your attacks.
  • Force Beastmaster to use Primal Roar defensively; the stun and slow give you a window to disengage or counter‑engage.
  • Push the lane after a successful Razorback or Raptor death; Beastmaster’s lane presence drops dramatically without his summons.

Itemizing Against Beastmaster

Manta Style — dispels the Boar’s poison and the slow from Primal Roar, while the split images can dodge axes.
Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — a reliable way to interrupt Primal Roar and give you time to reposition or kill summons.
Ghost Scepter — makes you untargetable by the Boar’s melee attacks and Wild Axes, forcing Beastmaster to rely on his limited ranged damage.
Black King Bar — provides full magic immunity, nullifying Wild Axes, Drums of Slom, and the damage amplification from Grimstroke’s Ink Swell.

bloodseeker.name: Bloodseeker
bloodseeker.guideHtml:
Bloodseeker is a high‑damage, mobility‑focused hero who thrives on hunting low‑health enemies. In patch 7.41 he is still a viable carry/disabler with a 52.0 % win rate across 147 k recent ranked games, placing him slightly above average. His toolkit—Thirst, Blood Rite, Bloodrage, and Rupture—makes him deadly in both early skirmishes and late‑game team fights when he can lock down fleeing heroes.

How to Play Bloodseeker

Laning Phase

  • Use Thirst to scout low‑HP enemy heroes; the movement‑speed bonus lets you dodge harass and set up early ganks.
  • Cast Blood Rite on enemy pull‑or‑push abilities (e.g., Rubick’s Telekinesis) to silence and damage them before they can react.
  • Trade with Bloodrage when you have lane control—accept the small HP loss for a massive attack‑speed boost and extra spell damage.
  • Prioritize a Rupture on high‑mobility heroes (e.g., Spirit Breaker) to punish any attempt to close the gap.
  • Against lane‑dominant heroes (Rubick, Disruptor) play conservatively, focusing on last‑hits and using Thirst vision to avoid surprise disables.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 6: Rupture + Blood Rite combo can instantly shut down enemy initiators.
  • Roam with Thirst vision; look for wounded heroes in the river or jungle and initiate with Bloodrage → Rupture → Blood Rite.
  • Secure objectives (Roshan, tier‑2 towers) when the enemy’s core damage dealers are low enough for Thirst to grant you chase speed.
  • Group with your team for early‑mid fights; a well‑timed Blood Rite silences multiple spellcasters, allowing your cores to focus.

Late Game

  • Win condition: isolate and Rupture the enemy carry or mid‑lane hero, then chase them down with Thirst‑granted speed and finish with Bloodrage‑enhanced attacks.
  • Position near the front of your team to land Blood Rite on clustered enemies; avoid being caught in enemy silences or disables that nullify your chase.
  • Losing the game usually comes from being caught out by strong counters (Rubick, Disruptor) who can silence you before you land Rupture, or from lacking vision so Thirst cannot trigger.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango + Healing Salve — sustain against early harassment.
  • Stout Shield — mitigates harass from ranged heroes.
  • Observer Ward — grants vision for Thirst to spot low‑HP enemies.

Core Items

  • Phase Boots — adds burst movement for chasing and synergizes with Thirst.
  • Mask of Madness — amplifies attack speed and damage, complementing Bloodrage’s bonus.
  • Black King Bar — essential against heavy magic damage and silences (Rubick, Disruptor).
  • Abyssal Blade — provides a reliable stun to lock down targets before Rupture.

Situational Items

  • Sange and Yasha — extra movement speed and status resistance for chasing.
  • Manta Style — dispels silences and creates confusion against heroes like Disruptor.
  • Heart of Tarrasque — survivability when you’re forced to stay in fights longer.
  • Linken’s Sphere – blocks single‑target disables (e.g., Rubick’s Spell Steal).
  • Radiance – adds consistent damage during team fights, making Rupture even more punishing.

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑using Bloodrage without accounting for the health‑per‑second loss, leading to early deaths.
  • Casting Blood Rite without checking enemy positioning; the 2.9‑second channel can be interrupted or wasted.
  • Failing to leverage Thirst for map awareness, missing opportunities to chase low‑HP heroes.
  • Rupturing tanky heroes who can afford the movement damage, instead of focusing on squishy carries.

FAQ

Is Bloodseeker good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 52.0 % win rate on 147 k recent ranked matches, Bloodseeker is a slightly above‑average pick in 7.41, especially effective when you can capitalize on his Thirst‑based chase potential.

What lane does Bloodseeker play?

Bloodseeker is most commonly played in the safe lane as a carry, but he can also function in the mid lane if you need a high‑damage initiator and have a reliable lane partner to protect him from early disables.

Who counters Bloodseeker?

The toughest matchups right now are Rubick (27 % win rate), Disruptor (32.4 %), and Spirit Breaker (33.3 %). These heroes can silence or lock you down before you land Rupture, nullifying your chase and burst potential.
bloodseeker.counterHtml:
