The key to shutting him down is to deny him safe movement, silence or burst him before his rupture can be applied, and keep his health high enough that Thirst offers little speed.

Why These Heroes Beat Bloodseeker

Rubick

Rubick can Spell‑Steal Bloodseeker’s Rupture and Blood Rite, turning Bloodseeker’s own tools against him and silencing him for long windows. A well‑timed Telekinesis can also pull Bloodseeker out of his own Rupture zone. Tip: Prioritize stealing Rupture early; a single Rupture on Bloodseeker forces him to stay immobile and makes him an easy target for your team.

Disruptor

Disruptor’s Glimpse constantly resets Bloodseeker’s positioning, negating the chase advantage from Thirst and pulling him back into your team’s kill zone. Static Storm silences Bloodseeker, preventing Blood Rage activation and the damage from Blood Rite. Tip: Pair Glimpse with a stun or burst damage after you pull him back to guarantee a kill.

Spirit Breaker

Spirit Breaker’s Charge of Darkness and Nether Strike give him unstoppable global presence, allowing him to close the distance before Bloodseeker can activate Thirst. His Greater Bash interrupts Blood Rage and Rupture, and the constant pressure forces Bloodseeker to play overly defensive. Tip: Initiate with Charge, then follow up with a stun to lock Bloodseeker down before he can Rupture.

Shadow Fiend

Shadow Fiend’s Shadowrazes and Requiem of Souls provide massive burst damage that can kill Bloodseeker before he can apply Rupture. His Presence of the Dark Lord armor reduction amplifies physical hits, making Bloodseeker’s Blood Rage attacks less effective. Tip: Harass early with Shadowrazes to keep Bloodseeker’s health high, then finish with a well‑timed Requiem when he attempts to engage.

Pangolier

Pangolier’s Swashbuckle grants high mobility and burst that can dodge Rupture damage while dealing lethal damage. Shield Crash silences Bloodseeker, preventing Blood Rite and Blood Rage, and the Roll ultimate makes him untargetable, nullifying Rupture’s damage over movement. Tip: Use Roll to dodge Rupture, then follow up with Swashbuckle when Bloodseeker is forced to stay still by your silence.

Drafting Against Bloodseeker

  • Prioritize heroes with hard disables (stuns, silences) that can interrupt Blood Rage and Rupture.
  • Pick high‑mobility or global‑presence heroes that can close the distance faster than Thirst grants.
  • Include burst damage sources that can kill Bloodseeker before he lands Rupture.
  • Avoid pure right‑click carries without escape tools; they are vulnerable to Rupture’s damage.

Laning Against Bloodseeker

  • Harass him early to keep his health above the Thirst trigger (≥ 50 %); he loses speed and aggression.
  • Use silence or stun on his Blood Rite cast to deny the area damage and silence.
  • Trade when his Blood Rage is on cooldown; his attack speed boost is gone, making him vulnerable.
  • Position near creep wave or allied towers to limit his movement—any forced movement under Rupture will damage him heavily.

Itemizing Against Bloodseeker

Eul's Scepter of Divinity — silences and lifts Bloodseeker, breaking his Rupture channel and buying time for your team.
Ghost Scepter — makes you ethereal, so Rupture’s movement‑based damage does not apply while you kite.
Force Staff — instantly removes you from Rupture’s radius, nullifying the damage from forced movement.
Heaven's Halberd — disarms Bloodseeker, preventing the amplified attacks from Blood Rage and reducing his burst potential.

bounty-hunter.name: Bounty Hunter
bounty-hunter.guideHtml:
Bounty Hunter is a high‑mobility, vision‑centric hero whose kit excels at hunting down high‑value targets and creating space for his team. On patch 7.41 his overall pub win rate sits at 51.6% across nearly 180 k ranked games, making him a solid but not dominant pick, especially in the current escape‑focused meta.

How to Play Bounty Hunter

Laning Phase

  • Track early on to grant true sight on enemy supports and reveal invisible pulls or smokes; prioritize heroes with low mobility (e.g., Dragon Knight) where the extra vision translates directly into kills.
  • Use Shuriken Toss to harass and apply the slow, then bounce to any already‑tracked enemy to amplify damage and force them to retreat.
  • Jinada should be timed on the first successful hit after a successful Track; the bonus damage and gold steal swing lane equilibrium in your favor.
  • When the enemy roams or attempts a gank, drop Friendly Shadow on a teammate to give them instant invisibility and a 0.5 s fade, allowing safe disengage or counter‑gank.
  • Against hard‑lane matchups like Ember Spirit or Tusk, play conservatively, rely on Shadow Walk to dodge their burst and only engage when you have a Track on the enemy.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 6: Shadow Walk gives you the ability to initiate ganks with a stun on the first attack; coordinate with allies to capitalize on the stun.
  • Prioritize big‑game targets (top‑3 net‑worth enemies) and apply Track before a team fight; the extra damage and gold bounty from Big Game Hunter can swing the economy.
  • Roam aggressively once you have Shuriken Toss upgraded (level 12) – the bounce range of 1200 units lets you hit multiple tracked heroes in a clustered fight.
  • Keep an eye on enemy vision; use Shadow Walk to scout high‑ground or jungle camps, then drop Friendly Shadow on a teammate to secure a safe pick‑off.

Late Game

  • Win condition: Secure the enemy’s core heroes with Track and Shadow Walk‑initiated stuns; the gold from Big Game Hunter plus the kill gold often outpaces the enemy’s net‑worth.
  • Position near the backline but stay within 1200 units of a tracked target so Shuriken Toss can bounce; avoid clustering where enemy AoE (e.g., Tiny, Puck) can punish you.
  • Losing the game usually stems from over‑extending without a Track or getting caught by invisibility‑breakers (e.g., Ember Spirit, Chen) that negate your primary advantage.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane, especially against aggressive early heroes.
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery after trades.
  • Observer Ward — early vision to protect against ganks and to set up Track.
  • Quelling Blade — helps secure last hits when you’re forced to farm under pressure.

Core Items

  • Phase Boots — extra movement speed for chasing and the 30 % speed boost synergizes with Shadow Walk.
  • Shadow Blade — provides a second source of invisibility and a burst damage initiation, complementing the stun from Shadow Walk.
  • Aghanim’s Shard (optional) — upgrades Shuriken Toss to bounce to an additional target, increasing team‑fight impact.
  • Black King Bar — essential against heavy magic burst (e.g., Puck, Queen of Pain) to ensure you can land the stun and finish big‑game targets.

Situational Items

  • Manta Style — counters silences and dispels Track‑removing disables from heroes like Chen.
  • Eul’s Scepter — provides self‑save against burst (e.g., Ember Spirit) and can be used to set up a Track on a fleeing target.
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Shadow Walk to a longer duration and gives an extra stun on the first attack, great against tanky lineups.
  • Monkey King Bar — counters evasion from heroes such as Hoodwink and Timbersaw.
  • Glimmer Cape — additional invisibility for team‑fight positioning when enemy vision is high.

Common Mistakes

  • Casting Shadow Walk on yourself and then attacking immediately, forgetting the stun only applies to the first attack; many players waste the invisibility without the stun.
  • Neglecting Track on high‑net‑worth enemies; without it you lose the extra damage and gold from Big Game Hunter.
  • Over‑extending without vision, especially against heroes with strong invisibility counters (Ember Spirit, Chen).
  • Relying solely on Jinada for damage; Bounty Hunter’s true strength is map control and pick‑offs, not sustained lane damage.

FAQ

Is Bounty Hunter good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 51.6 % win rate across 178 k recent ranked games, Bounty Hunter is a reliable pick, especially in escape‑heavy lineups where his mobility and vision give a consistent advantage.

What lane does Bounty Hunter play?

Bounty Hunter is typically played in the safe lane (hard lane) as a support, using Track and Shadow Walk to protect the carry and set up early kills. He can also be flexed to the off‑lane if a team needs additional vision and pick‑off potential.

Who counters Bounty Hunter?

The toughest matchups right now are Ember Spirit, Chen, Hoodwink, Tusk, Windranger, and Tiny, all of which win ≤ 51.6 % of their games against him. Their burst, disables, or strong invisibility‑break mechanics neutralize Bounty Hunter’s core strengths.
bounty-hunter.counterHtml:
Bounty Hunter thrives on vision, surprise ganks, and the extra gold from tracking high‑value targets. The fastest way to neutralize him is to deny his invisibility + track combo and to force early, unavoidable fights where his burst and stun are ineffective.

Why These Heroes Beat Bounty Hunter

Ember Spirit

Ember’s Sleight of Hand grants him instant movement speed and a brief invisibility that outpaces Bounty Hunter’s Shadow Walk, letting him close the distance or escape before a stun lands. His Flame Guard also blocks the burst from Jinada and the shuriken bounce damage. Tip: Use Fire Remnant to jump behind Bounty Hunter after you spot his track, forcing him to waste Shadow Walk defensively.

Chen

Chen’s Holy Persuasion can pull a neutral creep onto Bounty Hunter, instantly breaking his invisibility and providing a cheap frontline that punishes Bounty Hunter’s low durability. The creep also blocks the shuriken bounce radius. Tip: Drop a creep near the lane’s edge and force Bounty Hunter to engage on a non‑hero target, then follow up with a Penitence‑enhanced attack.

Hoodwink

Hoodwink’s Acorn Shot and Bushwhack give her reliable crowd control that triggers before Bounty Hunter can land his stun, especially when she spots a tracked hero. Her Scurry provides a burst of movement that outruns Shadow Walk, allowing her to kite and avoid the initial attack. Tip: Place Bushwhack traps in common track zones; when Bounty Hunter steps on them his invisibility is broken and he is stunned.

Tusk

Tusk’s Ice Shards creates a wall that blocks the shuriken bounce chain and forces Bounty Hunter into a predictable path. Snowball can pull him out of Shadow Walk range and stun him before he can react. Tip: Initiate with Ice Shards on the lane’s edge, then Snowball the tracked Bounty Hunter into the wall for a guaranteed stun.

Windranger

Windranger’s Shackleshot provides a long‑range stun that can be cast on a tracked Bounty Hunter before he reaches attack range, nullifying his stun‑on‑break mechanic. Windrun gives her a speed boost and evasion that outruns Shadow Walk, letting her dodge the initial shuriken. Tip: Keep a Shackleshot charge ready whenever you see a track icon; a well‑timed cast forces Bounty Hunter to retreat without gold.

Drafting Against Bounty Hunter

  • Prioritize heroes with built‑in invisibility detection or true sight (e.g., Zeus, Slark, Brewmaster).
  • Choose heroes with strong early‑game burst or lockdown that can punish Shadow Walk before it lands.
  • Include at least one mobile hero that can outrun or out‑maneuver Bounty Hunter’s 1200 radius shuriken bounce.
  • Ban or avoid picking heroes that heavily rely on high net‑worth gold spikes (e.g., Storm Spirit) where Big Game Hunter becomes a threat.

Laning Against Bounty Hunter

  • Trade when his Track is on cooldown; his damage and gold vision are nullified.
  • Punish early ganks by staying grouped and using vision wards; a tracked Bounty Hunter loses the element of surprise.
  • Force him to use Shadow Walk defensively by initiating with a stun or a gap‑closer, then counter‑attack while his invisibility is on cooldown.
  • Harass him with ranged attacks or creeps when his Jinada cooldown is up, as the bonus damage is his primary kill threat.

Itemizing Against Bounty Hunter

Gem of True Sight — grants permanent true sight, nullifying Track and shuriken bounce vision.
Force Staff — lets you escape Shadow Walk’s stun range or reposition to avoid his burst.
Eul’s Scepter — cyclones Bounty Hunter, breaking his invisibility and delaying his stun.
Blink Dagger — provides instant gap‑close to dodge his stun or to initiate before he can react.

brewmaster.name: Brewmaster
brewmaster.guideHtml:
Brewmaster is a versatile initiator and durable front‑liner who excels at creating chaos with his Primal Split and disrupting teamfights with Thunder Clap and Cinder Brew. On patch 7.41 his overall pub win rate sits at 50.8% over 56,258 ranked games, making him a solid but not dominant pick in the current meta.

How to Play Brewmaster

Laning Phase

  • Use Thunder Clap on the wave to both damage and apply a strong attack‑speed slow, helping you and your lane partner win lane control.
  • Cinder Brew works as a ranged skillshot; aim the barrel through enemy creep blocks to harass the off‑lane hero and force them to miss last hits.
  • When you drop below 50 % health, Liquid Courage grants status‑resistance and a burst of movement speed—use it to escape ganks or to chase down low‑HP opponents.
  • Against hard‑counters like Bristleback and Rubick (Brewmaster win ≈ 31–41 % in those matchups), play defensively, prioritize stacking neutral camps for later split‑push, and avoid extended duels.
  • Pull the lane creep equilibrium toward your tower with Thunder Clap + Cinder Brew combos to force the enemy mid‑lane hero (often a ranged nuker) to overextend, setting up gank opportunities.

Mid Game

  • Power spike: hitting level 6 and acquiring Primal Split gives you three independent units, each with its own Thunder Clap/Cinder Brew‑style abilities; this dramatically increases teamfight presence.
  • Look for objective‑based rotations: split‑push a lane while the three elements apply pressure elsewhere, then collapse on Roshan or a vulnerable tower.
  • Prioritize vision around Roshan and high‑ground jungle; the three elements can scout safely while you stay behind with Liquid Courage for survivability.
  • When you have a Core item like Aghanim’s Scepter (enhances Primal Split duration) or Blink Dagger, initiate on squishy back‑line heroes—your split units can lock them down with overlapping slows.

Late Game

  • Win condition: force the enemy team to split its focus across the three elements; the side that survives re‑merges you, often turning a 2v2 into a 3v2.
  • Positioning: keep the primary Brewmaster near the front line to absorb focus fire, while the Earth and Storm elements flank or peel for you.
  • Game‑losing mistake: committing all three elements to a single target without backup; if the enemy disables or bursts one element, the remaining two die quickly, leaving you vulnerable.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango + Healing Salve — sustain against harassment in solo lane.
  • Quelling Blade — helps secure last hits when you’re forced to farm under tower.
  • Iron Branch x2 — cheap stat boost and later upgrade into a Magic Wand.

Core Items

  • Blink Dagger — primary initiation tool; combo with Primal Split to jump onto high‑value targets.
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — extends Primal Split duration and adds extra damage to each element, crucial for late‑game teamfights.
  • Vanguard — provides the durability needed to survive burst from heroes like Invoker and Puck (matchup win ≈ 42 %).

Situational Items

  • Black King Bar — mandatory against heavy magical burst lineups (e.g., Puck, Invoker).
  • Shiva’s Guard — adds armor and an AoE slow that synergizes with Thunder Clap against Bristleback.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target disables from Rubick and Beastmaster.
  • Pipe of Insight — mitigates magical damage from Phoenix and Skywrath Mage.
  • Mekansm or Guardian Greaves — boost team survivability when you’re the primary front‑liner.

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑committing the split units to a single target, leaving the primary Brewmaster exposed.
  • Neglecting vision around Roshan; enemies can easily ambush your split units.
  • Using Cinder Brew without accounting for its linear path, often missing the intended hero and wasting mana.
  • Relying on Liquid Courage too early; the buff only activates below 50 % health and can be a death trap if you dive without backup.

FAQ

Is Brewmaster good in the current patch?

Yes. Brewmaster sits at a 50.8% win rate on 56 k recent ranked matches, making him a viable pick, especially on teams that can capitalize on his split‑push and teamfight disruption.

What lane does Brewmaster play?

Brewmaster is most commonly played in the off‑lane (solo safe lane) where his durability and wave‑clear from Thunder Clap let him survive against aggressive mids and provide early tower pressure.

Who counters Brewmaster?

The toughest matchups are Bristleback, Rubick, Beastmaster, Invoker, Puck, and Phoenix, where Brewmaster’s win rates drop to 31.6–44.2 %. These heroes either out‑scale his early damage or can reliably disable his split units.
brewmaster.counterHtml:
Brewmaster’s strength lies in his chaotic split‑push and the sheer survivability of his three elemental clones. The key to shutting him down is to deny him the space to create his split, lock down his stuns, and burst the elements before they can regenerate his health.

Why These Heroes Beat Brewmaster

Bristleback

Bristleback’s Warpath and passive Bristleback give him massive damage reduction from the rear and a stacking damage bonus that outscales Brewmaster’s burst. Brewmaster’s Primal Split forces him into melee range where Bristleback’s Quill Spray repeatedly hits all three elements, quickly draining their health. Tip: Keep your back turned to force Brewmaster’s split to engage from the rear, maximizing Quill Spray’s damage.

Rubick

Rubick can Spell‑Steal Brewmaster’s Primal Split and Thunder Clap, instantly turning Brewmaster’s own crowd control against him. With Null Field he also reduces the magical damage Brewmaster’s elements deal. Tip: Prioritize stealing Primal Split early; the cloned elements die instantly, denying the rebirth.

Beastmaster

Beastmaster’s Primal Roar provides a long‑range stun that can lock down Brewmaster’s primary form before he splits, while his Call of the Wild summons high‑damage summons that quickly shred the three elements. Tip: Use Primal Roar to stun Brewmaster right after he casts Thunder Clap, then focus the summons on the split elements.

Invoker

Invoker’s Sun Strike and Chaos Meteor are pure damage spells that ignore Brewmaster’s armor and can be cast on the split elements simultaneously. Cold Snap adds extra stun uptime, preventing Brewmaster from re‑activating abilities while Brewmastered Up. Tip: Combo Cold Snap with Sun Strike on each element to burst them before they can heal.

Puck

Puck’s Illusory Orb and Dream Coil provide AoE damage and a reliable stun that can hit all three elements at once. Phase Shift lets Puck dodge Brewmaster’s Cinder Brew and Thunder Clap, while Waning Rift reduces Brewmaster’s magic resistance. Tip: Cast Dream Coil just after Brewmaster splits; the coil’s radius covers all three elements, forcing a quick kill.

Drafting Against Brewmaster

  • Prioritize heroes with reliable AoE stuns or silences (e.g., Lion, Shadow Shaman).
  • Pick burst magic damage heroes that can hit multiple targets instantly (Invoker, Puck).
  • Choose heroes with strong lane sustain or early aggression to deny Brewmaster farm (Bristleback, Beastmaster).
  • Consider banning heroes that provide strong split‑push or survivability (e.g., Tidehunter, Phoenix).

Laning Against Brewmaster

  • Trade when Brewmaster’s Thunder Clap is on cooldown; his damage and slow drop significantly.
  • Harass him early with ranged attacks; his Cinder Brew is a skill shot that can be easily avoided.
  • Punish his low health window before Liquid Courage activates (below 50%).
  • Force him to use Primal Split defensively by applying constant pressure and vision, reducing his split‑push potential.

Itemizing Against Brewmaster

Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — provides a reliable disable to interrupt Primal Split and can be used to cyclone Brewmaster before he splits.

Scythe of Vyse — hard‑locks Brewmaster and his elements, preventing any of their abilities from triggering.

Aghanim’s Scepter (Invoker) — upgrades Sun Strike to a global, instant‑cast spell that can finish split elements from anywhere.

Gleipnir — AoE root and damage that can hit all three elements simultaneously, shortening their lifespan.

bristleback.name: Bristleback
bristleback.guideHtml:
Bristleback is a tanky front‑liner who thrives on soaking damage, spitting quills, and turning fights into attrition wars. On patch 7.41 his overall win rate sits at 48.7% (308 k+ ranked games), making him a solid but not dominant pick in the current meta.

How to Play Bristleback

Laning Phase

  • Viscous Nasal Goo early on to apply armor‑slow on the enemy off‑lane; stack it on creep waves to harass and reduce their damage output.
  • Quill Spray on the first wave of creeps to secure lane equilibrium and start building damage‑per‑second; remember the damage bonus from recent hits (14 s window).
  • Use Bristleback passive to soak tower and hero hits from the side/rear; position yourself so most enemy attacks land on your back, triggering the passive damage reduction.
  • When the enemy laner is a high‑burst hero (e.g., Nyx Assassin), keep Hairball ready to burst them from a distance and apply Goo stacks before they can dive.
  • Prioritize a sentry ward if you suspect enemy support vision; Bristleback’s lack of early mobility makes him vulnerable to ganks.

Mid Game

  • Warpath spikes: each spell cast grants +% movement speed and damage; rotate spells (Goo → Hairball → Quill Spray) to stay at peak Warpath.
  • Aim for side‑rear engagements; let enemies focus you front‑on to waste their damage while your passive and Prickly amplify damage to heroes behind you.
  • Join split‑pushes with a Vanguard or Crimson Guard core; Bristleback can tank tower hits while his Quill Sprays chip towers and heroes.
  • Target enemy supports with Hairball followed by a quick Quill Spray combo to force them out of fights; the Goo stacks also make them easier to kill later.

Late Game

  • Win condition: out‑last the enemy front line while your Quill Sprays and Goo‑debuffed heroes crumble; force fights where you can stay on the back side of the enemy.
  • Position near high‑ground or cliffs to limit enemy flank routes; Bristleback’s rear armor reduction is less useful if you can’t turn.
  • Lose the game if you get caught out of position by burst heroes (Nyx, Terrorblade) or if you waste Warpath stacks on non‑damage spells; staying on the front without side‑rear protection makes you a death trap.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango + Healing Salve — sustain against harass.
  • Stout Shield — mitigates early creep damage and reduces harassment from ranged heroes.
  • Quelling Blade — helps secure last hits while you’re focused on positioning.
  • Observer Ward — vision to avoid early ganks.

Core Items

  • Vanguard — massive block and health pool; synergizes with Bristleback’s passive.
  • Crimson Guard — armor block against physical burst (Nyx, Terrorblade).
  • Boots of Travel — global presence for split‑pushing and joining fights.
  • Warrior Greaves — armor, movement speed, and HP regen; keeps you tanky and mobile for Warpath uptime.

Situational Items

  • Abyssal Blade — lock down high‑mobility heroes that can bypass your rear (e.g., Terrorblade).
  • Heart of Tarrasque — extreme survivability when you need to be the sole front‑liner.
  • Shiva’s Guard — extra armor and an AoE slow that complements Goo‑slow and Quill Spray.
  • Black King Bar — against heavy magical burst (Pugna, Keeper of the Light) when you must stay alive to spam Warpath.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects targeted disables; useful vs. Chen’s leash or Viper’s poison.

Common Mistakes

  • Facing the enemy front‑on – ignoring Bristleback’s side/rear damage reduction wastes his biggest defensive tool.
  • Spamming Quill Spray without Goo – failing to apply Viscous Nasal Goo reduces both armor‑slow and the damage amplification from recent hits.
  • Wasting Warpath on non‑damage spells – casting only Goo or Hairball without following up with Quill Spray drops the movement‑speed and damage bonus.
  • Over‑extending without vision – Bristleback’s low mobility makes him an easy target for ganks, especially from Nyx Assassin and Terrorblade.

FAQ

Is Bristleback good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 48.7 % win rate across over 300 k ranked games, Bristleback is a viable pick, especially on the safe lane where his durability and scaling damage shine.

What lane does Bristleback play?

Bristleback is most effective on the safe lane (hard lane) as a carry/durable, allowing him to farm while building the armor and health items that make his passive and Warpath most potent.

Who counters Bristleback?

The toughest matchups are Nyx Assassin (30.8 % win rate), Terrorblade (36.5 %), Chen (36.7 %), Viper (37.0 %), Keeper of the Light (37.7 %), and Batrider (38.1 %). These heroes either burst him before he can stack Warpath or bypass his rear‑side armor reduction.
bristleback.counterHtml:
Br​istleback’s massive health pool, damage‑reduction on his sides and rear, and the ever‑growing damage from Quill Spray make him a nightmare in prolonged fights. The key to shutting him down is to punish his low front‑line armor, force him into the front where his damage reduction is weakest, and deny the stack‑up of Quill Spray and Warpath buffs.

Why These Heroes Beat Bristleback

Nyx Assassin

Nyx’s Mana Burn instantly spikes Bristleback’s damage taken, and his Spiked Carapace reflects damage back when Bristleback tries to spam Quill Spray from the sides. Practical tip: open with a stun (Vendetta) from behind to catch Bristleback before he can turn his back for his damage reduction.

Terrorblade

Terrorblade’s Metamorphosis gives him pure ranged damage that ignores Bristleback’s side‑damage reduction, while Sunder can instantly flip Bristleback’s health advantage. Practical tip: push early with Metamorphosis and force Bristleback to fight front‑on, then follow up with a quick Reflection to punish his low front armor.

Chen

Chen’s Penitence reduces Bristleback’s armor dramatically, making his Quill Spray stacks far less threatening, and his Holy Persuasion can pull a neutral creep to harass Bristleback’s rear, denying the damage‑reduction zone. Practical tip: keep a neutral creep near Bristleback’s flank and use Penitence on him before engaging.

Viper

Viper’s Nethertoxin strips Bristleback’s Viscous Nasal Goo armor debuff and continuously reduces his armor, while Poison Attack applies a lingering damage over time that bypasses Bristleback’s side‑damage reduction. Practical tip: drop a Nethertoxin on the lane before Bristleback can stack Quill Spray, then harass with Poison Attack from the front.

Keeper of the Light

Keeper’s Mana Leak drains Bristleback’s mana, preventing him from spamming Quill Spray and Hairball, while Illuminate provides burst damage that hits through Bristleback’s side‑damage reduction. Practical tip: keep Keeper’s Blinding Light ready to block Bristleback’s Hairball when he tries to close the gap.

Drafting Against Bristleback

  • Prioritize heroes with strong front‑line armor penetration or pure damage (e.g., Viper, Terrorblade).
  • Pick disables that can lock Bristleback from his rear (stuns, silences, hexes).
  • Include early‑game burst damage to punish his low initial health.
  • Ban or avoid heroes that give Bristleback easy lane sustain or armor (e.g., heavy healers).

Laning Against Bristleback

  • Trade from the front where his damage reduction is minimal; avoid standing on his sides or rear.
  • Harass with armor‑reducing spells early to prevent Quill Spray stacks from becoming lethal.
  • Force him to use Hairball defensively; a well‑timed stun on its cast nullifies its damage.
  • Capitalize on his long cooldowns after a Quill Spray trigger—he’s vulnerable while the stacks reset.

Itemizing Against Bristleback

Assault Cuirass — shreds his armor and reduces the effectiveness of his Quill Spray stacks.
Heaven’s Halberd — disarms Bristleback, preventing him from delivering the melee damage that triggers his rear‑damage reduction.
Silver Edge — breaks his passive damage reduction and provides a burst of damage from the front.
Gleipnir – roots Bristleback in place, denying him the ability to reposition to his sides or rear for damage mitigation.

broodmother.name: Broodmother
broodmother.guideHtml:
Broodmother is a high‑mobility, split‑pushing specialist who excels at creating map pressure with webs and spiderlings. In patch 7.41 she sits at a 49.6 % win rate on ranked play (74 k+ games), making her a solid but not dominant pick. Her strength lies in lane dominance and late‑game siege, while certain spell‑heavy heroes still give her trouble.

How to Play Broodmother

Laning Phase

  • Spin Web early: cast the first web on the lane’s edge to gain the passive movement‑speed and turn‑rate boost; use the free movement to dodge harass and secure last‑hits.
  • Incapacitating Bite on enemy heroes or creeps: the slow and miss‑chance lets you trade safely and deny experience.
  • Spawn Spiderlings on the enemy hero when they step into your web: the damage + slow forces them to retreat, while the hatchlings add lane pressure.
  • Prioritize Spider’s Milk on neutral creeps in the jungle: the heal over time sustains you and your spiderlings, especially against harass from heroes like Shadow Demon.
  • Against hard‑lane opponents (e.g., Batrider, Shadow Demon), keep your web centered on the lane to limit their ability to land spells and use bite to mitigate their burst.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 6 – you now have all four abilities; start rotating to side lanes with a web placed near the river to create a safe tunnel for split‑pushing.
  • Map control: place webs in high‑traffic areas (Roshan pit, jungle entrances) to grant vision and fast travel for you and your team.
  • Teamfight positioning: stay behind your webs, use Bite to cripple initiators, and let spiderlings soak damage; avoid direct fights with heroes that have strong disables (Batrider, Warlock).
  • Objective focus: push towers behind your web line while the enemy is forced to respond elsewhere; the heal from Spider’s Milk lets you sustain prolonged sieges.

Late Game

  • Win condition: dominate the map with multiple webs, forcing the enemy to split and defend; a single well‑placed web can let you slip into the enemy base and take the Ancient.
  • Positioning: keep a web within 600 units of you at all times; losing web coverage makes you vulnerable to burst from heroes like Dark Willow or Jakiro.
  • What loses the game: getting caught out of web range and killed by disables, or over‑extending without spiderlings to absorb damage.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — basic sustain for early lane harassment.
  • Healing Salve — emergency HP for burst from Batrider or Shadow Demon.
  • Quelling Blade — helps secure creep last‑hits while you’re on webs.
  • Observer Ward — vision to protect your web line from ganks.

Core Items

  • Power Treads — attack speed for spiderlings and flexible stat switching.
  • Echo Sabre — extra burst on Bite and Spiderlings, plus mana sustain.
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Spawn Spiderlings to a global spawn, letting you reinforce any lane instantly.
  • Black King Bar — essential against heavy magical disables (Warlock, Dark Willow, Jakiro).

Situational Items

  • Manta Style — dispels silences and gives extra movement speed for web hopping.
  • Linken’s Sphere — blocks single‑target disables from Batrider or Shadow Demon.
  • Satanic — massive survivability when you’re deep in enemy territory.
  • Heart of Tarrasque — raw HP pool for late‑game sieges against burst heroes.
  • Scythe of Vyse — extra control when you need to lock down elusive heroes like Morphling.

Common Mistakes

  • Neglecting webs – dropping webs too far from you removes the movement‑speed buff and makes you an easy target.
  • Over‑extending without spiderlings – attacking towers without a healthy spiderling army leads to quick deaths against heroes with burst.
  • Ignoring Spider’s Milk – failing to kill neutral creeps wastes a reliable heal that can keep you alive in fights.
  • Chasing teamfights – Broodmother shines in split‑push; joining full‑team engagements without BKB often results in being locked down by disables.

FAQ

Is Broodmother good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 49.6 % win rate on recent ranked matches, she is a viable pick, especially on maps with many jungle paths where her webs give superior map control.

What lane does Broodmother play?

Broodmother is typically played in the safe lane (radiant bottom or dire top) as a carry/pusher, using Spin Web to dominate the lane and transition into split‑push.

Who counters Broodmother?

Heroes with strong disables and burst—Batrider (37 % win vs. BM), Shadow Demon (39 %), Dark Willow (40.9 %), Jakiro (41.8 %), and Warlock (41.9 %)—are the toughest matchups according to recent OpenDota data. Building BKB and keeping webs active are the primary ways to mitigate their impact.
broodmother.counterHtml:
Broodmother thrives on map control through her webs and relentless spiderlings, turning any lane into a choke point that forces opponents to fight on her terms. The key to shutting her down is denying safe web space, bursting her early health pool, and applying consistent pressure that prevents her from snowballing spiderlings.

Why These Heroes Beat Broodmother

Batrider

Batrider’s Flamebreak instantly destroys Broodmother’s webs and silences her, cutting off her mobility and the safety net for her spiderlings. Pair Flamebreak with Firefly to chase her out of the lane and keep her from re‑webbing.
Tip: Aim Flamebreak at the web itself; the explosion removes the web and deals damage to Broodmother, forcing her to retreat.

Shadow Demon

Shadow Demon’s Disruption can pull Broodmother out of her web, removing the movement‑speed bonus and exposing her to enemy focus. Soul Catcher amplifies damage taken, making even her modest early damage lethal when combined with burst.
Tip: Time Disruption just as Broodmother casts Spawn Spiderlings to interrupt the spawn and force a reset.

Dark Willow

Bramble Maze blocks web placement and creates a zone where Broodmother cannot move freely, while Cursed Crown silences her, preventing the use of Incapsitating Bite and Spin Web. The damage over time also punishes her low health pool.
Tip: Drop Bramble Maze near the lane’s choke point to force Broodmother onto a longer, unsafe path.

Jakiro

Jakiro’s Dual Breath and Ice Path apply constant AOE damage and slow, quickly melting spiderlings and preventing web stacking. The silence from Liquid Fire also stops Broodmother from casting Spin Web while she’s engaged.
Tip: Use Ice Path to cut off the lane’s primary web line, then follow with Dual Breath to force her out.

Warlock

Warlock’s Fatal Bonds links Broodmother to her spiderlings; any damage to the hero spreads to the minions, making her own army a liability. Shadow Word provides sustain for allies while the damage from the bonds punishes her aggressive pushes.
Tip: Cast Fatal Bonds as soon as you see a spiderling spawn; the bond will kill the spiderlings and severely damage Broodmother if she stays in melee range.

Drafting Against Broodmother

  • Prioritize heroes with strong AOE silence or root (e.g., Batrider, Shadow Demon, Dark Willow).
  • Pick heroes that can clear webs quickly (Flamebreak, Bramble Maze, Ice Path).
  • Include at least one reliable early‑game burst or lane‑dominant hero to pressure her before spiderlings multiply.
  • Avoid heavy reliance on melee heroes that can be trapped by webs unless they have strong gap‑close or dispel.

Laning Against Broodmother

  • Harass her before she can lay a web; her early health is low and she lacks escape without webs.
  • Force trades near the river edge where you can retreat to safety without stepping into her web radius.
  • When she casts Spawn Spiderlings, interrupt with a stun or silence to prevent the hatch.
  • Keep the lane clear of creep equilibrium; a balanced wave denies her easy kills for Spider’s Milk.

Itemizing Against Broodmother

Mekansm — provides burst heal to allies after a fight, offsetting the damage from her spiderlings and Incapsitating Bite.
Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — cyclone removes her from webs, interrupts Spawn Spiderlings, and gives a window to destroy webs.
Glimmer Cape — grants magic immunity to dodge Incapsitating Bite slow and the damage from spiderlings, while allowing safe web destruction.
Force Staff — lets you escape web‑locked zones instantly, preventing her from locking you down with webs.
Abyssal Blade — single‑target stun forces her out of web range and disables her ability to attack or spawn more spiderlings.

centaur-warrunner.name: Centaur Warrunner
centaur-warrunner.guideHtml:
Centaur Warrunner remains a solid front‑line initiator in the 7.41 meta, posting a 51.0% win rate across over 300 k recent ranked games. His blend of durability, stun, and the game‑changing Stampede keeps him relevant in both solo and team‑fight centric lineups.

How to Play Centaur Warrunner

Laning Phase

  • Use Hoof Stomp early (level 2) to punish aggressive melee heroes; the brief wind‑up lets you retreat while still delivering a stun.
  • Trade with Double Edge when you have a health buffer; the self‑damage is mitigated by your high base HP and the “cannot die from Double Edge” clause.
  • Stack Retaliate damage by building strength early (e.g., Tango, Healing Salve, Iron Branch); the extra return damage deters harass from ranged heroes.
  • Against hard‑disablers like Treant Protector or Brewmaster, prioritize safe farming and pull neutral camps to avoid being stunned before you can land Hoof Stomp.
  • If the lane is safe, pull a Work Horse early (level 6) to grant yourself and a teammate Stampede‑level movement for quick rotations or tower dives.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 12–16 when you have Stampede + Work Horse; look for 4‑man engages with Hoof Stomp → Double Edge → Stampede.
  • Use Hitch A Ride on a high‑damage ally (e.g., Phantom Assassin, Lifestealer) to protect them while you charge into the enemy backline.
  • Prioritize taking Roshan after you have a Heart of Tarrasque or Aghanim’s Scepter; the extra health makes you a reliable tank for the team.
  • When you see enemy Nyx Assassin or Grimstroke positioning for burst, keep Hoof Stomp on cooldown to punish their initiation.

Late Game

  • Win condition: force Stampede‑enabled team fights that collapse enemy positioning; the speed boost lets you and allies bypass vision and catch squishy backliners.
  • Positioning: stay just behind the front line; your Retaliate punishes any enemy that tries to focus you, while Hoof Stomp can still stun multiple heroes.
  • Lose the game if you waste Stampede on a single target or get caught by long‑range disables (e.g., Timbersaw’s Shackles) before you can land Hoof Stomp.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain for early lane trades.
  • Healing Salve — essential for surviving Double Edge self‑damage.
  • Stout Shield — mitigates harass from melee opponents.
  • Iron Branch ×2 — cheap strength for early Retaliate damage.

Core Items

  • Phase Boots — provides the 30 % movement bonus from Horsepower and the extra burst speed for initiations.
  • Blink Dagger — enables instant Hoof Stomp → Double Edge combos and lets you start Stampede from unexpected angles.
  • Heart of Tarrasque — maximizes survivability; you cannot die from Double Edge, and the massive HP pool makes you a true front‑line tank.
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Work Horse to grant Stampede to all allies and reduces cooldown, turning you into a global mobility tool.

Situational Items

  • Black King Bar — against heavy magical burst from Grimstroke, Nyx Assassin, or Timbersaw.
  • Shiva’s Guard — armor and aura to counter Medusa, Morphling, and other right‑click heroes; also provides an AoE slow that synergizes with Stampede.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects targeted disables (e.g., Treant Protector’s Nature’s Guise, Brewmaster’s Primal Split).
  • Pipe of Insight — mitigates magical damage from Silencer, Lich, and Grimstroke in team fights.
  • Crimson Guard — blocks burst physical damage from Timbersaw and Marci.
  • Mekansm — extra lane sustain and team fight healing when you’re the primary front‑liner.

Common Mistakes

  • Wasting Double Edge on low‑HP enemies instead of using it to secure a kill while already high on health.
  • Casting Hoof Stomp without checking for enemy disables; getting stunned before the wind‑up nullifies the stun.
  • Neglecting Work Horse after level 6, missing out on early Stampede speed for rotations and tower dives.
  • Over‑extending without Blink; without a gap‑closer you become an easy target for heroes like Timbersaw and Nyx Assassin.

FAQ

Is Centaur Warrunner good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 51.0% win rate across 306 k recent ranked games, Centaur remains a reliable initiator and tank, especially against lineups lacking strong disables.

What lane does Centaur Warrunner play?

Centaur is most commonly played in the off‑lane (solo safe lane) where his durability and Hoof Stomp allow him to survive and punish aggressive opponents.

Who counters Centaur Warrunner?

The toughest matchups are Treant Protector, Brewmaster, Marci, Timbersaw, Grimstroke, and Nyx Assassin, all of which have win rates against him below 44% in the current data set. Their disables and burst damage can neutralize his initiation if you’re not careful.
centaur-warrunner.counterHtml:
Centaur Warrunner’s threat comes from his massive burst — Double Edge + Retaliate — and his game‑changing global mobility with Stampede. The key to shutting him down is denying him the strength‑based damage and the ability to initiate safely, while forcing him to waste his limited disables.

Why These Heroes Beat Centaur Warrunner

Treant Protector

Treant’s Nature’s Grasp and Leech Seed keep Centaur rooted and constantly losing HP, neutralizing his self‑damage and preventing him from closing distance for Double Edge. Tip: stack a Living Tree in the lane to block Centaur’s path and force him into a long fight where his burst is less decisive.

Brewmaster

Brewmaster’s Primal Split creates three controllable units that can each stun or disarm Centaur, breaking his combo and making his Retaliate ineffective against multiple sources. Tip: prioritize Storm Hammer on the Brewmaster hero to lock him down while the other spirits focus Centaur.

Marci

Marci’s Rebound and Dispose provide a burst of crowd control that interrupts Centaur’s Hoof Stomp wind‑up and punishes his melee approach. Tip: use Dispose on Centaur right after he lands Double Edge to deny his self‑damage and force a costly retreat.

Timbersaw

Timbersaw’s Whirling Death and Reactive Armor shred through Centaur’s strength‑scaled damage while his pure‑damage spells ignore Retaliate’s damage return. Tip: keep Flame Guard active to absorb the burst from Double Edge and stay in range to spam Timber Chain for vision.

Grimstroke

Grimstroke’s Soul Bind links Centaur to an ally, making his Hoof Stomp and Stampede punish both heroes, while Phantom Pain provides a shield that blocks the self‑damage from Double Edge. Tip: cast Soul Bind before Centaur initiates and follow up with Dark Rift to reposition the linked ally out of Stampede’s path.

Drafting Against Centaur Warrunner

  • Prioritize heroes with strong disables or silences (e.g., Lion, Silencer) to stop Hoof Stomp and Stampede.
  • Pick strength‑based burst heroes or those with pure damage (Timbersaw, Marci) that ignore Retaliate’s return.
  • Include split‑push or high‑mobility heroes that can outrun Stampede (e.g., Phantom Lancer, Anti‑Mage).
  • Consider banning or limiting heroes that give Centaur massive strength items (e.g., Satanic, Heart of Tarrasque).

Laning Against Centaur Warrunner

  • Trade when his Hoof Stomp is on cooldown; his damage spikes are short‑lived.
  • Harass him with ranged poke to force him to use Double Edge defensively, then punish the self‑damage.
  • Exploit his lack of early lane sustain; deny him farm and force him to rely on jungle stacks.
  • Use tower aggression when his Retaliate is on a long cooldown, as he cannot safely dive.

Itemizing Against Centaur Warrunner

Ghost Scepter — blocks the physical burst from Double Edge and makes you untargetable by Retaliate.
Eul’s Scepter — cyclone disables Centaur during Hoof Stomp wind‑up, removing his initiation window.
Heaven’s Halberd — disarms Centaur, nullifying Double Edge and his melee damage.
Aghanim’s Shard (Marci) — gives Dispose to interrupt his combo and deny self‑damage.
Pipe of Insight — mitigates the magic damage from his Strength‑scaled abilities and reduces the impact of his burst.

chaos-knight.name: Chaos Knight
chaos-knight.guideHtml:
Chaos Knight remains a high‑damage, illusion‑centric carry whose 50.7 % win rate across 169,958 ranked games (OpenDota, July 2026) keeps him viable in the current meta, though he leans toward a risk‑heavy playstyle.

How to Play Chaos Knight

Laning Phase

  • Use Chaos Bolt early to punish low‑HP supports and secure last‑hits; the random stun often forces enemy heroes to miss creep waves.
  • Pair Reality Rift with a right‑click to pull a melee opponent into your tower range, then follow up with a bolt for a cheap kill.
  • Prioritize farming over fighting when against lane‑dominant heroes (e.g., Jakiro, Mars) because your win rate vs them is below 40 % (OpenDota, July 2026).
  • Stack neutral camps with your lane partner when you have a free moment; the extra gold accelerates your Phantasm timing.
  • Keep an eye on the enemy support’s mana; a depleted Chaos Bolt combo can be a lane‑control tool that forces the opponent to play defensively.

Mid Game

  • Hit level 16 for Phantasm; the illusion wave is your primary damage source for team fights.
  • Group with your team and look for Reality Rift + Chaos Bolt combos on squishy back‑liners; the armor reduction from Rift makes them easier to finish.
  • Split‑push side lanes while your cores farm; your durability and Chaos Strike crits let you survive tower dives and force enemy rotations.
  • Avoid extended fights against heroes with strong disables (e.g., Invoker, Windranger) until you have at least one Satanic or Heart of Tarrasque.

Late Game

  • Win condition: force fights where you can unleash Phantasm and quickly eliminate the enemy carry with Chaos Bolt + Reality Rift.
  • Position near your frontline; your Chaos Strike lifesteal sustains you while your illusions tank damage (they take 350 % damage).
  • Losing the game often comes from being caught without Phantasm or Satanic against high‑burst heroes like Queen of Pain, who can shred you before you can create enough illusion pressure.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango + Healing Salve — sustain in the lane against harassment.
  • Quelling Blade — secure early creep kills and help with jungle stacking.
  • Stout Shield — mitigates harass from melee supports.
  • Iron Branch x2 — cheap stats and can be later built into a Magic Wand.

Core Items

  • Power Treads — attack speed for faster illusion damage and flexibility between Strength/Agility.
  • Mask of Madness — massive attack speed and lifesteal boost your Chaos Strike crits.
  • Black King Bar — essential against heavy magical burst (Invoker, Queen of Pain).
  • Satanic — provides survivability in late‑game fights, especially versus burst heroes.
  • Heart of Tarrasque — amplifies your durability and illusion tanking.

Situational Items

  • Manta Style — extra illusion count and a way to dispel silences; useful vs heroes like Windranger.
  • Abyssal Blade — lockdown for slippery carries; works well when you already have Phantasm.
  • Butterfly — evasion against right‑click heavy heroes (e.g., Tiny, Ember Spirit).
  • Linken’s Sphere – blocks single‑target disables from heroes such as Invoker’s Sun Strike or Queen of Pain’s Sonic Wave.
  • Assault Cuirass – armor reduction synergizes with Reality Rift and helps your phantasms survive longer.

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑extending without Phantasm – diving early fights leaves you vulnerable to burst heroes who currently give you sub‑40 % win rates.
  • Neglecting lifesteal on creeps – Chaos Strike lifesteal is reduced on creeps; relying on it for sustain in lane leads to unnecessary deaths.
  • Spamming Reality Rift on tanky heroes – the armor reduction is modest; prioritize Rift on squishy targets to maximize damage.
  • Building pure damage items – ignoring survivability (BKB, Satanic) makes you an easy target for disables and burst.

FAQ

Is Chaos Knight good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 50.7 % win rate across nearly 170 k ranked games (OpenDota, July 2026), Chaos Knight sits slightly above average. He excels when he can farm into Phantasm, but struggles against heroes that give him sub‑40 % win rates such as Jakiro, Mars, and Invoker.

What lane does Chaos Knight play?

Chaos Knight is typically played in the safe lane as a carry, often paired with a support who can help secure early Chaos Bolt kills and protect him while he farms. The lane allows him to accumulate the gold needed for his core items and early Phantasm.

Who counters Chaos Knight?

Heroes that apply strong disables and burst damage—Jakiro, Mars, Invoker, Windranger, and Queen of Pain—currently have the lowest win rates against him (35.7 %–40.8 %). Building early defensive items (BKB, early Satanic) and avoiding prolonged fights with these heroes is essential.
chaos-knight.counterHtml:
Chaos Knight’s threat comes from his burst potential with Chaos Bolt, the massive damage swing of Phantasm, and his ability to close gaps with Reality Rift. The key to shutting him down is denying his survivability and preventing his illusions from ever becoming a decisive damage source.

Why These Heroes Beat Chaos Knight

Jakiro

Jakiro’s Dual Breath and Ice Path apply constant magic damage and a reliable slow, out‑damaging Chaos Knight’s early burst while his Liquid Fire burns down the armor‑reduced target from Reality Rift. Tip: Keep a Static Link on Chaos Knight to sap his health as he tries to engage, then follow up with a stun from Dual Breath.

Mars

Mars’s Spear of Mars creates an impassable arena that blocks Reality Rift’s teleport and isolates Chaos Knight from his team. Inside the arena, God’s Rebuke deals a massive burst that scales with Chaos Knight’s strength, punishing his high‑damage potential. Tip: Time the arena entry just after Chaos Bolt lands to force a defensive retreat.

Invoker

Invoker’s Cold Snap locks Chaos Knight in a rapid stun‑damage loop, nullifying the random stun of Chaos Bolt and preventing him from positioning for Phantasm. Sun Strike and Chaos Meteor provide global, armor‑ignoring damage that bypasses the reduced armor from Reality Rift. Tip: Use Cold Snap on Chaos Knight right after he casts Reality Rift to keep him frozen while you finish him with Sun Strike.

Windranger

Windranger’s Shackleshot can pin Chaos Knight (or his Phantasm) to a tree, instantly disabling his mobility and forcing a long‑duration stun. Her Powershot deals high physical damage that ignores the 350% damage taken by his illusions, making Phantasm easy to shred. Tip: Aim Shackleshot at the point where Chaos Knight is about to use Reality Rift; the tether will break the teleport.

Queen of Pain

Queen of Pain’s Scream of Pain and Shadow Strike apply consistent magic damage and a strong slow, counter‑ing Chaos Knight’s burst window. Her Blink lets her dodge Chaos Bolt and escape Reality Rift, while Sonic Wave can finish a low‑health CK even through his Phantasm’s damage reduction. Tip: Blink out of Reality Rift’s line of sight and immediately cast Scream of Pain to force a trade while his Phantasm is still on cooldown.

Drafting Against Chaos Knight

  • Prioritize heroes with strong disables that can interrupt Reality Rift (e.g., Mars, Jakiro).
  • Choose magic‑damage heavy lineups; Chaos Knight’s armor reduction is physical‑focused.
  • Include heroes with global or long‑range burst to punish his low early‑game win rate.
  • Ban or avoid heroes that grant massive lifesteal or armor, which amplify Chaos Strike.

Laning Against Chaos Knight

  • Harass aggressively before he lands his first Chaos Bolt; his early damage is limited.
  • Trade when his Reality Rift is on cooldown (6 s) – he cannot reposition or reduce armor.
  • Force him to use Phantasm early; his illusions are vulnerable to magic damage and take 350% damage.
  • Keep lane equilibrium low; a higher creep wave gives him more space to pull with Reality Rift.

Itemizing Against Chaos Knight

Ghost Scepter — makes you untargetable by his physical attacks and Phantasm’s 100 % damage.
Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — cyclone removes him from fights, nullifying Reality Rift and Chaos Bolt.
Black King Bar — prevents the stun from Chaos Bolt and the armor‑reduction debuff from affecting you during teamfights.
Scythe of Vyse — hard‑disable that stops both CK and his Phantasm from initiating.

Heroes that apply strong disables and burst damage—Jakiro, Mars, Invoker, Windranger, and Queen of Pain—currently have the lowest win rates against him (35.7 %–40.8 %). Building early defensive items (BKB, early Satanic) and avoiding prolonged fights with these heroes is essential.

chen.name: Chen
chen.guideHtml:
Chen is a niche support/pusher who thrives on creep control and global presence. On patch 7.41 his pub win rate sits at 44.8% over 17,195 recent ranked matches, placing him below average but still viable in coordinated play.

How to Play Chen

Laning Phase

  • Use Penitence on enemy heroes or creeps to slow them and amplify allied right‑click damage, especially against melee off‑laners that rely on early aggression.
  • Early Holy Persuasion on neutral camps (e.g., small camps in the river) gives you extra gold and a foothold for lane pressure; the converted creep’s health is capped at 400, so prioritize low‑HP units.
  • Pair Divine Favor with your lane partner’s defensive items (e.g., Vanguard) to boost armor and regeneration, making the lane more sustainable against harass.
  • When the enemy supports roam, drop a Penitence on a neutral creep and pull it into the lane; the slowed creep can be used to block pull camps or to force the enemy to waste mana on dispels.
  • Keep an eye on Hand of God cooldown; a well‑timed global heal can save a struggling lane partner from a gank and also keep your converted creeps alive for continued lane presence.

Mid Game

  • Power spike: After the first Hand of God (level 6) and a few converted creeps, you gain a reliable global heal and extra lane pressure.
  • Roam with Divine Favor + Hand of God to assist mid‑lane or safe‑lane allies; the heal applies to all allied heroes and your controlled creeps, turning skirmishes in your favor.
  • Prioritize taking neutral camps in the jungle (e.g., Ancient camps) with Holy Persuasion to build a small army that can push towers or contest Roshan.
  • Use Penitence on high‑damage enemy heroes (e.g., Storm Spirit, Queen of Pain) before a teamfight; the slow makes them easier targets for your allies and your converted creeps.

Late Game

  • Win condition: Use a swarm of converted creeps to split‑push while your team secures objectives; the global Hand of God keeps your push alive against enemy damage.
  • Position near the front of your creep army, casting Divine Favor on yourself or a frontline ally to boost armor and regen, making you harder to kill.
  • Avoid being caught out of position without a Hand of God ready; a single death can wipe out your creep army and give the enemy a decisive advantage.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane while you wait for a neutral creep to convert.
  • Healing Salve — quick burst heal for you or your lane partner after early harassment.
  • Observer Ward — vision to protect your converted creeps and set up safe pulls.
  • Iron Branch ×2 — cheap stat boost; can later be used for Magic Wand.

Core Items

  • Tranquil Boots — massive movement speed and passive regen, essential for repositioning your creeps and staying alive.
  • Mekansm — provides a strong area heal and armor aura, synergizing with your Divine Favor for team fights.
  • Aghanim’s Shard — upgrades Holy Persuasion to target any enemy unit, allowing you to steal high‑value enemy creeps or even a hero’s summoned unit.
  • Hand of God (upgrade from Mekansm) — global heal that keeps your creep army and allies alive during late‑game pushes.

Situational Items

  • Glimmer Cape — escape tool when enemy initiates on you; also useful to protect key converted creeps.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target spells, great against heroes like Jakiro who rely on disables.
  • Pipe of Insight — counters magic‑heavy lineups; useful against Storm Spirit and Queen of Pain.
  • Solar Crest — amplifies damage on a target creep or hero, turning your converted creeps into a true damage threat.
  • Ghost Scepter — safety against right‑click heavy heroes such as Ursa and Primal Beast.

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑extending without a creep army: New players often push lanes alone, forgetting that Chen’s strength lies in his converted units.
  • Neglecting Hand of God timing: Using the global heal too early or too late wastes its potential; keep it for decisive team fights or to rescue a dying push.
  • Spamming Penitence on heroes: Penitence is far more effective on creeps to control lane equilibrium; using it on heroes wastes mana and cooldown.
  • Failing to upgrade Holy Persuasion: Not purchasing Aghanim’s Shard limits you to neutral creeps, missing opportunities to steal enemy summons or low‑HP heroes.

FAQ

Is Chen good in the current patch?

Chen’s win rate is 44.8% on patch 7.41, placing him below the median for support heroes. He remains viable in coordinated play thanks to his global heal and creep‑pushing potential, but he requires good macro and creep‑control skill.

What lane does Chen play?

Chen is typically played as a support in the safe lane (radiant or dire) where he can farm neutral camps early with Holy Persuasion and provide lane sustain with Divine Favor and Penitence. He can also be flexed to off‑lane in lower‑MMR games to apply early pressure.

Who counters Chen?

The toughest matchups statistically are Abaddon (43.6% win), Nature’s Prophet (47.0%), and Jakiro (50.3%). These heroes either out‑heal Chen’s sustain or can lock down his converted creeps, making it difficult for him to establish a creep army. Use early vision and prioritize safe creep conversions to mitigate their impact.
chen.counterHtml:
Chen is a high‑impact support whose strength lies in converting neutral creeps into a mobile army and sustaining his team with massive global heals. His threat spikes when he can stack creeps early and keep his allies alive through teamfights, so shutting down his creep‑control and healing windows is the fastest way to neutralize him.

Why These Heroes Beat Chen

Abaddon

Abaddon’s Aphotic Shield can purge the heal from Hand of God and block the health‑regen from Divine Favor, while his Mist Coil gives him a cheap, reliable source of self‑heal that outpaces Chen’s sustain. Tip: keep a shield on your core during Chen’s early creep‑pulls to deny the extra health he grants his converted units.

Nature’s Prophet

Nature’s Prophet’s global Teleport lets him scout and contest Chen’s neutral stacks before they become a threat, and his Sprout can trap Chen and his converted creeps, preventing the micro‑controlled pushes that Chen relies on. Tip: drop a split‑push lane early and force Chen to waste time defending rather than stacking.

Jakiro

Jakiro’s Dual Breath and Ice Path apply constant AoE slow and damage, crippling the movement speed boost Chen gives his creeps and making them easy targets for his own team. Tip: place Ice Path on Chen’s creep‑pull spot to interrupt his conversion and force a disengage.

Primal Beast

Primal Beast’s Onslaught can smash through Chen’s frontline and the converted creeps, while his Trample deals pure damage that ignores the bonus damage Chen grants his units. Tip: engage Primal Beast early; his burst will kill Chen’s converted creeps before they can contribute.

Dragon Knight

Dragon Knight’s Dragon Tail provides a reliable stun that interrupts Chen’s Holy Persuasion channel and his Breathe Fire burns the health of converted creeps, reducing their effectiveness. Tip: stun Chen as soon as he attempts a creep conversion to deny him the extra unit and the associated bounty.

Drafting Against Chen

  • Prioritize heroes with strong global presence or split‑push (e.g., Nature’s Prophet, Templar Assassin).
  • Pick heroes with reliable single‑target disables or silences to interrupt Holy Persuasion.
  • Include early‑game damage dealers who can contest neutral stacks (e.g., Juggernaut, Luna).
  • Ban or avoid heroes that give Chen extra creeps or amplify his healing (e.g., Dazzle).

Laning Against Chen

  • Harass Chen before he can pull a neutral camp; his early game damage is low.
  • Force him to waste mana on Penitence by positioning aggressively; the slow is weak against heroes with movement speed items.
  • Punish his creep‑pull attempts with quick burst damage; a dead converted creep denies him both gold and lane pressure.
  • Keep a defensive tower shield or a cheap heal (e.g., Infused Raindrop) ready to mitigate his early Hand of God burst.

Itemizing Against Chen

Glimmer Cape — grants magic immunity, nullifying Hand of God’s global heal and Divine Favor’s aura.
Heaven’s Halberd — disarms Chen, preventing him from using Penitence and Holy Persuasion on the fly.
Eul’s Scepter of Divinity – cyclone Chen out of a creep‑pull or heal window, buying time for your team to engage.
Black King Bar — blocks the heal and armor bonus from Divine Favor, letting you trade freely in fights.

clinkz.name: Clinkz
clinkz.guideHtml:
Clinkz remains a high‑damage, high‑mobility carry with strong split‑push and escape tools. On patch 7.41 his pub win rate sits at 49.3 % over 196 k recent ranked games, placing him solidly in the mid‑tier of carries—strong enough to pick games when played well, but vulnerable to several melee initiators.

How to Play Clinkz

Laning Phase

  • Skeleton Walk early to scout and avoid early harass; the invisibility also lets you place the first Skeleton Archers for lane pressure.
  • Use Searing Arrows on the first creep wave to secure a fast Death Pact on a large neutral, granting health and a larger pool for early survivability.
  • Keep Strafe toggled when you have a clear line of sight; the attack‑speed bonus also buffs nearby Skeleton Archers, making them harder for enemy supports to kill.
  • Prioritize a Death Pact on a stacked neutral camp rather than a hero kill when you’re behind; the heal and max‑health gain offset early tower pressure.
  • Against aggressive lane opponents (e.g., Spirit Breaker, Pudge) stay under tower, use Skeleton Walk to dodge their initiation, and only trade when you have Searing Arrows ready.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 12 when Burning Barrage becomes available; look for 2‑v‑2 fights or tower dives where you can channel safely.
  • Split‑push with Burning Army + Skeleton Archers; the row of archers forces the enemy to split, and the armor‑piercing Infernal Shred lets you shred towers quickly.
  • Join team fights only when you have Strafe active and a clear line of sight; your arrows now benefit from the 40 % attack‑speed transfer to nearby archers, amplifying burst.
  • Use Death Pact on high‑HP creeps or allied archers after a fight to instantly recover health and increase your max HP for the next engagement.

Late Game

  • Win condition: force the enemy to defend multiple lanes with Burning Army and Skeleton Archers, then collapse onto a single target with Burning Barrage and Strafe for massive true‑damage spikes.
  • Positioning: stay on the edge of vision; use Skeleton Walk to reposition behind enemy lines, but never attack or use items until you’re certain the fight is favorable.
  • Game‑losing mistake: diving into fights without Strafe active or without a safe Skeleton Walk entry, especially against heroes like Spirit Breaker or Slardar who can lock you down.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain for early lane and early Death Pact creep kills.
  • Healing Salve — emergency health after early ganks.
  • Iron Branch ×2 — cheap stats and can be later built into a Magic Wand.
  • Quelling Blade — helps last‑hit creeps faster while you’re still low on attack speed.
  • Observer Ward — vision to avoid ganks from Spirit Breaker and Pudge.

Core Items

  • Power Treads — attack speed for Strafe and better chase potential.
  • Mask of Madness — huge attack‑speed boost that synergizes with Strafe and Burning Barrage.
  • Black King Bar — essential against disables from Slardar, Luna, and Templar Assassin.
  • Satanic — lifesteal to survive prolonged fights after you’ve built Mask of Madness.
  • Butterfly — evasion and damage; crucial against right‑click heroes like Luna and Slardar.

Situational Items

  • Manta Style — extra Skeleton Archers and a way to dispel silences from Skywrath Mage or Clockwerk.
  • Abyssal Blade — lock down slippery heroes (e.g., Spirit Breaker) when you need a guaranteed kill.
  • Heart of Tarrasque — extra survivability against burst from Pudge and Hoodwink.
  • Monkey King Bar — counters evasion from Luna and ensures your Burning Barrage lands.
  • Linken's Sphere — blocks single‑target spells like Pudge’s Meat Hook or Slardar’s Corrosive Haze.
  • Sange & Yasha — movement speed and status resistance for better chase and escape.

Common Mistakes

  • Casting Strafe without archers nearby – the 40 % attack‑speed transfer is wasted; always keep a few Skeleton Archers alive before toggling.
  • Using Burning Barrage in open fights – the channel can be interrupted; wait for vision or a brief window after a stun.
  • Over‑extending without Skeleton Walk – losing invisibility removes your primary escape tool, making you an easy target for Spirit Breaker or Pudge.
  • Neglecting Death Pact on large creeps – missing the health and max‑HP boost delays your mid‑game power spike.

FAQ

Is Clinkz good in the current patch?

Clinkz sits at a 49.3 % win rate across 196 k recent ranked games, making him a viable but not dominant carry. He shines in split‑push and high‑damage bursts, yet struggles against hard‑initiate heroes like Spirit Breaker and Pudge.

What lane does Clinkz play?

Clinkz is typically played in the safe lane as a carry, using early Skeleton Walk and Searing Arrows to survive harassment and farm efficiently.

Who counters Clinkz?

The toughest matchups are Spirit Breaker, Pudge, Slardar, Hoodwink, Templar Assassin, and Luna, where Clinkz’s win rates drop to the low‑40 % range. Their disables, burst, and armor‑shredding tools neutralize Clinkz’s reliance on pure damage.
clinkz.counterHtml:
Clinkz is a hyper‑mobile, pure‑damage hero whose threat comes from his ability to burst down squishy targets from invisibility and to sustain through his Skeleton Army. The core way to shut him down is to deny him the space to hide, punish his low early‑game health pool, and apply armor‑based or burst‑damage tools that outpace his Searing Arrows and Burning Barrage.

Why These Heroes Beat Clinkz

Spirit Breaker

Spirit Breaker’s Charge of Darkness and Nether Strike close the distance instantly, forcing Clinkz out of Skeleton Walk before he can position his Burning Barrage. The constant pressure also prevents him from safely stacking Skeleton Army. Tip: Use a early Blink Frost or Shadow Blade on Spirit Breaker to surprise‑gank Clinkz before he can escape.

Pudge

Pudge’s Meat Hook pulls Clinkz out of invisibility and into a vulnerable spot, while Rot applies constant magic damage that ignores Clinkz’s armor‑piercing debuff. The hook also disrupts Clinkz’s Strafe timing, reducing his attack‑speed burst. Tip: Aim hooks at the trees where Clinkz is likely to hide; a successful hook often ends the lane.

Slardar

Slardar’s Slithereen Crush provides a reliable stun that interrupts Clinkz’s channeling Burning Barrage and prevents him from activating Skeleton Walk. His Amplify Damage reduces Clinkz’s armor, neutralizing the benefit of Infernal Shred. Tip: Keep Slardar’s Corrosive Haze on Clinkz to amplify all physical damage, especially from tower shots.

Hoodwink

Hoodwink’s Acorn Shot applies a strong armor‑reduction debuff, directly countering Clinkz’s reliance on armor‑piercing attacks. Her Bushwhack roots Clinkz, breaking his invisibility and preventing him from escaping with Skeleton Walk. Tip: Use Scurry to close the gap quickly after a successful Bushwhack, denying Clinkz any safe retreat.

Templar Assassin

Templar Assassin’s Refraction blocks the first few hits of Clinkz’s Searing Arrows and Burning Barrage, while Trap provides vision that forces Clinkz to reveal himself. Her Meld grants burst physical damage that outpaces Clinkz’s sustained output. Tip: Place Trap near likely Skeleton Walk exit points to catch Clinkz the moment he attacks.

Drafting Against Clinkz

  • Prioritize heroes with hard‑crowd‑control (stuns, roots, pulls) that can interrupt Skeleton Walk and Burning Barrage.
  • Pick armor‑reduction or armor‑shredding abilities to nullify Infernal Shred.
  • Choose early‑game burst damage or lane‑dominant heroes to exploit Clinkz’s low starting health.
  • Include at least one vision‑heavy or detection hero to deny safe invisibility.

Laning Against Clinkz

  • Harass him before he can secure a Skeleton Army; his early HP is very low.
  • Use tower range and creep wave to force him into the river where his Skeleton Walk is limited.
  • Punish any attempt to cast Strafe by timing attacks just after he activates it—his attack‑speed boost is wasted if he is forced to retreat.
  • Maintain constant vision (wards, Sentry) to catch him when he exits invisibility to last‑hit.

Itemizing Against Clinkz

Blink Dagger — lets you close the gap instantly, breaking his invisibility and preventing a safe Burning Barrage.
Force Staff — pushes Clinkz out of his optimal range, disrupting Skeleton Army placement and forcing him to reposition.
Ghost Scepter — makes you ethereal, nullifying his physical burst from Searing Arrows and Burning Barrage.
Crimson Guard — provides a massive armor block that mitigates the damage from his armor‑piercing attacks.
Eul’s Scepter — cyclone removes him from the fight, canceling Skeleton Walk and giving your team time to respond.

clockwerk.name: Clockwerk
clockwerk.guideHtml:
Clockwork Warr​rior (Clockwerk) is a durable initiator who excels at locking down enemies with his Power Cogs and setting up team fights with global vision from Rocket Flare. On patch 7.41 his overall pub win rate sits at 48.7% over 147 k ranked games, placing him as a solid but not dominant pick in the current meta. He shines when he can control space and protect teammates, but struggles against heroes that can outrange or out‑maneuver his relatively slow turn rate.

How to Play Clockwerk

Laning Phase

  • Use Jetpack to scout the lane and maintain safe distance while last‑hitting; the flying vision also denies enemy jungle pulls.
  • Drop a Power Cog when the enemy off‑lane attempts a dive; the trap gives you armor (via Overclocking) and punishes their aggression.
  • Spam Battery Assault on melee creeps to add minor magical damage and a ministun, helping you secure early lane control.
  • If the lane is heavily harassed (e.g., by Venomancer or Clinkz), toggle Jetpack off and stay behind the creep wave, using the armor from Power Cogs to mitigate damage.
  • Coordinate with your support for a Hookshot gank once you hit level 6; the stun radius (175) can catch multiple opponents and force early tower pressure.

Mid Game

  • Power Cogs + Overclocking become a strong zone‑control tool around objectives; place them near Roshan or high‑ground jungle entrances to deter picks.
  • Use Rocket Flare on contested jungle paths to gain vision and slow enemies, setting up rotations for your team.
  • Prioritize Armor Power stacks (consume Chainmail) once you have a reliable farm pattern; the 0.25 % damage per armor scales well into mid‑game team fights.
  • Look for Hookshot initiations on isolated heroes; a successful hook into a clustered enemy group can win a 2‑v‑2 skirmish.

Late Game

  • Position Power Cogs around your high‑ground or Roshan to create a “cage” that forces the enemy to fight on your terms; the armor bonus from Overclocked Cogs makes you hard to burst.
  • Use Rocket Flare to provide global vision on split‑push lanes; the slow and damage can deter heroes like Luna or Death Prophet from safely pushing.
  • Avoid long‑range poke from counters such as Venomancer, Magnus, or Enchantress—if you’re forced into a straight fight without Cogs, the game swings quickly against you.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango + Healing Salve — sustain against early harass.
  • Enchanted Mango — provides burst mana for early Battery Assault and Hookshot.
  • Stout Shield — mitigates harassment from right‑click heroes (e.g., Clinkz).
  • Observer Ward — early vision for safe Jetpack scouting.

Core Items

  • Phase Boots — extra mobility for closing gaps after Jetpack toggle.
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Hookshot to a longer range and adds a second stun, crucial against mobile heroes like Monkey King.
  • Shiva’s Guard — armor, AoE slow, and the active armor aura synergizes with Armor Power.
  • Black King Bar — protects you while channeling Power Cogs or Hookshot in team fights.

Situational Items

  • Lotus Orb — reflects disables from Venomancer’s Poison Nova and Magnus’s Reverse Polarity.
  • Heaven’s Halberd — disarms right‑click carries such as Clinkz and Luna.
  • Aeon Disk — survivability against burst from Enchantress or Death Prophet.
  • Glimmer Cape — dodge magical nukes and provide temporary invisibility for safe repositioning.
  • Assault Cuirass — extra armor and attack speed for team‑fight presence when you need to push high‑ground.

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑relying on Jetpack for aggression – the limited turn rate makes you easy to kite; use Jetpack mainly for scouting and positioning.
  • Dropping Power Cogs without armor focus – forgetting to activate Overclocking leaves you vulnerable to burst from heroes like Magnus.
  • Hookshot spamming without vision – missing the target wastes cooldown and leaves you exposed; always pair Hookshot with a ward or Rocket Flare.
  • Neglecting Chainmail consumption – failing to stack armor early reduces the scaling damage from Armor Power, weakening your late‑game impact.

FAQ

Is Clockwerk good in the current patch?

Clockwerk sits at a 48.7% win rate in pub ranked, making him a viable but not top-tier pick. He excels in space control and durability, especially against heroes like Death Prophet and Tidehunter, but struggles versus high‑mobility or strong magical damage heroes (e.g., Venomancer, Monkey King).

What lane does Clockwerk play?

Clockwerk is typically played in the off‑lane (solo safe lane) where his tankiness and initiation can deter enemy dives. He can also be flexed to a mid position if the team needs a hard‑initiate and vision control, but off‑lane remains his most common role.

Who counters Clockwerk?

The toughest matchups are Venomancer, Clinkz, Monkey King, Magnus, Beastmaster, and Enchantress, where Clockwerk’s win rates drop below 42 %. These heroes either outrange his initiation, apply constant magical pressure, or have strong disables that bypass his armor and Cogs. Counter‑play includes early vision, consistent warding, and building items like Lotus Orb or Heaven’s Halberd.
clockwerk.counterHtml:
Clockwork’s strength lies in its relentless lockdown: Power Cogs can trap a hero for several seconds while Battery Assault and Hookshot add damage and stun. The key to beating him is to deny him the opportunity to land a cog‑trap or to force him into a position where his short‑range toolkit is useless.

Why These Heroes Beat Clockwerk

Venomancer

Venomancer’s Poison Nova and Venomous Gale apply constant damage‑over‑time that outpaces Clockwerk’s burst, and his slow makes it hard for Clockwerk to close the distance for a cog‑trap. Tip: Keep a Poison Nova ready for the moment Clockwerk activates Power Cogs; the damage will force him to retreat before the trap expires.

Clinkz

Clinkz’s Searing Arrows and Death Pact give him high burst damage that can kill Clockwerk before he can land a cog, while Burning Barrage provides a reliable source of magic damage that bypasses Clockwerk’s armor scaling. Tip: Use Burning Barrage from range when Clockwerk is on Jetpack; the vision from Rocket Flare won’t help him dodge the spell.

Monkey King

Monkey King’s Tree Dance grants untargetable movement, letting him dodge Hookshot and Power Cogs, while Jungle Strike and Wukong’s Command apply area damage that punishes Clockwerk’s clumped cogs. Tip: Initiate with Tree Dance into a safe tree, then drop Jungle Strike when Clockwerk attempts to engage with Jetpack.

Magnus

Magnus’s Skewer can pull Clockwerk out of his own Power Cogs, breaking the trap, and Reverse Polarity groups enemies together, making Clockwerk’s single‑target stun less effective. Tip: Time Skewer to hit Clockwerk as he toggles Jetpack; the forced movement cancels his limited turn rate and leaves him vulnerable.

Beastmaster

Beastmaster’s Wild Axes provide constant physical damage that ignores Clockwerk’s armor scaling, and his Primal Roar stun can interrupt a Hookshot or Power Cogs activation. Tip: Position Primal Roar when Clockwerk is about to cast Power Cogs; the stun prevents the trap from forming and forces a reset.

Drafting Against Clockwerk

  • Prioritize heroes with strong long‑range poke or slows (e.g., Venomancer, Viper).
  • Choose mobile heroes that can dodge Hookshot and Power Cogs (Monkey King, Anti‑Mage).
  • Pick heroes with reliable disables that can interrupt his abilities (Magnus, Lion).
  • Avoid heavy armor‑stackers unless you have a way to bypass his Armor Power (e.g., pure damage sources).

Laning Against Clockwerk

  • Trade early with ranged harass; Clockwerk’s Battery Assault deals low damage.
  • Exploit his weak early game before he can afford Chainmail armor stacks.
  • When he toggles Jetpack, focus on vision and burst damage to force him back.
  • Punish missed Hookshots by counter‑engaging immediately; his turn rate is limited.

Itemizing Against Clockwerk

Manta Style — breaks disables and lets you dodge Power Cogs while providing additional damage.

Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — cyclone can lift Clockwerk out of his own cog trap and nullify his stun.

Black King Bar — immunity to his magical damage and stuns lets you chase or survive his Hookshot.

Ghost Scepter — makes you untargetable by his physical attacks and reduces the impact of his Armor Power scaling.
