crystal-maiden.name: Crystal Maiden
crystal-maiden.guideHtml:
Crystal Maiden is a classic support hero whose kit revolves around mana sustain, crowd‑control, and a late‑game burst ultimate. On patch 7.41 she sits at a solid 51.6 % win rate across ≈ 479 k ranked games, making her a reliable pick in the current meta despite a few tough lane match‑ups【OpenDota July 2026】.

How to Play Crystal Maiden

Laning Phase

  • Arcane Aura early – keep the aura active to give yourself and your lane partner extra mana regen; it lets you spam Crystal Nova for harassment without draining your pool.
  • Frostbite on low‑HP creep waves or enemy heroes to secure kills; the 4× damage bonus on non‑ancient creeps makes it a cheap lane clear tool.
  • Crystal Nova + Frostbite combo: cast Nova to slow, then lock the target with Frostbite for guaranteed damage and zone control.
  • Prioritize a support‑heavy lane (e.g., safe lane with a hard‑carry) because your mana regen aura scales better when allies stay nearby.
  • Watch for the toughest match‑ups (Razor, Batrider, Mirana, Techies, Puck, Keeper of the Light) – play ultra‑conservative, avoid over‑extending, and rely on vision and defensive Crystal Clone to survive ganks.

Mid Game

  • Freezing Field spike at level 6 + 200 mana: look for clustered enemy fights; the 10‑second channel deals massive AoE damage if you can stay alive.
  • Use Crystal Clone to initiate or disengage: slide into a fight, place the clone, then let it shatter for a burst of Frostbite on nearby foes.
  • Roam with Arcane Aura and Frostbite to set up kills for your cores; your mana regen lets you spam disables while teammates farm.
  • Secure vision around Roshan and enemy jungle; your low‑cost Crystal Nova provides both damage and slow for early picks.

Late Game

  • Position Freezing Field behind your front line; the channel is vulnerable, so use your allies as a shield and time it when enemies are locked by Frostbite or Crystal Clone.
  • Win condition: force team fights where you can land a full Freezing Field while your cores follow up; the combination of slows and burst often decides late‑game engagements.
  • Avoid being the primary target: if you die before channeling, you give the enemy a huge mana and cooldown advantage.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane, especially against aggressive heroes.
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery after early skirmishes.
  • Observer Ward — vision to protect against ganks from Razor, Batrider, etc.
  • Clarity ×2 — keep mana for frequent Crystal Nova/Frostbite usage.
  • Iron Branch ×2 — cheap stats and can be later built into a Magic Wand.

Core Items

  • Tranquil Boots — massive movement speed and passive mana regen complement Arcane Aura.
  • Glimmer Cape — defensive tool to survive focus fire while channeling Freezing Field.
  • Force Staff — helps position yourself for optimal Freezing Field placement and escapes.
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Crystal Clone to a larger shield and adds extra damage on shatter, increasing teamfight impact.

Situational Items

  • Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — extra disable and self‑save against heroes like Puck or Mirana.
  • Ghost Scepter — counter right‑click heroes (e.g., Luna, Sniper) when you need to survive burst.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target spells such as Razor’s Static Link or Batrider’s Flaming Lasso.
  • Scythe of Vyse — adds a second hard‑disable if your Frostbite is on cooldown.
  • Aether Lens — extends the range of Frostbite and Crystal Nova, useful against mobile heroes.

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑using Frostbite on heroes with strong escape (e.g., Puck) and getting caught out of position.
  • Neglecting vision: without wards, Razor and Batrider can easily silence and pull you out of fights.
  • Trying to spam Freezing Field without proper front‑line protection, leading to early deaths and wasted cooldowns.
  • Buying too many mana items early and ignoring survivability; Crystal Maiden’s low health makes her a prime target.

FAQ

Is Crystal Maiden good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 51.6 % win rate across nearly half a million ranked games, she remains a solid support. Her mana‑regen aura and reliable disables keep her relevant, especially on teams that can protect her to unleash Freezing Field.

What lane does Crystal Maiden play?

She is typically played in the safe lane as a position 5 support, pairing with a hard‑carry. The lane provides space to farm mana and use Arcane Aura, while her early disables help secure lane equilibrium.

Who counters Crystal Maiden?

The toughest match‑ups right now are Razor, Batrider, Mirana, Techies, Puck, and Keeper of the Light, where her win rates dip below 43 % (e.g., 30.5 % vs Razor). These heroes either silence, burst, or out‑maneuver her, making it essential to buy defensive items and maintain vision.
crystal-maiden.counterHtml:
Crystal Maiden’s threat comes from her global mana‑regen aura, strong lane harassment with Frostbite and Crystal Nova, and the massive burst of Freezing Field in team fights. The key to shutting her down is to deny her mana, punish her low mobility, and force her to waste her limited burst on heroes that can survive or counter‑spell it.

Why These Heroes Beat Crystal Maiden

Razor

Razor’s Static Link drains damage‑based heroes of their attack power, turning Crystal Maiden’s low‑damage spells into near‑nothing while his Unstable Current silences her, preventing her from casting Frostbite or Freezing Field.
Tip: Keep Razor’s Static Link on CM early; the mana‑drain from her Arcane Aura also fuels Razor’s Eye of the Storm for extra lane pressure.

Batrider

Batrider’s Flamebreak instantly removes Crystal Maiden’s Crystal Nova and Frostbite slows, while his Firefly provides high mobility to dodge Freezing Field and close the gap for a Sticky Napalm combo.
Tip: Use Flamebreak right after CM casts Crystal Nova to nullify the slow and set up a quick Firefly‑initiated kill.

Mirana

Mirana’s Leap lets her dodge the channel of Freezing Field, and her Arrow can stun CM before she can react with Frostbite. The Moonlight Shadow invisibility also negates CM’s global aura vision, allowing safe split‑pushing.
Tip: Time Leap to land just outside the Freezing Field radius, then follow with Arrow to lock CM down before she can channel.

Techies

Techies’ Stasis Trap and Remote Mine provide constant zone control that forces CM to stay far from her Arcane Aura radius, cutting her mana regen. The burst from Remote Mine punishes CM’s low HP and can kill her before she finishes a Freezing Field.
Tip: Plant mines near CM’s safe lane spot; when she steps in to cast Frostbite, detonate for a quick kill.

Puck

Puck’s Illusory Orb and Dream Coil give high mobility and crowd‑control that can interrupt Freezing Field and block Frostbite. Waning Rift reduces CM’s mana pool, making her aura and spells fade faster.
Tip: Use Dream Coil to pull CM out of her Freezing Field channel; the damage and silence force her to stop the ultimate.

Drafting Against Crystal Maiden

  • Prioritize heroes with silences or spell interrupts (e.g., Silencer, Puck, Bane).
  • Pick high‑mobility heroes that can dodge Freezing Field (e.g., Mirana, Anti‑Mage).
  • Include lane‑dominant heroes that can out‑farm her early and force mana loss (e.g., Razor, Lifestealer).
  • Consider bans that remove strong global mana‑regen counters (e.g., Keeper of the Light).

Laning Against Crystal Maiden

  • Harass her with right‑clicks or abilities that force her to use Frostbite defensively, draining her mana.
  • Attack when she is out of Arcane Aura range (beyond 1200 units) to minimize her mana regen.
  • Punish her after she casts Crystal Nova; the cooldown leaves her vulnerable to a quick kill.
  • Use lane creeps to block her Frostbite line of sight, forcing her to waste the spell.

Itemizing Against Crystal Maiden

Eul's Scepter — provides a reliable way to purge Frostbite and interrupt the channel of Freezing Field.
Manta Style — dispels the slow from Crystal Nova and creates illusion confusion that can dodge Freezing Field damage.
Black King Bar — grants magic immunity, nullifying all of CM’s spell damage during team fights.
Diffusal Blade — burns her mana directly, crippling her Arcane Aura and limiting her ability usage.

dark-seer.name: Dark Seer
dark-seer.guideHtml:
Dark Seer is a high‑mobility initiator and escape hero whose toolkit revolves around moving allies and enemies with Surge, Vacuum, and Ion Shell. In the current 7.41 meta his pub win rate sits at 48.7% over 109 k ranked games, making him a solid but not dominant pick.

How to Play Dark Seer

Laning Phase

  • Surge early levels on a melee off‑lane carry (e.g., Bristleback or Mars) to grant them instant max speed and untargetable movement, allowing safe farm and aggressive harassment.
  • Use Ion Shell on yourself or the carry to punish enemy heroes that try to engage; the damage‑over‑time scales with your Intelligence and works well against melee heroes like Pudge or Tiny.
  • Vacuum on a 2‑mana‑cost level can be saved for a surprise pull on a lone support (e.g., Phoenix) to set up a kill with your lane partner.
  • Prioritize last‑hitting while maintaining lane equilibrium; Dark Seer’s attack speed scales with Intelligence via Quick Wit, so a few early kills snowball his damage.
  • Watch for the toughest match‑ups (Phoenix, Ember Spirit, Templar Assassin, Marci, Pudge, Tiny) – play extra conservatively and look for ganks from your mid‑lane.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 6: unlock Wall of Replica and start creating lanes for split‑push or to block high‑damage heroes (e.g., Queen of Pain).
  • Group with your core and use Surge + Vacuum on enemy team‑fights; the combo grants instant burst damage and disables, especially effective against heroes that rely on mobility (e.g., Puck, Tusk).
  • Secure Roshan with Ion Shell on your tank and a well‑timed Surge on the melee carry; the extra damage from Ion Shell often turns the fight.
  • Rotate to lanes where your Wall of Replica can trap squishy back‑line heroes; this is especially potent against easy match‑ups like Queen of Pain and Disruptor.

Late Game

  • Win condition: force team fights where you can chain Surge → Vacuum → Wall of Replica on the enemy back‑line, then let your carry clean up with the replicas.
  • Positioning: stay just behind your front‑line; you need to be close enough to cast Vacuum but far enough to avoid being instantly killed by burst heroes (e.g., Tiny, Ember Spirit).
  • Losing the game: over‑extending without a Wall or failing to protect your Surge target lets the enemy’s disables (Phoenix’s Supernova, Pudge’s Meat Hook) turn fights in their favor.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango + Healing Salve — sustain in a tough off‑lane.
  • Iron Branch ×2 — cheap stats; can later be used for a Magic Wand.
  • Observer Ward — vision to avoid ganks from Phoenix or Ember Spirit.
  • Quelling Blade — helps secure early creep kills.

Core Items

  • Arcane Boots — reliable mana for frequent Vacuum and Ion Shell casts.
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Wall of Replica to a larger, longer‑lasting wall, crucial against heroes like Pudge and Tiny.
  • Force Staff — gives you an extra escape and lets you reposition Surge targets into Vacuum range.
  • Guardian Greaves — provides burst heal and magic resistance, essential when facing bursty heroes (Queen of Pain, Ember Spirit).

Situational Items

  • Black King Bar — needed against heavy magical burst (Phoenix, Puck).
  • Lotus Orb — reflects targeted disables such as Pudge’s Hook or Tiny’s Toss.
  • Scythe of Vyse — additional hard‑disable when you lack enough Vacuum casts.
  • Pipe of Insight — mitigates magic damage from Ember Spirit and Disruptor.
  • Mekansm — extra team sustain in fights where you’re the primary initiator.

Common Mistakes

  • Casting Vacuum without a follow‑up Surge – enemies often escape; always pair Vacuum with a Surge on a teammate.
  • Over‑relying on Wall of Replica – the wall has a limited duration; use it to trap key heroes, not as a permanent barrier.
  • Neglecting Ion Shell on yourself – many players only shield carries, forgetting the self‑damage helps clear enemy creep waves and punishes melee initiators.
  • Positioning too far forward – Dark Seer is squishy; being caught by burst heroes (Tiny, Ember Spirit) before you can cast your combo leads to early deaths.

FAQ

Is Dark Seer good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 48.7% win rate across over 109 k ranked matches, Dark Seer is a viable initiator. He shines against easy match‑ups like Queen of Pain (60.3% win) and struggles more against Phoenix (30.9% win), so pick him when you can avoid those counters.

What lane does Dark Seer play?

Dark Seer is typically played in the off‑lane (safe lane for Radiant, dire’s safe lane) where he can use Surge on a melee carry and farm safely. He can also be flexed to solo mid if the team needs extra initiation, but off‑lane remains the meta choice.

Who counters Dark Seer?

The toughest counters are Phoenix, Ember Spirit, Templar Assassin, Marci, Pudge, and Tiny, all of which have win rates under 43% against him. Their burst, disables, or high‑damage spells can punish Dark Seer’s low survivability if you fail to land Vacuum‑Surge combos.
dark-seer.counterHtml:
Dark Seer thrives on early‑game lane dominance and team‑fight control, using Vacuum + Ion Shell combos to burst heroes and Surge to grant allies unstoppable mobility. To shut him down you must deny his ability to pull multiple targets together and punish his low early health pool before his wall and replicas become viable.

Why These Heroes Beat Dark Seer

Phoenix

Phoenix’s Supernova forces Dark Seer to choose between pulling a massive, untargetable unit or losing the combo, while Sun Ray provides constant damage that outpaces Dark Seer’s early burst.
Tip: Position Phoenix near the lane so a well‑timed Sun Ray can hit Dark Seer when he attempts a Vacuum on your carry.

Ember Spirit

Ember’s Sleight of Fist can dodge Vacuum and instantly return damage, and his Flame Guard gives magic immunity that nullifies the burst from Ion Shell.
Tip: Initiate with Sleight of Fist right after Dark Seer casts Surge on you to punish his short‑duration mobility boost.

Templar Assassin

TA’s Refraction blocks the initial Ion Shell damage, and her Psi Blades give high burst that can kill Dark Seer before he can set up a wall. Her Meld also makes her invisible to Vacuum pulls.
Tip: Save Meld for the moment Dark Seer casts Vacuum on your lane partner; you’ll emerge unharmed and can counter‑engage.

Marci

Marci’s Rebound provides a quick escape from Vacuum, while her Side‑Swipe and Dispose deliver massive physical damage that overwhelms Dark Seer’s modest early HP.
Tip: Use Rebound to jump out of the pull radius, then immediately Dispose the stunned Dark Seer for a kill.

Pudge

Pudge’s Meat Hook can yank Dark Seer out of his own Vacuum zone, and Rot applies constant magic damage that stacks with Ion Shell, forcing Dark Seer to retreat.
Tip: Hook Dark Seer just after he casts Surge on an ally; the hook interrupts the speed boost and leaves him vulnerable to a follow‑up Rot burst.

Drafting Against Dark Seer

  • Prioritize heroes with strong magic immunity or burst (e.g., Phoenix, Ember Spirit, Templar Assassin).
  • Pick mobile heroes that can dodge Vacuum and outrun Surge (e.g., Marci, Pudge).
  • Include at least one hero with reliable crowd‑control that isn’t a point‑target pull (e.g., Lion, Shadow Shaman).
  • Consider banning heroes that synergize with his wall, such as strong illusion‑based lineups.

Laning Against Dark Seer

  • Trade early when his Ion Shell is on cooldown; his damage spikes are short‑lived.
  • Harass him with ranged attacks or spells while he is channeling Vacuum—the cast time leaves him vulnerable.
  • Force him to use Surge on a non‑essential unit; the buff expires quickly and gives you a window to disengage.
  • Keep a creep wave near the tower to limit his ability to pull multiple heroes into a single Vacuum.

Itemizing Against Dark Seer

Ghost Scepter — grants magic immunity, nullifying the burst from Ion Shell and Sun Ray.
Eul’s Scepter — cyclones Dark Seer, interrupting his Vacuum and buying time for your team to reposition.
Black King Bar — prevents the stun from Vacuum and the damage from Ion Shell during team fights.
Manta Style — creates illusions that split the focus of Vacuum, reducing the effectiveness of his combo.

dark-willow.name: Dark Willow
dark-willow.guideHtml:
Dark Willow is a versatile support‑nuker who excels at disabling teamfights and creating chaos with her crowd‑control toolkit. In the current 7.41 meta she sits at a 48.1% win rate over 190,439 ranked games, making her a solid but not dominant pick. Her strength lies in burst lockdown and survivability, while she struggles against heroes that can out‑maneuver or out‑damage her early game.

How to Play Dark Willow

Laning Phase

  • Use Cursed Crown on the enemy off‑lane hero to force a stun and secure early kills or zone them away from farm.
  • Drop Bramble Maze defensively when the enemy dives; the 500 AoE roots and damage deter aggression and protect your carry.
  • Keep Pixie Dust active while staying in lane to boost health/mana regen, especially when you are frequently targeted.
  • Pair Shadow Realm with a short attack on a low‑HP enemy; the untargetable window lets you dodge harass and finish the kill with the bonus range.
  • Anticipate hard‑disables from matchups like Treant Protector or Brewmaster—play more conservatively and rely on Bramble Maze to create safe spacing.

Mid Game

  • Power spike: Level 6 unlocks Terrorize, a game‑changing ultimate that can force enemies to run toward their fountain. Use it after a successful Cursed Crown combo to turn fights.
  • Secure vision around Roshan and enemy jungle; Bramble Maze can block enemy rotations and protect your team while you set up picks.
  • Look for opportunities to Bedlam in clustered fights; the rapid auto‑attacks amplify damage on heroes already stunned by Cursed Crown or Terrorize.
  • Prioritize ganking lanes where you have lane advantage (e.g., against Witch Doctor or Weaver) and force early tower pressure.

Late Game

  • Win condition: lock down high‑damage cores with Cursed Crown + Terrorize while your team focuses them down.
  • Position near the backline; use Shadow Realm to dodge initiations and re‑engage with a long‑range attack.
  • Avoid extended straight‑line fights against heroes like Nyx Assassin or Pugna who can burst you before you land a stun; instead, look for pick‑offs with Bramble Maze and Bedlam.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango + Healing Salve — sustain in lane against harass.
  • Observer Ward — early vision to avoid ganks from Brewmaster or Treant.
  • Clarity — keep mana for frequent Cursed Crown casts.

Core Items

  • Tranquil Boots — mobility and constant HP regen, synergizes with Pixie Dust.
  • Glimmer Cape — additional untargetable safety to complement Shadow Realm.
  • Aghanim's Shard — reduces Cursed Crown cooldown, increasing stun frequency.
  • Eul's Scepter — extra disable and self‑save; works well with Shadow Realm for double untargetable windows.

Situational Items

  • Force Staff — escape from Treant Protector’s overgrowth or Brewmaster’s stun.
  • Ghost Scepter — against right‑click heavy heroes like Luna or Faceless Void.
  • Lotus Orb — reflect single‑target spells from Nyx Assassin or Pugna.
  • Aeon Disk — survive burst from Ringmaster or Dazzle’s Shallow Grave.
  • Scythe of Vyse — additional hard‑lock on slippery heroes such as Storm Spirit.

Common Mistakes

  • Spamming Bedlam while the enemy still has Terrorize cooldown, leaving you vulnerable to counter‑engage.
  • Using Cursed Crown on a single target without coordinating Bramble Maze or Terrorize, resulting in wasted stuns.
  • Neglecting vision in the mid‑late game, allowing enemy initiators like Brewmaster to catch you out of position.
  • Overcommitting with Shadow Realm early; the bonus attack range is modest and can be wasted if you’re not near a killable enemy.

FAQ

Is Dark Willow good in the current patch?

Yes. Dark Willow sits at a 48.1% win rate in patch 7.41, making her a viable support pick. She shines against heroes like Witch Doctor and Weaver (61.8% and 61.0% win rates) but struggles versus hard‑disablers such as Treant Protector and Brewmaster (both ~33% win).

What lane does Dark Willow play?

Dark Willow is typically played as a position 5 support in the safe lane, pairing with a core to provide early disables and lane control. She can also roam to the off‑lane for aggressive Cursed Crown plays against vulnerable heroes.

Who counters Dark Willow?

The toughest matchups are against Treant Protector, Brewmaster, Ringmaster, Nyx Assassin, Pugna, and Dazzle, where her win rates drop below 40%. These heroes either out‑range her disables or burst her before she can land a stun. Using early vision and items like Force Staff or Lotus Orb can mitigate their impact.
dark-willow.counterHtml:
Dark Willow thrives on burst crowd‑control and surprise damage: her Cursed Crown and Bramble Maze lock enemies down while Bedlam and Terrorize dump massive magic damage. The key to shutting her down is to stay mobile, purge or out‑range her disables, and punish the moments she must retreat into Shadow Realm.

Why These Heroes Beat Dark Willow

Treant Protector

Treant’s Nature’s Grasp and Leech Seed provide instant, long‑duration roots and sustain that outlast the brief stun window of Cursed Crown, while his Living Armor blocks the damage from Bramble Maze. Tip: keep a Nature’s Grasp on Dark Willow when she tries to engage; the root forces her to waste Shadow Realm on a stationary target.

Brewmaster

Brewmaster’s Storm Hammer and Primal Split give him reliable stun and split‑push pressure that forces Dark Willow to waste her limited disables. Tip: initiate with Storm Hammer to lock her before she can cast Bramble Maze, then quickly Primal Split to overwhelm her with multiple targets.

Ringmaster (Ring of Templar Assassin)

Ringmaster’s high burst damage and Manta Style‑based evasion let him dodge Bramble Maze roots and survive Cursed Crown’s stun, while his Mana Burn punishes Dark Willow’s low mana pool. Tip: use Manta Style to break the root and instantly counter‑attack with a Mana Burn combo.

Nyx Assassin

Nyx’s Spiked Carapace reflects the magic damage from Bramble Maze and Bedlam, and his Vendetta provides true‑strike invisibility that bypasses Dark Willow’s vision‑dependent abilities. Tip: wait for Dark Willow to drop Shadow Realm, then pop Spiked Carapace and follow up with Vendetta for a guaranteed kill.

Pugna

Pugna’s Decrepify amplifies the magic damage Dark Willow deals, turning her own burst against her, while Nether Ward punishes her spellcasting, especially the costly Cursed Crown. Tip: place Nether Ward near the lane; every Cursed Crown cast drains her mana and deals damage back to her.

Drafting Against Dark Willow

  • Prioritize heroes with reliable long‑range stuns or silences (e.g., Lion, Shadow Shaman).
  • Pick mobile heroes that can dodge Bramble Maze and Cursed Crown (e.g., Anti‑Mage, Ember Spirit).
  • Include strong magic damage mitigators or purgers (e.g., Oracle, Dazzle).
  • Consider early game lane dominators that can force her out of lane before she gets Bedlam/Terrorize levels.

Laning Against Dark Willow

  • Harass her before she hits level 6; she is vulnerable without Shadow Realm and Bedlam.
  • Trade when she attempts to cast Bramble Maze—the 0.3 s delay gives you a window to attack the bramble center and force a miss.
  • Use ranged harass or lane creeps to force her to use Pixie Dust early, draining her regen advantage.
  • Punish the cooldown of Cursed Crown; after a stun lands, she is forced to retreat and loses lane presence.

Itemizing Against Dark Willow

Eul's Scepter of Divinity — provides a 2.5 s cyclone to dodge Bramble Maze roots and set up a counter‑spell during her Shadow Realm.

Glimmer Cape — grants temporary invisibility, allowing you to slip past her Cursed Crown and Bramble Maze while she is on cooldown.

Black King Bar — makes you immune to the magic damage from Bedlam and the stun from Cursed Crown, letting you stay in fights.

Force Staff — instantly removes you from the 500‑unit Bramble Maze radius and can pull you out of Terrorize’s fear zone.

Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target spells like Cursed Crown back at Dark Willow and removes debuffs such as Bramble Maze root.

dawnbreaker.name: Dawnbreaker
dawnbreaker.guideHtml:
Dawnbreaker is a durable, semi‑carry hero who excels at initiating fights and sustaining through her hammer‑based toolkit. With a 51.8 % win rate on the latest 7.41 ranked data, she sits comfortably in the meta as a reliable front‑liner, especially on the safe lane.

How to Play Dawnbreaker

Laning Phase

  • Use Starbreaker (first two spins) to harass melee opponents and secure last hits while staying out of enemy range.
  • Pull the hammer back with Converge to close the gap on ranged heroes and force them to miss CS.
  • When the enemy pulls creep aggro, unleash the third spin of Starbreaker for a stun, creating space for a safe tower dive or escape.
  • Trade with heroes like Death Prophet or Vengeful Spirit early; the data shows a >60 % win rate against them, so play aggressively.
  • Avoid extended trades against Chen, Treant, or Morphling—your hammer’s cooldown leaves you vulnerable to their disables and burst.

Mid Game

  • Aim for a Solar Guardian at 6 minutes to grant daylight over a contested area; the vision and heal boost team fights and tower pushes.
  • Prioritize farming a second Starbreaker spin upgrade (if using talent) to increase stun duration, giving you a clear power spike around 12 minutes.
  • Join ganks with Celestial Hammer → Converge combo: fling the hammer onto a target, then recall it to pull enemies together for a team‑wide stun.
  • Target back‑line heroes (e.g., Lina, Shadow Shaman) after you’ve secured a stun; your damage plus the heal from Solar Guardian makes you hard to kill.

Late Game

  • Use Solar Guardian to create daylight over high‑ground objectives; the constant pulses heal allies and pressure enemy heroes who lack true sight.
  • Position near the front line but keep Celestial Hammer ready to pull out squishy carries; a well‑timed recall can turn team fights.
  • Losing the game often comes from over‑committing without Solar Guardian support or getting caught by strong disables from heroes like Bane and Alchemist.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane against harassment.
  • Healing Salve — quick HP recovery after early skirmishes.
  • Quelling Blade — easier last‑hits on creeps and jungle.
  • Stout Shield — mitigates damage from aggressive melee opponents.

Core Items

  • Radiance — synergy with hammer swings; provides constant damage and vision during daylight.
  • Black King Bar — essential against heavy magical disables from Bane, Alchemist, and Morphling.
  • Mekansm / Guardian Greaves — amplifies the heal from Solar Guardian and gives team survivability.
  • Aghanim’s Shard (optional) — reduces Celestial Hammer cooldown, increasing poke and pick‑off potential.

Situational Items

  • Satanic — huge survivability against burst from Chen and Treant.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target disables from Bane and Alchemist.
  • Blade Mail — punishes heroes who focus you, especially Morphling.
  • Heaven’s Halberd — disables high‑damage right‑click carries like Morphling and Phantom Lancer.
  • Shiva’s Guard — armor and aura against physical burst, also slows enemy movement for better hammer hits.

Common Mistakes

  • Holding the hammer too long – waiting for the full 2‑second pause on Celestial Hammer wastes damage and leaves you vulnerable.
  • Ignoring daylight – failing to use Solar Guardian early reduces your sustain and vision, especially against heroes with invisibility or high ground.
  • Over‑extending without BKB – engaging after a Starbreaker stun without BKB lets Bane, Alchemist, or Morphling lock you down.
  • Mis‑timing Converge – pulling the hammer when enemies are out of range results in a wasted pull and a long cooldown.

FAQ

Is Dawnbreaker good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 51.8 % win rate across over 300 k recent ranked games, Dawnbreaker is a solid pick, especially on the safe lane where her durability and initiation shine.

What lane does Dawnbreaker play?

She is most commonly played as a carry on the safe lane, though she can also be flexed to off‑lane when a team needs extra durability and frontline presence.

Who counters Dawnbreaker?

The toughest matchups are Chen, Treant Protector, Morphling, Bane, Alchemist, and Kez (win rates below 40 %). These heroes either out‑scale her durability or provide disables that nullify her hammer‑based initiations.
dawnbreaker.counterHtml:
Dawnbreaker’s strength lies in her relentless melee presence, burst‑damage + stun combo from Starbreaker and the zone‑control of Solar Guardian. To shut her down you must deny her the close‑range engagements she thrives on and exploit the long cooldowns and reliance on positioning of her abilities.

Why These Heroes Beat Dawnbreaker

Chen

Chen’s Hand of God and Holy Persuasion let him keep a neutral creep army at safe distance, denying Dawnbreaker the melee targets she needs for her hammer spin. A practical tip: pull a neutral creep with Penitence onto Dawnbreaker’s path right before she initiates Starbreaker to interrupt the spin and force a miss.

Treant Protector

Treant’s Living Armor and Nature’s Guise give him high survivability and invisibility, making it hard for Dawnbreaker to land a reliable stun. Tip: place a Leech Seed on Dawnbreaker’s hammer‑return path; the damage over time punishes her when she tries to retrieve the hammer with Converge.

Morphling

Morphling’s Morph and Waveform let him outrange Dawnbreaker’s melee reach and instantly reposition after a Starbreaker stun. Tip: keep Adaptive Strike on cooldown and use Morph to swap attribute boosts, then burst Dawnbreaker the moment she lands her hammer‑slam.

Bane

Bane’s Nightmare and Fiend’s Grip lock Dawnbreaker in place, preventing her from using Solar Guardian or the hammer‑return mechanic. Tip: chain‑cast Nightmare right after Dawnbreaker’s Starbreaker animation finishes; the stun window is tiny, so timing is crucial.

Alchemist

Alchemist’s Acid Spray applies a strong slow that hampers Dawnbreaker’s ability to chase, while Unstable Concoction can be detonated to burst her before she lands a Starbreaker. Tip: buy Aghanim’s Shard for the extra stun on Acid Spray and use it to interrupt her hammer‑throw from Celestial Hammer.

Drafting Against Dawnbreaker

  • Prioritize heroes with strong disengage or long‑range disables (e.g., Bane, Chen, Treant).
  • Pick heroes that can sustain through her burst (high HP regeneration or heal shields).
  • Ban heroes with strong early game melee dominance that complement Dawnbreaker’s aggression.
  • Include at least one true‑sight or invisibility‑counter (e.g., Bounty Hunter, Slark) to punish her reliance on vision from Solar Guardian.

Laning Against Dawnbreaker

  • Trade when her Starbreaker cooldown is up; she is vulnerable during the wind‑up.
  • Harass her before she can pull the hammer back with Converge, forcing a missed return.
  • Force her to use Celestial Hammer on a distant target; the 2‑second pause leaves her exposed.
  • Exploit the early‑game window before Break of Dawn grants her daytime bonuses.

Itemizing Against Dawnbreaker

Ghost Scepter — blocks her melee attacks and the final stun of Starbreaker.
Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — cyclone removes her from the fight, cancelling Solar Guardian pulses.
Lotus Orb – reflects her stun back and removes the slow from Celestial Hammer’s trail.
Heaven’s Halberd — disarms her, nullifying the hammer swing that powers both damage and stun.

dazzle.name: Dazzle
dazzle.guideHtml:
Dazzle remains a staple support in the current meta, offering unparalleled survivability with Shallow Grave and team‑wide sustain through Shadow Wave. With a 50.6 % win rate across 181 k recent ranked games, he sits comfortably in the mid‑tier of supports on patch 7.41.

How to Play Dazzle

Laning Phase

  • Use Poison Touch on enemy creeps to secure lane equilibrium and harass heroes; the slow refreshes on each attack, making it a potent tool against melee supports.
  • Drop Shallow Grave on the carry or yourself when you anticipate burst from heroes like Lion (45 % win‑rate vs Dazzle) to negate early deaths.
  • Cast Shadow Wave immediately after a kill or when your core takes damage; the heal also buffs you, allowing aggressive trades.
  • Apply Weave via any ability to increase your lane partner’s armor and reduce the enemy’s, especially effective against physical‑damage heroes such as Slardar (41.4 % win‑rate).
  • Keep an eye on enemy rotations; if a Shadow Demon or Void Spirit ganks, prioritize a quick Shallow Grave and a defensive Poison Touch slow.

Mid Game

  • Power spike: Level 6 Nothl Projection – use it to scout, cast spells safely, or initiate fights while staying untargetable.
  • Secure vision around Roshan and high‑ground jungle; Dazzle’s Nothl Projection can safely place wards and deward.
  • Group with your cores for early team fights; a well‑timed Shallow Grave on a diving carry can turn a 5‑vs‑4 into a win.
  • Prioritize protecting squishy damage dealers (e.g., Skywrath Mage, 63.7 % win‑rate vs Dazzle) with Shallow Grave and Weave armor buffs.

Late Game

  • Win condition: keep your carries alive with Shallow Grave and sustain them with Shadow Wave; Dazzle’s armor/shield from Weave becomes decisive in prolonged fights.
  • Position near the backline; Nothl Projection lets you dodge enemy disables while still casting Shallow Grave on allies.
  • Lose the game if you over‑extend without Shallow Grave—hard‑kill heroes like Gyrocopter (44.6 % win‑rate) can burst you quickly.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane while you focus on casting spells.
  • Healing Salve — emergency self‑heal for early skirmishes.
  • Observer Ward — vision to avoid ganks from mobile heroes like Void Spirit.
  • Clarity — mana for frequent Poison Touch and Shadow Wave usage.

Core Items

  • Tranquil Boots — movement speed and passive regen to stay mobile for Shallow Grave drops.
  • Mekansm — provides an additional burst heal and armor, synergizing with Weave.
  • Glimmer Cape — defensive save for yourself or a carry when you cannot fit Shallow Grave in time.
  • Aghanim’s Shard (optional) — upgrades Poison Touch to a stronger slow, useful against high‑mobility heroes.

Situational Items

  • Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — extra disable and self‑save against Pugna’s Nether Blast.
  • Force Staff — reposition allies into Shallow Grave or escape from Gyrocopter’s Rocket Barrage.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects targeted disables from Lion and Shadow Demon.
  • Guardian Greaves — upgrade from Mekansm when you need both armor and a strong team heal.
  • Scythe of Vyse — hard‑disable for heroes that otherwise out‑scale you, such as Shadow Demon.

Common Mistakes

  • Saving Shallow Grave for yourself – opponents often focus your core; use it on them instead.
  • Over‑using Poison Touch on creeps – you lose mana and miss opportunities to harass enemy heroes.
  • Neglecting vision – without wards, Dazzle cannot place Shallow Grave safely against mobile threats like Void Spirit.
  • Late‑game positioning – staying too far forward makes you vulnerable to burst from Gyrocopter and Pugna.

FAQ

Is Dazzle good in the current patch?

Yes. Dazzle holds a 50.6 % win rate across 181 k recent ranked matches, making him a reliable support choice on patch 7.41.

What lane does Dazzle play?

Dazzle is typically a support in the safe lane (position 5) but can also be flexed to off‑lane (position 4) when a strong lane partner is needed.

Who counters Dazzle?

Hard‑kill, burst heroes such as Slardar, Shadow Demon, Void Spirit, Pugna, Gyrocopter, and Lion have sub‑45 % win rates against Dazzle, exploiting his reliance on Shallow Grave and armor buffs.
dazzle.counterHtml:
Dazzle’s strength lies in his survivability tools—Shallow Grave and the armor‑shifting Weave—combined with strong lane sustain from Shadow Wave. To shut him down you must pressure him before he can lock down an ally, strip his armor buffs, and force his projection to be wasted.

Why These Heroes Beat Dazzle

Slardar

Slardar’s Amplify Damage instantly reduces enemy armor, nullifying Dazzle’s Weave armor boost and making his Wave‑heal less effective. Use Slardar’s Sprint to close the gap before Dazzle can cast Shallow Grave, then burst the target with Corrosive Haze‑enhanced attacks. Tip: keep Slardar’s Bash ready to interrupt Dazzle’s Nothl Projection channel.

Shadow Demon

Shadow Demon’s Disruption can pull Dazzle out of his projection tether, forcing a vulnerable return to his body, while Soul Catcher amplifies damage taken, punishing Dazzle’s low‑damage spells. Pair Disruption with a stun from an ally to prevent Dazzle from re‑casting Shallow Grave on a teammate. Tip: time Disruption just as Dazzle finishes a Wave to maximize the damage spike.

Void Spirit

Void Spirit’s Aether Remnant silences Dazzle and blocks his ability casts, preventing Shallow Grave and Wave from being used in fights. His Astral Step lets him dodge the initial Poison Touch and close in for a quick Resonant Pulse burst before Dazzle can react. Tip: chain Astral Step with a stun to keep Dazzle locked down while his projection is on cooldown.

Pugna

Pugna’s Nether Ward punishes Dazzle for casting spells, draining his mana and forcing him to rely on items rather than abilities. Decrepify reduces Dazzle’s attack and spell damage, making his Wave and Projection far less threatening. Tip: place Nether Ward near the lane’s pull‑creep spot to punish Dazzle’s early Wave spam.

Gyrocopter

Gyrocopter’s Flak Cannon and Rocket Barrage apply consistent AoE damage that overwhelms Dazzle’s limited burst, while Homing Missile can target Dazzle’s body during Projection, forcing a premature return. Gyrocopter’s Call Down also provides a burst of armor that counters Weave’s armor reduction on enemies. Tip: keep Gyrocopter’s Rocket Barrage active when Dazzle attempts a Shallow Grave on a teammate to force a trade.

Drafting Against Dazzle

  • Prioritize heroes with armor‑reduction or silencing tools (e.g., Slardar, Shadow Demon, Void Spirit).
  • Pick strong early‑game damage dealers who can force Dazzle to waste Shallow Grave.
  • Include at least one hero with a reliable stun or disable to interrupt Nothl Projection.
  • Avoid picking multiple high‑mana‑spending supports that could be easily shut down by Nether Ward.

Laning Against Dazzle

  • Harass him before he lands his first Poison Touch; his early damage is low.
  • Force Dazzle to use Shallow Grave on a creep or himself, then trade while the cooldown is up.
  • Attack his body during Projection; the tether prevents him from casting, leaving him vulnerable.
  • Pressure his support items (e.g., Arcane Boots) to limit his Wave sustain.

Itemizing Against Dazzle

Manta Style — breaks Shallow Grave and dispels Weave armor buffs.
Diffusal Blade — burns mana, reducing Dazzle’s ability spam and making Projection costly.
Heaven's Halberd — disarms Dazzle, nullifying his Poison Touch and Wave damage.
Eul's Scepter — cyclone Dazzle out of his projection, forcing a return to his body and delaying Shallow Grave.

death-prophet.name: Death Prophet
death-prophet.guideHtml:
Death Prophet is a ranged magical damage dealer who excels at pushing lanes and teamfighting with her sustained AoE spells. In the current 7.41 meta she sits at a 47.3% win rate over 147,735 ranked games, making her a solid but not dominant pick. She thrives when she can get early farm and transition into a high‑damage, lane‑clearing core.

How to Play Death Prophet

Laning Phase

  • Spirit Siphon early on to harass and sustain against melee off‑laners; the heal scales with your damage, letting you stay in lane longer.
  • Silence can be used to block enemy spell casts (e.g., Clockwerk’s Battery Assault) and secure kills when paired with a support’s stun.
  • Prioritize Crypt Swarm on creep waves to accelerate tower damage and gain lane control, especially against ranged heroes like Sniper who lack early burst.
  • Trade aggressively against heroes you have an advantage over (e.g., Shadow Shaman, Slardar) and play more passively versus the toughest matchups (Sniper, Clockwerk, Dawnbreaker).
  • Keep an eye on your mana pool; use Spirit Siphon sparingly until you have a bottle or early mana regen items.

Mid Game

  • Hit the Exorcism power spike at level 6 + 120 intelligence; start joining team fights to provide continuous AoE damage.
  • Split‑push with Crypt Swarm while your team applies pressure elsewhere; the ability’s tower‑damage scales with your attack damage, making you a formidable pusher.
  • Target enemy backlines in fights—Exorcism and Spirit Siphon together can quickly melt squishy carries like Sniper if you have vision.
  • Secure vision around Roshan and high‑ground jungle paths; a well‑placed Silence can shut down enemy initiations from Spirit Breaker or Hoodwink.

Late Game

  • Win condition: force the enemy to defend multiple lanes simultaneously with relentless Crypt Swarm pressure while your team picks off key heroes in fights using Exorcine + Silence.
  • Positioning: stay just behind your front line; Exorcism is vulnerable to disables, so avoid standing directly in front of heroes like Dawnbreaker or Snapfire who can stun you.
  • Lose the game if you get caught without Exorcism active and the enemy initiates with hard crowd control (e.g., Clockwerk’s Hookshot + Battery Assault).

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane, especially against harass from Sniper or Spirit Breaker.
  • Healing Salve — emergency health for early trades.
  • Faerie Fire — cheap burst to finish low‑HP enemies when using Silence.
  • Observer Ward — vision to avoid ganks from mobile heroes like Hoodwink.

Core Items

  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Exorcism to fire additional spirits, dramatically increasing damage and tower‑clear speed.
  • Black King Bar — essential against heavy disable lineups (Clockwerk, Dawnbreaker, Snapfire).
  • Mekansm — provides team‑wide burst heal, synergizes with your lane‑sustain and keeps you alive in fights.
  • Radiance — amplifies Crypt Swarm and Exorcism damage, turning you into a true late‑game pusher.

Situational Items

  • Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — a safe escape from heroes like Spirit Breaker and a setup for Silence on key targets.
  • Shiva’s Guard — armor and AoE slow against physical heroes (Sniper, Slardar) who try to kite you.
  • Scythe of Vyse — additional hard‑disable when you lack reliable crowd control from allies.
  • Heart of Tarrasque — massive survivability if you are frequently targeted by burst damage.
  • Octarine Core — reduces cooldowns on all abilities, letting you spam Silence and Spirit Siphon more often in prolonged fights.

Common Mistakes

  • Spamming Crypt Swarm without mana management – leads to being out‑of‑mana when a fight breaks out.
  • Using Exorcism without proper positioning – standing too far forward invites disables from Clockwerk or Dawnbreaker, cutting the channel early.
  • Neglecting vision – you rely on long‑range damage; missing wards lets mobile heroes catch you out of position.
  • Building pure damage items – ignoring survivability (BKB, Mekansm) makes you an easy target for the toughest matchups (Sniper, Clockwerk).

FAQ

Is Death Prophet good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 47.3% win rate across over 147k ranked games, she is a viable pick, especially on teams that need a strong pusher and AoE damage source.

What lane does Death Prophet play?

Death Prophet is typically played in the safe lane (radiant or dire) as a carry/pusher, allowing her to farm Crypt Swarm and hit her early Spirit Siphon trades safely.

Who counters Death Prophet?

The toughest matchups are Sniper, Clockwerk, Dawnbreaker, Spirit Breaker, Hoodwink, and Snapfire, where her win rates drop below 38% (e.g., 29.5% vs Sniper). These heroes either outrange her or bring hard disables that shut down her channelled spells.
death-prophet.counterHtml:
Death Prophet’s strength lies in her sustained magical damage — Crypt Swarm and Exorcism can melt teamfights if she stays alive, while Silence and Spirit Siphon give her lane dominance and healing. The key to shutting her down is to deny her the time and mana needed to build up those damage‑over‑time spells, either by forcing early deaths or by constantly disrupting her channeling.

Why These Heroes Beat Death Prophet

Sniper

Sniper’s extreme range lets him harass Death Prophet before she can close the gap for Crypt Swarm or Exorcium, and his Assassinate can finish her off when she is low on health. Tip: Keep a safe distance, use Take Aim to increase vision, and punish any attempt by Death Prophet to use Silence—the long cast time makes her vulnerable to a quick Assassinate.

Clockwerk

Clockwerk’s Hookshot and Power Cogs create a mobile cage that isolates Death Prophet, preventing her from positioning for Exorcism and cutting off her escape routes. Tip: Initiate with Power Cogs as soon as Death Prophet steps into range; the stun and slow force her to waste mana on Silence while you burst her down.

Dawnbreaker

Dawnbreaker’s Starbreaker provides a reliable stun and burst damage that can interrupt Death Prophet’s channeling, and her Celestial Blessing grants survivability against the magical damage of Exorcism. Tip: Engage with Starbreaker the moment Death Prophet starts Exorcism—the stun ends the channel and the follow‑up damage often kills her before she can heal.

Spirit Breaker

Spirit Breaker’s Charge of Darkness closes the distance instantly, denying Death Prophet the space she needs for Crypt Swarm and forcing her to use Silence defensively. His Greater Bash also interrupts Exorcism and adds burst. Tip: Time the charge to hit her just as she begins Exorcism; the stun cancels the spell and the subsequent bash can finish her off.

Hoodwink

Hoodwink’s Acorn Shot and Bushwhack provide reliable poke and a hard root that stops Death Prophet from moving or channeling. The root also prevents her from retreating to safety, making her an easy target for follow‑up damage. Tip: Land Bushwhack when Death Prophet tries to cast Silence—the root disables the spell and forces her to waste mana on a failed cast.

Drafting Against Death Prophet

  • Prioritize heroes with long‑range harass or hard disables (e.g., Sniper, Clockwerk, Hoodwink).
  • Pick mobile initiators who can close distance quickly (Spirit Breaker, Dawnbreaker).
  • Include at least one true‑damage or magic‑resist item core (e.g., Hurricane Pike, Black King Bar).
  • Consider banning heroes that give her safe farm or mana sustain (e.g., Shadow Shaman).

Laning Against Death Prophet

  • Harass aggressively with ranged attacks; force her to use Silence early, draining her mana.
  • Trade when her Crypt Swarm is on cooldown—she is vulnerable to burst damage.
  • Punish her after she casts Spirit Siphon; the link provides her with health, so a quick kill after the cast wastes that heal.
  • Keep the lane fluid; avoid static positioning that lets her land Crypt Swarm on multiple creeps.

Itemizing Against Death Prophet

Black King Bar — blocks Silence and the magic damage from Exorcism, letting you stay in fights.
Hurricane Pike — gives you range to safely poke and an escape tool when she tries to close in for Crypt Swarm.
Glimmer Cape — provides magic resistance and invisibility, allowing you to dodge Exorcism damage and reposition.
Scythe of Vyse — a hard disable that can interrupt her channeling and prevent her from healing with Spirit Siphon.

disruptor.name: Disruptor
disruptor.guideHtml:
Disruptor remains a solid support‑disabler in the current 7.41 meta, sitting at a 49.8% win rate across roughly 280 k ranked games. He excels at zone‑control and team‑fight initiation, but his effectiveness swings heavily with lane match‑ups and item timing.

How to Play Disruptor

Laning Phase

  • Use Thunder Strike on the enemy off‑lane hero to harass and force them to miss last hits; the 100 % slow also makes it easy to pull creep aggro.
  • Pair Thunder Strike with a support’s pull (e.g., Vengeful Spirit’s Nether Swap) to chain‑stun lane opponents and secure early kills.
  • Keep Glimpse on cooldown for the first 2 minutes to punish aggressive heroes that over‑extend; the damage component is negligible early, but the reposition is priceless.
  • Against mobile heroes (e.g., Io, Kez) place Kinetic Field near your tower to block their escape routes and force them into your vision.
  • Stack the neutral camp in the lane (if playing safe lane) and use Thunder Strike on the stacked camp to gain extra XP while denying the enemy.

Mid Game

  • Aim for a Static Storm + Kinetic Field combo in mid‑lane or jungle skirmishes; the storm’s scaling damage and silence lock down enemy cores.
  • Prioritize taking Roshan after you have Aghanim’s Scepter (adds a second Static Storm) to secure Aegis and force team fights around your vision.
  • Use Glimpse on enemy heroes that have just used a mobility spell (e.g., Blink, Leap) to pull them back into your Kinetic Field or Static Storm.
  • When you have Electromagnetic Repulsion, position near high‑damage allies; taking a tower hit or a burst from the enemy will trigger the repulsion and give you a surprise AoE burst.

Late Game

  • Win condition: lock down the enemy’s carry with Static Storm + Kinetic Field while your cores dish out damage; the silence and barrier make it nearly impossible for them to escape.
  • Position behind your frontline; a mis‑step that puts you within 250 damage without a ready Electromagnetic Repulsion can let the enemy burst you and lose the fight.
  • Keep Glimpse for the final 4 seconds of a fight to pull a fleeing enemy back into your storm or into your team's AoE spells.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane.
  • Healing Salve — emergency health for early harass.
  • Observer Ward — vision control; essential for early Thunder Strike scouting.
  • Sentry Ward — counter enemy pull/ward.
  • Clarity — mana for spamming Thunder Strike and Kinetic Field.

Core Items

  • Tranquil Boots — movement speed and passive regen to stay mobile for Electromagnetic Repulsion triggers.
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — adds a second Static Storm, dramatically increasing team‑fight control.
  • Glimmer Cape — defensive magic block; lets you survive burst while still being able to cast Thunder Strike and Glimpse.
  • Force Staff — extra repositioning for you or allies to complement Glimpse and Kinetic Field.

Situational Items

  • Ghost Scepter — against right‑click heavy heroes like Drow Ranger or Sven.
  • Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — extra disable and self‑save; works well with Static Storm for double silence.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target spells; useful vs Io’s tether or Chen’s Holy Persuasion.
  • Pipe of Insight — armor and magic resistance when facing heavy magical burst (e.g., Outworld Destroyer).
  • Scythe of Vyse — additional hard‑disable when you need more lockdown than Kinetic Field provides.
  • Aether Lens — extends cast range of Thunder Strike and Glimpse, improving safety and utility.

Common Mistakes

  • Wasting Glimpse on low‑damage targets – the damage cap is tiny early; use it for reposition, not damage.
  • Casting Kinetic Field without vision – enemies can slip through the gap; always place a ward or use Thunder Strike vision first.
  • Holding onto Static Storm for too long – the storm’s damage ramps up, but the silence is immediate; drop it early to lock down key spells.
  • Ignoring Electromagnetic Repulsion – many low‑MMR players forget to position near allies or towers, missing a free AoE burst.

FAQ

Is Disruptor good in the current patch?

Yes. Disruptor sits at a 49.8% win rate on patch 7.41, making him a viable support pick. His control tools are strong in both mid‑game skirmishes and late‑game team fights, especially with Aghanim’s Scepter.

What lane does Disruptor play?

Disruptor is typically played as a hard support in the safe lane (radiant bottom or dire top) to secure early vision and protect the carry. He can also be flexed to off‑lane if a teammate needs a strong disable.

Who counters Disruptor?

The toughest match‑ups are against mobile, high‑damage heroes: Broodmother (28.3% win), Kez (35.9%), Io (37.9%), and Chen (38.6%). Their ability to bypass or out‑range Kinetic Field and Static Storm makes them the biggest threats. Use early vision and Glimpse to limit their mobility, and consider items like Ghost Scepter or Lotus Orb to survive their burst.

The quickest way to neutralize him is to pick heroes that can bypass or punish his static control, stay out of his vision radius, and force him to waste his limited mana on survivability instead of disruption.

Why These Heroes Beat Disruptor

Broodmother’s Spiderlings and Web can constantly move through Disruptor’s static zones, while her ability to hide in the trees denies Thunder Strike vision and makes Glimpse ineffective on a hero that is rarely on the map. Tip: push early lanes and force Disruptor to farm under tower; his lack of mobility makes him vulnerable to spider‑swarm pressure.

Kez

Kez’s Void Rift creates a moving safe zone that can pull allies out of Kinetic Field/Fence, and his Chronosphere (when upgraded) can lock Disruptor in place, nullifying Static Storm’s silence. Tip: time Chronosphere to land just after Disruptor casts Glimpse, preventing the follow‑up combo.

Io

Io’s Relocate gives a permanent “out‑of‑range” escape, rendering Disruptor’s global vision moot, while Tether continuously heals through damage, offsetting Electromagnetic Repulsion’s burst. Tip: keep Tether on a hero with high magic resistance to survive Static Storm’s scaling damage.

Chen

Chen’s Hand of God can instantly purge the silence from Static Storm, and his Holy Persuasion summons creeps that can safely block Kinetic Field/Fence, letting Chen’s team walk through Disruptor’s walls. Tip: use summoned creeps to bait Glimpse, then counter‑attack when Disruptor’s mana is low.

Treant Protector

Treant’s Nature’s Grasp creates a long‑range wall that blocks Kinetic Field/Fence and can be placed behind Disruptor’s position, forcing him to waste Glimpse on a hero that can’t be pulled back. His Living Armor also mitigates the burst from Electromagnetic Repulsion. Tip: plant a tree in the middle of Disruptor’s static storm to reduce its damage radius.

Drafting Against Disruptor

  • Prioritize heroes with global mobility or teleport (Io, Anti‑Mage, Spectre) to outrun Glimpse and Thunder Strike vision.
  • Choose strong silences or dispels (Silencer, Oracle) to counter Static Storm’s silence.
  • Pick tanky or high‑magic‑resistance heroes (Tidehunter, Bristleback) to survive Electromagnetic Repulsion bursts.
  • Ban or avoid heroes that heavily rely on static positioning (e.g., Dark Seer) that synergize with Disruptor’s zones.

Laning Against Disruptor

  • Harass early with ranged attacks; Disruptor’s Thunder Strike has a long cooldown at low levels.
  • Force him to use Glimpse defensively by diving his position; each Glimpse costs mana and reveals his location.
  • Trade when his Kinetic Field is on cooldown—he cannot block escapes or chase.
  • Push the lane when he is low on health; his Electromagnetic Repulsion only triggers after 250 damage, which is hard to reach in early lane.

Itemizing Against Disruptor

Black King Bar — grants magic immunity, nullifying Static Storm’s silence and damage.
Manta Style — dispels the silence and creates illusion copies that survive Glimpse’s instant kill on illusions.
Glimmer Cape — provides temporary invisibility, breaking Thunder Strike vision and allowing safe repositioning.
Aghanim’s Shard (for heroes like Pugna) — adds a spell shield that blocks Glimpse’s damage component.

doom.name: Doom
doom.guideHtml:
Doom remains a high‑impact initiator and disabler in the current meta, sitting at a 46.6% win rate across 210,086 ranked games (OpenDota, July 2026). While his durability and ability to permanently shut down enemy heroes keep him relevant, the patch 7.41 tweaks have nudged him toward a more disciplined, timing‑focused playstyle.

How to Play Doom

Laning Phase

  • Devour early creep‑kill to secure lane equilibrium and deny enemy farm; alt‑cast when you need the cooldown for a later Doom on a hero.
  • Use Scorched Earth to mitigate harass from ranged mid heroes (e.g., Keeper of the Light) while gaining movement speed for safe rotations.
  • Infernal Blade provides a short stun and a burn that scales with the target’s max HP—great for finishing low‑HP heroes or forcing them to retreat.
  • Prioritize a Doom on a high‑damage or heal‑dependent opponent (e.g., Pugna, Bane) as soon as you hit level 6 and have enough mana.
  • Keep an eye on creep stacks; devouring a neutral with a useful ability (e.g., a Nature’s Prophet split‑push beacon) can give you a surprise edge.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 12 + first Doom—look for 2‑v‑2 skirmishes where you can lock a core hero.
  • Secure Roshan with a Doom on the enemy carry; the curse prevents healing from Aegis and Cheese.
  • Use Scorched Earth to chase down mobile heroes (e.g., Morphling, Razor) and to escape ganks; the movement speed boost is crucial for positioning.
  • Rotate to lanes where your Devoured abilities (if you stole a useful spell) can tip the balance—e.g., a stolen Nature’s Prophet teleport for split‑push pressure.

Late Game

  • Win condition: lock the enemy’s primary damage dealer with Doom and force them to die under the burn/curse damage while your team follows up.
  • Position near the front line but keep Scorched Earth ready to mitigate burst damage from heroes like Magnus or Shadow Demon.
  • Over‑extending without a Doom on a high‑impact hero (e.g., Keeper of the Light) often leads to a quick loss; always have a backup disable or escape.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain against harass in solo lane.
  • Healing Salve — quick health top‑up after early skirmishes.
  • Quelling Blade — faster creep last‑hits for early farm.
  • Observer Ward — vision to avoid early ganks while you focus on devouring creeps.

Core Items

  • Blink Dagger — essential for instant Doom initiation on key targets.
  • Heart of Tarrasque — maximizes durability, allowing you to stay in fights while the curse ticks.
  • Black King Bar — prevents silences and disables that can break your Doom (important vs. Keeper of the Light, Bane).
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Scorched Earth to a larger radius and adds a second charge, improving chase and escape potential.

Situational Items

  • Shiva’s Guard — armor and AoE slow counter Morphling and Razor physical damage.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects targeted disables that could purge your Doom (useful vs. Pugna, Magnus).
  • Pipe of Insight — mitigates magical burst from Keeper of the Light, Shadow Demon, and Nature’s Prophet.
  • Assault Cuirass — armor and attack speed help when you need to push lanes after a successful Doom.
  • Mekansm / Guardian Greaves — team‑wide sustain in prolonged fights, especially against high‑heal heroes.

Common Mistakes

  • Rushing Devour on heroes instead of creeps, wasting the cooldown and losing lane control.
  • Using Doom without vision—the curse is useless if the target can escape through fog of war.
  • Over‑committing without Blink; getting caught out when the Doom is on cooldown leads to early deaths.
  • Neglecting Scorched Earth for movement speed, causing poor positioning against mobile matchups like Morphling.

FAQ

Is Doom good in the current patch?

Yes. Doom’s 46.6% win rate (210 k games) shows he’s a solid pick, especially when you capitalize on his level 6 Doom and Scorched Earth mobility. He excels against heroes that rely on healing or spells, though he struggles against highly mobile or burst‑damage heroes.

What lane does Doom play?

Doom is most commonly played in the solo mid lane, allowing him to farm quickly, hit level 6 early, and start roaming with Doom. He can also be flexed to off‑lane if you need a durable initiator early.

Who counters Doom?

The toughest matchups are Keeper of the Light, Nature’s Prophet, Bane, Magnus, Shadow Demon, and Pugna, where Doom’s win rate hovers around 40‑43%. These heroes either out‑maneuver his initiation or provide strong magical burst that can kill him before Doom lands. Use BKB, early Scorched Earth, and vision to mitigate their impact.
doom.counterHtml:
Doom’s threat comes from his Devour ‑ stealing powerful abilities ‑ and his ultimate Doom, which silences and prevents healing while dealing damage over time. The key to shutting him down is denying him the chance to lock down a hero with Doom and stripping away the utility he can steal with Devour.

Why These Heroes Beat Doom

Keeper of the Light

Keeper’s Illuminate and Chakra Magic give him strong lane sustain and burst damage that can outpace Doom’s early Infernal Blade damage, while his Mana Leak provides a reliable way to purge the Doom curse before it detonates. Tip: land a quick Illuminate after Doom’s first stun to force him to retreat and waste his cooldown.

Nature's Prophet

Nature’s Prophet’s Teleportation lets him dodge Doom’s Infernal Blade and Doom entirely, and his Sprout can trap Doom, preventing him from using Devour or Scorced Earth effectively. Tip: keep a Sprout ready for the moment Doom initiates his combo; a well‑timed root forces him to waste his stun.

Bane

Bane’s Nightmare and Fiend’s Grip provide hard disables that can interrupt Doom’s Devour and keep him locked down while the Doom curse is active, nullifying the damage‑over‑time component. Tip: chain Nightmare into Fiend’s Grip as soon as Doom casts his ultimate to deny him any spell‑casting window.

Magnus

Magnus’s Skewer and Reverse Polarity can pull Doom out of his Scorched Earth zone and group him for burst damage, while his Empower amplifies allied right‑clicks to melt Doom’s health pool before he can Devour. Tip: time Reverse Polarity just after Doom’s Infernal Blade stun lands to catch him while his cooldowns are on lock.

Shadow Demon

Shadow Demon’s Disruption creates a clone that can absorb Doom’s Doom and Infernal Blade damage, and his Soul Catcher amplifies damage taken by the target, making Doom’s burn more lethal to the clone and less to the real hero. Tip: use Disruption pre‑emptively when Doom engages; the clone will take the curse and explode, buying you a safe window.

Drafting Against Doom

  • Ban or pick heroes with strong single‑target disables (e.g., Bane, Shadow Demon).
  • Prioritize heroes with global or blink mobility to outrange Doom’s Infernal Blade and Scorched Earth (Axe, Nature’s Prophet).
  • Choose heroes that can purge or block spells (e.g., Oracle, Abaddon) to neutralize the Doom curse.
  • Include at least one hero with reliable lane sustain or escape to survive early Doom pressure.

Laning Against Doom

  • Trade when Doom’s Infernal Blade cooldown is up; his damage spikes are short‑lived.
  • Harass him before he gets a creep kill for Devour; without a devoured ability he is far less threatening.
  • Punish the window after he uses Scorched Earth — his movement speed boost expires quickly, leaving him vulnerable.
  • Force him to use Devour on a neutral creep rather than a hero; the loss of a potential stolen ability reduces his late‑game impact.

Itemizing Against Doom

Black King Bar — blocks Doom’s ultimate and any stolen spell, letting you fight without being silenced.
Manta Style — creates illusion copies that can absorb the Doom curse and Scorched Earth damage, while also providing a purge on activation.
Eul's Scepter of Divinity – cyclones Doom, removing him from the fight and resetting his cooldowns, plus it grants a brief spell‑immune window.
Lotus Orb — reflects Doom’s Infernal Blade and Doom back at him, and provides a basic dispel to remove the curse.

drow-ranger.name: Drow Ranger
drow-ranger.guideHtml:
Drow Ranger is a ranged agility carry whose strength lies in her exceptional single‑target damage and global scaling through Marksmanship. On patch 7.41 she sits at a solid 51.0% win rate across 614 k recent ranked games, making her a reliable pick in the current meta despite a few hard counters.

How to Play Drow Ranger

Laning Phase

  • Use Frost Arrows on every attack to harass melee off‑laners and force them to miss last hits; the 1.5 s slow makes lane equilibrium easier to control.
  • Gust is a potent early‑game tool against invisible heroes (e.g., Slark, Riki) and to silence aggressive supports like Clockwerk; aim the knock‑back toward your tower to keep the enemy safe.
  • When you have a Glacier charge, position it near the creep wave to knock back enemy supports and gain the bonus attack range and damage—great for trading with heroes such as Dragon Knight.
  • Prioritize getting Precision Aura levels early; the extra agility boosts both your own damage and that of any allied ranged mid‑lane partner.
  • Against tough matchups (Dragon Knight, Treant Protector, Warlock) play conservatively, focus on farming, and look for Gust‑silence windows to secure safe kills.

Mid Game

  • Marksmanship spikes at level 6 and again at level 12; aim to hit level 12 before committing to team fights.
  • Secure a Glacier on a high ground or near a Roshan/ancient pit to create a vision bubble and extend your attack range for team skirmishes.
  • Join split‑push lanes once you have a Core Item (e.g., Power Treads, Maelstrom) and use Multishot to quickly clear creep waves while maintaining a safe distance.
  • In contested team fights, position behind front‑liners, use Gust to silence initiators like Slardar or Clockwerk, then let Multishot rain arrows on the back‑line.

Late Game

  • Win condition: dominate the map with split‑push and force the enemy to defend towers; your Marksmanship + Multishot can take towers in ~30 s when supported by Glacier vision.
  • Positioning is critical: stay behind melee front‑line or on a Glacier hill to avoid being caught by disables (e.g., Warlock’s Fatal Bonds).
  • Losing the game usually stems from over‑extending without Glacier vision or failing to shut down hard counters (Dragon Knight, Treant, Warlock) early, allowing them to close the gap and silence you.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane against harass.
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery after early trades.
  • Slippers of Agility — early agility for better last‑hits and damage.
  • Iron Branch ×2 — cheap stats and can later be used for Magic Wand.
  • Faerie Fire — emergency burst damage to secure a last hit.

Core Items

  • Power Treads — flexible stats; attack speed helps with Multishot uptime.
  • Maelstrom — adds chain lightning to your high attack speed, synergizes with Multishot for massive wave clear.
  • Dragon Lance — boosts attack range and agility, making it easier to stay out of enemy disable zones.
  • Black King Bar — essential against heavy silence/disables from Warlock, Slardar, and Clockwerk.

Situational Items

  • Manta Style — dispels silences and provides illusion split‑push; strong against Warlock’s Fatal Bonds and Nature’s Prophet’s Teleport.
  • Satanic — survivability when you get caught by burst heroes like Dragon Knight.
  • Butterfly — huge evasion boost against right‑click heavy heroes (e.g., Terrorblade, Slardar).
  • Hurricane Pike — extra range and a knock‑back to escape Clockwerk’s Hookshot or Treant’s Nature’s Grasp.
  • Abyssal Blade — lockdown for slippery heroes such as Nature’s Prophet; also provides a reliable stun for team fights.

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑extending without Glacier – diving without the vision and range bonus makes you an easy target for hard counters.
  • Neglecting Gust – many players forget to use the silence early, allowing initiators to start fights unhindered.
  • Itemizing too early into tanky items – Drow’s power spikes come from damage items; delaying Maelstrom or Dragon Lance stalls her mid‑game impact.
  • Ignoring split‑push timing – waiting for a full team fight instead of pressuring side lanes wastes the advantage of Marksmanship.

FAQ

Is Drow Ranger good in the current patch?

Yes. Drow holds a 51.0% win rate across over 614 k recent ranked matches, placing her among the top carries on patch 7.41. Her scaling Marksmanship and reliable Glacier vision keep her relevant despite a few tough matchups.

What lane does Drow Ranger play?

Drow is typically played in the safe lane as a solo carry, often paired with a support who can provide early Gust silences (e.g., Lion, Shadow Shaman) and help secure farm.

Who counters Drow Ranger?

The hardest opponents right now are Dragon Knight (36.2% win vs. Drow), Treant Protector (37.9%), and Warlock (38.0%). These heroes have strong disables or armor‑based survivability that can neutralize Drow’s damage before she reaches her Marksmanship spikes.
drow-ranger.counterHtml:
Drow Ranger’s strength lies in her pure damage output and long‑range presence, amplified by Frost Arrows, Precision Aura, and Marksmanship. She thrives when she can stay safe, kite opponents, and continuously shred heroes with Multishot. The fastest way to shut her down is to apply early pressure, limit her spacing, and force her into melee fights where her damage falls off.

Why These Heroes Beat Drow Ranger

Dragon Knight

Dragon Knight’s Dragon Tail and Elder Dragon Form give him reliable crowd control and burst armor that directly counters Drow’s physical damage. His Breathe Fire also reduces Drow’s armor, making even her Frost Arrows less effective. Tip: Initiate with Dragon Tail as soon as Drow casts Multishot; the stun interrupts the channel and forces her to retreat.

Treant Protector

Treant’s Nature’s Grasp creates a massive slow that outpaces Drow’s Frost Arrow slow, preventing her from kiting. His Living Armor grants massive damage mitigation, neutralizing Drow’s consistent right‑click damage. Tip: Plant a Living Armor tree near the lane’s creep equilibrium; Drow’s attempts to harass will be heavily mitigated.

Warlock

Warlock’s Fatal Bonds links Drow to her allies, spreading any damage she deals back to herself and her teammates. When combined with Chaotic Offering, the stun and damage burst force Drow out of position before she can land a Multishot. Tip: Use Fatal Bonds early in lane and follow up with a Golem‑drop when Drow tries to push; the stun will cancel her Gust and Multishot.

Slardar

Slardar’s Slithereen Crush applies a hard‑stop and armor‑reduction aura that makes Drow’s physical attacks far less threatening. His Amplify Damage further shreds her armor, turning even a single arrow into a lethal hit. Tip: Time a Slithereen Crush right after Drow’s Gust; the silence is broken and she loses her primary defensive tool.

Clockwerk

Clockwerk’s Hookshot pulls Drow into his Power Cogs, instantly negating her range advantage and silencing her. The Battery Assault damage over time punishes her low health pool while she’s trapped. Tip: Initiate with Hookshot from the side of the lane; the forced melee engagement prevents her from using Multishot safely.

Drafting Against Drow Ranger

  • Prioritize heroes with hard‑stuns, silences, or armor‑reduction (e.g., Dragon Knight, Slardar, Clockwerk).
  • Pick melee initiators who can close the distance quickly and force Drow into close‑quarters combat.
  • Ban or avoid heroes with strong late‑game scaling and pure right‑click damage that complement Drow (e.g., Sniper, Medusa).
  • Include vision‑heavy or detection heroes to negate Drow’s Glacier and hidden‑unit advantage.

Laning Against Drow Ranger

  • Trade when Drow’s Frost Arrows are on cooldown; her damage spikes are short‑lived.
  • Punish her early when she lacks Glacier and her Precision Aura is still low‑level.
  • Use creep equilibrium to force her into a position where your stun or slow lands before she can fire a Multishot.
  • Harass with ranged attacks that are not affected by her Gust silence (e.g., heroes with innate magic damage).

Itemizing Against Drow Ranger

Blade Mail — reflects Drow’s high right‑click damage back to her, making aggressive trades risky.
Black King Bar — grants spell immunity against Gust and prevents her silence from disrupting your combos.
Manta Style — dispels Frost Arrows slow and provides extra movement speed to dodge Multishot.
Satanic — offers lifesteal and a strong active heal that can survive the burst from a successful Multishot.

dragon-knight.name: Dragon Knight
dragon-knight.guideHtml:
Dragon Knight is a versatile melee hero who can function as a carry, pusher, and durable initiator thanks to his strong scaling and reliable disables. On patch 7.41 his overall pub win rate sits at 49.0% across 137,335 ranked games, placing him slightly below the meta average but still viable in the right hands.

How to Play Dragon Knight

Laning Phase

  • Use Dragon Tail early to secure last hits and punish aggressive melee opponents; the stun also deters ganks from heroes like Bounty Hunter who currently give DK a 33.8% win rate.
  • Breathe Fire provides lane sustain and armor reduction; cast it on wave creeps to accelerate lane clearing against siege‑heavy matchups such as Treant Protector (DK win 39.0%).
  • Prioritize Dragon Blood upgrades after the first level‑up to boost HP regen and armor, helping you survive harassment from ranged heroes like Drow Ranger (DK win 63.8%).
  • When you hit level 6, consider Fireball to harass enemy supports and force them to pull back, especially effective against low‑mobility heroes like Techies (DK win 40.0%).
  • Keep an eye on enemy rune control; a well‑timed Dragon Tail on a roaming support can secure early kills and give you lane dominance.

Mid Game

  • Aim for the Elder Dragon Form transition at level 16; the ranged attack and AoE increase make you a potent tower pusher and team‑fight threat.
  • Group with your cores to take mid‑lane towers; Breathe Fire in Elder form now hits multiple targets, making it ideal against clustered enemies like Venomancer (DK win 36.9%).
  • Look for pick‑offs on squishy supports using Dragon Tail followed by a quick Fireball combo; the stun‑damage chain is especially lethal when you have a Blink Dagger or Force Staff.
  • If you have a Black King Bar, initiate fights after your allies have engaged; your durability and the armor‑reduction from Breathe Fire swing team fights in your favor.

Late Game

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain against harass in lane.
  • Healing Salve — quick HP recovery after early skirmishes.
  • Stout Shield — mitigates damage from aggressive melee heroes like Bounty Hunter.
  • Quelling Blade — improves last‑hit reliability and early tower damage.
  • Iron Branch x2 — cheap stat boost and later builds into a Magic Wand.

Core Items

  • Power Treads — attack speed for faster farm and flexibility to switch to strength for survivability.
  • Armlet of Mordiggian — huge burst damage and survivability; synergizes with Dragon Blood regen.
  • Black King Bar — essential against heavy magical disables (Keeper of the Light, Venomancer).
  • Blink Dagger — provides initiation range for landing Dragon Tail and escaping Techies mines.
  • Satanic — late‑game sustain in prolonged fights, especially when you become the primary front‑line.

Situational Items

  • Manta Style — counters silences and provides extra split‑push speed against heroes like Clinkz (DK win 39.8%).
  • Abyssal Blade — extra lockdown when you need to lock down elusive carries such as Phantom Lancer (DK win 60.0%).
  • Assault Cuirass — boosts your armor and reduces enemy armor, amplifying the damage from Breathe Fire.
  • Shiva’s Guard — adds armor and an AoE slow, useful versus high‑attack‑speed heroes like Troll Warlord (DK win 56.3%).
  • Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target spells, handy against Bounty Hunter’s tracking or Techies’ mines.

  • Relying on early damage instead of scaling – DK’s true power comes from Elder Dragon Form; over‑extending before level 16 often leads to deaths.
  • Neglecting BKB timing – facing magic‑heavy line‑ups (Keeper of the Light, Venomancer) without a BKB makes you an easy disable target.
  • Using Fireball as a primary damage tool – its damage is modest; treat it as a zoning tool and focus on Breathe Fire and auto‑attacks in Elder form.
  • Failing to split‑push efficiently – DK’s tower‑damage is massive; staying grouped when you could be pressuring side lanes wastes a key win condition.

FAQ

Is Dragon Knight good in the current patch?

Dragon Knight sits at a 49.0% win rate on patch 7.41, slightly below the meta average but still viable, especially when you can reach Elder Dragon Form and leverage his strong push and durability.

What lane does Dragon Knight play?

He is most commonly played in the safe lane (position 1) as a carry/pusher, though he can also be a solid off‑lane initiator when the team needs a durable front‑liner.

Who counters Dragon Knight?

The toughest matchups right now are Bounty Hunter (33.8% win), Venomancer (36.9%), Keeper of the Light (38.0%), Treant Protector (39.0%), Clinkz (39.8%), and Techies (40.0%). These heroes exploit his relatively low early mobility and can lock him down before he hits his key power spikes.
dragon-knight.counterHtml:
