Why These Heroes Beat Dragon Knight

Bounty Hunter

Bounty Hunter’s Track reveals Dragon Knight’s position, nullifying the surprise stun from Dragon Tail and allowing safe harassment. His Shuriken Toss and Jinada proc apply burst damage that outpaces DK’s early HP pool. Tip: Keep vision on DK and punish his 6‑second cooldown on Dragon Tail with quick retaliations.

Venomancer

Venomous Gale and Poison Nova apply constant damage‑over‑time that ignores DK’s armor, while his Plague Ward blocks the line of sight needed for Breathe Fire to hit multiple targets. The lingering poison also reduces DK’s healing from Dragon Blood. Tip: Position wards to force DK into melee range where his AoE is least effective.

Keeper of the Light

Illuminate and Chakra Magic give Keeper massive mana sustain, letting him spam Mana Leak to drain DK’s mana before he can cast Breathe Fire or Fireball. Keeper’s Recall provides a safe escape from Dragon Tail stuns, forcing DK to waste cooldowns chasing. Tip: Use Recall right after DK lands a stun to reset lane equilibrium.

Treant Protector

Living Armor on the lane creeps and himself mitigates DK’s Breathe Fire damage, while Nature’s Guise grants invisibility that negates the vision component of Dragon Tail. Treant’s Overgrowth can root DK, preventing him from closing the gap needed for his melee attacks. Tip: Time Overgrowth just after DK’s Dragon Tail lands to lock him down while his cooldowns are on lock.

Clinkz

Clinkz’s Searing Arrows add pure damage that pierces DK’s armor, and his Death Pact grants massive HP to survive the early burst. The ranged attack range lets Clinkz kite DK, staying out of Dragon Tail range while continuously harassing with Burning Barrage. Tip: Keep distance > 600 units and use Burning Barrage to force DK to use Breathe Fire defensively.

Drafting Against Dragon Knight

  • Prioritize heroes with reliable long‑range disables or silences (e.g., Lion, Shadow Shaman).
  • Pick high‑mobility heroes that can dodge Dragon Tail and kite his melee form.
  • Choose magic‑damage‑heavy lineups to bypass his armor scaling from Dragon Blood.
  • Consider early‑game burst heroes that can kill DK before he hits level 6 and unlocks Elder Dragon Form.

Laning Against Dragon Knight

  • Trade when DK’s Dragon Tail is on cooldown (6 s) and before he gets a level 2 Breathe Fire.
  • Harass with ranged attacks from outside his attack range; his Breathe Fire only reduces enemy damage, not his own.
  • Force him to use Fireball for lane control; the reduced cast range in melee makes it easy to dodge.
  • Punish his low early HP after a Dragon Tail stun by quickly following up with a stun or burst spell.

Itemizing Against Dragon Knight

  • Manta Style — breaks silences and dispels Dragon Blood armor boost, while providing extra mobility to dodge stuns.
  • Eul's Scepter of Divinity — cyclone removes DK from fights, nullifying his Dragon Tail and Breathe Fire during the duration.
  • Ghost Scepter — makes you ethereal, so DK’s physical attacks and Dragon Tail do no damage while you can safely cast spells.
  • Heaven’s Halberd — disarms DK, preventing his high‑damage melee attacks and reducing the threat of his Elder Dragon auto‑attacks.

earth-spirit.name: Earth Spirit
earth-spirit.guideHtml:
Earth Spirit is a high‑skill initiator who excels at chaining disables, creating space with Stone Remnants, and turning fights into chaotic boulder‑roll combos. On patch 7.41 his overall win rate sits at 50.4% across 181 k ranked games, making him a solid but not dominant pick—strong in coordinated play and weaker against mobile heroes that can dodge his rolls.

How to Play Earth Spirit

Laning Phase

  • Stone Remnant + Boulder Smash: Place a Remnant near the creep wave and use Boulder Smash on it to pull enemy heroes into your lane, setting up early kills or forcing them to miss last‑hits.
  • Rolling Boulder on low‑HP heroes: With 60 + 100% STR damage, Rolling Boulder can finish off squishy supports (e.g., Lion, Rubick) before they can escape.
  • Geomagnetic Grip on allied heroes: Grip a Remnant or an allied hero (e.g., a support) to silence an approaching enemy, buying you time to reposition or call a second Remnant.
  • Enchant Remnant for lane sustain: Enchant yourself or a support to give them the durability of a Remnant, allowing aggressive trades against melee off‑laners like Timbersaw.
  • Watch for high‑mobility matchups: Against Ringmaster, Ember Spirit, Gyrocopter, Puck, Snapfire, and Pangolier (win ≈ 44‑45%), avoid over‑committing rolls; keep a Remnant for a quick escape.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 6 (Magnetize): Magnetize a frontline hero (your own or an ally) before a teamfight; the damage over time and the explosion of nearby Remnants can quickly melt enemy cores.

  • Roam after securing a lane: Use Rolling Boulder to traverse terrain quickly and gank side lanes; prioritize heroes you have good win‑rates against (Timbersaw, Pudge, Lion).
  • Stack and pull with Stone Remnant: Set up double‑stack camps and pull enemy heroes into the stack with Boulder Smash, then follow up with Magnetize for burst damage.

Late Game

  • Win condition: lock down the enemy carry – chain Boulder Smash → Rolling Boulder → Magnetize on the high‑damage hero; the combo forces them to die quickly or be forced out of fights.
  • Positioning: Stay near a cluster of Remnants; if you get caught, Enchant Remnant on yourself to survive and still deliver a stun on death.
  • What loses the game: Over‑extending without a Remnant safety net, especially against the toughest matchups (Ringmaster, Ember Spirit, Gyrocopter); they can out‑maneuver your rolls and silence your Magnetize.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain for early lane trades.
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery after aggressive Boulder Smashes.
  • Iron Branch ×2 — cheap stats and can be later built into Magic Wand.
  • Observer Ward — vision to protect your Remnants and spot enemy ganks.

Core Items

  • Phase Boots — extra mobility for Rolling Boulder initiations and to close gaps on mobile heroes.
  • Blink Dagger — essential for instant positioning of Remnants and surprise Magnetize combos.
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Enchant Remnant, letting you turn an ally into a durable, damage‑dealing Remnant for teamfights.
  • Force Staff — provides an additional escape tool when your Remnants are on cooldown, useful against Ringmaster and Puck.

Situational Items

  • Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — extra disable and self‑save against Ember Spirit and Gyrocopter.
  • Black King Bar — necessary when facing heavy magical burst from Puck, Snapfire, or Lina.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects targeted spells (e.g., Ringmaster’s Ring of Terror) and provides armor.
  • Shiva’s Guard — armor and AOE slow to counter high‑damage carries like Gyrocopter and Puck.
  • Aether Lens — extends the range of Boulder Smash and Rolling Boulder, helping you reach mobile heroes.

Common Mistakes

  • Rolling Boulder without a Remnant backup – getting stunned or silenced mid‑roll leaves you vulnerable.
  • Overusing Magnetize on low‑damage allies – the damage tick is negligible; prioritize high‑damage heroes or yourself.
  • Neglecting vision on Remnant placements – enemies can destroy or bypass them, nullifying your combo potential.
  • Chasing mobile heroes into the jungle – Ringmaster, Ember Spirit, and Gyrocopter can kite your rolls; keep a Remnant for a quick pull‑back instead.

FAQ

Is Earth Spirit good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 50.4% win rate on 181 k recent matches, Earth Spirit is a viable pick, especially on coordinated teams that can capitalize on his combo potential. He shines against heroes like Timbersaw, Pudge, and Lion, where his win rates exceed 60%.

What lane does Earth Spirit play?

Earth Spirit is most commonly played off‑lane (hard lane) where his Stone Remnants can be used to disrupt enemy pull‑stuns and secure early kills. He can also flex to a safe mid lane if the enemy draft lacks strong lane‑dominant heroes.

Who counters Earth Spirit?

The toughest matchups are Ringmaster, Ember Spirit, Gyrocopter, Puck, Snapfire, and Pangolier, where Earth Spirit wins only ~40‑45% of games. Their mobility and burst damage let them dodge Boulder Smashes and out‑range Magnetize, making them the primary counters on patch 7.41.

Why These Heroes Beat Earth Spirit

Ringmaster

Ringmaster’s Ring of the Dead grants a large, mobile shield that blocks Earth Spirit’s Boulder Smash and Rolling Boulder damage, while his Cursed Ring silences Earth Spirit, preventing Geomagnetic Grip and Magnetize. Tip: Keep the shield active near your Stone Remnants and use the silence to interrupt Magnetize chains.

Ember Spirit

Ember Spirit’s Sleight of Fist lets him dodge Rolling Boulder and quickly close distance, while Flame Guard provides magic immunity that blocks Geomagnetic Grip’s silence and the damage from Magnetize explosions. Tip: Initiate with Sleight of Fist to weave through remnants, then activate Flame Guard before Earth Spirit lands a pull.

Gyrocopter

Gyrocopter’s Flak Cannon and Rocket Barrage deliver constant AoE damage that forces Earth Spirit to stay on the back foot, and his Rocket Boost gives the speed needed to outrun Rolling Boulder. Tip: Position near a Stone Remnant, let Gyrocopter’s rockets shred the remnant, then use Flak Cannon to punish the brief stun window after a roll.

Puck

Puck’s Illusory Orb provides long‑range poke that can chip Earth Spirit before he sets up a pull, while Dream Coil can trap him after a Rolling Boulder, preventing escape and forcing a costly Magnetize reset. Tip: Time Dream Coil to land just after Earth Spirit’s roll lands; the coil’s silence also blocks Geomagnetic Grip.

Snapfire

Snapfire’s Firesnap Cookie gives a burst of burst damage that can kill a low‑HP Earth Spirit before he can finish a combo, and Lil’ Shredder’s stun interrupts Rolling Boulder and Magnetize. Tip: Drop a Cookie on a Stone Remnant to force Earth Spirit to waste a pull, then follow up with Lil’ Shredder for a guaranteed stun.

Drafting Against Earth Spirit

  • Prioritize heroes with strong mobility (e.g., Blink, Phase Shift) to outrun Rolling Boulder.
  • Choose magic‑immune or silence‑immune heroes to negate Geomagnetic Grip and Magnetize.
  • Pick heroes with AoE burst that can quickly destroy Stone Remnants.
  • Ban or avoid heroes that heavily rely on static control (e.g., Lion, Shadow Shaman) which complement Earth Spirit’s kit.

Laning Against Earth Spirit

  • Harass early with ranged attacks before he can place his first Stone Remnant.
  • Trade when his Boulder Smash is on cooldown; his damage drops dramatically without it.
  • Force him to use Rolling Boulder defensively by maintaining distance; the long cast delay makes him vulnerable.
  • Punish any missed pull with a quick counter‑engage (e.g., stun or burst damage) while his Magnetize is inactive.

Itemizing Against Earth Spirit

Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — provides a 2.5 s cyclone to dodge Rolling Boulder and a purge to remove Magnetize.
Black King Bar — grants magic immunity, nullifying Geomagnetic Grip’s silence and Magnetize damage.
Ghost Scepter — makes you ethereal, causing Rolling Boulder to miss and preventing damage from pulled remnants.
Force Staff — gives the burst distance needed to escape a Rolling Boulder or a pulled Stone Remnant.

elder-titan.name: Elder Titan
elder-titan.guideHtml:
Elder Titan is a durable initiator and disabler who excels at reducing enemy defenses and setting up team fights. In the current 7.41 meta his win rate sits at 50.5% over 37,457 ranked games, making him a solid but not dominant pick. He shines when paired with strong front‑line allies and struggles against heroes that can dodge or out‑range his tools.

How to Play Elder Titan

Laning Phase

  • Astral Spirit scouting – Send the spirit early to reveal fog‑of‑war and check for hidden pulls; the spirit’s damage on contact also deters aggressive harass.
  • Natural Order – Position the spirit near enemy creeps to strip their armor and magic resistance, making your own lane harass and last‑hits more effective.
  • Echo Stomp timing – Use the channeled stomp when the enemy off‑lane commits to a pull or when you need to block a gank; the knock‑up buys you time to escape or retaliate.
  • Momentum armor – Stack movement speed with items like Phase Boots or Power Treads; the extra armor from Momentum makes you harder to kill in lane trades.
  • Matchup awareness – Play conservatively against the toughest lanes (Hoodwink, Rubick, Mars) and look for early rotations; against easy matchups (Pugna, Pangolier) you can press for kills with early Echo Stomp combos.

Mid Game

  • Earth Splitter timing – Drop it in chokepoints after a 3‑second delay; the damage scales with max HP, so prioritize tanky heroes and use it to force enemy backlines to scatter.
  • Astral Spirit + Natural Order – In team fights, send the spirit into the enemy cluster first, then activate Natural Order to strip armor before you or your allies unleash spells.
  • Power spike at level 12 – Unlocks Echo Stomp’s stun and the spirit’s movement speed bonus, allowing you to initiate reliably.
  • Map control – Use the spirit’s movement ability to scout Roshan, enemy jungle, and high‑ground vision spots; the information lets your team set up picks.

Late Game

  • Win condition: armor‑shred + burst – Combine Natural Order with your teammates’ magical damage to quickly melt tank heroes; Earth Splitter adds a massive chunk of HP‑based damage.
  • Positioning – Stay just behind your front‑line; the spirit’s armor reduction is centered on you, so you need to be close enough to affect the enemy but far enough to avoid being focused.
  • What loses the game – Getting caught without your spirit (e.g., after a failed Return Astral Spirit) leaves you vulnerable to burst; also, failing to land Echo Stomp on key targets lets the enemy team disengage.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango + Healing Salve — sustain against harass and early tower pressure.
  • Observer Ward — vision for early spirit scouting.
  • Iron Branch ×2 — cheap stat boost; can later be used for Magic Wand.

Core Items

  • Phase Boots — provides the movement speed needed for Momentum armor and quick initiations.
  • Blink Dagger — essential for closing the gap to land Echo Stomp and position Earth Splitter.
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Earth Splitter to a larger area and reduces its delay, making it a decisive team‑fight tool.
  • Shiva’s Guard — adds armor, an AoE slow, and extra armor reduction synergy with Natural Order.

Situational Items

  • Black King Bar — against heavy magical burst (e.g., Pugna, Rubick).
  • Lotus Orb — reflects targeted disables that would otherwise lock you down.
  • Heart of Tarrasque — when you need extra survivability against sustained physical damage (Mars, Beastmaster).
  • Assault Cuirass — further armor reduction for enemies and armor boost for you in fights.
  • Octarine Core — reduces cooldowns on Echo Stomp and Earth Splitter, helpful in high‑tempo games.

Common Mistakes

  • Chaining Echo Stomp without vision – using the stomp blindly often wastes the stun on invisible heroes (e.g., Hoodwink) and leaves you exposed.
  • Leaving the Astral Spirit unattended – forgetting to Return Astral Spirit makes you lose the armor bonus and the spirit’s damage, turning fights against burst heroes.
  • Over‑committing Earth Splitter – dropping it in open terrain where enemies can dodge the 3‑second delay wastes its massive HP‑based damage.
  • Neglecting armor/shred synergy – relying only on your own damage instead of coordinating Natural Order with magic‑damage allies reduces your overall impact.

FAQ

Is Elder Titan good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 50.5% win rate on 37,457 recent ranked matches, Elder Titan is a viable pick, especially when paired with heroes that can capitalize on his armor‑shred and crowd‑control. He performs best against easy matchups like Pugna and Pangolier (≈65% win rate) and struggles against tough lanes such as Hoodwink and Rubick (≈25‑27% win rate).

What lane does Elder Titan play?

Elder Titan is most commonly played in the off‑lane (solo safe lane) where his durability and ability to disrupt enemy pulls shine. He can also be flexed to the mid lane if your team needs a hard‑initiate and you have a strong early‑game support.

Who counters Elder Titan?

The toughest opponents right now are Hoodwink, Rubick, Mars, Jakiro, Beastmaster, and Templar Assassin, each giving Elder Titan win rates below 45% (25.9%–42.3%). These heroes either dodge his stun, out‑range his tools, or apply constant pressure that prevents him from safely using his spirit and Earth Splitter.

Hoodwink’s Acorn Shot and Bushwhack can stun Elder Titan before he finishes the channel of Echo Stomp, and her Scurry lets her dodge the follow‑up knock‑up. Play aggressively in lane; land a Bushwhack on his Spirit when it moves, then follow up with a quick Acorn Shot for a guaranteed kill.

Rubick can Spell‑Steal Echo Stomp or Natural Order, turning Titan’s own crowd control and armor‑reduction against his team. Use Telekinesis to lift the Astral Spirit out of range, forcing Titan to stay vulnerable while you steal his key spell.

Mars’ Arena of Blood creates an impenetrable barrier that blocks the line of sight needed for Echo Stomp to affect enemies, and his Spear of Mars can pin Elder Titan while his Spirit is on the other side of the arena. Initiate with the arena, then spear the Titan before he can channel Earth Splitter.

Jakiro’s Dual Breath and Ice Path apply constant slows and damage, making it hard for Titan to position his Spirit for a successful Natural Order. The Liquid Fire burn also reduces Titan’s effective health, so keep the lane soaked and force him to retreat before he can cast Earth Splitter.

Beastmaster’s Primal Roar provides a long‑range stun that can interrupt Echo Stomp’s channel, while his Wild Axes and Hawk give vision on the Astral Spirit’s path, allowing you to anticipate and dodge its return. Harass with axes early and stun Titan the moment he begins a channel.

Drafting Against Elder Titan

  • Prioritize heroes with reliable hard‑stuns or silences that can interrupt channeling (e.g., Lion, Shadow Shaman).
  • Pick mobile heroes that can outrun the Astral Spirit’s Momentum armor gain (e.g., Anti‑Mage, Ember Spirit).
  • Include magic‑damage burst heroes to punish the low magic resistance after Natural Order is applied.
  • Consider bans that remove strong early‑game lane pressure, as Titan’s win rate suffers when he cannot secure lane dominance.

Laning Against Elder Titan

  • Harass aggressively before he can summon his Astral Spirit; his early damage is limited.
  • Trade when his Spirit is away from him—Titan loses the armor bonus from Momentum and the extra damage on return.
  • Punish any attempt to channel Echo Stomp with a stun or silence; the channel time is a clear vulnerability.
  • Keep the lane warded to spot the Spirit’s movement; deny him vision to prevent Natural Order from hitting multiple units.

earthshaker.name: Earthshaker
earthshaker.guideHtml:
Earthshaker is a hard‑lane support whose toolkit revolves around area‑control stuns and massive burst damage from Echo Slam. He excels as an initiator and disabler, turning team fights into chaos with his combo of Fissure + Aftershock. On patch 7.41 his overall win rate sits at 50.2% across 510 k ranked games, making him a solid but not dominant pick in the current meta.

How to Play Earthshaker

Laning Phase

  • Fissure early on to block creep equilibrium and punish aggressive lane partners; the impassable ridge forces enemy supports to reposition or lose farm.
  • Enchant Totem on the first few melee attacks gives a burst of damage that can secure early kills on squishy supports (e.g., Bane) who tend to dive you.
  • Pair Aftershock with any ability cast (especially Fissure) to add a stun and extra damage to nearby creeps, speeding up lane clearing and denying XP to enemy off‑laners.
  • Prioritize vision and a ward at the river to protect against jungle ganks from heroes like Monkey King, who currently gives Earthshaker only a 33.3 % win rate in 69 games.
  • When facing high‑mobility heroes (e.g., Void Spirit), keep a short distance and use Fissure’s long line to split them from their allies before they can blink in.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 6 with Echo Slam; look for 2‑v‑2 or 3‑v‑3 engagements where you can hit multiple heroes to maximize echo damage.
  • Roam with Fissure + Aftershock to create instant 2‑second stuns on clustered enemies; coordinate with your mid‑lane for early tower dives.
  • Secure Aegis or BKB for yourself before committing to a full‑team fight, as Echo Slam’s damage drops dramatically against BKB‑protected heroes.
  • Prioritize objectives that benefit from crowd control (e.g., Roshan) where a well‑timed Fissure can block enemy escape routes.

Late Game

  • Win condition: land a clean Echo Slam on the enemy core team after a successful initiation; the double‑echo on real heroes can instantly swing a 5‑v‑5.
  • Position near the front line but stay just out of enemy vision; your Aftershock will still trigger on ability casts, giving you a safety net.
  • Avoid over‑extending without vision—heroes like Necrophos (40.3 % win rate vs. Earthshaker) can out‑heal you if you’re caught without a stun.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane against harassment.
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery after early skirmishes.
  • Observer Ward — essential for map control and early gank prevention.
  • Sentry Ward — counter enemy vision, especially against invisible heroes like Bane.
  • Iron Branch ×2 — cheap stat boost and can be later used for a Magic Wand.

Core Items

  • Arcane Boots — provides the mana needed for frequent Fissure/Aftershock combos.
  • Blink Dagger — primary initiation tool; pair with Fissure for instant stun‑and‑lock.
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Echo Slam to hit a larger radius and adds a third echo on heroes, dramatically increasing team‑fight impact.
  • Force Staff — helps you reposition for optimal Echo Slam placement or to save allies from pulls.

Situational Items

  • Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — extra disable and a way to dodge enemy spells like Bane’s Fiend’s Grip.
  • Ghost Scepter — protects against right‑click heroes such as Sven (67 % win rate vs. Earthshaker) who can burst you down.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target spells; useful against Bane and Void Spirit.
  • Heaven’s Halberd — disarms high‑damage cores like Chaos Knight (40 % win rate vs. Earthshaker).
  • Shiva’s Guard — armor and AOE slow; great against physical heroes like Axe (57 % win rate vs. Earthshaker).
  • Abyssal Blade — provides a reliable stun when Blink is on cooldown, sealing kills on mobile heroes.

Common Mistakes

  • Casting Fissure without Aftershock – forgetting that Aftershock automatically adds a stun and damage, wasting a crucial crowd‑control window.
  • Over‑committing without vision – roaming into enemy jungle without wards, leading to easy kills by Monkey King or Void Spirit.
  • Saving Blink for late‑game only – using Blink defensively early reduces your initiation power; the combo of Blink + Fissure is the core of Earthshaker’s impact.
  • Ignoring Echo Slam timing – casting Echo Slam when enemies are spread out yields minimal damage; aim for clustered fights or after a successful Fissure/Aftershock lock.

FAQ

Is Earthshaker good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 50.2 % win rate across over half a million ranked matches, Earthshaker remains a viable support/initiator. His ability to lock down teams with Fissure + Aftershock and scale into a game‑ending Echo Slam keeps him relevant despite a few tough matchups.

What lane does Earthshaker play?

Earthshaker is typically a hard‑lane support, sharing the safe lane with a core (often a carry). This placement gives him space to farm early Fissure charges, place wards, and set up early ganks.

Who counters Earthshaker?

Mobile and high‑burst heroes currently give him trouble: Monkey King (33.3 % win rate), Bane (37.1 %), Void Spirit (40.5 %), and Necrophos (40.3 %). Vision control and early Blink + Fissure pressure are the best ways to mitigate their impact.
earthshaker.counterHtml:
Earthshaker’s massive AoE stuns and burst damage make him a nightmare in teamfights, especially when he lands a well‑timed Echo Slam after a crowd‑control combo. The key to shutting him down is denying him the opportunity to land his spells—by staying mobile, silencing or disarming him, and forcing early deaths before he can buy items that amplify his aftershocks.

Why These Heroes Beat Earthshaker

Monkey King

Monkey King’s Boundless Strike and Jungle Smash give him high burst damage and a brief stun immunity window, while Tree Dance lets him dodge the linear Fissure and escape Echo Slam radius.
Tip: Use Wukong’s Command or a well‑timed Jungle Smash right after Earthshaker’s first ability to break his combo and force a miss.

Bane

Bane’s Nightmare provides a reliable single‑target disable that prevents Earthshaker from casting any ability, and Enfeeble drastically reduces the damage of Enchant Totem and Echo Slam.
Tip: Chain Nightmare into Brain Sap right after Earthshaker lands Fissure to keep him locked down through his aftershocks.

Chaos Knight

Chaos Knight’s Reality Rift instantly pulls Earthshaker into a vulnerable position, breaking his line‑of‑sight for Fissure and allowing Chaos Knight to follow up with Chaos Bolt for a guaranteed stun.
Tip: Initiate with Reality Rift before Earthshaker can cast Fissure, then burst him with Chaos Bolt while his Aftershock is on cooldown.

Necrophos

Necrophos’s Heartstopper Aura continuously chips Earthshaker’s health, and Reaper’s Scythe provides a long‑duration stun that can outlast Earthshaker’s Aftershock window.
Tip: Time Reaper’s Scythe just after Earthshaker lands Enchant Totem; the stun prevents the follow‑up Echo Slam and forces a death if his health is low.

Enchantress

Enchantress’s Enchant grants a massive movement speed boost, letting her slip out of Fissure and stay out of Echo Slam range, while Nature’s Attendants provides sustain against burst.
Tip: Keep Enchant active and kite Earthshaker’s Aftershock‑enhanced attacks; a quick Impetus‑based chase can force him to miss his combo entirely.

Drafting Against Earthshaker

  • Prioritize heroes with reliable silences or disables (e.g., Bane, Silencer, Lion).
  • Pick mobile heroes that can dodge linear stuns (Monkey King, Anti‑Mage, Puck).
  • Include early‑game burst damage to kill Earthshaker before he gets Enchant Totem and Echo Slam upgrades.
  • Consider banning Earthshaker if the enemy team is heavy on melee initiators.

Laning Against Earthshaker

  • Trade when his Fissure is on cooldown; his early game damage is limited without it.
  • Harass with ranged attacks or spells that force him to use Enchant Totem defensively.
  • Punish his low mobility by pulling creep waves and forcing him to over‑extend for last hits.
  • Keep a defensive ward near the river to spot his Fissure placement and avoid being caught.

Itemizing Against Earthshaker

Ghost Scepter — blocks physical damage from Enchant Totem and lets you dodge the initial hit of Echo Slam.
Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — provides a 2.5 s cyclone to nullify his combo and reset his cooldowns.
Force Staff — instantly escapes the impassable ridge created by Fissure and the stun radius of Aftershock.
Black King Bar — grants magic immunity, negating the stun and damage from Echo Slam and Aftershock.

ember-spirit.name: Ember Spirit
ember-spirit.guideHtml:
Ember Spirit is a high‑mobility, magic‑damage core who excels at weaving spells and dashes to burst enemies and escape dangerous situations. In the current 7.41 meta his overall pub win rate sits at 49.6% over 240 k ranked games, making him a solid but not dominant pick. He thrives when he can leverage his fire‑based toolkit to out‑maneuver opponents and snowball after his early‑mid power spikes.

How to Play Ember Spirit

Laning Phase

  • Sleight of Fist early levels to harass and secure last hits; the AoE damage lets you trade with melee supports while staying safe.
  • Flame Guard on a 2‑mana‑cost level to mitigate early magic harass from lane opponents such as Bane or Io (both are current tough match‑ups).
  • Plant Fire Remnants near the creep wave or jungle entrance; they give you a quick escape route or a surprise engage when the enemy overextends.
  • Use Searing Chains defensively when the enemy support dives; the root and damage punish aggressive positioning and can force a pull‑back.
  • Prioritize a balanced lane (mid or safe‑lane carry) against heroes like Witch Doctor or Venomancer, where your win rates are above 60 %, to maximize early farm and experience.

Mid Game

  • Hit level 6 and unlock Fire Remnant activation; start split‑pushing and creating flank opportunities with instant dashes.
  • Core power spike at 20‑25 k gold: acquire Aghanim’s Scepter (or Eul’s Scepter for extra control) to boost Sleight of Fist damage and give you a reliable escape from heroes like Puck and Treant Protector.
  • Roam with Sleight of Fist + Fire Remnant to gank lanes where the enemy lacks mobility; prioritize heroes you already have a favorable win rate against (e.g., Sniper, Dark Seer).
  • Keep Flame Guard active when diving into team fights against heavy magic damage teams (e.g., Void Spirit, Tidehunter) to survive their spells.

Late Game

  • Win condition: use Sleight of Fist + Fire Remnant combos to burst priority carries (Sniper, Witch Doctor) while staying out of enemy disables.
  • Positioning: stay on the edge of fights, using Searing Chains to lock down initiators (Bane, Lycan) and then dash out with a Remnant.
  • Game‑losing mistake: over‑committing without a Remnant or Flame Guard active, especially against disables from Io or crowd‑control from Puck, which currently give you sub‑44 % win rates.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango + Healing Salve — sustain in lane against harassment.
  • Iron Branch x2 — cheap stats and can later be used for a Magic Wand.
  • Faerie Fire — burst health for early trades.
  • Orb of Venom — helps secure early kills against low‑HP supports.

Core Items

  • Phase Boots — provides the extra speed needed for Sleight of Fist dashes and Remnant activation.
  • Maelstrom — synergizes with Sleight of Fist’s multi‑hit to amplify magical burst.
  • Black King Bar — essential against heavy disable lineups (Bane, Io, Puck).
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Fire Remnant to a larger AoE and reduces cooldown, turning Ember into a true split‑push threat.

Situational Items

  • Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — extra disable and self‑save against initiators like Treant Protector.
  • Satanic — lifesteal to survive prolonged fights against tanky heroes (Lycan, Tidehunter).
  • Shiva’s Guard — armor and aura against right‑click heavy lineups such as Clinkz.
  • Linken’s Sphere — blocks single‑target disables from Bane or Io.
  • Octarine Core — reduces cooldowns for all spells, great when you have multiple active Remnants.

Common Mistakes

  • Spamming Sleight of Fist without Flame Guard – leaves you vulnerable to burst magic from Bane, Io, and Puck.
  • Neglecting Fire Remnants – missing the primary escape/engage tool, especially against heroes you currently lose to (e.g., Bane).
  • Over‑extending in lane – trying to duel melee supports without the safety net of Searing Chains or a ready Remnant.
  • Delaying core items – waiting too long for Black King Bar or Phase Boots lets enemy disables dominate the mid game.

FAQ

Is Ember Spirit good in the current patch?

Yes. Ember Spirit sits at a 49.6% win rate across over 240 k ranked matches, making him a viable pick. He performs especially well against heroes like Witch Doctor (69.8% win) and Venomancer (62.5% win), while struggling more against Bane, Io, and Clinkz.

What lane does Ember Spirit play?

Ember Spirit is most commonly played in mid or as a safe‑lane carry. These lanes give him the farm needed to hit his early power spikes and allow safe use of Flame Guard against early magic harassment.

Who counters Ember Spirit?

The toughest match‑ups are Bane, Io, Clinkz, Treant Protector, Lycan, and Puck, where Ember’s win rates dip below 44 %. These heroes bring strong disables, burst magic, or sustained right‑click damage that can outpace Ember’s mobility and fire‑based defenses.
ember-spirit.counterHtml:
Ember Spirit’s strength lies in his burst mobility and magic‑damage output: Sleight of Fist lets him weave through fights, while Fire Remnants give him instant repositioning and extra damage. The most reliable way to shut him down is to lock him down before he can blink away, punish his low early‑game health pool, and negate the magic damage he relies on.

Why These Heroes Beat Ember Spirit

Bane

Bane’s Nightmare and Fiend’s Grip provide long‑duration disables that Ember cannot escape with Sleight of Fist or Fire Remnants, forcing him to sit still while Bane drains his mana and health. Tip: Keep a Nightmare on Ember whenever he initiates; the cooldown on his Fire Remnant dash is long enough that a single lock can win the trade.

Io

Io’s Tether and Relocate give constant vision and the ability to pull Ember into a controlled zone, while Overcharge grants allies extra attack speed to out‑damage his Flame Guard. Tip: Pair Io with a hard‑disable (e.g., Lion’s Hex) and use Relocate on Ember after he blinks, then burst him before he can reactivate a Remnant.

Clinkz

Clinkz’s Searing Arrows and Death Pact give him high single‑target physical damage that bypasses Ember’s magic‑damage shield. Clinkz’s Burning Barrage also silences Ember, preventing him from casting Flame Guard. Tip: Build Satanic early; when Ember dives in with Sleight of Fist, a well‑timed Death Pact + Searing Arrows combo can kill him before his Remnants return.

Treant Protector

Treant’s Nature’s Grasp and Overgrowth create a large, immobile area that Ember cannot escape with his dash, while Living Armor mitigates the physical damage from Ember’s attacks. Tip: Plant a Tree of Restoration near the lane; when Ember uses Fire Remnant to close distance, Overgrowth will instantly root him for a guaranteed kill.

Lycan

Lycan’s Summon Wolves and Feral Impulse give him sustained physical damage that ignores Ember’s magic shield, and his Shapeshift provides a health buffer against Ember’s burst. The Lycan’s Howl slows Ember’s movement, making his Remnant dashes predictable. Tip: Use a Wolf pack to block Ember’s path; when he tries to dash through, the wolves’ auto‑attacks and the slow from Howl will force a bad trade.

Drafting Against Ember Spirit

  • Prioritize heroes with long‑duration disables (e.g., Bane, Lion, Shadow Shaman).
  • Pick magic‑damage‑immune or high‑physical‑damage cores (Clinkz, Lycan, Troll Warlord).
  • Include at least one strong lane‑control hero that can create zones Ember cannot cross (Treant Protector, Dark Seer).
  • Consider early‑game burst heroes who can kill Ember before he acquires Fire Remnants (Pugna, Lina).

Laning Against Ember Spirit

  • Harass him before he gets a Fire Remnant; his early health pool is low.
  • Force him to use Sleight of Fist on creeps rather than heroes; the cooldown leaves him vulnerable.
  • Trade when his Flame Guard is on cooldown—his magic shield is the only thing that mitigates burst.
  • Use lane‑control abilities (e.g., Treant’s Nature’s Grasp) to block his dash routes.

Itemizing Against Ember Spirit

Black King Bar — prevents Ember’s Flame Guard and Sleight of Fist from dealing magic damage during team fights.
Scythe of Vyse — a reliable hard‑disable that Ember cannot blink out of, shutting down his mobility.
Ghost Scepter — makes Ember’s physical attacks from Sleight of Fist miss, forcing him to rely on his weaker magic damage.
Lotus Orb — reflects Ember’s Searing Chains and Flame Guard back at him, turning his own control into self‑damage.

enigma.name: Enigma
enigma.guideHtml:
Enigma remains a high‑impact disabler and initiator in the current meta, hovering just under a 50 % win rate (49.8 % across 135 k recent ranked games). His strength lies in team‑fight control with Event Horizon and Black Hole, while his early game is fragile but can snowball with proper lane play.

How to Play Enigma

Laning Phase

  • Use Malefice on the enemy off‑lane hero to apply a predictable stun every 2 seconds, trading damage and forcing them to miss last‑hits.
  • Pair Demonic Summoning with a safe creep wave; the three Eidolons provide extra lane pressure and early tower damage while costing only a modest amount of health.
  • Prioritize a Midnight Pulse on stacked neutral camps to secure additional farm and chip away at enemy health, especially against low‑armor heroes.
  • When facing ranged lane opponents (e.g., Sniper, Ember Spirit), keep distance and only engage with Malefice + Event Horizon after you have a reliable vision of their positioning.
  • Against aggressive melee heroes (e.g., Earthshaker, Terrorblade), pull the wave with Demonic Summoning and use Malefice to punish their attempts to dive you.

Mid Game

  • Hit level 6 and start looking for Event Horizon + Black Hole combos in 4‑v‑4 or 5‑v‑5 skirmishes; the synergy is the primary power spike.
  • Secure a Manta Style or Aghanim’s Scepter (if you prefer extra Eidolons) before committing to a mid‑lane split push, as the extra damage helps break high‑HP cores.
  • Prioritize vision around Roshan and enemy jungle; a well‑timed Black Hole on a Roshan contest can win the game outright.
  • Rotate with your team after a successful Event Horizon stun to capitalize on the enemy’s disarray, focusing on squishy back‑line heroes.

Late Game

  • Win condition: land a clean Black Hole on the enemy’s core while your team follows up with burst damage; Enigma’s damage scales with enemy HP via Midnight Pulse.
  • Position near the center of team fights but stay just out of enemy initiation range; a mis‑step can let the enemy’s Earthshaker or Silencer interrupt your channel.
  • Avoid prolonged fights without Black Hole—Enigma’s damage falls off against tanky late‑game heroes, and a missed Event Horizon can hand the advantage to counters like Sniper or Nature’s Prophet (both ~32 % win rates vs. Enigma).

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in the lane while you farm Eidolons.
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery after using Demonic Summoning.
  • Observer Ward — early vision to protect against ganks from mobile heroes (Sniper, Nature’s Prophet).

Core Items

  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Black Hole radius and adds a fourth Eidolon, dramatically increasing team‑fight impact.
  • Manta Style — provides a way to purge disables and adds extra damage; useful against Silencer and Earthshaker.
  • Black King Bar — essential for surviving burst from heroes like Ember Spirit and Terrorblade while channeling Black Hole.

Situational Items

  • Shiva’s Guard — armor and aura help survive against physical cores such as Lifestealer (where you already have a 79 % win rate).
  • Lotus Orb — reflects targeted spells; strong against Silencer and Ember Spirit.
  • Scythe of Vyse — extra hard‑disable when you need more control against mobile heroes like Nature’s Prophet.
  • Refresher Orb — allows a second Black Hole in late‑game fights, decisive against high‑HP heroes.
  • Aether Lens — increases cast range of Event Horizon and Black Hole, useful when you’re being kited by Sniper.

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑using Demonic Summoning early and dropping too much health, making you an easy gank target.
  • Casting Event Horizon without vision, allowing enemy initiators (Earthshaker, Silencer) to dodge and turn the fight.
  • Waiting for a perfect Black Hole and missing the window; delayed casts give the enemy time to purge or BKB out.
  • Neglecting split‑push potential; Enigma can take towers quickly with Eidolons and Midnight Pulse, but many players stay only in team fights.

FAQ

Is Enigma good in the current patch?

Yes. Enigma sits at a 49.8 % win rate in recent ranked matches, making him a viable pick, especially in coordinated team‑fight compositions where his Event Horizon + Black Hole combo shines.

What lane does Enigma play?

Enigma is typically played in the off‑lane (safelane) where he can farm Demonic Summoning Eidolons safely and use Malefice to harass the enemy solo hero.

Who counters Enigma?

Long‑range, high‑mobility heroes such as Sniper, Nature’s Prophet, and Terrorblade have the lowest win rates against Enigma (≈32–34 %), mainly because they can stay out of Event Horizon range and avoid being caught in Black Hole.
enigma.counterHtml:
Enigma’s threat comes from his massive team‑fight presence: a cheap Demonic Summoning, a zone‑control Event Horizon, and the game‑ending Black Hole. The key to shutting him down is denying the space and time he needs to set up his vortex, and forcing him to waste health on summons while he is still vulnerable.

Why These Heroes Beat Enigma

Sniper

Sniper’s extreme range lets him harass Enigma before he can get close enough to cast Event Horizon or Black Hole, and his Assassinate can finish Enigma when he’s low on health from Demonic Summoning.
Tip: Position on high ground and use Take Aim to push the lane, forcing Enigma to retreat or waste his summons on a dead‑weight target.

Nature's Prophet

Nature's Prophet can split‑push and appear anywhere with Teleportation, denying Enigma the farm needed for his summons and forcing him to split his attention. His Sprout can trap Enigma’s eidolons, and Wrath of Nature damages Enigma’s low‑health Eidolons, reducing his overall damage output.
Tip: Keep a Teleport ready to join fights only after Enigma’s Black Hole is on cooldown, then burst him with Nature’s Call.

Terrorblade

Terrorblade’s Metamorphosis gives him massive ranged damage that can shred Enigma’s low‑health Eidolons and the hero himself, while Sunder can turn Enigma’s health‑sacrificing Demonic Summoning against him. The illusion army also forces Enigma to waste Black Hole on non‑threats.
Tip: Initiate with Reflection to block Enigma’s Malefice stun, then drop Sunder when Enigma’s health dips below 30%.

Silencer

Silence from Global Silence or Last Word prevents Enigma from casting Event Horizon and Black Hole, effectively neutering his combo. Silencer’s Glaives of Wisdom also pierce through Eidolon clusters, dealing consistent damage.
Tip: Time Global Silence just before Enigma starts channeling Black Hole; follow up with a burst of Mana Leak to keep his mana low for summons.

Ember Spirit

Ember’s Sleight of Fist can dodge the stun from Malefice and quickly burst the three Eidolons, while Flame Guard provides magic immunity against Midnight Pulse and the damage from Black Hole. His mobility lets him escape the pull of Event Horizon.
Tip: Use Fire Remnant to reposition behind Enigma after he casts Event Horizon, then unleash Sleight of Fist on the Eidolons.

Drafting Against Enigma

  • Prioritize heroes with long range or global presence (e.g., Sniper, Nature’s Prophet, Terrorblade).
  • Pick strong silence or spell‑interrupt abilities (Silencer, Night Stalker).
  • Include high‑mobility heroes that can dodge Event Horizon and Black Hole (Ember Spirit, Puck).
  • Consider early‑game aggression heroes that can pressure Enima before he can afford Demonic Summoning.

Laning Against Enigma

  • Harass him with ranged attacks to force early Demonic Summoning and drain his health.
  • Trade when his Malefice cooldown is up; his stun leaves him vulnerable to counter‑attacks.
  • Push the lane aggressively after he uses Event Horizon, as his mobility is limited.
  • Keep the lane near tower range to deny him safe space for Midnight Pulse.

Itemizing Against Enigma

Manta Style — dispels Malefice stun and Black Hole pull, while the split images pressure his Eidolons.
Ghost Scepter — makes you untargetable by Midnight Pulse and the physical damage from Eidolons.
Eul’s Scepter — cyclones Enigma, interrupting Event Horizon and buying time for your team to reposition.
Aghanim’s Shard (Silencer) — grants Global Silence, shutting down Enigma’s combo entirely.

enchantress.name: Enchantress
enchantress.guideHtml:
Enchantress is a scaling, ranged support/pusher who thrives on long‑range harassment and relentless lane pressure. On patch 7.41 her overall pub win rate sits at 47.8% over 93,985 ranked games, placing her solidly in the mid‑tier of support heroes.

How to Play Enchantress

Laning Phase

  • Impetus active on every attack lets you punish enemies that stay far from you; use it to harass ranged off‑laners and force them to pull back.
  • Enchant on enemy heroes provides a brief dispel and a 3.5 s slow while granting you bonus attack range—use it to secure last‑hits and deny creeps against aggressive supports.
  • Nature's Attendants should be toggled on when you or your lane partner take burst damage (e.g., from Keeper of the Light or Marci) to sustain through early harassment.
  • Position near the edge of the lane to maximize Impetus damage while staying safe from early ganks; keep a mental note of enemy Slardar or Juggernaut who can close the distance quickly.
  • If the enemy lane has a strong early tower‑pusher (e.g., Ursa), use Sproink to dodge their initial burst and immediately follow up with an Impetus attack on the farthest creep to keep lane equilibrium.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 12 when Impetus reaches max damage and you unlock Little Friends—start grouping with your cores to apply constant pressure on enemy towers.
  • Use Little Friends on high‑value targets (e.g., Doom, Shadow Fiend) to force them to fight under your creeps while your allies focus them.
  • Prioritize Nature's Attendants in team fights; the heal over time can out‑heal sustained AoE damage from heroes like Disruptor or Clockwerk.
  • When you have Rabble‑Rouser, pull neutral camps into lane or jungle fights; the extra damage synergizes well against tanky front‑liners such as Slardar.

Late Game

  • Win condition: stay at maximum attack range, continuously trigger Impetus on enemy heroes, and force them to retreat or waste cooldowns.
  • Positioning is critical—keep behind your frontline, use Sproink to dodge key disables (e.g., Keeper of the Light's Will‑of‑the‑Wisp) and instantly launch a long‑range Impetus on the two farthest foes.
  • Losing the game usually comes from being caught out of range by burst heroes (e.g., Juggernaut's Omni‑Slash) or from lacking Nature's Attendants when the enemy has high AoE sustain.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango + Healing Salve — basic sustain for early harassment.
  • Faerie Fire — cheap burst to secure last‑hits when Impetus isn’t active.
  • Observer Ward — vision to avoid early ganks from mobile heroes like Marci.

Core Items

  • Mekansm — strong AoE heal that synergizes with Nature's Attendants and keeps you alive against burst lineups.
  • Glimmer Cape — provides magic immunity for surviving disables from Keeper of the Light and Doom.
  • Force Staff — essential for escaping Slardar’s Corrosive Haze or repositioning to maintain Impetus distance.
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Little Friends to affect a larger radius and grants extra attack/move speed, amplifying your push and team‑fight presence.

Situational Items

  • Solar Crest — against high‑armor heroes like Slardar or Ursa, increasing your damage output.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target disables (e.g., Doom's Devour or Marci's Rebound) and provides armor.
  • Heaven’s Halberd — strong counter to right‑click heavy carries such as Juggernaut and Ursa.
  • Black King Bar — only if you must survive prolonged magical bursts from Disruptor or Shadow Fiend.
  • Guardian Greaves — swap Mekansm for extra armor and movement speed when you need more survivability in late‑game sieges.

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑extending without Sproink – forgetting to leap back when enemies close the gap, leading to early deaths against mobile heroes.
  • Neglecting Nature's Attendants – turning it off during fights wastes a massive sustain tool, especially versus AoE damage from Disruptor.
  • Using Impetus on nearby targets – the ability scales with distance; hitting close‑range creeps wastes its damage potential.
  • Chasing kills instead of pushing – Enchantress’s true strength is sustained tower damage, not 1‑v‑1 duels; over‑committing lets counters like Keeper of the Light snowball.

FAQ

Is Enchantress good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 47.8% win rate across nearly 94k games, Enchantress remains a viable support/pusher. Her scaling damage and strong sustain make her especially effective in mid‑game team fights, though she can struggle against very mobile or burst‑heavy heroes.

What lane does Enchantress play?

Enchantress is typically played in the safelane (hard lane) as a support, but she can also be flexed to the offlane when a team needs extra pushing power. Her lane presence shines against heroes like Earthshaker (59.6% win) and Disruptor (58.9% win).

Who counters Enchantress?

The toughest matchups are Keeper of the Light (38.2% win), Marci (39.0%), Slardar (40.0%), Juggernaut (44.2%), Doom (45.2%) and Shadow Fiend (45.3%). These heroes either close the distance quickly, apply heavy burst, or have strong disables that negate her long‑range harassment.
enchantress.counterHtml:
Enchantress thrives on her long‑range Impetus damage and the relentless pressure from her “Little Friends” swarm, turning even a single creep into a moving damage source. The key to shutting her down is to deny her the space she needs to kite and to punish her low early‑game health and lack of escape tools.

Why These Heroes Beat Enchantress

Keeper of the Light

Keeper’s Mana Leak and Will‑of‑the‑Wisp constantly burn Enchantress’s mana, preventing her from spamming Impetus and Nature’s Attendants. His Spirit Form provides a magic‑immune bubble that blocks Enchantser’s Enchant and Little Friends while allowing him to close the distance with Recall. Tip: Use Recall on the lane to pull Keeper into a 2‑vs‑1 fight when Enchantress overextends.

Marci

Marci’s Dispose and Rebound give her burst damage and a reliable gap‑closer that can jump onto Enchantress before she can kite with Sproink. Unleash applies a strong stun that interrupts Enchant’s charm and the Little Friends activation. Tip: Initiate with Rebound from a side lane, then follow up with Dispose for a quick kill.

Slardar

Slardar’s Slithereen Crush applies a hard stun and armor reduction, making Enchantress’s Impetus hits far more lethal while also disabling her Untouchable slow. His Guardian Sprint lets him chase her down, and Corrosive Haze reduces her armor permanently, crippling her damage output. Tip: Time a Corrosive Haze before a 2‑v‑1 fight; the armor loss stacks quickly against her ranged attacks.

Juggernaut

Juggernaut’s Blade Fury provides magic immunity and high burst damage that can wipe Enchantress before she can react with Sproink. Healing Ward out‑heals Nature’s Attendants, and Omni‑Slash can jump onto Enchantress even when she’s trying to keep distance. Tip: Use Blade Fury to block the first Impetus hit, then follow with Healing Ward to sustain through her harassment.

Doom

Doom’s Doom ultimate silences Enchantress, nullifying Impetus, Enchant, and Nature’s Attendants for 5 seconds—exactly the window where she is most vulnerable. Devour also removes her “Little Friends” creeps, denying her the swarm damage. Tip: Save Doom for the moment Enchantress activates Impetus on a high‑value target; the silence will end her damage spike instantly.

Drafting Against Enchantress

  • Prioritize heroes with reliable gap‑closers or hard disables (stuns, silences).
  • Pick magic‑immune or burst‑damage heroes to survive her early Impetus harass.
  • Ban or avoid heroes that give her extra movement speed or attack range (e.g., Blink‑based initiators).
  • Include at least one hero with strong lane pressure to force her out of the safe farming zone.

Laning Against Enchantress

  • Trade when her Impetus is on cooldown; her attacks revert to low‑damage auto‑attacks.
  • Harass early with ranged harass that forces her to use Nature’s Attendants defensively, draining her mana.
  • Punish her after she uses Sproink—the leap leaves her vulnerable and slows her attack speed.
  • Keep the lane tight; the closer she is, the less Impetus damage she can deal.

Itemizing Against Enchantress

Mekansm — provides a burst heal that outpaces Nature’s Attendants and grants armor to survive her Impetus spikes.
Ghost Scepter — makes you untargetable by her Impetus attacks, forcing her to rely on melee heroes or creeps.
Black King Bar — grants magic immunity, nullifying Enchant, Little Friends, and the damage from her Impetus when she tries to combo with other magic sources.
Diffusal Blade — burns her mana, limiting the frequency of Impetus and Nature’s Attendants, and the purge can remove Enchant slows.

faceless-void.name: Faceless Void
faceless-void.guideHtml:
Faceless Void remains a high‑skill carry whose win‑rate sits at 49.4% over 373,955 ranked games on patch 7.41, placing him solidly in the middle of the meta. His toolkit—Time Walk, Time Dilation, Time Lock, Chronosphere and the new Distortion Field—makes him a potent initiator and escape artist, but his effectiveness swings heavily on matchup and timing.

How to Play Faceless Void

Laning Phase

  • Time Walk is your primary safety tool; use it to dodge early harass and to back‑track damage taken in the last 2 seconds, especially against aggressive mid‑lane heroes like Tidehunter or Axe.
  • Time Lock procs on every attack; aim for melee creeps and the enemy hero to build early damage and apply the extra attack that can trigger a stun‑like lock.
  • Distortion Field gives you and nearby allies a 40 % projectile‑speed slow; position near your carry to mitigate enemy right‑click pressure from heroes such as Sniper and Juggernaut.
  • Prioritize a sentry or observer ward at the rune spot; Void’s Chronosphere is useless without vision, and early enemy vision often leads to the toughest matchups (Tidehunter, Sniper).
  • Against lane opponents with strong early damage (e.g., Axe, Keeper of the Light), play conservatively: farm safely with Time Walk, and only contest when you have a Time Lock proc or an ally’s support is present.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at 20 minutes: first Manta Style or Black King Bar plus a Blink Dagger enables a reliable Chronosphere initiation.
  • Map control: use Time Dilation on high‑cooldown heroes (e.g., Storm Spirit, Weaver) before team fights; each stack slows their cooldowns, making them less threatening inside Chronosphere.
  • Pick‑offs: look for isolated heroes with low mobility (e.g., Templar Assassin, Dawnbreaker)—your Chronosphere can secure kills even without a full team.
  • Objective timing: aim to take Roshan after a successful Chronosphere on the enemy’s core; the extra damage from Time Lock and your high attack speed make you a strong Aegis carrier.

Late Game

  • Win condition: secure a clean Chronosphere on the enemy backline, then focus the high‑damage hero (often the enemy carry). Your Time Lock procs add burst that can finish heroes before they escape.
  • Positioning: stay near the center of the Chronosphere; the new Distortion Field protects you and allies from projectile‑based heroes like Sniper and Weaver.
  • What loses the game: getting caught outside Chronosphere by heroes with strong AoE or silence (e.g., Axe’s Berserker’s Call, Keeper of the Light’s Chakra Magic). Losing vision or failing to time Chronosphere correctly often leads to a loss.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane.
  • Healing Salve — emergency health against early harass.
  • Quelling Blade — faster creep last‑hits.
  • Iron Branch ×2 — cheap stats and can be later built into a Magic Wand.
  • Observer Ward — early vision for rune control and enemy movement.

Core Items

  • Power Treads — attack speed and attribute flexibility; switch to Agility for damage spikes.
  • Manta Style — provides the attack speed needed for frequent Time Lock procs and a way to dispel silences from heroes like Keeper of the Light.
  • Blink Dagger — essential for positioning Chronosphere on key targets.
  • Black King Bar — protects you while channeling Chronosphere against heavy magic damage (e.g., Muerta, Storm Spirit).

Situational Items

  • Satanic — survivability against burst heroes (Axe, Juggernaut).
  • Satanic — provides lifesteal to offset damage taken during Chronosphere.
  • Abyssal Blade — lockdown for heroes that can break out of Chronosphere (e.g., Tidehunter).
  • Heart of Tarrasque — extreme durability when you need to survive long fights against tanky heroes like Abaddon.
  • Butterfly — extra evasion against right‑click heroes (Sniper, Weaver).
  • Linken’s Sphere — block single‑target disables from Keeper of the Light or Muerta.
  • Shiva’s Guard — armor and AoE slow to counter high‑damage physical carries (Juggernaut, Sniper).

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑committing Chronosphere without vision – leads to wasted ult and easy enemy escape.
  • Neglecting Time Dilation – failing to stack it on cooldown‑heavy heroes reduces Chronosphere’s impact.
  • Positioning too far from allies – Distortion Field only protects units within 1200 range; staying isolated makes you vulnerable to projectile heroes.
  • Rushing Blink before a reliable farm item – without sufficient damage, Chronosphere fails to secure kills and can be punished by counter‑initiators.

FAQ

Is Faceless Void good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 49.4% win‑rate on over 370 k ranked games, Void sits near the median of carries. His win‑rate improves dramatically against heroes like Templar Assassin (61.9%) and Dawnbreaker (59.7%), while he struggles against Tidehunter (36.2%) and Sniper (39.6%). Proper itemization and timing can mitigate his weaker matchups.

What lane does Faceless Void play?

Faceless Void is traditionally a safe‑lane carry (radiant bottom or dire top) to allow him to farm safely with Time Walk and Time Lock. He benefits from a support that can provide early vision and occasional disables to keep aggressive lane opponents in check.

Who counters Faceless Void?

The toughest matchups are Tidehunter, Sniper, Juggernaut, Muerta, Axe, and Keeper of the Light, where Void’s win‑rate drops below 42 %. These heroes either out‑range him, have strong early damage, or can silence/disrupt his Chronosphere. Building early defensive items and securing vision are essential to survive against them.
faceless-void.counterHtml:
Faceless Void’s threat comes from his game‑changing Chronosphere and the burst damage he can lock onto a single target with Time Lock. The key to shutting him down is to deny him the time and space to land a clean Chronosphere and to punish his low early‑game durability before he can accumulate the items needed for a decisive late‑game push.

Why These Heroes Beat Faceless Void

Tidehunter

Tidehunter’s Ravage can hit Void and any allies inside the Chronosphere, breaking the sphere’s isolation and dealing massive damage that Void cannot dodge. Use Anchor Smash to lower Void’s armor before the fight, and time Ravage just as Void lands his Chronosphere for a guaranteed kill.

Sniper

Sniper’s Assassinate has an extremely long cast range, allowing him to finish Void from outside Chronosphere range while Void’s Time Walk can’t close the gap fast enough. Pair with Headshot to chip away at Void’s health during the early laning phase, and keep a Blink Dagger ready to reposition if Void tries to engage with a Chronosphere.

Juggernaut

Juggernaut’s Omni‑Slash can spin through the Chronosphere, dealing damage to Void and any allies trapped inside, while Blade Fury provides magic immunity that blocks Void’s Time Lock procs. Prioritize a quick Healing Ward after a Chronosphere fight to sustain through the burst.

Muerta

Muerta’s Dead Shot applies a strong slow and damage over time that stacks quickly on Void, and her Soul Release can purge the Chronosphere’s debuff, allowing her to escape or re‑engage. Use Shackles to tether Void before he can Time Walk away, forcing him into a vulnerable position.

Axe

Axe’s Berserker’s Call forces Void to attack him, triggering Void’s Time Lock on Axe’s own attacks and granting Axe a guaranteed stun that can interrupt a Chronosphere cast. Follow up with Counter Helix for splash damage that punishes Void’s low health pool.

Drafting Against Faceless Void

  • Prioritize heroes with long‑range disables or global ultimates that can hit Void outside Chronosphere.
  • Pick heroes with strong early‑game damage or armor‑reduction to exploit Void’s fragility before his core items.
  • Ban or avoid heroes that provide heavy mobility (e.g., Anti‑Mage) which can easily escape Chronosphere.
  • Include at least one magic‑immune or purge‑capable hero to neutralize Time Lock and Chronosphere effects.

Laning Against Faceless Void

  • Harass with ranged attacks and harass abilities; Void’s Time Walk only rewinds damage taken in the last 2 seconds, so constant poke forces him to waste it.
  • Punish his Time Dilation stacks by spacing out your spell usage; the more stacks he has, the slower your cooldowns become.
  • Trade when Void is low on health and before he has a Scepter or Manta Style, as his survivability drops dramatically.
  • Force him to use Time Walk defensively by baiting aggressive trades; after he lands, immediately follow with a stun or burst.

Itemizing Against Faceless Void

Manta Style — breaks silences and dispels Chronosphere’s slow, allowing you to dodge or escape his ultimate.

Black King Bar — grants magic immunity, nullifying Time Lock procs and the damage from Chronosphere‑trapped enemies.

Ghost Scepter — makes you ethereal, preventing Void’s attacks and Time Lock from affecting you while you reposition.

Eul’s Scepter of Divinity – cyclones Void out of his Chronosphere, buying time for your team to regroup or follow up with damage.

Abyssal Blade – provides a hard stun that can interrupt Chronosphere casting and lock Void in place, removing his primary threat.

grimstroke.name: Grimstroke
grimstroke.guideHtml:
Grimstroke remains a solid support‑nuker in the current meta, posting a 51.5% win‑rate across over 235 k ranked games on patch 7.41. His toolkit—strong lane control, a game‑changing Soulbind, and scalable damage—keeps him relevant despite a few tough match‑ups.

How to Play Grimstroke

Laning Phase

  • Use Ink Swell on yourself or the carry to grant movement speed and apply early poke; the 3‑second stun after the damage pulse can punish aggressive opponents.
  • Pair Stroke of Fate (curved or straight via alt‑cast) with your lane partner’s disables to chain damage and slow multiple creeps or heroes.
  • Phantom's Embrace is an excellent tool against melee heroes like Slardar—latch, silence, and force a disengage before they can initiate.
  • Prioritize a Soulbind on a high‑damage enemy (e.g., Sniper) and bind them to your own carry; the extra damage and forced positioning can swing early trades.
  • Watch for the toughest lane match‑ups (Shadow Shaman, Sniper, Slardar, Batrider, Techies, Monkey King) and play more conservatively, using Ink Trail on yourself to reduce incoming damage.

Mid Game

  • Aim for a Soulbind + Ink Swell + Stroke of Fate combo on enemy cores during 2‑v‑2 skirmishes; the bind spreads your damage and disables across both teams.
  • Secure vision around Roshan and high‑traffic jungle paths; Grimstroke’s Ink Swell can quickly turn a contested area into a damage zone.
  • Look for power spikes at level 12 (max Soulbind) and level 16 (upgraded Ink Swell stun radius). Initiate fights when you have a reliable Soulbind on a key enemy.
  • When your team has strong AoE ultimates (e.g., Tidehunter, Enigma), position Ink Swell on the primary target to maximize the stun and follow‑up damage.

Late Game

  • Win condition: lock down the enemy carry with Soulbind and follow up with Ink Swell stun + team ultimates; the combined burst often decides team fights.
  • Position near the front line but stay behind a frontline hero; your Ink Trail reduces incoming damage, letting you stay alive to cast Soulbind repeatedly.
  • Avoid over‑extending into pick‑heavy heroes like Monkey King or Batrider—if you miss a Soulbind, you become an easy target for their burst.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane.
  • Healing Salve — emergency health.
  • Observer Ward — early vision, crucial against Techies and Batrider.
  • Sentry Ward — detect invisible traps and wards.
  • Clarity — mana for early Ink Swell and Soulbind.

Core Items

  • Tranquil Boots — movement speed for roaming and Ink Swell shroud, plus passive health regen.
  • Glimmer Cape — survivability against burst (Sniper, Monkey King) and can be used on a bound ally.
  • Aether Lens — increases cast range of Soulbind and Ink Swell, making binds safer.
  • Force Staff — extra mobility to reposition yourself or a bound ally, especially against Slardar’s impale.

Situational Items

  • Lotus Orb — reflects targeted spells like Shadow Shaman’s Hex or Techies’ Stasis Trap.
  • Ghost Scepter — counter physical burst from Sniper or Monkey King.
  • Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — additional disable and self‑save; works well with Soulbind to lock enemies in the cyclone.
  • Shiva’s Guard — armor and AoE slow against right‑click heroes; useful vs Slardar and Batrider.
  • Aeon Disk — prevents death from sudden burst in late‑game fights.

Common Mistakes

  • Casting Soulbind on the wrong target – binding a low‑impact hero wastes the ability; aim for the enemy carry or a hero with strong AoE spells.
  • Using Ink Swell on a hero that dies quickly – the stun and damage only trigger after 3 seconds; apply it to allies with survivability or to heroes that can stay alive long enough.
  • Neglecting vision – without wards Grimstroke’s long‑range setup is blind; early wards prevent Techies’ mines and Batrider’s fire traps.
  • Over‑committing with Phantom's Embrace on tanky heroes – the latch damage and silence are less effective on heroes like Slardar; save it for squishier targets or to finish off low‑HP enemies.

FAQ

Is Grimstroke good in the current patch?

Yes. Grimstroke sits at a healthy 51.5% win‑rate on patch 7.41, making him a reliable support pick with strong lane control and a game‑changing Soulbind.

What lane does Grimstroke play?

Grimstroke is typically played as a position‑5 support in the safe lane, but he can also function in the off‑lane as a position‑4 when paired with a strong carry.

Who counters Grimstroke?

The toughest match‑ups are against Shadow Shaman, Sniper, Slardar, Batrider, Techies, and Monkey King, where Grimstroke’s win‑rate drops to around 39‑41%. Their strong disables, burst, or mobility make it hard to land Soulbind and Ink Swell safely.
grimstroke.counterHtml:
Grimstroke’s strength lies in his global‑scale crowd control and damage amplification: Soulbind links enemies to allies, Ink Swell bursts damage in a wide area, and Stroke of Fate scales with each hero it hits. The quickest way to neutralize him is to deny him safe targets for his binds and to force him into fights where his spells can’t land on multiple heroes.

Why These Heroes Beat Grimstroke

Shadow Shaman

Shadow Shaman’s long‑range disables (Hex and Shackles) outrange Grimstroke’s Stroke of Fate and can lock him down before he can land a Soulbind. His Aghanim’s Scepter‑upgraded Shackles also prevents the bound pair from moving, nullifying the core synergy of Soulbind. Tip: Initiate with Hex → Shackles on Grimstroke while your team follows up with burst damage.

Sniper

Sniper’s extreme attack range lets him stay out of Ink Swell’s AoE and avoid the phantom latch of Phantom’s Embrace. The combination of Headshot and Assassinate punishes Grimstroke’s low mobility, and Sniper’s Take Damage aura reduces the effectiveness of Ink Swell’s damage over time. Tip: Position behind a creep wave and use Take Damage to mitigate any lingering Ink Trail damage.

Slardar

Slardar’s Amplify Damage instantly reduces Grimstroke’s armor, making his relatively low burst from Ink Swell and Stroke of Fate far less threatening. Corrosive Haze also silences Grimstroke, preventing him from casting Soulbind or Ink Swell during a fight. Tip: Use Corrosive Haze early to silence Grimstroke, then follow with a well‑timed Amplify Damage before he can bind.

Batrider

Batrider’s Flaming Lasso drags Grimstroke away from his allies, breaking the distance requirement for Soulbind to be useful. The fire damage over time also burns through Ink Swell’s damage shield, and Batrider’s mobility lets him dodge Stroke of Fate’s linear path. Tip: Catch Grimstroke with Flaming Lasso right after he casts Ink Swell; the stun and pull cancel the burst.

Techies

Techies’ mines and Stasis Trap force Grimstroke to move cautiously, denying him the straight‑line positioning needed for Stroke of Fate and Phantom’s Embrace. A well‑placed Remote Mine can instantly kill Grimstroke before he can bind anyone, and the constant threat of mines makes Ink Swell’s channeling unsafe. Tip: Plant mines in the lane and near high‑traffic jungle paths to punish Grimstroke’s attempts to chase or bind.

Drafting Against Grimstroke

  • Prioritize heroes with long‑range disables or silences (e.g., Shadow Shaman, Silencer, Lion).
  • Choose tanky or high‑armor heroes that can survive Ink Swell’s burst (e.g., Bristleback, Timbersaw).
  • Include at least one hero with strong single‑target burst to punish the lone‑target focus of Phantom’s Embrace.
  • Consider early game aggression heroes that can force Grimstroke out of lane before he gets his core items.

Laning Against Grimstroke

  • Harass him before he lands a Soulbind; his early game damage is low without a bound pair.
  • Keep a minimum distance of 600 units to stay out of Ink Swell’s initial damage radius and avoid the phantom latch.
  • Use creep equilibrium to block his Stroke of Fate line, forcing him to waste the ability on empty space.
  • Punish the 3‑second channel of Ink Swell with a quick stun or burst damage; he is vulnerable while the spell is casting.

Itemizing Against Grimstroke

Ghost Scepter — blocks the physical component of Ink Swell’s burst and Phantom’s Embrace latch.
Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — cyclone interrupts Soulbind and Ink Swell, buying time for your team to reposition.
Black King Bar — grants magic immunity, rendering Soulbind, Ink Swell stun, and Stroke of Fate ineffective.
Heaven’s Halberd — disarms Grimstroke, preventing him from casting Ink Swell or Phantom’s Embrace while you focus him down.

gyrocopter.name: Gyrocopter
gyrocopter.guideHtml:
Gyrocopter is a high‑damage, mobile carry who excels at burst AoE damage and sustained harassment with his rockets. In the current 7.41 meta his overall pub win rate sits at 42.8% over 109 k recent ranked games, placing him as a solid but not dominant pick. He thrives when he can leverage his burst and mobility against heroes that lack reliable disables.

How to Play Gyrocopter

Laning Phase

  • Use Rocket Barrage early to harass melee off‑laners and secure last hits; the 3‑second radius is great for denying creep equilibrium.
  • Pair Flak Cannon with a short‑range creep wave to clear waves quickly and force enemy supports to use costly spells.
  • When the enemy has a stun (e.g., Lion, Earthshaker), keep Homing Missile on cooldown and rely on mobility from Afterburner to dodge the initiation.
  • Prioritize a safe lane (safe lane for Radiant, off‑lane for Dire) against hard counters like Nyx Assassin and Treant Protector, whose win rates against you are sub‑30%.
  • Keep an eye on enemy vision; the missile can be intercepted by towers or spell‑immune units, so aim for isolated targets.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 12 when Flak Cannon gains its full 12‑second duration—start joining team fights and split‑pushing.
  • Use Call Down to zone out enemy initiators (e.g., Razor, Keeper of the Light) and force them to reposition; the staggered missiles are excellent for breaking formations.
  • Secure objectives after winning a fight; Gyrocopter’s mobility lets him scout Roshan and take towers while enemies are on cooldown.
  • When you have Afterburner active, chase down fleeing heroes; the speed boost synergizes with your rocket damage to finish them off.

Late Game

  • Win condition: leverage Flak Cannon + Rocket Barrage in team fights to melt high‑HP cores (e.g., Alchemist, Shadow Demon) while staying out of enemy disables.
  • Position near the front line but keep a retreat path; a well‑timed Afterburner can save you from Axe or Earthshaker initiations.
  • Losing the game usually stems from being caught by hard disables (Nyx Assassin, Razor) before your cooldowns are up, so always track enemy cooldowns and use fog of war.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane against harassment.
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery after rocket trades.
  • Slippers of Agility — early damage boost for last hitting and early Rocket Barrage damage.
  • Iron Branch ×2 — cheap stats and can be later used for a Magic Wand.

Core Items

  • Maelstrom — synergizes with Flak Cannon for massive AoE damage in fights.
  • Manta Style — provides a second Flak Cannon instance and a way to dispel silences from Keeper of the Light.
  • Black King Bar — essential against heavy magical burst from Razor, Shadow Demon, and Keeper of the Light.

Situational Items

  • Satanic — survivability against burst heroes like Axe and Sven (who are easier matchups).
  • Butterfly — evasion against right‑click heroes such as Sven and Axe, and extra damage.
  • Monkey King Bar — counters evasion from heroes like Templar Assassin and ensures Homing Missile lands.
  • Abyssal Blade — lock down a key enemy carry when you lack reliable disables.
  • Linken’s Sphere — blocks single‑target disables from Nyx Assassin or Razor.

Common Mistakes

  • Spamming Homing Missile without checking for enemy towers or spell‑immune units, causing the missile to be wasted.
  • Ignoring Afterburner cooldowns and overextending into enemy vision, leading to easy catches by Nyx Assassin or Razor.
  • Building pure damage items (e.g., Butterfly) without a defensive item like BKB, making you vulnerable to magical burst.
  • Forgetting to use Flak Cannon on creep waves, which results in slower lane progression and missed farm.

FAQ

Is Gyrocopter good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 42.8% win rate across over 109 k recent ranked matches, Gyrocopter is a viable carry, especially against easier matchups like Sven (60% win) and Earthshaker (57.7% win). His burst AoE damage and mobility keep him relevant despite some tough counters.

What lane does Gyrocopter play?

Gyrocopter is typically played in the safe lane (carry position) for Radiant and the off‑lane for Dire, allowing him to farm safely while using Rocket Barrage and Flak Cannon to harass enemy supports.

Who counters Gyrocopter?

The hardest counters are Nyx Assassin (27.5% win), Treant Protector (27.8%), and Razor (35.6%)—all of which have strong disables or armor‑based damage that mitigate his rockets. Building defensive items like BKB and positioning to avoid their disables is crucial.
gyrocopter.counterHtml:
Gyrocopter’s burst damage, mobility from Afterburner, and area‑of‑effect threat make him a nightmare in mid‑lane and team fights. The key to shutting him down is to deny his ability to land a clean Homing Missile or Flak Cannon combo while punishing his low early‑game survivability and reliance on vision.

Why These Heroes Beat Gyrocopter

Nyx Assassin

Nyx’s Mana Burn and Spiked Carapace punish Gyrocopter’s high‑damage, low‑mana playstyle, while Vendetta provides a silent gap‑closer that can ambush Gyrocopter before he can activate Afterburner.
Tip: Use a quick Impale on Gyrocopter’s first wave of rockets to silence his Flak Cannon and force a disengage.

Treant Protector

Treant’s Nature’s Grasp and Living Armor grant massive lane sustain, outlasting Gyrocopter’s early burst, while Overgrowth roots him, preventing the Afterburner chase and Homing Missile lock‑on.
Tip: Drop a Living Armor on your core carry and time Overgrowth when Gyrocopter tries to dive with Call Down.

Razor

Razor’s Static Link drains Gyrocopter’s attack damage, severely weakening Flak Cannon and Rocket Barrage, and Eye of the Storm gives armor against his physical burst. Unstable Current also silences Gyrocopter, canceling Homing Missile.
Tip: Initiate with Static Link as soon as Gyrocopter lands his first rocket; the damage drain compounds quickly.

Keeper of the Light

Keeper’s Illuminate and Chakra Magic provide constant mana pressure, forcing Gyrocopter to play conservatively, while Blinding Light disables his attack‑based Flak Cannon. Spirit Form offers a safe escape from Afterburner chases.
Tip: Keep Illuminate on cooldown and pop Blinding Light right before Gyrocopter fires Homing Missile to miss the stun.

Alchemist

Alchemist’s Acid Spray and Unstable Concoction punish Gyrocopter’s low health pool, and Greevil’s Greed gives him the gold to out‑item Gyrocopter early. Chemical Rage provides massive survivability against Rocket Barrage.
Tip: Stack Acid Spray in the lane; Gyrocopter’s rockets will waste damage on the poison ticks instead of the hero.

Drafting Against Gyrocopter

  • Prioritize heroes with silence or spell‑block (e.g., Silencer, Counterspell heroes) to cancel Homing Missile.
  • Pick high‑armor or damage‑reduction heroes to blunt Rocket Barrage and Flak Cannon (e.g., Bristleback, Treant).
  • Include early‑game burst or mana‑drain heroes to exploit Gyrocopter’s fragile laning phase.
  • Consider mobility‑heavy picks that can outrun Afterburner and close the gap quickly (e.g., Anti‑Mage, Puck).

Laning Against Gyrocopter

  • Trade when Gyrocopter’s Afterburner is on cooldown; his attack speed boost is gone.
  • Harass with spell‑damage or mana‑burn before he can land a Homing Missile—the missile can be dodged if the target is stunned.
  • Force him to use Rocket Barrage on creeps; the AoE damage is wasted and his mana drops.
  • Punish his early lack of sustain by zoning him with tower aggression or creep equilibrium that denies safe rocket launches.

Itemizing Against Gyrocopter

Eul’s Scepter — provides a reliable way to cyclone Gyrocopter, canceling Homing Missile and delaying Rocket Barrage.
Ghost Scepter — makes you immune to his physical Flak Cannon attacks, forcing him to rely on less‑effective spells.
Black King Bar — blocks the stun from Homing Missile and the damage from Call Down, letting you stay in fights.
Pipe of Insight — grants magic resistance to all of Gyrocopter’s magic damage sources, especially Rocket Barrage and Call Down.
