hoodwink.name: Hoodwink
hoodwink.guideHtml:
Hoodwink is a mobile, burst‑damage support hero who excels at pick‑offs and lane harassment with her ranged attacks and tree‑based tricks. In patch 7.41 her overall win rate sits at 48.1% over 361 k recent ranked games, placing her slightly below the median support but still viable thanks to strong early pressure and escape tools.

How to Play Hoodwink

Laning Phase

  • Acorn Shot on creep waves to add extra damage and slow; the bounce can harass multiple enemy heroes when they stand near trees.
  • Bushwhack + a planted tree (from Acorn Shot or natural) to set early‑game stun zones; aim near the enemy’s pull‑creep or a stacked neutral camp for guaranteed lock‑down.
  • Use Scurry to dodge incoming harass and to chase down low‑HP enemies that step into your Bushwhack radius.
  • Decoy can be cast pre‑emptively when you suspect a gank; the invisible movement speed lets you reposition while the illusion draws skillshots.
  • Prioritize a support‑oriented lane (safe lane with a reliable carry) against heroes like Underlord or Silencer, where your win rates are highest (63.3% and 59.2% respectively).

Mid Game

  • Look for Hunter’s Boomerang + Sharpshooter combos: Boomerang slows and applies vulnerability, then charge Sharpshooter for a break and massive burst.
  • Scurry + Bushwhack is a potent gank tool; sprint into the enemy jungle, plant a tree, and instantly stun a target caught in the net.
  • Power spike occurs at level 6 (Decoy) and level 12 (Sharpshooter). Use Decoy to initiate or escape, then follow up with a charged Sharpshooter for a game‑changing kill.
  • Avoid prolonged fights against Naga Siren, Keeper of the Light, and Lycan—your win rates against them are sub‑40% (33.3‑38.6%). Focus on split‑pushing and picking off isolated heroes instead.

Late Game

  • Win condition: Use your mobility (Scurry, Decoy) to isolate and burst squishy carries with Sharpshooter, then secure kills with Acorn Shot bounce damage.
  • Positioning: Stay near trees or create them with Acorn Shot to guarantee Bushwhack triggers; never stand in open areas where enemy initiators can lock you down.
  • Losing the game: Getting caught without a tree or Scurry makes you vulnerable to strong initiators like Kunkka and Broodmother (your win rates vs them are only ~40%).

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain for the early lane.
  • Healing Salve — emergency health for occasional burst from enemy supports.
  • Enchanted Mango — mana for early Acorn Shot/Bushwhack spam.
  • Observer Ward — vision control; essential for setting up Bushwhack traps.

Core Items

  • Phase Boots — extra movement speed and the active phase for chasing or escaping.
  • Glimmer Cape — provides invisibility and magic resistance, synergizes with Decoy for double‑hide.
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Decoy into a true invisibility with longer duration and adds a second decoy, vastly increasing pick‑off potential.

Situational Items

  • Force Staff — extra positioning tool when trees are scarce.
  • Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — additional disable and self‑save against heroes like Bane or Lycan.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects targeted disables; useful against Keeper of the Light and Bane.
  • Aether Lens — extends the range of Sharpshooter and Bushwhack, making long‑range pick‑offs easier.
  • Octarine Core — reduces cooldowns on all abilities, especially valuable for frequent Decoy and Scurry usage.

Common Mistakes

  • Casting Bushwhack without a tree – the stun only triggers when a tree is present; always create a tree with Acorn Shot or wait for natural foliage.
  • Over‑committing with Decoy – the illusion is fragile; if the enemy sees the real hero, they can focus you while the decoy dies.
  • Neglecting vision – without wards, you lose the ability to set safe Bushwhack traps and become an easy gank target.
  • Saving Sharpshooter for team fights – the ability shines on isolated targets; waiting for a full fight often wastes its break and burst potential.

FAQ

Is Hoodwink good in the current patch?

Yes. Hoodwink’s 48.1% win rate shows she is slightly below average but still competitive, especially against heroes like Underlord and Silencer where she wins over 59% of games. Her mobility and burst make her a strong pick‑off hero in the current meta.

What lane does Hoodwink play?

Hoodwink is typically played as a support in the safe lane (position 4) or as a roaming support. Her early harassment tools (Acorn Shot, Bushwhack) work best when paired with a reliable carry, and she can transition to mid‑lane ganks once she hits level 6.

Who counters Hoodwink?

Heroes that can deny trees or lock you down before you can use Bushwhack are toughest: Naga Siren, Keeper of the Light, Lycan, Kunkka, Broodmother, and Bane all have win rates below 41% against her. Play around their initiation range and avoid isolated fights against them.
hoodwink.counterHtml:
Hoodwink’s burst damage, tree‑based crowd control, and mobility make her a lethal lane bully and mid‑game skirmisher. She thrives when she can hide in foliage, land a Sharpshooter, and follow up with Bushwhack, so shutting her down means denying trees, limiting her vision, and forcing her into straight‑up fights where her tricks are useless.

Why These Heroes Beat Hoodwink

Naga Siren

Naga’s Song of the Siren creates a global, uninterruptible stun that wipes out Hoodwink’s burst window and prevents her from using Bushwhack or Sharpshooter. When the Siren awakens, she can also Mirror Image to dodge the initial Acorn Shot and force Hoodwink to waste mana on a missed Sharpshooter. Tip: keep a ward on the river to spot Naga’s split‑push and punish her when she re‑enters lane without Song.

Keeper of the Light

Keeper’s Illuminate and Mana Leak punish Hoodwink’s low mana pool, while Chakra Magic gives him the sustain to survive the early harass. When Hoodwink attempts Bushwhack, Keeper can Recall to a safe spot or Blinding Light to blind her, nullifying the net’s stun. Tip: build a Glimmer Cape to block Bushwhack vision and let Keeper’s spells land safely.

Lycan

Lycan’s Summon Wolves and Feral Impulse give him constant pressure and high burst that outranges Hoodwink’s Acorn Shot. His Shapeshift grants massive armor and movement speed, making him hard to lock down with Bushwhack, and his Howl silences Hoodwink, preventing Sharpshooter’s charge. Tip: force a lane fight early; Lycan’s wolves can tank the Acorn bounces while his ultimate forces Hoodwink to retreat.

Kunkka

Kunkka’s Torrent and Ghost Ship provide area damage that can out‑damage a Sharpshooter volley and clear trees, removing Hoodwink’s Bushwhack anchors. His X‑Mark forces Hoodwink to chase a moving target, wasting her mobility from Scurry, while Ghost Ship’s stun interrupts her Decoy and any follow‑up. Tip: time Torrent to land on the tree where Hoodwink intends to Bushwhack, denying the trap entirely.

Broodmother

Broodmother’s Spin Web creates a web‑filled lane that blocks Hoodwink’s tree‑walking and limits her ability to place Bushwhack nets. Her Silence shuts down Sharpshooter’s charge, and Spawn Spiderlings apply constant pressure that forces Hoodwink to use Acorn Shot defensively. Tip: keep a Mekansm or Pipe of Insight on your support to mitigate the spiderling damage and stay in lane longer.

Drafting Against Hoodwink

  • Prioritize heroes with global stuns or silences (e.g., Naga Siren, Keeper of the Light).
  • Pick heroes that can clear trees or deny foliage (Kunkka, Earthshaker).
  • Ban or avoid heavy reliance on invisibility/decoy counters that rely on vision (e.g., Bounty Hunter).
  • Choose early‑game aggression to force Hoodwink to burn mana on Acorn Shot and Sharpshooter.

Laning Against Hoodwink

  • Trade when she is out of tree range; her Acorn Shot loses bounce damage.
  • Punish her after she uses Bushwhack—she is vulnerable while the net is on cooldown.
  • Force her to use Decoy early; the vision loss and movement speed penalty give you a window to harass.
  • Keep a ward on the lane to spot hidden trees and deny her Scurry‑enabled escapes.

Itemizing Against Hoodwink

Glimmer Cape — blocks the vision reduction from Bushwhack and lets you dodge Sharpshooter’s charge.
Mekansm — provides burst healing against Acorn Shot bounces and spiderling damage from Broodmother.
Pipe of Insight — reduces magical damage from Bushwhack’s DOT and Keeper’s spells.
Force Staff — lets you escape the pull of Bushwhack and close the gap on a decoy‑hiding Hoodwink.

huskar.name: Huskar
huskar.guideHtml:
Huskar remains a high‑risk, high‑reward hero in patch 7.41, excelling as a durable carry/initiator that trades health for damage. With a 44.6 % win rate over 147,945 recent ranked games, he sits slightly below the median but still finds space in aggressive lineups and off‑lane fire‑team comps.

How to Play Huskar

Laning Phase

  • Use Burning Spear on every attack to pressure the enemy; the health loss fuels Berserker’s Blood, granting attack speed and magic resistance as you drop below 50 % HP.
  • Pull Inner Fire on wave clears or to push back aggressive supports (e.g., Shadow Shaman) while silencing them for a safe retreat.
  • Trade with melee heroes by timing Life Break when you have > 70 % HP; the leaping damage and slow can force early tower pressure.
  • Manage health loss: avoid unnecessary attacks when low on HP against burst heroes like Hoodwink (Huskar wins only 40.4 % vs 89 games).
  • Stack the Burning Spear damage early to deny creep XP against ranged lane opponents such as Skywrath Mage, whose low win‑rate against Huskar (60.3 %) reflects Huskar’s lane dominance.

Mid Game

  • Hit the Berserker’s Blood power spike at ~ 25 % missing health; attack speed spikes to ~ 2.5 attacks/sec, making you a threat in 2‑v‑2 skirmishes.
  • Group with your team and look for Inner Fire + Life Break combos on isolated supports; the silence and slow set up kills for your cores.
  • Prioritize taking Roshan once you have a reliable Life Break damage window (≈ 30 % of enemy HP) and a tanky front line; the Aegis synergizes with your health‑based survivability.
  • Avoid extended fights against Nature’s Prophet (38.1 % win‑rate) unless you have strong magic resistance items, as his split‑push can out‑pace your health drain.

Late Game

  • Win condition: force Life Break onto enemy cores when they are below 40 % HP, then follow with Inner Fire to silence and finish.
  • Position near the front line; your Berserker’s Blood scaling makes you harder to kill the lower your health, but over‑extending without Blood Magic mitigation invites burst from heroes like Marci (42.5 % win‑rate).
  • Losing the game usually stems from poor health management—spending too much HP on items or fights without adequate magic resistance, allowing enemy magic damage to convert into lethal health loss.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain for early health‑loss from Burning Spear.
  • Healing Salve — quick HP recovery after aggressive trades.
  • Quelling Blade — easier creep last‑hits while sacrificing little health.
  • Stout Shield — reduces incoming harassment damage.

Core Items

  • Armlet of Mordiggian — massive HP boost; toggle off to avoid extra health loss from Blood Magic.
  • Black King Bar — essential against heavy magic burst (e.g., Skywrath Mage, Rubick).
  • Satanic — lifesteal to offset health costs; active provides burst survivability in fights.
  • Heart of Tarrasque — huge health pool, amplifies Berserker’s Blood scaling.

Situational Items

  • Mekansm — team‑wide heal; works well when you’re the front‑line tank.
  • Vanguard — extra block against physical burst from heroes like Beastmaster.
  • Shiva’s Guard — armor and AoE slow; great against physical right‑clickers and to mitigate Nature’s Prophet’s split‑push.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target spells; useful versus Hoodwink’s Bushwhack or Marci’s Unleash.
  • Abyssal Blade — reliable stun to lock down mobile heroes such as Storm Spirit (62.5 % win‑rate vs Huskar).

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑using Burning Spear without monitoring health, leading to early deaths against burst heroes.
  • Ignoring magic resistance; many counters (e.g., Rubick, 45.3 % win‑rate) exploit the health‑to‑mana conversion of Blood Magic.
  • Mis‑timing Life Break when low on HP, which can be fatal against heroes with strong counter‑damage like Marci.
  • Positioning too far forward without a frontline tank or defensive items, allowing split‑push heroes like Nature’s Prophet to out‑farm.

FAQ

Is Huskar good in the current patch?

Yes. Huskar’s win rate sits at 44.6 % across nearly 148 k ranked games, showing he remains viable despite being slightly below average. His scaling health‑based mechanics still reward aggressive play, especially against heroes he currently counters well (e.g., Silencer at 68.6 % win‑rate).

What lane does Huskar play?

Huskar is most commonly played in the off‑lane as a durable solo, but he can also function as a safe lane carry when paired with a support that can protect his health loss. The lane choice often depends on the enemy draft; avoid early pressure from Hoodwink or Marci if possible.

Who counters Huskar?

The toughest matchups are Nature's Prophet (38.1 % win‑rate), Hoodwink (40.4 %), and Marci (42.5 %). These heroes either out‑farm him or burst his health quickly, so building magic resistance and timing your Life Break carefully are essential to survive them.
huskar.counterHtml:
Huskar thrives on low‑health aggression: his Berserker’s Blood grants massive attack speed and magic resistance as his HP drops, while Burning Spear and Life Break let him trade aggressively and punish any hero that steps too close. The key to shutting him down is denying him the space to drop below critical health thresholds and exploiting his lack of true mana and reliance on health‑cost items.

Why These Heroes Beat Huskar

Nature’s Prophet

Nature’s Prophet’s global split‑push and high mobility force Huskar to chase across the map, draining his health with every attack and preventing him from safely farming. Tip: Use Teleport Scrolls or the Prophet’s Teleport to constantly pressure side lanes while keeping a safe distance from Huskar’s Burning Spear range.

Hoodwink

Hoodwink’s Bushwhack and Acorn Shot provide long‑range poke and crowd control that can harass Huskar before he can close in, while her ultimate, Scatterblast, silences and damages him even at low health. Tip: Position in the forest early and use Bushwhack to lock Huskar’s movement, then follow up with Acorn Shot to chip away his HP.

Marci

Marci’s high burst damage from Rebound and her ability to quickly close gaps with her Leap give her the tools to burst Huskar before his Berserker’s Blood ramps up. Her ultimate, Spirit Bond, also provides a safety net for allies when Huskar tries a Life Break. Tip: Initiate with Leap, land a Rebound combo, and retreat before Huskar can activate Blood Magic.

Beastmaster

Beastmaster’s summons apply constant pressure and vision, denying Huskar safe jungle camps, while his Primal Roar provides a long‑range stun that interrupts Huskar’s combos. The aura from his summons also adds extra damage over time, compounding Huskar’s health loss. Tip: Keep a summons alive near Huskar’s lane to force him to waste health on minion kills or retreat.

Shadow Shaman

Shadow Shaman’s Ether Shock and Hex give reliable poke and disable, preventing Huskar from initiating with Life Break. His Mass Hex can lock Huskar down long enough for allies to burst him while his mana‑draining abilities force Huskar to spend even more health via Blood Magic. Tip: Chain Hex → Ether Shock → Mass Hex to lock Huskar in place and force a quick kill.

Drafting Against Huskar

  • Prioritize heroes with strong early‑game harassment and burst (e.g., Hoodwink, Marci).
  • Include at least one reliable hard‑disable or long‑range stun (Shadow Shaman, Beastmaster).
  • Pick heroes with global or split‑push presence to force Huskar to waste health chasing (Nature’s Prophet).
  • Avoid heavy tanky front‑liners that let Huskar safely drop into Berserker’s Blood.

Laning Against Huskar

  • Harass with ranged attacks or spells before Huskar can get low enough for Berserker’s Blood to kick in.
  • Pull creep equilibrium to keep Huskar on the edge of the lane, forcing him to overextend for last hits.
  • Punish his Life Break cooldown: when he leaps, retreat and let him take damage while he’s vulnerable.
  • Use silences or stuns to interrupt Inner Fire, preventing his area‑silence and knock‑back.

Itemizing Against Huskar

Ghost Scepter — blocks Huskar’s physical attacks and Burning Spear damage while he is low on health.
Heaven’s Halberd — disarms Huskar, nullifying his attack‑based Burning Spear and Life Break damage.
Lotus Orb — reflects his Inner Fire and removes debuffs, letting you stay in melee range safely.
Pipe of Insight — provides magic resistance that reduces the health cost of his Blood Magic‑based item usage.

invoker.name: Invoker
invoker.guideHtml:
Invoker is a high‑skill, spell‑combo hero who excels at burst damage and crowd control. In the current 7.41 meta he sits at a modest 51.1 % win rate across 673,692 ranked games, making him a viable pick in solo queue but still vulnerable to several hard counters. His flexibility lets him fill carry, nuker, disabler, escape, or pusher roles depending on itemisation and team composition.

How to Play Invoker

Laning Phase

  • Quas + Quas + Quas (Cold Snap) – use the triple‑Quas combo to harass melee off‑laners and force early tower pressure; the freeze proc scales with Quas level, giving you reliable lane control.
  • Wex + Wex + Wex (EMP) – clear creep waves quickly and punish enemy spellcasters who over‑extend; the movement‑speed boost from Wex also lets you dodge ganks.
  • Exort + Exort + Exort (Sun Strike) – place long‑range Sun Strikes on low‑HP heroes hiding in the fog of war; a good way to secure kills against heroes like Lina who lack early vision.
  • Ghost Walk – activate when you sense an incoming gank; the invisibility and regen buy you time to reposition or escape, especially against burst heroes such as Tinker.
  • Orb Management – keep a mental map of your three orb slots; swapping orbs costs only a fraction of a second, so practice rapid sequences to stay ahead of lane opponents.

Mid Game

  • Power Spike at Level 12 – you now have access to all ten invoked spells; prioritize Deafening Blast (Quas‑Wex‑Exort) for team‑fight initiation.
  • Map Pressure with Sun Strike – place global Sun Strikes on contested objectives (Roshan, mid tower) to force enemy rotations; the spell’s global range is a constant threat.
  • Pick‑offs with Tornado + Chaos Meteor – combo Tornado (Quas‑Quas‑Wex) into Chaos Meteor (Exort‑Exort‑Wex) for massive burst on squishy targets like Weaver or Troll Warlord.
  • Vision Control – buy a Sentry Ward and Observer Ward early; without vision, your long‑range spells are easy to dodge, and you become vulnerable to invisible counters like Nyx Assassin.

Late Game

  • Win Condition: Spell‑Combo Burst – lock down high‑value targets with Cold Snap → Tornado → Sun Strike → Deafening Blast before they can react.
  • Positioning: Stay Behind Frontline – use Ghost Walk to reposition if you get caught; being caught out of position usually results in a rapid loss due to your low survivability.
  • Avoid Over‑committing – Invoker’s mana pool depletes quickly; running out of mana in a team fight often means you become a dead weight, handing the win to hard counters like Treant Protector.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango + Healing Salve — sustain against harass from lane opponents.
  • Iron Branch ×2 — cheap attribute boost; can later be used for Magic Wand.
  • Faerie Fire — instant burst of HP for clutch survivability.

Core Items

  • Boots of Travel — global presence for Sun Strikes and split‑pushing; essential on 7.41 where map control decides games.
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — reduces Invoke cooldown and adds a second Deafening Blast charge, increasing combo speed.
  • Octarine Core — 25 % cooldown reduction on all spells, making rapid combos like Cold Snap → Tornado → Chaos Meteor far more reliable.

Situational Items

  • Black King Bar — when facing heavy magical burst (e.g., Lina, Oracle) or disables from Nyx Assassin.
  • Scythe of Vyse — provides additional hard‑disable against mobile heroes like Monkey King and Lycan.
  • Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — extra setup for Sun Strike and a defensive escape against assassins.
  • Refresher Orb — allows double‑invoke of Deafening Blast in late‑game team fights; useful against line‑ups with multiple squishy carries.
  • Shiva’s Guard — armor and AoE slow counter melee heroes such as Treant Protector and Lycan.

Common Mistakes

  • Spamming the Same Combo – relying solely on Cold Snap + EMP makes you predictable; mix in Tornado and Sun Strike to keep opponents guessing.
  • Poor Orb Management – forgetting to pre‑load the correct orbs leads to wasted Invoke casts and lost damage windows.
  • Over‑extending Without Ghost Walk – diving too deep without the invisibility escape often results in deaths to gankers like Nyx Assassin.
  • Neglecting Mana Economy – casting high‑cost spells back‑to‑back without a Mana Potion or Arcane Boots forces you to sit idle during crucial fights.

FAQ

Is Invader good in the current patch?

Yes. Invoker holds a 51.1 % win rate on patch 7.41, making him slightly above average. His versatility lets him adapt to many roles, though he remains vulnerable to hard counters such as Treant Protector and Tinker.

What lane does Invoker play?

Invoker is typically played in the safe lane (position 1) as a carry, but he can also be flexed to mid if the team needs additional spell pressure. In the safe lane he leverages Cold Snap and Sun Strike to dominate early farm.

Who counters Invoker?

The toughest matchups are against Treant Protector (25 % win rate), Tinker (39 %), Nyx Assassin (39.7 %), Oracle (40 %), Monkey King (41 %), and Lycan (42.9 %). These heroes either out‑scale his early game or provide constant disables and burst that exploit his low survivability.
invoker.counterHtml:
Invoker’s strength lies in his massive spell toolbox and the ability to adapt on‑the‑fly with Quas/Wex/Exort combos. The fastest way to neutralize him is to deny his early‑game tempo, force him into long cooldown windows, and exploit his reliance on precise positioning.

Why These Heroes Beat Invoker

Treant Protector

Treant’s Nature’s Grasp and Leech Seed apply strong lane pressure and sustain while his Living Armor blocks the burst from Invoker’s Sun Strike and Chaos Meteor. Use the global Nature’s Guise to scout Invoker’s positioning and punish his long cast animations.
Tip: Keep a Tree Grab ready to block Invoker’s Cold Snap chain‑freeze and force him to waste mana on ineffective spells.

Tinker

Tinker’s Laser and Heat‑Seeking Missile constantly harass Invoker, draining his mana and forcing frequent Invoke cycles. The Rear Pulse from March of the Machines punishes Invoker’s low mobility, while Boots of Travel let Tinker stay out of Ghost Walk range.
Tip: Maintain a high mana pool (e.g., Aghanim’s Scepter) to keep the pressure on; Invoker will struggle to find a safe window to cast his high‑damage spells.

Nyx Assassin

Nyx’s Mana Burn directly counters Invoker’s high intelligence and spell‑heavy play, while Spiked Carapace reflects Cold Snap and EMP damage back at him. The Vendetta invisibility forces Invoker to waste Sun Strike and Deafening Blast on a target he can’t see.
Tip: Time Spiked Carapace just after Invoker finishes an Invoke; the reflected stun will lock him down while you close the gap.

Oracle

Oracle’s Fate’s Edict silences Invoker, preventing him from Invoke or casting any spell for a crucial 2‑second window. Purifying Flames burns mana and health, shortening Invader’s sustain, while Fortune’s End can purge Ghost Walk invisibility.
Tip: Use Fate’s Edict right after you see Invoker start a combo; the forced pause often makes his Sun Strike miss and his Chaos Meteor fall off‑target.

Monkey King

Monkey King’s Jungle and Boundless Strike give him high burst and mobility, allowing him to dodge Sun Strike and close the distance before Invoker can Invoke a defensive spell. Wukong’s Command creates a zone where Invoker’s Cold Snap and EMP are ineffective.
Tip: Activate Boundless Strike when Invoker begins an Invoke animation; the stun interrupts his combo and forces a costly re‑invoke.

Drafting Against Invoker

  • Prioritize heroes with silence or mana‑burn (e.g., Oracle, Nyx Assassin, Anti‑Mage).
  • Pick high‑mobility heroes that can dodge Sun Strike and close gaps quickly (Monkey King, Puck, Ember Spirit).
  • Include global or long‑range vision tools to track Invoker’s Teleport and Ghost Walk (Troll Warlord’s Berserker’s Call, Beastmaster’s Hawk).
  • Avoid stacking multiple late‑game spellcasters that give Invoker more combo opportunities.

Laning Against Invoker

  • Harass him before he reaches Quas 3; his early Cold Snap is weak without enough HP regen.
  • Force him to Invoke under tower pressure; the 2‑second cast window is a prime time to trade.
  • Punish his mana‑heavy spells (e.g., EMP, Chaos Meteor) by baiting them and then counter‑engaging while he’s on cooldown.
  • Keep a ward on the rune spot to deny his Ghost Walk escape and force a direct fight.

Itemizing Against Invoker

Ghost Scepter — blocks physical damage from his Sun Strike and Chaos Meteor when he’s forced to melee.
Eul’s Scepter — roots Invoker, interrupting his Invoke and buying time for your team to focus him.
Scythe of Vyse — hard‑disables him during his long cooldown windows, preventing any spell combo.
Aghanim’s Shard (Nyx Assassin) — adds a second Mana Burn on attack, draining Invoker’s mana pool faster.

io.name: Io
io.guideHtml:
Io is a high‑mobility support that excels at keeping allies alive and amplifying their damage through Tether, Overcharge, and Relocate. On patch 7.41 Io sits at a 50.6 % win rate in pub (173 k+ games), making him a solid but not dominant pick in the current ranked meta.

How to Play Io

Laning Phase

  • Tether an allied core (usually a safe lane carry) early; the movement‑speed bonus lets you dodge ganks and the health transfer helps survive harass from tough matchups like Pudge or Necrophos.
  • Use Spirits Out to keep the spirits on the edge of the lane; they provide free poke and can deter aggressive supports such as Puck or Ancient Apparition.
  • Cast Overcharge on the tethered ally when you anticipate a wave of damage (e.g., enemy tower hits or a Storm Spirit burst). The attack‑speed and spell‑amp boost helps the carry trade more effectively.
  • When the enemy lane pushes, Spirits In to cluster the spirits around you and block creep damage while you safely pull the tethered ally back with Break Tether if needed.
  • Keep an eye on Equilibrium: stay above ~70 % health to maximize damage amplification for yourself and your partner, and dip lower when you need extra healing against burst heroes.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 6 with Relocate – start making split‑pushes and rescuing allies from dangerous zones (e.g., pulling a Wraith King out of his death‑run).
  • Prioritize vision around high‑traffic areas (Roshan, enemy jungle) so you can safely Relocate into fights without being caught by Pudge hooks or Puck silences.
  • Pair Overcharge with your core’s ultimate (e.g., Legion Commander’s Duel) to maximize damage during team fights; the extra attack speed often decides the duel.
  • Use Spirits to scout and zone: a well‑timed Spirits Out into a choke point can force enemy backs and create space for your team to take objectives.

Late Game

  • Win condition: use Relocate to create 2‑v‑1 picks or to force the enemy team to split, then follow up with Overcharge on the ally who initiates the fight.
  • Position near the front of your team but keep Tether on the primary damage dealer; over‑extending without a safe Relocate exit path can be fatal against heroes like Storm Spirit.
  • Losing the game usually stems from getting caught without Relocate ready (e.g., enemy Pudge hooks you while you’re low on mana) or from tethering to a hero who dies early, stripping you of your main source of damage amplification.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane, especially against harass from Necrophos or Pudge.
  • Healing Salve — quick health boost for early trades.
  • Observer Ward — vision to protect your tethered ally from ganks.
  • Faerie Fire — cheap burst heal for clutch moments.

Core Items

  • Tranquil Boots — high movement speed for chasing or escaping, plus passive heal that synergizes with Equilibrium.
  • Mekansm — group heal that benefits the whole team and works well with Tether’s health transfer.
  • Guardian Greaves — upgrade from Mekansm, adds armor and removes debuffs, crucial against heavy magic damage like Ancient Apparition.
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — reduces Relocate cooldown, lets you save multiple allies and increases overall map pressure.

Situational Items

  • Lotus Orb — reflect targeted spells (e.g., Pudge’s Hook, Puck’s Dream Coil) and cleanse slows that would break Tether.
  • Glimmer Cape — protect your tethered ally from burst magic (e.g., Storm Spirit, Necrophos) and hide you when you need to Relocate safely.
  • Force Staff — extra mobility for yourself or the tethered hero when Relocate is on cooldown.
  • Eul’s Scepter — set up Relocate combos or escape from heroes like Wraith King who rely on melee aggression.
  • Pipe of Insight — mitigate magic damage from Ancient Apparition or Skywrath Mage in fights where you are the primary conduit of damage.

Common Mistakes

  • Tethering to a low‑damage hero or one that dies early, leaving Io without a meaningful damage amplifier.
  • Using Spirits aggressively without toggling Spirits In, causing unnecessary spirit loss and reduced poke.
  • Forgetting to keep Relocate off cooldown; many players waste it on unnecessary saves instead of setting up picks.
  • Ignoring Equilibrium scaling and staying at high health, missing out on the extra damage amplification Io can provide.

FAQ

Is Io good in the current patch?

Yes. Io holds a 50.6 % win rate in pub on patch 7.41, making him a reliable support pick. His mobility and healing keep cores alive, and the new Relocate cooldown reduction from Aghanim’s Scepter boosts his impact in both early and late game.

What lane does Io play?

Io is typically played in the safe lane as a support, tethering to the carry. He can also roam to the off‑lane to provide Relocate saves and Overcharge boosts, but his primary role is to stay with the core in the safe lane.

Who counters Io?

Heroes that can burst him or break his tether early are the toughest matchups: Wraith King, Necrophos, Pudge, Puck, Ancient Apparition, and Storm Spirit all have win rates below 40 % against Io. Vision control and items like Lotus Orb or Glimmer Cape are essential to survive their pressure.
io.counterHtml:
Io’s strength lies in its relentless sustain and mobility: Tether lets it heal and protect an ally while Overcharge fuels huge attack‑speed bursts, and Relocate gives instant repositioning. The most reliable way to shut Io down is to deny its healing, force it out of range, and punish the low‑damage early game before its spirits and Overcharge become threatening.

Why These Heroes Beat Io

Wraith King

Wraith King’s Reincarnation gives him a reliable safety net that Io’s Relocate can’t bypass, and his Mortal Strike crits ignore the modest damage boost from Overcharge. In lane, Wraith King’s high base health and armor make the early Tether‑heal negligible. Tip: Force a duel early; if Wraith King dies, Io’s Relocate is on cooldown and the tether is broken, leaving Io vulnerable to a follow‑up kill.

Necrophos

Necrophos’s Heartstopper Aura constantly chips Io’s health, while Death Pulse deals pure damage that isn’t mitigated by Io’s Equilibrium scaling. The constant HP loss prevents Io from reaching the health thresholds that grant its damage amplification. Tip: Keep the lane tight and spam Death Pulse on Io and its tethered ally to keep both under the 50 % health sweet spot.

Pudge

Pudge’s Meat Hook can pull Io out of its tether range, instantly breaking the link and denying the heal transfer. Once Io is isolated, Rot deals continuous pure damage that Io’s modest armor can’t absorb. Tip: Position near a wall or neutral camp so a successful hook forces Io to retreat, breaking the tether and exposing it to Rot.

Puck

Puck’s Illusory Orb and Dream Coil provide burst magic damage and silence, preventing Io from casting Relocate or Overcharge. The waning Rift damage is pure and scales with the enemy’s max health, which hits Io hard when it’s low. Tip: Initiate with Dream Coil when Io’s tether is on an ally; the coil forces the tethered unit to stay close, making it easy to land a follow‑up Orb and kill both.

Ancient Apparition

Ancient Apparition’s Ice Blast applies a damage‑amplifying debuff that stacks with Io’s Equilibrium, turning Io’s own healing into amplified damage taken. The global Cold Feet also forces Io to stay in place, making Relocate risky. Tip: Time Ice Blast just before Io attempts a Relocate; the debuff will persist through the teleport, making the return kill much easier.

Drafting Against Io

  • Prioritize heroes with strong pure‑damage or magic‑damage burst (e.g., Necrophos, Pudge, Ancient Apparition).
  • Pick heroes with reliable disables that can break tether range (hooks, stuns, silences).
  • Include at least one tank with high base health/armor to soak early Tether heals (Wraith King, Bristleback).
  • Consider global or long‑range ultimates that can punish Io’s Relocate cooldown (Nature’s Prophet, Spectre).

Laning Against Io

  • Trade early when Io’s health is above 70 %; its Equilibrium gives little boost and its Overcharge damage is low.
  • Force the tethered ally to move away from Io, breaking the link and denying the heal transfer.
  • Harass with spells that apply damage over time (Rot, Corruption) to keep Io’s health low, preventing Equilibrium scaling.
  • Punish any attempt to use Relocate by staying near neutral camps or towers, where the return path is predictable and can be intercepted.

Itemizing Against Io

  • Spirit Vessel — amplifies incoming damage and provides a heal‑reduction burst that nullifies Io’s Tether healing.
  • Heaven’s Halberd — disarms Io, preventing Overcharge attacks and forcing him to rely on low‑damage spirits.
  • Ghost Scepter — makes you immune to Io’s spirit explosions and Overcharge‑boosted attacks during Relocate.
  • Black King Bar — blocks the magic damage from spirits and prevents Io’s spell amplification from affecting you.

jakiro.name: Jakiro
jakiro.guideHtml:
Jakiro is a dual‑headed elemental support who excels at area denial, lane control, and team‑fight damage. In the current 7.41 meta his overall win‑rate sits at 47.7% over 392 k ranked games, making him a solid but not dominant pick. He shines as a support/nuker/pusher and is especially valuable against heroes that lack mobility or burst.

How to Play Jakiro

Laning Phase

  • Use Dual Breath on creep waves to add damage and slow, making last‑hits easier and denying enemy farm.
  • Drop Ice Path on the enemy off‑lane when they try to harass; the stun and damage punish aggressive supports.
  • Alternate Liquid Fire and Liquid Frost on your own attacks to apply both attack‑slow and increased damage taken, forcing melee heroes to back off.
  • When the lane is pushed, cast Dual Breath into the enemy tower to chip it and zone the opponent.
  • Against hard‑disablers (e.g., Treant Protector, Dark Seer) keep a safety ward and stay near your tower, as Jakiro’s lane win‑rate drops to ~38‑40% vs those matchups.

Mid Game

  • Macropyre on chokepoints (river, Roshan pit) to control enemy movement and force rotations.
  • Pair Ice Path with a stun from an ally (e.g., Lion) for combo kills; the stun duration stacks with the ice damage.
  • Prioritize split‑pushing towers with Dual Breath + Liquid Fire while your cores farm; Jakiro’s pusher identity shines here.
  • Watch for enemy Io or Enigma pushes—use Ice Path to block their pull/black hole setups.

Late Game

  • Position Macropyre behind your front line; its long‑lasting line can decimate clustered enemies in team fights.
  • Use Dual Breath to zone high‑damage carries (e.g., Chaos Knight, Tinker) who try to dive your backline.
  • Avoid over‑extending into enemy vision; a missed Ice Path can leave you vulnerable to burst from heroes like Lone Druid.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane, especially against poke‑heavy opponents.
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery after early skirmishes.
  • Observer Ward — vision to protect against ganks from Io or Enigma.
  • Sentry Ward — detect invisible threats (e.g., Clinkz) that currently counter Jakiro (40.7% win‑rate).
  • Faerie Fire — cheap damage boost for early tower pushes.

Core Items

  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Liquid Fire/Frost to a larger AoE, increasing lane pressure and team‑fight impact.
  • Glimmer Cape — protects you while casting long‑duration spells like Macropyre.
  • Force Staff — escape tool against initiators (Treant, Dark Seer) and to reposition for optimal Macropyre placement.
  • Eul’s Scepter — provides a self‑disable and additional crowd control; useful vs mobile heroes like Weaver (58.2% win‑rate advantage).

Situational Items

  • Ghost Scepter — against right‑click heavy carries (Chaos Knight, Anti‑Mage).
  • Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target spells such as Io’s tether or Enigma’s Black Hole.
  • Solar Crest — amplify damage on a target for a quick kill when you have Macropyre on them.
  • Aether Lens — increase cast range of Ice Path and Macropyre for safer positioning.
  • Refresher Orb — double Macropyre in late‑game team fights when you need to lock down multiple fronts.

Common Mistakes

  • Casting Ice Path without vision – often wasted on invisible heroes like Clinkz, leading to unnecessary mana loss.
  • Over‑committing with Macropyre – standing too close to the line makes you an easy target for burst heroes.
  • Neglecting attack‑slow – forgetting to toggle Liquid Frost on melee carries reduces your overall lane pressure.
  • Relying on damage instead of utility – Jakiro shines when he zones and disables; focusing solely on raw damage wastes his strengths.

FAQ

Is Jakiro good in the current patch?

Yes. Jakiro’s 47.7% win‑rate across 392 k ranked games shows he is a viable support, especially against heroes with limited mobility. He excels in lane control and team‑fight zoning, though he struggles versus high‑mobility or strong push heroes like Treant Protector and Dark Seer.

What lane does Jakiro play?

Jakiro is typically played as a position 5 support in the safe lane, pairing with a carry to provide lane sustain and crowd control. He can also slot into position 4 for more aggressive roaming, but his win‑rate is strongest when he can safely farm and set up Ice Path/Dual Breath.

Who counters Jakiro?

Heroes that can bypass his area control or out‑maneuver his slows are hardest for him: Treant Protector, Lone Druid, Io, Enigma, Dark Seer, and Clinkz all have sub‑40% win‑rates against Jakiro. Building vision, early Sentry, and items like Ghost Scepter or Lotus Orb can mitigate these counters.
jakiro.counterHtml:
Jakiro’s strength lies in his relentless area‑of‑effect damage and crowd‑control: Dual Breath, Ice Path, and Macropyre can lock down teamfights and shred tanky heroes. The key to neutralizing him is to deny his lanes of safe vision, out‑maneuver his static AoE, and bring burst or sustain that outpaces his damage‑over‑time.

Why These Heroes Beat Jakiro

Treant Protector

Treant’s Nature’s Guise grants invisibility and a burst of movement speed, allowing him to dodge Ice Path and Macropyre’s line attacks while setting up Leech Seed for constant healing. Use the hidden tree‑form to ambush Jakiro when he’s channeling Macropyre, then follow up with Living Armor to mitigate his damage.
Tip: Position Treant’s Overgrowth just after Jakiro’s Macropyre ends to lock him down while his cooldowns are on lock.

Lone Druid

Lone Druid’s Spirit Bear can tank Jakro’s AoE and absorb the damage from Dual Breath and Macropyre, while the hero’s True Form provides high burst damage to finish Jakro before he can re‑activate his spells. The bear’s Savage Roar silences Jakro, preventing the use of Liquid Frost/Fire during crucial engagements.
Tip: Keep the bear near the lane’s edge to force Jakro to over‑extend his Ice Path, then pull the bear in for a quick kill.

Io

Io’s Tether and Overcharge give allied cores massive attack speed and survivability, letting them out‑damage Jakro’s DoT while staying mobile enough to dodge Ice Path. Relocate can instantly pull a teammate out of Macropyre’s line, nullifying its sustained damage.
Tip: Pair Io with a hero that has a strong escape (e.g., Puck) to repeatedly reposition out of Jakro’s static spells.

Enigma

Enigma’s Midnight Pulse deals pure damage over time that ignores Jakro’s magic resistance, while Black Hole can pull Jakro out of his own Macropyre line, forcing him to waste the ultimate on a non‑optimal position. The constant Demonic Conversion pressure also forces Jakro to split his attention between lane and jungle.
Tip: Initiate Black Hole right after Jakro casts Macropyre; the pulled Jakro will take the full line damage plus the burst from the vortex.

Dark Seer

Dark Seer’s Ion Shell adds constant damage that stacks with Jakro’s DoT, quickly killing him if he stays in lane. Vacuum can pull Jakro into his own Ice Path or Macropyre, turning his crowd‑control against him. The Surge speed boost lets allies outrun his slows and reposition.
Tip: Use Vacuum to yank Jakro out of Macropyre’s line right before the spell expires, then follow with Ion Shell on the enemy core for a lethal combo.

Drafting Against Jakiro

  • Prioritize heroes with strong gap‑closers or blink abilities to escape Ice Path and Macropyre lines.
  • Pick mobile, burst‑damage heroes that can kill Jakro before he activates his AoE spells.
  • Include sustain or magic‑immune heroes to blunt his DoT and slow effects.
  • Consider bans that remove his primary lane partners (e.g., strong push heroes) to limit his farm.

Laning Against Jakiro

  • Trade when Jakro’s Dual Breath is on cooldown; his damage drops dramatically without the ice‑fire combo.
  • Harass early with ranged attacks to force him to use Liquid Frost for the damage‑increase debuff, then disengage before Ice Path lands.
  • Punish his over‑extension after he casts Macropyre—he is vulnerable while the line is channeling.
  • Maintain lane equilibrium near your tower to reduce the effective length of his Macropyre and Ice Path.

Itemizing Against Jakiro

Eul's Scepter of Divinity — can purge the damage‑increase debuff from Liquid Frost and provide a safe window to dodge Ice Path.
Black King Bar — grants magic immunity, nullifying Dual Breath, Liquid Fire/Frost, and Macropyre damage.
Manta Style — splits you into multiple units that each take only a portion of Jakro’s AoE, and the dispel removes his slows.
Ghost Scepter — makes you ethereal, causing Jakro’s physical attacks and Liquid Frost to miss while you wait out his spell cooldowns.

juggernaut.name: Juggernaut
juggernaut.guideHtml:
Juggernaut remains a solid carry/pusher/escape hero in the current meta, holding a 51.8% win rate across 596,691 recent ranked games on patch 7.41. His toolkit—high burst, sustain, and a strong late‑game scaling—keeps him relevant despite a few tough matchups.

How to Play Juggernaut

Laning Phase

  • Use Blade Fury early (level 1) to secure last hits and deter aggressive supports; the 80 % magic resistance and dispel on exit protect against early disables.
  • Trade with melee heroes (e.g., Sniper, Timbersaw) by timing Blade Fury just before they land a spell, then follow up with a normal attack to trigger Blade Dance crits.
  • Drop a Healing Ward when you have lane control; its movement speed (325) lets it chase enemy creeps and heal you through tower damage.
  • Stack Bladeform by avoiding damage for 2 seconds after a fight—each stack grants extra Agility and movement speed, letting you out‑farm or chase.
  • Watch for the toughest matchups (Sniper, Abaddon, Venomancer, Kez, Snapfire, Timbersaw) and play conservatively until you have a defensive item (e.g., Mekansm or Phase Boots).

Mid Game

  • Hit Omnislash (level 6) after you have at least one Bladeform stack; the invulnerability window lets you dive in on squishy targets like Zeus or Pangolier.
  • Prioritize Healing Ward placement in team fights; its 18‑second uptime can swing engagements, especially against heroes without strong burst (e.g., Magnus, Faceless Void).
  • Power spike at ~15 k gold with Battle Fury for farm acceleration; combine with Blade Fury to clear jungle camps quickly.
  • Start taking objectives (Roshan, tier‑2 towers) when you have Manta Style or Satanic for survivability against burst heroes.

Late Game

  • Win condition: use Omnislash to eliminate the enemy carry first, then follow up with Blade Fury and auto‑attacks while your Healing Ward sustains your team.
  • Position near the front line but keep distance from disables; Bladeform stacks will give you the extra Agility needed to out‑damage melee cores.
  • Losing the game usually comes from being caught by hard‑lock crowd control (e.g., Abaddon’s Aphotic Shield, Snapfire’s Mortimer Kisses) before you can activate Bladeform or Omnislash.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain against harass, especially vs. Sniper and Venomancer.
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery after early trades.
  • Stout Shield — reduces damage from harassment and early tower hits.
  • Quelling Blade — helps secure last hits against ranged lane opponents.

Core Items

  • Battle Fury — farm speed and damage; synergizes with Blade Fury for jungle clearing.
  • Manta Style — dispels silences, provides agility, and gives extra Blade Fury uptime.
  • Satanic — survivability in late‑game fights; active heal offsets burst from Sniper or Timbersaw.
  • Butterfly — massive agility boost and evasion, crucial against right‑click heroes like Sniper.

Situational Items

  • Mekansm — counter heavy magical burst (e.g., Zeus, Snapfire).
  • Diffusal Blade — mana burn against heroes reliant on spells such as Abaddon and Venomancer.
  • Abyssal Blade — lockdown for slippery targets like Kez or to finish off a fleeing Zeus.
  • Black King Bar — mandatory against lineups with multiple disables (e.g., Snapfire + Abaddon).
  • Heart of Tarrasque — extra tankiness when you need to survive prolonged fights against Timbersaw.

Common Mistakes

  • Spamming Blade Fury without vision – you become an easy target for long‑range heroes like Sniper.
  • Neglecting Bladeform stacks – missing the free Agility and speed makes you vulnerable to ganks.
  • Using Healing Ward too early – it dies quickly to enemy AoE spells; wait for a favorable positioning.
  • Delaying Omnislash – waiting for a perfect moment often lets the enemy carry escape; use it as soon as you have a clear target and a Bladeform stack.

FAQ

Is Juggernaut good in the current patch?

Yes. Juggernaut sits at a 51.8% win rate on patch 7.41, making him a reliable carry despite a few unfavorable matchups (Sniper, Abaddon, etc.). His mix of damage, sustain, and escape keeps him viable in both solo and team‑fight scenarios.

What lane does Juggernaut play?

Juggernaut is typically played in the safe lane as a carry, but he can also be flexed to the off‑lane for a more aggressive early game, especially against heroes he can out‑farm with Blade Fury.

Who counters Juggernaut?

The toughest opponents right now are Sniper (41.8% win rate), Abaddon (41.9%), Venomancer (42.0%), Kez (43.5%), Snapfire (44.5%), and Timbersaw (44.6%). These heroes either outrange his damage or apply strong disables that can prevent him from building Bladeform stacks and landing Omnislash.
juggernaut.counterHtml:
Juggernaut’s threat comes from his high sustained damage, Blade Fury’s magic‑resistant spin, and the burst potential of Omnislash. The key to shutting him down is to deny him the uninterrupted aggression that builds Bladeform stacks and to exploit his reliance on melee range and limited defensive tools.

Why These Heroes Beat Juggernaut

Sniper

Sniper’s extreme attack range lets him harass Juggernaut before he can close the gap for Blade Fury or Omnislash, and his Headshot proc punishes any melee approach. Tip: Keep a safe distance and use Assassinate to finish Juggernaut when his Healing Ward is down.

Abaddon

Abaddon’s Aphotic Shield instantly removes Juggernaut’s Blade Fury damage over time and can be detonated to burst Juggernaut when he jumps in with Omnislash. His Mist Coil provides reliable self‑heal that outpaces Juggernaut’s Healing Ward. Tip: Time Mist Coil right after Juggernaut’s Blade Fury ends to negate the heal and force him to retreat.

Venomancer

Venomancer’s Poison Nova and Venomous Gale apply lingering damage that bypasses Blade Fury’s magic resistance, while his Poison Sting slows Juggernaut’s chase speed, making it hard for him to stack Bladeform. Tip: Plant a Poison Nova when Juggernaut attempts to engage; the damage over time will eat away his health even through his ward.

Kunkka (Kez)

Kunkka’s Torrent and X‑Mark provide strong burst and a reliable stun that interrupts Blade Fury and Omnislash, denying Juggernaut the invulnerability window. The Ghostship’s armor reduction further weakens Juggernaut’s survivability. Tip: Use Torrent to force Juggernaut to retreat before he can accumulate Bladeform stacks, then follow with X‑Mark for a guaranteed kill.

Snapfire

Snapfire’s Cookie provides a burst of damage and a brief stun that can interrupt Blade Fury, while Firesnap Cookie grants a shield that mitigates the burst from Omnislash. Her Mortimer Kisses force Juggernaut to stay at range, limiting his ability to engage. Tip: Position Mortimer Kisses to zone Juggernaut away from creep wave, then pop a Cookie when he attempts a spin.

Drafting Against Juggernaut

  • Prioritize long‑range physical damage heroes (Sniper, Drow Ranger) that can harass before Blade Fury.
  • Include reliable hard‑disable or burst (Abaddon, Kunkka, Snapfire) to interrupt Omnislash.
  • Pick heroes with strong anti‑heal or magic‑damage over time (Venomancer, Dark Willow) to negate Healing Ward.
  • Consider early‑game lane control heroes who can deny farm and prevent Bladeform stacking.

Laning Against Juggernaut

  • Trade when Juggernaut’s Blade Fury is on cooldown; his attack damage drops without the spin.
  • Harass with ranged attacks or spells that force him to use Blade Fury defensively, then disengage.
  • Punish his Healing Ward placement: attack the ward early to force him to waste mana and time.
  • Keep distance; Juggernaut is weakest when he cannot close for an attack, especially after a recent damage instance that resets Bladeform stacks.

Itemizing Against Juggernaut

Butterfly — high evasion and agility reduce his physical burst and Blade Fury damage.
Manta Style — dispels Blade Fury’s lingering effects and creates confusion for Omnislash targeting.
Ghost Scepter — makes you immune to his physical attacks during Blade Fury and Omnislash.
Heaven’s Halberd — disarms Juggernaut, preventing both his normal attacks and the critical chance from Blade Dance.

keeper-of-the-light.name: Keeper of the Light
keeper-of-the-light.guideHtml:
Keeper of the Light (Ezalor) is a utility‑heavy support who excels at mana sustain, vision control, and burst magical damage through Illuminate. In the current 7.41 meta his win rate sits at 50.6% over 258 k ranked games, making him a solid but not dominant pick. He thrives in lineups that need reliable disables and mana regen, while struggling against heroes that can close distance quickly or silence him.

How to Play Keeper of the Light

Laning Phase

  • Chakra Magic on yourself early gives the 30 % extra mana restore and cooldown reduction, letting you spam Illuminate and stay in lane longer.
  • Use Illuminate as a zoning tool: channel a short burst (≈1 s) to harass enemy off‑laners and force them to pull back, then release early with Release Illuminate to keep vision on the wave.
  • Blinding Light is a strong anti‑harass against melee supports (e.g., Pudge, Centaur) – drop it when they try to engage, the knock‑back and miss chance buys you time to retreat or heal.
  • Pair Solar Bind with a slow‑heavy ally (e.g., Viper, Phoenix) to amplify magic‑resist reduction and make enemy escapes painful.
  • Keep moving at least 300 units every few seconds to leave luminescent vision; this grants you and your carry safe farm and early map control against roaming heroes like Monkey King.

Mid Game

  • Spirit Form is your first power spike: the extended cast range lets you Illuminate from safety and heal allies while roaming.
  • Prioritize Will‑O‑Wisp on high‑ground objectives (Roshan, towers) to force enemy positioning and provide vision for your team’s pushes.
  • Look for pick‑offs on squishy supports (e.g., Silencer, Queen of Pain) using a combo of Blinding Light → Solar Bind → Illuminate for burst damage.
  • When you have a Glimmer Cape or Eul’s Scepter, use Illuminate on the enemy’s frontline while you’re invisible/disabled to avoid being silenced by heroes like Viper.

Late Game

  • Position near the front line but not in the immediate melee range; Illuminate channel time is vulnerable to disables (e.g., Batrider’s Flaming Lasso).
  • Win the game by providing continuous mana sustain (Chakra Magic) and vision (luminescent trails, Will‑O‑Wisp) for your carries during late‑stage team fights.
  • Avoid getting caught by heroes with strong gap‑close or silence (Treant Protector’s Nature’s Grasp, Monkey King’s Tree Dance, Batrider’s Flaming Lasso) – these are the toughest matchups according to recent data (e.g., Keeper wins only 38.8% vs Treant Protector).

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango + Healing Salve — sustain in lane while you’re channeling spells.
  • Observer Ward — early vision to complement your luminescent trail.
  • Clarity ×2 — mana for early Illuminate and Chakra Magic usage.

Core Items

  • Tranquil Boots — movement speed for the 300‑unit vision trigger and cheap regen.
  • Glimmer Cape — safety for channeling Illuminate and to dodge silences from Viper or Batrider.
  • Aghanim’s Shard — upgrades Solar Bind to a stronger slow, synergizing with your team’s chase.

Situational Items

  • Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — extra disable and a way to set up Illuminate on a stunned target.
  • Force Staff — escape from aggressive initiators like Monkey King or Pudge.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target spells (e.g., Treant Protector’s Nature’s Grasp).
  • Scythe of Vyse — hard lock on mobile heroes that otherwise outrange you (Centaur, Batrider).
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — if you need a permanent Spirit Form for constant long‑range Illuminate and extra healing.

Common Mistakes

  • Channeling too long without vision – enemies can dive and silence you, wiping out your damage.
  • Neglecting luminescent vision – staying static forfeits the free 400‑range sight that can win early ganks.
  • Using Chakra Magic on allies when you need the 30 % self‑bonus for your own mana pool during team fights.
  • Over‑relying on Illuminate as damage instead of a utility tool; forgetting to pair it with Blinding Light or Solar Bind reduces its effectiveness.

FAQ

Is Keeper of the Light good in the current patch?

Yes. Keeper sits at a 50.6% win rate in patch 7.41, making him a viable support pick. He shines against heroes like Warlock (69.1% win) and struggles against close‑range initiators such as Treant Protector (38.8% win).

What lane does Keeper of the Light play?

Keeper is typically played as a hard support in the safe lane (radiant bottom or dire top) alongside a core carry. His early Chakra Magic and luminescent vision help the lane stay safe and maintain farm.

Who counters Keeper of the Light?

Heroes with strong gap‑close and silence are his biggest threats: Treant Protector, Monkey King, Batrider, Pudge, Viper, and Centaur Warrunner all have sub‑50% win rates against him (e.g., 38.8% vs Treant). Building Lotus Orb, Force Staff, or Eul’s can mitigate these counters.
keeper-of-the-light.counterHtml:
Keeper of the Light thrives on sustained presence: his channel‑based Illuminate, mana‑sustaining Chakra Magic, and global vision make him a constant threat in team fights and split‑push scenarios. The core way to shut him down is to deny his channel time, burst him before he can restore mana, and apply consistent disables that outpace his Bright Speed‑based mobility.

Why These Heroes Beat Keeper of the Light

Treant Protector

Treant’s Nature’s Guise grants invisibility and a burst of movement speed, letting him dodge the channel of Illuminate and close the gap for a quick Leech Seed or Nature’s Grasp block. The constant tree‑placement also creates terrain that forces Keeper to channel through vision‑blocking foliage, reducing the effectiveness of his vision‑leaving passive. Tip: Drop a tree right before you start channeling; the sudden loss of vision forces Keeper to abort or waste channel time.

Monkey King

Monkey King’s Boundless Strike and Jingu Mastery give him high burst damage that can kill Keeper before Chakra Magic can replenish his mana. Additionally, Tree Dance provides a safe escape route that Keeper cannot chase through his limited vision radius, nullifying Keeper’s chase potential. Tip: Use Tree Dance to hop out of Illuminate’s line of sight and immediately counter‑engage with a stun from your support.

Batrider

Batrider’s Flamebreak provides a reliable stun that interrupts Illuminate’s channel and silences Keeper, preventing Chakra Magic activation. Firefly grants Batrider constant movement speed and a damage‑over‑time aura that punishes Keeper’s low health pool when he tries to stay in lane. Tip: Position Flamebreak just outside Keeper’s vision radius; the stun will still land while Keeper can’t see you coming.

Pudge

Pudge’s Meat Hook can pull Keeper out of his channel and into a dangerous position, instantly breaking the Illuminate cast. Once hooked, Rot applies a damage‑over‑time that drains Keeper’s mana faster than Chakra Magic can restore it. Tip: Save Hook for the moment Keeper begins channeling; the forced movement also disrupts his Will‑O‑Wisp placement.

Viper

Viper’s Nethertoxin creates a poison field that reduces magical resistance and continuously burns mana, directly countering Keeper’s Solar Bind and Chakra Magic. The lingering damage also forces Keeper to retreat before he can finish a channel. Tip: Plant Nethertoxin in the lane’s choke point; Keeper will have to either waste channel time or lose a significant portion of his mana pool.

Drafting Against Keeper of the Light

  • Prioritize heroes with hard disables (stuns, silences) that can interrupt channeling.
  • Pick high burst damage heroes who can kill Keeper before he restores mana.
  • Include mobile heroes or those with strong gap‑closers to outrun his Bright Speed scaling.
  • Avoid picking heroes reliant on long‑range magical damage that can be mitigated by Solar Bind.

Laning Against Keeper of the Light

  • Harass him early; his mana pool is small before the first Chakra Magic.
  • Force him to channel Illuminate under tower vision—tower sight negates his 400‑range vision trail.
  • Punish his channel start: a well‑timed stun or hook will abort the cast and give you a kill opportunity.
  • Trade when his Will‑O‑Wisp is on cooldown; his lane control drops dramatically.

Itemizing Against Keeper of the Light

Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — silences and lifts Keeper, cancelling Illuminate and preventing Chakra Magic activation.
Scythe of Vyse — long‑duration hex removes his ability to channel and blocks Spirit Form’s extended range.
Ghost Scepter — makes you ethereal against his Illuminate damage while you wait for his cooldowns.
Spirit Vessel — applies a strong heal‑reduction debuff, neutralizing his occasional heal from Spirit Form.

kez.name: Kez
kez.guideHtml:
Kez is a versatile melee hero who toggles between a katana and a sai to adapt his damage and utility. On patch 7.41 he lands at a 44.8% win rate in ranked play, making him a solid but not dominant pick. His blend of burst, escape, and disable gives him a unique carry‑escape‑disabler identity that thrives on timing his weapon swaps.

How to Play Kez

Laning Phase

  • Use Echo Slash early to harass enemy heroes and apply the 100 ms impact slow, making it easier to land follow‑up attacks or Grappling Claw pulls.
  • When you have the Kazurai Katana, focus on stacking the damage‑over‑time from basic attacks; this makes your lane trades progressively stronger.
  • Switch to Shodo Sai before a contested 2‑v‑2; the critical strike chance from Shodo Sai and the silence from Talon Toss give you a lane‑kill threat.
  • Against hard‑pushing lanes (e.g., Keeper of the Light, Treant Protector) keep the wave near your tower and use Grappling Claw on trees to create safe escape routes.
  • Prioritize a sentry ward or observer near the river to protect against early Disruptor or Lich ganks, where you have a statistical advantage.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 12 when you unlock Raptor Dance; the 0.2 s invulnerability window lets you dive into fights and survive burst from heroes like Drow Ranger.
  • Look for Falcon Rush engagements after you have a Blink Dagger or Shadow Blade; the phased movement and slow resistance let you close distance on squishy targets such as Windranger.
  • Split‑push with Echo Slash and the katana’s DoT to force towers while your team secures objectives elsewhere.
  • When you have Talon Toss, target enemy supports (e.g., Lich, Disruptor) to silence them before a teamfight, capitalizing on your higher win rates against those heroes.

Late Game

  • Win condition: Use Raptor Dance to initiate on high‑value backline heroes, then follow up with Falcon Rush and Echo Slash to cascade damage while your DoT ticks down.
  • Positioning: Stay near trees or cliffs to maximize Grappling Claw escape routes; avoid long sightlines where Keeper of the Light can chain‑heal you.
  • Game‑losing mistake: Over‑committing with Falcon Rush without a retreat option; you become vulnerable to counter‑initiates from Centaur Warrunner or Bane.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango + Healing Salve — sustain against harassment.
  • Iron Branch x2 — cheap stats and can be later built into a Magic Wand.
  • Quelling Blade — helps secure last hits while you’re toggling weapons.
  • Observer Ward — vision against early ganks from Disruptor or Lich.

Core Items

  • Power Treads — attack speed for faster DoT stacks and flexibility between strength/agility.
  • Echo Sabre — synergizes with Echo Slash and provides a reliable stun for follow‑up combos.
  • Blink Dagger — essential for positioning Falcon Rush initiations and escaping Keeper of the Light’s Lucent Beam.
  • Black King Bar — protects you during the 1‑second Raptor Dance window against magical burst.

Situational Items

  • Sange & Yasha — extra movement speed and status resistance, useful against Centaur Warrunner and Bane.
  • Aghanim’s Shard — upgrades Talon Toss damage and silence duration, great versus Disruptor and Lich.
  • Heaven’s Halberd — disarms right‑click heavy heroes like Drow Ranger and Windranger.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target disables (e.g., Keeper of the Light’s Will‑O‑Wisp).
  • Manta Style — creates illusion confusion and removes silences, helpful when facing Bane’s nightmare.

Common Mistakes

  • Never swapping weapons in fights, missing the critical strike or DoT windows.
  • Using Falcon Rush without a clear escape path, getting caught by crowd‑control from Centaur or Bane.
  • Over‑relying on Echo Slash for damage; forgetting the DoT from Kazurai Katana reduces sustained kill potential.
  • Ignoring vision in the mid lane, allowing Disruptor or Lich to set up deadly disables.

FAQ

Is Kez good in the current patch?

Yes. Kez sits at a 44.8% win rate across over 150 k ranked games, making him a viable pick. He excels against heroes like Disruptor, Lich, and Lifestealer, where his win rates exceed 60%.

What lane does Kez play?

Kez is typically played in the safe lane as a carry, but his escape tools let him survive in the mid lane against aggressive matchups. Adjust your lane based on the enemy draft; avoid early heavy‑push lanes such as Treant Protector unless you can keep the wave near your tower.

Who counters Kez?

The toughest matchups are Keeper of the Light, Treant Protector, Drow Ranger, Windranger, Centaur Warrunner, and Bane, where Kez’s win rate drops to 33‑46%. These heroes either out‑heal his burst or lock him down before he can swap weapons and use his combo.
kez.counterHtml:
Kez is a high‑damage, mobility‑heavy hero whose threat comes from rapid burst combos and the ability to chase down squishy targets with Echo Slash and Falcon Rush. The key to shutting him down is denying his early‑game aggression, limiting his ability to stick to heroes, and exploiting his relatively low survivability against hard‑crowd‑control and sustained poke.

Why These Heroes Beat Kez

Keeper of the Light

Keeper’s Mana Leak and Illuminate apply consistent magic damage and a strong silence that interrupts Kez’s weapon swaps and the channel of Raptor Dance. His Blinding Light also provides a brief invulnerability window, forcing Kez to waste his burst. Tip: Position near a tree and use Blinding Light right as Kez initiates his Grappling Claw to nullify the hook and force a disengage.

Treant Protector

Treant’s Nature’s Guise grants invisibility and a movement speed boost, allowing him to dodge Grappling Claw and Echo Slash. Overgrowth roots Kez, preventing the follow‑up slashes and Falcon Rush. Tip: Time Overgrowth just after Kez lands his first Echo Slash; the root cancels the second wave and leaves him vulnerable to a counter‑attack.

Drow Ranger

Drow’s Gust silences and slows, shutting down Kez’s ability to chain his attacks, while Marksmanship scales damage against Kez’s low‑health heroes. The constant multishot from her Frost Arrows forces Kez to stay at range. Tip: Use Gust when Kez is about to switch weapons; the silence blocks both Katana and Sai abilities, buying you a safe window to trade.

Windranger

Windranger’s Shackleshot can pin Kez to a tree or ally, instantly cancelling his Grappling Claw and preventing the follow‑up Echo Slash. Windrun grants evasion and a movement speed boost, making it hard for Kez to land his hook. Tip: Wait for Kez to start his Falcon Rush, then Shackleshot him to a tree—he cannot phase through the root and his burst is fully negated.

Centaur Warrunner

Centaur’s Hoof Stomp provides a reliable AOE stun that interrupts Kez’s combo chain, while Double Edge punishes Kez’s low health after a failed engage. Culling Blade can finish him off once his health drops below 25%. Tip: Use Hoof Stomp the moment Kez lands his Grappling Claw; the stun stops the second Echo Slash and forces a disengage.

Drafting Against Kez

  • Prioritize heroes with reliable silences or stuns (e.g., Keeper, Treant, Centaur).
  • Pick mobile lane‑dominants who can outrange his Grappling Claw (e.g., Windranger, Drow).
  • Include at least one strong magic‑damage dealer to exploit his low magic resistance.
  • Consider banning heroes that give Kez free kill lanes (e.g., high‑mobility melee supports).

Laning Against Kez

  • Trade early when his Kazurai Katana damage‑over‑time is still low (first 2–3 minutes).
  • Punish his Grappling Claw miss; the hook leaves him vulnerable for ~1.5 s.
  • Keep a tree or warded terrain between you and Kez to block his line‑skill Echo Slash.
  • Force him to use Raptor Dance early; the 0.2 s invulnerability is too short to offset the loss of his combo.

Itemizing Against Kez

Ghost Scepter — blocks Kez’s physical burst from Echo Slash and Falcon Rush, forcing him to rely on less‑effective magic damage.

Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — cyclone removes Kez from the fight, cancels his weapon swap, and gives you time to reposition or cast a defensive ability.

Black King Bar — grants magic immunity during the window of his Katana’s damage‑over‑time and prevents his silence from Talon Toss.

Abyssal Blade — the stun interrupts his combo chain and the added damage punishes his low‑health state after a missed Grappling Claw.

kunkka.name: Kunkka
kunkka.guideHtml:
Kunkka remains a versatile initiator and damage dealer in the current meta, sitting at a 49.1% win rate across 179,694 recent ranked matches on patch 7.41. He can flex between carry and support roles, but his effectiveness hinges on timing his spells and leveraging his strong early‑game presence. While his overall win rate is near median, he struggles against high‑mobility burst heroes such as Templar Assassin (37.8% win) and shines against tanky front‑liners like Bristleback (61.7% win).

How to Play Kunkka

Laning Phase

  • Use Torrent on wave clears and to punish aggressive melee heroes; the stun and slow set up early kills, especially against heroes with low mobility.
  • Land X Marks the Spot on an enemy hero before a fight; the delayed return can catch them out of position when you follow up with Ghostship.
  • Prioritize Tidebringer cleave on creep waves to maintain lane equilibrium and deny farm to enemy off‑laners.
  • Against hard‑kill lanes (e.g., Shadow Shaman, Necrophos), play defensively and save Ghostship for counter‑initiations rather than aggressive pushes.
  • Coordinate Torrent + X Marks the Spot with your support’s disables to secure early tower dives.

Mid Game

  • Hit the Tidebringer damage spike at level 12 (first upgrade) to start split‑pushing and forcing rotations.
  • Group with your team and look for Ghostship + Tidal Wave combos; the wave’s drag disables enemy attacks, allowing your cores to clean fights.
  • Prioritize objectives after winning a team fight—use X Marks the Spot on a high‑value target to pull them back into your damage zone.
  • Keep an eye on enemy mobility heroes (Templar Assassin, Storm Spirit); deny them space with well‑timed Torrent and Ghostship to limit their pick‑off potential.

Late Game

  • Win condition: force team fights where you can land Ghostship followed by Tidal Wave, then burst the enemy backline with Torrent and X Marks the Spot.
  • Position near the front line but not so far that you miss the Tidal Wave drag; staying just behind your front liners maximizes your cleave and spell impact.
  • Losing the game often stems from mistiming Ghostship—if it lands on a cleared area or is intercepted by enemy stuns, you give the opposition a free window to disengage.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane, especially against harassment from Shadow Shaman and Necrophos.
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery after early Torrent trades.
  • Iron Branch ×2 — cheap stats and can be later used for a Magic Wand.
  • Faerie Fire — burst health for early survivability against burst heroes like Templar Assassin.

Core Items

  • Phase Boots — provides the chase speed needed to land Torrent and X Marks the Spot combos.
  • Echo Slam — synergizes with Tidebringer cleave and Tidal Wave drag, exploding multiple enemy units.
  • Black King Bar — essential against heavy magical burst (Necrophos, Shadow Shaman) and disables from Storm Spirit.
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Ghostship to a larger radius and adds a second X Marks the Spot, dramatically increasing team‑fight control.

Situational Items

  • Shiva’s Guard — armor and aura help against right‑click heroes like Monkey King and Skywrath Mage.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target disables, useful versus Shadow Shaman’s Hex and Storm Spirit’s Electric Vortex.
  • Assault Cuirass — boosts lane pressure and reduces enemy armor, great when facing physical heroes such as Tiny.
  • Manta Style — provides purge and extra damage; works well against silences from Shadow Shaman and the slow from Templar Assassin’s Refraction.
  • Heart of Tarrasque — survivability when you’re the primary front‑liner against burst lineups.

Common Mistakes

  • Wasting Ghostship on empty space – without proper vision, the ship often misses its stun, giving the enemy free movement.
  • Using Torrent on creeps only – the ability shines when it hits heroes; prioritize enemy heroes over wave clears.
  • Failing to combo X Marks the Spot with Ghostship – the delayed return is a powerful follow‑up; neglecting it reduces kill potential.
  • Over‑extending without BKB – against magic‑heavy lineups (Necrophos, Shadow Shaman), diving in without Black King Bar leads to early deaths.

FAQ

Is Kunkka good in the current patch?

Kunkka sits at a 49.1% win rate on patch 7.41, making him a solid but not dominant pick. He excels against tanky heroes like Bristleback (61.7% win) and struggles versus high‑mobility burst heroes such as Templar Assassin (37.8% win).

What lane does Kunkka play?

Kunkka is most commonly played in the safe lane as a carry, but his strong early gank potential also allows him to function as an off‑lane or even a support in duo‑lane setups, especially when paired with a strong lane partner.

Who counters Kunkka?

Heroes with strong burst and mobility—Templar Assassin, Shadow Shaman, Necrophos, and Storm Spirit—have the lowest win rates against Kunkka (below 44%). Their ability to dodge Torrent or quickly silence Ghostship makes them the toughest matchups.
kunkka.counterHtml:
Kunkka’s burst damage, long‑range disables, and game‑changing ultimate make him a nightmare in mid‑lane and team fights. The key to shutting him down is denying his ability to land Torrent + X Marks the Spot combos and preventing his Ghostship from catching allies in its stun radius.

Why These Heroes Beat Kunkka

Templar Assassin

TA’s Refraction blocks the initial Torrent damage and the follow‑up X Marks the Spot pull, while Meld lets her burst Kunkka before he can position his Tidebringer cleave. Tip: keep a Blink ready to dodge Ghostship’s landing zone and force Kunkka to waste his ultimate on a miss.

Shadow Shaman

Hex and Shackles silence Kunkka, cancelling his Torrent cast and making his X Marks the Spot return impossible to time. Tip: chain‑lock Kunkka after a successful Torrent to force a premature Ghostship, where you can bait the ship’s stun onto your own allies.

Necrophos

Necrophos’s Death Pulse provides constant heal that mitigates Torrent’s burst, and Heartstopper Aura punishes Kunkka’s melee aggression. Tip: build Aghanim’s Shard for the Ghost Shroud to become immune to Ghostship’s stun and force Kunkka into a losing trade.

Shadow Demon

Disruption can instantly dodge Torrent and pull Kunkka’s X Marks the Spot target out of range, while Soul Catcher amplifies the damage Kunkka deals to you, making his burst self‑punishing. Tip: use Disruption right after Kunkka lands Torrent to turn his own stun into a free kill.

Storm Spirit

Storm’s Electric Vortex can yank Kunkka out of his Torrent radius, and his high mobility lets him dodge Ghostship and X Marks the Spot returns. Tip: keep Overload charges high and wait for Kunkka to commit Torrent before zipping in for a quick kill.

Drafting Against Kunkka

  • Prioritize heroes with reliable silences or hard disables (e.g., Hex, Shackles, Stun) to stop Torrent and X Marks the Spot.
  • Pick high‑mobility heroes that can outrun Ghostship’s drag (e.g., Storm Spirit, Anti‑Mage).
  • Choose heroes with strong lane sustain or self‑heal to survive Torrent burst (e.g., Necrophos, Viper).
  • Consider bans on strong lane‑dominant melee heroes that can out‑farm Kunkka early (e.g., Bristleback, Abaddon).

Laning Against Kunkka

  • Harass him before he gets a level 2 (Torrent + X Marks the Spot) to force a missed hook.
  • Trade when his Tidebringer is on cooldown; his cleave leaves a large window of vulnerability.
  • Zone him from the creep wave when his Torrent is on cooldown; he loses lane equilibrium.
  • Punish any early Ghostship attempt by staying spread out, forcing the ship to miss its stun.

Itemizing Against Kunkka

Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — can purge Torrent’s stun and set up a counter‑spell on X Marks the Spot.
Ghost Scepter — makes you untargetable by Ghostship’s splash damage and stun.
Black King Bar — grants magic immunity, nullifying Torrent, Ghostship, and Tidebringer’s magical component.
Force Staff — instantly escapes Torrent’s pull or the Ghostship drag, preserving positioning.
