legion-commander.name: Legion Commander
legion-commander.guideHtml:
Legion Commander remains a solid front‑line carry with a 52.6 % win rate across over half a million recent ranked games, making her a reliable pick in the current 7.41 meta. Her blend of durability, initiation, and the game‑changing Duel lets her snowball when played aggressively, though she still struggles against certain mobile and burst heroes.

How to Play Legion Commander

Laning Phase

  • Use Overwhelming Odds on creep waves to secure early farm and gain bonus attack speed, especially against melee opponents that stack the damage.
  • Pair Press The Attack with a support’s early heal or shield to stay healthy while contesting lane equilibrium.
  • Prioritize last‑hitting with the attack‑speed boost from Overwhelming Odds; avoid extended trades until you have at least two stacks of Moment of Courage.
  • Against hard‑disables like Tusk or Shadow Fiend, keep a safe distance and rely on your passive armor from Outfight Them! to mitigate early harassment.
  • If you’re lane‑partnered with a ranged support, coordinate early Duel attempts on low‑HP enemy heroes to force early kills and gain gold advantage.

Mid Game

  • Aim for a Duel on an isolated enemy after you have a few items (Phase Boots, Blink Dagger) – this is the primary power spike that can turn the game.
  • Secure rune control and jungle camps; the armor bonus from allied abilities within 1200 range makes you tankier for objective fights.
  • Start split‑pushing with Overwhelming Odds on creep waves; the damage scales with enemy count, making it deadly against stacked towers.
  • Avoid chasing heroes like Juggernaut or Tusk who can escape with mobility; instead, look for 2‑v‑1 situations where your Moment of Courage lifesteal can outlast them.

Late Game

  • Win condition: force Duel on key enemy carries (e.g., Luna, Timbersaw) while your team disables the rest; the extra armor from allies’ abilities makes you hard to kill.
  • Position near your frontline to absorb damage; use Press The Attack on yourself or a tanky ally before initiating a Duel to purge slows and gain regen.
  • Lose the game if you overextend without Blink/Force Staff, allowing mobile heroes like Tusk or Shadow Fiend to kite you and pick you off before you can land Duel.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tangoes — sustain in lane, especially against harassment from Shadow Fiend or Crystal Maiden.
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery after early trades.
  • Stout Shield — mitigates damage from ranged harassers like Luna and Silencer.
  • Iron Branch ×2 — cheap stats and can be later used for a Magic Wand.

Core Items

  • Phase Boots — provides the burst speed needed to close gaps for Duel and synergizes with the attack‑speed boost from Overwhelming Odds.
  • Blink Dagger — essential for initiating Duel on isolated targets and escaping heroes such as Tusk.
  • Black King Bar — protects you from disables and magical burst (e.g., Lina’s Light Strike, Shadow Fiend’s Shadowraze) during Duel.
  • Satanic — maximizes the lifesteal from Moment of Courage, allowing you to survive prolonged fights.

Situational Items

  • Abyssal Blade — guarantees a stun on slippery heroes like Juggernaut; also works as a backup initiation tool.
  • Heart of Tarrasque — extra durability against burst lineups (Abaddon, Crystal Maiden).
  • Shiva’s Guard — adds armor and an AoE slow, countering fast‑attack heroes like Luna and Timbersaw.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects targeted disables from Tusk or Shadow Fiend and provides additional armor.
  • Assault Cuirass — boosts your armor further and reduces enemy armor, making Overwhelming Odds damage more effective against tanky heroes.

Common Mistakes

  • Rushing Duel without stacks – entering a Duel before you have at least two Moment of Courage stacks often results in a loss.
  • Over‑extending without Blink – chasing mobile heroes leaves you vulnerable to counter‑ganks, especially against Tusk and Shadow Fiend.
  • Neglecting armor buffs – failing to position near allies casting abilities wastes the 6‑second armor bonus that makes you tankier in fights.
  • Itemizing for damage only – ignoring survivability items (BKB, Satanic) makes you an easy target for burst lineups like Lina and Abaddon.

FAQ

Is Legion Commander good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 52.6 % win rate across 548 k+ recent ranked games, Legion Commander remains a reliable front‑line carry. Her ability to snowball through Duel and the armor‑granting mechanics keep her relevant despite tougher matchups.

What lane does Legion Commander play?

Legion Commander is typically played in the safe lane as a carry, though she can also be flexed to the off‑lane when a strong early tower push is needed. Her durability and scaling Overwhelming Odds make her comfortable farming in solo lane.

Who counters Legion Commander?

The toughest matchups are against highly mobile or burst heroes: Tusk (32.2 % win), Abaddon (35.6 %), Juggernaut (38.0 %), Shadow Fiend (41.8 %), Crystal Maiden (41.9 %), and Vengeful Spirit (42.2 %). These heroes can either kite Legion Commander or out‑burst her before she can land a decisive Duel.
legion-commander.counterHtml:
Legion Commander thrives on winning duels and snowballing with Duel and Moment of Courage, turning every fight into a permanent advantage. The quickest way to shut her down is to deny her the opportunity to land a clean duel and to punish the moments when her lifesteal and armor buffs are still on cooldown.

Why These Heroes Beat Legion Commander

Tusk

Tusk’s Ice Shards creates a wall that blocks Legion Commander’s approach, while Snowball can pull LC out of position and force a duel on a non‑ideal target. His Walrus Punch provides a reliable stun that interrupts the channel of Duel. Tip: start with a Snowball into Ice Shards to force LC to waste her duel on a minion or a tower.

Abaddon

Aphotic Shield can absorb the burst damage from Duel and the lifesteal from Moment of Courage, then burst the shield to deal pure damage back. Borrowed Time grants a short window of invulnerability that nullifies the duel’s kill potential. Tip: keep a shield active on yourself or a core ally whenever you suspect LC is about to initiate.

Juggernaut

Blade Fury provides magic immunity, completely negating the damage from Duel and the bonus attack speed from Overwhelming Odds. After the spin, Omnislash can punish LC’s low health and force her to retreat before she can re‑engage. Tip: time Blade Fury just before LC initiates; the duel will be cancelled and she will be left vulnerable.

Shadow Fiend

Shadow Fiend’s Shadowraze deals high burst magic damage at range, forcing LC to use Press The Attack defensively and draining her mana. His Presence of the Dark Lord reduces enemy armor, making the damage from Duel and Moment of Courage less effective. Tip: harass with a quick Raize before the lane reaches 6‑8 minutes to keep LC’s health low and her duel cooldown high.

Crystal Maiden

Crystal Nova and Frostbite provide strong area slows and a reliable root, preventing LC from closing the gap for Duel. Her Arcane Aura denies LC the mana needed for Press The Attack and Duel in the early game. Tip: maintain vision and use Frostbite on LC when she steps forward to attack; the root will cancel the duel entirely.

Drafting Against Legion Commander

  • Prioritize heroes with strong disables or magic immunity (e.g., Tusk, Juggernaut, Abaddon).
  • Include at least one hero with reliable burst magic damage to punish LC before she gets a duel.
  • Pick heroes that can sustain or shield allies (e.g., Crystal Maiden, Abaddon) to mitigate Moment of Courage lifesteal.
  • Avoid stacking multiple melee initiators that can synergize with LC’s duel.

Laning Against Legion Commander

  • Harass aggressively before she reaches level 6; her duel is her only true threat.
  • Trade when her Overwhelming Odds is on cooldown; the damage and attack‑speed boost will be missing.
  • Force her to use Press The Attack on a non‑essential target, then punish the slowed movement.
  • Keep a defensive ward or rune control to deny her easy access to the jungle for early Duel attempts.

Itemizing Against Legion Commander

Ghost Scepter — makes you untargetable by her melee attacks during a duel, nullifying the bulk of her damage.
Eul's Cyclone — provides a reliable disable that can interrupt Duel and give you time to reposition.
Lotus Orb — reflects the single‑target stun from Walrus Punch or Aphotic Shield, and also removes debuffs from Press The Attack.
Heaven’s Halberd — disarms LC, preventing her from dealing damage during the duel and stopping Moment of Courage lifesteal.

lich.name: Lich
lich.guideHtml:
Lich remains a solid support‑nuker with a 52.3% win rate across 390 k recent ranked games, making him a reliable pick in the current 7.41 meta. His toolkit—strong lane harassment, a game‑changing ultimate, and mana‑stealing sustain—lets him control team fights while staying safe behind cores.

How to Play Lich

Laning Phase

  • Frost Blast on enemy creeps and the off‑lane hero to secure last hits and apply a 4‑second slow, making it easier for your carry to farm.
  • Frost Shield on your carry or yourself to reduce incoming damage and add a periodic ice damage + slow aura that punishes aggressive melee opponents (e.g., Sven, Ursa).
  • Sinister Gaze on low‑mana heroes (especially mid‑lane spell‑casters) to drain mana and force them to retreat, buying lane control.
  • Sacrifice early creep kills to replenish your mana pool, enabling constant spell usage without needing frequent regen items.
  • Prioritize harassing heroes that rely on attack speed (Sven, Ursa) since they are among Lich’s easiest matchups (≈58% win).

Mid Game

  • Chain Frost on a well‑positioned Ice Spire to initiate fights; the bounce‑damage scaling can wipe out squishy cores (Sniper, Muerta) despite their current low win‑rate vs Lich.
  • Place Ice Spires in choke points or near Roshan to create zones that slow enemies and provide a safe target for Chain Frost.
  • Rotate with your support lane to secure vision and set up Sinister Gaze on high‑mana heroes (Keeper of the Light, Kunkka) before a team fight.
  • Push towers with Frost Blast + Ice Spire combos while maintaining lane pressure on the enemy off‑lane.

Late Game

  • Position behind frontline heroes; use Frost Shield on carries during team fights to mitigate burst from heroes like Chaos Knight and Treant Protector (your toughest matchups, sub‑35% win).
  • Time Chain Frost after enemy initiators have used their disables; the bounce can still hit multiple targets even through spell‑immune heroes after the initial slow.
  • Win the game by forcing fights where your Ice Spire + Chain Frost combo can chain through enemy backlines, turning the tide despite unfavorable matchups.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain for lane harassment.
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery after early skirmishes.
  • Observer Ward — vision to protect your carry and set up Sinister Gaze.
  • Sentry Ward — deny enemy detection and protect your Ice Spire placements.
  • Faerie Fire — cheap burst heal for early trades.

Core Items

  • Arcane Boots — provides the mana needed for constant Frost Blast and Chain Frost usage.
  • Glimmer Cape — gives magic immunity for yourself or a carry when facing high‑magic‑damage heroes like Kunkka or Keeper of the Light.
  • Aghanim’s Shard — upgrades Ice Spire to a larger radius, increasing its utility in team fights.

Situational Items

  • Force Staff — reposition allies into Sinister Gaze range or pull them out of danger from Chaos Knight’s Chaos Bolt.
  • Eul’s Scepter — additional disable and mana regen; great against Sniper and Muerta who rely on positioning.
  • Ghost Scepter — protect against physical burst from Ursa or Sven when they become fed.
  • Lotus Orb — reflect targeted spells from Chaos Knight and Treant Protector, mitigating their toughest matchup impact.
  • Scythe of Vyse — extra hard‑disable when you need more control than Sinister Gaze provides.

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑using Sinister Gaze on high‑mana heroes without proper positioning, allowing them to break the channel and turn the fight.
  • Forgetting to Sacrifice creeps, leading to mana starvation and reduced lane presence.
  • Placing Ice Spires in open areas where enemies can easily destroy them before a fight, wasting the potential Chain Frost bounce.
  • Ignoring vision; without wards, enemies can ambush you and your carry, especially against heroes like Chaos Knight.

FAQ

Is Lich good in the current patch?

Yes. Lich enjoys a 52.3% win rate on patch 7.41, making him a consistently strong support and nuker, especially against melee cores such as Sven and Ursa (≈58% win).

What lane does Lich play?

Lich is typically played as a hard support in the safe lane, pairing with a carry to provide lane harassment, mana sustain, and damage mitigation.

Who counters Lich?

Heroes with high burst damage and low reliance on mana—Chaos Knight, Treant Protector, and Sniper—currently have the lowest win rates against Lich (34‑39%). Vision denial and early aggression can also exploit Lich’s reliance on spell uptime.
lich.counterHtml:
Lich’s strength lies in his global mana‑drain, massive burst from Chain Frost, and the defensive utility of Frost Shield. To shut him down you need heroes that can either survive his early harass, deny his mana drain, or out‑scale his burst before he can land a full bounce.

Why These Heroes Beat Lich

Chaos Knight

Chaos Knight’s Reality Rift and Phantasm give him huge burst damage that can kill Lich before Chain Frost is cast, while his innate Chaos Bolt bypasses Lich’s low armor. Tip: force a duel early; if Lich lands a Frost Blast, immediately use Reality Rift to close the distance and kill him before the bounce chain starts.

Treant Protector

Treant’s Nature’s Guise grants invisibility and a free Leech Seed that steals Lich’s mana, nullifying Sinister Gaze and Chain Frost mana‑cost scaling. Tip: start with a high‑ground Tree of Ages to block Lich’s Frost Shield vision and force him to waste spells on creeps.

Kez

Kez’s Mortal Coil provides a reliable stun that interrupts the channel of Sinister Gaze and can break the bounce chain of Chain Frost with a timely Cloak of Shadows‑style silence. Tip: time Mortal Coil just as Lich begins to channel Chain Frost; the stun resets the bounce timer and kills Lich’s primary target.

Sniper

Sniper’s long‑range Headshot and Assassinate outrange Lich’s Frost Blast and force Lich to stay far back, making his Sacrifice ineffective. Tip: keep a safe distance, use Take Aim to increase attack range, and punish any attempt by Lich to use Frost Shield on you.

Muerta

Muerta’s Dead Shot deals pure damage that pierces Lich’s Frost Shield, and her Soul Siphon steals mana, directly countering Sinister Gaze’s drain. Tip: land a Dead Shot on Lich’s Frost Shielded ally to force the shield off, then follow up with a quick burst before Lich can react.

Drafting Against Lich

  • Prioritize heroes with strong early burst or true‑damage (e.g., Chaos Knight, Sniper, Muerta).
  • Pick mana‑draining or silence abilities to cripple Sinister Gaze (e.g., Kez, Silencer).
  • Include high‑mobility heroes that can dodge Chain Frost bounces (e.g., Anti‑Mage, Puck).
  • Consider early‑game tanky heroes that can absorb Frost Blast and stay in lane (e.g., Bristleback).

Laning Against Lich

  • Trade when Lich’s Frost Blast is on cooldown; his damage spikes are predictable.
  • Harass him with creep kills to force Sacrifice early, denying him mana and experience.
  • Punish his channeling of Sinister Gaze by interrupting with stuns or silences.
  • Position near your own tower to mitigate his Frost Shield’s damage reduction.

Itemizing Against Lich

Manta Style — dispels Frost Shield and provides split‑push pressure that forces Lich to waste spells.
Black King Bar — grants magic immunity during Chain Frost, preventing bounce damage and slowing.
Eul’s Scepter — cyclone can remove Lich from a Chain Frost bounce chain and interrupt Sinister Gaze.
Ghost Scepter — makes you ethereal, causing Chain Frost’s damage to miss and allowing safe repositioning.

leshrac.name: Leshrac
leshrac.guideHtml:
Leshrac remains a high‑damage, lane‑dominant nuker with a solid 51.6% win rate across 97,948 recent ranked games on patch 7.41, making him a viable pick in both solo‑mid and off‑lane roles. His mix of pure damage, strong wave clear, and mobility‑boosting Nihilism lets him transition from a lane bully to a late‑game siege threat, though he still struggles against heavy‑disables and burst‑heavy heroes.

How to Play Leshrac

Laning Phase

  • Use Lightning Storm on the enemy hero to harass and apply the movement‑slow, then follow up with a quick Split Earth stun when they step forward.
  • Spam Pulse Nova on creep waves; the mana drain is manageable early and it forces enemy supports to either waste mana or lose lane control.
  • When you have mana surplus, cast Diabolic Edict on the enemy tower after a wave clear to chip down early tower health—its pure damage scales with fewer targets.
  • Keep Nihilism ready to dodge incoming disables or to chase heroes that try to escape; the speed boost also helps you reposition for a second Split Earth.
  • Prioritize a safe lane against heroes like Grimstroke and Magnus (Leshrac win ≈ 36‑41% in those matchups) by playing defensively until you hit level 6.

Mid Game

  • Hit level 6 and look for Split Earth + Lightning Storm combos on isolated heroes; the stun and slow set up easy kills.
  • Push towers aggressively with Diabolic Edict after a successful team fight—its pure damage is especially effective when enemy heroes are dead or low on health.
  • Aim for a second Pulse Nova upgrade (if you built Aghanim’s Scepter) to increase wave clear and siege speed, turning you into a primary pusher.
  • Join fights where you can land Nihilism on both yourself and enemies, amplifying magic damage taken by foes while you gain movement speed to escape or chase.

Late Game

  • Position near the front of team fights to maximize Pulse Nova uptime; maintain enough mana (through Scythe of Vyse or Octarine Core) to keep the pulses constant.
  • Use Split Earth as a zoning tool on high‑ground objectives (Roshan, Tier‑2 towers) to lock down enemies while your team deals damage.
  • Avoid being caught by strong disables (e.g., Bane, Dawnbreaker) as they dramatically reduce your effectiveness and can swing the win‑rate against you (Leshrac win ≈ 42‑45% vs those heroes).

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain for early lane harassment.
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery after taking damage from Split Earth retaliation.
  • Faerie Fire — cheap burst to finish low‑HP enemies after a Lightning Storm combo.
  • Observer Ward — vision to avoid ganks from Bane or Grimstroke.

Core Items

  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Pulse Nova to fire multiple pulses per second, vastly improving wave clear and siege.
  • Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — provides mana regen, movement speed, and a self‑save against disables; synergizes with Nihilism for aggressive plays.
  • Scythe of Vyse — hard‑disable to lock down mobile heroes that can dodge your Split Earth (e.g., Lina, Slark).
  • Octarine Core — reduces cooldowns and gives spell lifesteal, keeping Pulse Nova and Diabolic Edict active longer.

Situational Items

  • Black King Bar — essential against heavy magical burst from Grimstroke, Bane, or Dawnbreaker.
  • Shiva’s Guard — armor and aura to survive against physical heroes like Axe and to slow enemy movement for easier Lightning Storm hits.
  • Heart of Tarrasque — massive health pool for tanking burst from Queen of Pain or Batrider.
  • Linken’s Sphere – blocks single‑target disables such as Bane’s Nightmare or Grimstroke’s Soul Bind.
  • Aghanim’s Shard – adds a cast‑range increase to Lightning Storm, useful for poking from safety against melee heroes.

Common Mistakes

  • Spamming Pulse Nova without mana management – early‑game mana runs out quickly, leaving you vulnerable to ganks.
  • Overcommitting with Split Earth – missing the stun wastes cooldown and gives enemy heroes like Grimstroke space to turn the fight.
  • Neglecting Nihilism’s speed boost – many players think it only provides ethereal protection; using it to chase or escape is crucial.
  • Building pure damage items too early – without proper survivability, you die before your damage can impact the game.

FAQ

Is Leshrac good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 51.6% win rate across nearly 98k recent ranked matches, Leshrac is a strong pick, especially on lanes where he can leverage his pure damage and wave clear.

What lane does Leshrac play?

Leshrac is most commonly played in solo mid or off‑lane, but his flexibility allows him to be a safe lane carry when paired with a supportive partner.

Who counters Leshrac?

Heroes with strong disables and burst, such as Grimstroke, Magnus, Bane, Dawnbreaker, Batrider, and Queen of Pain, currently give Leshrac win rates below 46%, making them his toughest matchups.
leshrac.counterHtml:
Leshrac’s high burst damage and relentless wave‑clear make him a constant threat in both lane and mid‑game team fights. The key to shutting him down is to deny his mana‑intensive combos, lock him down before he can unleash Pulse Nova, and force him into unfavorable melee engagements where his pure‑damage output is minimized.

Why These Heroes Beat Leshrac

Grimstroke

Grimstroke’s Soul Bind instantly links Leshrac to an ally, preventing the long‑range positioning required for Diabolic Edict and Pulse Nova while exposing him to follow‑up disables. A quick Ink‑Bound after the bind silences Leshrac, cutting his spell‑cast window; aim to land the bind as soon as Leshrac begins channeling his combo.

Magnus

Magnus’s Skewer and Reverse Polarity pull Leshrac into close quarters where his pure‑damage spells are far less effective and he can be killed before his mana pool sustains a full Pulse Nova. Use Empowered on a teammate with burst damage to finish Leshrac once he’s caught in the polarity field.

Bane

Bane’s Nightmare and Fiend’s Grip provide long‑duration lockdown that completely halts Leshrac’s channel‑based abilities. Cast Nightmare early to force Leshrac to waste mana on a failed Diabolic Edict, then follow with Fiend’s Grip for a near‑guaranteed kill.

Dawnbreaker

Dawnbreaker’s Starbreaker and Celestial Hammer give her a reliable melee presence that can close the distance on Leshrac before he can set up his AoE spells. Her Luminosity reduces Leshrac’s magic resistance, amplifying any magical burst from allies while she continuously interrupts his combo with Starbreaker.

Batrider

Batrider’s Flamebreak and Firefly grant sustained magic damage and a strong escape tool that forces Leshrac to chase, draining his mana. Landing Flamebreak on Leshrac interrupts Diabolic Edict, and the subsequent Firefly chase forces him to waste mana on movement instead of damage.

Drafting Against Leshrac

  • Prioritize heroes with reliable hard‑crowd control (stuns, silences, long‑duration disables).
  • Pick mobile melee heroes who can close the gap quickly (e.g., Dawnbreaker, Batrider).
  • Include magic‑damage amplifiers or armor‑reduction abilities to make his pure damage less threatening.
  • Consider bans on heroes that give Leshrac extra mana or lane safety (e.g., heroes with strong sustain or lane control).

Laning Against Leshrac

  • Harass him early before he hits level 6; his damage spikes dramatically after Pulse Nova becomes available.
  • Force him to use Split Earth defensively; each cast burns mana and leaves him vulnerable to a counter‑harass.
  • Trade when his Diabolic Edict is on cooldown—his damage output drops sharply without it.
  • Keep the lane wave near your tower to limit his ability to safely cast Lightning Storm from a distance.

Itemizing Against Leshrac

Ghost Scepter — makes you ethereal, nullifying his pure‑damage Diabolic Edict and Pulse Nova.
Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — provides a self‑disable to dodge his burst and a spell‑block to interrupt his channel.
Black King Bar — grants magic immunity, rendering his stun and damage spells ineffective during fights.
Scythe of Vyse — a hard‑disable that can lock Leshrac down for the duration of his combo, preventing any damage output.

lifestealer.name: Lifestealer
lifestealer.guideHtml:
Lifestealer is a durable, escape‑oriented carry whose strength lies in sustained fights and health‑stealing burst. With a 52.4% win rate across 403,521 recent ranked games, he remains a solid pick in the current meta, especially when paired with strong frontline allies.

How to Play Lifestealer

Laning Phase

  • Infest early to pull neutral creeps into lane, gaining free experience and denying enemy farm while staying invisible.
  • Use Open Wounds on melee opponents (e.g., Axe, Bristleback) to provide constant heal for you and your support; the slow also makes lane control easier.
  • Feast should be toggled on against high‑HP lane heroes (e.g., Morphling, Alchemist) to maximize the heal‑per‑damage component.
  • Position near your tower and time Rage when the enemy tries to harass; the debuff immunity and magic resistance let you survive burst from heroes like Phoenix.
  • Prioritize last‑hits on creeps that grant higher max‑HP gain from Feast (large creeps, neutral stacks) to scale survivability.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 6 with Infest → Consume: look for isolated enemy cores or supports to burst down.
  • After acquiring Mask of Madness or Satanic, use Rage to initiate on enemy backlines; the movement speed and magic resistance let you chase down heroes like Night Stalker or Phantom Assassin.
  • Join team fights around objectives; Open Wounds amplifies team healing, making you a focal point for sustained engagements.
  • Split‑push with Infest on a creep wave to create pressure while staying hidden; pop out with Consume when the enemy attempts to contest.

Late Game

  • Win condition: use Infest → Consume on high‑value targets (e.g., Morphling, Alchemist) while your frontliners keep you alive with Open Wounds healing.
  • Position near the frontline but keep Rage ready for enemy disables; losing Rage to a well‑timed Doom or Slardar can swing the fight.
  • Avoid extended fights against pure magic burst (e.g., Phoenix) unless you have Rage active and sufficient armor items; getting locked down often leads to a loss.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane, especially important while you’re building health for Feast.
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery after early skirmishes.
  • Quelling Blade — easier creep last‑hits to trigger Feast heal.
  • Stout Shield — mitigates harassment from melee heroes.

Core Items

  • Mask of Madness — massive attack speed for Ghoul Frenzy, synergizes with Feast lifesteal.
  • Satanic — provides survivability and a strong active heal to complement Open Wounds.
  • Black King Bar — essential against heavy magical burst (Phoenix, Doom) and disables.
  • Manta Style — gives extra movement speed, dispels silences, and adds a second Infest‑style escape.

Situational Items

  • Abyssal Blade — lockdown for slippery heroes like Morphling; works well with Rage.
  • Heart of Tarrasque — huge HP pool for prolonged fights against heroes with high burst (Alchemist, Doom).
  • Butterfly — evasion against right‑click heroes such as Phantom Assassin; also adds damage.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target spells (e.g., Slardar’s Corrosive Haze) and provides armor.
  • Shiva’s Guard — armor and AoE slow to counter high‑mobility heroes like Night Stalker and to mitigate burst from Morphling’s Ethereal Blade.

Common Mistakes

  • Wasting Infest on heroes with strong AoE damage (e.g., Phoenix) instead of using it on isolated targets.
  • Neglecting Rage: entering fights without Rage makes Lifestealer vulnerable to disables and magic burst.
  • Over‑relying on Feast against heroes with low max health; better to focus on damage items when the enemy is primarily burst.
  • Poor positioning in late‑game team fights—standing too far from the front line reduces the healing benefit of Open Wounds.

FAQ

Is Lifestealer good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 52.4% win rate across over 400k recent ranked matches, Lifestealer is a viable carry, especially against heroes like Witch Doctor and Night Stalker where his win rates exceed 60%.

What lane does Lifestealer play?

Lifestealer is typically played in the safe lane as a carry, often paired with a support that can capitalize on his Open Wounds healing (e.g., Witch Doctor, Vengeful Spirit).

Who counters Lifestealer?

The toughest matchups are against Morphling, Alchemist, Kez, Doom, Slardar, and Phoenix, where Lifestealer’s win rates drop below 40%. These heroes either out‑damage him or apply disables that negate his Rage and Infest effectiveness.
lifestealer.counterHtml:
Lifestealer thrives on closing the distance, bursting down heroes with Feast‑heal and sustaining through Infest. The key to shutting him down is denying his ability to get inside melee range and stripping away the healing and survivability he gains from each kill.

Why These Heroes Beat Lifestealer

Morphling

Morphling’s Waveform and Morph give him massive burst mobility and the ability to out‑maneuver Lifestealer’s Rage‑induced chase. A well‑timed Adaptive Strike can burst Lifestealer before he can Infest, while the attribute shift can instantly give Morphling a health buffer that Lifestealer’s Feast can’t overcome. Tip: Keep Morphling’s health high with Morph before engaging; the extra HP makes Lifestealer’s heal negligible.

Alchemist

Alchemist’s Acid Spray and Unstable Concoction apply strong magic damage that bypasses Lifestealer’s increased magic resistance from Rage, while Greevil’s Greed provides a huge health pool that scales with gold, outlasting Lifestealer’s Feast heals. The Chemical Rage active also grants lifesteal that directly counters Lifestealer’s damage output. Tip: Use Acid Spray early to force Lifestealer to retreat, then follow up with a timed Unstable Concoction for a kill.

Kez (Keziah)

Kez’s Mana Void deals damage based on the opponent’s missing mana, and his Arcane Supremacy provides a magic shield that blocks the burst from Lifestealer’s Feast. Additionally, Kez’s Mana Burn reduces Lifestealer’s effective health pool, making his permanent HP gains from kills less impactful. Tip: Harass with Mana Burn in lane to keep Lifestealer’s HP low before he can secure a kill.

Doom

Doom’s Doom ultimate provides a hard silence and disables Lifestealer’s Infest and Consume, preventing any surprise burst from inside a host. Doom’s Scorched Earth also reduces Lifestealer’s sustain by dealing constant damage over time, which is not mitigated by Lifestealer’s magic resistance. Tip: Cast Doom as soon as Lifestealer attempts to Infest a creep or ally; the silence forces him to fight on his own terms.

Slardar

Slardar’s Slithereen Crush applies a strong armor‑reduction debuff, amplifying the physical damage of Lifestealer’s opponents and making his Feast less effective. Corrosive Haze provides true sight, exposing Lifestealer when he is inside a host, while his Bash proc punishes Lifestealer’s attempts to close distance. Tip: Use Corrosive Haze on a creep before Lifestealer Infests it; the true sight forces him to reveal himself early.

Drafting Against Lifestealer

  • Prioritize heroes with strong burst magic damage (e.g., Morphling, Doom).
  • Include at least one true‑sight source or detection tool (e.g., Slardar, Bounty Hunter).
  • Pick heroes with high base armor or armor‑reduction abilities to mitigate Feast.
  • Consider heroes with silences or disables that can interrupt Infest/Consume.

Laning Against Lifestealer

  • Harass early with ranged attacks; Lifestealer is weakest before he gets a few levels of Ghoul Frenzy.
  • Keep the lane wave near your tower to deny easy access for Infest on creeps.
  • Punish his Open Wounds cooldown by pulling back when he initiates; the slow and heal are wasted if he can’t follow up.
  • Use vision (wards, sentries) on low‑health creeps to catch him attempting to Infest.

Itemizing Against Lifestealer

Blade Mail — reflects Lifestealer’s Feast damage back to him, turning his own sustain into a liability.
Heaven’s Halberd — disarms Lifestealer, preventing his high‑damage attacks while he’s in Rage.
Lotus Orb — reflects Lifestealer’s Infest and Consume attempts, forcing him to stay out of melee.
Assault Cuirass — provides armor reduction to allies and increases your own armor, diminishing Lifestealer’s physical damage output.

lina.name: Lina
lina.guideHtml:
Lina remains a high‑damage nuker and semi‑carry in the 7.41 meta, sitting at a 49.5% win rate across 645,398 recent ranked matches. She excels at burst damage and snowballing mid‑game, but her win‑rate dip against mobile, burst‑resistant heroes makes lane and item choices critical.

How to Play Lina

Laning Phase

  • Harass with Dragon Slave early; the wave’s 600‑unit range lets you poke safely while stacking Fiery Soul for attack‑speed.
  • Light Strike Array on the first wave of creeps to secure lane control and deter aggressive supports (e.g., Lion, Shadow Shaman).
  • Activate Flame Cloak when you anticipate heavy harass or a gank; the magic resistance and max Fiary Soul stacks give a temporary survivability window.
  • Prioritize slow‑burn damage on tanky lane opponents (e.g., Tidehunter, Bristleback) to turn Lina’s spell damage into sustained pressure.
  • Against mobile heroes like Pangolier or Monkey King (who currently give Lina only ~36% win‑rate), play more defensively and look for early rotations rather than extended trades.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 6 – Laguna Blade becomes a reliable kill‑steal and tower‑damage tool; pair it with Light Strike Array for stun‑follow‑up.
  • Roam after securing a lane advantage; use the mobility of Light Strike Array and the burst of Laguna Blade to pick off squishy supports in the mid lane.
  • Stack Fiery Soul before team fights: cast Dragon Slave or Light Strike Array repeatedly to reach the 6‑stack cap, maximizing attack speed and movement speed.
  • Target backline heroes (e.g., Invoker, Leshrac) who currently give Lina sub‑40% win‑rates; a well‑timed Light Strike Array + Laguna Blade can swing the odds in your favor.

Late Game

  • Win condition: burst down the enemy core before they can activate their ultimates; Lina’s single‑target damage is lethal when Fiery Soul is at max.
  • Positioning: stay behind front‑line tanks; use Flame Cloak’s movement speed to reposition after casting spells.
  • Avoid prolonged fights against heroes with strong disables or high burst (e.g., Timbersaw, Slardar) – Lina’s relatively low survivability can turn a fight into a loss.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain against harass in solo lanes.
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery after early trades.
  • Iron Branch ×2 — cheap stats and can be later built into Magic Wand.
  • Faerie Fire — emergency burst damage to finish low‑HP enemies.

Core Items

  • Eul's Scepter of Divinity — provides mana, movement speed, and a reliable self‑disable to dodge dangerous spells.
  • Aghanim's Scepter — upgrades Laguna Blade to a pure‑damage spell, essential against magic‑resistant heroes like Underlord (where Lina enjoys a 59.7% win‑rate).
  • Black King Bar — necessary against heavy disable lineups (e.g., Invoker, Leshrac) that currently suppress Lina’s win‑rate.
  • Boots of Travel — enhances map mobility for late‑game roams and split‑pushing.

Situational Items

  • Shiva's Guard — armor and aura against physical heroes like Axe (54.4% win‑rate) and Slardar.
  • Scythe of Vyse — additional hard‑disable when Light Strike Array’s stun is on cooldown.
  • Octarine Core — reduces cooldowns on Fiery Soul and Laguna Blade, boosting sustained damage.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target spells, useful versus Timbersaw’s reactive abilities.
  • Glimmer Cape — extra magic resistance and invisibility to survive burst from Pangolier or Monkey King.

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑committing with Light Strike Array without Flame Cloak, getting caught by enemy disables.
  • Neglecting Fiery Soul stacks; failing to cast spells between fights wastes the attack‑speed boost.
  • Itemizing too early for damage (e.g., jumping straight to Daedalus) instead of securing survivability against mobile counters.
  • Chasing kills with Laguna Blade on heroes that have high magic resistance or are under protective auras, leading to wasted cooldown.

FAQ

Is Lina good in the current patch?

Yes. Lina’s 49.5% win rate across over 645 k ranked games shows she’s a viable pick, especially against heroes like Underlord and Axe where she enjoys >54% win rates. Her burst potential remains strong, but she must avoid matchups where she currently wins <40% (e.g., Pangolier, Leshrac).

What lane does Lina play?

Lina is most commonly played in the mid lane as a semi‑carry, but she also sees play as a support in off‑lane or safe‑lane setups, leveraging her stun and burst to create space for the carry.

Who counters Lina?

Mobile, burst‑resistant heroes such as Pangolier (35.8% win rate vs. Lina), Leshrac (35.9%), Monkey King (36.0%), Invoker (37.6%), Timbersaw (38.8%), and Slardar (39.3%) are the toughest matchups. Building defensive items and playing conservatively against them is essential.
lina.counterHtml:
Lina’s burst damage and ever‑growing Fiery Soul make her a lethal mid‑lane threat, but she is extremely squishy and relies on spell‑casting to stay alive. The key to shutting her down is denying her spell‑damage windows, out‑lasting her burst, and forcing her into unfavorable melee engagements.

Why These Heroes Beat Lina

Pangolier

Pangolier’s Shield Crash and Swashbuckle give him high burst armor and mobility, allowing him to dodge Lina’s Light Strike Array and Dragon Slave while closing the distance. Use Swashbuckle to weave through Lina’s spell cooldowns and punish her when her Fiery Soul stacks expire.

Leshrac

Leshrac’s Lightning Storm and Pulse Nova provide constant AoE magic damage that forces Lina to stay on the defensive, while his Split Earth offers a reliable stun that interrupts Laguna Blade. Play aggressively after a successful Split Earth when Lina’s Fiery Soul stacks are low.

Monkey King

Monkey King’s Tree Dance and Jungle Rush give him superior mobility to evade Lina’s stun and burst, and his Wukong’s Command creates a barrier that blocks Dragon Slave’s linear wave. Initiate with Jungle Rush when Lina’s Flame Cloak is on cooldown to capitalize on her reduced survivability.

Invoker

Invoker’s Cold Snap and EMP punish Lina’s spell‑spam by delivering repeated stuns and massive mana burn, nullifying her Fiery Soul stacks. Pair Cold Snap with a quick Sun Strike after Lina casts Laguna Blade to maximize burst before she can react.

Timbersaw

Timbersaw’s Whirling Death and Timber Chain give him pure damage and a way to dodge Lina’s Light Strike Array, while his Reactive Armor mitigates magic damage from Laguna Blade. Engage with Whirling Death after Lina’s Flame Cloak expires to exploit her low magic resistance.

Drafting Against Lina

  • Prioritize heroes with strong early magic resistance or innate spell‑block (e.g., Timbersaw, Pugna).
  • Pick mobile melee heroes that can close the gap before Lina lands Light Strike Array.
  • Ban or avoid picking heroes that synergize with Fiery Soul stacks (e.g., Scepter‑dependent spellcasters).
  • Include at least one reliable stun or silence to interrupt Laguna Blade.

Laning Against Lina

  • Harass with ranged attacks or creeps when Lina’s Fiery Soul stacks are low (first 18 seconds after a spell).
  • Force her to use Light Strike Array defensively; the stun leaves her vulnerable to counter‑harass.
  • Trade after she activates Flame Cloak—her spell damage spikes but her movement is predictable, making her an easy target for burst.
  • Keep a ward on the river to prevent her from roaming with Light Strike Array and catching you off‑guard.

Itemizing Against Lina

Black King Bar — blocks Lina’s stun and burst, allowing you to survive her combo.
Pipe of Insight — provides magic damage reduction that mitigates Dragon Slave and Laguna Blade.
Eul’s Scepter — silences Lina, cancels Fiery Soul stack buildup, and can be used to dodge Light Strike Array.
Aghanim’s Scepter (for heroes like Timbersaw) — upgrades pure‑damage abilities to ignore magic resistance, neutralizing Lina’s high spell damage.

lion.name: Lion
lion.guideHtml:
Lion is a high‑burst, disable‑heavy support whose kit excels at locking down key targets and delivering massive single‑target damage with Finger of Death. On patch 7.41 his overall pub win rate sits at 48.6 % across 932,819 ranked games, placing him solidly in the middle of the support tier. He remains a reliable pick in coordinated play, though his effectiveness swings sharply against certain heroes.

How to Play Lion

Laning Phase

  • Early Earth Spike: Use the 2‑second cast to punish melee heroes that overextend; the stun also blocks creep aggro, keeping the lane safe.
  • Pre‑level 2 Hex on the enemy off‑laner (often a melee core) to force a safe lane equilibrium and deny experience.
  • Mana Drain on yourself when you run low on mana; the 50 % mana transfer also grants you movement speed, helping you stay with the carry.
  • Stack neutral camps with Earth Spike on the far side of the lane; the stun prevents neutral creep from attacking you while you pull.
  • Watch for Lycan, Treant, and Undying – these match‑ups have sub‑40 % win rates for Lion (36.1 % vs Lycan, 38.9 % vs Treant, 39.3 % vs Undying) and require extra caution in lane (e.g., early Hex on their summons).

Mid Game

  • Hit a level 6 Finger of Death on a high‑value target; the damage spike often forces the enemy to retreat or die.
  • Combo Hex → Earth Spike → Finger of Death to maximize burst; the stun from Earth Spike extends Hex’s duration.
  • Roam with Mana Drain to assist other lanes; the channel can be broken if you need to drop a quick Hex on a fleeing hero.
  • Secure objectives (Roshan, towers) after a successful kill; Lion’s 20 % spell amplification from To Hell and Back lasts 90 s after a kill/assist, amplifying subsequent spells.

Late Game

  • Pick off squishy carries with Finger of Death followed by a quick Hex; the amplified damage can turn fights even when you’re outnumbered.
  • Stay behind front‑liners; a misplaced Earth Spike can stun your own team, and a missed Hex on a high‑impact hero (e.g., Sven, Tinker) can cost the game.
  • Win condition: force enemy cores to die before they can use their ultimates; Lion’s burst and disables are decisive in 5‑v‑5 engagements.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane.
  • Healing Salve — emergency health after early skirmishes.
  • Clarity — keep mana for early Earth Spike/Hex.
  • Observer Ward — vision to protect against ganks and set up early rotations.
  • Sentry Ward — detect invisible heroes (e.g., Io, Templar Assassin) that can punish Lion.

Core Items

  • Arcane Boots — 250 mana pool and movement speed; fuels Mana Drain and Finger of Death.
  • Aether Lens — 75 % cast range increase on all spells, making Hex and Earth Spike safer.
  • Blink Dagger — instant positioning for surprise Hex/FoD combos and to escape dangerous fights.
  • Glimmer Cape — survivability against burst heroes like Sven and Tinker; also useful for protecting allies during a Hex.

Situational Items

  • Force Staff — extra mobility when you’re locked down by Earth Spirit or Monkey King.
  • Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — additional disable and self‑save against melee initiators; also synergizes with Mana Drain for extra mana steal.
  • Ghost Scepter — against right‑click heavy heroes (Sven, Monkey King) when you need to survive a focus fire.
  • Aghanim’s Shard — upgrades Mana Drain to also give a small movement speed boost to allies, improving lane sustain.
  • Scythe of Vyse (upgrade from Hex) — if you need a permanent hard‑disable on a core that is otherwise hard to lock down.

Common Mistakes

  • Spamming Earth Spike without vision – you often stun your own creeps or miss the enemy, giving them free farm.
  • Using Mana Drain on enemies with no mana – the extra slow is minor; better to switch to Hex or save the channel for an ally.
  • Waiting too long for Finger of Death – missing the early‑game burst window lets enemy cores snowball; aim for a FoD on level 6 whenever possible.
  • Positioning too aggressively – Lion’s low HP makes him a prime target for initiators like Earth Spirit; always stay behind a front‑liner or with a Blink escape.

FAQ

Is Lion good in the current patch?

Yes. Lion’s overall win rate of 48.6 % places him as a viable support on patch 7.41, especially on teams that can capitalize on his burst and disable potential.

What lane does Lion play?

Lion is typically played as a position 5 support in the safe lane, pairing with a carry to provide early lane control via Earth Spike and Hex, then roaming to mid and off‑lane as the game progresses.

Who counters Lion?

Heroes that can survive his burst and punish his low survivability—Lycan, Treant Protector, Undying, Earth Spirit, Monkey King, and Abaddon—currently give Lion sub‑40 % win rates (e.g., 36.1 % vs Lycan). Vision denial and early aggression are key to neutralizing his impact.
lion.counterHtml:

The key to shutting him down is to survive his stun‑hex combo, out‑mana him, and force fights where his burst cannot be followed up by a kill.

Why These Heroes Beat Lion

Lycan

Lycan’s summons and Summon Wolves give him constant frontline pressure that forces Lion to waste mana on early disables, while Lycan’s Feral Impulse provides burst damage that can kill Lion before he lands Finger of Death.
Tip: Push early and force Lion to defend; his mana pool empties quickly against multiple wolves.

Treant Protector

Treant’s Nature’s Guise grants invisibility and Living Armor mitigates Lion’s burst damage, while his Overgrowth silences Lion, preventing Hex and Finger of Death from being cast.
Tip: Time Overgrowth right after Lion lands Earth Spike to lock him down and punish his low mobility.

Undying

Undying’s Decay and Soul Rip drain Lion’s health and mana, shrinking his ability window, and his Flesh Golem provides massive armor that negates Lion’s burst.
Tip: Stack Decay early; the mana loss forces Lion to miss his crucial disables.

Earth Spirit

Earth Spirit’s Rolling Boulder and Geomagnetic Grip can interrupt Lion’s channel on Mana Drain and reposition him away from his own stun line. His Stone Remnant creates terrain that blocks Lion’s linear Earth Spike.
Tip: Place a Stone Remnant behind Lion before casting Earth Spike to break the stun.

Monkey King

Monkey King’s Tree Dance gives him vertical mobility that dodges Lion’s linear Earth Spike, and his Jungle Strike provides burst damage that can kill Lion before the Finger of Death cooldown. His Wukong’s Command creates a zone where Lion’s Hex can’t reach.
Tip: Engage from the trees; the height advantage forces Lion to waste his stun on a moving target.

Drafting Against Lion

  • Prioritize heroes with high mana pools or mana‑regeneration (e.g., Alchemist, Keeper of the Light).
  • Choose line‑breakers or heroes with strong early wave clear to deny Lion lane control.
  • Pick silences/disables that can interrupt Mana Drain and Finger of Death (e.g., Earth Spirit, Silencer).
  • Avoid picking heroes that heavily rely on mana‑intensive spells without sustain.

Laning Against Lion

  • Trade when Lion’s Mana Drain is on cooldown; his burst window shrinks dramatically.
  • Exploit the 2‑second stun from Earth Spike: attack immediately after the stun ends, before Hex can be cast.
  • Harass with creep‑pull or aggressive lane equilibrium to force Lion to over‑extend and lose mana.
  • Punish his early aggression with a well‑timed Jungle Strike or Feral Impulse to kill him before he can secure a kill for the “To Hell and Back” buff.

Itemizing Against Lion

Mekansm — provides burst heal and armor to survive Earth Spike + Hex combo.
Glimmer Cape — grants temporary magic immunity, nullifying Finger of Death and Mana Drain.
Eul’s Scepter — cyclone removes Lion from the fight, breaking his channel and buying time for allies.
Aghanim’s Shard (Lion) — if you must play Lion, the shard’s extra stun reduces his own vulnerability to counters.

lone-druid.name: Lone Druid
lone-druid.guideHtml:
Lone Druid is a unique carry/pusher who fights alongside his damage‑soaking Spirit Bear. On patch 7.41 his win‑rate sits at 48.6 % over 80 k recent ranked games, making him a viable but slightly below‑average pick in the current meta. He excels when he can isolate a single target and scale into a late‑game siege engine, but struggles against heroes that can quickly burst or silence both him and his bear.

How to Play Lone Druid

Laning Phase

  • Summon Spirit Bear early – buy a Tango and Iron Branch for the bear, then use Summon Spirit Bear at level 1 to secure lane equilibrium and scout enemy rotations.
  • Entangle for lane control – at level 2 the bear can apply 2 stacks of Entangle to enemy heroes; once the enemy reaches 5 stacks the bear can root them, allowing you to deny farm or secure a kill.
  • Spirit Link for sustain – keep the bear within 1100 units; the shared lifesteal mitigates creep damage and lets you stay in lane longer against aggressive opponents like Timbersaw or Lifestealer.
  • Avoid over‑extending the bear – if the bear strays >1100 units you lose its attack and take 20 % max‑health backlash; always keep a safe retreat path.
  • Play around the enemy’s early disables – heroes such as Shadow Shaman (easy matchup) give you space to farm, while Slardar and Void Spirit require you to keep the bear hidden until you have a Blink Dagger or Force Staff.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 12–16 – you now have Savage Roar and a fully upgraded bear; start taking outer towers and forcing rotations.
  • Use Savage Roar for disengage – the 20 % movement speed boost and fear effect lets you and the bear escape tight fights or chase low‑HP heroes.
  • Pick off isolated targets – combine Entangle (5 stacks on creeps) with the bear’s high burst to eliminate squishy supports (e.g., Viper, Dark Willow) who are currently easy matchups.
  • Secure vision and split‑push – place deep wards, then use the bear’s tankiness to pressure side lanes while you farm jungle or build items.

Late Game

  • True Form as a win condition – morph into a bear when you need extra durability and damage in team fights; the bonus armor and health let you front‑line while the bear continues to dish out damage.
  • Position the bear as the front line – keep the bear between you and enemy disables; its high HP and armor let it absorb Keeper of the Light’s mana‑burn or Doom’s suppression longer.
  • Avoid being caught without Entangle – if you lose the bear or its stacks, you become vulnerable to burst heroes like Lifestealer and Timbersaw, the toughest matchups on the patch.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain for both you and the bear in lane.
  • Enchanted Mango — cheap burst for early Entangle combos.
  • Iron Branch x2 — cheap stats and can be later built into a Magic Wand.
  • Faerie Fire — emergency health for the bear when it gets caught.

Core Items

  • Power Treads — flexible stats and attack speed for both hero and bear.
  • Mask of Madness — huge lifesteal boost for the bear’s melee attacks.
  • Manta Style — provides a second Entangle on the bear and a way to dispel silences from Keeper of the Light.
  • Black King Bar — essential against heavy magic damage and disables (e.g., Void Spirit, Doom).

Situational Items

  • Blink Dagger — instant repositioning for Entangle catches and escaping Savage Roar pushes.
  • Force Staff – saves the bear from backlash distance and helps close gaps on mobile heroes like Timbersaw.
  • Aghanim’s Scepter – upgrades Savage Roar radius, making fear more reliable in team fights.
  • Heart of Tarrasque – extra survivability when you’re forced into front‑line fights against Slardar or Lifestealer.
  • Assault Cuirass – armor aura protects the bear against physical burst and improves lane pressure.

Common Mistakes

  • Leaving the bear too far – exceeding the 1100 unit limit triggers backlash damage and removes the bear’s attack.
  • Using Entangle without stack buildup – casting too early wastes the root; wait until the enemy has 5 stacks for a guaranteed lock.
  • Ignoring vision – without deep wards the bear can be picked off by gank‑heavy heroes like Timbersaw.
  • Rushing True Form – morphing before you have sufficient items leaves you vulnerable to burst and reduces your ranged harassment.

FAQ

Is Lone Druid good in the current patch?

Lone Druid’s win‑rate of 48.6 % makes him a borderline pick on patch 7.41. He can dominate in easy matchups (e.g., Shadow Shaman 85.7 % win) but struggles against bursty, silencing heroes like Lifestealer (45.0 % win) and Timbersaw (45.5 % win).

What lane does Lone Druid play?

Lone Druid is typically played in the safe lane as a carry, using his Spirit Bear to secure farm and control the lane with Entangle. The bear’s tankiness also allows him to safely solo the off‑lane in some lower‑skill games.

Who counters Lone Druid?

The toughest counters are Lifestealer, Timbersaw, Keeper of the Light, Slardar, Void Spirit, and Doom, all of which have win‑rates around 45‑52 % against him. Their burst damage, silences, and mobility can quickly eliminate both Lone Druid and his bear if you’re caught without proper defensive items.
lone-druid.counterHtml:
Lone Druid’s threat comes from his high‑damage, mobile Spirit Bear and the ability to share lifesteal and movement speed with Spirit Link. The core way to shut him down is to apply constant, bursty pressure that forces the bear to stay close to its master, then punish the inevitable backlash damage when the bear is pulled away.

Why These Heroes Beat Lone Druid

Lifestealer

Lifestealer’s Infest lets him dive onto the Spirit Bear, forcing the bear to stay within 1100 units or suffer the 20 % max‑health backlash on Lone Druid. Open Wounds adds a strong heal‑steal that outpaces the bear’s lifesteal, while Rage provides magic immunity against Entangle damage.
Tip: Start with a quick Infest → Open Wounds combo on the bear; the bear’s forced proximity will trigger Lone Druid’s backlash and give you a health swing.

Timbersaw

Timbersaw’s pure‑damage Whirling Death and Timber Chain shred the bear’s health regardless of armor, and his Reactive Armor reduces the impact of the bear’s burst. The constant AoE damage forces Lone Druid to stay near the bear, quickly draining his mana and health.
Tip: Use a short‑range Timber Chain to pull the bear into a tree, then unleash Whirling Death while the bear is stuck—Lone Druid will take the backlash and lose lane control.

Keeper of the Light

Keeper’s Illuminate and Mana Leak drain the bear’s mana pool, limiting the bear’s ability to use items and the Spirit Link lifesteal. Chakra Magic gives Keeper a shield that blocks the bear’s burst damage, and Blinding Light silences Lone Druid, preventing a timely Savage Roar retreat.
Tip: Spam Mana Leak on the bear early; a mana‑starved bear can’t sustain fights, and Keeper’s shield will absorb the bear’s retaliation.

Slardar

Slithereen Crush applies a hard‑stop and armor reduction that makes the bear’s physical attacks far less effective. Amplify Damage further lowers the bear’s armor, letting you kill it quickly. Slardar’s Bash also provides a reliable stun on Lone Druid, preventing him from repositioning with Spirit Link.
Tip: Initiate with Slithereen Crush on the bear, then follow up with a Bash on Lone Druid; the combined armor loss and stun forces a lane loss for the Druid.

Void Spirit

Void’s Aether Remnant roots the bear, breaking the distance requirement for the backlash damage and making the bear vulnerable to burst. Resonant Pulse and Astral Step give Void high mobility to dodge Entangle and chase the bear. His Dissimilate provides a magic shield that mitigates the bear’s damage over time.
Tip: Drop an Aether Remnant on the bear as soon as it appears; the root forces the bear to stay close, and you can follow with a quick Resonant Pulse combo for a lethal kill.

Drafting Against Lone Druid

  • Prioritize heroes with strong burst magic damage or pure damage (e.g., Timbersaw, Void Spirit).
  • Include at least one hero with reliable disables that can hit both Lone Druid and the bear (e.g., Slardar, Lion).
  • Pick heroes that can drain or deny mana/health regeneration (Keeper of the Light, Lifestealer).
  • Avoid picking long‑range right‑click carries that give Lone Druid time to farm the bear.

Laning Against Lone Druid

  • Harass the bear early; the bear’s damage drops sharply before it gets a core item.
  • Force Lone Druid to stay within 1100 units of the bear to trigger the 20 % max‑health backlash.
  • Trade when Lone Druid attempts to use Savage Roar—the movement speed boost can be wasted if you have a stun ready.
  • Keep the lane tight; the bear loses attack range quickly when pulled away, giving you a window to all‑in.

Itemizing Against Lone Druid

Manta Style — creates duplicate bears that split the Spirit Link lifesteal and can break Entangle’s stack buildup.
Heaven’s Halberd — disarms the bear, nullifying its primary source of damage and forcing Lone Druid into a vulnerable position.
Diffusal Blade — burns the bear’s mana, preventing it from using items and reducing the effectiveness of Spirit Link.
Ghost Scepter — blocks the bear’s physical attacks, allowing you to survive its burst while you focus on Lone Druid.

luna.name: Luna
luna.guideHtml:
Luna is a hard‑carry hero whose kit revolves around burst magical damage, fast attack speed, and strong night‑time presence. In the current 7.41 meta she sits near the middle of the spectrum with a 49.8% win rate across 363,586 recent ranked matches, making her a viable but not dominant pick.

How to Play Luna

Laning Phase

  • Use Lucent Beam early to harass and secure last hits; the brief stun helps win lane against melee heroes.
  • Position Lunar Orbit so the rotating glaives block incoming harass from ranged opponents and add extra damage to creeps.
  • Against aggressive supports (e.g., Clockwerk, Techies) keep distance and rely on the stun from Lucent Beam to punish their initiation.
  • Stack the lane with Moon Glaives empowered attacks; the bounces increase farm speed and can clear creep waves faster than most carries.
  • If the lane is contested, pull the wave and use Lunar Blessing to grant yourself extra damage while denying enemy experience.

Mid Game

  • Hit the first power spike at Level 6 – Eclipse becomes a reliable team‑fight tool and a strong tower‑damage source.
  • Prioritize taking mid tier towers with Eclipse + Moon Glaives; the global night vision from Lunar Blessing aids map awareness.
  • Join fights when you have at least Manta Style or Black King Bar; Luna’s damage output peaks when she can freely bounce glaives.
  • Use Lunar Blessing at night to push multiple lanes simultaneously—its global effect provides a damage boost to allies and extra vision.

Late Game

  • Win condition: force night‑time team fights where Eclipse can hit multiple heroes and Lunar Blessing is global, overwhelming enemy backlines.
  • Position behind front‑liners; Luna’s low health makes her vulnerable to burst heroes like Legion Commander and Bane.
  • Avoid being caught out of vision; losing Luna early in a late‑game fight usually means the enemy can shut down your carry potential.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane, especially against harass from Clockwerk or Techies.
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery after Lucent Beam stuns.
  • Iron Branch ×2 — cheap stats and can be later built into a Magic Wand.
  • Slippers of Agility — early attack damage for better last‑hitting.

Core Items

  • Power Treads — attack speed and attribute flexibility; switch to agility for burst damage.
  • Manta Style — amplifies Moon Glaives bounce damage and provides a dispel against Bane’s Nightmare.
  • Black King Bar — essential against Legion Commander’s Duel and Bane’s ultimate.
  • Satanic — survivability in late‑game fights; lifesteal offsets burst damage.

Situational Items

  • Butterfly — counters high‑evasion heroes like Monkey King and increases damage output.
  • Monkey King Bar — reliable against evasion; useful when facing Monkey King (40.7% win rate).
  • Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — self‑save against Techies mines and to set up Lucent Beam stuns.
  • Linken’s Sphere — blocks single‑target disables from Legion Commander and Bane.
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Eclipse to hit more targets, great for team fights against clustered heroes like Earthshaker.
  • Satanic — alternative to Butterfly when you need more survivability against burst.

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑extending without BKB – diving into fights before Black King Bar leaves Luna vulnerable to Legion Commander and Bane.
  • Neglecting Lunar Blessing timing – failing to capitalize on the global night‑time damage boost wastes a major source of team utility.
  • Using Moon Glaives on single‑target heroes – bouncing is most effective on clustered creeps or team‑fight clusters; on lone targets it wastes damage.
  • Poor wave management – stacking creeps too early can invite ganks from Clockwerk and Techies, reducing farm efficiency.

FAQ

Is Luna good in the current patch?

Luna sits at a 49.8% win rate on the latest 7.41 patch, making her a solid but not top‑tier carry. She excels in mid‑game pushes and night‑time team fights, though she can struggle against hard‑counter heroes.

What lane does Luna play?

Luna is typically played in the safe lane as a carry, often paired with a support that can protect her early game and set up Lucent Beam stuns. She can also be flexed to the mid lane if a team needs a strong late‑game damage source.

Who counters Luna?

The toughest matchups right now are Clockwerk (36.4% win rate), Techies (38.5%), Legion Commander (39.0%), Bane (40.4%), Monkey King (40.7%), and Keeper of the Light (41.2%). These heroes either lock her down, out‑farm her, or nullify her night‑time advantage.
luna.counterHtml:
Luna’s damage spikes come from her Moon Glaives‑enhanced attacks and the burst of Lucent Beam/Eclipse. She thrives when she can stay alive long enough to bounce glaives across clustered foes, so shutting her down hinges on disrupting her positioning, silencing or stunning her before she can unleash her glaive wave, and forcing early deaths.

Why These Heroes Beat Luna

Clockwerk

Clockwerk’s Hookshot pulls Luna out of position and his Battery Assault silences her, preventing Lucent Beam and Eclipse casts. A well‑timed Hookshot into a wall or a tower isolates Luna and forces a fight on his terms.
Tip: Aim Hookshot at the edge of the lane to trap Luna against the creep block, then follow up with Battery Assault for a quick kill.

Techies

Techies’ Remote Mines and Stasis Trap provide constant zoning that punishes Luna’s need to stay in melee range for Moon Glaives. A mine detonated on Luna’s path instantly kills her before she can bounce glaives.
Tip: Plant mines in the lane’s high‑traffic spots and keep a Remote Mine on cooldown to react to Luna’s approach.

Legion Commander

Legion Commander’s Overwhelming Odds deals massive damage to multiple units, and her Duel forces Luna into a 1‑v‑1 where Luna’s low burst damage is outclassed. The stun from Press the Attack also interrupts Luna’s Lucent Beam.
Tip: Initiate Duel as soon as Luna lands her first Moon Glaive bounce; the stun from Duel prevents further bounces and often secures a kill.

Bane

Bane’s Nightmare and Enfeeble silence Luna, shutting down both Lucent Beam and Eclipse while drastically reducing her attack damage. His Brain Sap provides sustain, allowing him to survive Luna’s early harass.
Tip: Chain‑cast Nightmare on Luna whenever she steps up for a glaive bounce; follow with Enfeeble to cripple her damage output.

Monkey King

Monkey King’s Jungle Cry provides a strong AoE silence that blocks Luna’s Lucent Beam and Eclipse, while his Tree Dance lets him dodge Moon Glaives and reposition. His Wukong’s Command creates a barrier that blocks Luna’s glaive rotation.
Tip: Use Tree Dance to jump over Luna’s glaive radius, then activate Jungle Cry to silence her before she can cast Eclipse.

Drafting Against Luna

  • Prioritize heroes with reliable silences or stuns (e.g., Clockwerk, Bane, Legion Commander).
  • Pick high‑burst, low‑mana heroes that can kill Luna before she gets a few Moon Glaive bounces.
  • Include mobile or gap‑closer heroes that can dodge or interrupt her glaive rotation.
  • Consider anti‑push heroes that can force early fights, denying Luna farm.

Laning Against Luna

  • Harass Luna when she steps up for her first Moon Glaive bounce; she is weakest before she lands a second bounce.
  • Use tower range and creep block to deny her safe positioning for Lucent Beam.
  • Punish her when she uses Lucent Beam—she is vulnerable during the brief stun animation.
  • Keep lane equilibrium low to force Luna into contested fights where her damage is less effective.

Itemizing Against Luna

Force Staff — pushes Luna out of her glaive radius and interrupts Lucent Beam casts.
Eul’s Scepter — cyclone disables Luna, preventing her from using Moon Glaives and Eclipse.
Ghost Scepter — makes you untargetable by Luna’s physical attacks and Moon Glaives.
Scythe of Vyse – long‑duration hex removes Luna from fights, nullifying all her abilities.

lycan.name: Lycan
lycan.guideHtml:
Lycan remains a high‑damage, split‑pushing juggernaut in the current meta, hovering around a 48.4% win rate over 55 k recent ranked games (OpenDota, July 2026). His toolkit of wolves, global night Howl, and Shapeshift makes him a potent late‑game carry, but the win‑rate dip shows he still needs careful play against certain mid‑lane heroes.

How to Play Lycan

Laning Phase

  • Summon Wolves early (level 1) to harass and secure last hits; the wolves’ damage scales with your Feral Impulse and Apex Predator later.
  • At level 3, the wolves gain Permanent Invisibility – use this to scout enemy jungle or set up surprise ganks on lane opponents like Leshrac or Beastmaster, who currently give you sub‑40% win rates.
  • Howl on a 2000‑range can cripple aggressive mid‑lane heroes (e.g., Ogre Magi, Tusk) by reducing their armor and attack damage, making them easier to kill with wolves.
  • Use Wolf Bite on a lane ally (support or off‑lane) to grant both 40 % lifesteal; this synergy is especially useful against sustain heroes such as Bane.
  • Prioritize a safe creep equilibrium; Lycan’s early damage is low, so avoid extended trades until Feral Impulse gives you reliable HP regen.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 6 – unlock Shapeshift for critical strikes and immunity to slows; immediately start split‑pushing tier‑2 towers.
  • Group with your wolves and Howl at night for a global armor/attack damage debuff, enabling coordinated pushes or team fights against heroes like Terrorblade (you still win only ~43 %).
  • Take neutral camps with Apex Predator to accelerate farm; prioritize Ancient camps for extra gold and experience.
  • When you have Summon Wolves level 4 (Cripple), target enemy cores in fights; the 20 % cripple proc adds 8 dps and reduces attack speed, which is crucial against high‑damage heroes like Sven (your win rate vs him is 68.7%).

Late Game

  • Win condition: Use Shapeshift + wolves to force high‑ground or tier‑3 pushes while your team secures vision; the global night Howl can turn the tide of any late‑game team fight.
  • Positioning: Stay near your wolves; they provide damage, invisibility, and cripple. Keep a safe distance from burst magic (e.g., Leshrac, Bane) that still give you poor win rates.
  • Losing the game: Getting caught without wolves or after losing Shapeshift cooldown often leads to being focused down by enemy cores; avoid over‑extending without vision.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango & Healing Salve — sustain in lane while you farm wolves.
  • Stout Shield — mitigates harassment from early magic damage heroes.
  • Quelling Blade — helps secure creep last hits before you have wolves.
  • Observer Ward — early vision to protect invisible wolves.

Core Items

  • Echo Sabre — synergy with Shapeshift’s critical strikes and provides early damage.
  • Phase Boots — extra movement for split‑pushing and to stay out of enemy disables.
  • Mask of Madness — amplifies lifesteal from Wolf Bite and gives high burst damage in fights.
  • Black King Bar — essential against magic‑heavy matchups (Leshrac, Bane) where your win rate is lowest.

Situational Items

  • Abyssal Blade — lockdown for heroes like Tusk or Ogre Magi that can otherwise kite you.
  • Heart of Tarrasque — survivability against burst damage and to sustain long pushes.
  • Manta Style — dispels silences and provides extra split‑push speed; useful vs Beastmaster’s summons.
  • Sange & Yasha — extra movement and status resistance when you need to chase down Terrorblade.
  • Linken’s Sphere — blocks single‑target disables from Bane or Lion.

Common Mistakes

  • Ignoring wolf invisibility – many low‑MMR players forget to level wolves to 3, losing a huge scouting and gank advantage.
  • Delaying Shapeshift – waiting too long to upgrade to Shapeshift wastes the critical‑strike window and slows split‑push pressure.
  • Over‑extending without vision – pushing tier‑2 towers without wards lets enemies like Leshrac catch you with nukes.
  • Neglecting night Howl – failing to coordinate night pushes means missing the global armor/attack damage debuff that can swing fights.

FAQ

Is Lycan good in the current patch?

Yes. Lycan sits at a 48.4% win rate on the latest ranked data, making him a viable carry/pusher. He excels against heroes like Sven (68.7% win) and Axe (64.4% win), though he struggles against magic‑heavy mid‑laners such as Leshrac and Beastmaster.

What lane does Lycan play?

Lycan is typically played in the safe lane (carry) or as a solo off‑lane for early wolf pressure. The lane choice depends on your team’s draft; safe lane gives you farm for core items, while off‑lane can exploit early wolf invisibility against aggressive opponents.

Who counters Lycan?

Heroes with strong magic burst and disables—Leshrac, Beastmaster, Ogre Magi, Bane, and Tusk—currently give Lycan sub‑40% win rates. Building early Black King Bar and maintaining vision are essential to survive their pressure.
lycan.counterHtml:

Why These Heroes Beat Lycan

Leshrac

Leshrac’s Lightning Storm and Split Earth deal pure damage that ignores armor, cutting through the armor reduction from Howl and the wolves’ low survivability. Use Pulse Nova to clear Lycan’s wolves in a wide radius before he can engage. Tip: Keep Leshrac’s mana high and position near the river to punish Lycan’s attempts to farm jungle camps.

Beastmaster

Beastmaster’s Call of the Wild summons permanent summons that out‑last Lycan’s wolves and can tank his damage, while Primal Roar provides a long‑duration stun that interrupts Lycan’s Shapeshift and Howl. The vision from Hawk also reveals Lycan’s split‑push routes. Tip: Prioritize early Boar and Hawk upgrades to scout and kill wolves before they become a threat.

Ogre Magi

Ogre’s Fireblast and Ignite apply reliable stun and damage over time, easily bursting wolves that lack magic resistance. Multicast on Fireblast can chain‑stun Lycan and his pack, preventing him from using Howl effectively. Tip: Build Aether Lens for longer cast range, allowing you to harass Lycan from safety.

Terrorblade

Terrorblade’s Metamorphosis grants massive ranged damage that melts wolves, and his Sunder can turn Lycan’s own health against him after a successful wolf kill. The Reflection illusion from Conjure Image also forces Lycan to split his focus, weakening his pack cohesion. Tip: Push lanes early with Metamorphosis to force Lycan to defend, denying him farm for wolves.

Bane

Bane’s Nightmare and Enfeeble silence Lycan, stopping him from casting Howl or summoning wolves at crucial moments. Fiend’s Grip locks Lycan down for 5 seconds, letting allies burst his wolves and the hero himself. Tip: Pair Bane with a strong disable or burst hero to capitalize on the long channel of Fiend’s Grip.

Drafting Against Lycan

  • Prioritize heroes with strong AoE magic damage or pure damage (e.g., Leshrac, Lina).
  • Pick heroes with reliable single‑target stuns or silences to interrupt Howl and Shapeshift.
  • Choose lane‑dominant heroes that can kill wolves early (e.g., Beastmaster, Ogre Magi).
  • Avoid heroes that scale poorly into late‑game split‑push and lack crowd control.

Laning Against Lycan

  • Harass Lycan before he gets a level 2 Summon Wolves; early tower pressure forces him to miss wolf spawns.
  • Trade when his wolves are on cooldown; his damage drops dramatically without them.
  • Punish his attempts to farm jungle camps with lane‑clear spells that also damage wolves (e.g., Leshrac’s Lightning Storm).
  • Keep vision on the river and jungle to spot and kill wolves before they accumulate.

Itemizing Against Lycan

Mekansm — burst heal and armor buff that mitigates the armor reduction from Howl and keeps allies alive against wolf damage.

Scythe of Vyse — provides a reliable hex to lock Lycan and his wolves, preventing Shapeshift and Howl activation.

Aghanim’s Scepter (for heroes like Leshrac) — upgrades spells to larger AoE, allowing you to clear wolf packs instantly.

Ghost Scepter — makes you ethereal, negating the physical damage from wolves and Lycan’s critical strikes during Shapeshift.

Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — cyclone can temporarily remove Lycan from fights, buying time for your team to kill his wolves.
