magnus.name: Magnus
magnus.guideHtml:
Magnus remains a high‑impact initiator and damage‑dealer in the current meta, sitting at a 48.5% win rate across 398,310 recent ranked matches (OpenDota, July 2026). His blend of crowd‑control, knock‑back resistance, and Empower‑boosted cleave makes him a frequent pick in both solo‑mid and off‑lane, though he still struggles against late‑game hyper‑carries.

How to Play Magnus

Laning Phase

  • Use Shockwave early to harass and pull enemy heroes into your creep wave, setting up easy last‑hits and denying experience.
  • Pair Skewer with a timed Shockwave to drag a ranged opponent into your tower range for a quick kill or forced retreat.
  • Prioritize Empower on yourself when you have a reliable source of attack speed (e.g., early Phase Boots or Power Treads) to maximize cleave damage against stacked neutral camps.
  • Against lane matchups like Juggernaut or Terrorblade (where Magnus win rates dip to ~36‑38%), play conservatively: focus on farm, use Shockwave only when you can guarantee a kill or safe disengage.
  • Keep an eye on Solid Core passive; if the enemy has strong knock‑back (e.g., Batrider), position behind minions to mitigate displacement.

Mid Game

  • Power Spike: Level 6 + Empower (30 % larger bonus) + Skewer at level 4 gives you a devastating combo; look for 3‑v‑2 fights around Roshan or mid‑lane.
  • Roam with Horn Toss followed by Skewer into the enemy backline; the stun and drag combo isolates high‑value targets for your team.
  • Secure vision around enemy jungle and Roshan; Magnus excels at turning pick‑offs into team fights thanks to his area control.
  • When facing hard‑carries like Terrorblade, force early fights before they can acquire Butterfly or Abyssal Blade—your Empower cleave can still outdamage them at 20‑30 % health.

Late Game

  • Win condition: use Horn Toss + Skewer to lock down the enemy core, then Empower your carry for massive burst; aim to take objectives immediately after a successful pick.
  • Position near the front of your team but keep a safe distance from enemy disables; Solid Core gives you extra resilience against knock‑back from Batrider or Pugna.
  • Avoid over‑extending into enemy vision without backup; a missed Horn Toss can leave you vulnerable to counter‑initiations and swing the game.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango & Healing Salve — sustain in lane.
  • Iron Branch x2 — cheap stats and can be later upgraded to Magic Wand.
  • Stout Shield — mitigates harass from ranged opponents like Juggernaut.
  • Faerie Fire — burst health for early survivability.

Core Items

  • Power Treads — attack speed for Empower cleave and flexible stats.
  • Echo Sabre — adds burst damage and mana regen, synergizes with Empower.
  • Black King Bar — essential against heavy magical disables (Rubick, Invoker).
  • Blink Dagger — provides the positioning needed for Horn Toss‑Skewer combos.
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Empower to affect allies globally and adds extra damage.

Situational Items

  • Satanic — survivability in prolonged fights, especially versus Terrorblade.
  • Shiva’s Guard — armor and aura against right‑click heroes like Sven and Juggernaut.
  • Heaven’s Halberd — counter‑disables against melee cores such as Beastmaster.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target spells, useful against Rubick and Invoker.
  • Assault Cuirass — armor and attack speed for team fights when facing physical carries.
  • Linken’s Sphere — block single‑target disables from Batrider or Pugna.

Common Mistakes

  • Wasting Horn Toss on low‑value targets; aim for enemy cores or heroes with crucial ultimates.
  • Neglecting Empower on yourself or a high‑damage ally, missing out on the 30 % larger cleave bonus.
  • Over‑extending without Blink—Magnus lacks innate escape, so always keep a gap‑closer ready.
  • Ignoring Solid Core: positioning too close to enemy knock‑back abilities can nullify its passive benefit.

FAQ

Is Magnus good in the current patch?

Yes. Magnus holds a solid 48.5% win rate in the current meta, making him a reliable initiator and damage source despite a few tough matchups.

What lane does Magnus play?

Magnus is most commonly played in solo mid or off‑lane, where he can farm early Empower cleave and transition into a team‑fight initiator.

Who counters Magnus?

Hard‑carries with strong late‑game scaling such as Terrorblade (36 % win rate vs. Magnus) and Juggernaut, as well as spell‑heavy heroes like Rubick and Invoker, can out‑scale or disable Magnus if he is not protected by BKB or proper positioning.
magnus.counterHtml:
Magnus thrives on his ability to initiate with Skewer and Horn Toss, then amplify his team's damage through Empower. The key to shutting him down is denying his combo—surviving the pull, avoiding the stun, and nullifying the damage boost he grants allies.

Why These Heroes Beat Magnus

Terrorblade

Terrorblade’s Reflection and Metamorphosis give him high sustain and damage output that outpaces Magnus’s short‑duration burst, while his Sunder can reverse any advantage Magnus gains from a successful combo.
Tip: Keep Terrorblade’s Reflection active when Magnus dives; the reflected damage punishes Magnus’s Skewer and Horn Toss.

Juggernaut

Juggernaut’s Blade Fury provides magic immunity, nullifying the damage from Magnus’s Shockwave and Skewer, and his Omnislash can quickly eliminate Magnus after the stun wears off.
Tip: Time Blade Fury to overlap Magnus’s Horn Toss stun window to completely dodge the follow‑up damage.

Batrider

Batrider’s Flamebreak pushes Magnus away, breaking the Skewer pull and resetting the engagement, while Firefly lets Batrider kite and avoid the stun.
Tip: Use Flamebreak the moment Magnus initiates; the knock‑back forces him to lose momentum and leaves his Empower ineffective.

Rubick

Rubick can Spell‑Steal Empower or any of Magnus’s disables, turning Magnus’s own tools against his team, and his Telekinesis can interrupt Skewer mid‑charge.
Tip: Prioritize stealing Empower early; without the damage boost, Magnus’s presence is far less threatening.

Invoker

Invoker’s Cold Snap and Sun Strike punish Magnus’s close‑range initiations, while EMP drains the mana needed for multiple Empower casts.
Tip: Chain Cold Snap on Magnus after a Horn Toss stun; the rapid stuns cripple his ability to follow up with Skewer.

Drafting Against Magnus

  • Ban or pick heroes with strong magic immunity or displacement (e.g., Juggernaut, Batrider).
  • Prioritize heroes that can silence or purge buffs, limiting Empower’s effectiveness.
  • Include at least one hero with reliable crowd‑control that can interrupt Skewer or Horn Toss.
  • Favor split‑push or high‑mobility lineups that force Magnus to chase rather than initiate.

Laning Against Magnus

  • Trade early when Magnus’s Shockwave is on cooldown; his damage spikes are limited without it.
  • Harass him when his Empower is on the ally’s cooldown, reducing his lane pressure.
  • Punish missed Skewer attempts with a quick counter‑spell or auto‑attack, as he is vulnerable during the charge.
  • Keep lane equilibrium low; a pushed wave invites a Magnus dive that can be turned into a kill.

Itemizing Against Magnus

Black King Bar — grants magic immunity, nullifying Shockwave, Skewer, and Empower‑boosted damage.
Eul’s Scepter — cyclone can dodge Horn Toss and give time to reposition or cast disables.
Lotus Orb – reflects targeted disables back to Magnus, breaking his combo chain.
Manta Style – creates illusion copies that split the damage from Empower and can dispel slows from Solid Core.

marci.name: Marci
marci.guideHtml:
Marci is a versatile initiator who blends strong displacement, burst damage, and survivability through her lifesteal passive. In patch 7.41 she sits near the middle of the meta with a 49.3 % win rate over 139,236 ranked games, making her a solid pick for both support and off‑lane roles.

How to Play Marci

Laning Phase

  • Use Dispose on the enemy hero to pull them behind you, dealing damage and applying a slow that eases last‑hit safety and forces the opponent to reposition.
  • Pair Dispose with a short Rebound combo to stun the enemy after the throw; this trades well against melee supports and denies early aggression.
  • When paired with a ranged carry, cast Dispose on your ally to grant them 75 % of your lifesteal and attack‑damage bonus, turning them into a mini‑tank for lane harassment.
  • Prioritize farming the creep wave while keeping an eye on enemy support rotations; Marci’s Bodyguard lifesteal makes her unusually durable for a support.
  • Against the toughest matchups (e.g., Phoenix, Dazzle, Puck) play conservatively, avoid extended trades, and look for pick‑offs with Rebound after they waste their disables.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 6: Unleash gives you Fury charges for rapid strikes; combine it with Dispose to lock down key targets before unleashing a full combo.
  • Roam with Rebound to create surprise initiations; the bounce off an ally lets you land behind enemy lines and stun multiple foes with the final lunge.
  • Secure objectives after winning a team fight: Marci’s barrier from Bodyguard protects allies while you push towers or take Roshan.
  • In matchups where you are behind (e.g., against Rubick or Razor), focus on split‑pushing and using Dispose defensively to peel for your carry.

Late Game

  • Win condition: use Dispose + Rebound to isolate the enemy core, then unleash a full Unleash combo while your team follows up with burst damage.
  • Position near your frontline; your shared damage barrier and lifesteal let you absorb damage while creating space for back‑line heroes.
  • Avoid over‑extending without an ally to Rebound from—being caught alone removes your primary initiation tool and can cost the game.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane, especially against high‑harass heroes.
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery for early trades.
  • Enchanted Mango — mana for early Dispose and Rebound usage.
  • Observer Ward — vision to protect against ganks from heroes like Puck and Rubick.

Core Items

  • Phase Boots — adds mobility for better Rebound angles and chase potential.
  • Blink Dagger — instant initiation; combo with Dispose → Rebound → Unleash for maximum burst.
  • Aghanim’s Shard (grants Special Delivery) — instant courier summon for item swaps during fast‑paced fights.
  • Black King Bar — essential against magic‑heavy lineups (Phoenix, Dazzle, Puck) where you need to land your combo.

Situational Items

  • Lotus Orb — reflects disables from Rubick or Ancient Apparition, keeping your Dispose combo safe.
  • Heaven’s Halberd — disarms right‑click cores like Razor or Ursa when you need to neutralize them.
  • Shiva’s Guard — armor and AoE slow against right‑click heroes (Ursa, Centaur) and helps mitigate Razor’s damage.
  • Mekansm / Guardian Greaves — strengthens the shared barrier from Bodyguard and provides team healing in prolonged fights.
  • Abyssal Blade — extra lockdown when you lack reliable stuns against elusive heroes like Puck.

Common Mistakes

  • Wasting Dispose on allies without a follow‑up stun, leaving you vulnerable to counter‑engage.
  • Over‑committing Rebound without a clear escape path; you can get caught mid‑jump by heroes with strong disables.
  • Neglecting lifesteal timing: failing to attack after a successful Dispose/Rebound combo wastes the passive damage and survivability.
  • Itemizing too early for damage (e.g., rushing Daedalus) and losing the essential initiation tools that define Marci’s role.

FAQ

Is Marci good in the current patch?

Yes. Marci holds a 49.3 % win rate across 139,236 ranked matches, placing her as a reliable pick in both support and off‑lane roles on patch 7.41.

What lane does Marci play?

Marci is most commonly played as a support or off‑lane initiator. Her durability and displacement make her effective in solo safe lane or as a roaming support alongside a core.

Who counters Marci?

The toughest matchups are against Phoenix, Dazzle, Puck, Rubick, Razor, and Ancient Apparition, where Marci’s win rates dip into the low‑40 % range. Their strong disables and magic damage can interrupt her combos and out‑scale her burst.
marci.counterHtml:
Marci’s threat comes from her burst‑style engage: Dispose pulls enemies into a tight spot, Rebound follows up with a stun‑and‑damage leap, and Unleash adds rapid, slowing strikes. To shut her down you must either prevent her from landing a clean grab + stun combo or out‑scale the burst with strong disables and survivability.

Why These Heroes Beat Marci

Phoenix

Phoenix’s Supernova creates an invulnerable egg that forces Marci to waste her Dispose and Rebound on a non‑threatening target, while the surrounding Sun Ray and Fire Spirits punish her positioning. Tip: Time Supernova just as Marci initiates; the egg’s explosion also deals massive damage to her if she’s caught in the blast radius.

Dazzle

Shallow Grave denies Marci’s kill potential by making her target untargetable, and Shadow Wave heals allies who survive Marci’s burst. The Weave armor reduction makes Marci’s physical damage less effective. Tip: Keep Shallow Grave on a frontline hero who can tank Marci’s combo; the cooldown is short enough to re‑apply after each engage.

Puck

Puck’s Illusory Orb and Waning Rift provide instant AOE magic damage and silence, breaking Marci’s combo before she can Dispose. Dream Coil forces Marci to stay in place, and the Phase Shift dodge on the stun makes her Rebound miss. Tip: Initiate with Dream Coil as soon as Marci steps forward; the coil’s pull punishes her escape attempts.

Rubick

Rubick can Spell‑Steal Marci’s Dispose or Rebound, turning her own tools against her and instantly disabling her burst. Even without stealing, Telekinesis can lift Marci mid‑combo, interrupting her damage chain. Tip: Prioritize stealing Dispose early; a well‑timed Telekinesis on Marci after she lands her Rebound stun can lock her down for a kill.

Razor

Razor’s Static Link saps Marci’s attack damage, reducing the impact of Unleash and her passive lifesteal. Eye of the Storm gives Razor a shield that absorbs the burst from Dispose + Rebound. Tip: Open with Eye of the Storm before Marci engages; the shield mitigates the initial burst, letting Razor retaliate with Static Link.

Drafting Against Marci

  • Pick heroes with hard disables (stuns, silences) that can interrupt her combo early.
  • Prioritize magic burst or A‑OE damage to punish her short‑range engage.
  • Include strong sustain (healing, shield) to survive the initial burst.
  • Consider mobile heroes that can dodge Dispose or outrun Rebound.

Laning Against Marci

  • Trade when Marci’s Fury charges are low; her damage spikes drop dramatically.
  • Harass her with ranged harass or poke before she can land a Dispose on a creep.
  • Force her to use Bodyguard on a teammate by threatening that ally, then punish the cooldown.
  • Keep the lane wave near your tower to limit her ability to grab you into dangerous terrain.

Itemizing Against Marci

Ghost Scepter — blocks her physical burst from Unleash and Dispose when she tries to grab you.
Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — cyclone interrupts her Rebound stun and buys time for a counter‑engage.
Lotus Orb — reflects Dispose back onto Marci and removes debuffs from Unleash.
Pipe of Insight — magic shield mitigates the damage from her Unleash pulse and any allied magic burst you pair with.

mars.name: Mars
mars.guideHtml:
Mars is a durable initiator and frontline disabler who excels at locking down teamfights with his arena. In the current 7.41 meta his pub win‑rate sits at 46.5% over 174,782 ranked games, placing him solidly in the middle of the hero tier list. He remains a reliable pick for both carry‑style farming and hard‑initiation, but his effectiveness varies sharply against certain heroes.

How to Play Mars

Laning Phase

  • Use Spear of Mars to harass and secure last hits; the spear’s push can force enemy heroes into your creep wave or a tree for extra damage.
  • Toggle Bulwark when you anticipate enemy harass (e.g., from ranged mid heroes) to block a portion of incoming physical damage.
  • Pair God's Rebuke with a right‑click attack to maximize the true‑strike crit damage, especially against low‑HP heroes.
  • Stack Dauntless regen by staying near the enemy tier‑1 tower when outnumbered; the extra HP helps survive early aggression from heroes like Monkey King.
  • Prioritize a safe lane (off‑lane or solo mid) against hard‑pushing lanes; avoid extended trades with Treant Protector or Ancient Apparition, whose win rates vs. Mars are below 40%.

Mid Game

  • Arena of Blood is your primary teamfight tool—drop it after you have at least one teammate inside to maximize the spear‑damage zone.
  • Aim for a power spike at 22 k HP (after getting Vanguard or Crimson Guard) to survive burst from Phoenix or Shadow Demon.
  • Rotate with God's Rebuke to punish enemies that dive your arena; the knock‑back can pull them into the spear line.
  • Secure objectives (Roshan, tier‑2 towers) when you have vision and at least two allies ready to follow your arena initiation.

Late Game

  • Win condition: lock down the enemy core with Arena of Blood and follow up with Spear of Mars + God's Rebuke while your teammates focus fire.
  • Position near the front of the arena; if you get caught outside, you lose the shield block and become an easy target for high‑damage heroes like Outworld Destroyer.
  • Avoid fighting alone against heroes with strong disengage (e.g., Phoenix’s Supernova) – the arena’s walls block most spells, but you still need allies to finish the kill.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane, especially against poke from Ancient Apparition.
  • Healing Salve — quick burst heal after early trades.
  • Iron Branch ×2 — cheap stats and can be later used for a Magic Wand.
  • Stout Shield — reduces harassment damage from ranged opponents.
  • Quelling Blade — helps secure last hits when you’re forced to farm under tower.

Core Items

  • Vanguard — provides damage block and HP, synergizes with Bulwark and Dauntless.
  • Blink Dagger — essential for instant arena placement and surprise initiations.
  • Aghanim’s Shard — upgrades Spear of Mars to pierce multiple heroes, increasing arena damage.
  • Heart of Tarrasque — huge HP pool lets you survive burst from Phoenix and Shadow Demon.
  • Black King Bar — necessary against heavy magical burst (e.g., Ancient Apparition, Shadow Demon).

Situational Items

  • Crimson Guard — swap for Vanguard when facing multiple physical attackers (e.g., Chaos Knight).
  • Shiva’s Guard — adds armor and an AoE slow, useful against high‑attack‑speed carries like Weaver.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target spells; strong against Phoenix’s Sun Ray and Monkey King’s Jingu Mastery.
  • Assault Cuirass — reduces enemy armor and boosts your team's physical damage, good vs. physical cores like Drow Ranger.
  • Aeon Disk — prevents instant death from burst combos (e.g., Outworld Destroyer’s Arcane Orb + Luna’s Luna Beam).

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑committing arena without backup – dropping Arena of Blood alone lets enemies kite you and waste the ultimate.
  • Neglecting Bulwark – forgetting to toggle it against physical harass leads to unnecessary HP loss.
  • Using Spear on trees too early – the push can backfire if the enemy hero dodges into a safe spot, wasting damage.
  • Ignoring Dauntless scaling – failing to stay near allies when outnumbered forfeits the extra HP regen, making early fights harder.

FAQ

Is Mars good in the current patch?

Yes. Mars maintains a respectable 46.5% win rate on patch 7.41, making him a solid pick for both carry and initiator roles despite some tough matchups.

What lane does Mars play?

Mars is most effective in a solo lane (off‑lane or mid) where he can farm safely and use Bulwark to block harassment; he also works as a hard‑carry in the safe lane when paired with a support that can protect him early.

Who counters Mars?

The hardest counters right now are Treant Protector, Ancient Apparition, Monkey King, Phoenix, Chen, and Shadow Demon, all of which have win rates against Mars below 43% in recent games. Their crowd‑control and burst damage exploit Mars’s reliance on arena placement.
mars.counterHtml:
Mars is a front‑line initiator whose strength lies in crowd‑control and damage mitigation through Bulwark and Arena of Blood. He thrives when he can lock enemies inside his arena and force prolonged fights, so the key to beating him is to deny his initiation, break his arena early, and exploit his lack of escape tools.

Why These Heroes Beat Mars

Treant Protector

Treant’s Nature’s Grasp and Living Armor let him block Mars’s spear and shield damage while providing a safe zone that Mars can’t easily enter with his arena. A practical tip: stack trees near the lane and use Overgrowth when Mars commits, rooting him before he can activate Arena of Blood.

Ancient Apparition

Ancient’s Ice Blast applies a permanent damage‑over‑time that ignores armor, nullifying Mars’s Bulwark and the damage reduction from his arena walls. Tip: time Ice Blast right before Mars lands his God’s Rebuke so the burst damage from the spell is amplified by the chill.

Monkey King

Monkey King’s Tree Dance gives him vertical mobility that lets him bypass the arena walls and avoid being trapped, while Jingu Mastery provides burst damage that overwhelms Mars before he can build up HP with Dauntless. Tip: engage from the opposite side of the arena and use Boundless Strike to knock Mars back into his own spears.

Phoenix

Phoenix’s Supernova forces Mars to either stay inside the arena and take massive damage or retreat, breaking his formation and wasting his Arena of Blood cooldown. Tip: coordinate the Supernova with a teammate’s stun to ensure Mars can’t interrupt the channel with God’s Rebuke.

Chen

Chen’s Penitence reduces Mars’s armor, making his God’s Rebuke and spear hits far less effective, while his Hand of God can heal allies caught in the arena, negating Mars’s sustain. Tip: use Holy Persuasion to pull a neutral creep into the arena and force Mars to split his attention between multiple targets.

Drafting Against Mars

  • Prioritize heroes with long‑range disables or vertical mobility that can bypass the arena (e.g., Monkey King, Phoenix).
  • Pick armor‑shredding or magic‑damage heroes to mitigate Bulwark (e.g., Ancient Apparition, Chen).
  • Include at least one strong lane bully or push hero to pressure Mars before he can secure his arena.
  • Consider banning heroes that grant Mars extra durability or easy arena setups (e.g., heroes with strong frontline sustain).

Laning Against Mars

  • Harass early with ranged attacks; Mars’s Bulwark only blocks a portion of damage, so consistent poke chips away his HP.
  • Force him to use Spear of Mars on creeps instead of you; the spear’s cooldown is long, leaving him vulnerable after the throw.
  • Punish the window after he attempts God’s Rebuke—the animation leaves him exposed for a brief moment.
  • Keep the lane free of trees when possible; a clear lane makes it harder for Mars to find a safe spot for his arena.

Itemizing Against Mars

Manta Style — breaks Arena of Blood and provides a way to dodge the spear’s skewering effect.
Diffusal Blade — burns Mars’s mana, limiting his ability to cast God’s Rebuke and Arena of Blood repeatedly.
Silver Edge — grants True Strike, bypassing Bulwark and allowing you to land a critical hit on Mars.
Eul’s Scepter – provides a reliable disable that can interrupt Mars’s arena formation and set up a follow‑up stun.

medusa.name: Medusa
medusa.guideHtml:
Medusa is a late‑game hyper‑carry whose strength comes from massive damage output and survivability through Mana Shield and Stone Gaze. In the current 7.41 meta she sits just below the 50 % win‑rate mark (49.6 % over 133,996 ranked games), making her a solid but not dominant pick.

How to Play Medusa

Laning Phase

  • Focus on farming Mystic Snake: use the bounce mechanic to clear creep waves quickly and replenish mana for early Split Shot damage.
  • Avoid hard engages: early Mana Shield is weak, so stay behind your support and only trade when you can safely retreat.
  • Watch for Ogre Magi and Shadow Shaman: both have low Medusa win rates (35.5 % and 36.2 % respectively); their disables can lock you down before you have enough mana for a shield.
  • Use Split Shot conservatively: early levels only add a small damage percent; prioritize last‑hitting over multi‑target harassment.
  • Pull neutral camps when possible: extra farm mitigates the slow early scaling and gives you a head start on items like Power Treads.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at 20 – 25 mana: once you have a decent Mana Shield (≈ 300 mana) and a few stacks of Split Shot, you can start joining team fights.
  • Secure Roshan after you have a reliable Mana Shield and at least one defensive item (e.g., Satanic); the Aegis gives you the survivability needed against burst heroes like Shadow Demon.
  • Pick fights on the outskirts: use Stone Gaze to punish enemies who chase you; the 2‑second gaze stun is especially effective against melee heroes.
  • Farm aggressively in the jungle: Mystic Snake’s mana return lets you sustain long clear times, pushing your net worth ahead of hard‑lane carries.

Late Game

  • Win condition: sustained DPS from Split Shot + high‑mana Mana Shield; stay in the backline, let your shield absorb damage while you output continuous arrows.
  • Positioning is king: keep vision on enemy positions; if you get caught by disables from heroes like Centaur Warrunner (38 % win rate vs Medusa) you’ll quickly run out of mana.
  • Avoid over‑extending without Aegis or Black King Bar: a single stun can lock you in Stone Gaze long enough for the enemy to focus you down.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — basic sustain for early lane.
  • Healing Salve — emergency health against burst.
  • Slippers of Agility — early damage for Mystic Snake.
  • Iron Branch ×2 — cheap stats and can be later used for Magic Wand.

Core Items

  • Manta Style — splits your attacks, synergizes with Split Shot, and provides a purge against disables from Shadow Shaman and Ogre Magi.
  • Monkey King Bar — counters evasion from heroes like Terrorblade (Medusa win 39.7 %).
  • Satanic — massive lifesteal to complement Mana Shield in late fights.
  • Butterfly — adds evasion and attack speed, helping you survive against physical burst from Centaur Warrunner.

Situational Items

  • Black King Bar — essential against heavy magical control (e.g., Shadow Demon, Shadow Shaman).
  • Eye of Skadi — slows enemies, making Stone Gaze stuns land faster.
  • Abyssal Blade — provides a reliable stun when you need to lock down mobile heroes like Terrorblade.
  • Linken’s Sphere — blocks single‑target spells such as Ogre Magi’s Bloodlust or Shadow Shaman’s Hex.
  • Heart of Tarrasque — huge health pool for games where you lack enough defensive items.

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑relying on Split Shot early: the damage percent is low until later levels, causing missed last hits.
  • Neglecting Mana Shield management: running out of mana leaves you vulnerable to burst from heroes you already struggle against.
  • Chasing fights without Aegis or BKB: hard‑disable matchups (Ogre Magi, Shadow Demon) can lock you down and waste your mana.
  • Ignoring Stone Gaze positioning: turning enemies to stone requires them to look at you for 2 seconds; standing too far reduces its effectiveness.

FAQ

Is Medusa good in the current patch?

Medusa sits at a 49.6 % win rate in recent ranked matches, making her a viable but slightly below‑average pick. She shines in games where you can farm safely and reach her late‑game power spikes.

What lane does Medusa play?

Medusa is typically played in the safe lane as a carry, often paired with a support who can protect her from early disables and help secure early farm.

Who counters Medusa?

The toughest matchups are Ogre Magi (35.5 % win rate vs Medusa), Shadow Shaman (36.2 %), Shadow Demon (37.0 %), Centaur Warrunner (38.0 %), Dawnbreaker (39.7 %), and Terrorblade (39.7 %). Their disables, burst, and armor‑shredding abilities can prevent Medusa from scaling into her late‑game potential.
medusa.counterHtml:
Medusa’s threat lies in her scaling damage output and near‑immunity to burst thanks to Mana Shield and Stone Gaze. The key to shutting her down is to apply constant pressure, force her to spend mana on the shield, and capitalize on her vulnerability before she can amass the mana needed for her late‑game dominance.

Why These Heroes Beat Medusa

Ogre Magi

Ogre’s Bloodlust and Multicast turn his attacks into high‑frequency, high‑damage bursts that ignore Medusa’s low‑damage Split Shot arrows, while his Ignite applies a mana‑draining burn that hastens the depletion of Mana Shield. Tip: Keep Ogre’s Bloodlust active on a frontline hero and force Medusa to use her shield early in fights.

Shadow Shaman

Hex and Shackles provide reliable crowd control that prevents Medusa from positioning safely to fire Mystic Snake or activate Stone Gaze. The long‑duration Shackles also force her to use mana on Mana Shield while she’s immobilized. Tip: Chain Hex → Shackles as soon as Medusa steps into vision; the stun window is enough to kill her before she can react.

Shadow Demon

Disruption creates a temporary illusion of Medya, causing her Mana Shield to waste mana on a non‑existent target, while Soul Catcher amplifies incoming damage. The silence from Shadow Poison also blocks her Stone Gaze activation. Tip: Use Disruption right after Medusa lands a Mystic Snake jump to waste her mana and set up a kill.

Centaur Warrunner

Centaur’s Hoof Stomp and Double Edge deliver massive burst that bypasses Medusa’s Mana Shield because the damage is applied instantly, and his Bashed stun prevents her from kiting with Split Shot. The high health pool forces Medusa to waste mana on Mana Shield for little return. Tip: Initiate with Hoof Stomp to stun her, then follow with Double Edge while she’s still locked down.

Dawnbreaker

Solar Guard provides a shield that absorbs damage that would otherwise be fed to Mana Shield, and Starbreaker’s stun interrupts Medusa’s Mystic Snake chain. Dawnbreaker’s Radiance aura also forces Medusa to attack constantly, draining mana faster. Tip: Engage with Starbreaker when Medusa is low on mana; the stun prevents her from using Stone Gaze and forces a quick kill.

Drafting Against Medusa

  • Prioritize heroes with reliable hard‑crowd control (stuns, hexes, disables).
  • Include mana‑draining or mana‑burn abilities to cripple Mana Shield.
  • Pick high‑burst physical damage heroes that can out‑damage her shield early.
  • Avoid heavy magic damage reliance; Medusa’s Stone Gaze punishes spell‑focused lineups.

Laning Against Medusa

  • Harass her early with ranged attacks or spells to force Mana Shield usage before she has a sizable mana pool.
  • Zone her from farm; Medusa’s Split Shot is weak against a well‑positioned opponent with good lane control.
  • Punish her when she attempts to cast Mystic Snake—interrupt or silence her to deny the mana‑return.
  • Keep a creep equilibrium that forces her to over‑extend; a successful gank at level 4–5 often ends the lane.

Itemizing Against Medusa

Diffusal Blade — burns mana on each attack, rapidly depleting the pool that fuels Mana Shield.
Manta Style — dispels silences and slows, allowing you to dodge Stone Gaze while dealing extra damage.
Silencer’s Global Silence (or any global silence item) — prevents Stone Gaze activation and Mystic Snake jumps during team fights.
Crimson Guard — provides a physical damage block that mitigates the reduced‑damage arrows from Split Shot, making her less threatening in fights.

meepo.name: Meepo
meepo.guideHtml:
Meepo remains one of the most mechanically demanding carries in Dota 2, excelling at split‑pushing and chaotic team fights thanks to his clone mechanics. On patch 7.41 his overall pub win rate sits at 50.8% over 59,444 ranked games, placing him solidly in the mid‑tier of the current meta—strong enough to justify pick‑rates in solo‑queue but still vulnerable to several high‑impact heroes.

How to Play Meepo

Laning Phase

  • Earthbind early levels: use the net to lock down ranged opponents (e.g., Lich, Queen of Pain) and force them to miss farm, compensating for Meepo’s low early damage.
  • Poof timing: after a successful Earthbind, Poof a clone onto the victim for burst damage; remember the 1.5 s channel can be interrupted, so position safely.
  • Divided We Stand aggression: push the lane with two or three Meepos to deny creep experience; each clone shares items, so buying early Wraith Band or Orb of Venom benefits the whole army.
  • Dig defensive tool: when a hard‑kill gank (e.g., Tiny, Ogre Mage) appears, dig for 3 s invulnerability and health regen to survive and reset.
  • Lane matchups: prioritize safe lanes against high‑burst heroes (Lich, Tiny) by playing under tower and using Earthbind to set up your Poof combo; against easier matchups like Axe or Luna, play aggressively and stack early farm.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at 4 Meepos: once you have four clones, your net damage and Poof combos become exponential—look for 2‑v‑1 skirmishes near the mid lane.
  • Map control: split‑push with a clone while the main Meepo farms jungle camps; use Earthbind on rotating heroes (e.g., Rubick, Mars) to create pick‑offs.
  • Objective timing: after securing a Tier‑2 tower, send a clone to pull the enemy creep wave while the main Meepo teleports (Poof) to a side lane for a quick Roshan attempt.
  • Team fight entry: wait for enemy initiators (e.g., Mars) to use their ult, then drop a clone with Earthbind and instantly Poof the main Meepo into the fight for burst damage.

Late Game

  • Win condition – split‑push + pick‑offs: keep at least one clone constantly pushing a lane while the main Meepo farms high‑ground items; use Earthbind to catch rotating supports and create space for towers.
  • Positioning: never cluster all clones near a single tower; spread them to avoid AoE disables (e.g., Ember Spirit’s Sleight of Fist).
  • What loses the game: getting caught by hard‑crowd‑control heroes (Lich, Tiny, Ogre Mage) who currently give Meepo sub‑40% win rates; a single well‑timed Earthbind + Poof from them can wipe multiple clones.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango + Healing Salve — sustain for early digging and survivability.
  • Orb of Venom — adds slow to Poof combos, making Earthbind follow‑ups easier.
  • Quelling Blade — helps secure last hits with multiple clones.

Core Items

  • Power Treads — flexible stats; switch to Strength for survivability during early fights.
  • Aghanim’s Shard (if available) — reduces Poof channel time, increasing burst.
  • Mekansm — provides AoE heal for all clones, crucial against burst heroes like Tiny.
  • Heart of Tarrasque — massive health pool to survive focused disables; synergizes with Dig’s regen.

Situational Items

  • Black King Bar — against spell‑heavy lineups (Lich, Queen of Pain, Ember Spirit).
  • Sange‑Yasha — adds movement speed and status resistance, useful versus slows from Earthbind‑heavy opponents.
  • Linken’s Sphere — blocks single‑target disables from Ogre Mage or Tiny.
  • Scythe of Vyse — extra disable when you need to lock down a slippery hero (e.g., Skywrath Mage).
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades MegaMeepo, turning clones into a formidable frontline against melee heavy teams like Axe.

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑extending without Earthbind – diving into fights without a net leaves clones vulnerable to burst from Lich, Tiny, or Ogre Mage.
  • Neglecting Dig – many players forget the 3 s invulnerability window, getting killed by early ganks.
  • Clustering clones – keeping all Meepos together makes AoE spells (e.g., Ember Spirit’s Sleight) wipe the board.
  • Item sharing confusion – forgetting that items share cooldowns can lead to wasted activations; plan BKB or Mekansm usage across clones.

FAQ

Is Meepo good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 50.8% win rate across nearly 60 k ranked games, Meepo is a viable solo‑queue carry on patch 7.41. He shines against heroes like Axe (69.6% win) and Luna (68.2% win) but struggles versus burst disables such as Lich and Tiny.

What lane does Meepo play?

Meepo is typically played in the safe lane as a solo carry, allowing him to farm safely while stacking clones. In lower‑skill games he can also be flexed to the mid lane if a strong early gank is expected.

Who counters Meepo?

The toughest matchups right now are Lich, Tiny, Ogre Mage, Queen of Pain, Ember Spirit, and Nature’s Prophet, all of which keep Meepo’s win rate below 45%. Their strong disables, burst damage, and AoE spells punish Meepo’s reliance on multiple vulnerable clones.
meepo.counterHtml:
Meepo’s threat comes from his exponential damage and map control once he stacks multiple clones. The key to shutting him down is to deny him safe space to farm and to punish the moments when his clones are isolated or on long cooldowns.

Why These Heroes Beat Meepo

Lich

Lich’s Chain Frost can bounce between Meepo clones, dealing massive burst damage that scales with the number of Meepo units on the field. Pair this with Frost Blast for a reliable stun that prevents Meepo from using Poof to escape. Tip: Drop a Frost Shield on yourself or a tower to mitigate the damage from Meepo’s Poof hits.

Tiny

Tiny’s Avalanche + Toss combo can stun a Meepo clone and then toss it into the ground, instantly killing a lone Meepo while the rest are on cooldown. His Tree Grab also blocks Meepo’s Earthbind radius, limiting Meepo’s crowd‑control options. Tip: Aim Avalanche at the cluster of clones and follow up with a quick Toss before the Poof channel finishes.

Ogre Magi

Ogre’s Fireblast provides a hard stun that interrupts Meepo’s Poof channel, forcing the clone to finish the channel on a target they cannot escape from. Bloodlust grants melee allies a huge attack speed boost, allowing them to out‑trade Meepo’s low‑damage early game. Tip: Keep a Fireblast ready for the moment Meepo starts channeling Poof; a single stun often kills the primary Meepo.

Queen of Pain

Scream of Pain and Shadow Strike apply burst magic damage that bypasses Meepo’s relatively low magic resistance, and Blink lets QOP dodge Meepo’s Earthbind and chase down isolated clones. Her Sonic Wave can hit multiple Meepos simultaneously, punishing clustered formations. Tip: Use Blink to stay just outside Earthbind range, then cast Scream of Pain when Meepo attempts to Poof.

Ember Spirit

Ember’s Sleight of Fist hits all Meepos in a small area, delivering pure damage that scales with his attack speed, making it deadly against stacked clones. Flame Guard provides a magic shield that absorbs the damage from Meepo’s Poof and Ransack. Tip: Position Ember so that Sleight’s radius covers the cluster of Meepos; the instant damage often wipes out the primary Meepo before clones can react.

Drafting Against Meepo

  • Prioritize hard‑disable heroes (stuns, silences) that can interrupt Poof and Earthbind.
  • Pick heroes with burst magic damage that scales with the number of targets (e.g., AoE spells).
  • Include at least one hero with reliable gap‑close or blink to chase down isolated clones.
  • Consider bans that remove safe‑farm heroes (e.g., strong lane sustain) which Meepo relies on to stack.

Laning Against Meepo

  • Harass Meepo early with ranged attacks; his clones have low health before the first Divided We Stand.
  • Force Meepo to use Poof defensively; a well‑timed stun during the 1.5 s channel kills the primary Meepo.
  • Trade when Meepo’s Earthbind is on cooldown—he loses his primary lockdown tool.
  • Zone him away from neutral camps; without farm, his clone count stalls.

Itemizing Against Meepo

Scythe of Vyse — single‑target hex that removes the primary Meepo from the fight, preventing Poof chains.
Aghanim’s Shard (or similar burst item) — adds a stun or burst damage that can hit multiple clones at once.
Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — cyclone disables Meepo for 2.5 s, buying time for your team to focus the primary Meepo.
Ghost Scepter — makes you untargetable by Meepo’s physical Poof damage, forcing him to waste a Poof on a non‑damage target.

mirana.name: Mirana
mirana.guideHtml:
Mirana remains a versatile pick in patch 7.41, hovering at a 51.1% win rate across 327 k recent ranked games. She can swing between a hard‑carry or a roaming support thanks to her global stun, burst damage, and invisibility, making her a solid pick in both solo and duo lanes.

How to Play Mirana

Laning Phase

  • Use Sacred Arrow early to harass and secure last hits; the longer the arrow travels, the longer the stun and higher the bonus damage, perfect against low‑mobility heroes.
  • Pair Leap with a right‑click to win trades; the attack‑speed and movement‑speed boost lasts 5 seconds, allowing you to chase down melee opponents or retreat from aggressive supports.
  • Keep Celestial Quiver charges for a surprise burst on the enemy off‑lane hero; a single empowered attack adds magic damage that can tip the balance in tight 1v1s.
  • When the enemy lane has a strong wave clear (e.g., Tidehunter’s Gush), pull the wave with Starstorm to create space for your carry and force the enemy to miss farm.
  • Coordinate Moonlight Shadow with your support’s disables to set up early ganks; the global invisibility lets you flank from unexpected angles, especially effective against heroes like Sniper who rely on vision.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 6: Moonlight Shadow gives you and your team a global invisibility window—look for split‑push or pick‑off opportunities on isolated heroes.
  • Prioritize Starstorm upgrades (if you have Aghanim’s Shard) to increase AoE damage for team fights; it synergizes with your high‑ground positioning.
  • Use Sacred Arrow from high ground or jungle brushes to initiate fights; the stun scales with distance, making it a reliable tool against mobile heroes like Storm Spirit.
  • Rotate with Leap to secure objectives (Roshan, towers) after a successful pick; the movement‑speed boost helps you close gaps quickly and maintain pressure.

Late Game

  • Win condition: secure vision, then drop Moonlight Shadow on a key target before a team fight; the ensuing chaos lets your Sacred Arrow land from maximum range for a long stun.
  • Position near the edge of fights; your Starstorm provides consistent AoE damage while your Celestial Quiver gives you burst on high‑value targets.
  • Avoid being caught out of position after using Leap—the cooldown is long, and losing the attack‑speed buff can leave you vulnerable to burst heroes like Disruptor.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango + Healing Salve — sustain in lane against poke.
  • Iron Branch ×2 — cheap stats and can be later built into a Magic Wand.
  • Observer Ward — early vision to protect against ganks from heroes like Tusk.

Core Items

  • Power Treads — flexible stats; switch to agility for damage or strength for survivability.
  • Maelstrom — adds magical burst to your attacks, synergizing with Celestial Quiver.
  • Manta Style — provides a second Leap and a way to dispel silences from Disruptor or Jakiro.
  • Aghanim’s Shard — upgrades Starstorm to hit additional enemies, boosting team‑fight presence.

Situational Items

  • Blink Dagger — instant initiation; combine with Moonlight Shadow for surprise global ganks.
  • Black King Bar — essential against heavy magic damage lineups (e.g., Disruptor, Tidehunter).
  • Satanic — survivability when diving deep after a successful Sacred Arrow.
  • Scythe of Vyse — extra lockdown when your stun is on cooldown, especially against slippery heroes like Storm Spirit.
  • Eul’s Scepter — self‑save against burst and to set up a perfect Sacred Arrow after a brief delay.

Common Mistakes

  • Under‑using Sacred Arrow: low‑level players often fire it at short range, getting a 0.01 s stun; aim for maximum distance to secure a 2.6 s stun and extra damage.
  • Wasting Leap on pure movement rather than attack‑speed bursts; the buff lasts only 5 seconds, so combine it with a right‑click or a Starstorm combo.
  • Forgetting Moonlight Shadow after a successful pick; many players re‑engage without the global invisibility, giving the enemy team time to regroup.
  • Building too much damage early and neglecting vision; without wards, Tusk and Sniper can easily catch you out of position.

FAQ

Is Mirana good in the current patch?

Yes. Mirana sits at a 51.1% win rate on the latest 7.41 meta, making her a reliable pick both as a carry and a roaming support. Her global stun and invisibility give her strong pick‑off potential, especially against heroes with limited vision.

What lane does Mirana play?

Mirana is most effective in the safe lane as a semi‑carry or in the off‑lane as a roaming support. Her early Sacred Arrow and Leap allow her to harass and win trades, while Moonlight Shadow lets her transition to global ganks from any lane.

Who counters Mirana?

The toughest matchups right now are against heroes with strong gap‑closers and burst, such as Tusk (39.7% win rate), Sniper (44.0%), and Tidehunter (44.4%). These heroes can either out‑range her stun or survive her early damage, making lane control difficult.
mirana.counterHtml:
Mirana’s strength lies in her long‑range stun, burst damage from Starstorm, and global pressure with Sacred Arrow. To shut her down you need heroes that can survive or dodge her arrow, close the distance quickly, and punish her low early‑game health and reliance on positioning.

Why These Heroes Beat Mirana

Tusk

Tusk’s Ice Shards creates a wall that blocks Mirada’s Sacred Arrow and forces her to walk into a dangerous zone, while Snowball can close the gap instantly, preventing her from escaping with Leap. Tip: Use Snowball right after she lands her Arrow to catch her mid‑leap and burst her down before she can activate Moonlight Shadow.

Sniper

Sniper’s extreme attack range lets him outrange Mirana’s Leap and Starstorm, and his Assassinate forces her to stay hidden or die. The long cast time of Sacred Arrow also gives Sniper ample time to reposition with Take Aim. Tip: Keep a Blink Dagger ready to dodge the Arrow’s stun window and follow up with a quick Headshot combo.

Tidehunter

Tidehunter’s Gush applies a strong slow and armor reduction, making it hard for Mirana to escape after a successful Arrow. His Ravage punishes any clustered team fight that Mirana tries to initiate with Starstorm. Tip: Initiate with Gush as soon as she lands her Arrow, then immediately channel Ravage to wipe out her follow‑up damage.

Templar Assassin

Templar Assassin’s Refraction blocks the initial burst from Sacred Arrow and Starstorm, while her Psi Blades give her high burst damage to punish Mirana’s low health after a missed Arrow. Tip: Position near a wall and wait for Mirana to commit her Arrow; trigger Refraction just before impact to absorb the stun and then burst her with a combo.

Disruptor

Disruptor’s Glimpse pulls Mirana back after she leaps, often into her own team's fire, and Static Storm silences her while she tries to cast Starstorm. The constant threat of being pulled into a kill zone makes Mirana play overly cautiously. Tip: Save Glimpse for the moment she lands her Leap; a well‑timed pull into Static Storm can instantly end the engagement.

Drafting Against Mirana

  • Prioritize heroes with long‑range safe damage (e.g., Sniper, Gyrocopter).
  • Pick mobile initiators who can close distance quickly (Tusk, Puck).
  • Include strong disables or silences to interrupt Sacred Arrow and Starstorm.
  • Ban or avoid heroes that grant Mirana extra mobility or survivability (e.g., Blink‑enabled heroes).

Laning Against Mirana

  • Trade when her Arrow is on cooldown; her early damage spikes are limited.
  • Harass her under tower; she lacks a reliable escape tool besides Leap.
  • Punish her after a missed Arrow—she will be low on health and vulnerable to all‑in.
  • Keep warded vision to deny her the fog‑of‑war advantage for a surprise Arrow.

Itemizing Against Mirana

Blink Dagger — instantly dodge Sacred Arrow’s stun window and close the gap for a counter‑engage.
Eul’s Scepter — cyclone removes her from the fight, nullifying Starstorm and preventing her from following up with Leap.
Ghost Scepter — makes you untargetable by her physical attacks and Starstorm’s melee splash.
Force Staff — creates distance after she lands a Leap, forcing her to chase and waste mana on a second Arrow.

Mirana is most effective in the safe lane as a semi‑carry or in the off‑lane as a roaming support. Her early Sacred Arrow and Leap allow her to harass and win trades, while Moonlight Shadow lets her transition to global ganks from any lane.

The toughest matchups right now are against heroes with strong gap‑closers and burst, such as Tusk (39.7% win rate), Sniper (44.0%), and Tidehunter (44.4%). These heroes can either out‑range her stun or survive her early damage, making lane control difficult.

monkey-king.name: Monkey King
monkey-king.guideHtml:
Monkey King is a high‑mobility, burst‑damage carry who excels at diving into fights, stealing back‑line heroes, and creating chaos with his tree‑hopping toolkit. In the current 7.41 meta his overall pub win rate sits at 44.1% over 208,790 ranked matches, placing him as a situational pick that shines in the right lineups but still struggles against several hard counters.

How to Play Monkey King

Laning Phase

  • Tree Dance early to secure a safe perch on a nearby tree; use the height advantage to dodge harass and farm safely while scouting enemy movements.
  • Jingu Mastery: aim to land the fourth hit on your lane opponent as quickly as possible to unlock the 4‑charge burst; this is especially potent against melee heroes that stay in melee range.
  • Mischief: pop a quick disguise when the enemy roams or when you need to escape a gank; remember it breaks on any attack or item use, so use it primarily for repositioning or dodging skillshots.
  • Prioritize Boundless Strike on the first wave if you can land a clean line stun; the true‑strike component helps secure last hits against evasion heroes.
  • Against tough lane matchups (e.g., Zeus, Timbersaw, Slardar), play for a passive farm style—stay on the tree, avoid early aggression, and look for jungle stacks to compensate for low lane win rates (≈ 45 % vs those heroes).

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 12–13 when you have Wukong's Command plus a full Jingu Mastery charge; this is the window to start split‑pushing and forcing team fights.
  • Use Tree Dance to jump into enemy jungle or high‑ground vision points, then Primal Spring for a surprise AOE burst and slow when you commit to a fight.
  • Secure Bounty Runes and Roshan when you have at least one Mischief charge and a Wukong's Command active—your soldiers can tank the damage while you pick off key targets.
  • Target easy matchups first (e.g., Undying, Earthshaker, Bane) where your win rates exceed 65 %; they lack reliable gap‑close, letting you dictate the pace.

Late Game

  • Win condition: use Wukong's Command to create a “soldier wall” that isolates the enemy backline; follow up with Boundless Strike and a full Jingu Mastery burst to delete squishy carries.
  • Positioning: stay on a tree or near a high‑ground point until you can safely dive; falling from a destroyed tree gives a 3‑second stun, which is often fatal in late‑game team fights.
  • Losing the game: over‑committing without a Mischief escape or entering a fight without Wukong's Command active—especially against hard counters like Treant Protector (only 26.9 % win rate) and Marci (44.7 %).

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain for early tree‑hopping and lane survivability.
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery after early skirmishes.
  • Iron Branch ×2 — cheap stats and can be later built into a Magic Wand.
  • Quelling Blade — helps secure last hits while perched on a tree.

Core Items

  • Power Treads — flexible stats; switch to agility for damage or strength for survivability.
  • Echo Sabre — synergizes with Jingu Mastery’s burst; the double‑hit proc helps reach the fourth hit faster.
  • Black King Bar — essential against magic‑heavy lineups (e.g., Zeus, Skywrath Mage) where you need to stay alive during Wukong's Command.
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Wukong's Command to a larger radius and adds a damage aura, greatly enhancing late‑game team‑fight presence.

Situational Items

  • Monkey King Bar — against high‑evasion heroes such as Phantom Assassin or Slardar.
  • Sange & Yasha — provides movement speed and a chance to maim, useful when chasing mobile heroes like Weaver.
  • Butterfly — boosts survivability and damage versus right‑click heavy carries; works well when you have good vision to avoid Timbersaw bursts.
  • Linken’s Sphere – blocks single‑target disables from Marci or Crystal Maiden.
  • Heaven’s Halberd – disarms melee initiators like Treant Protector and Slardar, mitigating their lockdown.

Common Mistakes

  • Spamming Mischief for fun instead of saving it for a genuine escape or surprise engage.
  • Over‑relying on Tree Dance without checking for enemy vision; a destroyed tree gives a 3‑second stun that can turn a fight.
  • Ignoring Jingu Mastery timing—many low‑MMR players fail to land the fourth hit, missing out on the massive burst and lifesteal.
  • Pushing too early before acquiring Wukong's Command or a BKB, leading to easy pick‑offs from hard counters like Treant Protector.

FAQ

Is Monkey King good in the current patch?

Monkey King’s overall win rate is 44.1%, indicating a below‑average pick in the current meta. He performs well against heroes with weak gap‑close (e.g., Undying, Earthshaker) but struggles against hard counters such as Treant Protector (26.9% win rate) and Marci (44.7%).

What lane does Monkey King play?

Monkey King is typically played in the safe lane as a carry, though he can also be flexed to the mid lane if you need a high‑damage initiator and have a reliable early tower. His tree‑hopping makes lane control flexible, but safe‑lane farm is usually optimal for hitting his core item timings.

Who counters Monkey King?

The toughest matchups are Treant Protector, Marci, Zeus, Timbersaw, Slardar, and Crystal Maiden, all hovering around a 45% win rate against him. These heroes either lock him down, out‑damage him, or prevent him from safely using Tree Dance and Wukong’s Command. Use BKB, Linken’s Sphere, or early defensive items to mitigate their impact.

Zeus’s global Aghanim’s Shroud (Arc Lightning) and Lightning Bolt apply constant magic damage that bypasses MK’s armor and true‑strike advantage. His Static Field punishes MK’s high attack frequency, reducing his damage output. Tip: use Lightning Bolt right after MK’s Boundless Strike to force a defensive retreat and waste his stun.

Timbersaw

Timbersaw’s Whirling Death and Timber Chain shred MK’s health regardless of armor, while Reactive Armor punishes the melee attacks that trigger Jingu Mastery. Tip: engage with Whirling Death while MK is perched; the pure damage and purge remove any tree‑based safety.

Slardar

Slardar’s Slithereen Crush provides a reliable stun that stops MK’s tree jumps and Amplify Damage reduces his armor, making his physical burst far less effective. Tip: time the crush as soon as MK lands from Primal Spring to prevent him from repositioning with Tree Dance.

Drafting Against Monkey King

  • Prioritize heroes with hard disables (stuns, silences) that can interrupt Tree Dance/Primal Spring.
  • Pick magic‑damage‑heavy heroes; MK’s armor scaling is weak against pure or magical damage.
  • Include at least one tank with high base armor or damage‑reduction (e.g., Treant, Slardar) to survive his early burst.
  • Avoid picking heroes that rely heavily on right‑clicks without survivability, as Jingu Mastery will dominate them.

Laning Against Monkey King

  • Harass him before he can secure a tree; early lane pressure forces him to waste time climbing.
  • Trade when his Mischief is on cooldown; he loses the damage immunity and is vulnerable to burst.
  • Punish his attempts to use Boundless Strike by positioning just out of the line, forcing a miss.
  • Keep a ward on the jungle trees to deny safe perches and force him to fight on the ground.

Itemizing Against Monkey King

Ghost Scepter — blocks his physical burst and Jingu Mastery attacks during tree jumps.
Eul's Scepter — silences and lifts him, canceling Primal Spring channel and preventing Wukong’s Command placement.
Black King Bar — grants magic immunity, nullifying his True Strike and the damage from Wukong’s Command.
Heaven’s Halberd — disarms MK, removing his primary source of damage and Jingu Mastery stacks.

morphling.name: Morphling
morphling.guideHtml:
Morphling remains a high‑skill, late‑game carry whose burst damage and survivability hinge on precise attribute shifting. With a 47.2% win rate across 143,169 ranked games on patch 7.41, he sits slightly below the meta average but still outperforms many heroes when played well.

How to Play Morphling

Laning Phase

  • Attribute Shift (Agility Gain) early to maximize damage on the first few creep waves and secure a lane lead.
  • Use Waveform to dodge harass from tough matchups such as Axe and Doom, remembering you are invulnerable during the cast.
  • Adaptive Strike should be timed for stun + knock‑back on melee supports; the agility‑scaled damage spikes once you have at least 200 Agility.
  • Keep Ebb and Flow active to benefit from its movement‑speed boost, helping you escape ganks from heroes like Luna.
  • If you fall behind, flip to Strength Gain to survive early burst and buy time for a safe farm.

Mid Game

  • Aim for the 1200‑gold power spike (usually after getting Manta Style and Satanic) to start split‑pushing and forcing objectives.
  • Prioritize Morph on enemy cores (e.g., Sven, Windranger) to steal their ultimates for a decisive team‑fight edge.
  • Use Waveform to initiate or disengage; the invulnerability window is crucial against heroes with strong disables like Doom.
  • Secure vision around Roshan; Morphling’s burst can quickly eliminate Roshan’s melee damage while his Adaptive Strike shreds the boss.

Late Game

  • Win condition: burst down high‑value targets with a combo of Adaptive Strike → Waveform → Morph → Manta before the enemy can lock you down.
  • Position near the edge of fights; your Attribute Shift lets you toggle between tankiness and damage on the fly, essential against Treant Protector's lockdown.
  • Avoid being caught in Axe's Berserker Call or Doom's Doom; a missed Waveform or mistimed Strength Gain often leads to a game‑ending death.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane against harassment.
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery after early skirmishes.
  • Quelling Blade — easier last‑hits while you’re still low on Agility.
  • Slippers of Agility — early Agility boost for Adaptive Strike damage.

Core Items

  • Manta Style — provides burst damage, a second Waveform, and a way to dispel silences from Doom.
  • Satanic — lifesteal and survivability; crucial when you need to tank after a Strength shift.
  • Butterfly — massive Agility increase and evasion, amplifying Adaptive Strike and making you harder to lock down.
  • Eye of Skadi — adds Strength for durability and slows enemies, helpful against chase heroes like Axe.

Situational Items

  • Black King Bar — when facing heavy magical disable teams (e.g., Doom, Luna).
  • Linken's Sphere — blocks single‑target disables such as Doom's Doom or Axe's Berserker Call.
  • Aghanim's Scepter — upgrades Morph to grant an additional ultimate copy, great against heroes with game‑changing ultimates.
  • Sange & Yasha — extra movement speed and status resistance for chasing Weaver or escaping Sven.
  • Abyssal Blade — provides a reliable stun to lock down slippery heroes like Windranger.

Common Mistakes

  • Neglecting Strength shifts: low‑MMR players stay in Agility mode, getting killed by burst heroes (Doom, Axe).
  • Wasting Waveform on minions instead of using its invulnerability to dodge disables.
  • Over‑committing with Adaptive Strike without enough Agility, resulting in sub‑par damage and unnecessary cooldown loss.
  • Forgetting to Morph: many players ignore the Morph ability, missing out on stealing enemy ultimates that could swing team fights.

FAQ

Is Morphling good in the current patch?

Morphling sits at a 47.2% win rate on patch 7.41, slightly below the meta average, but his late‑game scaling and burst still make him a viable pick in coordinated play, especially against heroes he counters.

What lane does Morphling play?

Morphling is typically played in the safe lane as a core carry, allowing him to farm safely while using Attribute Shift to survive early harassment from heroes like Axe and Doom.

Who counters Morphling?

The toughest matchups are Doom (35.2% win), Luna (35.6%), Treant Protector (37.7%), Axe (37.9%), Windranger (38.0%), and Sven (38.0%). These heroes provide strong disables or burst that exploit Morphling’s early‑game fragility.
morphling.counterHtml:
Morphling’s threat comes from his insane burst potential and the ability to instantly shift between massive damage and tankiness with Attribute Shift and Morph. The key to shutting him down is denying the agility‑centric damage spikes and forcing him into a strength‑heavy, low‑mobility state where his Waveform and Adaptive Strike lose relevance.

Why These Heroes Beat Morphling

Doom

Doom’s ultimate Doom silences and disables Morphling for 5 seconds, preventing any Attribute Shift, Morph, or Adaptive Strike and leaving him vulnerable to burst damage. Tip: time the cast just after Morphling initiates Waveform or Adaptive Strike to catch him while his cooldowns are on lock‑out.

Luna

Luna’s Moon Glaives and Eclipse apply pure damage that scales with her own agility, bypassing Morphling’s high armor and magic resistance; additionally, Luna’s Lucent Beam can stun him during Waveform, cancelling the invulnerability. Tip: position Luna near a creep wave to force Morphling to use Waveform defensively, then follow up with Eclipse.

Treant Protector

Treant’s Nature’s Grasp creates a line of impassable trees that block Morphling’s Waveform escape routes, while Living Armor grants allies high armor that shrugs off Adaptive Strike’s physical component. Tip: place a tree line in the lane early; when Morphling tries to chase, the trees force him to waste Waveform and lose momentum.

Axe

Axe’s Berserker’s Call forces Morphling to attack him, triggering Counter Helix and punishing any attempt to stay in melee range; his Culling Blade also provides a reliable execute that ignores Morphling’s high health pool when his agility is low. Tip: bait Morphling into a melee fight with a low‑damage creep wave, then lock him with Call before he can shift to strength.

Windranger

Windranger’s Windrun grants near‑instant evasion and movement speed, making it extremely hard for Morphling to land Adaptive Strike or Waveform hits, while Shackleshot can stun him mid‑Waveform if timed right. Tip: keep Windrun active when you suspect Morphling is about to engage, then follow up with a well‑timed Shackleshot for a stun lock.

Drafting Against Morphling

  • Pick heroes with reliable silences or hard disables (e.g., Doom, Lion, Silencer).
  • Prioritize high‑armor or magic‑immune heroes to mitigate Adaptive Strike’s damage.
  • Include wave‑clear or split‑push heroes that can force Morphling to stay in the lane and waste Attribute Shift.
  • Consider heroes with long‑range stuns or slows that can interrupt Waveform (e.g., Windranger, Lina).

Laning Against Morphling

  • Abuse early aggression; Morphling’s damage is low before he accumulates agility.
  • Harass with creep‑pull or lane‑control abilities to force him to use Waveform defensively.
  • Trade when his Attribute Shift is on strength (low agility) – his Adaptive Strike damage drops sharply.
  • Keep vision on his Morph cooldown; a successful Morph can be punished with a stun or burst.

Itemizing Against Morphling

Black King Bar — grants magic immunity, nullifying Adaptive Strike’s stun and damage component.
Sange & Yasha — the movement speed and status resistance reduce the impact of Waveform chase and make him easier to lock down.
Ghost Scepter — makes you ethereal, causing Adaptive Strike’s physical damage to miss while still allowing you to trade with spells.
Abyssal Blade — provides a reliable stun that can interrupt Waveform and force Morphling into a vulnerable state.

muerta.name: Muerta
muerta.guideHtml:
Muerta is a late‑game carry that excels at burst damage and zone control with her soul‑stealing kit. On patch 7.41 she sits at a 46.5 % win rate over 146 k recent ranked games, making her a solid pick but one that still struggles against certain burst‑heavy or high‑mobility heroes.

How to Play Muerta

Laning Phase

  • Soul Harvest (Q) should be used to last‑hit and harass simultaneously; its stacking damage makes early lane dominance possible against melee heroes.
  • Spectral Bind (W) provides a cheap stun; aim it at enemy support or off‑lane heroes to force them to miss farm.
  • Prioritize Soul Siphon (E) on creeps when you’re low on health—its lifesteal helps you survive against aggressive lanes like Ursa (Muerta win ≈ 39.8 %).
  • Against lane opponents with strong early damage (e.g., Leshrac, Grimstroke), play conservatively and rely on Spectral Bind to set up ganks from your support.
  • Keep an eye on the enemy jungle; Muerta’s Soul Harvest can quickly clear neutral camps for early net worth if the lane is safe.

Mid Game

  • Power Spike: Level 6 Soul Requiem (R) – a massive AoE damage and silence; look for 4‑v‑4 fights where you can catch multiple heroes.
  • Roam with Spectral Bind to create pick‑offs; your stun plus silence makes you a nightmare for heroes like Techies (Muerta win ≈ 63.1 %).
  • Secure rune control and split‑push; Muerta’s damage scales well into the mid‑game, especially when you have a Battle Fury or Maelstrom.
  • Avoid prolonged fights against burst heroes like Grimstroke and Leshrac until you have at least one damage‑amplifying item.

Late Game

  • Win Condition: Use Soul Requiem to initiate team fights, then follow up with Soul Harvest on the stunned targets while your team focuses them down.
  • Position near the front line but stay just out of enemy AoE spells; a misstep into a Sand King or Primal Beast combo can quickly turn the fight (Muerta win ≈ 40 %).
  • Preserve your Soul Siphon cooldown for survivability; dying early in a late‑game fight usually means a loss for your team.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain for early lane harassment.
  • Healing Salve — emergency health against burst matchups.
  • Quelling Blade — helps secure last hits with Soul Harvest.
  • Iron Branch ×2 — cheap stats and can later be used for a Magic Wand.

Core Items

  • Battle Fury — provides farm speed and cleave that synergizes with Soul Harvest’s stacking damage.
  • Maelstrom — adds magical burst to trigger Spectral Bind + Soul Requiem combos.
  • Black King Bar — essential against heavy magical burst from Grimstroke, Leshrac, and Sand King.
  • Satanic — lifesteal to offset the high damage you’ll take from heroes like Ursa and Huskar.

Situational Items

  • Manta Style — breaks silences and dispels Soul Siphon‑based disables; great vs. Huskar’s Lifesteal.
  • Butterfly — evasion against right‑click heavy heroes such as Ursa and Primal Beast.
  • Linken’s Sphere — blocks single‑target disables from Grimstroke and Leshrac.
  • Abyssal Blade — lockdown for heroes that can otherwise dodge your stun (e.g., Tusk).
  • Heart of Tarrasque — raw survivability when you’re the primary front‑line damage dealer.

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑extending without Soul Siphon cooldown – leads to easy deaths against burst matchups.
  • Using Spectral Bind on creeps – wastes a cheap stun that should target enemy heroes.
  • Delaying Soul Requiem until after a fight starts – you lose the opportunity to silence multiple opponents early.
  • Neglecting BKB against high‑magic‑damage lineups (Grimstroke, Leshrac), causing early deaths and low win rates.

FAQ

Is Muerta good in the current patch?

Yes. Muerta sits at a 46.5 % win rate on 146 k recent ranked matches, making her a viable carry. She shines against heroes like Techies and Lich (win ≈ 60 %) but struggles against burst‑heavy heroes such as Grimstroke and Leshrac.

What lane does Muerta play?

Muerta is typically played as a safe‑lane carry (radiant bottom or dire safe lane) where she can farm with Soul Harvest and set up early ganks using Spectral Bind. She can also be flexed to the off‑lane if a strong support is present.

Who counters Muerta?

The toughest matchups are Grimstroke, Leshrac, Ursa, Sand King, Primal Beast, and Huskar, where Muerta’s win rate drops below 41 %. These heroes either out‑burst her early or can lock her down before she lands her key abilities.
muerta.counterHtml:
Muerta’s threat comes from her burst damage, lane‑dominance with Dead Shot and Soul Siphon, and the ability to quickly snowball with Dead of Night. The key to shutting her down is denying those spikes—either by silencing her cast windows, out‑lasting her sustain, or forcing her into unfavorable trades before she can land a lethal combo.

Why These Heroes Beat Muerta

Grimstroke

Grimstroke’s Stroke of Fate can interrupt Muerta’s channel on Dead of Night, while Ink Swell provides a shield that blocks the burst from Dead Shot. Use Soul Bind to tether Muerta and punish her with Phantom’s Embrace damage when she tries to reposition.

Leshrac

Leshrac’s Lightning Storm applies constant magic damage that outpaces Muerta’s Soul Siphon healing, and his Split Earth creates a zone where Muerta cannot safely land Dead Shot. Keep the lane pushed and force her to use Dead of Night defensively, wasting its cooldown.

Ursa

Ursa’s Overpower gives him rapid attack speed to burst Muerta before she can react with Dead Shot or Dead of Night. Pair Fury Swipes with a timely Enrage to survive her initial burst and then shred her health in a single engagement.

Sand King

Burrowstrike lets Sand King close the distance instantly, catching Muerta before she can cast Dead Shot. The stun from Caustic Finale also prevents her from using Dead of Night to escape, and the armor reduction synergizes with physical damage from Epicenter.

Primal Beast

Primal Beast’s Onslaught provides a gap‑closer that forces Muerta to waste Dead of Night defensively, while Trample reduces her armor, making her vulnerable to his high burst. Use Uproar to silence her and nullify Soul Siphon healing during fights.

Drafting Against Muerta

  • Prioritize heroes with reliable silences or stuns (e.g., Grimstroke, Sand King, Lion).
  • Pick high‑burst physical damage heroes that can kill before Dead Shot lands (Ursa, Juggernaut).
  • Include magic‑damage heavy heroes to outpace her Soul Siphon sustain (Leshrac, Lina).
  • Consider early‑game lane dominators to keep her from snowballing (Pugna, Shadow Demon).

Laning Against Muerta

  • Trade when her Dead Shot is on cooldown; she is most vulnerable after a cast.
  • Harass with ranged poke to force her to use Soul Siphon defensively, draining her mana.
  • Punish her when she attempts to stack Dead of Night—the channel is a long, interruptible window.
  • Maintain lane equilibrium near your tower to limit her ability to safely execute Dead Shot.

Itemizing Against Muerta

Black King Bar — blocks her magical burst and the silence from Dead of Night.
Ghost Scepter — makes you untargetable by her physical Dead Shot attacks.
Heaven’s Halberd — disarms her, preventing the auto‑attack component of Dead Shot and Soul Siphon.
Pipe of Insight — reduces the magic damage from Soul Siphon and Dead of Night.

naga-siren.name: Naga Siren
naga-siren.guideHtml:
Naga Siren is a high‑mobility, illusion‑centric hero that can dominate teamfights and push with relentless split‑pushing. In the current 7.41 meta she sits near the middle of the pack with a 48.0% win rate over 75,016 recent ranked games, making her a viable but not dominant pick.

How to Play Naga Siren

Laning Phase

  • Use Mirror Image early to harass and secure last hits while denying enemy creep equilibrium.
  • Pair Ensnare with a short Rip Tide window to lock down aggressive mid‑lane heroes (e.g., Storm Spirit) and force them to retreat.
  • Stack the lane and pull neutral camps with Mirror Image to create extra farm for yourself and your early‑game Eelskin stacks.
  • Prioritize Eelskin upgrades when you have multiple allies or your own illusions nearby to maximize evasion against burst heroes.
  • Keep an eye on enemy blink/teleport cooldowns; if they use them, follow up with Reel In to pull them into your range for a quick kill.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 6 with Song of the Siren – start coordinated ganks or protect your split‑push lanes.
  • Build a Manta Style or Mekansm (if playing support) to increase illusion count and survivability before taking Manta.
  • Use Reel In on isolated heroes (e.g., Ember Spirit) after catching them with Ensnare; the channel can be broken if they get far enough, so position wisely.
  • Transition to map control: create illusion farms in the jungle, then Song of the Siren to force enemy rotations and open objectives.

Late Game

  • Win condition: overwhelm with a massive illusion army while your team focuses high‑value targets; Song of the Siren + Mirror Image + Rip Tide provide unstoppable damage.
  • Position near the front of fights to keep your Eelskin stacks high; losing evasion makes you vulnerable to heroes like Terrorblade.
  • Avoid being caught out of Song range—if the enemy disables you (e.g., Sand King’s Burrowstrike) before you can cast, you lose the fight.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane and while farming neutral camps.
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery after early skirmishes.
  • Quelling Blade — easier last‑hitting and jungle stacking.
  • Observer Ward — vision for safe illusion farms and early gank detection.

Core Items

  • Manta Style — adds two extra illusion slots, amplifies Rip Tide, and provides a dispel against disables.
  • Mekansm (support) / Radiance (carry) — Mekansm gives team survivability for Song engagements; Radiance boosts illusion damage output.
  • Heart of Tarrasque — massive health pool to survive focus fire while channeling Reel In.
  • Butterfly — synergizes with Eelskin for extremely high evasion against right‑click heroes.

Situational Items

  • Aghanim’s Shard — reduces Reel In channel time, making pulls faster against mobile heroes.
  • Black King Bar — necessary against heavy magic damage lineups (e.g., Puck, Shadow Fiend).
  • Scythe of Vyse — extra lockdown when Ensnare is on cooldown.
  • Satanic — lifesteal to stay alive during prolonged Song fights.
  • Linken’s Sphere — blocks single‑target disables that can interrupt Reel In or Song.

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑extending without vision – jumping into fights without a ward lets enemies like Storm Spirit or Ember Spirit pick you off.
  • Using Song of the Siren too early – casting before you have sufficient illusion count wastes its teamfight potential.
  • Neglecting Eelskin stacks – forgetting to keep allies or illusions nearby reduces evasion, making you an easy target for burst heroes.
  • Chaining Reel In without escape – pulling a hero into a fight without a follow‑up Mirror Image or Song can leave you isolated and killed.

FAQ

Is Naga Siren good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 48.0% win rate on 75k recent matches, Naga Siren is a solid pick, especially on coordinated teams that can leverage her illusion army and Song of the Siren for decisive fights.

What lane does Naga Siren play?

Naga Siren is most commonly played in the safe lane as a carry, but she can also function as a support/pusher in the off‑lane thanks to her early Mirror Image and Ensnare utility.

Who counters Naga Siren?

The toughest matchups are against mobile, burst heroes: Storm Spirit (40% win rate), Ember Spirit (43.8%), Terrorblade (44.1%), Dragon Knight (44.1%), Sand King (44.4%), and Shadow Fiend (45.1%). Their ability to dodge Song or quickly burst down your illusions makes them effective counters.
naga-siren.counterHtml:
Naga Siren is dangerous because her Song of the Siren can lock team fights and her Mirror Image provides massive split‑push pressure. The key to shutting her down is to deny her the ability to land a clean Song and to punish the window while she is channeling Reel In or when her images are still on cooldown.

Why These Heroes Beat Naga Siren

Storm Spirit

Storm’s Electric Vortex pulls Naga out of Song range, instantly breaking the stasis, while Ball Lightning lets him zip past her mirror images and re‑engage.
Tip: Use a quick Electric Vortex followed by Overload damage before she can cast Reel In.

Ember Spirit

Sleight of Hand gives Ember the burst mobility to dodge Ensnare, and his Flame Guard blocks the armor‑reduction from Rip Tide.
Tip: Initiate with Sleight of Hand into a Flame Guard‑protected auto‑attack combo right after Naga’s Song ends.

Terrorblade

Terrorblade’s Metamorphosis provides long‑range damage that forces Naga to stay in lane, while Sunder punishes her low‑health mirror images.
Tip: Keep Metamorphosis active and wait for Naga to channel Reel In; a well‑timed Sunder on a pulled target can swing the fight.

Dragon Knight

Dragon Tail applies a strong stun that interrupts Reel In, and Elder Dragon Form’s splash damage quickly melts Naga’s images.
Tip: Land Dragon Tail as soon as Naga starts channeling; the stun cancels the pull and lets you focus her real self.

Sand King

Burrowstrike provides a reliable stun that breaks Song of the Siren, and Epicenter’s AoE damage punishes the clustered mirrors Naga often creates.
Tip: Initiate with Burrowstrike into the center of the Song radius; the stun ends the stasis and lets you drop Epicenter on the grouped units.

Drafting Against Naga Siren

  • Prioritize heroes with hard disables that can break Song of the Siren (stuns, silences, pulls).
  • Pick mobile heroes that can dodge Ensnare and outrun Reel In (e.g., Storm Spirit, Ember Spirit).
  • Include strong lane‑presence heroes that can force early tower pressure, limiting Naga’s split‑push time.
  • Consider early Black King Bar or Lotus Orb users to mitigate her armor‑reduction and control.

Laning Against Naga Siren

  • Harass her before she gets a Mirror Image upgrade; she is weakest when her images are on cooldown.
  • Trade when she attempts to use Ensnare—the channel time leaves her vulnerable to a quick burst.
  • Force her to use Song of the Siren defensively; a well‑timed stun or silence will cancel it and give you lane dominance.
  • Keep vision on the jungle to prevent her from safely farming and building up illusion numbers.

Itemizing Against Naga Siren

Black King Bar — blocks the silence from Ensnare and lets you fight through her Song.
Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target disables, negating Ensnare and Reel In pulls.
Manta Style — shatters her Song of the Siren stasis and creates additional sources of damage against her images.
Aghanim’s Shard (for heroes that gain a stun) — provides an extra hard‑disable to interrupt Reel In and break Song early.
