natures-prophet.name: Nature's Prophet
natures-prophet.guideHtml:
Nature's Prophet is a global‑presence hero who excels at split‑pushing, jungle control, and late‑game scaling. In the current 7.41 meta his overall win rate sits at 42.9% across 333 k ranked games, making him a solid but not dominant pick, especially strong against heroes like Phantom Lancer and weak against heavy‑disable picks such as Nyx Assassin and Bane【OpenDota July 2026】.

How to Play Nature's Prophet

Laning Phase

  • Use Teleportation to hop to the safe lane and pull the creep wave, allowing you to farm jungle camps while maintaining lane equilibrium.
  • Drop Sprout on aggressive enemy supports (e.g., Bane, Nyx) to trap them for a quick kill or force them to waste mana on escape.
  • Cast Nature's Call on dense forest patches near the lane (radiant side) to generate early Treants that both push the lane and provide extra damage for Spirit of the Forest.
  • Keep Curse of the Oldgrowth active when enemy heroes approach; the damage scales with nearby trees, so position near the Radiant jungle edge for maximum DPS.
  • Prioritize last‑hitting and stacking the small neutral camps (e.g., Sunken, Ancient) that will later feed your Treants and give you extra gold for early items.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 6–8: Wrath of Nature becomes a reliable global damage tool; use it before major team fights to soften enemy cores.
  • Split‑push with Nature's Call + Treants while the enemy team is grouped; the barrier from Teleportation protects you from counter‑ganks.
  • Join fights only when you can land Sprout on a key target (e.g., Nyx Assassin, Bane) or when Curse of the Oldgrowth can turn a 2‑vs‑2 into a favorable 2‑vs‑1.
  • Secure vision in the enemy jungle; the damage from Curse grows with tree count, so planting temporary trees (e.g., using Nature's Call on enemy foliage) can amplify it.

Late Game

  • Win condition: force the enemy to defend multiple lanes simultaneously with constant Nature's Call pushes; the cumulative pressure often forces a 5‑v‑5 disadvantage.
  • Position near trees or your own Treants to maximize Spirit of the Forest damage; a well‑placed Teleportation barrier can let you survive focused spells.
  • Avoid clustering with your team when the enemy has strong AoE disables (Nyx, Bane, Zeus); a single Sprout or Curse can isolate you and let the enemy focus you down.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango + Healing Salve — sustain for early jungle farming.
  • Enchanted Mango — cheap mana for frequent Sprout and Teleportation casts.
  • Observer Ward — vision to protect your split‑push routes.

Core Items

  • Power Treads — provides attack speed for Treants and the flexibility of switching to intelligence for mana.
  • Mekansm — gives lane sustain and a cheap early team‑fight heal; synergizes with Sprout traps.
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Nature's Call to spawn stronger Treants and reduces cooldown, dramatically increasing push speed.
  • Black King Bar — essential against heavy magical burst from Zeus, Bane, and Nyx Assassin.

Situational Items

  • Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — extra disable and a way to dodge incoming disables when you’re the focus.
  • Shiva’s Guard — armor and an AoE slow that complements your split‑push and counters high‑damage right‑click heroes like Juggernaut.
  • Scythe of Vyse — hard‑disable for the toughest matchups (Nyx, Bane, Zeus).
  • Heart of Tarrasque — survivability when you must stay in lane to defend against aggressive pushes.
  • Octarine Core — reduces cooldowns on all abilities, especially useful for frequent Teleportation and Wrath of Nature casts in late game.

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑committing to a single lane – Prophet’s strength is global; staying too long in one lane lets the enemy farm and nullifies your split‑push.
  • Neglecting tree density – Forgetting to plant or protect trees reduces the damage of Curse of the Oldgrowth and Spirit of the Forest.
  • Using Teleportation without the barrier – Jumping into fights without the post‑teleport shield makes you an easy target for disables.
  • Relying on Treants alone – In matchups against high‑burst heroes (Nyx, Bane) you need additional disables (Sprout, Scythe) rather than just pushing with Treants.

FAQ

Is Nature's Prophet good in the current patch?

Yes. His global presence and split‑push potential keep him relevant, reflected by a 42.9% win rate across 333 k games. He shines against heroes like Phantom Lancer and struggles against heavy‑disable picks such as Nyx Assassin and Bane.

What lane does Nature's Prophet play?

Prophet is most commonly played in the safe lane (radiant or dire) where he can farm jungle camps with Nature's Call while still providing lane pressure. He can also start in the off‑lane for a more aggressive split‑push style, but safe‑lane farming is the safer path to his mid‑game power spikes.

Who counters Nature's Prophet?

Heroes with strong single‑target disables and burst damage—Nyx Assassin, Bane, Zeus, Kunkka, and Juggernaut—have the lowest win rates against him (around 42–45%). Vision denial and early aggressive ganks also limit his ability to farm and split‑push effectively.
natures-prophet.counterHtml:
Nature's Prophet is dangerous because his global presence, split‑push potential, and tree‑based damage scaling force the enemy team to constantly react to his movements. The key to shutting him down is to deny his vision, burst him before he can summon treants, and punish his reliance on trees and mana‑intensive spells.

Why These Heroes Beat Nature's Prophet

Nyx Assassin

Nyx’s Mana Burn directly drains Prophet’s mana pool, crippling his Teleport and Nature’s Call, while Spiked Carapace can reflect the burst from Wrath of Nature. Play aggressively in lane and time a Vendetta ambush after Prophet uses Teleport to force a costly death.

Bane

Bane’s Nightmare and Enfeeble lock Prophet in place, preventing him from escaping with Teleport and nullifying his tree‑damage scaling. Follow up with a high‑damage spell (e.g., Fiend’s Grip) while Prophet is trapped to secure kills.

Zeus

Zeus’s Arc Lightning and Lightning Bolt deal pure damage that ignores Prophet’s tree‑based damage reduction, and his Static Field punishes Prophet’s low health after a failed Teleport. Keep a safe distance and use Thunderbolt to burst Prophet before he can summon treants.

Kez (Kunkka)

Kunkka’s Torrent and X Marks the Spot can interrupt Prophet’s Teleport and lock him in a small area, making him vulnerable to Ghostship or Keg Smash. Force a lane duel early; a well‑timed X Marks the Spot on Prophet’s Teleport destination can turn the fight.

Juggernaut

Juggernaut’s Blade Fury provides magic immunity, negating Sprout and Wrath of Nature damage, while Omni‑Slash can finish Prophet before he can escape with Teleport. Prioritize a quick Blade Fury on sight of Prophet’s Teleport animation to deny his split‑push.

Drafting Against Nature's Prophet

  • Heroes with strong mana‑burn or mana‑drain (e.g., Nyx Assassin, Anti‑Mage) to cripple his spell usage.
  • Hard‑disable heavy heroes who can lock him down (Bane, Lion, Shadow Shaman).
  • Global or long‑range burst heroes that can punish his global presence (Zeus, Lina).
  • Pick heroes with innate magic immunity or strong spell shields (Juggernaut, Pugna) to neutralize Sprout and Wrath of Nature.

Laning Against Nature's Prophet

  • Harass early before he can stack trees; his damage is weak in the lane phase.
  • Force him to use Teleport defensively; each Teleport costs significant mana and leaves him vulnerable to ganks.
  • Use Sprout or other root abilities to trap him, then follow with burst damage.
  • Punish his attempts to farm trees with quick trades; his Spirit of the Forest scaling is negligible until later in the game.

Itemizing Against Nature's Prophet

Diffusal Blade — burns mana on hit, shortening his Teleport and Nature’s Call cooldowns.
Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — cyclone disables Prophet, preventing Teleport and giving your team a window to kill him.
Black King Bar — grants magic immunity, nullifying Sprout, Wrath of Nature, and tree‑damage amplification.
Scythe of Vyse — long‑duration hex removes Prophet’s global threat and stops him from summoning treants.

necrophos.name: Necrophos
necrophos.guideHtml:
Necrophos remains a surprisingly resilient pick in the current 7.41 meta, boasting a 52.2% win rate across over 600 k ranked games. As a durable nuker who scales into a late‑game carry, he thrives on sustained fights and health‑drain pressure, but his effectiveness swings sharply with lane matchups.

How to Play Necrophos

Laning Phase

  • Harass with Death Pulse early and often; the heal component lets you stay in lane while chip‑damaging enemy cores and denying creep experience.
  • Ghost Shroud is your primary defensive tool against aggressive supports (e.g., Crystal Maiden, Keeper of the Light); activate it when you anticipate a gank to avoid taking damage and to apply the slow aura.
  • Heartstopper Aura synergizes with lane creep; keep the wave near enemy heroes to force them to lose HP over time, especially effective against low‑HP heroes like Sven.
  • Stack Sadist by last‑hitting and pulling neutral camps; each kill grants a burst of regen that can turn a close fight in lane.
  • Avoid Beastmaster and Pangolier early—both have high win rates against you (39 % and 42.2 %). Play conservatively, use Ghost Shroud to dodge their burst, and request early ganks.

Mid Game

  • Power Spike at 16 – 20 k HP after getting Aghanim’s Shard (Death Seeker) and Aghanim’s Scepter (upgraded Reaper’s Scythe). Your Death Seeker provides a long‑range wave that can finish off fleeing heroes.
  • Group with your team and use Heartbeat Aura (from Aghanim’s Shard) to pressure objectives; the aura’s constant HP loss forces enemies to either heal or retreat.
  • Target squishy carries (e.g., Witch Doctor, Void Spirit) with Reaper’s Scythe when they are low; the execute damage scales with missing health and grants you permanent regen on a kill.
  • Control the map’s vision; place deep wards to catch invaders like Invoker, whose matchup against you is poor (42.2 % win). Use your aura to force them into unfavorable fights.

Late Game

  • Win condition: force extended team fights where Heartstopper Aura can melt enemy HP pools while you stay alive with Sadist stacks and Reaper’s Scythe executes.
  • Positioning: stay just behind the front line; Ghost Shroud can be toggled to dodge critical spells (e.g., Invoker’s Sun Strike) while still applying your aura.
  • Losing factor: being caught out of Ghost Shroud without sufficient regen leaves you vulnerable to burst heroes (Beastmaster, Grimstroke) who currently dominate your win‑rate.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango + Healing Salve — sustain for early lane harassment.
  • Enchanted Mango — instant mana for Death Pulse spamming.
  • Observer Ward — vision to avoid early ganks from Beastmaster.

Core Items

  • Aghanim’s Shard — unlocks Death Seeker, giving you a long‑range execution tool.
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Reaper’s Scythe to a true execute and adds a second stun.
  • Spirit Vessel — amplifies enemy HP loss and provides additional regen, synergizing with Heartstopper Aura.
  • Guardian Greaves — upgrades from Mekansm; the active heal and armor boost keep you alive in prolonged fights.

Situational Items

  • Black King Bar — against heavy magical burst (e.g., Invoker, Keeper of the Light).
  • Lotus Orb — reflects targeted disables like Pangolier’s Swashbuckle.
  • Pipe of Insight — mitigates magical damage from teams with multiple spellcasters.
  • Satanic — massive lifesteal to survive burst from Beastmaster’s Primal Roar.
  • Mekansm — if you lack Guardian Greaves early and need a cheap team heal.

Common Mistakes

  • Spamming Death Pulse without positioning – overextending makes you an easy target for ganks.
  • Neglecting Ghost Shroud – many low‑MMR players forget to toggle it, getting caught by burst heroes.
  • Ignoring Sadist stacks – failing to secure kills or denies reduces your sustain dramatically.
  • Chasing kills after a successful Scythe – the permanent regen only applies on the kill; over‑extending after the execute often leads to death.

FAQ

Is Necrophos good in the current patch?

Yes. Necrophos enjoys a 52.2% win rate on patch 7.41, making him one of the few heroes with a positive edge in the current ranked meta.

What lane does Necrophos play?

Necrophos is typically played solo mid to maximize farm for his late‑game scaling, though he can also be a safe off‑lane carry when paired with a strong support.

Who counters Necrophos?

The toughest matchups are Beastmaster, Pangolier, Invoker, Keeper of the Light, Crystal Maiden, and Grimstroke, all hovering around a 42 % win rate against him. Their burst, disables, and lane pressure force Necrophos to play very conservatively.
necrophos.counterHtml:
Necrophos thrives on his sustain and scaling damage‑over‑time; shutting him down means denying his healing, forcing him to waste Ghost Shroud, and bursting him before his Sadist stacks become lethal.

Why These Heroes Beat Necrophos

Beastmaster

Beastmaster’s Inner Beast and Primal Roar provide constant pressure and a reliable stun that interrupts Necrophos’s Death Pulse and Reaper’s Scythe channel. His summons also force Necrophos to split his Heartstopper Aura between multiple targets, reducing its overall damage. Tip: Use Wild Axes to harass early and force Necrophos to use Ghost Shroud defensively, then follow up with a stun.

Pangolier

Swashbuckle’s burst damage and Rolling Thunder’s armor‑reduction make Necrophos’s low armor a liability, while the movement speed boost lets Pangolier dodge Ghost Shroud and stay out of the aura range. The ultimate also silences, preventing Necrophos from casting Reaper’s Scythe at the crucial moment. Tip: Initiate with Swashbuckle once Necrophos steps into Ghost Shroud, then immediately roll in with Rolling Thunder.

Invoker

Cold Snap and Sun Strike ignore Necrophos’s Ghost Shroud immunity and continuously chip his health, while EMP drains the mana Necrophos needs for Reaper’s Scythe and Sadist regen. Invoker’s high burst can kill Necrophos before his Sadist stacks become meaningful. Tip: Pair Cold Snap with EMP on a low‑mana Necrophos to lock him down and force a Ghost Shroud waste.

Keeper of the Light

Blinding Light and Mana Leak strip Necrophos of vision and mana, preventing him from sustaining with Death Pulse and from casting Reaper’s Scythe. Illuminate adds pure damage that bypasses the Heartstopper Aura heal. Tip: Keep Mana Leak active on Necrophos during lane; when his mana dips, follow with Blinding Light to force a Ghost Shroud and punish the cooldown.

Crystal Maiden

Crystal Nova and Frostbite provide reliable crowd control that can interrupt Necrophos’s Death Pulse and Reaper’s Scythe. Her Arcane Aura drains Necrophos’s mana pool, limiting his ability to spam Death Pulse and Sadist regen. Tip: Use Frostbite on Necrophos when he steps into lane to force a Ghost Shroud and then burst him with Crystal Nova while his mana is low.

Drafting Against Necrophos

  • Prioritize heroes with strong burst magic damage or armor‑reduction (e.g., Invoker, Pangolier).
  • Pick heroes that can silence or lock down Necrophos, preventing Reaper’s Scythe and Ghost Shroud usage.
  • Include at least one mana‑draining or mana‑burn hero to cripple his sustain.
  • Consider early‑game aggression heroes who can force Necrophos to use Ghost Shroud before he farms core items.

Laning Against Necrophos

  • Harass aggressively before his Sadist stacks; trade when his health is above 50% to avoid the aura’s kill potential.
  • Force him to use Ghost Shroud by pulling him into ranged harass or tower range; his damage output drops during the shroud.
  • Prioritize last‑hitting his creeps while denying him the heal from Death Pulse; use spells that damage both heroes and creeps.
  • Punish his lack of mobility after a Reaper’s Scythe cast—he is vulnerable to ganks while the stun is on cooldown.

Itemizing Against Necrophos

Nullifier — blocks his Heartstopper Aura and Sadist healing, making his sustain ineffective.
Eul's Scepter of Divinity — provides a self‑disable to dodge Reaper’s Scythe and a way to purge his Ghost Shroud slow.
Scythe of Vyse — hard‑locks Necrophos, preventing him from casting Death Pulse or Sadist while you burst him down.
Glimmer Cape — grants temporary magic immunity, negating his Death Pulse and Reaper’s Scythe damage during critical fights.

nyx-assassin.name: Nyx Assassin
nyx-assassin.guideHtml:
Nyx Assassin is a burst‑damage initiator who excels at mana‑burning squishy heroes and providing early‑game control. In the current 7.41 meta he sits at a solid 51.9% win rate over 250 k recent ranked games, making him a reliable pick despite a few tough match‑ups【OpenDota July 2026】.

How to Play Nyx Assassin

Laning Phase

  • Use Impale to harass and secure last‑hits against low‑mana lane opponents; the stun also deters aggressive supports.
  • Spam Mana Burn on enemy heroes with high mana pools (e.g., Storm Spirit, Outworld Devourer) to force early mana deficits.
  • Keep Spiked Carapace on cooldown for damage reflection against melee harassers and to punish enemy right‑clicks.
  • When the lane is safe, Burrow to extend Impale/​Mind Flare range and surprise gankers; the increased stun radius is especially useful against roaming supports.
  • Prioritize a supportive lane (off‑lane) where you can abuse your disables on enemy off‑laners and set up early kills for your carry.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 6 with Vendetta – look for isolated heroes to assassinate and create space for your team.
  • Use Burrow + Impale to initiate team fights from unexpected angles; the extended range lets you stun multiple targets before the front line engages.
  • Deploy Spiked Carapage pre‑emptively when you anticipate enemy spells or right‑clicks; the stun on damage sources can turn a duel in your favor.
  • Secure Mana‑burned kills on high‑mana heroes (e.g., Terrorblade, Phoenix) to keep them out of fights; coordinate with your team to focus them once their mana is depleted.

Late Game

  • Win condition: pick off key spellcasters with Vendetta + Impale + Mind Flare, then follow up with Spiked Carapace to survive retaliation.
  • Position near the edge of fights, using Burrow to stay hidden and jump onto back‑line targets; avoid front‑line engagements where you can be burst‑down.
  • Losing the game usually stems from getting caught out of position (e.g., by Pudge’s hook or Doom’s Doom) or failing to secure mana‑burn on the enemy core, allowing them to out‑scale you.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane.
  • Healing Salve — emergency health.
  • Observer Ward — vision for early gank setups.
  • Enchanted Mango — mana for early Mana Burn spam.
  • Iron Branch ×2 — cheap stats and can be later built into a Magic Wand.

Core Items

  • Arcane Boots — provides the mana pool needed for continuous Mana Burn and Impale usage.
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Impale to hit multiple targets in a larger area and reduces its cooldown, amplifying team‑fight impact.
  • Blink Dagger — essential for instant Vendetta initiations and surprise Burrow jumps.
  • Black King Bar — prevents disables from heroes like Pudge and Doom, allowing you to land your combo safely.

Situational Items

  • Force Staff — escape from heroes that can hook or pull you (Pudge, Rubick).
  • Eul’s Scepter — additional mana, slow, and a way to set up Impale or protect yourself from disables.
  • Scythe of Vyse — extra lockdown against mobile heroes such as Pangolier or Void Spirit.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects targeted spells (useful vs. Doom, Rubick) and provides armor.
  • Abyssal Blade — guarantees a stun on the primary target when you need to lock down a slippery core.

Common Mistakes

  • Wasting Vendetta on tanky heroes – the burst is far more effective on squishy, high‑mana targets.
  • Using Spiked Carapace too early – you lose its reflect shield for the whole fight; keep it for the moment you expect a big incoming spell or right‑click.
  • Over‑extending without Burrow – Nyx’s survivability hinges on surprise Burrow plays; staying visible makes you an easy hook or doom target.
  • Neglecting mana burn on heroes with low mana pools – focus on mana‑rich enemies; otherwise you waste damage and give the opponent free lane experience.

FAQ

Is Nyx Assassin good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 51.9% win rate across over 250 k ranked matches, Nyx remains a strong pick, especially against mana‑dependent heroes. His early‑game pressure and mid‑game burst keep him relevant in most lineups.

What lane does Nyx Assassin play?

Nyx is typically played in the off‑lane (solo or with a support) where he can harass the enemy carry, apply Mana Burn, and set up early kills with Impale and Spiked Carapace. He can also be flexed to a safe‑lane support role if the draft demands it.

Who counters Nyx Assassin?

The toughest match‑ups right now are Pudge (44.8% win), Pangolier (45.7%), Terrorblade (46.7%), Phoenix (47.1%), Rubick (48.1%), and Doom (48.3%). These heroes either have strong hooks, disables, or mana‑shielding that neutralize Nyx’s burst and mana‑burn potential.
nyx-assassin.counterHtml:
Nyx Assassin thrives on burst damage, mana‑drain, and the surprise factor of his burrowed Impale + Spiked Carapace combo. To shut him down you must deny his mana‑burn, punish his long‑range Impale and Mind Flare, and force him to stay unburrowed where his damage spikes are limited.

Why These Heroes Beat Nyx Assassin

Pudge

Pudge’s Meat Hook can pull Nyx out of his burrow before he lands an Impale, breaking the combo and exposing him to early damage. Pair Hook with Rot to sap Nyx’s mana and health while he’s stunned.
Tip: Position near the river or high‑ground cliffs where a well‑timed Hook catches Nyx mid‑burrow.

Pangolier

Swashbuckle provides a fast, low‑cooldown AoE that punishes Nyx’s low mobility and forces him to stay unburrowed; the armor reduction also weakens Nyx’s physical burst. Pangolier’s Shield Crash blocks incoming spells, mitigating Impale and Mind Flare.
Tip: Initiate with Rolling Thunder when Nyx is burrowed; the stun prevents him from using Spiked Carapace and forces a vulnerable unburrow.

Terrorblade

Terrorblade’s Metamorphosis gives him sustained right‑click damage that outscales Nyx’s burst, while Sunder can reverse a lethal Mana Burn into a health gain for Terrorblade. Terrorblade’s high armor and Reflection also reduce the impact of Impale’s stun.
Tip: Push early and force Nyx to farm under tower; his low lane presence makes it hard to secure kills.

Phoenix

Phoenix’s Supernova creates a large, invulnerable unit that forces Nyx to waste Impale and Mind Flare on a non‑target, while Sun Ray continuously burns Nyx’s mana, nullifying his Mana Burn advantage. Phoenix’s Icarus Dive grants mobility to dodge Impale.
Tip: Time Supernova when Nyx is about to burrow; the stun from the explosion interrupts his Burrow channel.

Rubick

Rubick can Spell‑Steal Nyx’s Impale or Spiked Carapace, turning Nyx’s own tools against him and denying the stun combo. Rubick’s Telekinesis also lifts Nyx out of burrowed range, breaking the Impale‑Spiked Carapace synergy.
Tip: Prioritize stealing Impale first; a stolen Impale can be cast on Nyx while he’s burrowed, guaranteeing a stun.

Drafting Against Nyx Assassin

  • Pick heroes with strong early disables (Hook, Stun, Pull) that can interrupt Burrow.
  • Favor high‑armor or magic‑immune heroes to survive Mana Burn and Mind Flare.
  • Include at least one hero with reliable long‑range vision or true‑sight to spot Nyx’s burrow.
  • Avoid stacking low‑mana, low‑damage heroes that Nyx can easily kill with Mana Burn.

Laning Against Nyx Assassin

  • Trade when Nyx is out of burrow; his damage drops dramatically without Impale + Spiked Carapace.
  • Harass his mana early; each Mana Burn reduces his ability to cast Impale and Mind Flare later.
  • Punish his Vendetta entry by warding the river and keeping a defensive creep wave; Nyx is vulnerable while invisible.
  • Use ranged harassment or creep‑pull to force him to use Burrow defensively, wasting his early game aggression.

Itemizing Against Nyx Assassin

Black King Bar — grants magic immunity, nullifying Mind Flare and Mana Burn during fights.
Ghost Scepter — makes you untargetable by Impale’s physical stun and reduces damage from Spiked Carapace.
Manta Style — creates illusion copies that split Nyx’s Mana Burn and can purge the break from Vendetta.
Lotus Orb — reflects Impale back at Nyx and removes the stun from Spiked Carapace.
Eul's Scepter — cyclones Nyx, interrupting his Burrow and giving you a safe window to reposition.

ogre-magi.name: Ogre Magi
ogre-magi.guideHtml:
Ogre Magi remains a reliable support‑style initiator in patch 7.41, boasting a 50.9% win rate across 627,917 recent ranked games. His toolkit of stun, burst damage, and the chaotic Multicast makes him a staple for teams that need cheap crowd control and utility. While his win‑rate is solid overall, he still struggles against certain late‑game cores (e.g., Pugna 39% win) and shines versus squishy carries like Medusa 64.5% win.

How to Play Ogre Magi

Laning Phase

  • Fireblast on the enemy off‑lane hero or support to secure early kills or force them to miss CS.
  • Use Ignite on a melee opponent to slow them and add damage while you or your lane partner harass.
  • Cast Bloodlust on your carry (or yourself) to boost early lane aggression and tower pressure.
  • Drop Fire Shield on yourself or the carry when expecting harass from heroes like Pugna or Magnus.
  • Prioritize stacking Multicast by buying early Strength items (e.g., Power Treads) and hitting level 6 for the talent that improves Multicast chance.

Mid Game

  • Hit level 6 and start looking for Multicast‑powered Fireblast combos on Roshan or enemy supports.
  • Roam with Bloodlust on a core into mid‑lane fights; the attack‑speed boost often decides skirmishes.
  • Use Fire Shield on towers during sieges to mitigate damage from heroes such as Phoenix or Treant Protector.
  • Prioritize vision and stack control; Ogre’s low mana cost on Unrefined Fireblast lets him spam stuns when you have map control.

Late Game

  • Position near the front line to Multicast Fireblast onto high‑value targets (e.g., Medusa, Lycan) while staying protected by allies.
  • Keep Bloodlust on the primary damage dealer; the movement speed also helps escape from dangerous pick‑offs like Mirana’s arrows.
  • Avoid over‑extending without a Fire Shield or a defensive item; being caught without backup can quickly turn a win into a loss.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane against harass.
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery after trades.
  • Observer Ward — early vision to protect against ganks.
  • Clarity — maintain mana for frequent Fireblast usage.
  • Iron Branch ×2 — cheap stat boost and later can be used for Magic Wand.

Core Items

  • Tranquil Boots — reliable movement speed and HP regen for roaming.
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Bloodlust to affect all nearby allies and grants a stronger Multicast on Fireblast.
  • Force Staff — provides escape and positioning for both you and your allies.
  • Blink Dagger (or Eul’s Scepter if you need extra disable) — essential for initiating with Fireblast.

Situational Items

  • Glimmer Cape — counter‑play against burst heroes like Pugna or Phoenix.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target spells, useful versus Mirana’s Arrow or Alchemist’s Acid Spray.
  • Guardian Greaves — strong against line‑damage cores (e.g., Bristleback, Lycan) and provides team‑wide heal.
  • Pipe of Insight — mitigates magical burst from Pugna, Magnus, or Phoenix.
  • Solar Crest — extra armor and attack‑speed buff for a carry in late‑game pushes.

Common Mistakes

  • Spam‑casting Fireblast without Multicast – early games waste mana; wait for level 6 or sufficient Strength before over‑using it.
  • Neglecting Bloodlust on towers – many players only buff heroes, missing the tower‑damage boost that can win sieges.
  • Over‑extending without Fire Shield – against heroes like Phoenix or Treant, failing to shield yourself leads to easy deaths.
  • Building pure damage items – Ogre’s strength lies in utility; items like Desolator rarely pay off.

FAQ

Is Ogre Magi good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 50.9% win rate across over 600 k ranked games, Ogre Magi is a solid pick, especially on support. He excels in early‑game control and scales well into late game with Multicast and Bloodlust.

What lane does Ogre Magi play?

Ogre Magi is typically played in the safe lane as a support, pairing with a carry to provide stun, Bloodlust, and vision. He can also be flexed to the off‑lane in lower‑skill brackets for additional durability.

Who counters Ogre Magi?

Heroes with strong magical burst and silence—such as Pugna (39% win vs. Ogre), Phoenix (40% win), and Magnus (43.4% win)—are the toughest matchups. Building defensive items like Glimmer Cape or Lotus Orb can mitigate their impact.
ogre-magi.counterHtml:
Ogre Magi’s threat comes from his insane Multicast‑driven burst and the insane attack‑speed boost of Bloodlust, which lets him turn a simple stun into a lethal combo. The key to shutting him down is denying him the mana and the early‑game space needed to land multiple casts, and forcing fights where his spells are either wasted or easily dispelled.

Why These Heroes Beat Ogre Magi

Pugna

Pugna’s Nether Blast and Decrepify both punish Ogre’s low damage output and can burst him before he lands a Fireblast. Nether Ward also punishes Ogre’s high‑mana spells, draining his mana pool with every cast. Tip: Keep Nether Ward up and time Decrepify right before Ogre’s Bloodlust to nullify his attack‑speed boost.

Phoenix

Phoenix’s Fire Spirits and Sun Ray force Ogre to waste Ignite and Fireblast on harmless spirits, draining his mana and breaking his Multicast rhythm. Tip: Position Phoenix near the lane so the Spirits block Ogre’s line of sight, then follow up with a Sun Ray when Ogre tries to cast Bloodlust.

Treant Protector

Treant’s Nature’s Grasp and Living Armor give him high survivability against Ogre’s stun‑and‑damage combo, while Overgrowth can root Ogre long enough to deny Multicast triggers. Tip: Use Overgrowth right after Ogre lands a Fireblast; the root stops him from recasting Bloodlust or Ignite.

Mirana

Mirana’s Sacred Arrow provides long‑range pick‑off potential that can kill Ogre before he can stack Multicast, and Leap lets her dodge Fireblast and Ignite. Tip: Aim Arrow at Ogre when he’s about to cast Bloodlust on a tower—killing him early removes the tower’s speed boost.

Alchemist

Alchemist’s Acid Spray and Unstable Concoction burn Ogre’s mana and health, while Chemical Rage gives massive HP regeneration that outpaces Ogre’s burst. Tip: Build a Mekansm early; the heal counters Ogre’s stun‑damage combo and forces him to waste Ignite on a tankier target.

Drafting Against Ogre Magi

  • Prioritize heroes with strong mana‑drain or spell‑interrupts (e.g., Pugna, Silencer).
  • Choose early‑game burst or lockdown heroes that can kill Ogre before Multicast scales.
  • Avoid picking multiple low‑mana, high‑mana‑cost heroes that give Ogre easy Multicast targets.
  • Ban or limit heroes that synergize heavily with Bloodlust (e.g., high‑attack‑speed carries).

Laning Against Ogre Magi

  • Harass him when his mana is low; each Fireblast/Ignite costs a sizable chunk of his pool.
  • Trade after he casts Bloodlust on a creep or tower—his damage spikes are temporary.
  • Use lane creeps or summons (e.g., Spirit Bear, Treant’s Nature’s Grasp) to soak his stuns and force him to waste Ignite.
  • Punish his early‑game weakness by pulling the wave and forcing a 1‑v‑1 where his Multicast chance is minimal.

Itemizing Against Ogre Magi

Mekansm — provides burst healing that counters his stun‑damage combo and forces him to waste Ignite.
Ghost Scepter — makes you untargetable by his Fireblast, nullifying the stun and the subsequent Multicast burst.
Eul’s Scepter — cyclones Ogre, interrupting Bloodlust and preventing him from casting multiple spells in quick succession.
Black King Bar — grants magic immunity, rendering Fireblast, Ignite, and Bloodlust ineffective during team fights.

omniknight.name: Omniknight
omniknight.guideHtml:
Omniknight is a durable support‑/nuker hybrid whose toolkit revolves around strong single‑target heals, magic resistance, and a game‑changing physical‑damage immunity. With a flat 50.0 % win rate over 106,732 recent ranked matches (OpenDota, July 2026), he sits in the middle of the meta—reliable in team fights but vulnerable to bursty, high‑mobility heroes.

How to Play Omniknight

Laning Phase

  • Purification on wave clears and punishes aggressive enemy harass; the instant heal also sustains your carry in the early game.
  • Repel on yourself or the carry before enemy spell bursts (e.g., Lina’s Light Strike) to soak magic damage and gain HP regen.
  • Use Degen Aura to slow enemy off‑lane heroes (Storm Spirit, Razor) and make them easier targets for your tower and support allies.
  • Prioritize Hammer of Purity upgrades after level 6 to extend attack range and add a pure‑damage component that synergizes with your tankiness.
  • When the lane is contested, position near your tower to maximize Guardian Angel’s physical immunity for both you and your lane partner.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 12 – you gain Guardian Angel; rotate to protect mid‑lane team fights or defend high‑ground objectives.
  • Push towers with Hammer of Purity attacks while keeping Repel active on yourself to survive enemy burst.
  • Group with your core and use Purification on clustered enemies; the damage and heal combo is especially effective against melee heroes like Beastmaster.
  • Avoid chasing heroes that counter you (Storm Spirit, Doom); instead, use Degen Aura to slow them and force engagements on your terms.

Late Game

  • Win condition: keep Guardian Angel active during sieges and team fights; the physical immunity lets your team trade blows against right‑click heavy lineups (e.g., Gyrocopter, Dragon Knight).
  • Position near the front line but stay just out of enemy spell range; your Repel mitigates magic while Guardian Angel shields allies from physical damage.
  • Lose the game if you overextend without Repel or let burst heroes (Lina, Shadow Demon) kill you before you can activate Guardian Angel.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane, especially against harass.
  • Healing Salve — quick burst heal for early trades.
  • Observer Ward — vision to protect against ganks from mobile heroes.
  • Faerie Fire — emergency health for yourself or the carry.
  • Clarity — mana for frequent Purification casts.

Core Items

  • Arcane Boots — reliable mana pool for constant Purification and Repel usage.
  • Mekansm — AoE heal and armor; synergizes with your supportive role.
  • Guardian Greaves — upgrades Mekansm, provides HP regen, and gives a strong aura for team fights.
  • Pipe of Insight — extra magic resistance against spell‑heavy lineups (Lina, Shadow Demon).

Situational Items

  • Lotus Orb — reflects targeted spells; great against Doom and Storm Spirit.
  • Eul's Scepter — self‑save and additional movement speed to chase or escape.
  • Aghanim's Shard — upgrades Purification to a larger radius, useful versus clustered heroes like Gyrocopter.
  • Heaven’s Halberd — disables right‑click carries (e.g., Dragon Knight) when you need to protect your core.
  • Scythe of Vyse — hard‑disable for high‑impact heroes such as Jakiro and Beastmaster.

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑using Purification on creeps – wastes the heal and damage; reserve it for allies or enemy heroes.
  • Neglecting Repel – failing to activate it before burst spells leaves you vulnerable to magic damage.
  • Chasing mobile counters – Storm Spirit, Doom, and Razor outrun your Degen Aura; stay near allies instead.
  • Late Guardian Angel activation – waiting until after the fight starts reduces its impact; pre‑cast before engagements.

FAQ

Is Omniknight good in the current patch?

Yes. Omniknight sits at a neutral 50.0 % win rate on the latest ranked data, making him a solid pick for teams that need a durable support with strong team‑fight presence.

What lane does Omniknight play?

Omniknight is typically played position 5 (hard support) in the safe lane, pairing with a carry and using his early Purification and Repel to keep the lane safe and sustain the core.

Who counters Omniknight?

High‑mobility, burst heroes such as Storm Spirit, Doom, and Jakiro have the lowest win rates against him (35.7 %–37.0 % in recent games). They can dodge Guardian Angel and quickly eliminate him before his defensive cooldowns come online.
omniknight.counterHtml:
Omniknight’s strength lies in his massive sustain and team‑fight durability: Purify + Guardian Angel can keep cores alive through bursts, while Repel nullifies most disables. The key to shutting him down is to deny his healing, apply constant pressure, and exploit his lack of mobility and reliance on close‑range engagements.

Why These Heroes Beat Omniknight

Storm Spirit

Storm’s high burst mobility lets him zip past Omniknight’s short‑range Hammer of Purity and land a full‑damage Electric Vortex + Overload combo before Omniknight can react with Repel. Tip: Use a quick Thunder Strike on Omniknight’s Repel‑active target to break the debuff immunity and follow with a stun from a teammate.

Jakiro

Jakiro’s dual‑area spells (Dual Breath, Ice Path) force Omniknight to stay at the edge of his Degen Aura, preventing him from getting close enough to Purify or protect allies. The constant slows also negate the effectiveness of Guardian Angel’s physical immunity. Tip: Drop an Ice Path through Omniknight’s positioning to lock him in place while your carry dishes out damage.

Doom

Doom’s ultimate completely disables Omniknight’s Repel and Guardian Angel, leaving him vulnerable to any burst damage. Doom’s Doom + Devour combo also strips away Omniknight’s healing sources. Tip: Time your Doom when Omniknight is channeling Purify on an ally to maximize the loss of his sustain.

Beastmaster

Beastmaster’s summons apply constant pressure and can tank Omniknight’s Purify damage, while his Primal Roar provides a long‑range stun that Omniknight cannot dodge. The extra vision from Hawk + Boar also forces Omniknight to stay defensive. Tip: Position your Boar near Omniknight’s lane to block his approach and force him into unfavorable trades.

Razor

Razor’s Static Link steals damage from Omniknight, directly reducing the potency of Purify’s heal‑and‑damage component. Additionally, Eye of the Storm’s armor‑shredding damage bypasses Guardian Angel’s physical immunity. Tip: Initiate with Static Link on Omniknight before he can activate Repel, then follow with a quick Eye of the Storm burst.

Drafting Against Omniknight

  • Prioritize heroes with strong burst magic damage (e.g., Storm Spirit, Lina).
  • Include disables that ignore Repel’s debuff immunity (e.g., Doom, Silencer’s Global Silence).
  • Pick mobility‑heavy carries that can outrange his Hammer of Purity.
  • Consider early‑game pressure heroes to prevent Omniknight from safely farming his core items.

Laning Against Omniknight

  • Harass him before he gets a level in Repel; his early game damage is low.
  • Abuse ranged poke to stay outside Degen Aura while forcing him to use Purify defensively.
  • Trade when his Hammer of Purity is on cooldown; his attacks then lack the pure‑damage component.
  • Force him to waste mana on Purify by baiting low‑health allies, then capitalize with a stun or burst.

Itemizing Against Omniknight

Heaven’s Halberd — disarms Omniknight, nullifying his Hammer of Purity and Purify damage.
Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — cyclone interrupts Repel and prevents Guardian Angel activation.
Diffusal Blade — mana burn shrinks his ability to cast Purify and Repel frequently.
Silencer’s Global Silence (or Aghanim’s Shard for Silencer) — disables all of Omniknight’s spells for the duration, removing his sustain.

oracle.name: Oracle
oracle.guideHtml:
Oracle is a high‑utility support whose toolkit revolves around strong dispels, damage mitigation, and delayed healing. On patch 7.41 his overall pub win rate sits at 49.1% across 159 k recent ranked games, placing him solidly in the mid‑tier of supports. He excels at protecting carries and turning fights, but struggles against heroes that can burst him before his defensive tools come online.

How to Play Oracle

Laning Phase

  • Fortune’s End on enemy supports (e.g., Windranger, Tusk) to root and dispel their buffs, buying space for your carry.
  • Use Purifying Flames on your lane partner to trade: the initial damage is offset by the strong heal‑over‑time, especially effective against lane harass.
  • Fate’s Edict on a diving enemy (e.g., Pudge) to disarm them and give your carry 100 % magic resistance, neutralizing burst.
  • Keep False Promise ready for early tower dives; the delayed damage lets you soak a burst and then burst back with amplified heals.
  • Prioritize vision and warding; Oracle’s lack of mobility makes him vulnerable to aggressive lane heroes like Queen of Pain.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 6 with False Promise + Fate’s Edict: you can now fully protect a core during team fights.
  • Roam with Rain of Destiny to contested jungle camps or objectives; the heal amplification helps allies sustain while denying enemy heals.
  • Pair with a strong initiator (e.g., Mars, Tiny) and use Fortune’s End to lock down key targets before they can react.
  • Save Fate’s Edict for enemy spell‑casters (e.g., Invoker, Puck) to blunt their burst during engagements.

Late Game

  • Win condition: Use False Promise on the primary carry during the final push; the amplified delayed heal can swing team fights and keep the core alive through enemy burst.
  • Positioning: Stay behind front‑liners; your low mobility makes you a prime target for flankers like Snapfire or Jakiro.
  • Losing the game: Over‑committing False Promise on a low‑health ally without backup often results in a death cascade, especially against heroes with strong disables (e.g., Windranger’s Shackleshot).

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane while you focus on dispelling and healing.
  • Healing Salve — quick burst heal to complement Purifying Flames.
  • Observer Ward — vision is Oracle’s biggest defensive tool.
  • Sentry Ward — counter enemy detection and protect your False Promise setups.
  • Clarity — mana for frequent ability usage.

Core Items

  • Tranquil Boots — movement speed and passive heal that synergizes with your delayed healing.
  • Glimmer Cape — extra magic resistance and invisibility to survive burst from QOP, Snapfire, etc.
  • Force Staff — provides the escape you lack and helps position allies for False Promise.
  • Mekansm — area heal and armor boost; works well with Rain of Destiny.

Situational Items

  • Ghost Scepter — against right‑click heavy heroes like Tiny or Mars.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects targeted spells and provides additional dispel.

  • Casting False Promise on a low‑HP ally without a follow‑up disable, letting the enemy kill them before the promise ends.
  • Using Fortune’s End on allies for a dispel only to waste its root on a hero that can break free (e.g., Windranger).
  • Ignoring vision; without wards Oracle cannot land his defensive spells effectively.
  • Over‑relying on Purifying Flames for damage; the ability is primarily a heal‑over‑time tool.

FAQ

Is Oracle good in the current patch?

Oracle sits at a 49.1% win rate in recent ranked matches, making him a viable but not dominant support. He shines in games where his delayed healing and strong dispels can protect a core, but he is vulnerable to burst heroes who can kill him before his defenses activate.

What lane does Oracle play?

Oracle is typically played in the safe lane as a position 5 support, pairing with a carry to provide sustain and protection. He can also roam to the off‑lane to counter aggressive supports, but his lack of mobility makes a steady safe‑lane presence optimal.

Who counters Oracle?

The toughest matchups are Windranger (37.3% win), Tusk (42.1%), Jakiro (42.9%), Queen of Pain (43.7%), Snapfire (43.8%), and Pudge (45.9%). These heroes either burst Oracle before his defensive spells can activate or have disables that outpace his limited escape tools.

outworld-destroyer.name: Outworld Destroyer
outworld-destroyer.guideHtml:
Outworld Destroyer (aka “Arc”) is a mana‑centric nuker who can also function as a late‑game carry thanks to his pure‑damage Arcane Orb and massive burst from Sanity’s Eclipse. On patch 7.41 his pub win rate sits at 49.8% over 156 k recent ranked games, placing him in the middle of the meta but vulnerable to several early‑game heroes.

How to Play Outworld Destroyer

Laning Phase

  • Use Arcane Orb on every attack to capitalize on your high mana pool; early mana from Essence Flux makes even low‑level hits surprisingly threatening.
  • Harass with Astral Imprisonment on melee opponents (e.g., Slardar, Beastmaster) to steal their mana and force them to waste regen, then follow up with a burst of Orb damage.
  • Keep your mana high; purchase a Faerie Fire or Tango and use Essence Flux procs to replenish after each spell, preventing mana starvation against lane‑dominant heroes like Leshrac.
  • When the enemy supports a lane‑push (e.g., Clockwerk’s Battery Assault), cast Astral Imprisonment on the hero to neutralize their initiation and set up a safe farm window.
  • Position near the creep wave edge to avoid being trapped by Clockwerk or Beastmaster summons; a well‑timed Astral Imprisonment can also block their pull or stun.

Mid Game

  • Hit level 12 for Objurgation; the mana shield gives you survivability against burst heroes (Sven, Lich) and lets you stay in fights longer.
  • Aim for Sanity’s Eclipse after you have a sizable mana lead (≥ 2500 mana) – the damage scales with the mana gap, making it lethal against low‑mana cores like Sven or Phantom Lancer.
  • Group with your team around Roshan; a successful Astral Imprisonment on a key enemy (e.g., Leshrac) can lock them out while you drop a high‑damage Eclipse.
  • Prioritize farming Tier 2 items (e.g., Aghanim’s Scepter, Scythe of Vyse) while maintaining vision to avoid being caught by Clockwerk or Dawnbreaker ganks.

Late Game

  • Win condition: dominate team fights with Sanity’s Eclipse + Arcane Orb on high‑mana targets; the pure damage bypasses most armor and magic resistance.
  • Position at the edge of fights; use Astral Imprisonment on the primary initiator (e.g., Beastmaster or Clockwerk) to remove their crowd‑control threat, then let your Eclipse hit the remaining heroes.
  • Avoid being caught in melee frontlines; heroes like Slardar and Dawnbreaker can close the gap and burst you before you can cast Eclipse.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane, especially against harass from Leshrac and Clockwerk.
  • Faerie Fire — cheap burst of HP for early survivability.
  • Mantle of Intelligence — early mana pool for stronger Arcane Orb damage.
  • Observer Ward — vision to prevent ganks from mobile heroes like Weaver.

Core Items

  • Aghanim’s Scepter — increases Sanity’s Eclipse damage and adds a second pulse, crucial for team‑fight dominance.
  • Scythe of Vyse — reliable single‑target disable; pairs well with Astral Imprisonment to lock down slippery heroes such as Weaver and Hoodwink.
  • Octarine Core — reduces cooldowns on all spells, letting you spam Astral Imprisonment and Eclipse more often.
  • Bloodstone — massive mana pool and regen; fuels higher Arcane Orb damage and provides a second mana shield via Essence Flux.

Situational Items

  • Black King Bar — essential against heavy magical burst from Lich, Jakiro, or Dawnbreaker.
  • Shiva’s Guard — armor and aura to survive Sven’s cleave and reduce attack speed of melee threats like Beastmaster.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects targeted disables (e.g., Clockwerk’s Power Cogs) and provides additional armor.
  • Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — extra disable and mana regen; useful when you need to peel for yourself against Leshrac’s Pulse Nova.
  • Aether Lens — extends cast range of Astral Imprisonment and Eclipse, making it safer to initiate from distance.

Common Mistakes

  • Wasting mana on early Orb attacks without securing a mana lead; this leaves you vulnerable to burst heroes.
  • Casting Astral Imprisonment on low‑mana targets (e.g., early‑game supports) – the mana steal is negligible and you lose valuable cooldown.
  • Delaying Objurgation until after the first team fight; the early mana shield can be the difference between surviving a Sven or Dawnbreaker engage.
  • Positioning too deep in fights, allowing heroes like Clockwerk or Slardar to lock you down before you can cast Eclipse.

FAQ

Is Outworld Destroyer good in the current patch?

Outworld Destroyer sits at a 49.8% win rate on patch 7.41, making him a viable but not dominant pick. He shines in games where he can build a large mana pool and land his late‑game burst, but struggles against early‑game heavy‑disruption heroes.

What lane does Outworld Destroyer play?

He is typically played in the safe lane as a mid‑to‑late‑game carry, though some players also run him solo mid to leverage his lane‑control with Astral Imprisonment.

Who counters Outworld Destroyer?

The toughest matchups are Leshrac, Clockwerk, Beastmaster, Dawnbreaker, Hoodwink, and Slardar, each winning less than 32% of their games against him. Their early‑game pressure and disables can prevent Arc from building the mana needed for his core damage.

Why These Heroes Beat Outworld Destroyer

Tip: Push the lane early and use Split Earth to interrupt OD’s channel on Sanity's Eclipse, denying the burst entirely.

Tip: Initiate with Hookshot into a tight space; the ensuing damage and mana loss will leave OD vulnerable to a follow‑up burst.

Tip: Use the summoned Boars to harass OD’s creep wave, forcing him to use mana on last‑hits instead of spells.

Dawnbreaker’s innate tankiness and Luminosity shield also absorb the pure damage from Arcane Orb. Tip: Engage with Starbreaker right after OD casts Astral Imprisonment; the stun prevents him from re‑targeting and the follow‑up hammer deals heavy damage.

Hoodwink

Hoodwink’s Acorn Shot and Bushwhack provide ranged poke that chips OD’s health while his Scurry grants the mobility needed to dodge Astral Imprisonment. The Sharpshooter ultimate can finish OD once his mana is drained. Tip: Keep a safe distance and constantly harass with Acorn Shot; the mana loss from each hit prevents OD from building a lethal Arcane Orb.

Drafting Against Outworld Destroyer

  • Prioritize heroes with high mana‑burn or mana‑drain abilities (e.g., Clockwerk, Leshrac).
  • Pick heroes with strong early physical damage that OD cannot mitigate with magic resistance (e.g., Beastmaster, Dawnbreaker).
  • Include at least one mobile or blink‑type hero to dodge Astral Imprisonment and force OD to waste spells.
  • Consider banning OD if the enemy team already has multiple mana‑reliant heroes.

Laning Against Outworld Destroyer

  • Trade early when OD’s mana is low; his Arcane Orb damage is negligible before he hits ~600 mana.
  • Harass with ranged attacks or spells that burn mana (e.g., Clockwerk’s Battery Assault) to keep his pool depleted.
  • Punish his Astral Imprisonment cooldown—if he uses it on a creep or a non‑threatening target, follow up with a burst of damage.
  • Force him to use Objurgation defensively; the barrier consumes mana and leaves him vulnerable after it expires.

Itemizing Against Outworld Destroyer

  • Diffusal Blade — burns mana on each attack, directly reducing OD’s Arcane Orb damage and preventing high‑mana spikes.
  • Nullifier — silences OD, stopping his mana‑draining Astral Imprisonment and Sanity's Eclipse from triggering.
  • Aghanim’s Shard (for heroes like Pugna) — adds a mana‑drain aura that continuously shrinks OD’s pool.
  • Spirit Vessel — provides a flat mana‑loss per hit and a heal block that counters OD’s sustain from Essence Flux.

pangolier.name: Pangolier
pangolier.guideHtml:
Pangolier is a mobile initiator and damage dealer who thrives on chaotic team fights, using Rolling Thunder to disrupt and Shield Crash to provide a temporary barrier. In the current 7.41 meta his pub win rate sits at 45.6% over 112 k recent ranked games, placing him as a solid but not dominant pick. He excels against heroes that lack mobility or burst, while struggling against high‑armor, split‑push, or heavy‑disable lineups.

How to Play Pangolier

Laning Phase

  • Use Swashbuckle to harass and secure last hits; the built‑in slow and Lucky Shot proc make it a reliable poke tool.
  • Pair Lucky Shot with early Swashbuckle trades to shred armor on melee opponents such as Juggernaut (one of his toughest matchups, 39.1% win rate).
  • Keep Roll Up ready for incoming disables; its debuff immunity and 80 % magic resistance let you survive early stuns from Bane or Nature’s Prophet.
  • Prioritize a support‑style lane (off‑lane or safe lane) where you can get a Stout Shield and Tango to survive the early aggression from heroes like Treant Protector (39.0% win rate).
  • When the enemy supports stack creep camps, use Shield Crash on the stacked wave to secure a quick creep kill and gain the barrier if you hit a hero.

Mid Game

  • Rolling Thunder + Shield Crash combo is your primary team‑fight tool; aim to hit multiple heroes with the crash to trigger the barrier and force enemy positioning.
  • Power spike at level 6 (unlock Rolling Thunder) and level 12 (upgrade Shield Crash damage). Start grouping for objectives once you have at least one core item (e.g., Phase Boots).
  • Target split‑push heroes like Naga Siren and Nature’s Prophet with Swashbuckle + Lucky Shot to reduce their armor and force them back; these are among your toughest matchups (≈40 % win rate).
  • Secure vision around Roshan; Rolling Thunder can quickly close distance to contest or steal if you have a Blink Dagger.

Late Game

  • Win condition: use Rolling Thunder to isolate a high‑value target (e.g., Lina, an easy matchup with 64.2% win rate) while your team follows up with burst.
  • Position near the front of your team; Roll Up provides safety against late‑game disables, but staying too deep can waste your barrier and leave you vulnerable to heroes like Marci (40.8% win rate).
  • Losing the game usually comes from being caught out of Rolling Thunder by crowd‑control (Bane, Treant) or failing to secure the barrier on a key enemy hero.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain against harassment.
  • Stout Shield — mitigates early damage from melee heroes.
  • Quelling Blade — helps secure last hits while you’re focused on rolling.
  • Healing Salve — emergency health for early skirmishes.

Core Items

  • Phase Boots — provides the burst speed needed to initiate with Rolling Thunder and chase down targets.
  • Blink Dagger — essential for positioning Rolling Thunder and catching split‑push heroes.
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Rolling Thunder to a larger radius and adds a stun, greatly increasing team‑fight impact.
  • Black King Bar — protects your Rolling Thunder from disables that would otherwise stop you mid‑roll.

Situational Items

  • Satanic — gives survivability against heroes like Juggernaut and Marci who can burst you down.
  • Shiva’s Guard — adds armor and an AoE slow, useful against high‑attack‑speed heroes such as Bloodseeker (57.7% win rate).
  • Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target spells, countering Bane’s Nightmare or Nature’s Prophet’s Teleport.
  • Mekansm / Pipe of Insight — team‑wide durability when facing heavy magical damage (e.g., Lina).
  • Assault Cuirass — reduces enemy armor, synergizing with Lucky Shot against armor‑heavy heroes like Treant Protector.

Common Mistakes

  • Rolling into crowd‑control without a Black King Bar or Roll Up, getting stopped and killed.
  • Using Shield Crash on low‑health creeps instead of heroes, missing the barrier proc.
  • Over‑committing with Rolling Thunder in the early game before acquiring any defensive items, leading to easy pick‑offs.
  • Ignoring Lucky Shot armor reduction on tanky heroes, reducing overall damage output.

FAQ

Is Pangolier good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 45.6% win rate across over 112 k ranked matches, Pangolier is a viable pick, especially against heroes he counters well like Lina (64.2% win rate) and Necrophos (57.8% win rate). His mobility and barrier make him a strong initiator in coordinated play.

What lane does Pangolier play?

Pangolier is most effective in the off‑lane or safe lane where he can farm safely and have space to use Swashbuckle and Roll Up against early harassment. He can also be flexed to a solo mid if the team needs an additional initiator.

Who counters Pangolier?

Heroes with strong disables and burst armor, such as Naga Siren, Treant Protector, Juggernaut, Nature’s Prophet, Bane, and Marci, have the lowest win rates against him (around 35‑41%). Building early magic resistance and timing your Roll Up are essential to survive their control.

The core of shutting him down is to deny his burst window, punish his long‑range skillshots, and force him into a position where his rolling ball can be intercepted or out‑scaled.

Naga Siren

Naga’s Song of the Siren creates a global stun that stops Pangolier’s roll mid‑flight, nullifying his primary damage source and forcing him to waste the barrier from Shield Crash. Tip: Initiate with Song as soon as you see Pangolier start Rolling Thunder; the stun also blocks his follow‑up Swashbuckle.

Treant Protector

Nature’s Guise grants Treant invisibility and a free Leech Seed on attack, allowing him to farm safely while Pangolier is forced to use Roll Up to avoid the seed’s damage over time. Treant’s Overgrowth also roots Pangolier, preventing the roll’s escape. Tip: Time Overgrowth just as Pangolier finishes his roll; the root disables his barrier and makes him vulnerable to a follow‑up.

Juggernaut

Juggernaut’s Blade Fury provides magic immunity, directly countering the magic‑heavy Rolling Thunder and Shield Crash damage. After Blade Fury, Omni‑Slash can hit Pangolier even while he’s rolling, and Healing Ward sustains the team through his burst. Tip: Activate Blade Fury the moment Pangolier begins his roll; the immunity blocks his damage and lets you close the gap for an Omni‑Slash.

Nature’s Prophet

Teleport lets Prophet appear behind or beside Pangolier, forcing a Roll Up that wastes his barrier. His Sprout roots enemies in place, instantly stopping a rolling Pangolier and exposing him to follow‑up damage. Tip: Use Sprout the moment you spot the roll; the root also prevents the roll from turning, making the hero an easy target.

Bane

Bane’s Nightmare silences and disables Pangolier, cancelling Swashbuckle and preventing the activation of Lucky Shot. Fiend’s Grip locks Pangolier in place for 5 seconds, rendering his rolling ball useless and allowing your team to focus fire. Tip: Chain Nightmare into Fiend’s Grip as soon as Pangolier attempts to roll; the combo removes his mobility and burst entirely.

Drafting Against Pangolier

  • Prioritize heroes with global stuns or hard disables (e.g., Naga Siren, Bane, Lion).
  • Pick magic‑immune or high‑magic‑resistance units to shrug off Rolling Thunder (Juggernaut, Timbersaw).
  • Include strong lane‑control heroes that can root or silence early (Treant Protector, Nature’s Prophet).
  • Avoid heroes that rely heavily on early physical damage without survivability, as Pangolier’s burst can punish them.

Laning Against Pangolier

  • Harass him before he gets a level 2 Swashbuckle; early lane pressure forces him to use Roll Up defensively.
  • Trade when his Roll Up is on cooldown; he is vulnerable to burst and cannot dodge disables.
  • Keep a safe distance from his Swashbuckle line; standing behind a creep wave or tree reduces the chance of being hit.
  • Force him to use Shield Crash on creeps rather than heroes; the barrier only triggers on hero hits.

Ghost Scepter — blocks physical damage from Swashbuckle and Rolling Thunder, forcing him to rely on his less‑impactful magical damage.

Lotus Orb — reflects targeted disables like Nightmares or Stuns back to Pangolier, negating his burst setup.

Heaven’s Halberd — disarms Pangolier, nullifying his Swashbuckle damage and preventing the activation of Lucky Shot.

phantom-assassin.name: Phantom Assassin
phantom-assassin.guideHtml:
Phantom Assassin (PA) is a high‑damage carry whose strength lies in her massive critical strikes and evasion. On patch 7.41 she sits around a 50.7 % win‑rate in ranked play (528 k games), making her a solid but not dominant pick. Her primary identity is a late‑game assassin with strong escape tools, while her early game is fragile and heavily dependent on lane control.

How to Play Phantom Assassin

Laning Phase

  • Use Stifling Dagger to harass and secure last hits; the damage scales with your attack damage, making it increasingly potent as you farm.
  • Blur gives you evasion and movement speed—activate it when enemy heroes dive or when you need to escape a gank.
  • Against hard‑aggro lanes (e.g., Pudge, Rubick) prioritize safe farming and pull the creep wave to deny experience; the win‑rates vs Pudge (37.5 %) and Rubick (36.2 %) show these matchups are risky.
  • If you have a supportive lane partner, coordinate Phantom Strike on the enemy hero to gain bonus attack speed and force a quick trade.
  • Keep an eye on enemy Disruptor or Queen of Pain casts; use Blur to dodge their skillshots and stay invisible until you can close in.

Mid Game

  • Aim for a Phantom Strike + Coup de Grace combo once you hit level 12 and have a few items; this is your first reliable crit window.
  • Power spike at 20‑item (usually Battle Fury); start split‑pushing and taking tier‑2 towers while your evasion from Blur still mitigates early fights.
  • Group with your team for pick‑offs when you have Fan of Knives ready; the break effect is useful against heroes with passive abilities (e.g., Lifestealer).
  • Avoid prolonged team fights against heroes with strong disables (Rubick, Disruptor) until you have Black King Bar or sufficient Blur stacks.

Late Game

  • Win condition: pick off high‑value targets with Coup de Grace crits while staying invisible with Blur; use Phantom Strike to jump onto squishy backs.
  • Positioning: stay just outside vision range, use Blur to stay unseen, and only engage when you have a clear line of sight or an ally to block disables.
  • You lose the game if you are caught without Blur or Black King Bar against heavy magical burst (e.g., Queen of Pain, Lion) and forced into a fight where your evasion is insufficient.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane.
  • Healing Salve — emergency health.
  • Quelling Blade — easier last‑hits.
  • Stout Shield — mitigates harassment from Pudge and Rubick.
  • Orb of Venom — early harass with extra slow.

Core Items

  • Battle Fury — provides cleave for farm and damage for mid‑game fights.
  • Sange and Yasha — attack speed, movement speed, and a modest status resistance to survive disables.
  • Black King Bar — essential against magic‑heavy lineups (Queen of Pain, Disruptor).
  • Butterfly — massive evasion and damage; synergizes with Blur for near‑invincibility.
  • Satanic — lifesteal for survivability in late‑game team fights.

Situational Items

  • Abyssal Blade — lock down slippery heroes like Lifestealer or Pudge.
  • Monkey King Bar — counters evasion‑heavy heroes (e.g., Luna, Disruptor).
  • Eye of Skadi — adds HP and slows enemies, useful versus high‑mobility heroes.
  • Manta Style — dispels silences and provides extra split‑push speed.
  • Linken’s Sphere – blocks single‑target spells from Rubick or Queen of Pain.

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑extending without Blur – diving into fights before Blur is active leads to easy deaths, especially against Rubick and Pudge.
  • Neglecting early farm – trying to chase kills before acquiring Battle Fury stalls farm and delays the critical damage spike.
  • Building too much damage early – ignoring survivability items (e.g., Black King Bar, Butterfly) makes PA vulnerable to disables and burst.
  • Using Phantom Strike on towers – the ability grants attack speed only against enemy heroes; using it on structures wastes a crucial mobility tool.

FAQ

Is Phantom Assassin good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 50.7 % win‑rate across over half a million ranked games, PA remains a viable carry. Her late‑game crit potential and evasion keep her competitive, though she still struggles against heavy‑disable heroes.

What lane does Phantom Assassin play?

Phantom Assassin is typically played in the safe lane (position 1) as a carry. She benefits from a supportive partner to mitigate early harassment from tough matchups like Pudge and Rubick.

Who counters Phantom Assassin?

The toughest opponents right now are Rubick (36.2 % win for PA), Pudge (37.5 %), Lifestealer (40.4 %), Queen of Pain (41.5 %), Luna (42.0 %), and Disruptor (42.2 %). Their disables, burst, and sustain make it difficult for PA to survive without proper evasion or magic immunity.

Phantom Assassin (PA) thrives on burst physical damage and evasion, turning every attack into a potential game‑ending crit. The key to shutting her down is denying her the freedom to pick off isolated targets and stripping away the survivability she gains from Blur and high‑damage spikes.

Why These Heroes Beat Phantom Assassin

Rubick

Rubick’s Telekinesis and Spell Steal let him lock PA in place and turn her own spells against her. A well‑timed Telekinesis followed by a Null Field (if stolen) or Frostbite from a stolen hero completely neuters her mobility and evasion. Tip: Save Rubick’s ultimate for the moment PA activates Blur; the stun from Telekinesis will break her invisibility and set up a kill.

Pudge

Pudge’s Meat Hook pulls PA out of safety, while Rot applies constant damage that ignores evasion. The combination forces her to fight on his terms, and the Dismember stun prevents her from using Phantom Strike to escape. Tip: Position near brush or high ground so a missed hook still forces PA to chase, exposing her to Rot.

Lifestealer

Lifestealer’s Rage grants him magic immunity and a massive damage block, rendering PA’s physical crits ineffective. His Infest can surprise‑kill PA from unexpected angles, and Open Wounds provides a reliable slow that counters her chase. Tip: Initiate with Infest from a neutral creep, then activate Rage before PA lands her first crit.

Queen of Pain

QoP’s Scream of Pain and Shadow Strike deal pure magic damage and apply a strong slow, bypassing PA’s evasion. Her Blink gives her the range to avoid Phantom Strike and stay out of melee range. Tip: Use Blink to stay just out of PA’s attack range, then harass with Shadow Strike to force her to retreat.

Luna

Luna’s Moon Glaives and Eclipse deliver pure damage that pierces evasion, while Lucent Beam provides a reliable stun. Her Lunar Blessing gives her a movement speed boost, allowing her to outrun PA’s chase. Tip: Initiate with Lucent Beam to lock PA, then follow with Eclipse for a burst that PA cannot dodge.

Drafting Against Phantom Assassin

  • Prioritize heroes with reliable disables (stuns, hooks, teleports).
  • Choose magic‑damage heavy lineups; PA’s evasion only mitigates physical attacks.
  • Include heroes that can grant vision or true sight (e.g., Sentry Wards, True Sight abilities).
  • Ban or avoid high‑burst crit heroes that can out‑damage PA’s early game (e.g., Juggernaut, Faceless Void).

Laning Against Phantom Assassin

  • Harass early with ranged poke; PA’s damage output is low before level 6.
  • Force her to use Stifling Dagger defensively by threatening her with aggression or tower dives.
  • Keep a Sentry Ward in lane to reveal her Blur and punish her attempts to farm safely.
  • Trade when her Blur is on cooldown (after a recent activation) to capitalize on her reduced evasion.

Itemizing Against Phantom Assassin

  • Ghost Scepter — makes PA’s physical attacks miss, nullifying her crits during fights.
  • Heaven’s Halberd — disarms PA, preventing her from delivering any damage for several seconds.
  • Silver Edge — breaks Blur on activation, removing her evasion and vision advantage.
  • Manta Style – creates illusion copies that force PA to waste Stifling Dagger and reveal her target, while also providing a purge against slow effects.

phantom-lancer.name: Phantom Lancer
phantom-lancer.guideHtml:
Phantom Lancer is a high‑mobility, illusion‑centric carry whose strength lies in overwhelming opponents with sheer numbers and evasion. On patch 7.41 his overall win rate sits at 51.7 % across 372 k recent ranked games, making him a solid, though not dominant, pick in the current meta. He thrives when he can farm safely, build illusion‑friendly items, and force fights where his doppelgangers can create chaos.

How to Play Phantom Lancer

Laning Phase

  • Spirit Lance early on to harass and pull creep aggro while spawning a low‑damage illusion that helps last‑hit and zone the enemy.
  • Use Phantom Rush to dodge early harass from heroes like Queen of Pain and Windranger; the bonus movement speed also lets you secure the last hit on contested creeps.
  • Doppelganger on a 2‑second cooldown after level 6 is your escape tool—activate it when the enemy dives or when you need to reposition for a tower dive.
  • Prioritize stacking the lane’s neutral camp with your illusion; the extra damage from Illusory Armaments guarantees the illusion deals a minimum amount for 3 seconds.
  • Against lane‑dominant heroes (e.g., Queen of Pain, Shadow Demon) play passively, focus on safe farming, and only use Spirit Lance to secure a kill when you have a clear advantage.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 12–16 when you have Diffusal Blade and Manta Style; the combined evasion and illusion damage make you hard to lock down.
  • Start split‑pushing lanes with Spirit Lance + Doppelganger to create confusion; your illusions can tank tower hits while you retreat.
  • Group with teammates for Roshan after you have at least one Manta Style and a Black King Bar (if needed) to survive burst from heroes like QOP or Rubick.
  • Look for pick‑offs on squishy supports; a well‑timed Doppelganger can dodge a stun and let your illusion swarm the target.

Late Game

  • Win condition: overwhelm teamfights with a mass of high‑damage illusions; aim to force the enemy to use their AOE spells early.
  • Positioning: stay just behind your front‑line, using Doppelganger to dodge initiations and to reposition your illusion army.
  • Losing the game: over‑extending without a Black King Bar or failing to secure vision; enemy burst heroes (QOP, Shadow Demon) can instantly delete your core illusion pool.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain for early lane harassment.
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery after Spirit Lance trades.
  • Quelling Blade — helps secure creep last hits while your illusion farms.
  • Slippers of Agility → Wraith Band — early damage and attack speed for both you and your illusions.
  • Observer Ward — vision to avoid ganks from burst heroes.

Core Items

  • Diffusal Blade — mana burn on spell‑casters like QOP and Rubick; also provides a slow to chase down fleeing heroes.
  • Manta Style — grants a second Doppelganger, dispels silences, and multiplies your illusion count.
  • Mekansm (or Pipe of Insight) — team utility; Mekansm synergizes with your illusion‑based damage by providing burst heal.
  • Butterfly — massive evasion and damage, turning you into a near‑untargetable right‑click threat.

Situational Items

  • Black King Bar — essential against heavy magical burst (QOP, Shadow Demon, Rubick).
  • Heart of Tarrasque — survivability when you become the primary target in late‑game fights.
  • Satanic — lifesteal for sustained engagements, especially vs tanky heroes like Slardar.
  • Abyssal Blade — lockdown for heroes that can otherwise dodge your attacks (e.g., Storm Spirit).
  • Linken’s Sphere — blocks single‑target disables from Nature’s Prophet or Rubick.
  • Silver Edge — silence break and extra burst for early kills on elusive heroes like Hoodwink.

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑relying on Spirit Lance for damage; the real power comes from stacking high‑damage illusions with Manta Style and Illusory Armaments.
  • Using Doppelganger offensively without checking vision; it often lands you in enemy vision and gets caught by burst heroes.
  • Neglecting evasion items; without Butterfly or Manta, QOP and Shadow Demon can easily kill you before your illusion army grows.
  • Failing to farm safely in the early game; low‑win matchups (e.g., QOP 32.9 % win rate) punish reckless aggression.

FAQ

Is Phantom Lancer good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 51.7 % win rate on 372 k recent matches, PL is a reliable carry that scales well into the late game, especially when built with Diffusal Blade, Manta Style, and evasion items.

What lane does Phantom Lancer play?

Phantom Lancer is typically played in the safe lane as a carry, allowing him to farm safely while his early Spirit Lance and illusion generation keep lane opponents at bay.

Who counters Phantom Lancer?

Burst spell‑casters and silence heroes—Queen of Pain (32.9 % PL win), Shadow Demon (33.9 %), Hoodwink (37.3 %), Windranger (37.9 %), Nature’s Prophet (38.0 %), and Rubick (39.2 %)—are the toughest matchups on patch 7.41. Building a BKB or early Linken’s Sphere and maintaining vision are key to surviving their pressure.
phantom-lancer.counterHtml:
Phantom Lancer thrives on overwhelming illusion numbers, high mobility, and evasion that make him difficult to lock down in fights. The key to shutting him down is denying his ability to create or sustain those illusions and forcing him into predictable, low‑mobility engagements.

Why These Heroes Beat Phantom Lancer

Queen of Pain

Her burst damage and Scream of Pain AOE silence quickly melt both PL’s hero and his illusions before they can reposition with Doppelganger. Tip: land a Scream of Pain followed by an Sonic Wave when PL jumps with Phantom Rush to catch his re‑appearances.

Shadow Demon

Disruption removes PL and his current illusion pool from the fight for 1.5 seconds, while Soul Catcher amplifies the damage taken, making every illusion death costly. Tip: time Disruption just after PL uses Doppelganger to force a clean reset and deny his escape.

Hoodwink

Acorn Shot and Bushwhack provide reliable AOE damage and a stun that interrupts Doppelganger and Spirit Lance, preventing illusion spawn. Tip: aim Bushwhack at the spot PL is likely to re‑appear after a Doppelganger jump for an instant lock‑down.

Windranger

Shackleshot can tether PL and an illusion together, pulling them into a predictable spot where Windrun’s evasion is irrelevant, while Powershot deals pure damage to clustered phantoms. Tip: use Shackleshot on the hero when PL’s Phantom Rush closes the distance; the tether forces a forced melee fight.

Nature's Prophet

His global Teleport lets him gank PL before he can build illusion stacks, and Wrath of Nature deals AOE damage that hits both the hero and any nearby phantoms. Tip: split‑push and force PL to defend; a well‑timed Teleport into his lane catches him while his Doppelganger cooldown is up.

Drafting Against Phantom Lancer

  • Prioritize heroes with strong single‑target burst or silence (e.g., Queen of Pain, Shadow Demon).
  • Pick heroes with reliable AOE magical damage that pierces illusion damage caps (e.g., Hoodwink, Windranger).
  • Include at least one global or high‑mobility hero to punish PL’s reliance on lane dominance.
  • Ban or avoid heroes that grant PL extra survivability or illusion‑generation (e.g., heroes with Manta Style or high armor).

Laning Against Phantom Lancer

  • Harass early before Juxtapose can generate multiple phantoms; use ranged harass and creep equilibrium.
  • Force PL to use Spirit Lance on creeps; the slow and damage give you a window to trade.
  • Punish his Phantom Rush cooldown—when it’s on cooldown, his chase is limited and you can safely trade.
  • Stack the lane and use AOE spells to kill any newly created illusion instantly, denying his illusion count.

Itemizing Against Phantom Lancer

Diffusal Blade — applies mana burn and a purge that removes Doppelganger’s brief invulnerability, forcing PL to stay in combat.
Silencer's Global Silence (or any global silence) — shuts down PL’s Spirit Lance and Phantom Rush, preventing illusion creation.
Mekansm / Guardian Greaves — AOE heal and armor reduce the effectiveness of PL’s illusion damage and keep your core alive.
Abyssal Blade — provides a reliable stun that can lock PL even after he reappears from Doppelganger, allowing you to burst him down.
