phoenix.name: Phoenix
phoenix.guideHtml:
Phoenix is a versatile support‑nuker who excels at zone control and team‑fight healing. On patch 7.41 his win rate sits at 50.6 % across ≈ 200k ranked games, making him a solid but not dominant pick. He thrives when he can land his Sun Ray and Supernova safely, while struggling against heroes that can silence or burst him early (see toughest match‑ups).

How to Play Phoenix

Laning Phase

  • Fire Spirits: Use the rotating spirits to harass melee off‑laners and apply the massive attack‑speed slow; aim them at the enemy creep wave to force the opponent to pull or miss CS.
  • Icarus Dive: Dive forward to dodge early harass or to escape a gank; the slow on enemies can buy you a safe retreat or a quick counter‑engage.
  • Dying Light: Keep the passive ticking while you’re in lane; the extra 4 % missing‑health damage is especially strong against low‑HP early heroes.
  • Sun Ray (toggle movement): When you have a safe lane (e.g., against ranged supports), toggle the slow movement to stay in place and fire a short Sun Ray to heal your carry and chip enemy health.
  • Lane match‑ups: Prioritize safe lanes against heroes like Dark Seer or Sand King (your easiest match‑ups). Against tough lanes such as Keeper of the Light or Magnus, play ultra‑defensive, only using Fire Spirits for poke and saving Sun Ray for emergencies.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 6: Unlock Supernova; look for 3‑v‑3 or 4‑v‑4 fights where you can position the sun behind your frontline.
  • Map presence: Use Icarus Dive to scout Roshan or to quickly join a contested lane; the dive’s fixed distance lets you dodge vision and surprise enemies.
  • Sun Ray timing: In team fights, start Sun Ray after the enemy initiates; the health‑cost is offset by the massive heal on allies and the scaling damage.
  • Fire Spirit launches: When the enemy clusters near a tower or Roshan, launch all four spirits simultaneously for a burst of damage and a crippling attack‑speed debuff.

Late Game

  • Win condition – Supernova: Secure vision around the sun, force the enemy to waste disables on it, and let the timer run out while your team pushes.
  • Positioning: Stay just behind your front line; you need to survive long enough to fire Sun Ray and keep Dying Light ticking.
  • Avoid death: Dying to burst heroes (Juggernaut, Doom) or heavy silence (Keeper of the Light) ends your Supernova early and hands the win to the enemy.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane, especially against harass.
  • Healing Salve — quick HP recovery after early trades.
  • Observer Ward — vision for safe Sun Ray usage.
  • Clarity — mana for early Fire Spirits and Sun Ray.
  • Faerie Fire — cheap burst heal for clutch moments.

Core Items

  • Arcane Boots — reliable mana pool for constant Sun Ray and Fire Spirit launches.
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Sun Ray to a longer beam and adds a small cast‑range increase, making it far safer.
  • Glimmer Cape — provides magic immunity for you and allies while you channel Sun Ray or set up Supernova.
  • Force Staff — extra mobility to reposition for Icarus Dive escapes or to get into optimal Supernova range.

Situational Items

  • Ghost Scepter — against right‑click heavy heroes like Juggernaut; lets you survive their burst while you channel.
  • Eul’s Scepter — extra disable to set up Fire Spirit launches or to protect yourself from Doom’s ultimate.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target spells (Keeper of the Light, Bane) that otherwise shut you down.
  • Shiva’s Guard — armor and AoE slow against physical cores; also synergizes with Dying Light’s damage.
  • Mekansm / Guardian Greaves — extra team‑fight sustain when your carry lacks healing.

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑committing Sun Ray without vision, getting silenced or burst down before the heal finishes.
  • Launching Fire Spirits without targeting; random launches waste the attack‑speed slow and reduce damage output.
  • Using Icarus Dive aggressively in the early game, getting caught by enemy disables (Magnus, Keeper).
  • Neglecting Dying Light; many players forget it ticks automatically and miss free damage throughout the game.

FAQ

Is Phoenix good in the current patch?

Yes. Phoenix sits at a 50.6 % win rate on 7.41, making him a reliable support pick. His kit scales well into mid‑game team fights, especially with Aghanim’s Scepter and proper vision for Supernova.

What lane does Phoenix play?

Phoenix is most commonly played as a support in the safe lane (off‑lane for Radiant, safe lane for Dire). He can also be flexed to a dual‑lane position when paired with a strong early‑game carry, but his primary role remains support.

Who counters Phoenix?

The toughest match‑ups are Keeper of the Light (34.1 % win), Magnus (38.7 %), and Juggernaut (40.3 %). These heroes either silence, burst, or out‑damage Phoenix before he can land Sun Ray or Supernova. Building Ghost Scepter, Lotus Orb, or early Eul’s can mitigate their impact.
phoenix.counterHtml:
Phoenix is a high‑damage, high‑utility hero whose threat comes from relentless area damage (Sun Ray, Supernova) and the ability to heal allies while burning enemies. The core principle for shutting him down is to deny him the sustained fights he needs to build his health‑based damage and to force him into short, bursty trades where his cooldowns are on lock‑out.

Why These Heroes Beat Phoenix

Keeper of the Light

Keeper’s Recall and Spirit Form give him long‑range safety and the ability to dodge Phoenix’s Icarus Dive and Fire Spirits. His Mana Leak provides constant magic damage that chips Phoenix’s health, preventing the large health pool needed for Dying Light and Supernova.
Tip: Keep your Sun Ray on a safe distance and use Recall to reset Phoenix’s dive when he commits.

Magnus

Magnus’s Skewer and Reverse Polarity can instantly pull Phoenix out of his Sun Ray channel and lock him down before Supernova can be cast. The burst of physical damage from Skewer also reduces Phoenix’s missing‑health scaling for Dying Light.
Tip: Time Reverse Polarity right after Phoenix launches a Fire Spirit; the stun prevents the spirit from being redirected and forces Phoenix to retreat.

Juggernaut

Juggernaut’s Blade Fury provides magic immunity for the duration, nullifying Sun Ray, Fire Spirits, and the damage component of Dying Light. His Healing Ward restores health faster than Phoenix’s Dying Light can drain, and Omni‑Slash can finish Phoenix before he can revive from Supernova.
Tip: Activate Blade Fury when Phoenix begins Sun Ray; stay within Healing Ward range to out‑heal his Dying Light.

Dazzle

Dazzle’s Shallow Grave can protect a core ally from Phoenix’s burst damage, forcing Phoenix to waste Sun Ray on a dead target. Shadow Wave deals magic damage and heals simultaneously, counter‑balancing Phoenix’s heal‑on‑damage mechanic. His Weave slows Phoenix’s movement, making it harder for him to escape after a dive.
Tip: Place Shallow Grave on your mid‑lane hero pre‑emptively; when Phoenix dives, the grave forces him to either waste his dive or lose the kill.

Bane

Bane’s Nightmare silences Phoenix, preventing Sun Ray and Fire Spirit launches for up to 5 seconds. Enfeeble reduces Phoenix’s attack damage, making his early‑game harassment less threatening. The combination of Brain Sap and Nightmare can burst Phoenix down before he can accumulate enough missing health for Dying Light.
Tip: Initiate with Nightmare as soon as Phoenix starts channeling Sun Ray; follow up with Enfeeble to keep his damage low during the fight.

Drafting Against Phoenix

  • Prioritize heroes with magic immunity or strong burst silence (e.g., Juggernaut, Bane, Silencer).
  • Pick heroes with reliable long‑range disables that can interrupt Sun Ray or Supernova (Keeper of the Light, Magnus).
  • Ban or avoid heavy sustain heroes that can out‑heal Dying Light (e.g., Dazzle, Warlock).
  • Include at least one strong lane bully that can pressure Phoenix before he gets Fire Spirits.

Laning Against Phoenix

  • Trade when Phoenix’s Fire Spirits are on cooldown; his damage window is narrow.
  • Harass him early before he can build missing‑health damage for Dying Light.
  • Force him to use Icarus Dive defensively by zoning him with slows or blocks.
  • Punish the moment he begins Sun Ray—use a stun or silence to cancel the channel.

Itemizing Against Phoenix

Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — provides a reliable disable to interrupt Sun Ray and Supernova while granting a movement speed boost to escape Icarus Dive.
Black King Bar — grants magic immunity, nullifying Sun Ray, Fire Spirits, and Dying Light’s damage.
Heaven’s Halberd — disarms Phoenix, preventing him from casting Sun Ray or launching Fire Spirits during a fight.
Lotus Orb — reflects Phoenix’s Sun Ray and removes debuffs like Dazzle’s Shadow Wave, reducing his sustain.
Scythe of Vyse — a long‑duration hex that shuts down Phoenix’s channeling and prevents Supernova activation.

primal-beast.name: Primal Beast
primal-beast.guideHtml:
Primal Beast is a front‑line initiator and durable disabler who thrives on chaotic teamfights. With a 48.3% win rate across 108 k recent ranked games (OpenDota, July 2026), he sits in the mid‑tier of the meta—strong enough to pick, but vulnerable to several high‑impact disables.

How to Play Primal Beast

Laning Phase

  • Onslaught early charge can be used to secure the first blood or escape ganks; aim for a short charge (≈1 s) to stun enemies without over‑extending.
  • Trample provides reliable wave clear; use it when the enemy creep equilibrium is too far forward, but remember you’re disarmed while it’s active.
  • Uproar stacks quickly against heroes that spam high‑damage spells (e.g., Razor’s Lightning Rush); prioritize landing hits that exceed 50 damage to boost your attack.
  • Against hard‑line opponents like Earthshaker or Clockwerk, keep a safe distance and rely on Rock Throw to punish their positioning.
  • Pair Rock Throw with a quick Onslaught to catch roaming supports off‑guard and force early tower pressure.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 6 when you unlock Pulverize; start looking for 2‑v2 skirmishes where you can grab a key enemy and chain hits.
  • Use Onslaught to initiate after your team has vision; the stun and knock‑back are excellent for isolating squishy cores such as Gyrocopter or Muerta.
  • Prioritize objectives that let you leverage Uproar damage (e.g., Roshan) – each 50‑damage hit adds attack, making you a threat to tanky heroes like Ogre Magi.
  • When facing Razor or Shadow Demon, stay behind your frontline and wait for their disables to cooldown before committing Onslaught.

Late Game

  • Win condition: lock down the enemy’s primary damage dealer with Pulverize + Onslaught, then let your team follow up with burst.
  • Position near the front of your team; your Rock Throw provides a reliable stun for late‑game teamfights, especially against mobile heroes like Puck.
  • Over‑extending with a long Onslaught charge often leads to being caught by Faceless Void’s Chronosphere or Earthshaker’s Echo Slam—avoid long charges when those ultimates are up.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango + Healing Salve — sustain in lane against poke.
  • Stout Shield — mitigates harassment from heroes like Razor.
  • Quelling Blade — helps with last‑hits while using Trample.
  • Observer Ward — vision to avoid ganks from Clockwerk.

Core Items

  • Blink Dagger — essential for closing the gap before Onslaught or Pulverize.
  • Abyssal Blade — adds a reliable stun and extra burst to finish off high‑damage heroes (e.g., Shadow Demon).
  • Vanguard → Crimson Guard — counters physical burst from Ogre Magi and Razor.
  • Heart of Tarrasque — maximizes durability for front‑line engagements.

Situational Items

  • Black King Bar — against heavy magical burst (e.g., Puck, Shadow Shaman).
  • Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target disables from Earthshaker or Faceless Void.
  • Shiva’s Guard — provides armor and an AoE slow to mitigate Gyrocopter and Muerta damage.
  • Assault Cuirass — boosts attack speed for faster Uproar stacks and helps against Razor’s damage.
  • Pipe of Insight — team‑wide magic resistance when facing spell‑heavy lineups.

Common Mistakes

  • Charging too far with Onslaught – you get stunned by enemy disables and lose vision, especially against Earthshaker and Faceless Void.
  • Using Trample while enemy heroes have ready disables – the disarm leaves you vulnerable to Razor and Shadow Demon.
  • Neglecting Uproar stacks – failing to land 50‑damage hits wastes a major source of bonus attack that can turn fights.
  • Itemizing purely for damage – ignoring defensive items makes you an easy target for burst heroes like Gyrocopter.

FAQ

Is Primal Beast good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 48.3% win rate in recent ranked matches, Primal Beast is a viable pick, especially when paired with strong initiators and vision control. He shines against squishy heroes like Muerta and Gyrocopter, though he struggles versus hard‑disable lineups.

What lane does Primal Beast play?

Primal Beast is most commonly played in the off‑lane (solo safe lane) where his durability and wave‑clear from Trample allow him to survive against aggressive supports and set up early ganks with Onslaught.

Who counters Primal Beast?

Heroes with reliable disables and burst damage counter him best: Earthshaker, Razor, Shadow Demon, Clockwerk, Ogre Magi, and Faceless Void all have win rates below 42% against him, reflecting their ability to punish his charge and prevent effective Pulverize engagements.

Why These Heroes Beat Primal Beast

Earthshaker

Earthshaker’s Fissure and Echo Slam punish Primal Beast’s linear charge: a well‑timed Fissure blocks the Onslaught path and stuns the Beast mid‑rush, while Echo Slam deals massive damage to the clustered enemies that Primal Beast tries to hit with Trample. Tip: position a ward near the expected charge lane and use Fissure as soon as you see the charge animation.

Razor

Razor’s Static Link drains the Beast’s attack damage, directly weakening the damage multiplier on Trample and Pulverize. Additionally, Eye of the Storm provides armor that mitigates the burst from Rock Throw and Onslaught. Tip: keep Razor in lane and start linking as soon as Primal Beast gets a few stacks of Uproar; the link’s damage reduction scales with his attack, making his burst fall off quickly.

Shadow Demon

Shadow Demon’s Disruption can pull Primal Beast out of his charge trajectory, breaking the momentum needed for Onslaught and Trample. The subsequent Soul Catcher amplifies the damage taken from his own abilities, turning his self‑damage into a liability. Tip: save Disruption for the moment Primal Beast initiates Onslaught; the forced reposition forces a miss and gives you a window to follow up with nukes.

Clockwerk

Clockwerk’s Battery Assault and Hookshot create a hard wall that Primal Beast cannot charge through; the stun from Battery Assault also interrupts his channel on Pulverize. The constant lockdown pressure forces the Beast to waste his charge on a dead‑end. Tip: start Hookshot early in the lane to establish a “no‑charge” zone and follow with Battery Assault when he attempts to close in.

Ogre Magi

Ogre Magi’s Fireblast provides a reliable stun that can interrupt Onslaught mid‑run, while Multicast increases the chance of multiple stuns on a single charge. His innate tankiness also absorbs the burst from Rock Throw. Tip: prioritize casting Fireblast the moment you see the charge animation; a stun at the end of the charge negates both the stun and the Trample damage radius.

Drafting Against Primal Beast

  • Prioritize heroes with hard‑crowd control (stuns, silences) that can interrupt Onslaught or Pulverize.
  • Pick tanky or high‑armor heroes to survive the initial burst from Rock Throw and Trample.
  • Include early‑game lane disruptors that can deny Uproar stacks (e.g., heroes with displacement or silence).
  • Consider bans that remove strong burst carries who could synergize with Primal Beast’s damage (e.g., Gyrocopter, Muerta).

Laning Against Primal Beast

  • Harass him before he accumulates Uproar stacks; his damage spikes after each 50‑damage instance.
  • Force him to use Rock Throw from long range; the minimum‑range restriction leaves him vulnerable to counter‑harass.
  • Trade when his Trample is on cooldown—he is disarmed and cannot retaliate with damage.
  • Keep a ward near the expected Onslaught path to anticipate and pre‑empt his charge.

Itemizing Against Primal Beast

Ghost Scepter — makes you untargetable by his physical burst from Trample and Pulverize.
Heaven's Halberd — disarms Primal Beast, nullifying his Trample damage and reducing his overall threat.
Force Staff — lets you escape the linear charge corridor or reposition enemies into your own crowd‑control zones.

puck.name: Puck
puck.guideHtml:
Puck remains a high‑skill, high‑impact initiator in the current meta, sitting at a 47.3% win rate across 149,946 ranked games on OpenDota (July 2026). The hero’s blend of burst damage, silence, and mobility makes him a staple for teams that need reliable crowd control and escape tools, though his win‑rate dip against certain mid‑lane heroes shows he can be vulnerable in 1v1 matchups.

How to Play Puck

Laning Phase

  • Illusory Orb early harass: launch the orb into the enemy creep wave to chip health and force the opponent to pull, while the orb’s scaling damage (3 % per 0.5 s) adds extra pressure.
  • Waning Rift for lane control: use the instant silence + damage to punish aggressive melee heroes (e.g., Bounty Hunter) and to secure safe farm when the enemy roams.
  • Phase Shift as a defensive tool: time the channeled invulnerability to dodge incoming spells from burst heroes like Nyx Assassin or to survive early ganks.
  • Ethereal Jaunt combo: after landing Illusory Orb on a target, instantly jump to it with Jaunt to reposition or to escape a dangerous pull from Naga Siren.
  • Prioritize mana regeneration (e.g., Faerie Fire, Tango) because Puck’s spell‑heavy kit depletes mana quickly against heroes with high spell‑spam like Oracle.

Mid Game

  • Dream Coil + Waning Rift combo: initiate with Rift, follow up with Coil to lock multiple enemies, then use Phase Shift to survive any retaliation.
  • Power spike at Level 6 (Dream Coil unlock): start roaming to secure kills on soft lanes; look for easy targets like Crystal Maiden or Silencer where Coil’s stun will guarantee a kill.
  • Use Illusory Orb for split‑push scouting: the orb’s vision and damage can clear creep waves while providing map awareness of enemy movements.
  • Prioritize vision and smoke ganks: Puck’s silence and stun make him excellent at catching out isolated heroes, especially against easy matchups like Weaver (61.1 % win rate).

Late Game

  • Win condition: lock high‑damage carries (e.g., Morphling, Dark Seer) in Dream Coil while teammates focus fire; Puck’s burst and silence open the fight.
  • Positioning: stay on the edge of fights, using Phase Shift and Ethereal Jaunt to dodge initiations; over‑committing leads to being burst down by heroes like Nyx Assassin.
  • Game‑ending play: coordinate a full‑team Waning Rift → Dream Coil → Phase Shift chain to wipe out the enemy backline; a successful Coil snap can turn a 5‑vs‑5 into a 5‑vs‑3.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane, especially against poke‑heavy matchups (Oracle, Bounty Hunter).
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery after early skirmishes.
  • Faerie Fire — cheap burst damage and a small health buffer for early harass.
  • Observer Ward — vision to avoid ganks from mobile heroes like Naga Siren.

Core Items

  • Eul's Scepter of Divinity — provides mana regen, movement speed, and a self‑silence that synergizes with Phase Shift for survivability.
  • Aghanim's Scepter — upgrades Dream Coil to affect a larger area and adds a second coil, crucial against teamfights with multiple carries.
  • Octarine Core — reduces cooldowns on all spells, letting you spam Illusory Orb and Dream Coil more frequently.

Situational Items

  • Black King Bar — when facing heavy magical burst (e.g., Nyx Assassin, Oracle).
  • Scythe of Vyse — extra lockdown against slippery heroes like Naga Siren or Morphling.
  • Gleipnir — combines a stun and slow, useful when Dream Coil is on cooldown.
  • Linken's Sphere — blocks single‑target disables from Bounty Hunter or Nyx Assassin.
  • Force Staff — additional escape and positioning tool to complement Ethereal Jaunt.

Common Mistakes

  • Wasting Phase Shift on non‑damage spells; save it for high‑burst abilities (Nyx Assassin’s Mana Burn, Oracle’s Fate’s Edict).
  • Over‑committing with Dream Coil without a follow‑up escape, leading to easy counter‑initiations.
  • Ignoring mana management; spamming Illusory Orb and Waning Rift early can leave you vulnerable to ganks.
  • Failing to scout with Illusory Orb, missing opportunities to catch roaming heroes like Bounty Hunter.

FAQ

Is Puck good in the current patch?

Yes. Puck sits at a 47.3 % win rate across 149,946 ranked games, making him a solid pick in the current meta, especially against heroes like Weaver (61.1 % win rate) and Dark Willow (59.1 %). His high‑skill ceiling rewards players who can execute precise combos and map‑wide pressure.

What lane does Puck play?

Puck is typically played in the mid lane as a solo core, leveraging his burst damage and silence to dominate lane opponents and transition into a roaming initiator after level 6.

Who counters Puck?

The toughest matchups are against Naga Siren (34.5 % win rate), Nyx Assassin (39.8 %), Bounty Hunter (40.0 %), Oracle (40.7 %), Morphling (40.9 %), and Dark Seer (41.0 %). These heroes either out‑scale Puck’s early damage or possess tools that bypass his silence and burst. Counter‑play involves building early Linken's Sphere, Black King Bar, and maintaining strong vision to avoid being caught in Dream Coil.

Why These Heroes Beat Puck

Naga Siren

Naga’s Mirror Image creates multiple illusion copies that force Puck to waste Illusory Orb and Dream Coil on harmless targets, while her Ensnare can lock Puck in place after he teleports in with Waning Rift. Play aggressively in lane and look for a quick Riptide‑spam combo once Naga’s cooldowns are up.

Nyx Assassin

Nyx’s Mana Burn directly counters Puck’s mana‑intensive spell rotation, and Spiked Carapace can reflect the damage from Dream Coil back onto Puck when he tries to leash him. Aim to land Impale right after Puck uses Phase Shift to catch him during the channel.

Bounty Hunter

Track grants vision through Puck’s Phase Shift and Ethereal Jaunt, nullifying his escape and enabling early ganks. Bounty’s Shuriken Toss also interrupts Illusory Orb’s channel, forcing Puck to retreat. Prioritize a early track on Puck and follow up with a silence from an ally.

Oracle

Oracle’s Fate’s Edict makes Puck untargetable, preventing him from landing Dream Coil or Waning Rift during fights, while False Promise can save a teammate from the coil’s damage. Use Fortune’s End to purge the silence from Waning Rift and force Puck to waste his Phase Shift.

Morphling

Morphling’s Morph can amplify his damage to burst Puck before he can Phase Shift, and Waveform lets him dodge Dream Coil and close the gap instantly. Build Aghanim’s Scepter for the Morph Replicate to create a copy that can absorb Puck’s Illusory Orb damage. Engage when Morphling’s Attribute Shift is maxed for a quick kill.

Drafting Against Puck

  • Prioritize heroes with strong early damage or mana‑burn (e.g., Nyx Assassin, Bounty Hunter).
  • Include at least one reliable silence or purge to counter Dream Coil and Waning Rift.
  • Pick mobile heroes that can out‑maneuver Phase Shift and chase down Puck after he teleports.
  • Consider banning or limiting other high‑burst, low‑mana heroes that synergize with Puck’s playstyle.

Laning Against Puck

  • Harass him before he gets Phase Shift; his early HP is low and he lacks sustain.
  • Force him to use Illusory Orb on creeps to deny lane pressure, then punish the cooldown.
  • When he attempts Waning Rift, stay at the edge of its radius to avoid the silence and counter‑engage.
  • Use creep equilibrium to keep him on the defensive and deny vision for his Ethereal Jaunt.

Itemizing Against Puck

Eul's Scepter of Divinity — provides a reliable cyclone to interrupt Dream Coil and delay his Phase Shift.
Black King Bar — prevents Puck’s silences and damage from Illusory Orb in team fights.
Ghost Scepter — makes you immune to the magical damage of Illusory Orb and Dream Coil while you wait for his cooldowns.
Scythe of Vyse — a hard‑lock that stops Puck from escaping with Phase Shift or Ethereal Jaunt.

pudge.name: Pudge
pudge.guideHtml:
Pudge remains a high‑impact disabler and initiator in the current meta, boasting a 51.4% win rate across 1,035,768 ranked matches on patch 7.41. His blend of burst hook potential, sustain from Dismember, and scaling survivability via Flesh Heap makes him a top pick in both solo‑mid and off‑lane roles.

How to Play Pudge

Laning Phase

  • Hook early and often – land a successful Meat Hook on a support or low‑HP creep to secure early kills or force enemy rotations; the hook’s damage and pull are crucial for lane dominance.
  • Use Rot defensively – position Rot to deter aggressive harass; the self‑damage is offset by the damage it deals to opponents and the slow it applies.
  • Stack and farm with Meat Shield – activate Meat Shield when farming jungle or lane creeps to mitigate damage and accelerate last‑hits.
  • Prioritize Flesh Heap stacks – aim for at least one hero kill or assist per 2‑3 minutes to stack Flesh Heap, increasing strength and hook range.
  • Watch for counter‑hooks – against heroes like Lycan or Earth Spirit, keep distance and anticipate their mobility; a missed hook can leave you vulnerable to early ganks.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at 12 minutes – with two Flesh Heap stacks and a completed Aghanim’s Scepter, your hook range and Dismember damage surge.
  • Create pick‑off opportunities – roam with vision, look for isolated heroes, and use a combo of Hook → Rot → Dismember to secure kills.
  • Control objectives – position Rot near Roshan or towers to deter enemy pushes while you tank damage with Meat Shield.
  • Split‑push with Meat Hook – pull enemy cores away from objectives, forcing them to defend and opening space for your team.

Late Game

  • Win condition: pick‑offs and tanking – use Hook to isolate a key hero, Dismember for burst and self‑heal, and rely on Flesh Heap stacks for survivability in team fights.
  • Position near front line – your Meat Shield and high strength let you absorb damage; stay close enough to land hooks on high‑value targets.
  • Avoid being caught without Hook – if you lose your hook (e.g., silenced or stunned), you become a soft target; prioritize items that grant spell immunity or hook‑reset (e.g., Aghanim’s Shard).

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango & Healing Salve — sustain in lane while you farm with Rot.
  • Stout Shield — mitigates early harassment and creep damage.
  • Observer Ward — vision for safe Hook attempts and to spot rotations.

Core Items

  • Aghanim’s Scepter — increases Hook range and adds a second hook charge, crucial for mid‑game ganks.
  • Blink Dagger — provides the positioning needed to land Hooks from unexpected angles.
  • Vanguard — blocks the self‑damage from Rot and gives extra durability against burst heroes.
  • Heart of Tarrasque — synergizes with Flesh Heap stacks for massive tankiness and Dismember healing.

Situational Items

  • Black King Bar — against heavy magic burst (e.g., Bane, Earth Spirit).
  • Abyssal Blade — extra lockdown when Hook fails or against slippery heroes like Slark.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target disables, useful versus Bane and Earth Spirit.
  • Pipe of Insight — mitigates magic damage from heroes such as Morphling and Warlock.
  • Glimmer Cape — provides safety for a Hook‑initiated dive on vision‑heavy lineups.

Common Mistakes

  • Hook spamming without vision – missing Hooks wastes cooldown and leaves you vulnerable to counter‑ganks.
  • Over‑using Rot – taking excessive self‑damage reduces your survivability and can force early deaths.
  • Neglecting Flesh Heap stacks – failing to secure hero kills/assists stalls your strength scaling, making late‑game fights harder.
  • Positioning too far back – staying out of hook range eliminates your primary threat and lets the enemy dictate fights.

FAQ

Is Pudge good in the current patch?

Yes. Pudge enjoys a 51.4% win rate in the latest ranked data, making him one of the stronger disablers and initiators on patch 7.41.

What lane does Pudge play?

Pudge is most effective in solo‑mid or off‑lane, where he can farm safely, stack Flesh Heap, and have space to land Hooks on isolated enemies.

Who counters Pudge?

Heroes with high mobility and silence—such as Lycan (36.8% win vs. Pudge), Earth Spirit (39.5%), and Slark (41.0%)—are the toughest matchups, as they can dodge Hooks and punish Pudge’s self‑damage.
pudge.counterHtml:
Pudge thrives on surprise — a well‑timed Meat Hook followed by Rot or Dismember can instantly turn a lane or teamfight. The key to shutting him down is denying those hook opportunities and out‑pacing his Flesh Heap stacking, forcing him to waste Rot on non‑essential targets.

Why These Heroes Beat Pudge

Lycan

Lycan’s Summon Wolves and Feral Impulse give him constant, fast‑moving creeps that can dodge or block hooks, while his Howl provides a burst of movement speed that outruns Rot’s slow. Tip: Keep a wolf alive near the lane; a hook on a wolf is wasted and gives you vision of Pudge’s position.

Earth Spirit

Rolling Boulder and Stone Remnant let Earth Spirit create unpredictable terrain, breaking the straight line needed for a successful hook. His Magnetize also forces Pudge to stay out of range or waste Rot on a non‑hero. Tip: Drop a stone just before a hook; the boulder will block it and stun Pudge if he tries to follow up.

Slark (Shadow Dance)

Slark’s Dark Pact instantly removes the Rot damage-over-time, and Pounce grants a short‑range dash that can sidestep a hook. When Shadow Dance is active, Slark becomes untargetable, nullifying Dismember. Tip: Save Dark Pact for the moment you feel Rot tick; the cooldown reset on Pounce lets you re‑engage quickly.

Naga Siren

Mirror Image creates decoys that confuse Pudge’s hook trajectory, and Riptide slows enemies while also providing a brief movement‑speed boost for the Siren to slip away. Her Ensnare can lock Pudge in place, preventing him from pulling you back with Meat Hook. Tip: Position a Mirror Image near a potential hook line; a successful hook on an illusion wastes the cooldown.

Batrider

Flamebreak grants a burst of movement speed and a brief invulnerability window, letting Batrider dodge hooks and escape Rot’s area. His Firefly provides sustained mobility, making it hard for Pudge to land a hook at any distance. Tip: Use Flamebreak when you see the hook animation start; the speed boost often outruns the hook’s travel time.

Drafting Against Pudge

  • Prioritize heroes with high mobility (blink, dash, or speed‑boost) to outrun Meat Hook.
  • Pick heroes with strong self‑purge or damage mitigation (e.g., Dark Pact, Stone Remnant) to neutralize Rot.
  • Include at least one hero with reliable crowd‑control that can stun or silence Pudge before he channels Dismember.
  • Consider early‑game aggression heroes that can pressure Pudge out of the lane before his Flesh Heap stacks.

Laning Against Pudge

  • Trade when Pudge’s Meat Hook is on cooldown; his damage output drops dramatically.
  • Harass him with ranged attacks while staying behind creep wave to force him to use Rot on non‑heroes.
  • Punish the moment he attempts a hook on a creep—use the creep’s death timer to bait a hook and then counter‑engage.
  • Keep a ward near the river to spot his positioning; early vision forces him to play more cautiously.

Itemizing Against Pudge

Ghost Scepter — blocks Meat Hook and Dismember damage while you’re vulnerable to Rot.
Eul's Cyclone — lifts Pudge out of Rot’s area and interrupts Dismember, buying time for your team.
Force Staff — provides instant distance to escape a hook or close the gap before he can react with Rot.
Heaven's Halberd — disarms Pudge, preventing him from activating Meat Hook or Dismember while you focus him down.

pugna.name: Pugna
pugna.guideHtml:
Pugna remains a high‑impact nuker and pusher in the current meta, sitting at a 49.6 % win rate over 145,951 ranked games (OpenDota, July 2026). While his tower‑damage scaling and strong lane control keep him relevant, the win‑rate dip below 50 % reflects a meta that rewards mobile heroes and heavy early aggression.

How to Play Pugna

Laning Phase

  • Decrepify early on the enemy off‑lane hero to deny them right‑click damage and amplify your later Nether Blast or Life Drain.
  • Nether Ward placement near the creep equilibrium forces spell‑reliant opponents (e.g., Ogre Magi, Dark Willow) to waste mana, leveraging the 61 % win rate against those heroes.
  • Use Nether Blast on stacked neutral camps or low‑HP towers to secure early tower damage; the 65 % structure damage makes the first tower fall quickly.
  • Oblivion Savant lets you cast items (e.g., Bottle, Blink Dagger) while channeling Life Drain, so you can sustain or escape without breaking the channel.
  • Prioritize mana management: Pugna’s spells are mana‑heavy; keep a Mana Stone or Clarity early if the lane is mana‑draining (e.g., against Clockwerk).

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 6: Net​her Ward becomes a true zone‑control tool; place it near Roshan or high‑traffic jungle paths to punish spell‑casters.
  • Tower‑damage amplification: After each tower falls, Pugna gains 1.5 % spell amplification—focus on pushing the lane you have pressure in to snowball.
  • Life Drain on key targets (e.g., enemy mid‑core) during team fights; the channel can be protected by a nearby Nether Ward that punishes enemy spell casts.
  • Split‑push with Nether Blast on enemy structures while your team forces objectives elsewhere; the combination of high tower damage and spell amp makes you a formidable siege hero.

Late Game

  • Win condition: Use Nether Ward to force enemy spell‑casters to stay out of fights, then pick off isolated heroes with Decrepify + Life Drain.
  • Positioning: Stay just behind your frontline; your low mobility makes you vulnerable to initiators like Bristleback or Terrorblade (against whom you have ~40 % win rates).
  • Avoid being caught by heroes with strong disables or burst (e.g., Crystal Maiden, Naga Siren) – they are currently the toughest matchups (≈40 % win).

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane, especially against harass.
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery after Decrepify trades.
  • Clarity — mitigates mana pressure from frequent Nether Blast/Decrepify.
  • Observer Ward — vision to protect your Nether Ward placement.

Core Items

  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Life Drain to affect allies and enemies simultaneously, increasing team utility.
  • Aether Lens — extends cast range of Decrepify and Life Drain, allowing safer engagements.
  • Black King Bar — essential against heavy magic burst and disables from heroes like Crystal Maiden and Naga Siren.
  • Octarine Core — reduces cooldowns on all spells, making Nether Ward and Life Drain more frequent.

Situational Items

  • Glimmer Cape — against right‑click heroes (Bristleback, Terrorblade) who can quickly close distance.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects targeted spells, useful versus Chen or Clockwerk.
  • Scythe of Vyse — provides hard‑disable when your Nether Ward isn’t enough, especially versus mobile heroes like Naga Siren.
  • Shiva’s Guard — armor and aura to survive physical burst from heroes such as Beastmaster.
  • Guardian Greaves — if you’re the primary support and need team‑wide sustain.

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑committing Life Drain without a nearby Nether Ward, allowing enemies to silence or burst you.
  • Neglecting tower damage scaling; many players stop pushing after the first tower instead of leveraging the 1.5 % spell amp per destroyed tower.
  • Using Decrepify on allies too early; the heal boost is wasted if the ally isn’t taking damage.
  • Positioning too close to frontline; Pugna’s low mobility makes him an easy target for initiators like Bristleback and Terrorblade.

FAQ

Is Pugna good in the current patch?

Yes. Pugna’s win rate sits at 49.6 % across nearly 146 k games, and he excels against spell‑reliant heroes (e.g., Ogre Magi 61 % win). His tower‑damage amplification and strong lane control keep him viable, though he struggles against mobile, high‑burst heroes.

What lane does Pugna play?

Pugna is typically played in the mid lane as a nuker/pusher, but he can also be taken to safe‑lane for early tower pressure when the enemy mid is heavily ganked.

Who counters Pugna?

The toughest matchups are Chen, Bristleback, Terrorblade, Crystal Maiden, Clockwerk, and Naga Siren, each with win rates around 38‑42 % against Pugna. Their high mobility, strong disables, or sustained right‑click damage exploit Pugna’s low survivability.
pugna.counterHtml:
Pugna’s threat comes from his ability to amplify magic damage with tower kills, his relentless Life Drain sustain, and the burst potential of Nether Blast combined with a damage‑reflecting Nether Ward. The core of shutting him down is denying him mana, killing his ward early, and forcing him to fight without the tower‑based spell amplification that makes his spells lethal.

Why These Heroes Beat Pugna

Chen

Chen’s Penitence and Hand of God give him strong early lane sustain and a reliable way to purge Decrepify with Holy Persuasion‑controlled creeps. His Holy Persuasion also lets him steal a neutral creep that can tank Pugna’s Nether Blast and pressure the lane.
Tip: Use the creeps you control to block Pugna’s ward placement and force him to waste mana on ward‑clearing.

Bristleback

Bristleback’s Quill Spray triggers on any attack, and because Decrepify prevents the target from attacking, Pugna can’t safely harass without losing his own damage output. Bristle’s high armor and Bristleback passive make him extremely tanky against Nether Blast.
Tip: Stay behind your front‑line and let Bristle’s passive soak the burst while you force Pugna to waste Life Drain on a tanky target.

Terrorblade

Terrorblade’s Metamorphosis gives him massive right‑click damage that ignores the magic‑damage boost from tower kills, while his Sunder can turn Pugna’s own health drain against him. The Reflection from Nether Ward is less effective because Terrorblade’s spells are minimal.
Tip: Push early and force Pugna to defend; his Nether Ward will be overwhelmed by Terrorblade’s high attack speed and can be destroyed quickly with Manta Style.

Crystal Maiden

Crystal Maiden’s Arcane Aura drains Pugna’s mana pool, shortening the window for Nether Ward and Life Drain. Her Frostbite and Freezing Field provide reliable crowd control that can lock Pugna in place, making him vulnerable to tower hits and Nether Blast.
Tip: Keep her Arcane Aura active throughout the lane; a well‑timed Frostbite on Pugna when he attempts to cast Decrepify nullifies his burst.

Clockwerk

Clockwerk’s Hookshot and Power Cogs let him close the distance instantly, bypassing Decrepify’s attack‑stop and forcing Pugna into melee range where his low physical damage is a liability. The Battery Assault damage over time also punishes Pugna’s low health pool after a Life Drain miss.
Tip: Initiate with Hookshot right after Pugna casts Decrepify; the stun interrupts his channel and leaves his ward exposed.

Drafting Against Pugna

  • Prioritize heroes with strong mana burn or mana‑draining abilities (e.g., Anti‑Mage, Silencer).
  • Pick tanky, high‑armor heroes that can survive Nether Blast and force Pugna to rely on Life Drain.
  • Include at least one hard‑disable that can interrupt channeling (e.g., Stun, Silence).
  • Consider early‑game split‑push or tower‑race heroes to deny Pugna the 1.5% spell amplification per tower.

Laning Against Pugna

  • Harass him before he gets a Nether Ward; the ward’s damage reflection is a huge win‑win for him.
  • Trade when his Decrepify is on cooldown – his damage output drops dramatically.
  • Force him to use Life Drain on a high‑HP target; the channel makes him vulnerable to ganks.
  • Keep the lane wave near your tower to limit his ability to land Nether Blast on creeps and structures.

Itemizing Against Pugna

Ghost Scepter — blocks his magical burst from Nether Blast and Life Drain while you wait for his ward to die.
Black King Bar — prevents the damage from his Nether Ward and the amplified magic from tower‑based spell amplification.
Pipe of Insight — provides magic resistance to all allies, mitigating the amplified damage from his spells.
Aghanim’s Scepter (Silencer) — grants Global Silence, shutting down his spell rotation and neutralizing Nether Ward entirely.

queen-of-pain.name: Queen of Pain
queen-of-pain.guideHtml:
Queen of Pain is a high‑mobility, magic‑damage burst hero who excels at mid‑lane nuking and escaping dangerous situations. On patch 7.41 she sits at a 46.3 % win rate across 387,866 recent ranked games, making her a solid but not dominant pick in the current meta【OpenDota July 2026】.

How to Play Queen of Pain

Laning Phase

  • Harass with Shadow Strike + Scream of Pain: Shadow Strike’s initial burst plus the periodic damage forces safe‑lane cores to miss last hits, while Scream of Pain adds AoE pressure when the enemy groups.
  • Blink for safe trades: Use Blink to close the distance for a quick Shadow Strike‑Scream combo, then Blink back before the enemy can respond.
  • Maintain lane control: Keep the enemy creep wave near your tower with occasional Scream of Pain pushes; this denies farm to heroes like Keeper of the Light and Chen who thrive on free creep.
  • Watch for vision: Dark Seer and Treant Protector often set up early pushes; place a ward near the river to spot their rotations and avoid getting caught in a split‑push.
  • Stack and farm jungle: When the lane is pushed, use Blink to hop to a nearby jungle stack, kill the neutral camp with Shadow Strike‑Scream, and return to lane with minimal loss.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 6: Sonic Wave becomes a game‑changing tool for picking off squishy cores; look for isolated targets after successful ganks.
  • Roam with Blink: After securing a few core items, start rotating to side lanes. A well‑timed Sonic Wave followed by Shadow Strike can secure kills on heroes like Bounty Hunter who rely on vision.
  • Take objectives with Sonic Wave: Use the wave’s push to break towers or force enemy heroes out of Roshan; the knock‑back also disrupts Dark Seer's Vacuum‑Pulverize combos.
  • Avoid prolonged fights against high‑armor heroes: Treant Protector and Pugna’s high magic resistance reduce Sonic Wave’s effectiveness; focus on burst‑killing squishy targets instead.

Late Game

  • Win condition: burst‑kill the enemy carry – With core items, a single Sonic Wave + Shadow Strike combo can delete the opposing mid or safe‑lane core before they can react.
  • Positioning is king: Stay just outside enemy vision range, using Blink to dodge disables and to re‑engage with Sonic Wave when the enemy’s cooldowns are down.
  • Don’t over‑extend into team fights: If you miss a Sonic Wave, you become vulnerable to counter‑initiates from Dark Seer, Treant Protector, or Chen’s mass heal.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain for early harassment.
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery after a Shadow Strike trade.
  • Faerie Fire — cheap burst heal for clutch moments.
  • Observer Ward — vision to avoid ganks from Chen and Dark Seer.
  • Iron Branch ×2 — cheap stats and can later be used for Magic Wand.

Core Items

  • Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — provides mana, movement speed, and a self‑save against Chen’s Divine Favor or Dark Seer’s Vacuum.
  • Black King Bar — essential against heavy magical disables from Keeper of the Light, Pugna, and Treant Protector.
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — reduces Sonic Wave cooldown and adds a second wave, overwhelming heroes like Phantom Lancer and Chaos Knight.
  • Bloodthorn — amplifies burst on squishy targets (e.g., Phantom Assassin, Drow Ranger) and silences them, preventing escape.

Situational Items

  • Linken’s Sphere — blocks single‑target disables from Keeper of the Light’s Will‑of‑the‑Wisp or Chen’s Holy Persuasion.
  • Scythe of Vyse — extra crowd control against mobile heroes like Bounty Hunter.
  • Shiva’s Guard — armor and AOE slow help against physical‑heavy lineups such as Chaos Knight.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects targeted spells (useful vs. Dark Seer’s Surge) and provides armor.
  • Manta Style — dispels silences and gives extra mobility against Treant Protector’s Leech Seed.

Common Mistakes

  • Blinking in without Shadow Strike: New players often Blink straight into a fight, losing the initial burst and taking unnecessary damage.
  • Over‑using Sonic Wave in team fights: Casting it without proper positioning lets tanky heroes survive and the wave gets wasted on creeps.
  • Neglecting vision: Failing to ward early leaves you vulnerable to Chen’s early rotations and Dark Seer’s split pushes.
  • Itemizing for damage only: Skipping defensive items like BKB or Eul’s makes you an easy target for the listed counters (Keeper of the Light, Treant Protector, etc.).

FAQ

Is Queen of Pain good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 46.3 % win rate across nearly 388 k recent ranked games, she remains a viable mid‑lane carry, especially against squishy heroes like Phantom Lancer and Drow Ranger where she posts a 58‑67 % win rate.

What lane does Queen of Pain play?

Queen of Pain is typically played in the mid lane as a solo core. Her early burst from Shadow Strike and Scream of Pain lets her dominate the lane and transition quickly to roams.

Who counters Queen of Pain?

The toughest matchups are Keeper of the Light, Treant Protector, Chen, Dark Seer, Bounty Hunter, and Pugna, where her win rates dip into the mid‑30s to low‑40s percent. These heroes either out‑scale her burst, provide strong disables, or heal through her damage.
queen-of-pain.counterHtml:
Queen of Pain is a high‑mobility burst mage whose strength lies in quickly jumping onto squishy targets, applying Shadow Strike, and detonating a massive Sonic Wave. The key to shutting her down is denying her the ability to land that initial burst and forcing her into prolonged fights where her damage falls off.

Why These Heroes Beat Queen of Pain

Keeper of the Light

Keeper’s Mana Leak constantly saps QOP’s mana, limiting the number of Sonic Waves and Blink‑initiated combos she can pull off. His Illuminate provides long‑range poke that forces QOP to stay back, and Spirit Form grants spell immunity during the crucial window of her Sonic Wave. Tip: Time Spirit Form just as she begins her Blink‑in‑Sonic Wave combo to nullify the burst.

Treant Protector

Treant’s Nature’s Grasp and Leech Seed create a zone that heavily slows QOP, negating the advantage of her Blink mobility. The Living Armor on Treant’s tower or on an allied hero also mitigates the damage from Sonic Wave and Scream of Pain. Tip: Position a Tree of the False Wills near the lane to block QOP’s line of sight and force her into melee range where her burst is less effective.

Chen

Chen’s Penitence slows QOP’s movement and attack speed, making it harder for her to chase or escape. His Hand of God provides a global heal that can offset the damage from Sonic Wave, while his Holy Persuasion can pull a neutral creep into lane to tank QOP’s burst and apply constant pressure. Tip: Use Penitence right after QOP’s Blink to keep her chained and force a trade on your creep.

Dark Seer

Dark Seer’s Ion Shell adds a damage‑over‑time aura that punishes QOP’s melee approach and synergizes with his Surge to grant allies massive speed, out‑pacing her Blink. Vacuum can pull QOP out of her Sonic Wave’s line, breaking her positioning. Tip: Cast Surge on a teammate just before QOP blinks in, then follow with Vacuum to disrupt her combo.

Bounty Hunter

Bounty Hunter’s Shuriken Toss provides reliable ranged damage and a slow that hampers QOP’s Blink escape routes. Track reveals her location, preventing her from safely Blink‑in from fog of war, and the bounty gold forces her to play more cautiously. Tip: Keep Track active and position yourself near the rune spots where QOP is likely to Blink, forcing a 1v1 where you can out‑trade her.

Drafting Against Queen of Pain

  • Prioritize heroes with strong spell‑immune ultimates or long‑range poke (e.g., Keeper of the Light, Dark Seer).
  • Choose heroes that apply consistent slows or movement‑speed debuffs.
  • Pick global heal or sustain tools to offset her burst (Chen, Treant).
  • Avoid picking multiple high‑mobility melee cores that QOP can pick off early.

Laning Against Queen of Pain

  • Trade when her Shadow Strike is on cooldown; her damage spikes are then minimal.
  • Harass with ranged attacks or abilities that force her to use Blink defensively.
  • Punish her early after she uses Blink to escape—she is vulnerable while the cooldown is up.
  • Keep a creep wave near your tower to block her line of sight and limit her ability to land Sonic Wave from range.

Itemizing Against Queen of Pain

Ghost Scepter — grants temporary magic immunity, nullifying Sonic Wave and Scream of Pain bursts.
Eul's Cyclone — disables QOP, removes her Blink, and gives you time to reposition or force a kill.
Black King Bar — provides spell immunity through her magic damage, allowing you to stay in fights longer.
Heaven's Halberd — disarms QOP, preventing her from using Shadow Strike and Sonic Wave while you close the distance.

razor.name: Razor
razor.guideHtml:
Razor is a durable, lane‑dominating carry who excels at draining enemy damage and turning fights into attrition wars. On patch 7.41 his overall pub win rate sits at 50.0% over 218,646 ranked matches, placing him solidly in the middle of the hero tier list. He thrives when he can lock down a single target with Static Link and out‑scale most mid‑lane heroes, though several hard counters keep his win rate modest.

How to Play Razor

Laning Phase

  • Use Plasma Field early to harass and secure last hits; the damage and slow scale with distance, making it ideal for zoning melee opponents.
  • Initiate Static Link on the enemy off‑lane hero as soon as you have 2‑3 levels; the link grants you damage while you can still move and farm.
  • When the enemy tries to break the link with spells, Storm Surge will trigger, adding extra burst and a slow that helps you maintain lane control.
  • Prioritize a Tango + Healing Salve and a Stout Shield against harass from heroes like Viper or Shadow Fiend, whose early damage can outpace your link sustain.
  • Against hard‑lane matchups such as Treant Protector or Terrorblade, play conservatively and look for safe farm; avoid prolonged fights until you have a few items.

Mid Game

  • Hit level 6 and start using Eye of the Storm to finish off low‑HP enemies in team fights; its armor‑reduction synergizes with your damage.
  • Aim for the first 2‑3 kills on a single high‑damage hero (e.g., Phoenix or Huskar) to cripple their output and force them to buy defensive items.
  • Split push with Plasma Field to clear creep waves quickly while maintaining map pressure; transition to group fights when your Static Link can lock a core enemy.
  • Secure Roshan after you have a Mekansm or Pipe to mitigate its burst, using your link to steal damage from the boss.

Late Game

  • Win condition: lock the enemy’s primary damage dealer with Static Link and force them to die to your combined right‑click and Eye of the Storm damage.
  • Position near the front line but keep a safe distance; Storm Surge will punish any initiators that dive you, while your link provides survivability.
  • Losing the game usually stems from over‑extending without vision, allowing hard counters like Phoenix or Nature’s Prophet to pick you off before you can link them.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango + Healing Salve — sustain against early harass.
  • Stout Shield — mitigates damage from melee harass and reduces the impact of Storm Surge triggers.
  • Iron Branch ×2 — cheap stats and can be later built into Magic Wand.
  • Faerie Fire — emergency burst damage to finish a low‑HP opponent when the link is active.

Core Items

  • Power Treads — attack speed for faster link damage and flexibility between strength/intelligence.
  • Mekansm — provides team heal and armor, crucial for surviving burst from Phoenix and Huskar.
  • Black King Bar — guarantees uninterrupted Static Link and Eye of the Storm in fights against silences (e.g., Silencer, Disruptor).
  • Satanic — gives lifesteal to offset the damage you take while maintaining the link on high‑damage heroes.

Situational Items

  • Pipe of Insight — against magic‑heavy lineups like Phoenix and Warlock.
  • Shiva’s Guard — armor and AoE slow to counter Terrorblade and Nature’s Prophet split‑pushes.
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Eye of the Storm to a larger, faster‑casting storm, useful when you need to melt tanky heroes.
  • Heart of Tarrasque — for extreme durability against burst heroes such as Doom and Huskar.
  • Linken’s Sphere — blocks single‑target disables that can break your Static Link (e.g., Lion, Shadow Shaman).

Common Mistakes

  • Linking too early without sufficient health – the link transfers damage to you; low HP makes you an easy kill.
  • Using Plasma Field offensively without checking enemy positioning – the wave can hurt allies and waste mana if no enemy is caught.
  • Failing to transition to team fights after hitting level 6 – Razor’s late‑game power hinges on Eye of the Storm and sustained link damage.
  • Over‑extending in lane against hard counters – matchups like Treant Protector and Terrorblade require safe farming until you have core items.

FAQ

Is Razor good in the current patch?

Razor sits at a 50.0% win rate on patch 7.41, making him a solid but not dominant pick. He shines against heroes he can link early (e.g., Crystal Maiden, Silencer) but struggles versus high‑mobility or burst heroes like Phoenix and Doom.

What lane does Razor play?

Razor is typically played in the safe lane as a carry, using Static Link to secure the lane and transition into mid‑game fights. He can also be flexed to the off‑lane in solo queue when a strong lane partner is needed.

Who counters Razor?

The toughest matchups are Treant Protector, Terrorblade, Phoenix, Huskar, Nature’s Prophet, and Doom, where Razor’s win rates dip below 41% (e.g., 28.8% vs. Treant). These heroes either out‑scale his damage, break his link, or burst him before he can activate his core abilities.
razor.counterHtml:
Razor’s strength lies in his ability to sap damage with Static Link and punish melee heroes with his scaling Plasma Field. To shut him down you must deny him the sustained fights he thrives on, burst his link early, and force him into unfavorable trades where his damage‑steal is ineffective.

Why These Heroes Beat Razor

Treant Protector

Treant’s Nature’s Guise grants near‑instant invisibility and a burst of movement speed, allowing him to dodge Razor’s Plasma Field and disengage before Static Link can fully charge. Use the early Leech Seed to harass Razor’s health while staying out of his link range.
Tip: Initiate with Overgrowth once Razor’s link is broken; the massive root prevents him from re‑establishing the link and forces a disengage.

Terrorblade

Terrorblade’s Reflection creates a mirror image that mirrors Razor’s attacks, instantly returning the stolen damage back to Razor and breaking the Static Link’s damage flow. His Metamorphosis gives long‑range pure damage that bypasses Razor’s armor‑reduction from Eye of the Storm.
Tip: Push early with Sunder after a successful link break to flip Razor’s health advantage and force a retreat.

Phoenix

Phoenix’s Sun Ray deals constant pure damage over a large area, out‑pacing the damage Razor can steal with Static Link. Supernova forces Razor to choose between a massive burst of damage or staying out of the fight, nullifying his link’s sustain.
Tip: Time Fire Spirits to hit Razor just as he activates Plasma Field; the additional magic damage stacks with Sun Ray and overwhelms his health pool.

Huskar

Huskar’s Burning Spear scales with his current health, making him increasingly lethal as Razor tries to drain his damage via Static Link. Life Break provides a burst of true damage that Razor cannot mitigate, and the self‑damage component punishes Razor’s focus fire.
Tip: Trade early when Razor’s link is on cooldown; Huskar’s high HP regeneration from Inner Fire lets him survive Razor’s initial burst and retaliate.

Nature’s Prophet

Nature’s Prophet’s Teleportation lets him avoid Razor’s Plasma Field entirely and reposition to safe jungle spots, breaking the link’s continuity. His Sprout can trap Razor, preventing him from moving while the link is active, and Wrath of Nature deals global pure damage that ignores Razor’s armor reduction.
Tip: Use Teleport to a high‑ground warded area and force Razor to chase; the extra distance weakens his link’s damage transfer.

Drafting Against Razor

  • Prioritize heroes with strong burst or true damage (e.g., Huskar, Terrorblade, Phoenix).
  • Pick heroes with reliable invisibility or mobility to dodge Plasma Field (Treant Protector, Nature’s Prophet).
  • Include at least one global or long‑range magic damage source to outpace Razor’s armor‑shredding.
  • Consider bans that remove Razor’s typical lane partners who provide early lane sustain (e.g., Viper, Disruptor).

Laning Against Razor

  • Trade when Razor’s Static Link is on cooldown; his damage steal is nullified.
  • Harass with ranged attacks or spells that force him to use Storm Surge, wasting his defensive lightning proc.
  • Punish his early Plasma Field by staying just outside its radius and using a short‑range stun to break the link.
  • Force Razor into a 1v2 by pulling a support with a hook or stun, making his link ineffective against multiple targets.

Itemizing Against Razor

  • Black King Bar — prevents Razor’s Storm Surge from triggering and blocks the link’s damage transfer.
  • Manta Style — creates illusion copies that split Static Link’s damage, reducing the net loss per hit.
  • Ghost Scepter — makes you ethereal, causing Razor’s Plasma Field and Eye of the Storm to miss, while still allowing you to cast spells.
  • Lotus Orb – reflects Razor’s Static Link and Storm Surge back at him, breaking the link and punishing his aggression.

riki.name: Riki
riki.guideHtml:
Riki remains a high‑impact stealth assassin in the current meta, boasting a 52.0% win rate across 211,402 recent ranked games 【OpenDota July 2026】. His blend of escape, burst damage, and lane‑control makes him a solid pick for carry‑style play, though he still struggles against certain mid‑lane heroes.

How to Play Riki

Laning Phase

  • Use Cloak and Dagger to farm safely while staying invisible; the XP bonus from kills/assists helps you stay ahead in levels.
  • Harass with Blink Strike when you have vision; the instant teleport and bonus damage punish enemy heroes that over‑extend.
  • Deploy Smoke Screen on contested pulls or when the enemy support attempts to harass you; the silence and miss‑chance protect you and set up a quick Backstab.
  • Prioritize farming the enemy off‑lane creep and jungle camps; Riki’s low base damage is mitigated by his Backstab scaling with Agility.
  • Against heroes like Warlock or Shadow Demon (your toughest matchups, win ≈ 33‑37%) play conservatively and look for gank opportunities rather than 1v1 trades.

Mid Game

  • Hit the Backstab damage spike at ~20 Agility (around level 6–7) and start rotating with Smoke Screen + Blink Strike to pick off squishy supports.
  • Secure vision around Roshan and high‑traffic jungle paths; invisibility makes you a natural scout and initiator of Tricks of the Trade ambushes.
  • Group with your team for early Tricks of the Trade fights; the channeled damage and evasion allow you to survive burst from heroes like Queen of Pain (win ≈ 39%).
  • Prioritize taking towers with Backstab on the enemy’s backline; the extra damage accelerates map control.

Late Game

  • Win condition: split‑push and pick off isolated carries using Cloak and Dagger + Blink Strike, then finish with Tricks of the Trade to force team fights.
  • Positioning: stay invisible near enemy high‑ground or behind their front line; avoid obvious entry points where vision can be placed (e.g., wards from Rubick or Windranger).
  • Lose the game if you are caught without Smoke Screen or Blink Strike cooldowns, as enemy burst heroes can quickly eliminate you.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain against harassment in the lane.
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery after early skirmishes.
  • Orb of Venom — adds a slow to help land Blink Strike on targets.
  • Quelling Blade — easier last‑hits on melee creeps.

Core Items

  • Phase Boots — provides mobility for chasing and escaping, plus damage on hit.
  • Diffusal Blade — mana burn and purge help against spell‑heavy heroes like Warlock and Rubick.
  • Black King Bar — essential against heavy magic damage and silences (e.g., Shadow Demon, Queen of Pain).
  • Abyssal Blade — lockdown for fragile carries; synergizes with Backstab burst.

Situational Items

  • Sange and Yasha — extra movement speed and status resistance against disables.
  • Manta Style — dispels silences and provides additional Backstab attacks.
  • Heart of Tarrasque — survivability when you’re the primary front‑line threat.
  • Butterfly — evasion against physical burst from heroes like Windranger.
  • Linken’s Sphere – blocks single‑target spells from Rubick or Queen of Pain.
  • Shadow Blade – alternative invisibility for deeper split‑pushing when Cloak and Dagger is on cooldown.

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑extending without vision – Riki’s invisibility is useless if the enemy has wards; always scout before using Blink Strike.
  • Neglecting Smoke Screen – many players forget to cast it before a gank, losing the silence and miss‑chance that protect you.
  • Relying solely on Backstab – without Agility items, damage falls off; transition to Phase Boots/Diffusal early.
  • Trying to 1v1 tough matchups – against Warlock, Dawnbreaker, Shadow Demon, etc., avoid direct fights and look for pick‑offs instead.

FAQ

Is Riki good in the current patch?

Yes. Riki enjoys a solid 52.0% win rate in recent ranked matches, making him a reliable pick for carry or escape roles despite a few tough lane matchups.

What lane does Riki play?

Riki is typically played in the safe lane (carry) where he can farm with Cloak and Dagger and use Blink Strike to harass the enemy off‑lane.

Who counters Riki?

Why These Heroes Beat Riki

Warlock

Warlock’s Fatal Bonds instantly links Riki to his allies, turning any burst from Blink Strike into damage on multiple targets and making Riki’s back‑stab less rewarding. His Shackles provide a long‑duration, hard disable that breaks invisibility and forces Riki to stay in place. Tip: Drop a Shadow Word on the bonded ally to keep the lane pressured while Warlock’s Chaotic Offering supplies vision and additional disables.

Dawnbreaker

Starbreaker grants a brief stun and a large area of effect that reveals invisible units, instantly canceling Riki’s Smoke Screen and Tricks of the Trade. Her Celestial Hammer provides a reliable slow and extra damage that punishes Riki’s melee bursts. Tip: Time a Starbreaker right after Riki’s Blink Strike to lock him down before he can retreat into invisibility.

Shadow Demon

Disruption creates a clone of Riki that cannot be targeted by Backstab, forcing him to waste his primary damage source. The subsequent Soul Catcher slows Riki and amplifies incoming damage, making any follow‑up from allies deadly. Tip: Pair Shadow Demon’s Disruption with a teammate’s True Sight (e.g., Sentry Ward) to keep Riki visible after the clone expires.

Queen of Pain

Scream of Pain and Shadow Strike provide burst AoE magic damage that ignores armor and back‑stab scaling, quickly depleting Riki’s health. Her Blink lets her chase Riki into Smoke Screen, and the silence from Scream of Pain prevents him from casting Smoke Screen to escape. Tip: Use Scream of Pain right after you spot Riki’s Smoke Screen to force him out of invisibility and into a kill zone.

Rubick

Rubick’s Telekinesis is a single‑target lift that breaks invisibility and can be comboed into a Null Field‑free stun. His Spell Steal can copy Smoke Screen or Tricks of the Trade, turning Riki’s own tools against him. Tip: Prioritize stealing Smoke Screen early; the silence and miss‑chance cripple Riki’s escape and initiation.

Drafting Against Riki

  • Pick heroes with true sight or long‑range reveals (e.g., Bounty Hunter, Treant Protector).
  • Prioritize hard disables that break invisibility (stuns, silences, lifts).
  • Choose AoE magic damage sources that ignore armor and back‑stab scaling.
  • Consider heroes with built‑in vision on spells (Dawnbreaker’s Starbreaker, Shadow Demon’s Disruption).

Laning Against Riki

  • Keep a Sentry Ward or Gem of True Sight on the lane to deny his invisibility.
  • Trade when Riki is out of Smoke Screen cooldown; his burst is far weaker without the silence.
  • Punish missed Blink Strike attempts with a quick counter‑attack or a stun.
  • Force him to use Backstab on creeps by pulling the lane equilibrium; this wastes his primary damage.

Itemizing Against Riki

Force Staff — lets you escape his Blink Strike or push him out of Smoke Screen range.
Glimmer Cape (enemy) — denies his back‑stab by granting you temporary invisibility that he cannot see.
Abyssal Blade — hard stun that breaks invisibility and prevents him from using Tricks of the Trade to dodge.
Lotus Orb — reflects targeted disables back onto Riki, turning his own stuns against him.

ringmaster.name: Ringmaster
ringmaster.guideHtml:
Ringmaster is a versatile support‑style hero that blends crowd‑control, escape tools, and burst damage. On patch 7.41 his overall win rate sits at 47.6% across 199,179 ranked games, placing him in the middle of the meta—strong enough to pick but still vulnerable to several core supports.

How to Play Ringmaster

Laning Phase

  • Use Tame the Beasts early to harass enemy off‑laners; the fear can force them to miss last‑hits and give you lane control.
  • Pair Escape Act with a support tower or a lane‑creep to give yourself or your carry phased movement and magic resistance when the enemy initiates.
  • Drop Impalement Arts on a low‑HP enemy to apply bleed; the damage‑over‑time synergizes with your lane partner’s damage.
  • When the enemy has strong lane sustain (e.g., Chen, Dazzle), prioritize stacking Souvenir Slot on kills/assists to keep your gold flow.
  • Keep Spotlight ready for early invisibility checks; a quick sweep can reveal hidden pulls from heroes like Treant Protector.

Mid Game

  • Wheel of Wonder becomes a primary team‑fight initiator; roll it into the enemy’s positioning to knock aside and apply the -50 % slow.
  • Combine Spotlight with Tame the Beasts: the fear makes enemies walk into the light, increasing miss‑chance and making them easy targets for your damage.
  • Look for Escape Act ganks: box an allied hero into the box, then pop out near the enemy’s backline for a surprise engage.
  • Prioritize objectives when you have a Souvenir Slot advantage; the extra gold lets you transition to core items faster than the enemy support.

Late Game

  • Win condition: lock down high‑damage carries with Tame the Beasts + Spotlight, then follow up with Wheel of Wonder damage over time.
  • Position near the front of your team but stay behind a frontline creep; the box from Escape Act gives you a safety net if you get focused.
  • Avoid being the sole initiator against heroes with strong anti‑magic or burst (e.g., Alchemist, Grimstroke); without proper items you’ll die before your crowd‑control lands.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane.
  • Healing Salve — emergency health.
  • Observer Ward — vision for early ganks.
  • Sentry Ward — counter invisible supports (e.g., Dark Willow).
  • Iron Branch ×2 — cheap stat and can be later built into a Magic Wand.

Core Items

  • Arcane Boots — mana pool for frequent Tame the Beasts and Spotlight casts.
  • Glimmer Cape — adds extra magic resistance and can be used on yourself or an ally inside Escape Act.
  • Aghanim’s Shard (if available) — upgrades Impalement Arts to apply a stronger bleed.
  • Force Staff — synergizes with Escape Act to reposition allies or escape after a box.

Situational Items

  • Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — extra disable and self‑save; great against Alchemist’s Acid Spray.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target spells; useful versus Chen’s Penitence.
  • Ghost Scepter — protects you from right‑click burst from Huskar or Terrorblade.
  • Aether Lens — increases cast range of all abilities, especially Wheel of Wonder.
  • Scythe of Vyse — adds a hard‑lock on heroes that counter your fear (e.g., Grimstroke).

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑channeling Tame the Beasts – staying too long in the channel leaves you vulnerable to burst and reduces overall damage output.
  • Boxing the wrong target – using Escape Act on a low‑impact ally instead of a high‑damage carry wastes its utility.
  • Ignoring Souvenir Slot – failing to secure kills/assists means you fall behind in gold, making core items hard to reach.
  • Spamming Spotlight without vision – the beam only reveals invisibles; using it blindly wastes mana and cooldown.

FAQ

Is Ringmaster good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 47.6 % win rate on 7.41, Ringmaster is a solid pick, especially against heroes like Dark Willow (62.9 % win) and Skywrath Mage (60.6 % win). He shines in coordinated team fights where his crowd‑control can be layered.

What lane does Ringmaster play?

Ringmaster is most commonly played as a support in the safe lane, pairing with a carry that can benefit from his fear and escape tools. He can also roam to mid lane after the first wave to apply Spotlight and Wheel of Wonder pressure.

Who counters Ringmaster?

The toughest matchups are Alchemist (30.9 % win), Chen (36.4 % win), and Grimstroke (38.2 % win). These heroes either out‑farm Ringmaster or have spells that bypass his fear and box, so building Lotus Orb, Eul’s, or a Ghost Scepter is essential.
ringmaster.counterHtml:
Ringmaster’s toolkit revolves around fear, crowd‑control, and sustained bleed damage, making him a nightmare in prolonged fights and a strong lane bully when he can keep enemies locked down. The key to shutting him down is to deny his channel time, burst him before his bleed stacks, and bring tools that either purge fear or out‑scale his damage over time.

Why These Heroes Beat Ringmaster

Alchemist

Alchemist’s Chemical Rage gives massive health regeneration and damage reduction, allowing him to survive Ringmaster’s fear and bleed while out‑damaging him in extended fights. His Acid Spray also clears the fear field, and Greevil’s Greed provides gold to buy early survivability items.
Tip: Start with a Greevil’s Greed and Acid Spray early; the gold boost lets you buy early Mekansm or Vanguard to further blunt Ringmaster’s damage.

Chen

Chen can sprout a neutral creep to block Ringmaster’s line of sight, preventing the fear from landing, and his Hand of God instantly removes the bleed and fear debuffs. Additionally, his Holy Persuasion gives him a tanky creep that can absorb Ringmaster’s damage while providing lane pressure.
Tip: Use Hand of God right after Ringmaster lands a fear to instantly purge the bleed and reset the fight.

Grimstroke

Grimstroke’s Soul Bind links Ringmaster to an ally, forcing him to choose between damaging both or breaking the link, while Phantom Rush gives a quick escape from the fear zone. His Ink Swell provides burst damage that can kill Ringmaster before his bleed ramps up.
Tip: Cast Soul Bind as soon as Ringmaster begins his channel; the linked damage will often force him to abort the fear.

Dazzle

Dazzle’s Shallow Grave makes Ringmaster’s burst and bleed ineffective, and his Shadow Wave heals through the bleed damage, sustaining allies. Weave also reduces the magic damage from Ringmaster’s Wheel of Wonder.
Tip: Place Shallow Grave on the primary carry before Ringmaster initiates his fear; this forces him to waste his channel on a dead‑end.

Huskar

Huskar’s Burning Spear deals pure damage that bypasses Ringmaster’s magic resistance, and his Life Break can close the distance instantly, interrupting the fear channel. Huskar’s Inner Fire also silences Ringmaster, preventing the use of Spotlight and Wheel of Wonder.
Tip: Initiate with Life Break right after Ringmaster finishes a fear; the stun from Inner Fire will lock him down while his bleed is still low.

Drafting Against Ringmaster

  • Prioritize heroes with strong dispel or purge (e.g., Chen, Dazzle, Oracle).
  • Pick early‑game burst damage heroes who can kill before the bleed stacks (e.g., Lina, Ember Spirit).
  • Include at least one high‑mobility or escape hero to dodge the fear channel (e.g., Anti‑Mage, Puck).
  • Consider heroes with strong lane sustain to survive the early fear harassment (e.g., Treant Protector, Undying).

Laning Against Ringmaster

  • Trade when Ringmaster is channeling Tame the Beasts—the channel leaves him immobile and vulnerable to burst.
  • Harass with ranged attacks or spells before he can land the fear; his damage spikes only after a successful channel.
  • Use creep wave manipulation (pulls, spawns) to block his line of sight and deny the fear’s area of effect.
  • Punish his cooldowns: after he uses Spotlight or Wheel of Wonder, his damage output drops significantly for a few seconds.

Itemizing Against Ringmaster

Mekansm — provides burst heal and armor to offset bleed damage and reduces his overall sustain.
Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — a reliable self‑disable that can interrupt his channel and purge fear.
Black King Bar — grants magic immunity, nullifying Spotlight and Wheel of Wonder while allowing you to close in.
Ghost Scepter — makes you ethereal, preventing physical bleed damage from his daggers.
Aghanim’s Shard (Chen) — upgrades Hand of God to purge fear and bleed instantly.

rubick.name: Rubick
rubick.guideHtml:
Rubick is a versatile support whose strength lies in stealing enemy spells and turning them against the opposition. In the current meta he sits at a 49.2 % win rate across 678,598 ranked games (OpenDota, July 2026), making him a solid pick but not a guaranteed win‑rate hero. His toolkit of disables, damage amplification, and high‑impact stolen ultimates lets him shape team fights from the mid‑lane or safe lane depending on the draft.

How to Play Rubick

Laning Phase

  • Use Fade Bolt to harass and apply the attack/spell damage debuff, especially against right‑click heroes; the bounce can also chip at multiple creeps for lane control.
  • Keep Telekinesis ready to punish aggressive enemy supports or to secure kills on low‑HP heroes; the stun radius scales with the target’s landing spot, so aim for clustered enemies.
  • Prioritize Spell Steal on high‑impact spells (e.g., Lion’s Hex, Shadow Shaman’s Shackles) as soon as the enemy casts them within 1200 range to gain early game advantage.
  • Stack Curiosity by staying within vision of enemy casts; each stack grants extra base damage and slight duration buffs, helping your early harass.
  • Position safely behind your carry when facing lane opponents with strong early disables (e.g., Earth Spirit) to avoid being locked down before you can react with Telekinesis.

Mid Game

  • Roam with Telekinesis + Fade Bolt combo to create pick‑offs; the stun from Telekinesis plus the damage debuff can quickly eliminate squishy targets.
  • Look for opportunities to steal ultimates (e.g., Sven’s Storm Hammer, Magnus’ Reverse Polarity) and use them in team fights; this is Rubick’s primary power spike.
  • Maintain vision around key objectives; Rubick’s Arcane Supremacy gives increased cast range, allowing you to cast stolen spells from safer distances.
  • When your team has a lead, use Fade Bolt on clustered enemies to amplify your damage and set up your allies’ follow‑up.

Late Game

  • Focus on win conditions: stealing game‑ending ultimates (e.g., Brewmaster’s Primal Split, Lycan’s Shapeshift) and using Telekinesis to isolate high‑value targets.
  • Position behind front‑line heroes; a misplaced Telekinesis can be disastrous if you get caught by enemy burst (e.g., Bane’s Fiend’s Grip).
  • Avoid over‑extending without vision; late‑game Rubick is vulnerable to burst heroes and silences that can prevent you from stealing spells.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane.
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery after early harass.
  • Observer Ward — vision to spot enemy rotations and protect your Telekinesis.
  • Iron Branch ×2 — cheap stats and can be later built into Magic Wand.

Core Items

  • Arcane Boots — provides mana for frequent spell casts and can be upgraded to Aghanim’s Shard for additional utility.
  • Force Staff — extra mobility to reposition yourself or allies for Telekinesis combos.
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — reduces cooldown on Spell Steal and grants a second charge, dramatically increasing spell‑steal uptime.
  • Ghost Scepter — essential against right‑click heavy heroes (e.g., Lone Druid, Lycan) who currently give Rubick low win rates.

Situational Items

  • Eul's Scepter of Divinity — additional disable and self‑save against burst (useful vs. Bane, Leshrac).
  • Glimmer Cape — provides magic resistance and invisibility to survive initiation from Earth Spirit or Broodmother.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target spells; good against heroes with strong disables like Earth Spirit.
  • Scythe of Vyse — extra hard‑disable when you lack reliable stun options.
  • Octarine Core — reduces cooldowns on all abilities, especially valuable if you’re frequently stealing ultimates.

Common Mistakes

  • Casting Telekinesis on a single target when a clustered enemy group is present, wasting the stun radius.
  • Stealing low‑impact spells (e.g., minor abilities) instead of saving Spell Steal for game‑changing ultimates.
  • Over‑extending without vision, leading to easy kills by burst heroes such as Bane or Earth Spirit.
  • Neglecting Fade Bolt’s debuff, which is crucial for reducing enemy damage output throughout fights.

FAQ

Is Rubick good in the current patch?

Yes. Rubick sits at a 49.2 % win rate in recent ranked matches (OpenDota, July 2026), making him a viable support pick with strong pick‑off and team‑fight potential, especially when you can steal high‑impact ultimates.

What lane does Rubick play?

Rubick is most commonly played in the safe lane as a support, but he can also be effective in the mid lane when the draft lacks a dedicated mid‑laner and you need early spell‑steal pressure.

Who counters Rubick?

Heroes that can lock him down before he casts Telekinesis or Spell Steal—such as Earth Spirit, Bane, and Leshrac—are his toughest matchups (win rates around 40‑43 %). High‑burst right‑click heroes like Lone Druid and Lycan also pressure him heavily, so building Ghost Scepter or staying behind front‑liners is essential.
