The key to shutting him down is denying him the window to steal spells and forcing him into fights where his low base damage and limited mobility are liabilities.

Why These Heroes Beat Rubick

Lone Druid

Lone Druid’s Spirit Bear has a massive health pool and can out‑tank Rubick’s Telekinesis stun, while the hero’s high mobility with Savage Roar and Ravage forces Rubick to stay on the backline where he can’t land a steal. Tip: Keep the Bear alive and use its damage to punish Rubick’s low damage output during the early laning phase.

Earth Spirit

Earth Spirit’s Geomagnetic Grip and Stone Remnants create constant movement and crowd control that interrupt Rubick’s channel on Telekinesis and make his positioning predictable. Tip: Use early Rolling Boulder to block Rubick’s line of sight, denying him the chance to see enemy casts and steal spells.

Broodmother

Broodmother’s spiderlings and Spin Web give her lane dominance and vision control, making it hard for Rubick to land Telekinesis without being caught in the web’s stun. Tip: Push the lane aggressively; the constant pressure forces Rubick to waste mana on Telekinesis rather than stealing valuable spells.

Lycan

Lycan’s Summon Wolves and Feral Impulse provide burst damage that can quickly kill Rubick before he can cast Telekinesis, while Shapeshift gives him high mobility to dodge spell steals. Tip: Initiate with wolves to force Rubick into a defensive position and punish his low survivability.

Leshrac

Leshrac’s Lightning Storm and Split Earth have large AoE damage and stun, overwhelming Rubick’s limited health and preventing him from safely using Telekinesis. Tip: Chain Lightning Storm into Split Earth when Rubick attempts a steal to lock him down and secure a kill.

Drafting Against Rubick

  • Prioritize heroes with strong early burst or lockdown (e.g., Earth Spirit, Leshrac).
  • Pick mobile heroes that can dodge Telekinesis and stay out of Rubick’s 1200‑range sight.
  • Include lane‑dominant heroes that can pressure Rubick’s farm (Lone Druid, Lycan).
  • Ban heroes that give Rubick high‑impact stolen spells (e.g., high‑damage ultimates).

Laning Against Rubick

  • Harass him with ranged damage; Rubick’s low base attack makes him vulnerable.
  • Force him to use Telekinesis defensively by zoning him away from creep equilibrium.
  • Keep vision on Rubick’s cast range; deny him line‑of‑sight to limit Spell Steal opportunities.
  • Trade when his mana is low—without Telekinesis he cannot threaten you or steal spells.

Itemizing Against Rubick

Ghost Scepter — blocks Rubick’s Telekinesis and any stolen physical spells.
Eul’s Scepter — provides a self‑cyclone to dodge Telekinesis and a slow to interrupt his spell steal.
Black King Bar — grants magic immunity, nullifying Telekinesis stun and any stolen magical ultimates.
Force Staff — creates distance instantly, preventing Rubick from landing Telekinesis or getting within steal range.

sand-king.name: Sand King
sand-king.guideHtml:
Sand King remains a solid Initiator/Disabler in the current 7.41 meta, offering high burst damage and crowd‑control. With a 48.3% win rate across 158,935 recent ranked games, he sits around the middle of the hero spectrum—neither a top‑tier pick nor a clear ban, but a reliable pick when his strengths align with team composition.

How to Play Sand King

Laning Phase

  • Use Burrowstrike on the first wave to secure early CS and apply the Caustic Finale poison, forcing enemy supports to play cautiously.
  • Pair Sand Storm with a defensive tower dive; the invisibility lets you scout and harass without taking tower damage.
  • Against hard‑lane matchups like Warlock or Phoenix (Sand King win ≈ 34%), prioritize safe farming and only engage when you have a clear stun‑combo on a lone enemy.
  • Stack the creep wave early and use Stinger on the stacked wave to maximize damage and spread Caustic Finale, especially effective versus melee heroes.
  • Keep an eye on enemy Alchemist or Abaddon (win ≈ 38%); their high HP makes early burst less effective, so focus on zoning rather than killing.

Mid Game

  • Hit level 6 and look for Epicenter rotations; the 2‑second cast point can be mitigated by using Burrowstrike to close distance while your teammates provide vision.
  • Aim for objectives where you can land Epicenter on clustered enemies—Roshan, mid‑lane towers, or team fights around the jungle.
  • Power spike: 2‑item core (e.g., Blink Dagger + Aghanim’s Scepter) lets you initiate from unexpected angles, turning the 2‑second channel into a surprise.
  • Prioritize ganking lanes that lack strong disengage (e.g., Templar Assassin, Void Spirit – Sand King win ≈ 58‑59%) to snowball your lead.

Late Game

  • Win condition: land a clean Epicenter in team fights while staying invisible in Sand Storm to avoid being focused; the damage scales with enemy max health, making it deadly against tankier heroes.
  • Positioning: stay just outside enemy vision, using Burrowstrike to slip in, then Sand Storm to disappear while the combo resolves.
  • Losing the game often comes from over‑committing Epicenter without vision; enemy Lion or Pudge can easily catch you with a stun or hook if you’re caught out of position (Sand King win ≈ 57‑39% vs those heroes).

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane, especially against poke from Warlock or Phoenix.
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery after early skirmishes.
  • Observer Ward — vision to safely land Burrowstrike on enemy supports.
  • Iron Branch ×2 — cheap stat boost and can later be used for Magic Wand.

Core Items

  • Blink Dagger — primary initiation tool; pairs with Burrowstrike for instant gap‑close.
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — reduces Epicenter cooldown and adds a fourth pulse, dramatically increasing team‑fight damage.
  • Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — provides additional disable and a way to set up Epicenter without being interrupted.

Situational Items

  • Black King Bar — essential against heavy magical burst from Warlock or Phoenix.
  • Shiva’s Guard — armor and AoE slow synergize with Epicenter, great versus high‑HP heroes like Alchemist.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target spells; useful against Pudge’s hook or Lion’s stun.
  • Gleipnir — extra slow and burst; works well when you need to lock down mobile heroes like Ursa.
  • Force Staff — escape tool when you’re caught out of Sand Storm or need to reposition for a follow‑up.

Common Mistakes

  • Casting Epicenter without vision – enemies can bait the channel and kill you before the first pulse lands.
  • Overusing Sand Storm offensively – the invisibility ends when you leave the storm, leaving you vulnerable to counter‑initiations.
  • Ignoring Caustic Finale scaling – failing to stack creeps or target high‑HP heroes reduces the true damage potential of your combos.
  • Relying on early burst against tanky heroes – against Alchemist, Abaddon, or Luna, focus on zone control and pick‑offs rather than straight kills.

FAQ

Is Sand King good in the current patch?

Yes. Sand King sits at a 48.3% win rate in recent ranked matches, making him a viable pick. His burst initiation and scaling damage from Epicenter keep him relevant, especially against heroes he counters well (e.g., Underlord, Muerta).

What lane does Sand King play?

Sand King is typically played as an off‑lane (solo) or as a support in the safe lane. The off‑lane lets you farm while looking for early Burrowstrike ganks; as a support you can provide vision and early disables for your core.

Who counters Sand King?

Heroes with strong disables and long‑range poke—Warlock, Phoenix, and Pudge—have the lowest win rates against him (33‑39%). Vision‑heavy lineups and heroes with reliable saves (e.g., Abaddon’s Aphotic Shield) also make his initiations risky.
sand-king.counterHtml:
Sand King’s burst damage, crowd‑control, and the poison‑explosion from Caustic Finale make him a nightmare in tight team fights and gank‑heavy lanes. The quickest way to neutralize him is to pick heroes that can either out‑scale his early aggression or outright deny his core combos before he lands Burrowstrike and Epicenter.

Why These Heroes Beat Sand King

Warlock

Warlock’s Fatal Bonds instantly links Sand King to his allies, turning the Sand King + Epicenter combo into self‑damage for the entire enemy team. Coupled with Shackles and a well‑timed Chaotic Offering stun, Warlock can completely shut down Sand King’s initiation. Tip: Drop a Ghost‑Ship right after you see Sand King start his Burrowstrike to catch him in the stun and force a costly death.

Phoenix

Phoenix’s Supernova provides a large, invulnerable bubble that forces Sand King to waste his Burrowstrike and Epicenter on a harmless unit. The Sun Ray heal also offsets the poison damage from Caustic Finale, making Phoenix hard to kill in prolonged fights. Tip: Position Supernova near the center of the fight; Sand King’s AoE damage will hit the bubble instead of your heroes.

Luna

Luna’s Moon Glaives and Eclipse apply massive magical damage that bypasses Sand King’s armor and the physical damage reduction from his Sand Storm invisibility. The constant cleave punishes Sand King’s low health pool, and Luna’s Lucent Beam can stun him during Burrowstrike, interrupting the stun lock. Tip: Save Lucent Beam for the moment Sand King surfaces from Burrowstrike to lock him out of his combo.

Alchemist

Alchemist’s Acid Spray and Unstable Concoction deliver burst magic damage that scales with Sand King’s health, quickly shrinking his survivability. The Chemical Rage buff gives Alchemist massive HP and damage reduction, allowing him to tank Epicenter and stay alive to counter‑engage. Tip: Use Chemical Rage before a known Sand King engage; the increased HP pool makes Epicenter’s damage negligible.

Abaddon

Abaddon’s Aphotic Shield can absorb the damage from Sand King’s Burrowstrike and Epicenter, and the shield’s explosion deals pure damage back to Sand King, punishing his aggression. Borrowed Time grants Abaddon temporary invulnerability, rendering Caustic Finale’s death‑explosions harmless. Tip: Keep a shield active on your core carries; when Sand King dives, the shield will both block his burst and retaliate.

Drafting Against Sand King

  • Prioritize heroes with strong magical burst or shield mechanics (e.g., Warlock, Phoenix, Abaddon).
  • Choose heroes with reliable disables that can interrupt Burrowstrike (e.g., Lucent Beam, Shackles).
  • Favor tanky or HP‑scaling heroes that can survive Epicenter (Alchemist, Bristleback).
  • Avoid picking multiple melee initiators that synergize with Sand King’s AoE damage.

Laning Against Sand King

  • Harass him early with ranged attacks; Sand King’s low early HP makes him vulnerable before he gets Burrowstrike cooldown.
  • Trade when his Caustic Finale is on cooldown; his poison explosion is a key damage source.
  • Force him to use Sand Storm defensively; the invisibility gives you a window to push the lane while he is hidden.
  • Punish any missed Burrowstrike by following up with a stun or burst damage before he can reposition.

Itemizing Against Sand King

Glimmer Cape — grants magic immunity, nullifying the damage from Epicenter and the death‑explosion from Caustic Finale.
Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — cyclone can lift Sand King out of his Burrowstrike and delay Epicenter, buying time for your team.
Black King Bar — blocks the magical damage of Epicenter and the stun from Burrowstrike, allowing you to stay active in fights.
Mekansm / Guardian Greaves — provides burst healing and armor that mitigates the physical damage from Burrowstrike and Stinger.

shadow-demon.name: Shadow Demon
shadow-demon.guideHtml:
Shadow Demon is a utility‑heavy support whose toolkit revolves around disruption, damage amplification, and strong lane‑control with his poison. In the current 7.41 meta he sits at a 44.6% win rate across 84,987 ranked games, making him a solid but not dominant pick. His strengths shine against illusion‑based heroes and in games where vision control and burst damage are paramount.

How to Play Shadow Demon

Laning Phase

  • Disruption on a low‑HP enemy (or your carry) to force a short banishment, then immediately follow with Shadow Poison on the target’s retreat path; the poison will still hit the banished unit when it returns.
  • Pair Disseminate with a lane ally’s right‑click damage (e.g., a support with Vengeful Spirit or a Lifestealer) to spread damage to nearby creeps and amplify lane harassment.
  • Use Demonic Cleanse on yourself or your carry after a Disruption to remove silences and give a burst of healing, preventing early tower dives.
  • Prioritize stacking Menace on the enemy off‑lane hero; the extra damage taken synergizes with Shadow Poison Release and any subsequent burst from your core.
  • Against hard‑counters like Zeus or Monkey King, keep a Magic Stick and Observer Wards to anticipate their spells and avoid being baited into a bad Disruption.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 6: Disruption now creates two high‑damage illusions; look for pick‑offs on squishy heroes (e.g., Phantom Lancer, Medusa) who lack blink.
  • Roam with Disseminate + Shadow Poison to amplify damage on team fights; the 675‑range spread can turn a 2‑v‑2 skirmish into a 4‑v‑4 advantage.
  • Secure vision around Roshan and high‑ground jungle; a well‑timed Disruption on an enemy attempting to take Roshan can force a reset and give your team a numbers advantage.
  • When your core has Demon Edge or Divine Rapier, use Demonic Purge to strip their buffs (e.g., Alchemist’s Greevil's Greed) and slow them for follow‑up damage.

Late Game

  • Win condition: Use Disruption on the enemy carry during the final push, then instantly Shadow Poison Release to burst them down while your team focuses the remaining heroes.
  • Positioning: Stay behind your front line; you are extremely vulnerable to burst from Naga Siren, Alchemist, and Beastmaster, the toughest match‑ups (win rates ~40‑43%).
  • Losing the game: Overcommitting Disruption without vision can give the enemy team a free pick, especially against heroes with strong anti‑magic (e.g., Zeus).

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in the lane.
  • Healing Salve — emergency health for you or your carry after a failed Disruption.
  • Observer Ward — early vision to protect against ganks from high‑mobility heroes.
  • Sentry Ward — detect invisible threats like Naga Siren’s Song of the Siren.

Core Items

  • Tranquil Boots — mobility and constant HP regen for staying on the map.
  • Aghanim’s Shard — upgrades Disruption to create stronger illusions, increasing burst potential.
  • Glimmer Cape — defensive tool against burst heroes (Zeus, Monkey King) and to save allies after a Disruption.
  • Force Staff — reposition allies for a clean Disruption or to escape after a failed engage.

Situational Items

  • Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — extra disable and a way to set up Disruption combos.
  • Ghost Scepter — against right‑click heavy carries like Phantom Lancer and Medusa.
  • Lotus Orb — reflect targeted spells (useful vs. Alchemist’s Unstable Concoction).
  • Aeon Disk — survive burst from Naga Siren or Beastmaster when you are the primary focus.
  • Scythe of Vyse — additional hard‑crowd control for late‑game team fights.

Common Mistakes

  • Casting Disruption on the wrong target – using it on a tank instead of a squishy carry wastes the illusion damage.
  • Neglecting vision – without wards, enemies can bait a Disruption into a trap, especially against Zeus and Monkey King.
  • Over‑relying on Shadow Poison – failing to follow up with Disruption or Demonic Purge leaves the damage isolated and easy to dodge.
  • Itemizing too aggressively – buying damage items early (e.g., Aghanim’s Scepter) reduces your sustain and makes you an easy target for early ganks.

FAQ

Is Shadow Demon good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 44.6% win rate on 84,987 recent ranked matches, Shadow Demon remains a viable support, especially against illusion‑heavy heroes like Phantom Lancer (66.1% win rate) and in games that value burst and vision control.

What lane does Shadow Demon play?

Shadow Demon is typically played as a position 5 support in the safe lane, pairing with a carry to provide early harassment and protection via Disruption, Demonic Cleanse, and Menace.

Who counters Shadow Demon?

The toughest match‑ups are against Naga Siren, Alchemist, Zeus, Monkey King, Chen, and Beastmaster, where Shadow Demon’s win rate drops to 40‑44%. These heroes either out‑scale his early impact or can punish his low‑damage, high‑utility playstyle.
shadow-demon.counterHtml:
Shadow Demon’s kit revolves around disruption, damage amplification, and strong lane control through poison and purge. To shut him down you must deny his ability to create and protect illusions, neutralize his damage‑spread mechanics, and force him into a position where his low base damage and lack of escape become liabilities.

Why These Heroes Beat Shadow Demon

Naga Siren

Naga’s Song of the Siren provides a long, global stun that interrupts Shadow Demon’s Disruption and prevents him from safely banishing allies or himself. Her Mirror Image also spawns numerous low‑damage clones that overwhelm Shadow Demon’s illusion‑centric play. Tip: Use Song right after Shadow Demon casts Disruption to catch him mid‑banishment and force a costly early fight.

Alchemist

Alchemist’s Acid Spray and Unstable Concoction apply constant damage that triggers Demonic Purge’s slow and damage‑over‑time, quickly draining Shadow Demon’s health. More importantly, Chemical Rage grants massive HP and magic resistance, making the demon’s amplified damage from Menace and Disseminate far less threatening. Tip: Build Aghanim’s Shard for extra burst; a well‑timed Unstable Concoction can kill Shadow Demon before he can cleanse.

Zeus

Zeus’s Arc Lightning and Lightning Bolt provide pure magical burst that bypasses Shadow Demon’s low armor and can be cast through Disruption’s banishment window. Additionally, Thundergod’s Wrath reveals invisible units, nullifying Shadow Demon’s reliance on hidden illusions. Tip: Use Aghanim’s Scepter to gain Lightning Storm, forcing Shadow Demon to stay on the back‑line where he is vulnerable to burst.

Monkey King

Monkey King’s Tree Dance grants him true‑sight and mobility, allowing him to dodge Disruption and chase down fleeing Shadow Demon. His Jingu Mastery builds damage quickly, punishing the demon’s low base attack, while Wukong’s Command creates a zone where Shadow Demon’s Disruption cannot be safely used. Tip: Initiate with Boundless Strike right after Shadow Demon’s Disruption ends to capitalize on his brief vulnerability.

Chen

Chen’s Holy Persuasion can convert neutral creeps into allies that soak damage from Shadow Demon’s poison and provide vision, limiting the demon’s ability to safely farm. His Hand of God offers a global heal that counters Demonic Cleanse’s timing, keeping his cores alive through Shadow Demon’s burst. Tip: Keep a creep wave near your lane; the extra units will absorb poison stacks and force Shadow Demon to waste Disruption on non‑hero targets.

Drafting Against Shadow Demon

  • Prioritize heroes with long‑range stuns or silences (e.g., Lion, Silencer) to interrupt Disruption.
  • Pick high‑burst magic damage heroes that can kill Shadow Demon before he can cleanse.
  • Include strong lane‑dominant heroes who can out‑farm his low early damage.
  • Consider heroes with true‑sight or invisibility detection to negate his illusion reliance.

Laning Against Shadow Demon

  • Trade when his Shadow Poison is on cooldown; his damage output drops sharply.
  • Harass him early before he gets a Soul Catcher or Aghanim’s Shard, as his survivability is low.
  • Force him to use Disruption on creeps rather than allies; this wastes his primary utility.
  • Maintain lane equilibrium near your tower to limit his ability to safely banish and create illusions.

Itemizing Against Shadow Demon

Black King Bar — blocks his Disseminate and Menace amplification during team fights.
Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — provides a self‑banishment that out‑ranks Shadow Demon’s Disruption, buying time to reposition.
Glimmer Cape — grants magic immunity, negating poison damage and preventing his damage‑spread from triggering.
Linken’s Sphere – blocks the initial Disruption or Demonic Purge, forcing him to waste cooldowns.

shadow-fiend.name: Shadow Fiend
shadow-fiend.guideHtml:
Shadow Fiend (Nevermore) is a high‑damage mid‑lane carry whose strength comes from stacking souls with Necromastery and unleashing them with Requiem of Souls. On patch 7.41 his overall pub win rate sits at 48.5 % over 638 k recent ranked games, placing him slightly below the meta average but still viable in the right hands.

How to Play Shadow Fiend

Laning Phase

  • Use the three Shadowrazes (short, medium, long) to harass and secure last‑hits; the medium range is the safest for lane control while the long range can punish over‑extended opponents.
  • Prioritize killing creeps quickly to build souls; each soul grants 1.35 damage, so early farm translates directly into lane dominance.
  • When the enemy supports have disables, pull back and let Presence of the Dark Lord apply its armor‑reduction aura to help your mid‑lane partner win trades.
  • Against hard‑kill lane matchups (e.g., Lone Druid, Enigma) play conservatively, rely on Shadowraze to chip health and force them to waste spells.
  • Keep an eye on the Requiem of Souls damage timer; a quick 8‑second Feast of Souls window can let you swing a large soul count for a burst kill if you catch a support out of position.

Mid Game

  • Aim for the 2‑soul threshold (≈270 damage) before committing to fights; this is the sweet spot where your Requiem becomes a decisive team‑fight tool.
  • Take advantage of the 30 % soul loss on death by dying only when you have a comfortable soul buffer (≥15 souls) to minimize net loss.
  • Push split‑push lanes once you have a core item (e.g., Black King Bar or Satanic) and use Shadowraze to quickly clear waves and force rotations.
  • Target the toughest matchups (Lone Druid, Enigma, Alchemist) with Requiem after they have used their ultimates; the armor‑reduction from Presence makes their heroes even more vulnerable.

Late Game

  • Win condition: accumulate 20+ souls and force a Requiem on a clustered enemy team; the damage amplification from each soul line can instantly decide team fights.
  • Position near the front of your team but stay just out of enemy disables; a well‑timed Shadowraze can punish any initiator that jumps on you.
  • Avoid prolonged fights against heroes with strong sustain (e.g., Phoenix, Venomancer) unless you have Black King Bar and a high soul count, as their armor‑reduction and damage‑over‑time can outlast your burst.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain for early lane farming.
  • Healing Salve — emergency health against aggressive supports.
  • Faerie Fire — cheap burst to survive early Shadowraze harass.
  • Observer Ward — vision to avoid ganks while you stack souls.
  • Iron Branch ×2 — cheap stats and can be later used for a Magic Wand.

Core Items

  • Power Treads — attack speed and the ability to toggle between strength for survivability and agility for damage.
  • Black King Bar — essential against disables from Enigma, Phoenix, and Venomancer; guarantees a clean Requiem.
  • Satanic — provides lifesteal to sustain through extended fights once you have a large soul pool.
  • Butterfly — huge agility boost and evasion, crucial against right‑click heavy heroes like Medusa and Morphling.
  • Manta Style — splits your Shadowraze damage and can purge silences from Phoenix’s Sun Ray.

Situational Items

  • Aghanim’s Scepter — increases Requiem soul count to 30, turning you into a true late‑game pusher.
  • Monkey King Bar — counters evasion from heroes like Medusa and Winter Wyvern.
  • Linken’s Sphere – blocks single‑target disables from Lone Druid’s Spirit Bear or Enigma’s Black Hole.
  • Heart of Tarrasque – survivability when you lack BKB and need to stay alive against burst from Alchemist.
  • Scythe of Vyse – additional hard‑disable to lock down mobile heroes such as Monkey King or Night Stalker.
  • Gleipnir – provides an extra slow and AoE stun to complement Requiem against tightly grouped enemies.

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑extending without souls – diving in before reaching ~10 souls wastes your damage advantage and makes you an easy target for ganks.
  • Mis‑timing Shadowrazes – using the long‑range raze when the enemy is out of range leads to missed damage and lost lane control.
  • Neglecting armor reduction – forgetting to position Presence of the Dark Lord near fights reduces the effectiveness of both your razes and Requiem.
  • Item ordering errors – building damage items (e.g., Daedalus) before survivability (BKB, Satanic) often results in early deaths against the toughest matchups (Lone Druid, Enigma).

FAQ

Is Shadow Fiend good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 48.5 % win rate on 638 k recent ranked games, Shadow Fiend is a viable mid‑lane carry. He excels when he can quickly stack souls and has proper BKB timing against disables.

What lane does Shadow Fiend play?

Shadow Fiend is primarily a mid‑lane hero, though he can be flexed to safe‑lane if the draft lacks a strong solo mid. His lane success depends on efficient Shadowraze harass and early soul accumulation.

Who counters Shadow Fiend?

The toughest matchups right now are Lone Druid (32.7 % win), Enigma (33.8 %), and Alchemist (41.1 %). These heroes either out‑farm his souls or provide strong disables that nullify his burst. Vision, BKB, and early soul stacking are key to surviving them.
shadow-fiend.counterHtml:
Shadow Fiend’s threat comes from his massive early‑game burst with three Shadowrazes and the exponential damage boost from Necromastery. The key to shutting him down is denying souls and forcing him into prolonged fights where his damage‑per‑second falls off.

Why These Heroes Beat Shadow Fiend

Lone Druid

Lone Druid’s Spirit Bear provides a durable frontline that can soak the three Shadowrazes while the hero farms souls with Savage Roar and True Form, denying Shadow Fiend the early damage spike. Tip: Keep the Bear near the lane and use Entangling Claw to lock SF before he can stack enough souls.

Enigma

Enigma’s Black Hole forces Shadow Fiend to stay in a single spot, nullifying his mobility and making it impossible to dodge the three razes; the subsequent Midnight Pulse also shreds his low‑armor build. Tip: Pair Enigma with a lane‑partner that can provide early vision (e.g., a support with Dust) to catch SF’s positioning.

Alchemist

Alchemist’s Acid Spray and Unstable Concoction apply constant damage‑over‑time, draining SF’s health faster than the burst from Shadowrazes can compensate, while Chemical Rage gives him the tankiness to survive the initial razes. Tip: Stack Greevil’s Greed early to out‑farm SF’s souls and keep the lane contested.

Phoenix

Phoenix’s Fire Spirits and Sun Ray create persistent AoE damage that forces Shadow Fiend to retreat, while Supernova can instantly remove him from the lane if he over‑extends. Tip: Time Sun Ray to coincide with the moment SF casts his third raze for maximum overlap and armor reduction.

Venomancer

Venomancer’s Venomous Gale and Poison Nova apply heavy damage over time and a strong armor‑reduction aura, directly countering Shadow Fiend’s Presence of the Dark Lord and making his razes less lethal. Tip: Place Venomous Gale on the creep wave just before SF’s razes land to ensure the damage‑over‑time ticks on him.

Drafting Against Shadow Fiend

  • Prioritize heroes with strong AoE silence or stun (e.g., Enigma, Lion) to interrupt his Shadowrazes.
  • Pick tanky initiators that can survive the initial burst and force extended fights (Alchemist, Bristleback).
  • Ban or avoid high‑mobility mid‑laners that can dodge razes and snowball (e.g., Ember Spirit).
  • Include at least one hero with reliable magic damage amplification (Venomancer, Phoenix).

Laning Against Shadow Fiend

  • Harass him before he reaches 6 souls; his damage per raze is minimal early.
  • Use creep equilibrium to force him to over‑extend for last‑hit souls, then punish with disables.
  • Trade when his Requiem of Souls is on cooldown—he loses the armor‑reduction aura and burst potential.
  • Secure early vision (wards or sentry) to anticipate his three‑razes combo and pre‑emptively block the middle raze.

Itemizing Against Shadow Fiend

Black King Bar — prevents his Shadowrazes and Requiem from being cast during team fights.
Pipe of Insight — reduces the magic damage from his razes and Requiem, mitigating early burst.
Heaven’s Halberd — disarms him, nullifying the physical component of his burst and forcing him to rely on a weakened Requiem.
Manta Style — dispels the armor‑reduction from Presence of the Dark Lord and can be used to dodge the three razes.

shadow-shaman.name: Shadow Shaman
shadow-shaman.guideHtml:
Shadow Shaman is a versatile support‑turn‑pusher who excels at disabling, burst damage, and objective control. On patch 7.41 his overall win rate sits at 51.8 % across 572 k recent ranked games, making him a solid pick in the current meta, especially on coordinated teams that can capitalize on his late‑game ward power spikes.

How to Play Shadow Shaman

Laning Phase

  • Ether Shock early levels to harass and secure last hits; the cone damage works well against melee supports and can chip towers in off‑lane.
  • Hex on the enemy off‑laner (often a hard‑carry like Lycan or Beastmaster) to deny farm and force rotations; the transformation also blocks their disables.
  • Shackles on a mid‑lane hero that over‑extends (e.g., Kunkka or Morphling) – the channel is short enough to land before they can blink away if you have vision.
  • Pair Ether Shock + Hex to create a “double‑disable” combo that makes lane opponents vulnerable to tower hits.
  • Keep an eye on Fowl Play cooldown; if you take lethal damage, the chicken can survive a tower dive and still provide a cheap escape.

Mid Game

  • Urnaconda on contested jungle camps or Roshan to instantly clear creep waves and set up a Mass Serpent Ward push.
  • Aim for Mass Serpent Ward timing around 20 min when you have at least Aghanim’s Shard (if built) – the 10 wards can overwhelm towers before the enemy can react.
  • Group with your mid‑lane core to land Shackles on high‑value targets (e.g., enemy mid or off‑lane carry) and follow up with a ward siege.
  • Prioritize vision control; a well‑placed ward can let you land Shackles from unexpected angles, especially against mobile heroes like Dawnbreaker.

Late Game

  • Use Mass Serpent Ward as the primary win condition: a full‑stack of wards can force the enemy base to collapse if they lack sufficient anti‑ward items.
  • Position yourself behind front‑line heroes; Shackles and Hex are most effective when you’re safe from initiation.
  • Avoid over‑extending without Fowl Play safety; a missed Shackles on a tanky hero can leave you vulnerable to counter‑initiations and cost the game.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane, especially against poke from heroes like Beastmaster.
  • Healing Salve — quick burst heal after a Hex or Shackles trade.
  • Observer Ward — early vision to land Shackles safely.
  • Clarity — mana for frequent Ether Shock and Shackles casts.

Core Items

  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Urnaconda to a massive AoE burst and shortens Shackles channel.
  • Blink Dagger — essential for initiating Shackles and positioning Mass Serpent Ward pushes.
  • Force Staff — provides escape for you and allies, and helps close the gap for Hex on mobile heroes.
  • Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — extra disable and self‑save; can combo with Hex for a double‑disable.

Situational Items

  • Glimmer Cape — against burst heroes (e.g., Death Prophet) and to protect Mass Serpent Ward pushes.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target disables back to initiators like Wraith King.
  • Ghost Scepter — when facing right‑click heavy heroes such as Bristleback or Lycan.
  • Aether Lens — increases cast range of Shackles and Hex, making them safer.
  • Scythe of Vyse (if you prefer a second Hex) — extra disable on high‑impact targets.

Common Mistakes

  • Wasting Shackles on low‑value targets – aim for heroes that can’t blink away or have high impact in fights.
  • Over‑committing without vision – missing a ward often leads to being caught out when you try to channel Shackles.
  • Neglecting Fowl Play – players forget the chicken escape, leading to unnecessary deaths in early dives.
  • Delaying Mass Serpent Ward – waiting too long reduces its effectiveness; aim for the 20‑25 min window when you have core items.

FAQ

Is Shadow Shaman good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 51.8 % win rate across over half a million ranked games, Shadow Shaman remains a strong pick, especially on coordinated teams that can leverage his Mass Serpent Ward push and reliable disables.

What lane does Shadow Shaman play?

Shadow Shaman is most commonly played as a support in the off‑lane (hard‑support) or safe lane (soft‑support), using Ether Shock, Hex, and Shackles to control the lane and set up kills.

Who counters Shadow Shaman?

Heroes with strong burst or reliable disables tend to counter him best. The data shows Beastmaster, Lycan, Dawnbreaker, Wraith King, Treant Protector, and Death Prophet as his toughest matchups, each giving Shadow Shaman win rates below 42 %. Counter‑play includes building Lotus Orb, Ghost Scepter, or Glimmer Cape and maintaining vision to avoid his Shackles.
shadow-shaman.counterHtml:
Shadow Shaman’s threat comes from his long‑range disable chain (Hex → Shackles) and his massive late‑game damage with Urnaconda and Mass Serpent Ward. The quickest way to shut him down is to deny him the opportunity to land a full‑duration Shackles and to pressure him before his wards can be set up.

Why These Heroes Beat Shadow Shaman

Beastmaster

Beastmaster’s Primal Roar provides a hard‑crowd control that can interrupt Shackles and his Hawk Shot harasses Shadow Shaman’s low early HP, forcing him to play overly defensive. Tip: keep a Hawk active near the lane edge to scout and punish any attempt to cast Hex from a distance.

Lycan

Lycan’s Summon Wolves and Feral Impulse give him high burst damage and lane pressure, making it hard for Shadow Shaman to survive long enough to land a Hex‑Shackles combo. Tip: push early with wolves and force Shadow Shaman to retreat, denying him farm and ward placement time.

Dawnbreaker

Dawnbreaker’s Starbreaker provides a brief invulnerability window that blocks Hex and Shackles, while her Luminosity cleave punishes Shadow Shaman’s low HP pool. Tip: time Starbreaker right as he initiates a Hex to completely negate the disable.

Wraith King

Wraith King’s Reincarnation nullifies Shadow Shaman’s kill potential; his Stun from Wraithfire Blast also interrupts Shackles channeling. Tip: engage with Wraithfire Blast as soon as you see Shadow Shaman start a Shackles channel to break it instantly.

Treant Protector

Treant’s Living Armor and Nature’s Guise give him high survivability against Ether Shock and Hex, while Overgrowth can root Shadow Shaman, preventing him from positioning for Shackles. Tip: drop a Living Armor on yourself or a creep before fighting to absorb the early Ether Shock damage.

Drafting Against Shadow Shaman

  • Prioritize heroes with hard‑crowd control that can interrupt channelled abilities (e.g., stuns, silences, knockbacks).
  • Pick early‑game aggression or lane‑dominant heroes to deny him farm and ward‑placement time.
  • Include at least one magic‑resistant or tanky pick to survive Ether Shock and Hex.
  • Consider banning or limiting heroes that synergize well with his wards (e.g., high‑damage right‑click carries).

Laning Against Shadow Shaman

  • Trade when his Ether Shock is on cooldown; his damage spikes are short‑lived.
  • Harass aggressively after he casts Hex, as he is vulnerable to retaliation while the enemy is transformed.
  • Force him to use Shackles early; a broken channel gives you a gold/experience swing.
  • Keep a creep wave near your tower to limit his ability to place wards safely.

Itemizing Against Shadow Shaman

Ghost Scepter — blocks Ether Shock and the initial damage from Urnaconda, buying time to dodge Shackles.
Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — can purge Hex and provide a self‑silence to survive a Shackles channel.
Black King Bar — grants magic immunity, rendering Ether Shock and Hex ineffective during team fights.
Lotus Orb — reflects Hex back to Shadow Shaman and provides a strong dispel against his crowd control.

silencer.name: Silencer
silencer.guideHtml:
Silencer remains a surprisingly resilient pick in the current meta, boasting a 51.0% win rate across 435,445 ranked matches on patch 7.41. His blend of global silence, intelligence‑stealing attacks, and strong late‑game scaling lets him swing teamfights and snowball from a support or semi‑carry position. While he can still dominate many lineups, several heroes—especially those with high mobility or burst—still give him trouble.

How to Play Silencer

Laning Phase

  • Glaives of Wisdom early harass: weave auto‑attacks with the ability to steal intelligence; prioritize heroes with high base INT (e.g., Lina, Death Prophet) to gain lane dominance.
  • Arcane Curse for wave control: drop the curse on the creep wave to slow enemy movement and add damage, making it easier to pull or deny.
  • Last Word on aggressive opponents: place the enchantment on a hero that frequently casts (e.g., Huskar) to punish spell usage and force them to play passively.
  • Stack and pull using Arcane Curse’s slow to set up safe jungle camps; the slowed creeps are easier to pull and deny.
  • Watch for early Roshan: Silencer’s low health makes him vulnerable; keep the lane tight and use Last Word to silence any early aggression from off‑lane heroes.

Mid Game

  • Global Silence timing: coordinate with your team’s split‑push or teamfight; casting it just before a major engagement forces enemies to waste key spells.
  • Intelligence steal on kills: position near fights so that any enemy death within 925 range triggers the permanent INT steal, accelerating your damage and item progression.
  • Push with Arcane Curse: use the ability on enemy towers or high‑ground structures to slow defenders and add consistent damage while your cores take objectives.
  • Vision control: drop wards near enemy jungle entrances; Last Word provides vision of the enchanted target, giving you extra intel on roaming heroes.

Late Game

  • Teamfight anchor: stay near the front line with Suffer In Silence active; you deal extra damage to silenced foes and take less damage yourself.
  • Protect your cores: use Global Silence to shut down enemy spellcasters during crucial moments (e.g., when your carry is channeling).
  • Avoid being focused: Silencer is squishy; if the enemy has strong initiators (e.g., Spirit Breaker), stay behind your frontline and rely on Arcane Curse and Last Word to punish their spells.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane against harass.
  • Healing Salve — quick burst healing for early trades.
  • Observer Ward — vision for safe pulling and enemy tracking.
  • Sentry Ward — counter invisible support heroes.
  • Enchanted Mango — mana for early Glaives of Wisdom and Arcane Curse.

Core Items

  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Global Silence to a longer duration and reduces cooldown, making it a reliable teamfight tool.
  • Force Staff — provides the mobility you lack, lets you escape Spirit Breaker dives and position for Global Silence.
  • Glimmer Cape — protects you from burst (e.g., Razor, Huskar) and lets you cast Global Silence safely.
  • Mekansm — synergizes with Suffer In Silence, giving you and allies a burst of survivability in fights.

Situational Items

  • Black King Bar — when facing heavy magical burst (e.g., Lina, Leshrac).
  • Lotus Orb — reflects targeted disables and removes silences placed on you.
  • Guardian Greaves — upgrade Mekansm for stronger team sustain and faster cooldowns.
  • Scythe of Vyse — extra hard‑disable against slippery heroes like Razor or Keeper of the Light.
  • Aether Lens — increases Global Silence cast range, allowing you to silence from safer distances.

Common Mistakes

  • Casting Global Silence too early – using it before a fight starts wastes its impact; wait for the enemy’s key spells to be off cooldown.
  • Over‑extending without vision – Silencer’s low HP makes him an easy target for initiators; always have a ward or Glimmer Cape before diving.
  • Neglecting intelligence steal – forgetting to stay within 925 range of kills loses valuable permanent INT, slowing your scaling.
  • Relying solely on Glaives for damage – without proper items, Glaives alone won’t win fights; transition to Scepter and supportive items early.

FAQ

Is Silencer good in the current patch?

Yes. Silencer holds a solid 51.0% win rate in recent ranked games, making him a reliable pick in both support and semi‑carry roles on patch 7.41.

What lane does Silencer play?

Silencer is most commonly played in the safe lane (position 4) as a support, but his Glaives of Wisdom and intelligence steal allow him to flex into a semi‑carry role in the off‑lane when the matchup is favorable.

Who counters Silencer?

Heroes with strong mobility or burst damage—such as Treant Protector, Huskar, Razor, Leshrac, Keeper of the Light, and Spirit Breaker—have the lowest win rates against Silencer (30‑38% in recent games), making them his toughest counters.
silencer.counterHtml:
Silencer thrives on shutting down spell‑casters with Global Silence and draining their intelligence, turning team fights into a silent nightmare. The key to beating him is to force constant spell casts, out‑mana his silence, and exploit the short window before his Global Silence lands.

Why These Heroes Beat Silencer

Treant Protector

Treant’s Nature’s Guise grants invisibility and Living Armor provides massive damage reduction, allowing him to survive Silencer’s early harassment and stay out of Global Silence range. Use the Overgrowth stun to lock Silencer down while his silence is on cooldown. Tip: keep a Tree of Redemption active to mitigate Silencer’s Arcane Curse damage.

Huskar

Huskar’s Life Break and Burning Spear give him high HP regeneration and damage that scales with his health, making him hard to kill even when silenced. His Inner Fire can purge Silencer’s Glaives of Wisdom stacks and force Silencer to waste Global Silence on a moving target. Tip: stay aggressive early; Huskar’s low mana pool forces Silencer to waste spells.

Razor

Razor’s Static Link steals damage from Silencer, nullifying the intelligence‑stealing Glaives and punishing Silencer for staying in melee range. Unstable Current silences enemies, but more importantly it provides a reliable source of damage that Silencer cannot block with Global Silence. Tip: position Razor to keep the link on Silencer during laning to deny his Glaive hits.

Leshrac

Leshrac’s Split Earth and Lightning Storm have low mana costs and can be spammed, constantly extending Silencer’s Arcane Curse duration and forcing Silencer to waste Global Silence on a hero who is constantly casting. Leshrac’s high burst damage also punishes Silencer’s low mobility. Tip: push the lane early with Split Earth to keep Silencer pinned under tower.

Keeper of the Light

Keeper’s Mana Leak and Recall constantly force Silencer to spend mana, shortening his ability to sustain Global Silence. Blinding Light provides a reliable silence that stacks with Silencer’s, making enemy casters virtually useless. Tip: use Recall on Silencer when he attempts a Global Silence to reset his cooldown.

Drafting Against Silencer

  • Prioritize heroes with high spell‑cast frequency (e.g., Storm Spirit, Pugna) to force Silencer’s Global Silence on cooldown.
  • Pick mobile heroes with escape tools (e.g., Anti‑Mage, Ember Spirit) to dodge Global Silence and stay out of his radius.
  • Include strong early‑game lane dominators who can trade before Silencer gets his Glaives of Wisdom stacks.
  • Consider heroes with innate mana burn or regeneration suppression (e.g., Nyx Assassin, Dark Seer).

Laning Against Silencer

  • Harass with cheap spells to constantly extend Arcane Curse and force Silencer to waste Glaives.
  • Trade when Silencer is on cooldown after using Global Silence; his damage output drops sharply.
  • Use lane creeps to block his line of sight for Last Word vision, denying him the intelligence steal.
  • Push the lane aggressively; Silencer’s lack of wave clear makes him vulnerable to tower damage.

Itemizing Against Silencer

Black King Bar — grants spell immunity, nullifying Global Silence and Last Word during team fights.
Manta Style — creates illusion copies that Silencer cannot silence simultaneously, breaking his intelligence steal.
Eul's Scepter — cyclone removes Silencer from fights, buying time for allies to cast spells while his silence is on cooldown.
Aghanim’s Scepter (Keeper of the Light) — upgrades Recall to a global teleport, allowing you to reposition Silencer away from fights and waste his Global Silence.

skywrath-mage.name: Skywrath Mage
skywrath-mage.guideHtml:
Skywrath Mage is a high‑damage, intelligence‑based support whose kit revolves around burst magical nukes and silences. In the current 7.41 meta he sits at a 50.1 % win rate across 464 k ranked games, making him a solid but not dominant pick in the support role.

How to Play Skywrath Mage

Laning Phase

  • Arcane Bolt early harass: use its intelligence‑scaled damage to chip enemy cores and force them out of lane, especially against low‑armor heroes.
  • Concussive Shot for zone control: fire into the creep wave to slow opponents and set up kills with your carry’s disables.
  • Ancient Seal on high‑damage heroes (e.g., Death Prophet, Dragon Knight) to amplify your burst and silence their spells during trades.
  • Shield of the Scion stacking: stay aggressive when you land spells, as each hit gives you a magic barrier that mitigates enemy burst.
  • Prioritize safe lane partners (e.g., supports with strong disables) because Skywrath struggles against tanky, sustain‑heavy offlaners like Treant Protector and Lycan (win ≈ 30 % vs them).

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 6: look for 2‑v‑2 skirmishes where you can land Mystic Flare on clustered enemies; the ultimate scales with intelligence and can swing fights.
  • Roam with Ancient Seal: silence key enemy spellcasters (e.g., Phoenix, Dazzle) before initiating ganks with your carry.
  • Vision control: place deep wards and use Concussive Shot to scout; your burst is most effective when you catch heroes out of position.
  • Avoid prolonged fights against heroes with strong magic resistance or high HP pools (Lycan, Treant) – your damage falls off quickly.

Late Game

  • Win condition: burst down squishy backliners with Mystic Flare followed by an Ancient Seal‑enhanced combo.
  • Positioning: stay behind front‑line allies; your low HP and lack of escape tools make you vulnerable to initiators.
  • Game‑losing mistakes: over‑extending without vision, using Arcane Bolt on tanky heroes, or failing to stack Shield of the Scion before team fights.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane.
  • Healing Salve — emergency health.
  • Observer Ward — early vision for safe harass.
  • Clarity — mana for frequent spell casting.
  • Faerie Fire — cheap burst damage and a bit of health.

Core Items

  • Aether Lens — increase cast range of Arcane Bolt, Concussive Shot, and Ancient Seal, allowing safer poke.
  • Glimmer Cape — provides magic resistance and a save for yourself or an ally when you’re targeted.
  • Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — extra mana, movement speed, and a self‑cyclone to dodge dangerous disables.
  • Force Staff — helps you position for Mystic Flare and escape from initiators.

Situational Items

  • Ghost Scepter — against right‑click heavy heroes (Lycan, Treant) that can burst you.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects silences and dispels Ancient Seal from enemies like Dazzle.
  • Scythe of Vyse — adds a hard‑disable to complement your silence when you need extra control.
  • Aghanim’s Shard — upgrades Concussive Shot to a larger AoE slow, useful vs clustered teams.
  • Octarine Core — reduces cooldowns and gives extra health, helpful in prolonged late‑game fights.

Common Mistakes

  • Spamming Arcane Bolt on tanky heroes – the damage is intelligence‑scaled and ineffective against high‑HP units like Treant Protector.
  • Using Mystic Flare without proper positioning – casting it from the front line often results in being focused and killed.
  • Neglecting vision – without deep wards, you miss opportunities to land Ancient Seal on key spellcasters.
  • Over‑committing to lane fights – Skywrath lacks escape tools; staying too long against heroes with strong disables (e.g., Dazzle) leads to early deaths.

FAQ

Is Skywrath Mage good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 50.1 % win rate on 464 k recent ranked matches, Skywrath Mage remains a viable support, especially against squishy magic‑damage heroes. He excels in burst damage and silencing but struggles against tanky, sustain‑heavy offlaners.

What lane does Skywrath Mage play?

Skywrath Mage is typically played as a support in the safe lane (hard lane) alongside a carry, allowing him to harass with Arcane Bolt and set up kills with Ancient Seal. He can also be flexed to the mid lane if a team needs extra magical burst.

Who counters Skywrath Mage?

The toughest matchups are against Treant Protector, Lycan, Monkey King, Dazzle, Clinkz, and Phoenix, where his win rates drop to 30‑38 %. These heroes either have high magic resistance, strong sustain, or can close the distance quickly, nullifying Skywrath’s burst. Use early vision and pick‑off opportunities to mitigate their impact.
skywrath-mage.counterHtml:
Skywrath Mage’s strength lies in his massive burst of pure‑magic damage from Arcane Bolt, Concussive Shot, and especially Mystic Flare. The key to shutting him down is to deny him the intelligence‑scaled damage window, silence or burst‑damage him before he can stack his shield, and force fights where his long‑range spells are easy to dodge or ineffective.

Why These Heroes Beat Skywrath Mage

Treant Protector

Treant’s Nature’s Guise grants invisibility and a huge burst of armor, making Skywrath’s early magic hits miss and his Ancient Seal ineffective. Additionally, Living Armor can block the burst from Mystic Flare. Tip: Use the hidden tree to ambush Skywrath before he lands his first Arcane Bolt.

Lycan

Lycan’s Summon Wolves and Feral Impulse provide constant melee pressure that forces Skywrath to use his shield early, while Shapeshift gives him high health and magic resistance, reducing Mystic Flare’s impact. Tip: Push the lane aggressively with wolves to force Skywrath into a defensive position where his spells are out‑of‑range.

Monkey King

Monkey King’s Tree Dance lets him dodge Arcane Bolt and Mystic Flare, while Jingu Mastery gives burst physical damage that can kill Skywrath before his shield stacks. His Boundless Strike also silences, negating Ancient Seal. Tip: Initiate from the trees when Skywrath is channeling Mystic Flare to interrupt the ultimate.

Dazzle

Dazzle’s Shadow Wave and Shallow Grave give him sustain and a safety net against Skywrath’s burst, while Weave reduces magic damage taken, directly countering Mystic Flare. Tip: Keep Weave active on yourself and allies; it makes Mystic Flare’s damage negligible.

Clinkz

Clinkz’s Searing Arrows and Death Pact give him high burst physical damage that can outpace Skywrath’s shield, and his Skeleton Walk provides magic‑immune movement, allowing him to close the gap safely. Tip: Use Skeleton Walk to close distance, then burst with Searing Arrows before Skywrath can cast Ancient Seal.

Drafting Against Skywrath Mage

  • Prioritize heroes with magic resistance or spell‑nullifying abilities (e.g., Dazzle, Treant Protector).
  • Pick high‑burst physical damage heroes that can kill before the shield stacks (Monkey King, Clinkz).
  • Include silence or disables that can interrupt Mystic Flare (Lion, Silencer).
  • Avoid heavy intelligence‑based lineups that give Skywrath extra scaling.

Laning Against Skywrath Mage

  • Trade when his Arcane Bolt is on cooldown; his damage spikes are predictable.
  • Harass early with right‑clicks or low‑mana spells to force him to use Shield of the Scion prematurely.
  • Punish his Concussive Shot miss window by positioning just outside its AoE radius.
  • Force him to pull a creep; the extra distance makes his spells harder to land.

Itemizing Against Skywrath Mage

Pipe of Insight — grants team‑wide magic damage reduction, directly mitigating Mystic Flare and Arcane Bolt.
Black King Bar — provides spell immunity, nullifying all of Skywrath’s burst during team fights.
Ghost Scepter — makes you ethereal, causing Arcane Bolt and Mystic Flare to miss.
Eul’s Scepter — cyclone can remove Skywrath from the fight, breaking his channel on Mystic Flare and resetting his shield stacks.

slardar.name: Slardar
slardar.guideHtml:
Slardar remains a high‑impact initiator and tank in the current meta, sitting at a flat 50.0% win rate over 301,168 ranked games on OpenDota (July 2026). His blend of armor‑shredding, crowd control, and escape makes him a solid pick for both carry‑style damage and front‑line durability, though several matchups still suppress his effectiveness.

How to Play Slardar

Laning Phase

  • Use Guardian Sprint to dodge early harass and secure safe farm; the 2.5 s of 100 % slow resistance is especially useful against disables like Crystal Maiden’s Frostbite.
  • Drop Slithereen Crush when the enemy support steps up for a pull or when you need a quick stun to set up a kill on a melee opponent.
  • Aim to land the Bash of the Deep on a low‑HP enemy after the third attack; the guaranteed bash can turn a contested lane into a kill lane.
  • Position near river puddles to benefit from Seaborn Sentinel—the bonus movement speed and armor help you survive harass from heroes such as Marci.
  • Prioritize vision on the enemy off‑lane; Corrosive Haze’s True Sight reveals invisible heroes (e.g., Nyx Assassin) that otherwise dominate the lane.

Mid Game

  • Power spike: Level 6 – Corrosive Haze gives you true sight and armor reduction, enabling safe ganks on high‑armor cores like Lifestealer.
  • Group with your team and use Guardian Sprint to initiate, then follow up with Slithereen Crush and a Bash for a quick 2‑2‑2 stun‑bash combo.
  • Secure river control; staying in water maximizes Seaborn Sentinel and makes you harder to lock down for heroes like Vengeful Spirit.
  • Target enemy supports that lack mobility (e.g., Crystal Maiden) with Corrosive Haze to strip armor and force them out of fights.

Late Game

  • Win condition: lock down the enemy carry with Guardian Sprint → Slithereen Crush → Bash, then let your team focus the isolated target while you soak damage.
  • Position near the edge of fights; the water‑based bonuses from Seaborn Sentinel keep you survivable against burst heroes like Lina.
  • Avoid over‑committing into line‑ups with strong disables (Marci, Faceless Void); their crowd‑control can nullify your initiation and lead to early deaths.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane, especially against harassment from Vengeful Spirit.
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery after early trades.
  • Quelling Blade — helps secure creep last‑hits when you’re focusing on early damage.
  • Stout Shield — mitigates damage from lane harass and early tower hits.
  • Observer Ward — provides vision to protect against ganks and to spot invisible enemies.

Core Items

  • Phase Boots — extra movement speed for faster Guardian Sprint initiations and better chase potential.
  • Blink Dagger — essential for closing the gap instantly and landing Slithereen Crush on key targets.
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Corrosive Haze to affect a larger area, making it easier to shred armor on multiple heroes in team fights.
  • Shiva’s Guard — armor and aura complement Slardar’s tank role while the active slows enemies already affected by Slithereen Crush.

Situational Items

  • Black King Bar — needed against heavy magic burst line‑ups (e.g., Lina, Viper).
  • Crimson Guard — excellent when facing multiple physical damage cores such as Lifestealer or Vengeful Spirit.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target disables like Marci’s Unleash or Faceless Void’s Chronosphere pull.
  • Assault Cuirass — further amplifies armor reduction on enemies and boosts your team’s physical damage.
  • Mekansm / Guardian Greaves — provides team healing and stronger survivability in prolonged engagements.

Common Mistakes

  • Wasting Sprint on pure chase instead of using the built‑in slow resistance to dodge disables.
  • Casting Slithereen Crush without coordinating a follow‑up bash, leaving the stun isolated and reducing overall impact.
  • Neglecting Corrosive Haze on high‑armor heroes; failing to apply armor reduction makes your damage and team’s physical output much lower.
  • Standing outside water in late‑game fights, losing the defensive bonuses from Seaborn Sentinel and becoming an easy target for burst damage.

FAQ

Is Slardar good in the current patch?

Yes. Slardar sits at a 50.0% win rate across over 300 k ranked matches, making him a neutral to slightly favorable pick. He excels in games where you can secure early vision and leverage his armor‑shredding to neutralize tanky cores.

What lane does Slardar play?

Slardar is most commonly played in the off‑lane (safelane) where his durability and crowd‑control can protect the carry and disrupt enemy supports. He can also be flexed to a solo mid if you need a tanky initiator early.

Who counters Slardar?

The toughest matchups right now are Marci (40.1% win), Vengeful Spirit (41.0%), and Faceless Void (42.9%). These heroes either out‑disrupt Slardar’s initiation or out‑scale his tankiness, making lane control and early vision crucial against them.
slardar.counterHtml:
Slardar’s high mobility, armor‑shredding Corrosive Haze, and reliable stun make him a constant threat to any front‑line hero. The key to shutting him down is denying his burst + armor‑reduction combo and exploiting the moments before his sprint’s slow‑resistance fades.

Why These Heroes Beat Slardar

Marci

Marci’s Dispose instantly removes Slardar’s Corrosive Haze and any stun from Slithereen Crush, while her Rebound provides a burst of movement that outruns Guardian Sprint’s lingering slow‑resistance.
Tip: Initiate with Dispose on Slardar as soon as he lands his stun; follow up with a quick Rebound to keep the pressure before his sprint expires.

Vengeful Spirit

Vengeful Spirit’s Magic Missile applies a strong magic damage burst that bypasses Slardar’s armor, and her Nether Swap can pull Slardar out of his puddle, instantly canceling Seaborn Sentinel’s bonuses.
Tip: Time Nether Swap right after Slardar lands his stun to force him into a neutral zone where his movement speed is no longer amplified.

Faceless Void

Faceless Void’s Time Walk grants him a brief period of invulnerability, nullifying Slardar’s stun and armor reduction, while Chronosphere locks Slardar out of his sprint path and prevents him from using Corrosive Haze on allies.
Tip: Initiate Chronosphere after Slardar’s sprint ends; the slowed‑resistance window is gone, making his chase far less effective.

Crystal Maiden

Crystal Maiden’s Frostbite roots Slardar, preventing him from sprinting away and denying the movement‑speed boost from Seaborn Sentinel. Her Arcane Aura also provides mana sustain for frequent disables.
Tip: Pair Frostbite with a follow‑up stun (e.g., from a support) while Slardar is still in the puddle to maximize damage before his armor shred takes effect.

Naga Siren

Naga Siren’s Ensnare roots Slardar, cancelling his sprint and removing the advantage of his 100 % slow resistance. Her Mirror Image creates confusion, making it hard for Slardar to land a reliable bash.
Tip: Use Ensnare the moment Slardar initiates Sprint; the root will break his momentum and expose him to your team’s burst.

Drafting Against Slardar

  • Prioritize heroes with strong magic burst or disables that ignore armor (e.g., Lina, Lion, Vengeful Spirit).
  • Choose heroes that can purge or negate armor reduction (e.g., Marci, Oracle).
  • Include at least one hero with reliable crowd control that can lock Slardar down during his sprint cooldown.
  • Avoid picking multiple melee cores that rely heavily on physical damage unless you have armor‑shredding mitigation.

Laning Against Slardar

  • Trade when his Bash of the Deep is on cooldown; his burst window is then minimal.
  • Harass him before he can activate Seaborn Sentinel by forcing him out of water or river terrain.
  • Punish the 2.5 s of 100 % slow resistance by using a quick stun or burst right after his sprint starts—his resistance will fade quickly.
  • Keep a defensive ward near his potential puddle spawn points to anticipate his movement speed spikes.

Itemizing Against Slardar

Mekansm — provides burst healing and armor, countering the physical damage amplified by Corrosive Haze.
Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — cyclones Slardar, nullifying his sprint and giving you time to reposition or purge his haze.
Ghost Scepter — makes you ethereal, rendering Slardar’s physical attacks and armor shred ineffective.
Aghanim’s Shard (Marci) — grants the Dispose purge, instantly removing Corrosive Haze and stun.

slark.name: Slark
slark.guideHtml:
Slark is a high‑mobility, burst‑damage carry whose strength lies in stealing enemy attributes and escaping with Shadow Dance. On patch 7.41 his overall win‑rate sits at 49.4 % across 385 k recent ranked games, placing him slightly below the meta average but still viable in the right hands.

How to Play Slark

Laning Phase

  • Use Dark Pact early to purge early disables (e.g., Shadow Shaman’s Ether Shock) and to harass while taking only 30 % of the self‑damage.
  • Land the first Pounce on the enemy off‑lane hero to apply an Essence Shift stack and limit their escape distance; follow up with attacks to stack agility quickly.
  • Saltwater Shiv is excellent against heroes with strong movement‑speed or regen (e.g., Spirit Breaker, Treant Protector); cast it after a successful Pounce to cripple their chase.
  • Prioritize farming creeps while maintaining low health to trigger Shadow Dance for free regen and speed when hidden in the fog of war.
  • Against tough match‑ups like Leshrac or Spirit Breaker, play passively and wait for jungle rotations; your early game is fragile until you secure a few Essence Shift stacks.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 6 (Shadow Dance) and level 12 (Essence Shift permanent agility on kill); start looking for 2‑v‑2 skirmishes near your tier‑1 tower.
  • Use Depth Shroud on high‑ground objectives (Roshan, Tier‑2 towers) to hide yourself and teammates, then initiate with Pounce from the fog.
  • Target squishy back‑line heroes (e.g., Puck, Storm Spirit) with a combo: Dark Pact → Pounce → Saltwater Shiv → attack for rapid Essence Shift gains.
  • When you have a Shadow Dance charge, dive into fights where the enemy is distracted; the invisibility‑based regen lets you survive burst damage.

Late Game

  • Win condition: accumulate enough Essence Shift stacks to out‑scale opponents in agility, then pick off key heroes with Pounce + Dark Pact burst.
  • Position near neutral camps or high‑ground vision to keep Shadow Dance active; staying unseen maximizes your regen and movement speed.
  • Losing the game usually stems from being caught without Shadow Dance (e.g., when enemy vision is permanent) or over‑extending into vision without a Depth Shroud cover.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango & Healing Salve — sustain in lane while you trade with Dark Pact.
  • Slippers of Agility — early boost to attack damage for faster Essence Shift stacking.
  • Observer Ward — vision to avoid ganks from the toughest match‑ups (Leshrac, Spirit Breaker).

Core Items

  • Power Treads — agility for damage and movement speed; switch to strength for survivability when needed.
  • Echo Sabre — extra burst on the first hit after a Pounce, synergizes with Dark Pact damage.
  • Black King Bar — essential against spell‑heavy lanes (Leshrac, Jakiro) where you need to stay alive for Shadow Dance.
  • Sange & Yasha – provides movement speed, status resistance, and a chance to maim, helping you chase down heroes you’ve leashed with Pounce.

Situational Items

  • Abyssal Blade — lock down slippery heroes (e.g., Storm Spirit, Puck) that can otherwise escape your Pounce.
  • Manta Style — dispels silences and gives extra agility; useful versus Snapfire’s Mortimer Kisses.
  • Heart of Tarrasque — massive HP pool to survive prolonged fights against tanky heroes like Tidehunter.
  • Linken’s Sphere — blocks single‑target disables from Spirit Breaker or Jakiro, keeping your Shadow Dance uptime.
  • Butterfly — huge agility and evasion, perfect when you need to out‑damage heroes like Windranger.

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑using Dark Pact on low‑HP waves, causing unnecessary self‑damage and losing early Essence Shift stacks.
  • Pouncing without a follow‑up; many low‑MMR players miss the attack combo, letting the enemy escape and wasting the leash.
  • Ignoring Shadow Dance: playing visible in the lane forfeits the passive regen and speed, making Slark too fragile against burst heroes.
  • Itemizing too early on defensive items (e.g., early BKB) before hitting level 12, which delays the crucial agility scaling.

FAQ

Is Slark good in the current patch?

Yes. Slark’s win‑rate of 49.4 % across 385 k matches shows he is slightly below average but still competitive, especially when you capitalize on his mid‑game power spikes and escape tools.

What lane does Slark play?

Slark is typically played in the safe lane as a carry, allowing him to farm safely while stacking Essence Shift and using Depth Shroud to hide from early ganks.

Who counters Slark?

The toughest match‑ups right now are Leshrac (38.1 % win), Spirit Breaker (40.0 %), Treant Protector (41.9 %), Snapfire (42.4 %), Jakiro (44.4 %), and Windranger (44.4 %). Their strong disables, burst, or vision control make it hard for Slark to stay hidden and farm safely.
slark.counterHtml:
Slark thrives on burst damage, relentless aggression, and the ability to escape after a kill with Shadow Dance. To shut him down you need heroes that can lock him down, purge his Dark Pact debuff removal, and out‑scale his early‑game pressure.

Why These Heroes Beat Slark

Leshrac

Leshrac’s Lightning Storm and Split Earth provide constant AoE damage and a reliable stun that prevents Slark from leaping away with Pounce. The spell‑based damage also bypasses Slark’s Dark Pact damage reduction. Tip: Keep Leshrac’s mana high and force Slark into a Lightning Storm combo; the stun forces him to use Shadow Dance early, wasting his regen.

Spirit Breaker

Spirit Breaker’s Charge of Darkness and Nether Strike give a global, unstoppable lock‑down that ignores Slark’s Depth Shroud and Shadow Dance. The guaranteed stun removes Slark’s mobility and forces him to fight on Spirit Breaker’s terms. Tip: Position early towers or vision near the lane so Spirit Breaker can land a charge before Slark can escape with Pounce.

Treant Protector

Treant’s Living Armor and Nature’s Guise grant high survivability while his Overgrowth provides a long‑duration root that Slark cannot purge. The root nullifies Slark’s Pounce and Shadow Dance escape window. Tip: Stack trees and place a Living Armor ward on the lane; when Slark dives, immediately trigger Overgrowth to lock him down.

Snapfire

Snapfire’s Firesnap Cookie is a strong single‑target stun that can be cast from a distance, preventing Sliver’s Pounce escape. Her Mortimer Kisses deal AoE damage that hurts Slark even after his Dark Pact damage reduction. Tip: Use Cookie on the first Slark engage, then follow up with Mortimer to force him to retreat before he can secure a kill.

Jakiro

Jakiro’s Ice Path provides a long‑range stun and slows that block Slark’s Pounce and Depth Shroud movement. Dual Breath and Macropyre deal consistent magical damage that is less mitigated by Slark’s Dark Pact reduction. Tip: Position Ice Path at the edge of the lane; when Slark leaps, the stun and subsequent damage force him to waste his escape cooldown.

Drafting Against Slark

  • Prioritize heroes with reliable stuns or roots (e.g., Leshrac, Treant, Jakiro).
  • Choose global or long‑range lock‑downs that ignore Depth Shroud (e.g., Spirit Breaker).
  • Include strong magical damage sources to mitigate Dark Pact’s 30 % reduction.
  • Avoid picking heroes that rely heavily on mobility or evasion without hard disables.

Laning Against Slark

  • Harass early with ranged attacks; Slark is weakest before he gets Essence Shift stacks.
  • Punish his Pounce miss by zoning him with creeps or towers.
  • Force him to use Dark Pact on the lane; the self‑damage gives you a health advantage.
  • Keep vision on the river to anticipate his Depth Shroud jumps and respond with disables.

Itemizing Against Slark

Abyssal Blade — active stun forces a fight and prevents Slark from leaping away.
Eul’s Scepter — cyclone removes Slark’s Essence Shift stacks and buys time for teammates to focus him.
Scythe of Vyse – long‑duration hex nullifies Shadow Dance escape and blocks Pounce.
Glimmer Cape – provides a strong dispel to remove Dark Pact’s self‑damage and protects allies from Slark’s burst.

snapfire.name: Snapfire
snapfire.guideHtml:
Snapfire is a versatile support‑nuker who excels at zone control and burst damage with her cookie‑stun combo and Mortimer Kisses. On patch 7.41 she sits at a solid 53.2% win rate across 736,741 recent ranked games, making her one of the more reliable supports in the current meta. Her toolkit shines in team fights and skirmishes, while her win‑rate trends show she thrives against heroes like Tinker and Witch Doctor but struggles versus mobile, split‑push champions such as Broodmother and Bounty Hunter.

How to Play Snapfire

Laning Phase

  • Use Scatterblast at point‑blank range to maximize the 30% damage boost and the 50% longer slows, securing early lane dominance and deterring aggressive supports.
  • Drop a Firesnap Cookie on an allied creep or Mortimer to stun and damage any enemy that steps into the landing zone; this is especially effective against melee off‑laners who chase you.
  • Pair Lil' Shredder with a short‑range tower attack to shred armor on enemy heroes and creeps, speeding up creep equilibrium and making tower dives safer.
  • Prioritize pulling the small camp with Gobble Up (if you have a teammate with Mortimer) to deny lane creeps and create space for your carry.
  • Keep an eye on the enemy support’s mobility; against high‑mobility heroes (e.g., Bounty Hunter) stay near your tower and use Scatterblast to punish any over‑extension.

Mid Game

  • Power spike: Level 6 unlocks Mortimer Kisses; look for 5‑second windows to unleash the fire‑spit barrage before enemy initiations.
  • Roam with Firesnap Cookie onto enemy heroes in the jungle; the stun‑and‑damage combo can force early tower hits or secure vision.
  • Guard objectives with Lil' Shredder on Mortimer; the extra attack range and armor reduction make it ideal for taking down Roshan or high‑armor towers.
  • When your team has vision, position Mortimer near contested areas and use Spit Out to stun multiple foes, turning skirmishes into team‑fight wins.

Late Game

  • Win condition: Use Mortimer Kisses combined with Firesnap Cookie to lock down the enemy carry while your team focuses fire; the lingering firespit pools provide sustained damage and slow.
  • Stay just behind your frontline; a well‑timed Scatterblast can cripple enemy initiators and give your team the space to reposition.
  • Avoid being caught out by split‑push heroes (Broodmother, Clinkz) – maintain vision and keep Mortimer near high‑ground to quickly Gobble Up and Spit Out any diving units.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane, especially against aggressive melee opponents.
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery after early skirmishes.
  • Observer Ward — vision to protect against ganks from mobile heroes like Bounty Hunter.
  • Clarity — mana for frequent Scatterblast and Firesnap Cookie usage.
  • Enchanted Mango — instant burst mana for early Mortimer Kisses setups.

Core Items

  • Aether Lens — extends the cast range of Firesnap Cookie and Mortimer Kisses, allowing safer engagements.
  • Force Staff — provides escape against burst heroes (Bane, Io) and helps position Mortimer for optimal Spit Out angles.
  • Glimmer Cape — counters disables from Bane and Io while granting invisibility for surprise Cookie combos.
  • Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — additional crowd control and a way to set up Scatterblast + Firesnap Cookie combos.

Situational Items

  • Ghost Scepter — against right‑click heavy heroes like Clinkz and Phantom Lancer.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target spells from Bounty Hunter and Io.
  • Shiva’s Guard — armor and AoE slow to counter high‑damage physical cores (Treant Protector, Bounty Hunter).
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Firesnap Cookie to a larger stun radius, useful vs split‑push lineups.
  • Octarine Core — reduces cooldowns on all abilities, especially valuable for late‑game Mortimer Kisses uptime.

Common Mistakes

  • Casting Scatterblast from too far: the damage and slow bonuses only apply at point‑blank range, wasting its potential.
  • Using Firesnap Cookie on creeps only: the stun is far more valuable on enemy heroes or Mortimer for combo setups.
  • Neglecting vision: without wards, mobile heroes like Bounty Hunter and Broodmother can flank and nullify Snapfire’s zone control.
  • Over‑extending without Mortimer: trying to initiate fights without Mortimer’s presence often leads to being burst down by burst heroes (Bane, Io).

FAQ

Is Snapfire good in the current patch?

Yes. Snapfire enjoys a 53.2% win rate on patch 7.41, placing her among the top support picks. Her strong win rates against heroes like Tinker (63.5%) and Witch Doctor (62.3%) show she remains a reliable pick in the current meta.

What lane does Snapfire play?

Snapfire is typically played as a support in the safe lane (position 5) or as a roaming support (position 4). Her early Scatterblast and Firesnap Cookie give her lane control, while her mobility shines when she roams to other lanes.

Who counters Snapfire?

The toughest matchups are against high‑mobility or split‑push heroes: Broodmother (38.0% win), Bounty Hunter (38.1%), Clinkz (38.9%), Treant Protector (40.8%), Io (41.6%), and Bane (42.9%). Vision denial and early aggressive pressure are key to limiting her effectiveness against these heroes.
snapfire.counterHtml:
Snapfire’s strength lies in her burst zone‑control and the relentless pressure from Mortimer Kisses. To shut her down you must deny her the space to land a cookie‑stun or a turret‑driven armor‑shred, and force her into early fights where her damage spikes are muted.

Why These Heroes Beat Snapfire

Broodmother

Broodmother’s Spiderlings and Web can block Snapfire’s line of sight, preventing her from landing a precise Firesnap Cookie and limiting the effective radius of Mortimer Kisses. Tip: keep a Web on the lane’s high ground and force Snapfire to fight in the narrow tunnels where her cone attacks miss most of the time.

Bounty Hunter

Bounty Hunter’s Shuriken Toss and Track give him vision and burst that can punish Snapfire before she can set up a turret or a cookie. The stun from Shuriken Toss also interrupts Mortimer Kisses’ channel. Tip: use Track on Snapfire early and pressure her with quick ganks; the threat of a stun forces her to play defensively.

Clinkz

Clinkz’s Searing Arrows and high mobility let him dodge the cookie hop and stay out of the turret’s short‑range shred. His Death Pact provides survivability against the burst damage from Mortimer Kisses. Tip: keep a distance, use Burning Barrage to harass Snapfire’s creep wave, and jump in with Skeleton Walk when her cooldowns are on cooldown.

Treant Protector

Treant’s Living Armor and Nature’s Grasp give him and his allies high armor and a strong block, reducing the impact of Lil’ Shredder’s armor‑shredding attacks. Overgrowth can root Snapfire, stopping her from repositioning for a cookie or turret shot. Tip: place Living Armor on the lane creeps to blunt Snapfire’s early wave clear and wait for Overgrowth to lock her down before committing to a fight.

Io

Io’s Tether and Relocate let him constantly reposition Snapfire’s allies out of the cookie’s landing zone and pull them away from Mortimer Kisses’ area of effect. Overcharge grants Snapfire’s partner bonus attack speed, making it risky for Snapfire to focus them with turret fire. Tip: use Relocate on a safe spot when Snapfire starts channeling Mortimer Kisses, forcing her to chase and waste her damage window.

Drafting Against Snapfire

  • Prioritize heroes with long‑range disables or true‑sight (e.g., Bounty Hunter, Pugna, Nyx Assassin).
  • Choose mobile heroes that can dodge the cookie hop and turret range (Clinkz, Anti‑Mage, Ember Spirit).
  • Include tanky or high‑armor heroes that mitigate Lil’ Shredder’s armor‑shred (Treant Protector, Bristleback, Tidehunter).
  • Ban or avoid heroes that give Snapfire extra lane control or early damage (e.g., Tinker, Witch Doctor).

Laning Against Snapfire

  • Harass her before she can land a cookie; the stun window is ~1.5 s, so early aggression forces a miss.
  • Trade when her turret is on cooldown; Lil’ Shredder’s damage spikes are brief and predictable.
  • Pull the lane creep equilibrium away from her tower to deny the extra damage from Mortimer Kisses on stacked creeps.
  • Use vision (wards or Sentry) to spot her positioning and avoid being caught in a cone blast.

Itemizing Against Snapfire

Eul's Scepter of Divinity — provides a reliable stun to interrupt Mortimer Kisses and a movement speed boost to escape cookie hops.
Ghost Scepter — makes you ethereal, nullifying the physical damage from Lil’ Shredder and the cookie’s impact.
Black King Bar — grants magic immunity during the 5.5‑second Mortimer Kisses channel, negating the burst and slows.
Mekansm / Guardian Greaves — armor and heal burst counter the armor‑shred and sustain you through Snapfire’s early lane pressure.
