sniper.name: Sniper
sniper.guideHtml:
Sniper remains a high‑damage, long‑range carry whose primary job is to farm safely and pick off enemies from afar. With a 49.9 % win rate across ~765k recent ranked games, he sits near the middle of the meta—strong enough to justify a core position but vulnerable to mobile, gap‑close heroes.

How to Play Sniper

Laning Phase

  • Use Shrapnel on creep waves to secure lane equilibrium and deny experience to aggressive melee opponents (e.g., Ember Spirit, Earthshaker).
  • Position near the edge of the lane; Headshot provides extra damage and a short knock‑back that can disrupt early ganks.
  • Keep Take Aim active to maximize your attack range (up to 160 extra units) and stay out of enemy harass zones.
  • When the enemy supports attempt a Concussive Grenade dive, step back into your own Shrapnel zone to mitigate damage and slow their advance.
  • Prioritize last‑hitting with Keen Scope‑enhanced attacks; the farther you are, the more damage per hit, which also speeds up your farm.

Mid Game

  • Aim for a Power Spike at 20 – 25 k gold (usually after completing Dragon Lance → Manta Style) to start split‑pushing and taking objectives.
  • Use Shrapnel on jungle camps or Roshan to secure vision and chip damage while you farm safely.
  • Join team fights only when you have Assassinate ready and the enemy is already slowed or stunned; your mini‑stun can finish off a key target.
  • Position behind front‑liners; let initiators like Earthshaker or Crystal Maiden engage, then unleash Assassinate on the squishy back‑line.

Late Game

  • Win condition: out‑farm and out‑damage the enemy core while staying behind your frontline; use Shrapnel to control choke points and protect Roshan.
  • Maintain extreme positioning; a single Assassinate on a high‑value target (e.g., Nature’s Prophet, Ember Spirit) can swing a fight, but a mis‑step into a gap‑closer kills you instantly.
  • Avoid over‑extending without vision—enemy mobile heroes (e.g., Ember Spirit) can close the distance and exploit Sniper’s low survivability.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane, especially against harass.
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery after early trades.
  • Slippers of Agility — early damage boost for last‑hits.
  • Iron Branch ×2 — cheap stats and can later be used for a Magic Wand.

Core Items

  • Dragon Lance — adds 160 attack range (stacking with Take Aim) and a solid damage/HP boost.
  • Manta Style — provides a way to dispel slows from Shrapnel and Concussive Grenade, plus extra damage and split‑push potential.
  • Black King Bar — essential against heavy disable lineups (e.g., Earthshaker, Crystal Maiden).
  • Satanic — gives survivability in late‑game fights where you’re forced into the front line.

Situational Items

  • Butterfly — excellent against right‑click heroes like Luna and Nature’s Prophet; adds evasion to survive their burst.
  • Monkey King Bar — counters evasion or high‑miss chance heroes (e.g., Crystal Maiden’s fog of war).
  • Abyssal Blade — provides a reliable stun to lock down mobile heroes that currently counter Sniper (Ember Spirit, Earthshaker).
  • Heart of Tarrasque — if you’re frequently the focus of burst damage and need extra tankiness.
  • Sange & Yasha — adds movement speed and status resistance, helpful against knock‑back heavy matchups.

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑extending without vision – diving into enemy vision without Shrapnel or a ward leads to quick deaths against mobile heroes.
  • Neglecting Shrapnel cooldown – failing to use Shrapnel for zone control lets opponents like Earthshaker and Ember Spirit dictate the lane.
  • Waiting too long for Assassinate – missing the mini‑stun window often means the target escapes; cast it as soon as the enemy is slowed or stunned.
  • Itemizing too early into damage – skipping BKB or survivability items makes Sniper an easy target for burst heroes (e.g., Luna, Nature’s Prophet).

FAQ

Is Sniper good in the current patch?

Sniper sits at a 49.9 % win rate on patch 7.41, making him a viable but not dominant carry. He excels when he can farm safely and pick off squishy targets, but struggles against mobile, gap‑close heroes.

What lane does Sniper play?

Sniper is most commonly played in the safe lane (carry position) where he can use Shrapnel and Take Aim to farm from a distance while staying protected by his tower.

Who counters Sniper?

The toughest matchups are Ember Spirit (38.2 % win), Nature’s Prophet (38.3 %), and Earthshaker (38.8 %). These heroes have strong mobility or burst that can close the distance before Sniper can react.
sniper.counterHtml:
Sniper’s massive attack range and scaling damage make him a constant threat from afar, forcing the enemy team to either stay out of his sight or risk being picked off. The key to shutting him down is to close the distance quickly, apply disables that negate his vision / range, and punish his low mobility and reliance on positioning.

Why These Heroes Beat Sniper

Ember Spirit

Ember’s Sleight of Fist lets him jump into Sniper’s range and deal burst damage while staying mobile, and Flame Guard blocks the magical damage from Sniper’s Assassinate and Shrapnel.
Tip: Initiate with Sleight of Fist from the fog of war, then follow up with Fire Remnant to keep the pressure and force Sniper to retreat.

Nature’s Prophet

Teleport lets Prophet appear behind Sniper’s vision cone, and his Sprout roots Sniper, preventing the quick repositioning needed to stay safe. Nature’s Call provides a global threat that forces Sniper to split push, weakening his lane presence.
Tip: Use Teleport into the lane when Sniper’s Shrapnel is on cooldown, then drop Sprout immediately to lock him down.

Earthshaker

Fissure creates a long wall that blocks Sniper’s line of sight and can instantly kill him if he’s low‑health, while Echo Slam punishes the clustered allies that often protect Sniper. Enchanted Crystal (after Aghanim’s) gives a reliable stun that bypasses Sniper’s Assassinate mini‑stun.
Tip: Position Fissure just beyond Sniper’s attack range; when he steps forward to farm, the wall both blocks his shots and sets up a follow‑up Echo Slam.

Crystal Maiden

Her Freezing Field forces Sniper to stay out of its radius, and Frostbite provides a reliable single‑target stun that negates his Assassinate channel. The mana regeneration aura also lets her sustain long fights where Sniper tries to kite.
Tip: Drop Frostbite the moment Sniper initiates with Assassinate; the stun interrupts the channel and leaves him vulnerable to a quick kill.

Ringmaster (Rubick)

Rubick can Telekinesis Sniper out of position, and his Spell Steal turns Sniper’s own Shrapnel or Assassinate against him. The Null Field aura reduces Sniper’s damage output, making his long‑range shots less threatening.
Tip: Save Telekinesis for the moment Sniper lands a Headshot‑enhanced attack; the lift disrupts his follow‑up and opens a window for a kill.

Drafting Against Sniper

  • Prioritize heroes with strong gap‑closers or mobility (e.g., Ember Spirit, Nature’s Prophet).
  • Include at least one reliable hard‑disable that works through vision (e.g., Earthshaker’s Fissure, Crystal Maiden’s Frostbite).
  • Consider global or split‑push threats to force Sniper to split his attention (e.g., Nature’s Prophet, Pugna).
  • Avoid picking multiple long‑range, low‑mobility cores that Synergy with Sniper’s range.

Laning Against Sniper

  • Trade when Sniper’s Shrapnel is on cooldown; his lane damage drops sharply.
  • Harass early with melee heroes that can get within 300 units, forcing him to use Headshot and waste mana.
  • Punish his low health after a Assassinate miss—he’s vulnerable to burst damage.
  • Use creep equilibrium to keep the lane close to your tower, limiting his effective range.

Itemizing Against Sniper

Blink Dagger — closes the gap instantly, allowing you to land disables before Sniper can react.
Force Staff — pushes Sniper out of his optimal range or pulls him into your team’s front line.
Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — cyclones Sniper, negating his Assassinate channel and forcing him to waste mana on the escape.
Abyssal Blade — provides a reliable stun that works through his Shrapnel vision and prevents him from kiting.

spectre.name: Spectre
spectre.guideHtml:
Spectre remains one of the most durable carries in the current meta, boasting a 54.3% win rate over 493 k recent ranked games (OpenDota, July 2026). Her late‑game scaling and global presence through Haunt keep her a top pick, especially on farms that allow her to hit her power spikes safely.

How to Play Spectre

Laning Phase

  • Use Spectral Dagger to secure last hits and harass; the speed boost helps you stay out of enemy range while still farming.
  • Prioritize a safe lane (usually off‑lane) against early‑game nukers; the data shows you struggle vs Warlock, Rubick, and Snapfire, so play defensively and avoid extended trades.
  • Stack neutral camps early; the extra farm accelerates your transition to mid‑game items.
  • Keep an eye on enemy Desolate‑type heroes (e.g., Lifestealer, Timbersaw)—their lack of allied units around you makes them vulnerable to your Desolate damage.
  • Pull creep equilibrium when possible to deny lane experience to aggressive supports.

Mid Game

  • Hit the Haunt power spike (level 6) and start joining team fights from a distance; your illusion provides vision and split‑push pressure.
  • Farm aggressively in the jungle once you have Radiance or Manta Style; the extra damage synergizes with Dispersion and Desolate.
  • Prioritize objectives that grant map control (Roshan, towers) while staying behind frontline tanks; your survivability lets you soak damage and reflect it with Dispersion.
  • Avoid prolonged 1v1 duels against heroes with strong disables (e.g., Lion, Dark Willow) until you have a defensive item like Black King Bar.

Late Game

  • Position near the front of your team; Haunt gives you global presence, but you still need to stay within range of allies to benefit from Dispersion.
  • Aim to pick off isolated heroes; Desolate deals pure damage when enemies lack nearby allies, making split‑push and pick‑off plays deadly.
  • Lose the game if you overextend without vision—enemy Vision heroes can shut down your Haunt and kill your illusory copies quickly.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango + Healing Salve — sustain in the lane.
  • Quelling Blade — easier last‑hits on creeps.
  • Stout Shield — mitigates harassment from early nukers.

Core Items

  • Radiance — amplifies Dispersion and Desolate damage across team fights.
  • Manta Style — provides a second Haunt‑type illusion, removes silences, and boosts mobility.
  • Black King Bar — essential against disables from Lion, Rubick, and Dark Willow.
  • Butterfly — increases damage output and survivability against physical damage dealers.

Situational Items

  • Satanic — extra durability when you’re the primary front‑liner.
  • Heart of Tarrasque — maximizes your tankiness for prolonged fights.
  • Abyssal Blade — lockdown for slippery heroes like Windranger (easy matchup) or Timbersaw.
  • Linken’s Sphere – blocks single‑target spells from Warlock and Rubick.
  • Monkey King Bar – counters evasion from heroes such as Drow Ranger.

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑pushing early – without Radiance or Manta, Spectre is vulnerable to burst from Warlock and Rubick.
  • Ignoring vision – relying solely on Haunt without wards lets enemies shut down your global presence.
  • Buying too much damage early – neglecting survivability items leads to early deaths against disables.
  • Misusing Shadow Step – sending the illusion into dangerous zones wastes its potential; use it to scout or bait before teleporting with Reality.

FAQ

Is Spectre good in the current patch?

Yes. Spectre enjoys a 54.3% win rate in the latest ranked data, making her a strong pick especially on farms that let her reach her late‑game power spikes.

What lane does Spectre play?

Spectre is typically played in the off‑lane (solo safe lane) to give her space to farm safely and avoid the early aggression from heroes like Warlock, Rubick, and Snapfire, against whom she currently has the lowest win rates.

Who counters Spectra?

Heroes with strong early disables and burst—Warlock, Rubick, Snapfire, Dark Willow, and Lion—have the worst win‑rates versus Spectre (20‑39%). Building early Black King Bar or Linken’s Sphere, and playing defensively until you hit your core items, mitigates their impact.
spectre.counterHtml:
Spectre’s threat comes from her late‑game scaling: Haunt floods the map with global‑range, damage‑reflecting illusions that turn any team fight into a nightmare. The key to shutting her down is to deny her the farm and vision she needs to spawn those powerful Haunt copies, while forcing her to die before she can reliably trigger Desolate and Dispersion.

Why These Heroes Beat Spectre

Warlock

Warlock’s Fatal Bonds spreads a portion of incoming damage to all bonded enemies, instantly magnifying the damage Spectre deals to herself via Dispersion. Pair that with Chaotic Offering’s stun and Upheaval’s slow, and Spectre’s movement and illusion‑chasing become futile. Tip: land Fatal Bonds early in fights and follow up with a Golem smash to burst her while her Haunt is still on cooldown.

Rubick

Rubick can Spell‑Steal Spectre’s Haunt, turning her own global illusion against her and instantly removing her primary source of damage. Even without stealing Haunt, Telekinesis and Null Field give Rubick the burst and survivability to survive Dispersion spikes. Tip: prioritize stealing Haunt at the start of a team fight; the enemy’s Haunt disappears for the rest of the fight, leaving them vulnerable.

Snapfire

Snapfire’s Cookie provides a strong heal and a damage shield that mitigates the pure damage from Spectre’s Dispersion and Desolate. Meanwhile Firesnap Cookie and Mortimer Kisses apply heavy AoE damage and a stun that interrupts Spectre’s Shadow Step and prevents her from safely positioning for Haunt. Tip: keep a Cookie on hand for any Spectre dive; the shield buys you the time to force a retreat.

Dark Willow

Dark Willow’s Bramble Maze creates impassable terrain that blocks Spectre’s global Haunt from reaching key targets, while Cursed Crown silences and damages Spectre, preventing her from casting Shadow Step or Reality. The Shadow Realm ultimate grants invulnerability and a massive damage boost, letting you survive a Haunt onslaught and punish the delayed return. Tip: drop Bramble Maze around high‑ground or choke points before a fight to isolate Spectre’s Haunt.

Lion

Lion’s Mana Drain and Hex cripple Spectre’s ability to cast Shadow Step or Reality, effectively neutering her mobility and escape options. Finger of Death provides a burst of pure damage that bypasses Dispersion’s damage‑share reduction, allowing you to kill Spectre before she can spawn enough Haunt copies. Tip: open with Hex to lock Spectre in place, then immediately follow with Finger of Death while she’s still vulnerable.

Drafting Against Spectre

  • Prioritize heroes with strong early‑game kill pressure (e.g., burst mages, disables) to prevent her farm.
  • Choose global or vision‑granting ultimates that can track Haunt (e.g., Bounty Hunter’s Track, Zeus’s Thundergod’s Wrath).
  • Draft heroes with reliable silences or spell‑steal to shut down Haunt and Reality.
  • Include at least one reliable source of magical burst that ignores Dispersion’s damage split.

Laning Against Spectre

  • Harass aggressively before she can get a safe Spectral Dagger stack; she is weakest pre‑level 6.
  • Force her to use Shadow Step on creeps instead of heroes to waste its cooldown.
  • Trade when her Desolate is inactive (i.e., when allies are within 350 units of the target).
  • Use lane control abilities (e.g., pulls, slows) to keep her away from the creep wave, denying farm.

Itemizing Against Spectre

Black King Bar — blocks the magical burst from Haunt and prevents Dispersion from amplifying enemy spells.
Heaven’s Halberd — disarms Spectre, stopping her from dealing damage with her attacks and from triggering Desolate.
Manta Style — creates controllable illusions that can absorb Dispersion damage and provide vision on Haunt’s locations.
Scythe of Vyse — silences Spectre, denying her the use of Reality and Shadow Step during crucial engagements.

spirit-breaker.name: Spirit Breaker
spirit-breaker.guideHtml:
Spirit Breaker is a high‑mobility initiator and durable damage dealer who thrives on relentless pressure across the map. With a 51.7% win rate in the latest 548 k ranked games (OpenDota, July 2026), he sits comfortably in the meta as a semi‑carry that can both create space and finish fights.

How to Play Spirit Breaker

Laning Phase

  • Charge of Darkness early‑game vision: use the fixed‑sight component to scout enemy jungle or spot missing heroes; the charge’s speed ramps up after 1.5 s, so start a charge only when you can commit to the full run.
  • Bulldoze on the first level gives you +30% movement speed and 25% status resistance while charging; pair it with a short‑range Power Treads or Phase Boots to outrun lane creeps and secure early tower pressure.
  • Prioritize Greater Bash upgrades (level 2 at 6 min) to add a 20% stun chance on every attack—crucial against right‑lane heroes like Drow Ranger or Viper, who otherwise kite you.
  • Against lane‑dominant opponents (e.g., Huskar, Keeper of the Light), play a passive lane: last‑hit with your right‑click, use Charge of Darkness only to punish overextensions, and stack Bulldoze charges for later map‑wide ganks.
  • Use Empowering Haste procs from any successful Bash to chase down fleeing enemies; the duration pauses during a charge, so time your stuns right before initiating.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 12 (when Nether Strike becomes available): start split‑pushing and teleport‑style ganks; the extra knock‑back distance makes it easier to land a follow‑up Bash.
  • Secure vision around enemy jungle and high‑traffic lanes; a well‑timed Charge of Darkness into a fog‑of‑war gap can catch heroes like Marci off‑guard.
  • Group with your team after a successful Nether Strike to force fights; your combined Greater Bash stun and Empowering Haste speed boost make you the primary initiator.
  • When your core items (e.g., Phase Boots, Shadow Blade) are online, transition to a semi‑carry role: take towers with Charge of Darkness + Bulldoze, then finish with auto‑attacks that trigger Greater Bash.

Late Game

  • Win condition: use global Charge of Darkness to isolate and eliminate squishy back‑line heroes (e.g., Clinkz, Phantom Lancer) while your teammates focus the front line.
  • Positioning: stay near the front line to benefit from Greater Bash stuns; avoid prolonged fights against high‑magic‑damage heroes like Ancient Apparition unless you have Planar Pocket active.
  • What loses the game: getting caught in strong lane‑control heroes (e.g., Treant Protector, Keeper of the Light) who can block your charge and shut you down with disables; also, over‑extending without vision can lead to early deaths that waste your global presence.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in a potentially hostile lane.
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery after early skirmishes.
  • Stout Shield — mitigates harassment from right‑lane damage dealers.
  • Quelling Blade — helps secure last hits when you’re forced to farm under pressure.

Core Items

  • Phase Boots — the extra 20 % movement speed and the ability to phase through creeps amplify your charge and chase potential.
  • Shadow Blade — provides the invisibility needed to close the distance before a Charge of Darkness, and the burst damage on the break helps finish low‑HP targets.
  • Black King Bar — essential against magic‑heavy lineups (e.g., Ancient Apparition, Keeper of the Light) to ensure your charge and Bash land.
  • Aghanim’s Shard (optional) — upgrades Greater Bash damage and stun duration, making you more threatening in late‑game team fights.

Situational Items

  • Satanic — grants survivability against burst heroes like Huskar; active lifesteal can turn a Bash stun into a fight‑winning sustain.
  • Heart of Tarrasque — maximizes durability when you’re the primary front‑liner against tanky lineups.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target spells (useful vs. Keeper of the Light and Marci).
  • Manta Style — provides a way to dispel silences and slows, and the extra movement speed helps chase down evasive heroes like Slark.
  • Abyssal Blade — guarantees a stun when Greater Bash fails, useful against heroes with high evasion or blink (e.g., Phantom Lancer).

Common Mistakes

  • Charging without vision – using Charge of Darkness blindly often leads to wasted time and easy counter‑ganks; always check fog‑of‑war or place a ward first.
  • Ignoring Bash procs – failing to attack after a stun wastes Empowering Haste stacks; prioritize auto‑attacks to keep the speed boost active.
  • Over‑extending in lane – trying to farm aggressively against lane‑dominant heroes (e.g., Viper, Drow Ranger) leads to early deaths and loss of global impact.
  • Delaying core items – holding onto cheap items for too long reduces your threat level; aim for Phase Boots and Shadow Blade by 12 min to start effective global ganks.

FAQ

Is Spirit Breaker good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 51.7% win rate across over half a million ranked games (OpenDota, July 2026), Spirit Breaker remains a solid pick, especially on maps where global pressure can swing the game.

What lane does Spirit Breaker play?

Spirit Breaker is most commonly played in the safe lane (carry position) to farm while still having the freedom to roam with Charge of Darkness. He can also be flexed to the off‑lane if your team needs an early initiator.

Who counters Spirit Breaker?

The toughest matchups are against heroes that can block or punish his charge: Treant Protector, Huskar, Keeper of the Light, Drow Ranger, Marci, and Viper all have win rates below 45 % vs him, indicating they reliably limit his effectiveness. Vision, early disables, and strong lane control are key to countering him.
spirit-breaker.counterHtml:
Spirit Breaker’s threat comes from his unstoppable Charge of Darkness and the burst stun from Greater Bash, which lets him turn split‑pushing or farming into sudden ganks. The key to shutting him down is denying him a clean, uncontested target and forcing his charge to hit high‑mobility or crowd‑control heroes that can retaliate instantly.

Why These Heroes Beat Spirit Breaker

Treant Protector

Treant’s Nature’s Guise grants invisibility and a burst of movement speed, letting him slip out of a charge before the Bash lands, while Living Armor mitigates the damage from the charge’s impact. Tip: place a Living Armor ward on the lane’s trees and pop it when you see Spirit Breaker start his charge to block the stun and survive the follow‑up.

Huskar

Huskar’s Life Break and Burning Spear give him high burst damage that scales with his health, making a charge into him lethal for Spirit Breaker; his Inner Fire also provides a reliable stun that can punish a missed charge. Tip: keep your health above 50 % early so Huskar’s Lifesteal stays strong and his counter‑damage forces Spirit Breaker to think twice before committing.

Keeper of the Light

Keeper’s Illuminate and Chakra Magic give him sustained magical damage and mana sustain, while Mana Leak (when upgraded) can silence Spirit Breaker’s spell‑based abilities during a charge. Tip: use Recall to pull Spirit Breaker back into a dangerous position after he lands, turning his own charge distance against him.

Drow Ranger

Drow’s Gust provides a reliable knock‑back and silence that can interrupt a charge mid‑path, and her Precision Aura reduces Spirit Breaker’s attack damage, blunting his Greater Bash. Tip: position Drow near a wall or tree line so that a successful Gust pushes Spirit Breaker into terrain, extending his stun duration.

Marci

Marci’s Rebound lets her dash out of a charge’s line, and her Dispose can stun Spirit Breaker immediately after he lands, cancelling his Empowering Haste stack gain. Tip: bait Spirit Breaker into a charge, then use Rebound to close the gap and follow up with Dispose for a quick kill.

Drafting Against Spirit Breaker

  • Prioritize heroes with innate mobility or gap‑closers (e.g., Blink, Leap, or Phase Shift).
  • Choose strong early‑game disables that can stun or silence during a charge (e.g., stuns, silences, or hexes).
  • Ban or avoid heroes that give Spirit Breaker easy kill potential with high burst damage and low mobility (e.g., Clinkz, Death Prophet).

Laning Against Spirit Breaker

  • Harass him early; his damage output is low before level 6 and he lacks reliable lane control.
  • Trade when his Bulldoze is on cooldown, as he loses the extra movement speed and status resistance.
  • Force him to use Charge of Darkness on a tower or creep wave where you can predict the landing spot and set up a counter‑spell or trap.

Itemizing Against Spirit Breaker

Force Staff — pushes him out of melee range after a charge, breaking his follow‑up attack.
Eul’s Cyclone — suspends him mid‑charge, nullifying the Bash and buying time for a counter‑gank.
Ghost Scepter — makes you ethereal during his Greater Bash, negating the physical damage component.
Aghanim’s Shard (if applicable) — grants a short‑duration silence on attack, preventing him from using Empowering Haste after a stun.

storm-spirit.name: Storm Spirit
storm-spirit.guideHtml:
Storm Spirit remains a high‑skill, mobility‑centric hero that excels at picking off squishy targets and creating chaos in team fights. On patch 7.41 his overall pub win rate sits at 47.2 % across 247,489 ranked matches, placing him solidly in the mid‑tier of the current meta.

How to Play Storm Spirit

Laning Phase

  • Use Static Remnant to harass and zone out enemy off‑lane heroes; the 12‑second linger gives you a safe source of damage while you farm.
  • Pair Electric Vortex with a short‑range stun (e.g., Earthshaker’s Fissure) to secure early kills or force enemy pulls into your tower.
  • Manage mana carefully: each Ball Lightning cast costs 25 + 7.5 % of your total mana plus travel cost, so avoid spamming it before you have a reliable mana pool (e.g., early Arcane Boots).
  • Prioritize a mana regen source (e.g., Clarity or Arcane Boots) to keep Overload procs active for extra burst on your next attack.
  • Watch for the toughest lane matchups—Mirana, Chen, and Treant Protector—where your win rates drop to 31.6 %–35.7 % (OpenDota, July 2026). Play defensively and look for jungle rotations instead of forced trades.

Mid Game

  • Hit the 30‑level power spike (≈ 18 k HP, 700 + mana) and start looking for Ball Lightning ganks across the map; the mana cost scales with your pool, so a Kaya & Sange or Bloodstone will let you zip longer distances.
  • Secure Galvanized charges by farming heroes and neutral creeps; each kill gives you 0.2 mana regen and a permanent 0.1 regen, which fuels continuous Ball Lightning usage.
  • Target the easiest matchups—Naga Siren, Sven, Techies, Templar Assassin, Medusa, Death Prophet—where you win >56 % (OpenDota, July 2026). Use Electric Vortex to isolate them before a Ball Lightning dive.
  • Avoid prolonged fights against Faceless Void or Lycan until you have Eul’s Scepter or Black King Bar, as their lockdown can nullify your mobility.

Late Game

  • Win condition: pick off high‑value cores with a Ball Lightning → Electric Vortex → Overload combo, then finish with Static Remnant or a right‑click burst.
  • Positioning: stay just outside enemy vision, using Ball Lightning to reposition instantly; over‑extending without a BKB or Eul’s often leads to a quick death.
  • Losing the game usually stems from running out of mana on a Ball Lightning chase—ensure you have Bloodstone or Aghanim’s Scepter for mana sustain before committing.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango & Healing Salve — basic sustain in lane.
  • Faerie Fire — cheap burst to finish low‑HP enemies after a vortex.
  • Mantle of Intelligence — early gold boost for your first component.

Core Items

  • Arcane Boots — 250 mana and easy mana‑return for frequent Ball Lightning casts.
  • Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — provides a reliable stun, mana regen, and a way to dodge enemy disables.
  • Bloodstone — massive mana pool, regen, and death‑trigger charges that synergize with Galvanized.
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Static Remnant to a larger radius and reduces cooldown, amplifying wave clear and kill potential.

Situational Items

  • Black King Bar — essential against heavy lock‑down (e.g., Faceless Void, Enigma).
  • Kaya & Sange — adds damage, attack speed, and mana regen for longer Ball Lightning trips.
  • Shiva’s Guard — armor and aura against Huskar, Lycan, and other right‑click heavy heroes.
  • Linken’s Sphere — blocks single‑target spells like Chen’s Penitence or Mirana’s Arrow in your toughest matchups.
  • Scythe of Vyse — extra disable when you need reliable crowd control against elusive heroes.

Common Mistakes

  • Spamming Ball Lightning without mana backup – early games often end in a mana‑starved death; prioritize mana items first.
  • Ignoring Overload procs – many players forget that each spell adds a burst attack; weave spells between attacks for maximum damage.
  • Overcommitting into vision – diving without Eul’s or BKB against heroes like Faceless Void or Lycan leads to easy kills.
  • Neglecting Galvanized stacks – failing to farm kills early wastes the permanent mana‑regen benefit that powers late‑game mobility.

FAQ

Is Storm Spirit good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 47.2 % win rate across 247 k ranked games, Storm Spirit sits in the middle of the meta. His mobility and burst are strong, especially against the easier matchups where he wins >56 % (OpenDota, July 2026).

What lane does Storm Spirit play?

Storm Spirit is typically played in the mid lane. The lane offers the gold and experience needed to hit his 30‑level power spike and acquire the mana items essential for frequent Ball Lightning usage.

Who counters Storm Spirit?

The toughest counters are Mirana, Chen, Treant Protector, Huskar, Lycan, and Faceless Void, where his win rates drop to 31.6 %–41.2 % (OpenDota, July 2026). Their disables, high armor, or strong lockdown make it hard for Storm to survive long‑range engagements.
storm-spirit.counterHtml:
Storm Spirit’s threat lies in his insane mobility and burst damage: Ball Lightning lets him zip across the map, while Electric Vortex and Overload turn any skirmish into a lethal combo. The core of shutting him down is denying his mana, limiting his escape routes, and forcing him into fights where his burst cannot be followed up.

Why These Heroes Beat Storm Spirit

Mirana

Mirana’s Leap can close the distance before Storm can Ball‑Lightning away, and her Moonlight Shadow grants global invisibility that removes Storm’s vision for a crucial window, preventing him from targeting allies with Electric Vortex. Tip: Save Leap for the moment Storm initiates with Ball Lightning; a well‑timed stun from your support can lock him down while his mana is drained.

Chen

Chen’s Penitence and Hand of God provide constant sustain and a strong early‑game lane presence that forces Storm to waste mana on harass. More importantly, Chen’s Holy Persuasion can steal a neutral creep and later a Storm‑friendly creep, denying Storm the mana regeneration from kills that fuels his Galvanized. Tip: Prioritize pulling neutral camps early; each stolen creep delays Storm’s mana‑regen charge buildup.

Treant Protector

Treant’s Nature’s Guise grants invisibility and his Living Armor gives high survivability, making it hard for Storm to land a lethal Electric Vortex. The real counter is Overgrowth, which roots Storm in place, instantly draining his mana pool as he cannot Ball Lightning away while rooted. Tip: Time Overgrowth just after Storm initiates; the root forces him to either die or waste the large activation mana cost of Ball Lightning.

Huskar

Huskar’s Life Break scales with the target’s missing health, turning Storm’s low‑HP burst into a lethal suicide attack. Huskar’s Burning Spear applies constant damage that forces Storm to stay near a fountain for regeneration, while Inner Fire can stun Storm when he’s low on mana and trying to escape. Tip: Engage after Storm has used Ball Lightning once; his mana will be low, making his escape costly and his burst ineffective.

Lycan

Lycan’s Summon Wolves and Feral Impulse provide high sustained damage that forces Storm to spend mana on Overload and Electric Vortex to survive. More critically, Lycan’s Shapeshift gives him massive health and movement speed, allowing him to chase down Storm even when Ball Lightning is active, and the extra HP negates Storm’s burst. Tip: Push early with wolves; a well‑timed Shapeshift chase can catch Storm mid‑flight when his mana pool is already depleted.

Drafting Against Storm Spirit

  • Pick heroes with reliable disables (stuns, roots, silences) that can be cast before Ball Lightning is activated.
  • Prioritize global vision or invisibility detection (e.g., Sentry Wards, True Sight) to negate his mobility.
  • Choose heroes with high mana burn or mana‑draining abilities (e.g., Anti‑Mage’s Mana Void, Nyx’s Mana Burn).
  • Include at least one tanky front‑liner who can survive a burst and stay in lane to force Storm to waste mana on Overload.

Laning Against Storm Spirit

  • Harass aggressively early; Storm’s mana pool is small, so every spell cast (Static Remnant, Electric Vortex) drains his limited mana.
  • Trade when he is low on mana after a Ball Lightning chase—his attack damage and Overload burst are severely weakened.
  • Use creep equilibrium to keep him far from your tower; the longer he stays in lane, the more mana he loses to sustain.
  • Punish his attempts to use Electric Vortex on you by positioning behind a neutral creep or a warded area where you can quickly counter‑engage.

Itemizing Against Storm Spirit

Ghost Scepter — blocks his physical burst after he lands from Ball Lightning, buying time for mana‑drain abilities.
Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — cyclone removes Storm from the fight, forcing him to spend the massive activation mana for Ball Lightning to escape.
Scythe of Vyse — long‑duration hex neutralizes his mobility and prevents Electric Vortex pulls.
Aghanim’s Shard (Silencer) — Global Silence shuts down his spell‑based mana regeneration and makes Ball Lightning unusable.

faq.a: Storm Spirit is typically played in the mid lane. The lane offers the gold and experience needed to hit his 30‑level power spike and acquire the mana items essential for frequent Ball Lightning usage.

The toughest counters are Mirana, Chen, Treant Protector, Huskar, Lycan, and Faceless Void, where his win rates drop to 31.6 %–41.2 % (OpenDota, July 2026). Their disables, high armor, or strong lockdown make it hard for Storm to survive long‑range engagements.

sven.name: Sven
sven.guideHtml:
Sven is a melee strength hero famed for his burst damage and team‑fight presence, traditionally played as a hard‑carry who also brings decent disable and durability. On patch 7.41 his overall pub win rate sits at 50.3% across 240,835 recent ranked games, placing him solidly in the middle of the meta but still viable in coordinated play (OpenDota, July 2026).

How to Play Sven

Laning Phase

  • Storm Hammer early levels to secure last hits and harass melee supports; the small AoE stun is excellent against dual‑lane opponents like Lich or Sniper who rely on safe ranged harass.
  • Use Great Cleave on the first upgrade to pressure stacked creep waves and force the enemy off‑lane, especially effective against Lycan and Doom who like to farm jungle camps.
  • Warcry at level 6 gives armor and movement speed—activate before a contested pull or when the enemy support attempts a gank to mitigate early damage.
  • Prioritize a Tango‑Sentry‑Quelling Blade start; the extra damage from Great Cleave makes last‑hitting easier against high‑HP neutral creeps.
  • Keep an eye on the enemy mid‑lane hero’s Storm Hammer cooldown; a well‑timed stun from your own Storm Hammer can turn a 2‑vs‑1 into a kill.

Mid Game

  • God’s Strength at level 12 is a decisive power spike; look for 4‑man team fights where your cleave can hit multiple heroes.
  • Group with your cores and use Warcry before initiating; the armor boost lets you survive the initial burst from heroes like Earthshaker or Void Spirit (who currently give Sven sub‑40% win rates).
  • Secure Roshan once you have Black King Bar and Satanic; the extra health and damage from God’s Strength makes you the primary tank for the pit.
  • Split‑push with Great Cleave when the enemy team is distracted, but always keep a Storm Hammer ready to lock down any defender trying to contest.

Late Game

  • Win condition: force 5‑v‑5 engagements where you can land a single Storm Hammer followed by a God’s Strength‑boosted cleave, quickly eliminating the enemy back‑line.
  • Position near the front line but not at the extreme edge; you need to be close enough for cleave while staying out of long‑range nukes from Skywrath Mage or Sniper.
  • Losing the game usually stems from over‑extending without BKB against heroes with strong magical burst (e.g., Lich, Void Spirit) or failing to secure vision, allowing enemy initiators to lock you down before you can cast God’s Strength.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane against harass.
  • Quelling Blade — essential for efficient last‑hitting with Great Cleave.
  • Sentry Ward — block enemy vision and protect against invisible heroes like Phantom Lancer.
  • Healing Salve — emergency health after early ganks.

Core Items

  • Phase Boots — provides the movement speed needed to close the gap for Storm Hammer and improves cleave positioning.
  • Black King Bar — indispensable against magical burst from Earthshaker, Void Spirit, and Skywrath Mage (all hard counters).
  • Satanic — gives survivability in prolonged fights and synergizes with God’s Strength’s damage output.
  • Abyssal Blade — adds a reliable stun to complement Storm Hammer and helps lock down mobile heroes like Doom.

Situational Items

  • Echo Sabre — early damage and mana regen; great when facing high‑damage mid heroes.
  • Assault Cuirass — boosts armor for you and allies, useful against physical‑heavy lineups (e.g., Axe, Lycan).
  • Heaven’s Halberd — effective against right‑click carries such as Morphling or Phantom Lancer.
  • Monkey King Bar — counters evasion from Phantom Lancer or Doom’s Blink‑based escapes.
  • Shiva’s Guard — provides armor and an AoE slow, helpful versus Sniper and Skywrath Mage.

Common Mistakes

  • Relying on Storm Hammer cooldown – low‑MMR players often spam the stun without considering positioning, leaving them vulnerable to counter‑initiations.
  • Delaying God’s Strength – waiting too long to activate the buff wastes a major damage window; aim to cast it right before a team fight.
  • Over‑extending without BKB – engaging enemy back‑lines without magic immunity invites instant death from burst heroes.
  • Neglecting vision – failing to place wards lets enemy initiators flank and lock down Sven before he can cleave.

FAQ

Is Sven good in the current patch?

Yes. Sven holds a 50.3% win rate in recent pub games, making him a reliable pick in the current meta, especially when paired with strong team‑fight compositions.

What lane does Sven play?

Sven is most commonly played in the safe lane as a carry, where he can farm with Great Cleave and scale into the mid‑game power spikes provided by God’s Strength.

Who counters Sven?

The toughest matchups right now are Lycan, Earthshaker, Doom, Void Spirit, Lich, and Sniper, all of which give Sven sub‑40% win rates (OpenDota, July 2026). Building early BKB, maintaining vision, and timing God’s Strength are key to surviving their burst and disables.
sven.counterHtml:
Sven’s threat comes from his massive burst damage and team‑fight presence: Storm Hammer can lock down a target for a lethal combo, while Great Cleave and God’s Strength let him shred multiple heroes in seconds. The key to shutting him down is to deny him the early‑game space to farm his strength and to punish his long cooldowns with hard‑lock, silence, or burst damage before he can activate his ultimate.

Why These Heroes Beat Sven

Lycan

Lycan’s summons and Summon Wolves provide constant pressure and split‑push, forcing Sven to split his farm and lose the gold needed for God’s Strength. Use Feral Impulse to keep his wolves alive and Shapeshift to dodge Storm Hammer’s stun window. Tip: start with a early Lycan’s Summon Wolves and pressure the off‑lane; Sven will struggle to get a safe farm.

Earthshaker

Earthshaker’s Fissure creates an unbreakable wall that blocks Sven’s Great Cleave and isolates him from his teammates. Enchant Totem adds burst damage that can kill Sven before he lands Storm Hammer. Tip: time a Fissure just as Sven begins his Warcry; the armor boost is wasted when he’s trapped.

Doom

Doom’s Doom silence removes Sven’s ability to cast Storm Hammer and Warcry, while the damage over time punishes his low health pool before God’s Strength is up. Devour can also eat Sven’s Great Cleave damage. Tip: cast Doom the moment Sven initiates with Storm Hammer; the stun is instantly nullified.

Void Spirit

Void Spirit’s Astral Step lets him dodge Storm Hammer and Great Cleave, and his Resonant Pulse applies a strong silence that shuts down Warcry and God’s Strength. The burst from Aether Remnant can finish Sven before his ultimate cooldown. Tip: engage with Astral Step from the opposite side of Sven’s stun radius to avoid the stun entirely.

Lich

Lich’s Frost Blast and Ice Armor give him a reliable stun and damage block that mitigates Sven’s burst. Chain Frost can bounce through Sven’s cleaved allies, turning his own cleave radius against his team. Tip: keep Ice Armor active and bait Storm Hammer into a Frost Blast‑stunned Sven for a quick kill.

Drafting Against Sven

  • Prioritize heroes with hard‑lock or silence (e.g., Doom, Earthshaker, Silencer).
  • Choose split‑push or lane‑pressure heroes that deny farm (Lycan, Nature’s Prophet).
  • Pick mobile heroes that can dodge Storm Hammer’s stun radius (Void Spirit, Puck).
  • Ban heroes that give Sven easy strength spikes (e.g., Morphling) if you want to limit his late‑game scaling.

Laning Against Sven

  • Harass him before he gets a Warcry; his early attacks are weak and lack armor.
  • Trade when his Storm Hammer is on cooldown – his stun is a long 8‑second window.
  • Use ranged poke or sustain to force him to miss last hits; without farm he can’t reach God’s Strength.
  • Punish his attempts to use Great Cleave on creeps by pulling them into a neutral camp or tower range.

Itemizing Against Sven

Black King Bar — grants magic immunity, nullifying Storm Hammer and Warcry’s armor boost.
Heaven’s Halberd — disarms Sven, preventing his cleave damage and making his burst ineffective.
Ghost Scepter — makes you ethereal, causing Great Cleave to miss and reducing Storm Hammer’s damage.
Scythe of Vyse — a hard‑lock that removes Sven’s ability to cast any spells during his ultimate window.

techies.name: Techies
techies.guideHtml:
Techies is a niche Nuker/Disabler whose primary toolbox revolves around planting explosive mines and detonating them for massive burst damage. On patch 7.41 his overall pub win‑rate sits at 50.6 % (≈350 k recent ranked games), putting him just above average but still very situational.

How to Play Techies

Laning Phase

  • Plant early Proximity Mines near the creep wave edge; they provide lane control and force the enemy to either waste HP on explosions or pull back, buying you safe farm.
  • Use Sticky Bomb on enemy heroes that step into your mine radius to apply a slow and guarantee a follow‑up detonation.
  • M.A.D. should be leveled first for the mana regen boost, allowing you to sustain a high mine‑planting cadence.
  • When the lane becomes contested, drop a Minefield Sign to buff the mines in the contested area and make them harder to clear.
  • Against hard‑lane heroes like Bane or Muerta (Techies win ≈ 36 % vs them), play ultra‑defensive: keep mines hidden behind neutral camps and avoid aggressive trades until you have a safe Blast Off! window.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 6 with Blast Off! – look for team fights or split‑push opportunities where you can dive into the enemy’s backline and stun multiple heroes.
  • Rotate to high‑traffic jungle paths and river choke points; plant dense mine clusters behind trees and use Detonate Tazer on allies to create surprise burst damage.
  • Secure vision around your mines with Observer Wards and a Minefield Sign; the sign makes mines 15 % stronger and immune to enemy mine‑clearing abilities.
  • Prioritize taking Roshan after you have at least 2‑3 stacked mine fields around the pit; a single detonation can shred the boss and force the enemy to waste a second hand.

Late Game

  • Win condition: force the enemy to play ultra‑defensively by controlling key pathways with invisible mines; a well‑timed Blast Off! into a clustered minefield can end a game in seconds.
  • Position yourself behind front‑line heroes; you are extremely squishy, so stay out of vision until you can safely drop a mine or use Reactive Tazer on an ally to protect them while you detonate.
  • Losing the game usually comes from over‑extending without a mine backup or getting caught before you can Detonate; once you die, the death‑barrel explosion is weak compared to your mines, so avoid unnecessary fights.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain while you plant mines in lane.
  • Healing Salve — emergency HP for the inevitable early harass.
  • Observer Ward — early vision to protect your mine placements.
  • Clarity — mana for early Sticky Bomb and mine planting.

Core Items

  • Aghanim's Scepter — upgrades Blast Off! to a larger AoE and lower cooldown, turning Techies into a true team‑fight initiator.
  • Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — provides a reliable escape and a way to set up mine detonations on stunned enemies.
  • Force Staff — essential for repositioning into mine fields or escaping after a Blast Off! dive.
  • Mekansm — gives team survivability; the heal can offset the damage you take when diving.

Situational Items

  • Black King Bar — against heavy magical burst (e.g., Phoenix, Bane) where you need to survive long enough to detonate.
  • Ghost Scepter — when facing right‑click heroes like Monkey King or Bristleback who can quickly kill you.
  • Aether Lens — increases the cast range of Sticky Bomb and Detonate abilities, letting you trigger mines from safety.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target disables that would otherwise prevent you from using Blast Off! or Detonate Tazer.
  • Scythe of Vyse — extra disable to lock down heroes that can easily dodge mines (e.g., Marci).

Common Mistakes

  • Planting mines in obvious spots – enemies learn the patterns and use early detection items; vary depth and use the Minefield Sign to keep mines hidden.
  • Using Blast Off! without backup – diving alone into a well‑warded fight usually results in a quick death; always pair it with a stun or a teammate ready to follow up.
  • Neglecting mana management – forgetting to level M.A.D. early leads to a lack of mines; keep a steady supply of Clarity or Mana Potion until you have the regen item.
  • Over‑extending after a kill – many players celebrate a successful detonation by chasing; the enemy will often have vision and can collapse on you before you plant another mine.

FAQ

Is Techies good in the current patch?

Yes. Techies sits at a 50.6 % win‑rate on patch 7.41, slightly above average. His strength comes from map control and burst potential, though he remains vulnerable to heroes with strong early pressure like Bane or Muerta.

What lane does Techies play?

Techies is most commonly played in the safe lane (carry side) to give him space to plant mines and avoid early aggression. He can also be a solo off‑lane if the enemy lineup is weak to mines (e.g., against Viper or Luna).

Who counters Techies?

The toughest match‑ups are Bane, Muerta, Phoenix, Marci, Bristleback, and Monkey King, where Techies wins only 36‑41 % of games. These heroes provide strong disables, burst, or tankiness that can out‑maneuver or survive mine damage. Vision‑heavy lineups and early aggressive pressure are also effective counters.
techies.counterHtml:
Techies thrives on hidden damage, map control, and forcing opponents to play overly cautious. The key to shutting him down is denying his mines, bursting his low‑health hero quickly, and using mobility or purge to escape or destroy his explosive setups.

Why These Heroes Beat Techies

Bane

Bane’s Nightmare and Fiend’s Grip lock Techies in place, preventing him from detonating mines or using Blast Off! while you burst him with Brain Sap. Tip: keep a Soul Ring or Arcane Boots ready to sustain the mana‑heavy combo and finish Techies before he can retreat to a minefield.

Muerta

Muerta’s Dead Shot and Dead of Night provide reliable long‑range burst that can kill Techies before he can plant or detonate mines, and her Soul Rip grants a heal that offsets the self‑damage from Blast Off! Tip: position behind a neutral creep to block line‑of‑sight mines while you land your ultimate.

Phoenix

Phoenix’s Supernova forces Techies to reveal his position and makes his mines ineffective while the egg is alive; the subsequent Sun Ray deals massive AOE damage that can shred Techies’ low HP. Tip: use Fire Spirits to scout common mine locations before committing to a fight.

Marci

Marci’s Rebound and Sidekick give her the mobility to dodge mines and close the gap, while her Dispose instantly removes Techies from the fight, preventing any mine detonation. Tip: time Dispose just after Techies attempts Blast Off! to catch him mid‑air and nullify his stun.

Bristleback

Bristleback’s Quill Spray punishes Techies for standing near his own mines, and his Warpath grants high survivability against burst, allowing him to tank mine explosions and push lanes. Tip: build Vanguard early to further mitigate mine damage and force Techies to play even more defensively.

Drafting Against Techies

  • Prioritize heroes with hard disables (stuns, silences, long‑duration roots).
  • Choose high burst damage heroes that can kill Techies before he plants mines.
  • Include mobile heroes or those with blink/charge abilities to escape minefields.
  • Consider heroes with true‑sight or detection (e.g., Bounty Hunter, Slark) to reveal mines early.

Laning Against Techies

  • Harass Techies early; his early game damage is low and he lacks reliable escape.
  • Trade when his mines are on cooldown (≈30 s after a detonation).
  • Force him to use Reactive Tazer on allies, then quickly kill the stunned target.
  • Ward or place a Minefield Sign yourself to force his mines to explode harmlessly.

Itemizing Against Techies

Force Staff — pushes you out of mine blast radius and can pull Techies into your own AoE.
Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — cyclones Techies, nullifying his Blast Off! and giving you time to destroy mines.
Glimmer Cape — grants temporary invisibility, letting you walk through minefields without triggering them.
Black King Bar — prevents the disarm and damage from Reactive Tazer and lets you dive through mines safely.

templar-assassin.name: Templar Assassin
templar-assassin.guideHtml:
Templar Assassin (Lanaya) is a high‑damage, escape‑oriented core who thrives on burst damage and lane dominance. On patch 7.41 her overall win rate sits at 45.9 % across 147 k recent ranked games, placing her as a solid but not overwhelming pick in the current meta.

How to Play Templar Assassin

Laning Phase

  • Meld + Refraction: Start the lane with Meld for free invisibility; pop Meld on the first creep wave to secure a free Refraction charge and an early armor‑shred on the enemy offlaner.
  • Psi Blades: Use the extra attack range to harass melee supports and pull creep aggro, while the split damage helps clear stacked neutral camps for extra gold.
  • Trap placement: Drop a Psionic Trap near the enemy pull‑creep spot; spring it when they attempt to pull to punish them and gain a 20 % slow for follow‑up attacks.
  • Early Refraction stacking: Aim to have at least two Refraction charges (damage + evasion) by 10 minutes; this makes you much harder to kill against tanky matchups like Bristleback.
  • Lane matchups: Against hard‑kill heroes (e.g., Anti‑Mage, Kunkka) play aggressively; against durability heroes (Treant Protector, Bristleback) focus on farming and avoid extended trades.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at 6 k: With Meld, Psi Blades, and a Desolator or Eye of Skadi, you can burst‑kill most mid‑lane heroes and secure early Roshan.
  • Map control with traps: Plant traps in high‑traffic jungle paths and near enemy pull camps; use Psionic Projection to jump onto a sprung trap for surprise damage and vision.
  • Objective focus: Prioritize taking Tier 1 towers after a successful gank; your split damage from Psi Blades makes tower sieges efficient.
  • Pick fights wisely: Avoid prolonged fights against heroes with strong sustain or disables (e.g., Grimstroke, Bane) – use Meld to blink out after the burst.

Late Game

  • Win condition – burst and pick‑offs: With Refraction maxed and a Bloodthorn/Satanic combo, you can instantly eliminate squishy carries before they react.
  • Positioning: Stay near the backline, using Meld for safety and traps for zone control; a single mis‑step into a teamfight against Faceless Void or Huskar can be fatal.
  • What loses the game: Over‑extending without traps, getting caught by disables, or failing to secure vision for your traps, especially against heroes that can purge or out‑range you.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain for early lane farming.
  • Healing Salve — emergency health against early harass.
  • Iron Branch ×2 — cheap stats and can be later built into a Magic Wand.
  • Faerie Fire — burst health for clutch trades.
  • Observer Ward — early vision to protect against ganks.

Core Items

  • Desolator — amplifies Refraction’s armor‑shred, essential against tanky heroes.
  • Phase Boots — provides mobility to chase or escape after a Meld burst.
  • Black King Bar — necessary against heavy magical disables (Grimstroke, Bane).
  • Satanic — gives survivability in extended fights, especially versus Huskar or Faceless Void.

Situational Items

  • Eye of Skadi — adds health and a strong slow, great against mobile heroes like Weaver.
  • Bloodthorn — guarantees critical burst on squishy targets; ideal vs. Anti‑Mage or Kunkka.
  • Manta Style — dispels silences and provides extra damage; useful against Bane’s nightmare.
  • Linken’s Sphere – blocks single‑target disables from Grimstroke or Bane.
  • Abyssal Blade – adds a reliable stun for locking down heroes that can blink away.
  • Lotus Orb – reflects targeted spells, helpful versus Faceless Void’s Chronosphere setup.

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑relying on Meld for damage – Meld’s bonus damage ends once you attack; many players forget to follow up with Refraction or Psi Blades, wasting the burst.
  • Neglecting trap placement – Without traps, Lanaya loses her map‑control edge; low‑MMR players often forget to plant or spring them.
  • Poor timing of Psionic Projection – Using the channel on a fully charged trap is optimal; casting early wastes the 400 damage burst.
  • Engaging without BKB – Jumping into fights against heavy magical disables (Grimstroke, Bane) leads to easy deaths.

FAQ

Is Templar Assassin good in the current patch?

Yes. Although her overall win rate is 45.9 %, she performs strongly in favorable matchups (e.g., 62.2 % vs. Kunkka) and remains a viable carry/escape hero when played with proper trap control and burst items.

What lane does Templar Assassin play?

Templar Assassin is typically played in the safe lane as a core, allowing her to farm Refraction stacks and place Psionic Traps safely while scaling into a mid‑game burst threat.

Who counters Templar Assassin?

The toughest opponents right now are Treant Protector (32.8 % win), Bristleback (34.4 %), Grimstroke (34.4 %), Bane (36.5 %), Faceless Void (38.1 %), and Huskar (38.9 %). These heroes either out‑sustain her burst, provide strong disables, or can out‑range her trap‑based control.
templar-assassin.counterHtml:
Templar Assassin’s burst damage, Refraction‑based survivability, and long‑range Psi Blades make her a lethal lane‑dominant assassin who can quickly melt squishy cores. The key to shutting her down is to deny her the safe window for Refraction stacks and to force her into fights where her melee‑centric burst and trap‑based control are nullified.

Why These Heroes Beat Templar Assassin

Treant Protector

Treant’s Nature’s Grasp and Living Armor provide constant area control and damage reduction, preventing TA from safely stacking Refraction or landing Psi Blades on clustered heroes. Use Overgrowth to root TA mid‑lane, forcing her to waste Meld on a stationary target.
Tip: Drop a Living Armor on your core early; the armor bonus reduces the armor‑shredding from Meld and makes your hero harder to burst.

Bristleback

Bristleback’s Bristleback passive gives him massive damage reduction from the back, the direction TA’s Psi Blades usually hit after a split. His Quill Spray punishes TA’s attempts to chase, and Warpath grants him the sustain to out‑last Refraction’s barrier.
Tip: Stay behind your creeps and let Bristleback’s passive absorb TA’s burst; only engage when his Quill Spray is on cooldown.

Grimstroke

Grimstroke’s Soul Bind locks TA to an ally, instantly breaking Meld invisibility and exposing her to early damage. Phantom Rush provides mobility to dodge Psi Blades, while Stroke of Fate deals pure damage that ignores TA’s armor‑shredding.
Tip: Aim Soul Bind on TA and a nearby support; the tether forces her to waste Meld and makes her vulnerable to follow‑up disables.

Bane

Bane’s Nightmare and Enfeeble suppress TA’s burst window, preventing her from activating Refraction or landing a lethal Meld attack. Fiend’s Grip locks her down for 4 seconds, nullifying Psionic Projection and trap placement.
Tip: Save Nightmare for the moment TA attempts to spring a trap; the silence and damage over time cripple her early game momentum.

Faceless Void

Void’s Time Walk lets him close the distance while negating TA’s Refraction damage reduction, and Chronosphere immobilizes her, making her Meld useless and preventing trap detonation. The ultimate also blocks Psionic Projection’s channel.
Tip: Initiate Chronosphere when TA’s Refraction barrier is down; the guaranteed hit forces her to waste Meld and leaves her vulnerable to follow‑up damage.

Drafting Against Templar Assassin

  • Prioritize heroes with reliable disables or silences (e.g., Bane, Grimstroke, Lion).
  • Pick tanky or high‑armor heroes that can survive her burst (e.g., Bristleback, Treant Protector).
  • Include strong wave‑clear or split‑push to force her to use traps defensively.
  • Avoid pure right‑click heroes without escape tools; TA’s Psi Blades will punish them.

Laning Against Templar Assassin

  • Harass her before she can stack Refraction; use early harass spells or auto‑attacks.
  • Trade when she is out of Meld range—once she moves to attack, her invisibility is broken and she loses the armor‑shred bonus.
  • Force her to use Psionic Trap defensively; a well‑timed block or stun will waste the trap’s charge.
  • Keep a creep wave near your tower to limit her ability to jump onto back‑line heroes with Psi Blades.

Itemizing Against Templar Assassin

Mekansm — provides burst armor and heal that mitigates the armor loss from Meld and reduces burst damage.
Ghost Scepter — makes you ethereal, nullifying her melee Psi Blade damage and the bonus damage from Meld.
Lotus Orb — reflects her targeted disables (e.g., Psionic Projection) and removes Refraction stacks when she tries to lock you down.
Crimson Guard — high armor block absorbs the bulk of her burst, especially when Refraction is on cooldown.

terrorblade.name: Terrorblade
terrorblade.guideHtml:
Terrorblade is a late‑game hyper‑carry whose strength comes from massive illusion damage and a powerful Metamorphosis transformation. In patch 7.41 his overall pub win rate sits at 46.9% over 112,944 ranked games, making him a solid but not dominant pick in the current meta.

How to Play Terrorblade

Laning Phase

  • Conjure Image early to secure lane equilibrium; the illusion can harass and block creep aggro while you farm safely.
  • Use Reflection on enemy heroes that push aggressively (e.g., Axe, Centaur) to slow them and force them to fight their own reflection, buying you time to stack and farm.
  • Pair Demon Zeal with a short‑range illusion to gain burst movement and attack speed for quick tower hits; remember it cannot be cast while in Metamorphosis.
  • Prioritize stacking the off‑lane jungle when your lane opponent is a strong early‑game hero (Morphling, Drow Ranger) to compensate for Terrorblade’s weak start.
  • Keep an eye on Sunder cooldown; a well‑timed Sunder against a low‑HP enemy can turn a dangerous gank into a safe escape.

Mid Game

  • Hit Metamorphosis as soon as you have a reliable farm of 25‑30k net worth; the transformation also upgrades any illusion within 1200 range, dramatically increasing split‑push pressure.
  • Group with teammates after a successful Terror Wave to capitalize on the fear and the short Metamorphosis grant, forcing fights on your terms.
  • Start building Dark Unity‑enhanced illusion damage; push towers while the enemy is distracted elsewhere.
  • Avoid extended team fights against heroes with strong disables (Axe, Abaddon) until you have at least Heart of Tarrasque or Butterfly for survivability.

Late Game

  • Win condition: overwhelm towers and Roshan with a swarm of high‑damage Metamorphosed illusions while you stay protected behind Sunder and Demon Zeal bursts.
  • Position near the frontline but never front‑line; keep a safe distance to let your reflections and illusions soak damage.
  • Losing the game usually stems from being caught without Sunder ready against burst‑heavy heroes (e.g., Pugna, Razor) or from running out of mana for Metamorphosis during a decisive fight.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango & Healing Salve — sustain in the lane against harassment.
  • Slippers of Agility — early attack damage for the Conjure Image illusion.
  • Iron Branch x2 — cheap stats and can be later built into a Magic Wand.
  • Faerie Fire — emergency burst health for early gank survivability.

Core Items

  • Power Treads — attack speed and switchable attributes for better farming and survivability.
  • Manta Style — provides a second illusion, dispels silences, and synergizes with Dark Unity.
  • Black King Bar — essential against heavy disable lineups (Axe, Abaddon).
  • Butterfly — massive evasion and attack speed, turning your Metamorphosis into a true late‑game threat.
  • Satanic — gives reliable lifesteal and the Sunder safety net in team fights.

Situational Items

  • Heart of Tarrasque — when facing tanky frontliners like Centaur or Dawnbreaker.
  • Abyssal Blade — for a stun lock on slippery heroes (Morphling, Razor).
  • Mekansm / Guardian Greaves — if your team lacks reliable healing and you need to stay in front of fights.
  • Linken's Sphere – blocks single‑target disables from heroes like Pugna or Drow Ranger.
  • Divine Rapier – ultra‑high damage option when you have a safe farm and the enemy lacks burst kill potential.

Common Mistakes

  • Casting Demon Zeal while in Metamorphosis – the ability is disabled, wasting the HP cost and the movement/AS boost.
  • Over‑extending without Sunder – early‑game Terrorblade lacks durability; a missed Sunder often leads to a death against burst heroes.
  • Neglecting illusion upgrades – forgetting that only illusions within 1200 range gain Metamorphosis damage drastically reduces push potential.
  • Building too much damage before survivability – ignoring BKB or Heart makes you an easy target for Axe, Abaddon, and other disable‑heavy heroes.

FAQ

Is Terrorblade good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 46.9% win rate across over 112k games, Terrorblade remains a viable carry, especially against heroes he excels versus like Magnus (64% win) and Razor (64%). He does struggle against high‑disable heroes (e.g., Axe 39.2% win), so proper itemization is key.

What lane does Terrorblade play?

Terrorblade is traditionally played in the safe lane (position 1) to maximize early farm and allow safe stacking. In some aggressive lineups he can be flexed to the off‑lane, but the safe lane remains optimal for hitting his mid‑game power spikes.

Who counters Terrorblade?

The toughest matchups right now are Morphling (36.1% win), Abaddon (38.9%), Axe (39.2%), and Centaur Warrunner (41.2%). These heroes either out‑scale his early game or provide disables that prevent him from safely casting Metamorphosis and Sunder. Building BKB, Heart, or early defensive items can mitigate their impact.
terrorblade.counterHtml:
Terrorblade’s threat comes from his massive late‑game damage window: Metamorphosis‑empowered attacks, a swarm of high‑damage illusions, and the health‑stealing Sunder that can turn a 1‑vantage into a 10‑vantage. The core way to shut him down is to deny him the space and survivability he needs to build those illusions and to punish him before he can lock‑in Metamorphosis.

Why These Heroes Beat Terrorblade

Morphling

Morphling’s Adaptive Strike and Waveform let him close the distance and burst the illusion army before Terrorblade can scale, while his attribute shift can out‑heal the HP loss from Demon Zeal and Sunder. Tip: Keep Morphling’s Morph ability on cooldown and force him to use it defensively; then drop a well‑timed Waveform into Terrorblade’s Reflection zone to cancel the slow and force a melee fight.

Abaddon

Abaddon’s Aphotic Shield removes the damage from Terrorblade’s reflections and can instantly purge the slow from Reflection, while Mist Coil provides cheap sustain that outpaces Demon Zeal’s HP cost. His ultimate, Borrowed Time, makes him effectively untargetable for Sunder. Tip: Position yourself so that your Shield lands on Terrorblade’s Reflection; the shield will block the damage and the slow, forcing Terrorblade to waste his burst.

Axe

Axe’s Berserker’s Call forces Terrorblade to attack a nearby hero, instantly breaking the illusion‑only damage chain and preventing Metamorphosis from activating on the melee target. Counter Helix punishes Terrorblade’s low‑health pushes after Demon Zeal. Tip: Initiate with Call right after Terrorblade casts Demon Zeal; the forced melee attack interrupts his HP‑regen window and lets you follow with a Counter Helix combo.

Centaur Warrunner

Centaur’s Hoof Stomp provides a reliable AoE stun that hits both Terrorblade and his reflections, negating the slow and buying time for your team to focus the real hero. His ultimate, Stampede, lets allies outrun Terrorblade’s Reflection slow and escape his wave of fear. Tip: Time Hoof Stomp just as Terrorblade finishes his Reflection; the stun disables the illusion damage and lets you burst him with a follow‑up physical hit.

Drow Ranger

Drow’s Precision Aura reduces Terrorblade’s attack damage, making his illusion swarm far less threatening, while her Frost Arrows and Gust silence prevent him from casting Metamorphosis or Sunder in a clutch fight. Tip: Keep Drow’s Frost Arrows on Terrorblade’s melee attacks; the slow stacks with Reflection’s own slow, making it easier to kite him out of range.

Drafting Against Terrorblade

  • Prioritize heroes with strong early‑game burst or disables (e.g., Axe, Morphling, Centaur).
  • Include at least one tank with AoE stun or shield that can absorb Reflection damage (Abaddon, Centaur).
  • Pick heroes with silence or mana‑drain to delay Metamorphosis and Sunder (Drow Ranger, Silencer).
  • Consider banning high‑mobility split‑pushers that can give Terrorblade space to farm (e.g., Nature’s Prophet).

Laning Against Terrorblade

  • Harass him before he can stack a full Conjure Image; early tower pressure forces him to miss out on illusion farm.
  • Exploit his low HP after Demon Zeal—attack when his health dip is visible, as he cannot cast Zeal while in Metamorphosis.
  • Punish his reliance on ranged attacks by forcing melee trades; his Reflection slows both him and his target, making him vulnerable to counter‑attacks.
  • Use lane control abilities (e.g., Hoof Stomp, Waveform) to break his illusion line and force him to retreat.

Itemizing Against Terrorblade

Crimson Guard — blocks the massive illusion damage and Reflection’s burst, letting you survive the early game.
Heaven’s Halberd — disarms Terrorblade, preventing him from landing Metamorphosis attacks and Sunder swaps.
Ghost Scepter — makes you immune to his ranged Metamorphosis damage while you wait for your team’s disables.
Abyssal Blade — provides a reliable stun to lock Terrorblade down, stopping his illusion‑based escape and Sunder timing.

tidehunter.name: Tidehunter
tidehunter.guideHtml:
Tidehunter is a durable initiator and disabler whose kit revolves around massive area control and damage reduction. In the current 7.41 meta his overall pub win rate sits at 49.8% over 307,025 ranked games, making him a solid but not dominant pick.

How to Play Tidehunter

Laning Phase

  • Use Gush on enemy heroes to apply a strong slow and armor reduction, making it easier for your carry to secure last hits and for you to harass.
  • Kraken Shell passively blocks a chunk of incoming physical damage; stay near the creep wave to soak tower hits and force opponents to waste damage on a tanky hero.
  • Pair Anchor Smash with Gush on melee heroes (e.g., enemy offlaners) to cut their attack damage while you trade. The radius scales with your attack range, so you can hit multiple foes in a tight lane.
  • When the enemy support tries to zone you with disables, step back and let Kraken Shell purge the debuff if the damage threshold is met.
  • Against hard‑hitting lane opponents (e.g., Huskar, Ember Spirit), play conservatively and only engage when you have a clear Dead in the Water leash opportunity.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 6: Ravage gives you a game‑changing teamfight tool; look for clustered enemy groups near Roshan or after a tower dive.
  • Aim to secure Roshan with your tankiness; Kraken Shell absorbs the damage while your team focuses the boss.
  • Use Dead in the Water on high‑mobility heroes (e.g., Ember Spirit, Nyx Assassin) to lock them down before a teamfight.
  • Prioritize vision around enemy jungle entrances; a well‑timed Ravage on a caught group can swing the map control in your favor.

Late Game

  • Win condition: initiate with Ravage followed by a Dead in the Water leash on the enemy carry, then let your team follow up. Your durability lets you survive long enough for the damage to land.
  • Position near the front line but keep a safe distance from enemy disables; Kraken Shell will cleanse a stun only if you take enough damage, so avoid standing alone under burst.
  • Losing the game often comes from over‑extending without Ravage cooldown—enemy heroes will out‑maneuver you and focus your squishier teammates.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in the off‑lane while you build tank items.
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery after early skirmishes.
  • Stout Shield — extra block against harassment and creep damage.
  • Quelling Blade — helps secure last hits when you’re forced to farm under tower.

Core Items

  • Blink Dagger — provides the gap needed to land Ravage and Dead in the Water on key targets.
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Ravage to a larger radius and adds a stun, dramatically increasing teamfight impact.
  • Shiva’s Guard — armor and an active slow complement Gush and further reduce enemy attack damage.
  • Heart of Tarrasque — maximizes your tankiness, allowing you to stay in the fight while your teammates follow up.

Situational Items

  • Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target disables; useful against Clockwerk and Nyx Assassin.
  • Black King Bar — guarantees you can cast Ravage through heavy magical burst (e.g., from Ember Spirit).
  • Pipe of Insight — mitigates magic damage from heroes like Huskar and Ember Spirit in late‑game fights.
  • Crimson Guard — extra physical block when facing line‑ups with high physical DPS (e.g., Treant Protector).
  • Assault Cuirass — reduces enemy armor, synergizing with Gush and Anchor Smash.

Common Mistakes

  • Wasting Ravage on scattered enemies instead of waiting for a tight cluster.
  • Ignoring Kraken Shell’s purge mechanic and standing still to let the threshold trigger, which leaves you vulnerable to disables.
  • Over‑committing without a leash; casting Dead in the Water on a hero who can quickly escape (e.g., Ember Spirit) often results in wasted cooldown.
  • Building too much damage early and lacking tank items, causing you to die before you can use your teamfight tools.

FAQ

Is Tidehunter good in the current patch?

Yes. His 49.8% win rate across over 300k ranked games shows he’s a viable pick, especially when you can land Ravage and Dead in the Water reliably.

What lane does Tidehunter play?

Tidehunter is typically played in the off‑lane (solo safe lane) where his durability and crowd‑control abilities allow him to survive and create space for his carry.

Who counters Tidehunter?

The toughest match‑ups right now are Treant Protector (34.7% win), Clockwerk (36.1%), Huskar (37.7%), Ember Spirit (39.3%), Nyx Assassin (40.2%), and Clinkz (40.4%). These heroes either out‑maneuver his initiation or apply constant pressure that negates his tankiness.
tidehunter.counterHtml:
Tidehunter’s massive team‑fight presence comes from his long‑range Anchor Smash, his damage‑reducing Kraken Shell, and the game‑changing Ravage. To shut him down you must deny him the space to land Ravage, strip his armor‑reduction, and punish his low mobility before he can anchor you down.

Why These Heroes Beat Tidehunter

Treant Protector

Treant’s Nature’s Grasp and Overgrowth lock Tidehunter in place, preventing the anchor‑leash from pulling him and nullifying Ravage’s stun radius. Use the early Living Armor block to survive the first Gush‑hit and then force a fight when Treant’s ultimate is up. Tip: Stack trees and keep the lane tight so Treant can land Overgrowth on Tidehunter’s positioning.

Clockwerk

Clockwerk’s Hookshot can pull Tidehunter out of Ravage range, and his Battery Assault silences Tidehunter, cancelling Gush and Ravage’s channel. The Power Cogs shield blocks the anchor‑smash damage and reduces the effectiveness of Kraken Shell. Tip: Initiate with Hookshot as soon as Tidehunter steps into vision; the leash from Dead in the Water is useless against a stunned Clockwerk.

Huskar

Huskar’s Burning Spear and Life Break ignore armor reductions, rendering Anchor Smash’s damage drop negligible. His Inner Fire can stun Tidehunter before Ravage lands, and his Berserker’s Blood gives him the survivability to out‑trade Gush. Tip: Trade early with a spear‑stacked harass; Huskar’s health‑based damage scales faster than Tidehunter’s static burst.

Ember Spirit

Ember’s Sleight of Fist lets him dodge the anchor‑smash radius and quickly close the gap, while Flame Guard blocks the magic damage from Gush and Ravage. His Fire Remnant provides instant repositioning, making the anchor leash ineffective. Tip: Use Flame Guard pre‑emptively when you suspect a Ravage; the damage block also mitigates Gush’s armor‑reduction burst.

Nyx Assassin

Nyx’s Mana Burn directly counters Tidehunter’s high mana pool, forcing early cooldowns on Gush and Ravage. Spiked Carapace reflects the Anchor Smash damage back, and Vendetta grants invisibility to bypass the anchor leash. Tip: Spam Mana Burn in lane to keep Tidehunter’s abilities on long cooldown, then ambush with Vendetta when he attempts to initiate.

Drafting Against Tidehunter

  • Prioritize heroes with hard disables (stuns, silences) that can interrupt Ravage.
  • Pick tanky initiators that can survive Anchor Smash and still engage (e.g., Clockwerk, Treant).
  • Ban or avoid heroes with strong armor‑reduction or burst magic that synergize with Gush.
  • Include at least one hero with reliable magic damage block or damage mitigation (Flame Guard, Living Armor).

Laning Against Tidehunter

  • Harass early before Kraken Shell fully stacks; Gush’s armor reduction makes his early trades favorable.
  • Force him to use Gush on creeps or towers to waste the slow and armor‑debuff.
  • When his anchor leash is on cooldown, trade aggressively; his damage output drops sharply.
  • Keep the lane tight to limit his ability to pull you with Dead in the Water.

Itemizing Against Tidehunter

Mekansm — provides burst heal and armor that counteracts Gush’s armor reduction and mitigates Anchor Smash damage.
Crimson Guard — blocks a large portion of the physical damage from Anchor Smash, reducing his overall burst.
Glimmer Cape — grants temporary magic immunity, nullifying Gush and Ravage’s stun/damage.
Force Staff — lets you escape the anchor leash instantly, rendering Dead in the Water ineffective.
