timbersaw.name: Timbersaw
timbersaw.guideHtml:
Timbersaw remains a high‑skill, off‑lane bruiser whose durability and burst make him a strong front‑line presence. On patch 7.41 his pub win rate sits at 44.5 % across 159,933 ranked games, placing him solidly in the mid‑tier of durable nukers. He excels at shredding tanky heroes and controlling team fights, but struggles against heroes that can silence or burst him early.

How to Play Timbersaw

Laning Phase

  • Whirling Death early harass: use the attribute‑steal on enemy heroes to force them to lose damage and make your lane partner safer.
  • Reactive Armor stacks 4× on attacks: trade aggressively when you have a few stacks; the extra armor and regen let you survive tower hits.
  • Timber Chain for escape and tree‑damage: pull to a nearby tree to dodge ganks or to position for a quick Whirling Death combo.
  • Prioritize tree cutting (via Flamethrower or Chakram) to gain mana from Exposure Therapy and deny the enemy creep wave’s vision.
  • Against typical lane opponents (e.g., Bounty Hunter, Nyx Assassin) keep the distance and force them to waste disables on a hero that gains armor from each hit.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 6 with Chakram: start rotating around enemy heroes, applying the slow that scales with missing health.
  • Secure Roshan after you have Bloodstone or Shiva’s Guard; Timbersaw’s pure damage and tankiness make him an ideal tank for the pit.
  • Use Timber Chain to initiate or disengage from Earth Spirit and Legion Commander fights—your chain can dodge their pulls or stuns.
  • Split‑push lanes with Flamethrower + Timber Chain to cut trees, sustain mana, and force the enemy to respond.

Late Game

  • Win condition: lock down the enemy back‑line with Chakram while your Reactive Armor makes you nearly unkillable in prolonged fights.
  • Positioning: stay near trees to constantly trigger Exposure Therapy and to have escape routes with Timber Chain.
  • Losing the game: over‑committing without a Return Chakram or getting silenced (e.g., by Silencer, Death Prophet) removes your damage and leaves you vulnerable to burst.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango + Healing Salve — sustain against harass.
  • Stout Shield — reduces tower and creep damage while you stack Reactive Armor.
  • Quelling Blade — speeds up tree cutting for early mana gain.
  • Observer Ward — vision to avoid early ganks.

Core Items

  • Bloodstone — massive mana pool, regen, and damage on death; synergizes with tree‑cutting.
  • Shiva’s Guard — armor, aura, and the active slow that complements Chakram’s damage.
  • Mekansm — provides burst heal and armor to the team, amplifying your durability.
  • Black King Bar — essential against heavy silence/disables (e.g., Earth Spirit, Legion Commander).

Situational Items

  • Abyssal Blade — lock down slippery heroes like Anti‑Mage when you need a guaranteed stun.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target disables; useful vs Bounty Hunter and Nyx Assassin.
  • Heart of Tarrasque — extra survivability in games that go long without BKB.
  • Pipe of Insight — mitigates magical burst from heroes such as Lina and Witch Doctor.
  • Sange & Yasha — adds movement speed for better chaining and chase potential.

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑relying on Chakram without Return – forgetting to recall the blade leaves you vulnerable and wastes damage.
  • Neglecting tree cutting – without trees you lose mana from Exposure Therapy and become easy to kite.
  • Stacking Reactive Armor too early – buying too many early armor items delays your core damage items, reducing your mid‑game impact.
  • Chasing heroes without a clear escape – using Timber Chain without a nearby tree can trap you in enemy vision.

FAQ

Is Timbersaw good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 44.5 % win rate on 7.41, Timbersaw sits in the mid‑tier of durable nukers and remains a solid pick, especially against heroes like Anti‑Mage (64.1 % win) and Lina (61.2 % win).

What lane does Timbersaw play?

Timbersaw is typically played in the off‑lane (solo safe lane) where his tree‑cutting and Reactive Armor allow him to survive and pressure the enemy carry.

Who counters Timbersaw?

The toughest matchups are Earth Spirit, Bounty Hunter, Nyx Assassin, Legion Commander, Bane, and Alchemist, where Timbersaw’s win rates dip below 41 % (e.g., 36.5 % vs Earth Spirit). Heavy silence, burst magic, or strong early disables are the most effective counters.
timbersaw.counterHtml:
Timbersaw’s threat comes from his massive pure damage output, self‑sustain through Reactive Armor, and the ability to shred trees for mana. The core way to shut him down is to deny him the melee attacks and tree‑based mana that fuel his survivability while exploiting his relatively low burst damage and reliance on close‑range engagements.

Why These Heroes Beat Timbersaw

Earth Spirit

Earth Spirit’s Rolling Boulder and Geomagnetic Grip can stun Timbersaw from a distance, preventing him from chaining into trees for Reactive Armor. Use Stone Remnants to block Timbersaw’s path and force him into unfavorable positions where his Chakram and Whirling Death miss. Tip: Pull a stone remnant onto Timbersaw’s expected chain route to cancel his Timber Chain and isolate him.

Bounty Hunter

Bounty Hunter’s Track reveals Timbersaw’s location, negating his tree‑hiding potential and allowing allies to focus fire before he can react with Reactive Armor. Shuriken Toss and Shadow Walk let him harass Timbersaw from range, forcing him to use his mana‑heavy abilities defensively. Tip: Keep a safe distance and bait Timbersaw into using Whirling Death on trees, then burst him down while his armor regen is on cooldown.

Nyx Assassin

Nyx’s Mana Burn directly counters Timbersaw’s mana‑dependent sustain, while Spiked Carapace reflects the damage from Timbersaw’s close‑range Chakram and Whirling Death. The Vendetta invisibility allows Nyx to ambush Timbersaw after he commits to a chain, catching him without the benefit of Reactive Armor. Tip: Time Mana Burn when Timbersaw is mid‑chain; the damage amplification from his missing health makes the burn even deadlier.

Legion Commander

Legion Commander’s Overwhelming Odds and Press the Attack apply pure damage that bypasses Timbersaw’s armor, and her Duel forces a one‑on‑one where Timbersaw’s splash damage is useless. The duel also disables Timbersaw’s ability to retreat with Timber Chain, making him vulnerable to burst. Tip: Initiate Duel right after Timbersaw uses his Chakram; his cooldown leaves him exposed and unable to escape.

Bane

Bane’s Nightmare and Fiend’s Grip lock Timbersaw down, preventing him from activating Reactive Armor and using his mobility tools. While disabled, Timbersaw cannot destroy trees for mana, quickly draining his resources. Tip: Combine Nightmare with a follow‑up stun (e.g., from a support) to keep Timbersaw incapacitated through his entire cooldown window.

Drafting Against Timbersaw

  • Prioritize heroes with strong disables or burst pure damage (e.g., Bane, Lion, Lina).
  • Pick ranged agility or intelligence heroes that can harass from afar (e.g., Sniper, Viper).
  • Ban or avoid heroes that provide abundant trees or high mana pools (e.g., Treant Protector, Enchantress).
  • Include at least one early‑game lockdown hero to punish Timbersaw’s weak early levels.

Laning Against Timbersaw

  • Trade when Timbersaw is low on mana and before he lands his first Reactive Armor stack.
  • Harass from range; avoid standing near trees that he can destroy for mana.
  • Punish his Timber Chain cooldown—once it’s on cooldown, his mobility and escape are severely limited.
  • Use early armor‑piercing damage (e.g., Drow’s Frost Arrow, Viper’s Poison Attack) to reduce his survivability.

Itemizing Against Timbersaw

Ghost Scepter — blocks Timbersaw’s pure damage from Chakram and Whirling Death while you wait for his cooldowns.
Heaven’s Halberd — disarms Timbersaw, preventing the attacks that trigger Reactive Armor and denying his melee damage.
Pipe of Insight — reduces the magic damage from his Flamethrower and Chakram, shrinking his overall burst.
Eul’s Scepter of Divinity – provides a reliable disable to interrupt his chain and gives you a safe window to force a fight when his armor regen is down.

tinker.name: Tinker
tinker.guideHtml:
Tinker is a high‑mobility, spell‑spamming hero who excels at burst magical damage and lane control. On patch 7.41 his pub win rate sits at 46.6% over 190,967 recent ranked games, placing him as a viable but inconsistent pick in the current meta.

How to Play Tinker

Laning Phase

  • Use Laser early to blind enemy melee heroes (e.g., Axe, Timbersaw) and deny them auto‑attack damage while you harass with March of the Machines.
  • Prioritize a 2‑tower lane (mid or safe lane) to keep the creep equilibrium near your tower, allowing safe re‑use of Rearm after a quick Laser‑March combo.
  • When facing high‑burst lane opponents like Snapfire or Lion, keep Laser on cooldown for defensive blinds and save Rearm for a quick escape via Keen Conveyance.
  • Stack March of the Machines creeps on the enemy tower to force tower damage and create lane pressure; the minions also block enemy creep waves, buying you farm time.
  • Maintain a mana pool (tango, clarity) because each Laser + March combo costs ~140 mana; falling short will leave you vulnerable to aggressive lane heroes.

Mid Game

  • Hit Level 6 and unlock Rearm; this is the primary power spike—spam Laser, March, Warp Flare, then Rearm instantly.
  • Split‑push with March of the Machines while constantly Rearm‑ing; the minion wave forces towers to take damage and opens space for your team.
  • Use Warp Flare on high‑value targets (e.g., Queen of Pain, Shadow Demon) to root them and reduce their cast range, then follow up with Laser and a team‑fight initiation.
  • Keep Keen Conveyance on standby for quick escapes from dangerous engagements, especially against mobile heroes like Tusk or Jakiro.

Late Game

  • Win condition: global pressure – constantly teleport to split‑push lanes, forcing the enemy to defend multiple towers while your team secures objectives.
  • Position near the edge of vision: you need line‑of‑sight for Laser and a safe distance for Warp Flare to teleport enemies away from you.
  • Losing the game often stems from over‑committing without a Rearm ready; a missed Rearm leaves you vulnerable to burst from the toughest matchups (Snapfire, Shadow Demon, QOP).

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane, essential for long March trades.
  • Healing Salve — emergency health for early skirmishes.
  • Clarity — keep mana pool high for repeated Laser/March combos.
  • Observer Ward — vision to protect against ganks while you farm.

Core Items

  • Boots of Travel — global mobility for split‑pushing and quick Keen Conveyance usage.
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Rearm to reset all abilities, enabling near‑instant Laser‑March‑Warp‑Rearm cycles.
  • Octarine Core — reduces cooldowns (including Rearm) and grants lifesteal, improving survivability in prolonged fights.
  • Scythe of Vyse — solidifies lockdown; combo with Warp Flare to lock down slippery heroes like Tusk or Lion.

Situational Items

  • Black King Bar — counteracts heavy magical burst from Snapfire or Lion.
  • Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — additional disable and mana regen; useful against Shadow Demon’s Disruption.
  • Shiva’s Guard — armor and AOE slow against physical heroes (Axe, Timbersaw) that pressure you in lane.
  • Aether Lens — extends Laser and Warp Flare range, allowing safer poke from farther back.
  • Refresher Orb — double Rearm for extreme burst when you need to finish a high‑value target quickly.

Common Mistakes

  • Spamming abilities without a ready Rearm – leaves you on long cooldowns and easy prey for burst heroes.
  • Over‑extending without vision – Tinker’s low HP makes ganks deadly; always carry a ward or two.
  • Neglecting mana management – running out of mana forces you to farm passively, losing lane pressure.
  • Failing to use Warp Flare defensively – many players only use it offensively, missing the escape/root utility against heroes like Snapfire.

FAQ

Is Tinker good in the current patch?

Yes, Tinker remains a viable pick with a 46.6% win rate. His global split‑push pressure is strong, though he struggles against bursty heroes like Snapfire and Shadow Demon (win rates ~36‑41%).

What lane does Tinker play?

Tinker is typically played in mid or a safe lane (off‑lane) to keep the creep wave near his tower, allowing safe Rearm cycles and minimizing early gank risk.

Who counters Tinker?

The toughest matchups are Snapfire, Shadow Demon, Queen of Pain, Lion, Tusk, and Jakiro, where Tinker’s win rate drops to the low‑40s. Vision, early BKB, and aggressive lane pressure are key to neutralizing him.
tinker.counterHtml:
Tinker’s threat comes from his relentless burst damage and the ability to reset his combo with Rearm, allowing him to spam Laser, March of the Machines, and Warp Flare from anywhere on the map. The key to shutting him down is to deny his early‑game farm, punish his long‑range, low‑mobility playstyle, and force him into fights where his cooldown reset is useless.

Why These Heroes Beat Tinker

Snapfire

Snapfire’s Cookie provides a reliable source of burst damage and a stun that can interrupt Tinker’s channeled Rearm or Keen Conveyance. Use Mortimer Kisses from a safe distance to force Tinker to retreat, then follow up with a Cookie to lock him down.
Tip: Keep a Fire Spirit on cooldown for a quick escape if Tinker lands a Laser‑blind combo.

Shadow Demon

Shadow Demon’s Disruption can purge Tinker’s Laser blind and temporarily remove him from the fight, buying time for allies to close the gap. His Soul Catcher amplifies damage taken, making Tinker’s otherwise low‑HP burst lethal.
Tip: Position Disruption on a neutral creep near the lane to catch Tinker when he tries to Rearm from a distance.

Queen of Pain

QOP’s Scream of Pain and Sonic Wave outrange Laser and can punish Tinker’s stationary positioning during March of the Machines. Her Blink lets her dodge Laser blinks and close the gap for a quick Sonic Wave before Tinker can Rearm.
Tip: Initiate with Blink right after you see Tinker cast Laser, then unleash Sonic Wave while he’s on cooldown.

Lion

Lion’s Earth Spike and Hex provide instant crowd control that can blind‑immune Tinker, stopping his combo before Rearm can refresh it. His Mana Drain also drains the mana Tinker needs for continuous spamming.
Tip: Save Hex for the moment Tinker finishes March of the Machines; the stun forces him to retreat and wastes his mana.

Tusk

Tusk’s Ice Shards creates a barrier that blocks Tinker’s line‑of‑sight Laser and forces him to reposition. Snowball can pull Tinker out of his optimal range, and the resulting stun interrupts Rearm.
Tip: Drop Ice Shards just behind the tower when Tinker attempts a Keen Conveyance; the barrier forces him to take a longer, more dangerous route.

Drafting Against Tinker

  • Prioritize heroes with hard disables (stuns, hexes, silences) that can interrupt Rearm or Laser.
  • Pick high‑mobility heroes that can dodge Laser blinks and close the distance quickly.
  • Include mana‑draining or mana‑burn heroes to cripple Tinker’s ability to spam.
  • Consider early‑game lane dominators who can deny Tinker farm and push him out of the lane.

Laning Against Tinker

  • Harass him with ranged attacks or spells when his Laser is on cooldown; he is vulnerable after a miss.
  • Force him to use Rearm defensively by zoning him with creep aggro or tower hits.
  • Punish his Keen Conveyance attempts by placing wards near friendly structures; he will be caught mid‑teleport.
  • Trade aggressively when his March of the Machines is on cooldown, as his wave of minions is his primary lane damage source.

Itemizing Against Tinker

Eul's Scepter — silences Tinker, preventing Rearm and forcing a long cooldown window.
Ghost Scepter — makes you untargetable by Laser’s physical damage component and blocks the blind.
Scythe of Vyse — provides a long‑duration hex that stops Tinker’s combo and wastes his mana.
Aghanim's Shard (if on a hero like Lion) — adds a mana‑drain or additional disable that directly counters his spell spam.

tiny.name: Tiny
tiny.guideHtml:
Tiny is a high‑damage initiator who scales from a lane‑bully into a late‑game siege powerhouse. On patch 7.41 his overall win‑rate sits at 44.7% across 237 k recent ranked games, placing him solidly in the mid‑tier of carries. He excels when he can land big Toss + Avalanche combos, but struggles against heroes that can out‑range or out‑heal him.

How to Play Tiny

Laning Phase

  • Use Tree Grab early to gain extra attack range and splash; it lets you harass melee off‑laners while staying safe behind the creep wave.
  • Pair Avalanche with a short‑range Toss on the same target to chain‑stun and force enemy support rotations.
  • Against heavy‑harass lanes (e.g., Bane, Kez) prioritize a Tango / Healing Salve and a Quelling Blade to secure last hits while staying in tree‑grab range.
  • Pull the lane creep with Tree Throw on a neutral tree to create a temporary barrier, buying you extra safety from aggressive supports.
  • If the enemy has strong lane control (e.g., Naga Siren), aim to land a Toss on a creep and follow with Avalanche to clear the wave and force a tower dive.

Mid Game

  • Grow at level 6 gives a massive damage spike; start timing your first Toss + Avalanche combo on enemy cores after you hit 20 % health.
  • Join team fights around objectives; your Tree Volley channel can swing a clustered fight in your favor, but be aware of silences (e.g., from Bane).
  • Prioritize taking Tier 2 towers with a Tree Throw + Avalanche combo; the splash damage makes short‑range towers fall quickly.
  • When you have Insurmountable, you can front‑line against slows and status effects—use this to soak up crowd control while your teammates follow up.

Late Game

  • Focus on split‑pushing with Tree Grab and Tree Throw to force the enemy to split their defense; Tiny’s attack damage and armor from Grow make him hard to kill in 1‑v‑1.
  • In team fights, look for a Toss on a high‑value target (e.g., Carry or Keeper of the Light) followed by a full Avalanche channel; the stun and burst can decide the round.
  • Avoid being caught out of position without Tree Volley—if you’re isolated, the channel can be interrupted, leading to a quick death.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango + Healing Salve — sustain against harass lanes (Bane, Kez).
  • Quelling Blade — easier last‑hits while using Tree Grab range.
  • Stout Shield — mitigates early tower and creep damage.
  • Observer Ward — vision to prevent ganks while you farm.

Core Items

  • Echo Sabre — synergy with Toss + Avalanche burst; provides mana regen and a double‑hit.
  • Black King Bar — essential against heavy magical disables (Bane, Keeper of the Light).
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Tree Volley to a longer‑range, higher‑damage channel, turning Tiny into a true siege tool.
  • Satanic — gives survivability in prolonged fights, especially when you’re the primary initiator.

Situational Items

  • Blink Dagger — instant positioning for Toss combos on mobile heroes (Weaver, Void Spirit).
  • Shiva’s Guard — armor and AoE slow against melee‑heavy lineups (Sven, Bristleback).
  • Heart of Tarrasque — extra durability when you’re the main front‑liner against burst (Naga Siren, Treant).
  • Assault Cuirass — armor and attack speed for faster tree‑throw cycles against physical cores.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target disables, useful versus Bane’s Nightmare or Keeper’s Light Strike.

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑channeling Avalanche without a follow‑up Toss, allowing enemies to escape the stun.
  • Ignoring Grow’s attack‑speed penalty and spamming attacks; instead, focus on burst combos.
  • Wasting Tree Grab on early fights instead of using it to extend lane range and farm safely.
  • Failing to buy BKB against magic‑heavy lineups, leading to early deaths from disables.

FAQ

Is Tiny good in the current patch?

Yes. Tiny’s win‑rate of 44.7% shows he’s a viable pick, especially when you capitalize on his mid‑game damage spikes and late‑game siege potential. He shines against heroes like Death Prophet and Weaver, where his burst and tower‑taking power are hard to counter.

What lane does Tiny play?

Tiny is most commonly played in the safe lane as a carry, but he can also be a solo off‑lane when you need a strong initiator. In the safe lane he benefits from farm to hit his core items, while in the off‑lane his early stun pressure can dominate weaker supports.

Who counters Tiny?

The toughest matchups are Bane, Naga Siren, Kez, Lone Druid, Treant Protector, and Keeper of the Light, where Tiny’s win‑rates hover around 38‑41%. These heroes either out‑range him, provide strong disables, or can survive his burst with high armor/healing. Building BKB and maintaining good vision are key to surviving against them.
tiny.counterHtml:
Tiny is a burst‑damage melee hero whose threat comes from explosive Avalanche‑Toss combos and massive tree‑throw damage. He thrives when he can lock down a target with stun and follow up with a high‑damage toss, so shutting him down means denying vision, avoiding close‑range engagements, and out‑lasting his short‑window of burst.

Why These Heroes Beat Tiny

Bane

Bane’s Nightmare and Fiend’s Grip lock Tiny in place, preventing him from positioning for a Toss or Tree Throw and nullifying his Avalanche stun window. A practical tip: start with a Nightmare on Tiny as soon as he steps into lane, then follow up with Enfeeblement to reduce his damage output.

Naga Siren

Naga’s Riptide and Song of the Siren give her reliable crowd control that can interrupt Tiny’s channelled Tree Volley and keep him out of range of Avalanche. Tip: use Riptide to punish Tiny’s approach and immediately cast Song of the Siren to force a teamfight where his burst is less decisive.

Kez

Kez’s Mana Void scales with Tiny’s high mana pool, dealing massive damage after Tiny’s early‑game spell spam, while Null Field reduces Tiny’s spell damage and stun duration. Tip: force Tiny to waste Avalanche on creeps early; the mana loss will make his Mana Void hit harder later.

Lone Druid

Lone Druid’s Spirit Bear provides a durable frontline that can absorb Tiny’s Toss and Tree Throw damage, while Savage Roar grants bonus armor that mitigates Tiny’s physical burst. Tip: keep the Bear positioned between Tiny and your core heroes, using Entangling Claws to lock Tiny down when he attempts a Toss.

Treant Protector

Treant’s Nature’s Grasp and Living Armor give him strong lane sustain and a way to block Tiny’s Avalanche radius, while Overgrowth can root Tiny mid‑combo, canceling his Toss. Tip: plant a Living Armor tree on the lane creep line; when Tiny tries to Toss, the tree’s armor will reduce the damage and the stun will be delayed.

Drafting Against Tiny

  • Prioritize heroes with long‑range disables or silences (e.g., Bane, Shadow Shaman, Lion).
  • Pick tanky frontliners that can absorb Toss damage (e.g., Lone Druid’s Spirit Bear, Treant).
  • Include heroes with strong early lane sustain or escape tools to survive his burst.
  • Consider banning heroes that give Tiny extra damage on trees (e.g., Bristleback) to limit his late‑game scaling.

Laning Against Tiny

  • Trade when Tiny’s Grow cooldown is up; his attack speed is lowest and he lacks the bonus damage.
  • Harass with ranged nukes or stuns before he can land Avalanche—the stun window is only a few seconds.
  • Pull creep equilibrium away from the tree zone; without nearby trees his Tree Grab and Tree Throw are useless.
  • Punish any missed Toss by following up with a quick auto‑attack or spell, exploiting his brief vulnerability.

Itemizing Against Tiny

Ghost Scepter — blocks Tiny’s physical Toss and Tree Throw damage, forcing him to rely on less‑impactful spells.
Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — cyclone removes Tiny from the fight, nullifying his burst combo and buying time for allies to reposition.
Crimson Guard — the armor block mitigates the massive physical damage from Toss and Tree Throw, especially after Tiny’s Grow.
Aghanim’s Shard (Silence upgrade on Bane/Lion) — silences Tiny, preventing him from casting Avalanche or Tree Volley during engagements.

treant-protector.name: Treant Protector
treant-protector.guideHtml:
Treant Protector is a durable support/initiator who excels at vision control, team‑fight crowd control, and sustaining allies with Living Armor and Leech Seed. On patch 7.41 his overall win‑rate sits at 50.5% in over 150 k ranked games, placing him solidly in the middle of the meta—good enough to pick, but you must play his strengths correctly to stay above average.

How to Play Treant Protector

Laning Phase

  • Living Armor on the carry early mitigates harassment and gives a steady health regen; prioritize the lane partner with the highest damage output.
  • Use Leech Seed on aggressive melee heroes (e.g., Enchantress, Shadow Fiend) to root and disarm them while feeding pulses to your carry.
  • Nature's Grasp can be cast defensively to block enemy pull‑ins or offensively to zone creeps and force enemy support to miss farm. Remember it does 35 % less damage to creeps, so focus on heroes.
  • Drop Eyes In The Forest on the river or jungle entrance to deny vision and spot rotating ganks; the 360‑second duration is a cheap early‑game map‑control tool.
  • Keep an eye on Nature’s Guise: after 2.75 s of no damage you gain Tree Walking and can activate invisibility to escape ganks or reposition for a surprise Overgrowth.

Mid Game

  • Overgrowth becomes a decisive team‑fight tool once you have a few levels; look for clustered enemy initiators (e.g., Batrider, Rubick) to lock them down.
  • Build a Vision Ward network using Eyes In The Forest and Observer Wards around Roshan and high‑traffic jungle paths to maintain map control.
  • Pair Living Armor with a frontline hero (Centaur, Spirit Breaker) to create a “damage‑blocked tank” that can survive the enemy’s burst.
  • Start rotating to other lanes after securing a safe tower push; your presence with Overgrowth can swing mid‑lane fights even if you’re a support.

Late Game

  • Win condition: force the enemy to fight under your Overgrowth while your Living Armor‑tanked cores stay alive; the combination of crowd control and sustained healing often decides late‑game engagements.
  • Position near trees to leverage Nature’s Guise for surprise invisibility and quick escapes; avoid standing in open areas where you can’t tree‑walk.
  • Losing the game usually stems from poor vision (enemy Batrider or Rubick catching you out of position) or failing to protect your core during enemy Overgrowth‑free pushes.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango + Healing Salve — sustain in lane while you’re busy casting spells.
  • Observer Ward — early vision for gank safety and to start your Eyes In The Forest network.
  • Iron Branch x2 — cheap stats and can later be used for Magic Wand.

Core Items

  • Tranquil Boots — movement speed for tree‑walking and constant health regen.
  • Mekansm — synergizes with Living Armor and provides a team heal in fights.
  • Glimmer Cape — protects you or an ally from targeted disables (Rubick, Bane) and works well with your invisibility.
  • Pipe of Insight — blocks magical burst from heroes like Shadow Fiend and Enchantress, complementing your physical damage mitigation.

Situational Items

  • Aghanim’s Shard — upgrades Leech Seed to apply a stronger root and additional heal pulses.
  • Solar Crest — boosts a core’s damage and armor while giving you extra vision on the target.
  • Guardian Greaves — upgrades Mekansm and gives a strong dispel for fights against Bane or Shadow Demon.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target spells (Rubick’s Telekinesis, Batrider’s Flamebreak) and provides armor.
  • Force Staff — helps you or an ally escape from Batrider’s Flaming Lasso or get into range for Overgrowth.

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑using Nature’s Grasp on creeps – it deals 35 % less damage to creeps, wasting mana that could secure a hero root.
  • Neglecting vision – failing to place enough Eyes In The Forest lets enemy initiators catch you out of tree‑walk range.
  • Casting Overgrowth too early – low‑level Overgrowth has a short radius; wait until you have at least 6 mana and a clustered enemy group.
  • Saving Living Armor for towers – the biggest impact is on your core; using it on structures reduces its effectiveness in fights.

FAQ

Is Treant Protector good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 50.5 % win‑rate across 153 k ranked games, Treant sits in the mid‑tier of support heroes. His vision tools and team‑fight control are especially strong against heroes like Invoker and Monkey King, where his win‑rates exceed 70 %.

What lane does Treant Protector play?

Treant is typically a hard support in the safe lane (position 5) alongside the carry, but he can also be flexed to the off‑lane if you need extra tower protection and vision. His early Living Armor and Leech Seed make him a reliable lane‑partner for most carries.

Who counters Treant Protector?

Heroes that can bypass his crowd control and burst him before Overgrowth lands are the toughest: Enchantress, Rubick, Shadow Fiend, Batrider, Bane, and Shadow Demon all have win‑rates around 50 % or lower against Treant. Vision denial and early aggression from these heroes are the most effective counters.

Treant Protector’s strength lies in his global map control, burst lockdown with Overgrowth, and sustained survivability through Living Armor and Leech Seed. To shut him down you must deny his vision, avoid prolonged fights where his roots and heals can snowball, and force him to waste his high‑mana, long‑cooldown spells.

Why These Heroes Beat Treant Protector

Enchantress

Her Enchant gives a massive damage‑over‑time boost that ignores Treant’s armor, while Nature’s Attendants provide constant healing that outpaces Treant’s modest Leech Seed pulses. Play aggressively early; a quick Enchanted melee strike forces Treant to retreat or waste Living Armor on a low‑value target.

Rubick

Rubick can steal Overgrowth or Living Armor and turn Treant’s own tools against him, instantly removing the lockdown that Treant relies on. Prioritize Telekinesis to pull Treant out of his own Nature’s Grasp vines and follow up with a stolen Overgrowth for a free team‑fight win.

Shadow Fiend

Shadow Fiend’s Necromastery stacks give him huge burst damage that bypasses Treant’s armor, and his Shadowrazes shred the low‑HP trees Treant uses for Nature’s Guise. Push early and force a lane duel; a well‑timed Requiem after Treant casts Overgrowth punishes his long cooldown.

Batrider

Flamebreak instantly destroys Treant’s Living Armor on structures and heroes, while Sticky Napalm prevents Treant from safely using Leech Seed on allies. Use Firefly to bypass Treant’s Nature’s Grasp vines and position for a Flamebreak‑initiated team fight.

Bane

Bane’s Nightmare and Fiend’s Grip lock Treant down without triggering Overgrowth’s anti‑invisibility, nullifying his Tree Walking and Nature’s Guise escapes. Chain‑cast Brain Sap after a successful Nightmare to drain Treant’s health faster than Leech Seed can heal.

Drafting Against Treant Protector

  • Pick heroes with strong burst magic that can kill before Overgrowth lands (e.g., Shadow Fiend, Lina).
  • Prioritize vision‑denying tools and mobile heroes that can dodge Nature’s Grasp vines (e.g., Batrider, Puck).
  • Include at least one hero capable of stealing or nullifying Living Armor (Rubick, Silencer).
  • Avoid heavy tanky melee cores that benefit from Treant’s Leech Seed sustain.

Laning Against Trebot Protector

  • Harass him before he gets a Living Armor on you; his early damage is low.
  • Force him to use Nature’s Grasp on creeps—its damage is 35 % reduced on creeps, giving you a safe window to trade.
  • When he casts Leech Seed, immediately disengage or use a purge (e.g., Eul’s Scepter) to stop the heal pulses.
  • Punish his Tree Walking cooldown; after he takes damage, his invisibility is unavailable for ~2.75 s.

Itemizing Against Treant Protector

Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — stuns Treant, breaking his Leech Seed pulses and preventing a timely Overgrowth.
Black King Bar — grants magic immunity through Overgrowth, Nature’s Grasp, and Living Armor damage.
Force Staff — escapes the root and vine zone, nullifying the lockdown that Treant relies on.
Aghanim’s Scepter (for Rubick) — upgrades Spell Steal to steal Overgrowth, turning Treant’s own ultimate into a team‑fight win.

troll-warlord.name: Troll Warlord
troll-warlord.guideHtml:
Troll Warlord remains a high‑damage, split‑pushing carry with a 50.3 % win rate in recent ranked play (99 k games). His kit lets him toggle between a fast‑firing ranged form and a melee burst form, making him a versatile threat in both team fights and lane pressure. On patch 7.41 he sits in the meta as a solid mid‑lane/solo‑safe lane carry, though several heroes still give him trouble.

How to Play Troll Warlord

Laning Phase

  • Start with Whirling Axes (Ranged) to harass and zone opponents; the cone slows and chips health, making it hard for melee heroes to contest the lane.
  • Use Battle Stance early only when you need a melee trade; the 1.4 BAT improves damage but sacrifices range, so switch back after a quick kill.
  • Stack Fervor on a single target (usually the enemy off‑lane hero) to gain attack‑speed; avoid bouncing between creeps or heroes, as the stacks reset.
  • Against hard‑disablers like Lion or Pudge, keep a safe distance and rely on the ranged Whirling Axes to avoid being caught by hooks or stuns.
  • Pull the creep wave with the ranged axe’s slow to deny experience to heroes that are strong early (e.g., Sniper, Invoker).

Mid Game

  • Hit the 6‑item power spike (usually Echo Sabre → Maelstrom) to start split‑pushing; the extra attack speed synergizes with Fervor.
  • Join fights when you can stay in melee Battle Stance long enough for Berserker’s Rage to lock down a key enemy (e.g., a Timbersaw or Pudge).
  • Use Battle Trance on a flank to force continuous attacks on the nearest hero; the lifesteal and damage immunity let you survive burst damage and force a kill.
  • Prioritize taking towers with Whirling Axes (Ranged); the 950‑range cone can clear creep waves quickly while the slow makes tower dives safer.

Late Game

  • Win condition: dominate split‑push lanes and force the enemy to defend; your high attack speed and armor‑per‑attack‑speed make you hard to kill in 1‑v‑1 tower fights.
  • Position near the front of your team in melee form to apply Berserker’s Rage on high‑mobility heroes (e.g., Void Spirit, Invoker) and lock them down.
  • Avoid getting caught by strong disables or burst (e.g., Abaddon, Lion) – a single hook or death coil can wipe your momentum and swing the game.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain for early lane trades.
  • Healing Salve — emergency health against burst heroes.
  • Iron Branch ×2 — cheap stats and can later be used for Magic Wand.
  • Slippers of Agility — early attack damage for better last‑hitting.

Core Items

  • Echo Sabre — gives burst damage and a second attack that syncs with Fervor stacks.
  • Maelstrom — provides cleave damage, amplifying your melee Whirling Axes and overall DPS.
  • Manta Style — offers a second Battle Stance toggle, dispels silences, and adds mobility against disables.
  • Black King Bar — essential against heroes with heavy magical burst (e.g., Invoker, Lion).

Situational Items

  • Satanic — huge lifesteal for surviving prolonged fights, especially versus Abaddon or Timbersaw.
  • Butterfly — evasion and damage boost; works well when you need to survive heroes like Sniper or Medusa.
  • Abyssal Blade — reliable stun to lock down slippery targets such as Void Spirit or Pudge.
  • Shiva’s Guard — armor and AoE slow to counter right‑click heroes and reduce Pudge's damage.
  • Heart of Tarrasque — raw survivability for late‑game sieges and when you’re the primary front‑liner.

Common Mistakes

  • Switching forms too often – each toggle resets Fervor stacks; stay in one form long enough to build a solid stack before changing.
  • Over‑extending without Battle Trance – diving into fights without the lifesteal and damage immunity often leads to early deaths against burst heroes.
  • Ignoring tower pressure – Troll’s split‑push is his biggest late‑game advantage; many low‑MMR players focus on team fights instead of taking towers.
  • Chasing heroes with high mobility – trying to lock down Void Spirit or Invoker with melee Berserker’s Rage without proper positioning often results in being kited and killed.

FAQ

Is Troll Warlord good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 50.3 % win rate across nearly 100 k recent ranked matches, Troll Warlord is a solid carry on patch 7.41, especially on maps that favor split‑pushing and high attack‑speed scaling.

What lane does Troll Warlord play?

Troll Warlord is typically played in the solo safe lane (mid or off‑lane) as a carry. His early ranged harassment and later melee burst let him dominate lane control and transition into a split‑push threat.

Who counters Troll Warlord?

The toughest matchups are Abaddon, Invoker, Sniper, Pudge, Timbersaw, and Lion, where Troll wins only 34–42 % of games. These heroes bring strong disables, burst, or tankiness that can neutralize Troll’s damage and prevent him from building Fervor stacks.
troll-warlord.counterHtml:
Troll Warlord’s threat comes from his insane sustained DPS—Fervor’s attack‑speed stacks and Battle Trance’s forced aggression let him melt heroes in both ranged and melee form. The key to shutting him down is denying him the uninterrupted melee uptime he needs to snowball his damage.

Why These Heroes Beat Troll Warlord

Abaddon

Abaddon’s Aphotic Shield can purge the bonus attack speed from Fervor and block the burst from Whirling Axes, while Borrowed Time makes him untouchable during Troll’s Battle Trance. Tip: time your shield just as Troll switches to melee to wipe out his accumulated Fervor stacks.

Invoker

Invoker’s Sun Strike and Chaos Meteor provide pure magical damage that ignores Troll’s armor scaling from attack speed, and Cold Snap repeatedly stuns him, preventing the melee switch needed for Berserker’s Rage. Tip: lock down Troll with Cold Snap before he can activate Battle Trance, then follow up with a high‑damage spell combo.

Sniper

Sniper’s long‑range Assassinate and Take Aim outrange Troll’s Whirling Axes, and his Headshot adds burst that can kill Troll before he reaches melee range. Tip: keep distance and use Shrapnel to slow Troll’s approach, forcing him to stay in his weaker ranged stance.

Pudge

Pudge’s Meat Hook can yank Troll out of melee range, instantly stripping him of Fervor stacks, while Rot deals damage over time that scales with Troll’s low armor in ranged form. Tip: hook Troll the moment he initiates Battle Trance; the forced movement interrupt cancels the trance and leaves him vulnerable.

Timbersaw

Timbersaw’s pure‑damage Whirling Death and Timber Chain ignore Troll’s armor, and his Reactive Armor gives him survivability against the melee onslaught. Tip: engage with Timber Chain to pull Troll into a tight corridor, then spam Whirling Death while his attack speed is throttled by the lack of melee targets.

Drafting Against Troll Warlord

  • Prioritize heroes with strong magical burst or disables that can interrupt Battle Trance.
  • Pick heroes that scale well with armor‑ignoring damage (pure or magical).
  • Ban or avoid heroes that give Troll easy lane control or early attack‑speed items (e.g., early Power Treads).
  • Consider early silence or stun heavy picks to prevent him from building Fervor stacks.

Laning Against Troll Warlord

  • Harass him before he can secure a melee creep wave; his ranged Whirling Axes are less effective against low‑HP creeps.
  • Force him to stay in ranged form by denying melee creeps and using lane control abilities.
  • Punish his switch to melee with burst damage or a stun the moment he activates Battle Stance.
  • Keep a defensive ward to anticipate his Battle Trance initiation and react quickly.

Itemizing Against Troll Warlord

Ghost Scepter — blocks his melee attacks during Berserker’s Rage, nullifying his highest DPS phase.
Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — cyclone removes Troll from combat, resetting Fervor stacks and preventing Battle Trance activation.
Black King Bar — grants magic immunity, nullifying Whirling Axes and any magical burst from counters.
Abyssal Blade — stun forces Troll out of melee stance, dropping his attack‑speed stacks and breaking his damage rhythm.

tusk.name: Tusk
tusk.guideHtml:
Tusk remains a high‑skill initiator and disabler in the current 7.41 meta. With a 47.5% win rate across 194,849 recent ranked games, he sits near the middle of the hero spectrum—strong in coordinated play but vulnerable to several mid‑lane specialists.

How to Play Tusk

Laning Phase

  • Ice Shards early‑level zoning: cast the shard to block creep equilibrium and force enemy support to farm under tower, buying you lane control.
  • Drinking Buddies on yourself and the lane partner gives a burst of armor and movement speed, helping survive harass from ranged heroes like Mirana or Vengeful Spirit.
  • Use Tag Team on a melee ally (e.g., Legion Commander) to amplify damage and apply the slow, turning early trades in your favor.
  • When the enemy support is a Treant Protector or Bane, prioritize short‑range harassment with Ice Shards and Tag Team, as their win rates against Tusk are low (32.0% and 41.7% respectively).
  • Keep an eye on Bitter Chill passive; positioning near enemy heroes early reduces their attack speed, which is especially useful against high‑damage right‑click cores like Sven.

Mid Game

  • Snowball becomes a decisive pick‑off tool once you have 2–3 allies in range; roll into enemy jungle or around Roshan to catch over‑extended heroes.
  • Walrus Kick on a stunned target (e.g., after a successful Ice Shards + Tag Team combo) adds extra stun and AoE damage, perfect for setting up team fights.
  • Power spike at Level 12 when you unlock Walrus Punch! – use it on a key enemy carry to launch them into the air, creating a temporary numerical advantage.
  • Prioritize map control around mid‑lane and Roshan; the snowball’s 325 radius pull lets you swing across the map for surprise ganks on heroes like Muerta (41.0% win vs. Tusk) who rely on positioning.

Late Game

  • Win condition: use Snowball as a mobile initiation tool to isolate a single high‑value target (e.g., Ancient Apparition or Lifestealer) while your team follows up with burst damage.
  • Position near the front line but keep a safe distance; a mistimed Walrus Kick into a crowd‑controlled enemy can backfire if you get caught by enemy Bane or Pugna ultimates.
  • Losing the game often stems from over‑committing a snowball without backup, allowing enemy Treant Protector or Venomancer to turn fights with strong area control.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango + Healing Salve — sustain against early harassment.
  • Enchanted Mango — provides burst mana for Ice Shards and Tag Team.
  • Observer Ward — vision to protect against ganks from mobile heroes like Broodmother (37.3% win vs. Tusk).

Core Items

  • Phase Boots — extra mobility for closing gaps and escaping after a snowball roll.
  • Blink Dagger — primary initiation tool; combine with Snowball for instant surprise ganks.
  • Aghanim’s Shard (upgrade Ice Shards to a longer barrier) — improves lane control and team‑fight zoning.
  • Black King Bar — essential against magical burst from Ancient Apparition, Pugna, and Bane.

Situational Items

  • Abyssal Blade — lock down slippery targets like Muerta or Lifestealer.
  • Shiva’s Guard — armor and AoE slow counter high‑damage right‑click heroes (Sven, Lifestealer).
  • Lotus Orb — reflect targeted disables from Bane, Pugna, and Venomancer.
  • Glimmer Cape — protect yourself or an ally after a failed snowball initiation.
  • Mekansm / Guardian Greaves — boost team survivability when facing heavy AoE (Treant Protector, Venomancer).

Common Mistakes

  • Launching Snowball without backup – leads to easy counter‑ganks, especially against heroes with strong disables.
  • Overusing Ice Shards on creep wave – wastes mana and leaves you vulnerable to lane harassment from ranged supports.
  • Neglecting Tag Team – missing the extra damage and slow reduces early trade effectiveness.
  • Failing to buy BKB against high magical burst (e.g., Ancient Apparition) which often decides mid‑game fights.

FAQ

Is Tusk good in the current patch?

Yes. Tusk sits at a 47.5% win rate on 7.41, making him a viable pick especially in coordinated teams. He shines against heroes like Legion Commander (67.8% win) and struggles against Treant Protector (32.0% win), so draft accordingly.

What lane does Tusk play?

Tusk is most commonly played off‑lane (solo) where his Ice Shards and Tag Team can harass enemy cores. He can also be flexed to support in safe lanes if the team needs additional initiation and crowd control.

Who counters Tusk?

The toughest matchups are Treant Protector, Broodmother, Muerta, Venomancer, Bane, and Pugna, each giving Tusk a win rate below 42%. Their strong lane control, crowd control, or burst magic makes Tusk’s early aggression risky. Adjust your build (BKB, Lotus Orb) and play more conservatively against them.
tusk.counterHtml:
Tusk thrives on early‑game aggression: his Snowball and Walrus Kick let him initiate, while Tag Team amplifies burst damage. The key to shutting him down is denying those initiation tools and punishing his reliance on close‑range physical damage.

Why These Heroes Beat Tusk

Treant Protector

Treant’s Nature’s Grasp and Living Armor create a static front that blocks Snowball’s path and reduces the damage Tusk can land with Walrus Punch. Additionally, Overgrowth roots Tusk, preventing him from rolling away or repositioning with Drinking Buddies. Tip: Position your trees to force Tusk into a choke where Overgrowth can hit both him and any allies he tries to pull into the snowball.

Broodmother

Broodmother’s Spin Web grants her untargetable movement and vision denial, making it hard for Tusk to land a Snowball or Walrus Kick. Her Silk Shot slows Tusk’s approach, and the spiderlings provide constant harassment that forces Tusk to waste Snowball on minions instead of heroes. Tip: Keep a web near the lane’s edge; when Tusk engages, pull the web to block his line of sight and force him to chase into spiderlings.

Muerta

Muerta’s Dead Shot applies a strong slow and damage over time that counters Tusk’s burst, while Soul Siphon gives her sustain against the physical damage from Walrus Punch. Her Reaper’s Scythe can instantly remove Tusk’s health pool if he overcommits with Snowball. Tip: Save Reaper’s Scythe for the moment Tusk lands his Snowball; the delayed damage from Dead Shot will already have softened him.

Venomancer

Venomancer’s Poison Nova and Venomous Gale apply consistent magical damage that Tusk’s armor‑focused items cannot mitigate, and the slow from Venomous Gale hampers Snowball’s momentum. Plague Ward can block the path of a rolling snowball, forcing Tusk to detour or waste the ability. Tip: Plant a Ward in the expected Snowball lane; the ward will explode on contact and deny the initiation.

Bane

Bane’s Nightmare and Enfeeble neutralize Tusk’s damage output, while Fiend’s Grip can lock Tusk down during his Snowball cooldown, preventing any follow‑up. The silence from Enfeeble also stops Tusk from using Drinking Buddies to escape. Tip: Time Nightmare just before Tusk attempts a Snowball; the stun will cancel the roll and leave him vulnerable to a counter‑initiate.

Drafting Against Tusk

  • Prioritize heroes with long‑range disables or slows (e.g., Venomancer, Bane).
  • Pick heroes that can create static terrain or vision denial (Treant Protector, Broodmother).
  • Ban or avoid heavy armor‑stackers that mitigate Walrus Punch (e.g., Bristleback).
  • Include at least one reliable magical burst to outdamage his physical burst.

Laning Against Tusk

  • Trade when his Snowball is on cooldown; his early damage window is ~12 seconds.
  • Harass him with ranged attacks or creeps to force him to use Ice Shards defensively.
  • Punish his Drinking Buddies pull by positioning near a wall or tower, denying the follow‑up.
  • Keep the lane tight to limit his ability to roll a snowball around the map.

Itemizing Against Tusk

Ghost Scepter — blocks Walrus Punch’s physical damage and the burst from Snowball.
Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — cyclone removes Tusk from the fight during his Snowball roll, buying time for allies to reposition.
Heaven’s Halberd — disarms Tusk, nullifying his primary source of damage from Walrus Punch and Tag Team.
Pipe of Insight — provides magic resistance against Ice Shards and reduces the impact of his passive Bitter Chill.

underlord.name: Underlord
underlord.guideHtml:
Underlord is a durable, nuking support whose strength lies in zone control and team‑fight utility. In the current 7.41 meta his overall pub win rate sits at 49.9% over 242 k ranked games, making him a solid but not dominant pick.

How to Play Underlord

Laning Phase

  • Pit of Malice early‑level vision: drop the pit near the enemy creep wave to punish aggressive supports and force safe farming.
  • Atrophy Aura stacks quickly; keep it active while you and your carry last‑hit to shave a few damage off enemy cores (especially effective against right‑click heroes like Ursa).
  • Pair Firestorm with a short Pit to trap melee heroes (e.g., Treant Protector) and force them to retreat, buying lane equilibrium.
  • Use Invading Force on the first allied Teleport (e.g., from Blink or Enigma) to grant immediate damage reduction, letting you survive early ganks.
  • Prioritize stacking neutral camps when the lane is safe; the extra gold offsets Underlord’s relatively low early damage.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 6: Unlock Fiend’s Gate and start creating split‑push pressure or catching out‑of‑position carries.
  • Group with your team around objectives; Firestorm + Pit creates a “no‑go” zone that forces enemies like Monkey King to disengage.
  • Look for Invading Force opportunities after a teammate uses Teleport (e.g., from Blink or Dark Seer) to give them a temporary shield and speed boost for a decisive push.
  • Secure vision around Roshan and high‑ground jungle; a well‑placed Pit can block enemy rotations and set up your team’s A‑egis attempts.

Late Game

  • Win condition: lock down the enemy carry with a combo of Pit of Malice → Firestorm → Atrophy Aura while your cores deal damage.
  • Position near the front line but keep a safe distance (≈600 units) so you can drop Pit on initiators like Primal Beast without being caught.
  • Avoid over‑extending after a Fiend’s Gate teleport; if the enemy has strong burst (e.g., Drow Ranger), you’ll be the first target once the portal closes.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain for the lane.
  • Healing Salve — emergency HP for early ganks.
  • Observer Ward — vision to protect your Pit and spot enemy rotations.
  • Stout Shield — mitigates harassment from right‑click heroes.

Core Items

  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Firestorm to a larger radius and adds a stun, crucial against mobile heroes like Monkey King.
  • Pipe of Insight — provides magic resistance for you and allies, countering heavy magical lineups (e.g., Ancient Apparition, Zeus).
  • Guardian Greaves — combines Pipe with strong HP regen and a burst heal, synergizing with your durability.
  • Blink Dagger — enables instant Pit placement and quick escapes after a Fiend’s Gate push.

Situational Items

  • Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target disables from heroes like Drow Ranger and Hoodwink.
  • Heaven’s Halberd — disarms right‑click carries (Ursa, Drow) that currently give you a low win rate.
  • Aeon Disk — survivability against burst from Necrophos or Primal Beast.
  • Solar Crest — armor reduction on enemy cores, amplifying the damage loss from Atrophy Aura.
  • Glimmer Cape — invisibility to dodge focused spells and protect yourself when you’re the primary Pit holder.

Common Mistakes

  • Dropping Pit too early – using it before you have vision lets enemies dodge or bait you into a bad fight.
  • Neglecting Atrophy Aura – many players forget to keep it active, missing out on the consistent damage reduction against heroes like Ursa and Treant.
  • Over‑committing after Fiend’s Gate – teleporting forward without backup often results in being caught by burst heroes (Necrophos, Drow).
  • Itemizing purely for damage – ignoring defensive items reduces your survivability, which is why Underlord’s win rate against bursty heroes is low.

FAQ

Is Underlord good in the current patch?

Yes. Underlord’s win rate sits at 49.9% across 242 k ranked games, making him a viable support pick. He excels at zone control and team‑fight durability, though he struggles against high‑burst heroes.

What lane does Underlord play?

Underlord is typically played as a hard support in the safe lane (radiant bottom or dire top) alongside a core carry. His early Pit of Malice and Atrophy Aura help secure lane equilibrium.

Who counters Underlord?

Heroes that can bypass or quickly destroy his Pit and Firestorm zones perform best. Current data shows Treant Protector, Ursa, Necrophos, Monkey King, Drow Ranger, and Hoodwink each give Underlord win rates below 37%, making them his toughest match‑ups. Counter‑play includes early aggressive ganks and buying items like Heaven’s Halberd or Lotus Orb.
underlord.counterHtml:
Underlord’s strength lies in his global presence and area‑control: Firestorm and Pit of Malice punish clustered enemies, while Atrophy Aura drags down physical damage output. The key to shutting him down is to force early, high‑burst fights that deny him time to set up his portals and to exploit the fact that his damage is primarily magical and area‑based.

Why These Heroes Beat Underlord

Treant Protector

Treant’s Nature’s Grasp and Leech Seed force Underlord to fight in a tight, low‑mobility space where his Pit of Malice can’t be reliably placed, and his Atrophy Aura is nullified by Treant’s Living Armor reducing incoming damage. Play aggressively after your first tower; a well‑timed Overgrowth catches Underlord mid‑teleport and wipes him out.

Ursa

Ursa’s Fury Swipes stack quickly on the low‑HP Underlord, and Enrage grants magic resistance that mitigates Firestorm damage. Because Underlord’s damage is spread over time, Ursa can dive in, burst him with Overpower, and escape before the Pit roots him. Aim to engage when Underlord’s Invading Force cooldown is up, so he can’t grant you damage reduction.

Necrophos

Necrophos’s Heartstopper Aura continuously chips Underlord’s health, while Death Pulse deals pure damage that bypasses the magical mitigation of Firestorm. The hero’s Reaper’s Scythe can finish Underlord before he can activate Fiend’s Gate, denying his global pressure. Prioritize a early Mana Break‑heavy build to deplete Underlord’s mana for his spells.

Monkey King

Monkey King’s Tree Dance gives him constant mobility, letting him dodge Pit of Malice and stay out of Firestorm’s radius. His Wukong’s Command creates a large area of damage that punishes Underlord’s tendency to cluster enemies for his AoE. Use Boundless Strike to interrupt Underlord’s channeling of Fiend’s Gate and force a melee fight where you have the advantage.

Drow Ranger

Drow’s Gust silences Underlord, preventing Firestorm and Pit of Malice from being cast during the 1.5‑second silence window. Her Precision Aura reduces enemy armor, making the physical damage from her Multishot more lethal against Underlord’s relatively low armor. Keep distance, bait his Pit, and punish the cooldown with a quick Silence‑followed Gust combo.

Drafting Against Underlord

  • Prioritize heroes with strong single‑target burst and magic resistance (e.g., Ursa, Necrophos).
  • Include mobility or silence tools to dodge or interrupt Pit of Malice and Fiend’s Gate.
  • Avoid heavy reliance on melee heroes that need to cluster, as they fall prey to Firestorm.
  • Consider picking a global‑presence hero that can contest Invading Force (e.g., Nature’s Prophet).

Laning Against Underlord

  • Harass him before he gets a level 2 Atrophy Aura; his early damage is low.
  • Trade when his Firestorm is on cooldown; his damage spikes are predictable.
  • Force him to use Pit of Malice defensively, then capitalize on the 3.6‑second root interval.
  • Push the lane quickly to deny him farm and prevent a safe spot for his Atrophy Aura to affect your creeps.

Itemizing Against Underlord

Black King Bar — grants magic immunity, nullifying Firestorm and Pit of Malice damage.
Manta Style — dispels the root from Pit of Malice and provides extra movement speed to escape portals.
Sange and Yasha — gives status resistance to reduce the impact of the 3.6‑second root and adds movement speed to outrun Firestorm.
Abyssal Blade — provides a reliable stun that can interrupt Fiend’s Gate channeling and lock Underlord down before he can teleport.

undying.name: Undying
undying.guideHtml:
Undying is a durable support‑disabler whose toolkit revolves around Decay, Soul Rip, Tombstone, and Flesh Golem. With a 52.3 % win rate over 466 k recent ranked games, he sits comfortably in the meta as a lane‑control hero that excels at team‑fight zoning and sustaining allies.

How to Play Undying

Laning Phase

  • Use Decay early to trade with melee off‑laners; the strength steal also gives you extra health and damage.
  • Drop a Tombstone when the enemy tries to pull or stack creeps – the zombies force them to fight under tower or waste mana on clearing.
  • Pair Soul Rip with your partner’s burst (e.g., Lion) to either heal them or amplify damage on a target; the heal also mitigates harassment from tough matchups like Monkey King.
  • Prioritize stacking the neutral camp near your lane; the extra creep kills synergize with Decay’s 2× damage to creeps, giving you extra gold and lane dominance.
  • Keep an eye on enemy support rotations; if a hero like Earthshaker or Marci appears, stay behind your tower and use Tombstone to block their initiation.

Mid Game

  • Aim for Flesh Golem before major team fights; the strength boost and attack‑slow amplify the damage of your cores and make enemy heroes (especially those reliant on physical damage such as Alchemist) far less effective.
  • Control the map with Tombstone placed in high‑traffic choke points (Roshan, jungle entrances) to deter pushes from heroes like Beastmaster or Treant Protector.
  • Use Soul Rip on wounded allies during fights to keep them alive, or on enemy heroes to add extra burst when combined with your team's disables.
  • Transition to a semi‑core role by buying a Guardian Greaves or Mekansm to sustain front‑line fights and keep your Flesh Golem active longer.

Late Game

  • Win by forcing fights around your Tombstone and Flesh Golem; the combined slow and damage amplification can cripple high‑damage carries (e.g., Luna, Night Stalker).
  • Position yourself just behind your front line; over‑extending without a Tombstone leaves you vulnerable to burst from the toughest matchups (Monkey King, Earthshaker).
  • Secure objectives with Soul Rip‑healed teammates; a well‑timed Flesh Golem during Roshan or high‑ground pushes often decides the game.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane, especially against poke from Lion or Night Stalker.
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery after early trades.
  • Observer Ward — vision to protect Tombstone placements.
  • Iron Branch x2 — cheap stat boost and can be later used for a Magic Wand.

Core Items

  • Guardian Greaves — provides strong team heal, armor, and movement speed, synergizing with Soul Rip.
  • Pipe of Insight — counters magic burst from heroes like Lion and Marci, which are currently tough matchups.
  • Mekansm — extra burst heal and armor for team fights, works well with Flesh Golem’s damage amplification.

Situational Items

  • Vladmir’s Offering — great against physical‑damage lineups (Alchemist, Beastmaster).
  • Aghanim’s Shard — upgrades Soul Rip to affect a larger radius, useful when fighting clustered enemies.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects targeted disables from Earthshaker or Monkey King.
  • Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — self‑save against burst and sets up Tombstone placement.
  • Aghanim’s Blessing — if you need extra survivability against high‑damage carries like Luna.

Common Mistakes

  • Placing Tombstone too far forward – enemies can clear it before it spawns zombies, wasting its zoning potential.
  • Using Decay on heroes with low strength – the strength steal is minimal; focus on tankier opponents or creeps for gold.
  • Activating Flesh Golem without a follow‑up engage – the slow and damage amp are useless if you don’t have allies ready to capitalize.
  • Neglecting vision – without wards, opponents can dodge your Tombstone and isolate you, especially against mobile heroes like Monkey King.

FAQ

Is Undying good in the current patch?

Yes. Undying enjoys a 52.3 % win rate across 466 k recent ranked matches, making him a solid pick in the current meta, especially against heroes like Lion (60.7 % win) and Abaddon (57.6 % win).

What lane does Undying play?

Undying is typically played as a hard support in the safe lane (radiant bottom or dire top), where he can use Decay and Tombstone to control the lane and protect his carry.

Who counters Undying?

The toughest matchups are against Monkey King (30.1 % win), Treant Protector (37.3 % win), Alchemist (38.9 % win), Marci (39.0 % win), Beastmaster (40.0 % win), and Earthshaker (40.0 % win). These heroes either out‑maneuver his Tombstone or out‑damage him before Flesh Golem can turn the fight.

Monkey King

Monkey King’s high mobility and burst damage let him dodge Tombstone zombies and quickly close the distance to kill Undying before his Decay can swing the strength balance. Use Boundless Strike to jump over the Tombstone zone and Jungle Strike to burst him down before he can activate Flesh Golem.
Tip: Keep a Wukong’s Guard active to block Decay’s damage and reduce the strength he steals.

Treant’s Living Armor and Nature’s Guise give him strong sustain and invisibility, making Undying’s Decay and Soul Rip far less threatening. The Overgrowth ultimate can root Undying and his zombies, shutting down his damage amplification.
Tip: Position your Nature’s Guise near the lane to avoid Tombstone spawns and force Undying to waste his early aggression.

Alchemist

Alchemist’s Acid Spray and Unstable Concoction provide massive lane harassment that forces Undying to stay on low‑health creeps, preventing him from stealing strength. Chemical Rage gives Alchemist huge health pools, making him hard to kill with Decay or Soul Rip.
Tip: Use Goblins Greed to buy early Mekansm; the burst heal counters Undying’s damage and the armor helps survive Tombstone zombies.

Marci

Marci’s Rebound and Dispose give her superior chase and burst, allowing her to quickly close on Undying and kill him before he can set a Tombstone. Her Sidekick provides a shield that blocks Decay’s damage and reduces the strength gain.

  • Prioritize heroes with strong early burst or mobility (e.g., Monkey King, Marci).
  • Pick tanky heroes with self‑heal or damage‑reduction (Alchemist, Treant).
  • Include silences or strong disables to stop Decay and Tombstone activation.
  • Avoid heavy reliance on pure right‑click heroes that benefit from Undying’s damage amplification.

Laning Against Undying

  • Harass him before he can land Decay on multiple creeps; early damage denies strength gain.
  • Force him to use Soul Rip on creeps instead of allies, reducing his sustain.
  • Trade when his Tombstone is on cooldown – his zombie pressure drops dramatically.
  • Use ranged harassment or invisibility to stay out of his Decay radius and force him to over‑extend.

Crimson Guard — armor block reduces the physical damage amplification from Flesh Golem.
Glimmer Cape — temporary invisibility lets you dodge Tombstone zombies and avoid Decay’s strength steal.

ursa.name: Ursa
ursa.guideHtml:
Ursa remains a high‑damage, early‑to‑mid‑game carry with strong durability thanks to his innate HP scaling and Enrage. On patch 7.41 his overall pub win rate sits at 47.1% over 245 k ranked games, placing him as a solid but not dominant pick in the current meta.

How to Play Ursa

Laning Phase

  • Use Earthshock to secure the first creep kill and to harass enemy heroes; the 250‑unit leap also lets you dodge early harass.
  • Activate Overpower right before a 2‑second window of enemy cooldowns to maximize attack speed for a quick tower or creep wave clear.
  • Prioritize hitting the same target with Fury Swipes; each successive hit adds ~30 damage (scales with level), so focus on a single hero or creep for maximum burst.
  • Keep an eye on Maul – when you’re above ~70 % HP, the bonus damage becomes significant; avoid unnecessary trades that drop you below this threshold.
  • Trade aggressively against melee supports (e.g., Bounty Hunter) but play conservatively versus ranged harassers (e.g., Dark Willow) until you have a level 6 Enrage.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 6: Enrage gives damage reduction and status resistance, allowing you to dive into fights and survive burst.
  • Aim for Roshan after securing a few tier‑2 items; your HP‑based Maul damage makes you a natural tank for the pit.
  • Join split‑push lanes where you can Overpower a tower while using Fury Swipes on any defender; avoid full‑team fights against Enigma or Treant Protector until you have at least Heart of Tarrasque.
  • Use Earthshock to initiate on isolated targets; the slow helps you close the gap before Enrage expires.

Late Game

  • Win condition: Take high‑ground towers and Roshan while forcing the enemy to respond; your burst from Fury Swipes + Maul can eliminate squishies before they can react.
  • Position near the front line with Enrage active; your strong dispel and damage reduction let you absorb spells that would otherwise kill a typical carry.
  • Avoid prolonged fights against heroes with strong crowd‑control or magical burst (e.g., Enigma’s Black Hole) – you’ll lose the game if you get locked down before Enrage can purge.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango + Healing Salve — sustain for early trades and staying healthy for Maul.
  • Stout Shield — reduces harass damage from ranged supports.
  • Quelling Blade — faster creep last‑hits to snowball early farm.

Core Items

  • Phase Boots — provides the mobility needed for Earthshock initiations and tower dives.
  • Mask of Madness — huge attack‑speed boost that synergizes with Overpower and Fury Swipes.
  • Black King Bar — essential against spell‑heavy lineups; protects your Maul damage and Enrage uptime.
  • Heart of Tarrasque — maximizes Maul’s HP‑percentage damage and gives you the tankiness to survive team fights.

Situational Items

  • Abyssal Blade — reliable stun to lock down Enigma or Lycan; works well with Earthshock.
  • Satanic — lifesteal for late‑game survivability when you’re the primary front‑liner.
  • Linken’s Sphere — blocks single‑target disables from Chen, Alchemist’s Chemical Rage, or Treant Protector’s Overgrowth.
  • Assault Cuirass — armor reduction helps against high‑armor heroes like Timbersaw and improves your overall DPS.
  • Shiva’s Guard — provides additional armor and an AoE slow that pairs with Earthshock in team fights.

Common Mistakes

  • Wasting Overpower on creeps – use it on heroes or towers where the attack‑speed boost translates to burst, not on pure wave‑clear.
  • Ignoring Maul’s HP threshold – dropping below ~70 % HP drastically reduces your damage; back off to heal before re‑engaging.
  • Chasing into Enigma or Treant Protector – these are the toughest matchups (Ursa win ≈ 33 % vs Enigma); avoid extended fights without BKB or Linken’s.
  • Over‑extending without vision – Ursa’s lack of mobility after Enrage ends makes him vulnerable to ganks; always have a ward before diving.

FAQ

Is Ursa good in the current patch?

Yes. Ursa’s win rate of 47.1% across 245 k recent ranked games shows he’s a viable carry, especially on maps where early Roshan and tower pressure are possible.

What lane does Ursa play?

Ursa is typically played in the safe lane (position 1) as a carry, allowing him to farm safely while using Earthshock and Overpower to secure early lane dominance.

Who counters Ursa?

The hardest matchups are Enigma, Treant Protector, Alchemist, Chen, Lycan, and Bounty Hunter, where Ursa’s win rates dip below 40 %. Their strong disables, high armor, or burst damage can out‑scale Ursa’s early advantage.
ursa.counterHtml:
Ursa’s threat comes from his insane burst damage once he lands a few hits with Fury Swipes and stacks Overpower. The key to shutting him down is denying him the sustained melee trades that let his damage snowball, either by out‑lasting his burst window or by constantly removing his attack‑speed advantage.

Why These Heroes Beat Ursa

Enigma

Enigma’s Black Hole forces Ursa to stand in a massive AOE while his Overpower timer expires, nullifying his attack‑speed burst. Additionally, Astral Prison can lock Ursa away before he can close the distance. Tip: Use Midnight Pulse early to chip Ursa’s health and force him to play defensively.

Treant Protector

Treant’s Nature’s Guise grants true‑sight and a brief invisibility, letting him dodge Ursa’s Earthshock and avoid early trades. Living Armor gives Treant massive HP regeneration, out‑lasting Ursa’s burst, while Overgrowth roots Ursa, preventing the melee chase. Tip: Plant a Living Armor tree near the lane creep wave to keep your HP high while Ursa tries to engage.

Alchemist

Alchemist’s Acid Spray applies a damage‑over‑time that reduces Urna’s effective HP, and his Unstable Concoction forces Ursa to either waste a Overpower window or miss the explosion. Chemical Rage gives massive HP and damage reduction, making Ursa’s burst less lethal. Tip: Start with Acid Spray on the lane to chip Ursa and force him to use Overpower prematurely.

Chen

Chen’s Penitence slows Ursa’s movement, extending the time Ursa needs to close the gap for Earthshock and Overpower. His Holy Persuasion can pull a neutral creep onto Ursa, disrupting his focus and breaking Fury Swipes stacks. Tip: Keep a neutral creep with Holy Persuasion near the lane to constantly harass Ursa’s positioning.

Lycan

Lycan’s Summon Wolves provides constant pressure and extra sources of damage that force Ursa to split his attacks, breaking Fury Swipes stacks. Shapeshift gives Lycan high armor and HP, letting him survive Ursa’s burst and retaliate with Howl to boost his own attack speed. Tip: Use Summon Wolves early to contest the lane and force Ursa to waste Overpower on multiple targets.

Drafting Against Ursa

  • Prioritize heroes with strong disables or AOE crowd control (e.g., Black Hole, Overgrowth).
  • Pick tanks or heroes with high natural HP regeneration and damage reduction (e.g., Alchemist’s Chemical Rage, Lycan’s Shapeshift).
  • Include at least one hero with a reliable strong dispel to remove Enrage (e.g., Oracle, Abaddon).
  • Consider bans that remove Ursa’s primary lane partners who grant him early farm (e.g., Spirit Breaker, Tiny).

Laning Against Ursa

  • Trade when Ursa’s Overpower cooldown is up; his attack speed drops dramatically.
  • Harass him with slows or roots to keep his distance and prevent him from stacking Fury Swipes.
  • Force him to use Enrage early; once it expires, he is vulnerable to burst and dispels.
  • Pull the creep wave to deny him easy access to the neutral camp, limiting his early farm.

Itemizing Against Ursa

Ghost Scepter — blocks Ursa’s melee attacks, nullifying his Fury Swipes damage during his burst window.
Lotus Orb — reflects Ursa’s Earthshock and provides a strong dispel to remove Enrage.
Heaven’s Halberd — disarms Ursa, cutting his attack‑speed advantage and preventing Fury Swipes stacking.
Crimson Guard — high armor block mitigates the massive physical damage from Ursa’s combo.
