witch-doctor.name: Witch Doctor
witch-doctor.guideHtml:
Witch Doctor remains a solid support/nuker with a 51.8% win rate across 573,576 recent ranked games, making him a reliable pick in the 7.41 meta despite a few tough match‑ups. His toolkit—Paralyzing Cask, Voodoo Restoration, Maledict, and the game‑changing Death Ward—lets him control team fights, sustain allies, and punish over‑extended enemies. Play him aggressively in the early game and transition to a vision‑and‑damage backbone for your carry in the late game.

How to Play Witch Doctor

Laning Phase

  • Paralyzing Cask on wave clear: launch the cask into the creep block to stun and damage multiple enemy heroes when they stack for a pull or harass.
  • Voodoo Restoration early sustain: toggle on when you and your lane partner are low; manage mana carefully (≈3 %/sec) to avoid running out before the 2‑minute mark.
  • Maledict on low‑health heroes: place it on a wounded enemy (or their pull) to amplify damage; the burst every 4 s scales with missing health, making it lethal against squishy mid‑lane heroes.
  • Ward placement: prioritize a tier‑2 observer near the enemy jungle entrance to spot early rotations from Ember Spirit, Sniper, or Necrophos—your toughest match‑ups (win ≈ 30‑34 %).
  • Avoid over‑extending: the cask can bounce to your own creeps; keep a safe distance from aggressive mid heroes like Ember Spirit and Snapfire.

Mid Game

  • Death Ward timing: activate Voodoo Switcheroo before a team fight to become invisible and drop the ward; aim it at the enemy backline where heroes such as Sniper or Dark Willow are clustered.
  • Maledict combo: follow a successful Paralyzing Cask bounce with Maledict on the same target; the combined damage spikes during the 4‑second burst windows.
  • Vision control: buy a Sentry Ward and Observer Ward early; controlling Roshan and river vision lets you safely set up Death Wards and prevents ganks from Lifestealer or Ember Spirit.
  • Power spike: hitting level 6 (Death Ward) and acquiring Aghanim’s Shard (adds a second cask bounce) dramatically increases your team‑fight impact.

Late Game

  • Positioning for Death Ward: stay hidden behind allies or in fog of war; the ward’s 50 % bonus accuracy is wasted if you’re focused down.
  • Sustain through Voodoo Restoration: keep the heal active during prolonged sieges; the mana cost is offset by the gold stored in Gris‑Gris if you die, allowing a quick repurchase.
  • Win condition: force fights where you can land a full‑bounce Cask onto multiple enemies, then drop Death Ward for burst damage; this combo often decides late‑game engagements.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — basic sustain for the lane.
  • Healing Salve — emergency burst heal against early harass.
  • Observer Ward — essential vision against gank‑heavy mid heroes.
  • Clarity ×2 — mana for early Voodoo Restoration usage.

Core Items

  • Aghanim’s Shard — adds a second bounce to Paralyzing Cask, increasing stun potential.
  • Glimmer Cape — provides magic immunity for yourself or a carry when you’re about to drop Death Ward.
  • Force Staff — helps you escape the focus of Lifestealer, Ember Spirit, or Snapfire.
  • Mekansm — synergizes with Voodoo Restoration for team‑wide healing in team fights.

Situational Items

  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Death Ward to a longer channel and higher damage; ideal against line‑ups with multiple squishy heroes (e.g., Sniper, Zeus).
  • Lotus Orb — reflects targeted disables from Dark Willow or Snapfire.
  • Ghost Scepter — protects you from right‑click burst from Lifestealer or Ursa.
  • Eul’s Scepter — extra crowd control and a way to save yourself from Ember Spirit’s Sleight of Fist.
  • Scythe of Vyse — hard‑disable for heroes that otherwise out‑scale you, such as Necrophos.

Common Mistakes

  • Wasting Voodoo Restoration mana on full‑health allies instead of toggling it only when needed.
  • Casting Paralyzing Cask without checking bounce paths, often stunning your own creeps and losing lane control.
  • Delaying Death Ward until after the fight starts; you lose the window to catch multiple enemies.
  • Neglecting vision in the mid lane, allowing Ember Spirit or Sniper to roam and pick you off.

FAQ

Is Witch Doctor good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 51.8% win rate across over half a million ranked games, Witch Doctor is a reliable support/nuker. His ability to heal, stun, and deliver massive burst with Death Ward keeps him relevant despite a few unfavorable match‑ups.

What lane does Witch Doctor play?

Witch Doctor is typically played in the safe lane as a support, pairing with a carry to provide sustain and early crowd control. He can also be flexed to the mid lane against heroes he can harass with Paralyzing Cask, though match‑ups like Ember Spirit and Sniper are statistically tough (win ≈ 30‑34 %).

Who counters Witch Doctor?

The toughest opponents are Ember Spirit, Sniper, Necrophos, Snapfire, Dark Willow, and Lifestealer, each giving Witch Doctor sub‑35 % win rates. Their high mobility, burst damage, or strong disables can out‑pace Witch Doctor’s healing and crowd control if you lack vision and proper positioning.
witch-doctor.counterHtml:
Witch Doctor thrives on long‑range burst damage and sustained healing, making him a nightmare in mid‑to‑late game teamfights where his Paralyzing Cask, Maledict, and Death Ward can quickly swing fights. The key to shutting him down is to deny him the safe window to land his spells and to out‑scale his low‑damage, high‑utility kit with heroes that can either burst him before he casts or silence/disable his channeling.

Why These Heroes Beat Witch Doctor

Ember Spirit

Ember’s Sleight of Hand and Flame Guard let him dodge the initial Cask bounce and survive Maledict’s damage spikes, while Fire Remnant provides instant repositioning to avoid the Death Ward’s line of fire. Tip: land a Searing Chains after his first hit to lock him down while his Flame Guard is on cooldown.

Sniper

Sniper’s extreme range forces Witch Doctor to commit a long‑range Cask that often misses, and Assassinate can snipe Witch Doctor before he finishes a Maledict or Death Ward channel. Tip: keep Headshot stacks high and use Take Aim to stay out of Ember Spirit‑style bounces.

Necrophos

Necrophos’s Heartstopper Aura continuously chips Witch Doctor’s health, making the damage from Maledict’s burst ticks relatively insignificant, while Reaper’s Scythe can finish him off after a failed Paralyzing Cask. Tip: time a Soul Rip just after Witch Doctor lands a Cask to punish his mana‑heavy Voodoo Restoration.

Snapfire

Snapfire’s Cookie provides a shield that blocks the first Cask stun, and Mortimer Kisses can force Witch Doctor to retreat before he can set up a Death Ward. Tip: use Lil’ Snapper to scout and interrupt Witch Doctor’s channeling with a well‑placed stun.

Dark Willow

Bramble Maze creates terrain that blocks the ricocheting Cask, and Cursed Crown silences Witch Doctor, cancelling Maledict and Death Ward. Tip: follow up a successful Shadow Realm dive with a Vanish to escape any remaining Cask bounces.

Drafting Against Witch Doctor

  • Prioritize heroes with long‑range disables or silences (e.g., Silencer, Shadow Shaman).
  • Pick burst damage heroes that can kill before Witch Doctor finishes Maledict or Death Ward.
  • Ban or avoid high‑mana sustain heroes that can out‑heal his Voodoo Restoration (e.g., Warlock, Dazzle).
  • Favor mobile heroes that can dodge Cask bounces and reposition quickly.

Laning Against Witch Doctor

  • Harass him early; his Paralyzing Cask has a long cooldown at low levels, leaving him vulnerable to last‑hits.
  • Force him to use Voodoo Restoration defensively; the mana drain will limit his ability to cast Maledict later.
  • Trade when his Maledict is on cooldown—its damage over time is a major source of lane pressure.
  • Push the lane when you have a stun ready, as Witch Doctor’s escape relies on Paralyzing Cask bounce and limited mobility.

Itemizing Against Witch Doctor

Eul's Scepter — provides a reliable self‑silence to dodge Paralyzing Cask and a cheap way to interrupt Death Ward.

Ghost Scepter — makes you untargetable by his Death Ward and reduces damage from his Maledict bursts.

Black King Bar — grants spell immunity, nullifying Maledict, Paralyzing Cask, and Death Ward during crucial fights.

Scythe of Vyse — a hard‑disable that can lock Witch Doctor down before he finishes channeling his ultimate.

Abyssal Blade — burst stun removes his ability to reposition with Paralyzing Cask and forces him to lose his Voodoo Restoration mana pool.

wraith-king.name: Wraith King
wraith-king.guideHtml:
Wraith King remains a high‑impact carry with a simple, forgiving kit that thrives on raw damage and survivability. His 54.7 % win rate across 468 k recent ranked games shows he is still a solid pick, especially on the safe lane where his scaling and Reincarnation shine.

How to Play Wraith King

Laning Phase

  • Wraithfire Blast early harass: use the stun + damage + slow to zone out enemy off‑laners and secure last hits against ranged heroes.
  • Bone Guard charges from creeps: focus on efficient creep stacking to build charges quickly; each charge spawns a skeleton that provides extra lane presence and tankiness.
  • Mortal Strike timing: attack after the cooldown (≈ 8 s) to maximize burst, especially when trading with melee opponents.
  • Vampiric Spirit lifesteal: trade aggressively against low‑HP heroes (e.g., Zeus, Silencer) to sustain lane health.
  • Reincarnation safety: position near a creep wave or tower so the 600‑radius slow on death can protect you from immediate follow‑up kills.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 12 – unlocks Reincarnation and Bone Guard charges; start grouping for 2‑vs‑2 fights.
  • Push with skeletons: activate Bone Guard before sieging towers; the summoned skeletons tank tower shots and add damage.
  • Target soft‑carries: use Wraithfire Blast on heroes like Shadow Shaman or Lion who lack strong escape, then follow with a melee auto‑attack empowered by Mortal Strike.
  • Map control: place deep wards and use Reincarnation’s death‑radius slow to deter enemy ganks while you split‑push.

Late Game

  • Win condition – sustained front‑line damage: keep Reincarnation alive, build lifesteal/tank items, and force fights where your skeleton army can soak damage.
  • Positioning: stay just behind your frontline; if you die, the 600‑radius slow buys time for teammates to disengage.
  • What loses the game: getting locked down by stuns (e.g., Earthshaker) before you can trigger Reincarnation, or being forced to die repeatedly without enough charges for Bone Guard, which removes your skeleton buffer.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in lane, especially against poke heroes like Zeus.
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery after early trades.
  • Stout Shield — mitigates harassment from Pudge and Earthshaker.
  • Quelling Blade — improves last‑hit reliability for a farm‑heavy hero.
  • Iron Branch ×2 — cheap stats and can be later built into a Magic Wand.

Core Items

  • Power Treads — attack speed for Mortal Strike and flexibility between strength/attack speed.
  • Radiance — provides consistent damage and farming speed; synergizes with skeletons’ tankiness.
  • Black King Bar — essential against disables from Earthshaker, Pudge, and Necrophos.
  • Assault Cuirass — armor aura protects you and your skeletons, while reducing enemy armor for your attacks.

Situational Items

  • Abyssal Blade — locks down slippery heroes like Snapfire and Dragon Knight; the stun prevents them from interrupting Reincarnation.
  • Mekansm — extra team heal and armor when fighting Necrophos or Lich who rely on damage over time.
  • Heart of Tarrasque — massive survivability if you’re frequently targeted by burst (e.g., Earthshaker).
  • Satanic — lifesteal burst to survive extended fights; works well with Vampiric Spirit.
  • Shiva’s Guard — armor and AoE slow against high‑damage right‑click heroes; also reduces enemy attack speed.

Common Mistakes

  • Wasting Bone Guard charges on single‑target kills instead of stacking on creeps for larger skeleton waves.
  • Ignoring Reincarnation cooldown: fighting without a clear escape path leaves you vulnerable to stuns that prevent the revive.
  • Over‑extending without vision: Pudge hooks and Earthshaker fissures punish aggressive positioning, especially early.
  • Neglecting lifesteal: failing to build Vampiric Spirit‑compatible items leads to unnecessary deaths against sustain heroes like Necrophos.

FAQ

Is Wraith King good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 54.7 % win rate across nearly half a million recent ranked matches, Wraith King is a reliable carry, especially on the safe lane where his scaling and Reincarnation give him a strong late‑game presence.

What lane does Wraith King play?

Wraith King is most commonly played in the safe (carry) lane. His ability to farm with Bone Guard charges and survive early aggression makes him a classic position‑1 hero.

Who counters Wraith King?

The toughest matchups are Earthshaker, Pudge, Necrophos, Lich, Snapfire, and Dragon Knight, where Wraith King wins under 45 % of games. These heroes provide strong disables or damage over time that can prevent his Reincarnation and overwhelm his skeleton army.
wraith-king.counterHtml:
Wraith King’s threat comes from his unstoppable Reincarnation and the relentless pressure of Bone Guard skeletons, which let him stay in fights far longer than most melee carries. The key to shutting him down is to deny his survivability windows and punish the moments before he can trigger his resurrection.

Why These Heroes Beat Wraith King

Earthshaker

Earthshaker’s Fissure and Echo Slam punish the clustered skeletons from Bone Guard, while Enchant Totem provides a burst of damage that can kill Wraith King before Reincarnation finishes its cooldown. Tip: land a Fissure to block his retreat path, then follow up with Echo Slam when he dies to deny the resurrection.

Pudge

Pudge’s Meat Hook pulls Wraith King out of his safe lane position, forcing him into a vulnerable 1‑v‑1 where his low early damage is exposed. The Dismember silence prevents him from using Mortal Strike or activating Reincarnation. Tip: hook him when he attempts to farm the low‑creep wave; the stun also stops his skeletons from spawning.

Necrophos

Necrophos’s Death Pulse deals pure damage that ignores armor, cutting down both Wraith King and his skeletons, while Heartstopper Aura constantly chips his health, making the Reincarnation timer expire faster. Tip: time a Reaper & Scythe on the moment he resurrects to finish him before his skeletons can re‑engage.

Lich

Lich’s Frost Blast slows Wraith King, limiting his chase potential, and Chain Frost can bounce between the skeletons, wiping them out and draining his lifesteal from Vampiric Spirit. Tip: use Sacrifice on a high‑value creep to deny Bone Guard charges early in the lane.

Snapfire

Snapfire’s Cookie provides a strong burst of damage and a stun that interrupts Wraith King’s attack animation, while Mortimer Kisses can hit him from a safe distance, preventing him from getting close enough to trigger Reincarnation. Tip: position Mortimer Kisses behind his front line; the splash will also kill his skeletons, reducing his damage output.

Drafting Against Wraith King

  • Prioritize hard‑disable heroes (stuns, silences) that can lock him down before Reincarnation triggers.
  • Pick burst‑damage heroes with pure or magic damage to bypass his armor and lifesteal.
  • Include at least one hero that can reliably clear multiple units (e.g., Echo Slam, Death Pulse).
  • Consider early‑game aggression to prevent him from stacking Bone Guard charges.

Laning Against Wraith King

  • Harass him before he can secure two creep kills; his first Bone Guard charge comes only after 2 creeps.
  • Trade when his Mortal Strike cooldown is up, as his burst damage drops significantly.
  • Use lane control (pulls, denies) to keep his creep pool low, limiting his charge generation.
  • Punish any over‑extension with a well‑timed stun or hook, forcing him to retreat and lose farm.

Itemizing Against Wraith King

Heaven’s Halberd — disarms him, preventing the attack that would trigger Reincarnation.
Spirit Vessel — applies a heal‑reduction debuff that counters Vampiric Spirit lifesteal.
Crimson Guard — blocks the damage from his skeleton swarm and reduces the impact of Bone Guard.
Scythe of Vyse — provides a reliable long‑duration hex that stops him from casting Reincarnation or using Mortal Strike.

The key to shutting him down is to deny his survivability windows and punish the moments before he can trigger his resurrection.

faq.a: Wraith King is most commonly played in the safe (carry) lane. His ability to farm with Bone Guard charges and survive early aggression makes him a classic position‑1 hero.

The toughest matchups are Earthshaker, Pudge, Necrophos, Lich, Snapfire, and Dragon Knight, where Wraith King wins under 45 % of games. These heroes provide strong disables or damage over time that can prevent his Reincarnation and overwhelm his skeleton army.

zeus.name: Zeus
zeus.guideHtml:
Zeus is a pure magical nuker who can also function as a late‑game carry thanks to his global damage. On patch 7.41 his overall pub win rate sits at 51.7% over 749,786 ranked games, making him a solid pick in many lineups, though he still struggles against certain melee‑heavy heroes.

How to Play Zeus

Laning Phase

  • Use Lightning Bolt on enemy creeps to secure last hits and harass the off‑lane; the mini‑stun and vision also deny safe pulls.
  • Toggle Lightning Hands early (level 2) to turn every attack into an extra Arc Lightning, boosting lane damage against heroes like Juggernaut or Wraith King.
  • Drop Heavenly Jump on the first enemy hero that steps into vision to apply a movement/attack‑speed slow and force a defensive response.
  • Keep Arc Lightning ready to bounce between stacked neutral camps when you need extra farm or to clear the wave quickly.
  • Prioritize a Soul Ring (or Faerie Fire) if you find yourself mana‑starved against high‑damage lane opponents such as Void Spirit.

Mid Game

  • Aim for a Nimbus on contested jungle camps or near enemy towers to provide constant Lightning Bolt pressure and true sight for vision‑denying enemies.
  • Hit your Thundergod's Wrath after a successful gank or when the enemy team is clustered; the global true sight also reveals invisible heroes like Wraith King.
  • Pair Static Field with a high‑damage item (e.g., Aghanim’s Scepter) to punish any hero that attacks you, especially against melee heroes who rely on auto‑attacks.
  • Push lanes with Nimbus + Lightning Bolt while keeping an eye on Roshan; Zeus’s damage spikes when he has a few items and can take objectives safely from a distance.

Late Game

  • Position near the back of your team and use Thundergod's Wrath as the ultimate team‑fight finisher; the global range means you never need to be in the front line.
  • Maintain Nimbus on high‑traffic areas (e.g., near the enemy jungle entrance) to provide constant pressure and vision, forcing the enemy to waste resources on detection.
  • Lose the game if you overextend without Nimbus or Aghanim’s Scepter, as Zeus’s lack of mobility makes him vulnerable to heroes like Juggernaut and Void Spirit who currently give him sub‑35% win rates.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain against harass in solo lanes.
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery after early skirmishes.
  • Faerie Fire — cheap burst heal for clutch moments.
  • Observer Ward — early vision to protect against ganks from the toughest matchups (e.g., Juggernaut).
  • Iron Branch ×2 — cheap stats and can be later built into a Magic Wand.

Core Items

  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Nimbus to cast Lightning Bolt on a larger radius and adds a second global cast of Thundergod's Wrath.
  • Aghanim’s Shard — grants Heavenly Jump for extra mobility and a reliable stun.
  • Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — provides a defensive escape and a setup for Lightning Bolt on stunned targets.
  • Scythe of Vyse — solidifies Zeus’s control against mobile heroes like Void Spirit and Juggernaut.
  • Octarine Core — reduces cooldowns on all spells, making Nimbus and Thundergod's Wrath spammable.

Situational Items

  • Black King Bar — essential against heavy magical burst (e.g., Shadow Demon, Venomancer).
  • Shiva’s Guard — armor and AoE slow help survive against physical heroes such as Juggernaut and Wraith King.
  • Lotus Orb — reflects single‑target disables, useful versus Keeper of the Light’s Mana Leak.
  • Aether Lens — increases cast range, allowing safer Lightning Bolt and Heavenly Jump from farther away.
  • Refresher Orb — enables a double Thundergod's Wrath in late‑game team fights when you have enough mana.

Common Mistakes

  • Over‑committing without Nimbus – diving in without the global safety net leaves Zeus easy prey for melee heroes.
  • Neglecting mana management – spamming Lightning Bolt early can leave you powerless for a gank; always keep a Soul Ring or Mana Potion handy.
  • Ignoring vision – Zeus’s strength is vision; forgetting to place wards lets opponents hide, nullifying his true‑sight advantage.
  • Failing to toggle Lightning Hands – staying on default attack reduces lane damage and overall DPS, especially against heroes with high HP like Wraith King.

FAQ

Is Zeus good in the current patch?

Yes. Zeus holds a 51.7% win rate across nearly 750 k ranked games, making him a reliable pick. His global damage and vision tools remain strong, though he must be careful against melee carries that currently give him sub‑35% win rates.

What lane does Zeus play?

Zeus is most commonly played in the safe lane (position 1) as a late‑game carry, but he can also be flexed to the mid lane for early gank potential. In solo lanes he leverages Lightning Bolt and Lightning Hands to secure farm and harass.

Who counters Zeus?

The toughest matchups are Juggernaut, Void Spirit, Wraith King, Beastmaster, Keeper of the Light, and Venomancer, each giving Zeus win rates below 40%. Their high burst, mobility, or strong disables force Zeus to stay back and rely heavily on vision and defensive items.
zeus.counterHtml:
Zeus’s massive burst damage and global presence make him a constant threat, especially in the mid‑late game when Thundergod’s Wrath can finish fights from anywhere. The key to shutting him down is denying his vision, surviving his Lightning Bolt combo, and forcing him into melee range where his low survivability can be exploited.

Why These Heroes Beat Zeus

Juggernaut

Juggernaut’s Blade Fury provides continuous magic‑damage immunity to Zeus’s Arc Lightning and Lightning Bolt, while Healing Ward grants sustained lane sustain against Zeus’s poke. Tip: Time Blade Fury to overlap Zeus’s Nimbus cast; the constant damage negates the cloud’s burst and forces Zeus to retreat.

Void Spirit

Void Spirit’s Astral Step lets him dodge Lightning Bolt and close the distance instantly, while Resonant Pulse deals magic damage that scales with Zeus’s health, punishing his high‑damage output. Tip: Use Astral Step to jump behind Zeus after he lands Nimbus, then follow with Resonant Pulse to capitalize on his low mobility.

Wraith King

Wraith King’s high base armor and innate stun from Mortal Strike reduce Zeus’s damage and interrupt his spell chain, while Reincarnation forces Zeus to waste Lightning Bolt on a dead target. Tip: Initiate with Mortal Strike as soon as Zeus casts Lightning Bolt; the stun prevents the follow‑up Arc Lightning bounce.

Beastmaster

Beastmaster’s summons provide constant vision and tanking, negating Zeus’s True Sight advantage, while his Primal Roar stun blocks Zeus’s ability rotation. Tip: Position a Boar to block Zeus’s line of sight for Nimbus; the stun from Primal Roar then secures a kill.

Keeper of the Light

Keeper’s Chakra Magic grants mana sustain, allowing him to out‑spam Zeus’s Lightning Bolt, while Illuminate’s burst can instantly punish Zeus’s low health after a failed Nimbus. Tip: Save Illuminate for the moment Zeus uses Nimbus; the burst will often finish him before he can retreat with his vision.

Drafting Against Zeus

  • Prioritize heroes with built‑in magic immunity or spell‑block (e.g., Blade Fury, Astral Step).
  • Pick strong early‑game lane dominators who can out‑harass Zeus before he gets his core items.
  • Include at least one reliable stun or silence to interrupt his Lightning Bolt combo.
  • Ban or avoid heroes that grant Zeus extra vision or mana (e.g., heroes with many true‑sight sources).

Laning Against Zeus

  • Trade when Zeus is on cooldown after casting Lightning Bolt; his burst window is short.
  • Harass aggressively before he can secure his first Arc Lightning bounce, forcing him to waste mana on defensive items.
  • Exploit his lack of escape: engage when his Nimbus is on cooldown, as he loses global pressure.
  • Use creep wave manipulation to deny him the unobstructed vision radius from Lightning Bolt.

Itemizing Against Zeus

Black King Bar — blocks Lightning Bolt and Thundergod’s Wrath, letting you survive his global burst.
Manta Style — dispels the static field slow and creates confusion for Zeus’s single‑target focus.
Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — provides a reliable way to dodge Nimbus and set up a counter‑engage while silencing Zeus.
Pipe of Insight — grants magic resistance to all allies, reducing the impact of Arc Lightning and Nimbus.

night-stalker.name: Night Stalker
night-stalker.guideHtml:
Night Stalker is a night‑time ganker who thrives as a durable initiator and semi‑carry, leveraging his night‑enhanced mobility and crowd‑control to dominate the map after dusk. On patch 7.41 his overall pub win rate sits at 52.5% over 264 k recent ranked games, making him a solid pick in the current meta despite a few tough lane match‑ups.

How to Play Night Stalker

Laning Phase

  • Use Void early to harass and mini‑stun enemy heroes when the night timer is low; the stun component scales with the night bonus and can interrupt early channeling spells.
  • Pair Crippling Fear with a tower dive or aggressive creep block; the silence and damage‑over‑time are especially potent after the first night when the duration is longest.
  • Prioritize farming the off‑lane creep wave while keeping the enemy hero in the void’s slow zone; Night Stalker’s natural tankiness lets him survive trades that other cores would avoid.
  • Against heroes like Lifestealer or Shadow Fiend (who currently give you < 40% win rates), play conservatively until you hit level 6 and can initiate with Dark Ascension.
  • Keep an eye on the day/night cycle; transition to a more aggressive stance a few seconds before night falls to maximize the extra movement speed from Hunter in the Night.

Mid Game

  • Power spike at level 12: you gain the full night‑time movement speed bonus and can start rotating with Dark Ascension for early tower dives.
  • Use Dark Ascension to create vision‑free zones around key objectives (Roshan, high‑ground towers) and force fights where the enemy loses sight.
  • Coordinate with your team to secure night‑time pick‑offs; the combination of Void mini‑stun and Crippling Fear silence can lock down squishy cores like Zeus or Silencer (who are among your easiest match‑ups).
  • When you have Blink Dagger or Shadow Blade, look for split‑push opportunities: night vision and flight let you bypass enemy wards and catch out‑of‑position heroes.

Late Game

  • Win condition: force a decisive night‑time team fight where you can Dark Ascend, initiate with Void, and lock down multiple enemies with Crippling Fear; the extra damage and flight make it hard for the enemy to disengage.
  • Positioning tip: stay just outside enemy vision before night falls, then Hunter in the Night gives you the burst speed to close the gap instantly.
  • Losing the game often comes from being caught in daylight without Dark Ascension—you lose movement speed, vision, and the mini‑stun, making you vulnerable to heroes like Pugna or Beastmaster who excel at daylight engagements.

Item Build

Starting Items

  • Tango — sustain in the off‑lane while you wait for night.
  • Healing Salve — quick health recovery after early skirmishes.
  • Stout Shield — mitigates harassment from melee opponents.
  • Enchanted Mango — provides the burst mana needed for early Void casts.
  • Observer Ward — vision to track enemy rotations before night.

Core Items

  • Phase Boots — extra movement speed and the active charge to close gaps before night.
  • Blink Dagger — essential for instant initiation during Dark Ascension.
  • Black King Bar — protects you from magical burst (e.g., Pugna’s Nether Blast) when you’re the primary initiator.
  • Aghanim’s Scepter — upgrades Void to affect a larger area and reduces cooldown, amplifying night‑time teamfight impact.

Situational Items

  • Shadow Blade — alternative initiation tool; good against line‑of‑sight heavy heroes like Shadow Fiend.
  • Heart of Tarrasque — boosts survivability when you’re the front‑line tank in prolonged fights.
  • Assault Cuirass — provides armor to your team and reduces enemy attack speed, useful against physical cores like Lifestealer.
  • Sange and Yasha — extra movement speed and status resistance, helpful when facing silences from Oracle or Pugna.
  • Gleipnir — adds a powerful area slow/disable, synergizing with Crippling Fear in clustered fights.

Common Mistakes

  • Chasing at day – many low‑MMR players forget that Night Stalker loses his speed and stun at daylight, leading to unnecessary deaths.
  • Over‑relying on Void early – without the night bonus the mini‑stun is weak; aim to save Void for the first night or after Dark Ascension.
  • Neglecting vision – failing to place wards before night lets the enemy avoid your darkness and set up counter‑ganks.
  • Itemizing too quickly into damage – Night Stalker’s strength is durability and initiation; rushing items like Maelstrom can leave you too fragile for late‑game fights.

FAQ

Is Night Stalker good in the current patch?

Yes. With a 52.5% win rate across over 260 k recent ranked matches, Night Stalker remains a reliable pick, especially in night‑time coordinated play and against heroes like Storm Spirit or Zeus where his win rates exceed 56%.

What lane does Night Stalker play?

Night Stalker is typically played in the off‑lane (solo safe lane) to maximize farm and experience while he scales into a night‑time ganker. The lane allows him to use Void and Crippling Fear to harass enemy carries safely.

Who counters Night Stalker?

Heroes that excel in daylight and have strong burst or silence pressure—such as Lifestealer, Shadow Fiend, Pugna, Oracle, Beastmaster, and Windranger—currently give Night Stalker win rates below 42%, making them his toughest match‑ups.
night-stalker.counterHtml:
Night Stalker’s strength lies in his night‑time dominance: massive movement speed, damage, and crowd‑control that let him hunt heroes blind. To shut him down you must deny him the darkness, disrupt his early aggression, and force fights into daylight where his abilities lose potency.

Why These Heroes Beat Night Stalker

Lifestealer

Lifestealer’s Infest lets him bypass Night Stalker’s vision and ambush him from unexpected angles, while Rage provides magic immunity that blocks Night Stalker’s Void mini‑stun and the damage over time from Crippling Fear. Tip: open with Infest into a lane gank right after Dark Ascension ends to catch Night Stalker while his night‑time buffs are on cooldown.

Shadow Fiend

Shadow Fiend’s Shadowrazes and Requiem of Souls deal pure damage that ignores Night Stalker’s armor and the night‑time damage reduction from Dark Ascension. His high early‑game farm lets him out‑damage Night Stalker once the sun rises. Tip: stack souls quickly and force a night‑time duel; the burst will often kill Night Stalker before his Void can land.

Pugna

Pugna’s Nether Blast and Decrepify shred Night Stalker’s health and amplify magic damage, while Nether Ward punishes Night Stalker’s spell usage (Void, Crippling Fear). Tip: position Nether Ward near the lane’s night‑time vision spot so Night Stalker’s spells constantly trigger damage.

Oracle

Oracle’s Fate’s Edict grants magic immunity, nullifying Void’s mini‑stun and the damage component of Crippling Fear. Purifying Flames and False Promise provide strong sustain that outlast Night Stalker’s burst during night. Tip: use Fate’s Edict pre‑emptively when Night Stalker initiates with Dark Ascension to completely block his crowd‑control.

Beastmaster

Beastmaster’s Wild Axes and Primal Roar give reliable stun and damage that can interrupt Night Stalker’s channeling and force him out of the darkness. His summons provide vision that counters Night Stalker’s unobstructed sight during Dark Ascension. Tip: place a Hawk scout near the night‑time vision zone; the extra sight denies Night Stalker’s ability to ambush.

Drafting Against Night Stalker

  • Prioritize heroes with true‑strike or magic‑immune abilities (e.g., Oracle, Pugna).
  • Pick heroes with strong daylight damage or burst (Shadow Fiend, Lifestealer).
  • Include vision‑heavy picks or summons to negate Night Stalker’s unobstructed night sight.
  • Consider bans that remove hard‑disable or high‑mobility heroes that Night Stalker can easily chase (e.g., Anti‑Mage, Queen of Pain).

Laning Against Night Stalker

  • Harass early with ranged damage; Night Stalker is weakest before Dark Ascension (first 2‑3 minutes).
  • Trade when his Void is on cooldown—its mini‑stun is his primary kill tool.
  • Use lane creeps and towers to block his Crippling Fear radius; staying out of melee range reduces damage over time.
  • Force him to pull the lane early, wasting his night‑time mobility and delaying Dark Ascension.

Itemizing Against Night Stalker

Manta Style — dispels Crippling Fear and provides split‑push pressure that Night Stalker can’t chase at night.

Eul’s Scepter of Divinity — cyclones Night Stalker, removing him from fights during Dark Ascension and resetting his cooldowns.

Black King Bar — grants magic immunity, nullifying Void’s mini‑stun and the damage component of Crippling Fear.

Glimmer Cape — gives temporary invisibility and magic resistance, allowing you to dodge Night Stalker’s night‑time burst and escape his chase.
